product_title: SODA POP SHOPPE Jelly Belly Beans ~ 1/2 to 10 Pounds
review_headline: Tiny package, big bucks. NOT worth the money! Should be 1-2 dollars instead of *8* dollars!
review_body:
Okay, as for the TASTE of the jelly bean, they are good. They taste like what you\x27d expect a jelly bean to taste like. Nothing super special or gourmet. It needs to be said that these are *NOT* Jelly Belly and it\x27s misleading. Just because you put "Jelly Belly" on a piece of paper and tape it to a tiny bag, does NOT make it Jelly Belly. The beans are not marked like a jelly belly bean, and the packaging is *NOT* like a jelly belly package. You\x27ve been warned. These seem to be knock-off Jelly Belly\x27s. With *THAT* said, they aren\x27t bad, but my 1 star is only for the taste.

The price is absurd for this amount of jelly beans! I thought I\x27d be getting a bigger package and it\x27s tiny! It\x27s a little more than HALF the size of a vanilla business envelope! I was thinking for the price, I\x27d be getting a huge bag of jelly beans. Nope. That is *NOT* what you\x27ll be getting here. You\x27re better off going to Wally World and buying a few bags. You\x27ll save yourself the disappointment and time and money. I will *NEVER* trust reviews on here again and NEVER buy food off of here again. I get that it\x27s jelly beans and I may seem a bit over emotional about it, but I don\x27t like my money being wasted frivolously.

review_headline: Good tasting for lightly salted but TOO MANY EMPTY SHELLS
review_body:
Well the are good pistachios of course they aren\x27t as good as the regular salted ones but if you are addicted to them and want to be healthier these are the way to go since the main brand name lightly salted are near impossible to find in any good quantities. I will list the reasons I like these along with the one reason I dropped a star:

1. The huge bag at a decent price is great for a family that eats a lot of these like mine.
2. They taste good especially for only being lightly salted.
3. They are PEANUT FREE which of course pistachios are but a lot of companies use machines that process peanuts so it is a bonus because my kid has a peanut allergy.
4. They all seem to be ripe enough and cooked well enough where you don\x27t have those that are almost impossible to open without breaking a nail or a tooth.

All of that being said I dropped one star because there was an excessive amount of empty shells by excessive I mean there were easily visible empty shells in the bag just by glancing and every handful I grabbed had at least two empty shells in it which might not sound like much but considering this bag probably has upwards of 100 handfuls you can see where it adds up. I hate to say it but there are so many it almost seems as if they were purposely mixed in.

product_title: Tropical Traditions Organic Virgin Coconut Oil - Gold Label
review_body: This is an update to the original review, which I\x27ll leave below: Tropical Traditions sent a 32. oz  jar of the green label to try after the bad experience with the 16 oz gold label.  This was a generous gesture and much appreciated. It turns out the green label that we received is awesome, had none of the problems of the gold label, and was superior to other brands of coconut oils we\x27ve used.  I hope tropical traditions will sell the green label on Amazon, either directly or through a distributor.  I appreciate Tropical Traditions taking a risk to send a large free sample of their other product.  I\x27m leaving the two star review for the gold label because it tasted so terrible, but if the green label were on Amazon I would give it a 5-star review.    original review:   Product tasted and smelled foul.  I\x27m a daily coconut oil user and don\x27t mind paying a premium for the best, so I was excited to find this product.  I understand accidents, mistakes and "bad batches" happen, and that\x27s no problem.  I have no idea what category this falls into.  Unfortunately I didn\x27t open the jar until I used up the other coconut oil already in my cupboard and more than 30 days had passed.  If you do purchase, open and taste right away.  At first neither the seller, Natural Sweetie, nor the manufacturer, Tropical Traditions would assume responsibility and provide a label and / or a refund.  After several unsuccessful attempts for a resolution, I posted an honest negative review. After I did so, on the same day, the seller, Natural Sweetie gave me a refund and the manufacturer offered to send me their other product, "Green Label Coconut Oil" to sample.  This was greatly appreciated on both counts.  I won\x27t know if I got a bad batch or not, because I won\x27t be ordering another and neither party offered to send me another.  But, I will try the Green Label and see what happens.  I do think the negative review contributed to both the seller and manufacturer taking action, which on one hand is greatly appreciated, and on the other hand, has me concerned for other consumers whose requests for resolution could be refused unless they, too, post a negative review that the seller or manufacturer would prefer be taken down.  So, I\x27m changing my review from one star, which was a combination of a bad jar plus no action from the seller(s) to tw stars, which reflects a bad jar plus helpful action from the seller(s).

product_title: Bulksupplements Pure Stevia Powder
review_headline: and again it is good stuff. I have an old Kal brand container ...
review_body:
bought it again, and again it is good stuff. I have an old Kal brand container that I pour it into for use at work, and another Kal brand container I pour it into at home. Those containers are 1.3 oz each, and this bag (100g) is 3.5 oz. Well more than enough for two containers that\x27d be far more than the price of this bag. The taste is also quality! I use two of the little scoops (I have two of them, not sure if this comes with it or not) which tastes about like I put two teaspoons of sugar into my coffee. by the way, the 90% part isn\x27t how much stevia is in it, it\x27s how much of a concentration of stevia extract it is. (not using the right terms, but yeah) It\x27s next to impossible to get 100%.

So everyone knows, the reviews saying how it\x27s bad because it doesn\x27t dilute in their beverage is a little post-haste. Stevia doesn\x27t dilute well in cold beverages unless it\x27s stirred very well. It does dilute though, it just takes effort. The chemically taste people talk about? That happens when you use far too much, or you drop it directly on your tongue. It\x27s an intense sweet taste, don\x27t expect it to be exactly like sugar.

product_title: Light Grey Celtic coarse sea salt, 1 lb. bag
review_headline: Buy this product for the taste, not the purported health benefits.
review_body:
It\x27s true that this product contains a lot of trace minerals not present in common table salt, which has been processed precisely to remove such things for use in cooking.

As an "all-purpose" salt, regular processed salt (either table salt, kosher, or rock, depending on the texture you need) should remain your "go-to" salt. The trace minerals in gourmet salts may not be appropriate for a particular dish. (For instance, you don\x27t want the "mineral" taste in a cake or delicate savory dish.) Using processed salts eliminates such concerns. And processed salts have the advantage of being incredibly cheap (a canister of store-brand table salt is 38 cents where I shop), utterly ubiquitous, and completely consistent.

For starters, ALL salt is "sea salt"; the only difference is the age of the sea. Because it\x27s easier to purify, and assured to be free of man-made contaminants, table salt is produced by injecting brine into an underground salt deposit from an ancient ocean. The brine is pumped out, impurities removed (everything but Sodium Chloride) and the water evaporated in a vacuum chamber designed to produce a consistent grain size.

For table salt, a small-grain product is used, and then an anti-caking agent (usually calcium silicate), Iodine, and dextrose. (The dextrose keeps the iodine from breaking down, which would render it useless.) Calcium Silicate is present naturally in many foods; it\x27s added to salt because it does a great job absorbing water. Iodine was added to salt when it was discovered that many diets were deficient in the stuff, and this can cause developmental problems and thyroid issues. If you\x27ve analyzed your diet and discovered it has sufficient iodine, you can certainly depend on a non-iodized product, which is on the shelf right next to the iodized stuff in most stores; no need to buy fancy gourmet salt.

Table salt is ideal for baking, or in any food where you don\x27t want to stumble into a pocket of salt because the small grain size dissolves readily.

Kosher salt and rock salt have a higher grain size, and generally no additives.

Gourmet salts are generally produced through either evaporating sea water, or, in the case of this product, mined from the ground but using neither water injection nor explosives. (Explosives are used to mine salt for industrial use, but the explosive residue would make it unsuitable for human consumption, which is why human-consumption salt uses brine-based mining.) The drawback of such "natural" salts is the possibility of it coming from a contaminated source. The salt mines used for ordinary table salt are so far underground that the chance of contamination is zero.

It is certainly true that gourmet salts have trace minerals that have been removed from table salt. And depending on the specific mineral content of the salt, it can impart a unique taste. However, the amount of these minerals is so small, that the health benefits are negligible. If you rely on this salt for your Potassium, Magnesium, or "other important trace minerals", you will be quite deficient. The best source of those minerals is foods that contain them. A well-balanced diet should have more than enough of every mineral you need. (And, in salt used as a seasoning, you don\x27t WANT much, say, potassium chloride. (To discover how that tastes, try some "Salt Substitute"; THAT\x27s what KCl tastes like... it\x27s kinda close, but not an exact substitute.))

In conclusion, feel free to buy and use this product as a seasoning. But for routine use in recipes, a conventional salt of a grain size appropriate for your food is probably best. If you are nutritionally deficient in some minerals, there are better ways to get it vs. depending on your salt.

product_title: Fee Brothers Black Walnut Bitters 5oz
review_headline: Here\x27s my favorite way to use my favorite bitters.
review_body:
I love this bitters. Here is a recipe for my new favorite drink-
This is essentially a Utah sazerac, traditionally made with Absinthe which is very expensive and nearly unavailable at the state run liquor stores here. I substitute a little ouzo, I cannot stress enough how little. I just \x27wash\x27 the glass with it and let any extra run out before continuing.
2oz. of High West Double Rye
The barest whisper of Ouzo, just the tiniest splash.
1-2 dashes of Fee Brothers Black Walnut Bitters ( I like 2 but 1 is probably sufficient.)
One decent sized piece of Orange Peel, the less of the white bitter pith the better, I like to shoot for one thumb sized peel of just the zest part of the peel.
Throw it all together in a rocks glass over ice and enjoy.

3. Salt
4. Chili powder

Turbana Chili (ingredients):

review_headline: Quality of LouAna Peanut Oil Significantly Declines, Beware of Substandard Oil
review_body: I have used LouAna peanut oil exclusively for frying turkeys for over 10 years.  This Thanksgiving I used it again but the turkey did not fry properly.  The temperature was at the appropriate temperature and I cooked it for the proper time, like I have done in the past.  This turkey the skin was rubbery, and not at all crispy even though the temperature was right on.  I even cooked it for an extra 20 minutes, and it was still the same.  The temperature in the breast was fine (so it cooked), just not crispy, like it always had been.  I tried contacting LouAna customer service, and never received any response.  I have heard that they reformulated the oil, with additives to cost them less money, however the quality has taken a big hit.  I used LouAna exclusively, even though it was more expensive than competitors, because it was supposed to be dependable....no longer!  I will be looking at their competition now, no sense in paying more for the same or lower quality than their competitors.

product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_headline: 3.5 stars; I like it but I don\x27t love it...
review_body: I would probably give this 3.5 stars if I could, but I rounded down.  I went from the Flex to the Charge HR.  I wanted to love the Charge, and I like it, but it\x27s not perfect.    Here are the pros and cons:    Pros:  1) The heart-rate monitor is very cool, and the data it tracks and displays is very useful; it focuses on your baseline/resting heartrate each day, which is calculated using your sleeping heartrate plus your heartrate during prolonged periods of inactivity, such as sitting on the couch or sitting at your desk; the idea being, of course, that the lower your baseline heartrate, the generally more fit you are.  It is fun to focus long-term on improving cardio by hopefully watching the baseline heartrate decrease over time.  2) The screen is very customizable, in that you can easily (within the FitBit app) change the order of what stats are displayed, remove ones you don\x27t like (I removed floors climbed, for example, because it doesn\x27t work; see below); you can choose what is shown when you double-tap the front of the Charge (I chose time/date), and then you can set the order of what is displayed when you push the small button on the side (I chose heartrate first, then steps, then distance traveled, then date/time)  3) Exercise mode is improved over the Flex; you can still activate via the app, but you can now also activate via holding down the side button for a second or two; in exercise mode, your heartrate is measured every second, as opposed to every 5 seconds in regular mode.  4) The Charge is actually slightly smaller than I expected, it a good way.  Some of the reviews were making it out to be a huge monstrosity in comparison to the Flex.  It is not.  I am old-school and still wear a regular watch (gasp!) on my left wrist, so I wear the Charge on my dominant/right wrist and it\x27s not a problem and doesn\x27t interfere with using a computer/mouse, or other daily tasks.  5) Auto-tracking of sleep is AWESOME.  It even caught my couch-nap one late night before I got up and actually went to bed.  That in an of itself makes it a pretty worthwhile purchase in my humble opinion.    Cons:  1) \x5C\x22Floors climbed\x5C\x22 is completely inaccurate; it seems to count a bunch of floors in exercise mode when I\x27m jogging and not climbing any steps.  One day it randomly said I had done 5,247 floors, and another day it said 432.  In the course of my day, I usually actually climb 10-15 floors, so I have no idea where it got that information from.  2) Unlike the Flex, which basically has the jelly-bean-sized device inside the bracelets, the Charge HR is all one piece.  The rubberized \x5C\x22watch band\x5C\x22 seems like it may not last forever, so if you get a tear in the band I\x27m afraid you\x27ll render your HR useless at worst, or at best you\x27ll have to send it off to be repaired.  3) This one, unlike the flex, is not shower-proof.  That\x27s not a huge deal but annoying nonetheless.  4) The recommendation by FitBit is to wear this one finger-length above your wrist bone, or two finger-lengths above the wrist bone during exercise; because the device is thicker and bulkier than the Flex, wearing it that high on the arm is a bit awkward and uncomfortable; I am pretty much used to it after about 10 days of wear, but it can be annoying at times.    I WOULD purchase this again if given the choice, and I will continue to wear it.  I just wish the floors climbed would work, and I hope that I\x27m wrong about what appears to be a relatively flimsy watch-band situation.

review_headline: Fertility Blend---- cure for endometriosis pain
review_body:
First, I came across Fertility Blend in the \x27Hormone Cure\x27 book by Dr. Sarah Gottfried. I also read lot of reviews here on Amazon and then went to Fertility Blend\x27s site to check out the product a bit more. I have some hot flashes here and there, terrible endometriosis pain associated with period and ovulation, and spotting before cycle. Although I was skeptical, still bought this in last June for one month supply. First month, I had severe pain associated with my cycle. Then slowly I noticed that my pain went away and spotting was a bit better. I did try it for 3 months and took a break and then started again. My cycle is not heavy anymore, don\x27t have any pelvic pain and very regular cycle ( not that was a concern before). I am so thankful for this product that I cannot explain. Yes, I still have the spotting issue but it\x27s only for a day or two compared to how it was before. I wish I read about the reviews of this product before since I have been dealing with endo pain for a long time. Anyone out there with endometriosis, please do not take birth control pills or drugs to suppress your period all together. They are extremely harmful and don\x27t listen to your doctor if he/she wants to put you on Lupron. I have suffered long enough and don\x27t want anyone else to go through with what I been through in life. Start slow by taking only 1 or two capsules and then you can increase/lower dose depending on how you feel. Also don\x27t forget to take a month break after 3 months of therapy. Please do not take this while you are undergoing fertility treatments of any sort, just like it says on the label. I hope this review will help someone out there with endometriosis or ovulation issues.

Ladies also please try to use natural sanitary products like Seventh generation and stay away from plastic containers. Endo is a terrible disease but it can be controlled if you are willing to change your day to day activity. So please try Fertility Blend and don\x27t be discouraged inthe first 1-2 months with pelvic pains or even heavy flow/ spotting before period since, your hormones are changing with the supplement. It will go away in a few weeks. I also would like to say that I didn\x27t get paid by the Wellness company or Amazon to write this review. Hope my review helps someone out there.

product_title: Fitbit Charge Wireless Activity Wristband
review_body:
I had a Fitbit One and I was always forgetting to recharge it, or put it on for sleep, or activate it for sleep, or SOMETHING. I heard about the new Charge and upon read the other reviews and some of the comparisons, I was excited. I have really small wrists, but was right on the cusp between small and large. The Fitbit website says in that instance, GO BIIGGER! They\x27re right. :-) Bought the Large. I have found my Charge HR to be accurate, and being able to see the steps motivates me to move more. As my boyfriend said once when I told him "We can\x27t go to the grocery store, I have to go back to the house and get my Fitbit! (I had the One)," "You took the steps whether they are counted or not." I find that as someone who sits on the computer, moves my hand flipping pages of things I\x27m dictating, working my grad school retail job, my steps are fairly accurate. When it\x27s not as high as I want (625 on a lazy Sunday, YEESH!), I know I need to get out and move more.

Pros:
- I can see everything on my wrist - the One was hidden in my pocket, so all the nifty flowers, etc, I could never see. This also means it serves as a watch. :-)
- It tells me who\x27 s calling. If you connect it to your phone via bluetooth (which is what allows for syncing to the app), it will tell you who\x27s calling if the phones within range. It takes a second for it to buzz (I can hear the phone first), but I\x27ve already found this handy. No, you can\x27t answer the call, it\x27s just a notification.
- It automatically knows when I\x27m asleep. I\x27m trying to get sleep data and figure out sleep patterns, so this is helpful
- I can set it to default to whatever screen I want (this can be done at the fitbit website, in the devices screen)
- Splash proof. I\x27ve worn it doing dishes, and the websites states that you CAN technically wear it in the shower, but that they recommend you not in order to prevent anything from getting under the band and held against your skin. Because of the way the tracker sits against my wrist, it is nice to give it a little break (I\x27m actually going to set up a "charging station" in my bathroom so that I charge it while I shower, solving two problems at once).

Cons:
- It was a pain to figure out where the manual was. I only found an online manual, and it was a link posted in a forum I found after 5 minutes of searching. Perhaps some of the setup (like how to change what it defaults to) was intuitive for other people, but it didn\x27t occur to me that I would have to log in to the website and do it through there. If the set up software told me I would, I missed it when I turned to scold the cat. I found my One to be more intuitive to set up.

Overall: I love this tracker, I sprung for the HR model so that when I\x27m working out I can see my heart rate. I had the One, and I kept it so that when they add the ability to have multiple devices to one Fitbit account, if I\x27m going somewhere nice/fancy, I can use my One clipped to my bra instead of my Charge HR. The One is nice, and I like it. It\x27s great for people who don\x27t want something on their wrist, and don\x27t want/need to be able to see the data. I\x27m forgetful, and I needed something more in my face. Had the Charge been available last summer, I probably would have bought that. (it combines the things I wanted in the Flexx - being on the wrist, letting you see things - with the more numerous things I loved about the One - like counting all the stairs up to my apartment, ha). I also bought the Fitbit Aria scale, and thing that the Charge and Aria make a great combination.

And for anyone with questions about the step counting, here\x27s what the Fitbit website says:
"Fitbit trackers use a 3-axis accelerometer to understand your motions. An accelerometer is a device that turns movement (acceleration) of a body into digital measurements (data) when attached to the body. By analyzing acceleration data, our trackers provide detailed information about frequency, duration, intensity, and patterns of movement to determine your steps taken, distance traveled, calories burned, and sleep quality. The 3-axis implementation allows the accelerometer to measure your motion in any way that you move, making its activity measurements more precise than older, single-axis pedometers.
Fitbit trackers have a finely tuned algorithm for step counting. The algorithm is designed to look for motion patterns most indicative of people walking. One condition for a motion pattern to be recognized as a step is the motion must be large enough. The algorithm implements this by setting a threshold. If a motion and its subsequent acceleration measurement data meet the threshold, the motion will be counted as a step. If that threshold is not met, the algorithm won\xE2\x80\x99t count the motion as a step. Other factors can create enough acceleration to meet our threshold and therefore cause some over counting of steps, such as riding on a bumpy road. Equally, it\x27s possible for the algorithm to undercount (not meet the required acceleration threshold). Examples here include walking on a very soft surface such as a plush carpet."

review_body: I got the charge HR for the HRM was hoping to not have to wear a strap during activities. As far as a step tracker and sleep monitor it works great, tracks floors and distance, pretty much what all fitbit products do. Very happy with that.    As for the heart rate monitor it\x27s garbage. It\x27s only good for slow steady state activities like walking or a job maybe a bike ride. Thinks like a treadmill all seem to be okay. Anything where you heart rate will change rapidly, like weights, high intensity interval training, crossfit, sports like soccer. It\x27s way off and can\x27t handle the quick changes so it either just stops or gets stuck on a low reading. After doing several Insanity routines with an average heart rate of 146 using a polar H7 the charge HR clocked me at an average of 116 for 40 minutes and didn\x27t break 130 as a max heart rate. The polar had me in the 160+ range for over 20 minutes.    Even if I run up a flight of 8 floors, I know my heart rate is up to 150+ the Charge HR will show 90 lol    So if you\x27re looking to go for evening strolls and see what your heart rate is like great. For anyone serious about workouts it\x27s no where near a strap. As it stand I love the daily stuff but the HRM is just a novelty at this point. I can\x27t recommend it for anyone who is in any kind of HIIT, crossfit, weights or sports.

product_title: BRI Nutrition Caralluma Fimbriata - 20:1 Extract Maximum Strength Supplement - Made From Pure Indian Caralluma Fimbriata
review_body:
I am skeptical about the latest, greatest weight loss product. In my experience, the only thing that works is exercise and reduced food intake (not necessarily calories). I have, against my better judgement tried several things that are supposed to be WOW! like green coffee extract and raspberry ketons etc. and none of them work for me. I am sensitive to caffeine and sugar and tend to experience ugly mood changes when I take any kind of stimulant. Having said all of that, I will say that there is no jittery "high" from this product. It does suppress your appetite. Some of the reviews said that it helps burn fat and I don\x27t know if this is true or not. This is not a miracle product that you take and automatically lose weight. My weight issues generally come from eating for reasons other than hunger and also from overeating. So, I have been taking these for about 5-6 days and this is what I have found for myself: It has suppressed my appetite so that I don\x27t feel PHYSICALLY hungry. I seem to be more aware that I am full and that happens fairly quickly. I eat fast and this can lead to overeating, so it seems that maybe my stomach is communicating my fullness faster or maybe it\x27s just because I\x27m not ravenous when I do sit down to eat. I can still eat when I\x27m not hungry and I can still overeat while using this, but it is a conscious and deliberate decision. Another thing that I have noticed is that with other products is that by the end of the day, I want to eat everything in sight. This has not happened with the Caralluma.
I eat for many reasons. I have found out in the last couple of days that one of the reasons is because I may have an funny or unpleasant taste in my mouth. If I chew gum, it takes care of that and I refrain from eating because I am not HUNGRY. sometimes I eat because it\x27s a habit associated with other activities. I tend to eat in front of the TV so I find that I want something when I watch a show because it\x27s habit.
One person said in their review that they found they had better results by taking one in the morning and the 2nd in the afternoon. I tried that and it seemed that I didn\x27t want to go to sleep. I wasn\x27t wired, just not sleepy. I have switched back to the instructed dose of taking both pills in the morning and that seems to work well. I think that\x27s just individual choice.
As a skeptic of these wonder products, I have to say that it is worth a try. I have to say though that it will not do all the work for you. It will help you by suppressing appetite, but you have to be aware of and willing to change your habits. I believe that it is possible to lose weight without exercise, but you will lose it faster and tone your muscles if you do exercise.

product_title: Nature Babycare Eco-Sensitive Wipes
review_body:
I\x27m not 100% sure what happened, but the first time we used these wipes (and after I had used them for a couple of days), my son\x27s diaper area broke out in a horrible rash. After a few days of seeing raised red bumps, I stopped using the wipes (and switched back to our Seventh Generation wipes), and the rash disappeared.

I was all ready to write about our negative experience, but because I am such a dedicated reviewer (and possibly the worst mother in the world), I decided to give the wipes a second chance. I just wanted to be sure. Well, the second half of the wipes package was totally fine for us. No rash, no redness, nothing but clear, clear skin. So even though the rash initially showed up when we started the new wipes and left when we stopped using them, I think it must have been a coincidence. I don\x27t know. I can\x27t explain it. All I know is that my baby is completely fine with these wipes now, and we are on our third pack.

I did check all the ingredients (and it\x27s a short list) against Environmental Working Group\x27s Skin Deep database, ewg dot org slash skindeep. The ingredients in these wipes are pretty tame. A few of the preservatives scored a 3, but that was it. (Ideally, you\x27d want all the ingredients to be as close to zero as possible on EWG\x27s ten-point scale.)

So now that we aren\x27t having any problems with these wipes, I might even start using these instead of Seventh Generation\x27s, honestly. They are just slightly more expensive, but the fact that they are compostable is a huge selling point for me. I\x27m really happy with them.

product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_headline: Works amazingly well - remember to size it properly, as they want it higher up on your wrist for better HR accuracy.
review_body:
Hello everyone, this is a review for the Charge HR. This is my first and only exercise monitor device. This is written *after* day 4 of use, with 3 exercise periods in the evenings, and then worn to sleep for all 4 nights. I charged it up fully first, and it has plenty of charge left after this usage period.

- phase 1: unbox/setup. No problems. Account creation and first activation/sync went fine.
- phase 2: heavy usage. Evening 1 was exercise period 1. As the manual indicates, you toggle on "exercise mode" by briefly holding the button. This is a great feature. Elliptical 20mins, pushups, resistance bands. I did not have it on snugly enough! HR tracking and "steps" were very good, I was concerned the elliptical would throw it off. The unit seems to have great heart rate sensors even through sweat. It was quite close to the calorie burn estimate of the elliptical as well as distance traveled. Nice! Just make a mental note to hit the button again to stop the exercise mode timer.
- phase 3: SLEEP. This one will be a big selling point for folks, including myself. What\x27s your resting heart rate? How often do you essentially "wake up" each night? Well this unit will tell you just that! Over 4 nights, it says I\x27m restless 24 TIMES.... an average of 6 times per night? YIKES. Well, I suppose that\x27s accurate... I do toss and turn quite a bit. Gotta face the facts here. It also says I was full on "awake" twice. Hmm.
- phase 4: general wear. walking around, to a nearby place to get lunch, up and down actual stairs, just checking to see if it\x27s always tracking. Yes, it most certainly is.

Let\x27s just cover the dashboard briefly: your fitbit data is pushed to fitbit and retrieved via a web portal from which your account is used to view the synced up and aggregate data. It\x27s crisp, clean, and in a tile format that you can move on the web page for your own "at a glance" customization. I have sleep on the top as well as calories burned. That\x27s what we\x27re all aiming for, right? Burn those calories but also get a better night\x27s sleep, which then helps us burn more calories the next day instead of being sore or tired or depleted.

Don\x27t forget to go click on the sleep tile, or into the log - that\x27s where the sleep data is. The dashboard is just at a glance.

Overall, very pleased with this unit. It is very accurate and is eager to perform its job for you!

Final tip: DO NOT LOOK UNDERNEATH IT while it\x27s running. There is an epilepsy warning for good reason. The green lights are flashing extremely quickly. It will accidentally happen briefly to be sure when you are trying to get it on or off your wrist, but do your best not to stare right at it for a long period of time deliberately.

review_body:
This is a great balance of nutrition and value. There are other prenatals on the market that have more ingredients and higher nutrition, but they also cost more. On a positive note, I experienced less discomfort when I took the vitamins right before bed time. When I took the vitamins first thing in the morning, right around 5pm I would get super bloated and gassy. Just in time to ruin dinner and an evening with my husband. If I take the vitamins at night right before bed then my bloating arrives in the morning, and that timing just works out better for me personally.

product_title: Frankincense (Boswellia carterii) 100% Pure Therapeutic Grade Essential Oil by Edens Garden
review_body: Garbage.  Scam.  False Advertising.  These are the words I will associate with Edens Garden and their Frankincense oil.  I purchased this brand because I was looking for the Boswellia Carteri species/variety as it is known for its healing properties.  My previous purchase of Frankincense oil was from Simplers Botanicals.  The Frankincense oil they sell is exceptional!  The aroma is strong but pleasant and produces a very calming feeling when inhaled or applied topically.  However, 2ml costs $15 so I have been looking for something more affordable.  The Frankincense I received from Edens Garden was horrific.  There was a very faint smell of frankincense under the overwhelming smell of what was undoubtedly another chemical, presumable alcohol, and upon topical application it dried up and evaporated within a minute.  The aroma was foul, topically evaporated, and provided no medicinal value as compared to a higher end oil.  What does this tell you?  But Edens Garden says it is "100% Pure Therapeutic Grade Essential Oil"!  Yeah, don\x27t buy into it.  After further research, I found many of the cheap Frankincense oils on the market have been adulterated or distilled with alcohol and apparently oils can be labeled as \xE2\x80\x9Cpure\xE2\x80\x9D with only 3% of the pure oil in the bottle.  Tell me this isn\x27t a scam!  I really wanted to try some of their other line of oils as well but unfortunately this is a brand I cannot trust.  I will not order from them again because who knows what you are really getting in that bottle.  I will however try another manufactured of Frankincense oil.  And how this product received 4 1/2 stars is beyond me!  Maybe these 5 star reviews are fake too!

product_title: Muscle Feast Pure D-Ribose
review_headline: Beware - if you are a first time buyer of this product
review_body:
I bought this brand of D-Ribose because it had the best price per gram...

The instructions say to use "1 level scoop, 5 Grams." per dose. After a few weeks of using this dose,
I thought it odd the "scoop" inside this product seemed much smaller than other D-Ribose brands I have bought and used in the past... Fortunately I have a Gram scale, the scoop inside this product is NOT 5 grams as stated on the label, but rather 2.5 grams weighed on my scale.. So if the other packages of this product is sold with the same size scoop as mine, the actual dose everyone is getting is 2.5 grams and NOT 5 grams as stated on the package..

I gave this product 1 Star to alert others who may be buying this item for the first time, need to be sure they weigh the product inside of their scoop. If it is 2.5 grams as mine is, need to take 2 scoops per dose.. If I had not used other brands of D-Ribose in the past, I would never have known the scoop size was only 2.5 grams and thus I would have been using far too little of this product each dose. 2.5 grams is too light of a dose to use for this product..

And for that reason, I am disappointed in this product.

I am surprised the seller of this product did not catch this.

review_headline: Three stars, because it does not seem to measure ...
review_body:
Three stars, because it does not seem to measure "room" temperature accurately. I tested this in multiple ways, and I\x27ve come to the conclusion that it doesn\x27t even use the IR sensor to do room temperature, and is simply going off of whatever the temperature of the unit itself is. (I say this because I can take the temperature of a room/area that is verifiably 20 degrees different, and it will still be reading the previous rooms temp. And if I leave the unit in the area that is 20 degrees different for a long enough period of time, it will read the different temp, and then if I go to the previous room, it will read the same reading until it is left there long enough for the unit itself to come to that room\x27s temp.)

the body temp and surface temp readings seem to be accurate though, and thats the most important thing. I will still be keeping this unit.

review_headline: Very useful after wisdom molar extraction(s)
review_body:
Many people have different uses for these and while i can\x27t say whether it does the rest good i can say they did indeed help after my wisdom molars were removed.

After extraction you are left with \x27\x27holes\x27\x27 , holes which take time to fill back over time. The hollow space will be a gap where bone used to be, bone that the surgeon and or assistants hammered, broke and drilled.

This is very usefull because simply doing mouthwash won\x27t be able to clean those holes out and if you leave food in them while you are healing you are bound to get an infection. Also for the first first week or two its not recommended you swirl or spit too much after extraction so gently using these is a life saver to prevent infection in and around extractions.

I have no idea how some other users managed to use a SINGLE one of these for a long period of time but i can safely say for prolonged irrigation after every meal after extractions one of these will probably only last 2 weeks. After more use the plunger begins to get stuck and gradually make it moving back and forth very stiff.

So its good if you buy in sets as opposed to single ones, and buying online while not the most convenient if you need them right away it is the less expensive way. Many stores like walgreens, cvs, and such don\x27t even carry these well at least not the ones with the curved tips which are the only ones worthwhile using after wisdom extraction because of where they can reach.

Even after your extraction sites heal these are still good to use for overall irrigation around the gums and it does get some food out that possibly flossing might not.

If you are having or just had your wisdom molars extracted just be prepared for a long healing process, the holes take many months to fill maybe even more than a year ( bone regeneration takes a while) and even then you will still have a bit of dents where the molars used to be. You will probably be using these fora couple of months depending on how fast your healing process goes.

You don\x27t need to constantly be flushing food out with these after every meal ( if your schedule limits you) after your extraction sites have healed good ( after 2 months orso). However if food does get stuck in there for a day orso you can still get an infection so use these at least twice a day if you can even after extraction sites have healed

If you truly want to have zero anxiety, I don\xE2\x80\x99t think anything you can buy on Amazon will do that for you. Maybe therapy and a cocktail of prescriptions, but that is obviously not without its risks and downsides. If you are looking to feel quite a bit better and avoid taking an ssri, I think this is worth a try. review_body:
WHAT I LIKE ABOUT THIS PRODUCT:

1) It\x27s sublingual. (It bypasses the digestive system, so can be an effective alternative for those who don\x27t absorb B12 well from food)

2) It\x27s free of common irritants and allergens like wheat, gluten and dairy

3) The manufacturer, Solgar, is a respected company with a good reputation for quality control.

4) Unlike some B12 supplements, it contains the entire B12 complex. It\x27s especially important to supplement folic acid or folate if you take B12; it\x27s well supplied in this formula.

**************************************

THE CYANOCOBALAMIN QUESTION

Some reviewers have pointed out that this product contains cyanocobalamin, and they prefer the methylcobalamin form. They point out that the cyano form contains trace amounts of mercury and cyanide.

This is a legitimate point to raise, but to put it in context, there are actually five types of B12 (not just two). Each of them has advantages and disadvantages. The types are:

**************************************

1) CYANOBOBALAMIN (the type used in this product, and in B12 injections)

Cyanocobalamin is popular with manufacturers because it\x27s inexpensive. Critics point out that it contains traces of mercury and cyanide. Defenders point out that it\x27s more stable than the methyl form, and that the amount of mercury or cyanide is a fraction of what would be found in an organic apple or a typical dinner salad.

Side note: If you avoid the Solgar product because of the cyanocobalamin in it, you should probably also avoid B12 shots, as they also usually contain the cyano form.... and injecting mercury and cyanide, even in trace amounts, into the body is likely to be more problematic than taking them orally.

**************************************

2) METHYLCOBALAMIN (a popular alternative to the cyano form).

Those who criticize cyanocobalamin tend to promote methylcobalamin as an improvement over the cyano form. It does not contain even trace amounts of mercury or cyanide, and some studies have suggested it may be better absorbed. On the down side, the methyl form has been reported to cause agitation and hyperactivity. Dr. Russell Jaffe recommends against using it, and recommends using the hydroxo form instead.

**************************************

3) ADENOSYLCOBALAMIN (sometimes called coenzyme B12, cobamamide, or dibencozide)

This form can be stored in the body, unlike other forms that are washed out in the urine. This could be good or bad, because one nice thing about B vitamins is that because the body doesn\x27t store most forms of them, there\x27s less of an overdosing danger than there is with fat soluble vitamins, which build up in the bloodstream.

**************************************

4) HYDROXYCOBALAMIN (very powerful but expensive, and rare in supplements
This is the kind sold by a company called Perque, which is promoted as superior to either the methyl or cyano forms. On the down side, it\x27s more expensive, and some people have reported feeling jittery when taking this form.

**************************************

5) GLUTATHIONYLCOBALAMIN (found in a product called Reverse; a combination of glutathione and B12). (An interesting ideas but it costs several times more than the other alternatives).

Having tried several of them, I\x27ve come back to this product. I can feel a difference when I take it, which I don\x27t feel when I take the methylcobalamin form.

**************************************

MY RECOMMENDATIONS

1) This probably goes without saying: get your B12 from food if possible. Organ meats such as liver are a great source. Eating liver a couple of times a week is a great way to raise your B12 levels naturally.

If you\x27re vegan, though, or don\x27t absorb B12 well from foods, or have a higher than usual need for it, you should definitely supplement. It\x27s an essential nutrient, and if you\x27re not getting enough, you can experience irreparable neurological damage. No fun and not fixable, if you wait too long to start supplementing.

2) I know some people will make different choices, and I respect their right to do so, but I plan to keep taking the Solgar product because, frankly, it gives me better results than the methylcobalamin form. I feel a decided difference when I take it, similar to the effect I get from a B12 shot... and I don\x27t feel the same effect when I take the methyl form.

The truth seems to be that, these days, in this polluted world, it\x27s hard to completely avoid taking in heavy metals from food, air and supplements. You can\x27t even eat rice, or even organic fruit, for example, without getting a small amount of lead and arsenic. So rather than get too panicky about it, I prefer to go ahead and take the most effective supplements, then detox my body regularly to clean out any metals that may be accumulating.

(Taking daily doses of vitamin C, zinc and selenium is an effective way to clean out unwanted metals you may be getting from food, water, air, supplements or other sources, and to me makes more sense than avoiding what may be the most effective supplements.)

3) If you do decide to supplement, look not only at the form of B12, but the delivery method. Of the various methods I\x27ve tried, I have had the best results with this one (Solgar\x27s sublingual), and with transdermal (B12 cream). One very good product along those lines is Maxasorb B12, which is rubbed on the wrists and absorbed through the skin. This avoids the problems with both oral and sublingual forms.

4) I personally get the best results from taking both Solgar sublingual B12 and Maxasorb dermal B12 every day. Taken together, they feel as effective as getting B12 injections, and are a heck of a lot cheaper.

IS THERE MSG IN THIS PRODUCT?

One reviewer wrote that her relative had had a reaction after taking this product, so she concluded it had MSG in it. I\x27m sensitive to MSG (I get the "tight headband around the forehead" reaction when I eat foods containing it), and I\x27ve taken this product for months with no such reaction. So I doubt that it contains MSG.

It\x27s also important to remember that just because something happens after you take a product, does not mean the product caused the reaction. Amazon reviews are full of statements like, "I took this product, then got a headache... that means this product causes headaches!" or "I took this supplement, then passed my math test... the supplement made me pass my test!" review_body: I gave this one star because the only reviews I really read are the one star ones. The negative reviews left for this are such a croc, so I wanted people to see a real review. I will try to remember in 10 years to come back and tell you if the bock is still going strong. There does not appear to be a warranty like the Littman\x27s have, and I am not sure that you can get the Bock refurbished like you can the Littman. But at less than 1/4th the price, if it lasts 3 years, it will still be a good value. I hope this helps.

product_title: Crane Cool Mist Green Frog Humidifier
review_body:
I\x27ve been happy with my froggy I\x27ve been using it for 2 years now with distilled water and it does seem that it\x27s now dying the motor makes a loud growling noise when you first turn it on now and it\x27s getting a bit flakey in that some times the red light is on in the morning but there\x27s still water in the tank. I emailed customer service but I\x27m not anticipating much in return as I\x27ve had the product for 2 years. So a bit disappointing it didn\x27t last longer but I have also purchased the dew drop, owl and cow and I\x27m happy with how quiet they are and function so far (the cow and owl are pretty new yet).

You do need to read the manual. The only problem I\x27ve had with it was it wouldn\x27t start one day and I got the manual out and read I wasn\x27t supposed to move it as one piece with water in it so I removed some water and it started working, I find the water cap gets misthreaded easily but the cow and owl they seem to have corrected this issue.

I have never had any leaks with it or any of them but I do bring a towel with me when I go to empty them. There will be condensation in the lid. I take the character face off, wipe it and then wipe off the top of the water container before trying to lift it out. By having a towel handy I haven\x27t had any problems. I\x27ve never had water leak from the water basin.

I prefer the adorable over the dew drop because I found the dew drop to be slightly louder and I didn\x27t like how the light in the dew drop one lit up the water and created a lot of light so we use that one in the living room.

After froggy died my husband took it apart and he said the fan inside is similar to the cheap computer fans that are also notoriously flakey.

Replaced froggy with a dew drop model instead.

Upon suggestion of a physical therapist I purchased these pillows - one I leave at home and the other I brought with me to work, on airplanes, to the movies, etc. (That was how bad the pain was, I carried the darn pillow with me!!!)

Between using this pillow and rolling up a small towel for lumbar support, I immediately noticed a small improvement in the pain level as I was sitting. And over time (2-3 months or so), the pain went away!

I still use them at home while watching TV even though I am no longer in pain. And they still are as supportive as the day I bought them.

Some others mentioned numbness (that does not happen with me) or making you sit too high (I am 6\x27 tall and that has never been an issue for me either).

In sum, these pillows have been wonderful, look great after 3 years and are just as supportive. They absolutely worked for me!

I hope this is helpful to you!

product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_headline: Great for my needs with a few exceptions...
review_body:
I have to give the Fitbit Charge HR a four star rating only because I have a couple issues with the device that don\x27t allow it to reach its full potential for my own personal goals but overall I\x27m loving it!

Lets start with the fit: I have very small wrists, just around five inches so I had no problem with it being too small as I\x27ve read others have. I wore it too tight on the first day and felt like the sensor was pushing into my skin and causing irritation so I loosened it up one notch and wear it a little further up my wrist to allow some wiggle room. By the third day I hardly noticed it on my wrist. I only take it off to shower or if I have an extra hard workout when I allow my wrist to dry out.

This device couldn\x27t get any more simple to use-- you turn it on, put it on and go. The side button allows you to display the time, steps walked, heart rate, calories burned and floors climbed. If you hold down the button it allows you to track specific activities like a run or walk. At the end of the activity you just hold down the button again and the activity/workout is synched to your phone.

For me, the main purpose of this watch was to determine how many calories I was burning during certain activities like yoga, barre class and other non-running/walking activities and to track my sleep patterns. The downside to this watch comes with its ability to accurately track such activities. I don\x27t feel like it accurately tracks calories unless you are running, walking or riding a bike. For instance, the barre class I take has the potential to burn 300-500 calories in a 55 minute period on average. The Fitbit has told me on 2 occasions that I burned a mediocre 140 calories. Its slightly frustrating but not a deal breaker. I do feel like it accurately tracks calories burned on the three runs I\x27ve been on while wearing the watch by comparing the results to a separate heart rate monitor and phone app.

The other aspect of the Fitbit that I am pleased about is the sleep tracker. I can confidently say that it accurately tracks my sleeping patterns. Several mornings I woke up feeling like I got a poor night\x27s sleep and sure enough I had been restless or awake nearly 20 times. You don\x27t push any buttons to go into sleep mode, it does it on its own.

The battery life on my Fitbit has been about 4 days on average. I\x27ve had no problems synching the watch to the Fitbit app, it always does so automatically through the Bluetooth.

Overall this is a very useful tool to motivate anyone that has very low activity levels or for someone who wants a greater challenge and is looking to step up their activity a notch. Its a great feeling to have your Fitbit buzz at you when you reach your 10,000 steps for the day!

product_title: QardioArm Wireless Blood Pressure Monitor: Compact & Portable Digital Upper Arm Cuff - Bluetooth Compatible for Apple & Android Devices, Arctic White
review_headline: Easy to configure, to use, to carry--really amazing.
review_body:
I was a little hesitant to get this because I\x27ve had trouble before getting unrelated devices to work together. This one, was a piece of cake. At this time, I am using it only with my i-pad but I plan to upgrade my phone (which is almost prehistoric) as soon as this contract expires and pair it with my new phone as well. I think that the best and most convenient \x27pairing\x27 would be phone and monitor because you may not want to lug an i-pad around everywhere.

On the i-pad (and I suppose the phone would be the same thing), all I had to do was go to i-tunes; download the free-app; open it; answer a few questions and create a user name; remove the hard cover from my i-pad (just in case) and touch the two devices together. At this point, I was expecting to have to go to settings and go through some convoluted process but, no--a message appeared that said Paired. How that happened, I don\x27t know!

I\x27ve been taking my blood pressure daily with it but waited to write the review until after I had a doctor\x27s appointment so that I could compare a reading taken by me at the doctor\x27s office using this device to a reading taken by the doctor right after. They were very close, my doctor was impressed, and I was reassured.

The unit is small, light, and comfortable to carry around in a purse (or even a big pocket) or to take on trips. The instructions provided are extensive and clearly written. The app is super easy to use and clear to read. It has options which I haven\x27t explored because they\x27re not relevant to my situation but, for example, if you want to know if the place you\x27re at affects your blood pressure, you can name it "office" or whatever. (It seems to me that, yes, your blood pressure is going to be higher at work than at home, but you may want to document that). You also have a space that appears after each reading for you to enter a note specific to that reading.

product_title: Vicks Nursery 1 Gallon Vaporizer with Night-Light
review_headline: VERY LOW RUN TIME was the deal breaker. Very good amount and consistent flow of steam though.
review_body: I\x27d like to clear a few things up here. I don\x27t write reviews often, but for this, I had to. PLEASE read this review:    If I could give this 3.5 stars, I would have. It creates a good amount of steam with a consistent flow, especially if you add some salt. I have this in a much larger room than what it is intended for, and there is a noticeable spike in temperature, which is the reason I opted for \x5C\x22warm mist\x5C\x22 instead of \x5C\x22cool mist.\x5C\x22. Regardless of its good performance, there is a huge drawback. There is no way in H*** this thing has a run time of 12-18 hours!!! Running this, without salt, and also filling the tank ABOVE the max fill line, I am lucky to get a solid 5 hours, maybe 6 if I\x27m lucky, and although the flow is very consistent, during the final hour, the steam output is cut in half! When I fill the tank to the actual fill line, I\x27ll see about 4 hours, maybe 4.5. Now I have absolutely no prior experience with humidifiers, but even I can assume that the advertised \x5C\x2212-18 hours\x5C\x22 is not correct, and I knew that going in. I, however, did expect a run time of at least 8 hours. I sleep 6.5 to 8 hours a night, and since it cannot stay on during that duration, I had to return it. Those of you boasting 18 or in excess of 18 hours of run time, I simply can\x27t believe you. Either you are running a different product (perhaps the 1.5G, which is the one in the picture), which I already know won\x27t even come close to 18 hours (I actually bought one and am running it now), or your mineral content is so extremely low and you are content with a very minuscule amount of steam.    The second issue. I noticed some people questioning if the actual unit is the round shaped unit in the picture. It is not. The round unit is the 1.5G model. If you look at the other pictures, they show the actual unit you will receive. It is a little smaller and more of a rounded/square design. The heating elements for both the 1.5G and this one (the 1G) are identical in that they are the same size andemit the same level of steam. They both have the same color nightlight, and each shine at the same intensity. HOWEVER, the 1.5G has 2 slots where you can insert VICKS medicated pads, in addition to the cup where essential oil can be added. The 1G DOES NOT have the 2 slots, it ONLY has the cup for the oil, which I hear is much more of a hassle than the pads.    All-in-all, I was very satisfied with the PERFORMANCE of this unit. Great steam (consistent, but only until the last hour of operation before it shuts off), even more with salt, and I had absolutely no issues of it \x5C\x22spitting\x5C\x22 or simply not producing steam (like others have stated). However, the run time is the deal breaker. I not only want to go to sleep and sleep through the night with heightened humidity and heat, I also want to wake up to it at 5:15am in the cold, dry morning! If it\x27s going to shut off 2 hours before I wake up, and cut the steam output in half and hour before that, then I feel I am missing half the benefit of a humidifier. Most, or all, of the humidity and heat are gone after two hours in the winter.    This review is, of course, my opinion. 4-6 hours may completely satisfy your needs, and some others, although I have no idea how, may actually be getting more than 6 hours. All I can give is my own experience, and I simply bought a machine advertised at 12-18 hours of run time, more than happy to accept less than that (maybe 8-9 hours), but received something that literally only runs at 25%-40% of that advertised run time. I will now conclude my incessant ranting and raving about this.    I WILL admit, in regard to value, at $14.99 with FREE shipping, you can\x27t beat that and it does deliver...for the price. I\x27ve seen people complaining about the same things with units that cost three and four times that price.    For added information, I have included a picture of both the 1.5G (left) and 1G (right) models, side-by-side, so they can easily be compared. The 1.5G is noticeable larger, but theyeach produce the same amount of steam. Given that, I\x27m hoping to get my coveted 8 hours of run time with the extra half gallon (it\x27s advertised at 18-24 hours, which I can already tell you is WAYYYY inaccurate). As soon as I know the run time of the 1.5G model, I will post.    UPDATE 1/23/15    Using the 1.5G and very happy with it. Started it at 10:00pm and it was still going at 5:30am (8 hours). I didn\x27t add any salt (didn\x27t need it), I had to fill the unit past the max fill line, and it was definitely outputting 50% less steam when I woke up, but I expect it was only doing that for an hour or so. All-in-all, it gets the job done.    I don\x27t know how long it would have kept going because I had to leave, but without adding salt, and not filling it past the max fill line, it\x27s safe to say you can expect at least 8 hours of run time.

product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_body:
I 90% love it, 10% dislike it. First off, the HR monitor is great. Seems to be very accurate and I love seeing what my hr sits at throughout the day and during workouts. Calorie count, awesome. Step count, great. Overall features and interface, love.

2 main complaints:

It pushes into my arm just enough to leave a small impression and I have a dull ache in my arm from wearing it. Now, I believe this will go away with time, and there are times I forget I\x27m even wearing it, but I really want a softer, lighter feel in the future.

2. I WISH this had a GPS feature! The Fitbit has almost everything I want, except GPS. I don\x27t want to have to use another device to track my run. This gives me an estimate of how far I\x27ve gone, but I want accuracy, and I want it all in one little package.

If they can give me more comfort and add in GPS, I will be a Fitbit lifer. For now, I\x27ll take it as is and I still love what it does, but I hope they can make these changes in the future.

review_body:
This product seems to work well if the goal is to stimulate your scalp. I am using it in conjunction with http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00CNTJHQO/.

I have thick coarse hair (Caucasian) and it penetrates pretty well. I notice a little less penetration at the very back of my head below the apex (because most of my hair is being brushed back there, including hair from the top/sides of my head), but I can still get to my scalp if I press a little harder and lean my head forward. I am using this in conjunction with http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00CNTJHQO/.

I have noticed a little bending at the edges of the tips, but this seems to reset in between uses. I could see them eventually wearing down or breaking, but I\x27ve used it for about two months of non-daily use and so far they show no sign of that. As with all brushes and long hair, it will help to work out the tangles at the bottom of your hair before going to your scalp. This will pull your hair less and put less strain on the bristles.

It varies whether I think the bristles are too hard or just right on my scalp, but the vast majority of the time it just feels perfect. If it seems too scratchy or not scratchy enough for you, I\x27d encourage you to try it multiple times (perhaps over a few weeks or a month) and also realize that you may need to vary the pressure over different parts of your head depending on your hairstyle.

product_title: Thompson Royal Jelly, Ultra Potency, 2000 Mg, 60  Capsules
review_body:
I shopped recently for royal jelly. I did not choose this one in the end, mainly because I don\x27t know as to whether I might have an allergy to bee stings of the honeybee kind, and I thought it might be better to start out at a lower dosage than most people might want, just to check on a possible allergic reaction. I plan to creep up the dosage gradually until I find the right level for me as an individual, assuming I don\x27t react to the bee product.

If I do keep using royal jelly and end up wanting a product with as much royal jelly as this one, I certainly wouldn\x27t eliminate this Thompson product from consideration, based on what little I know about them, which is basically nothing, the same amount of knowledge I have for many of the other royal jelly listings.

I\x27d like to use this review to correct the misinformation that the two previous reviewers left to downrate this product, and to maybe pull its ratings a little higher based on what I do know something about - the product\x27s label.

It\x27s unusual to find anyone confidant enough to post a review who doesn\x27t know how to read a label. I\x27ve been a heavy user and reader of Amazon\x27s user opinions of various supplements for many years now, though, and the only times I recall misinformation being posted were the few times when someone admitted being confused as to what the label said and used their review to ask for help while admitting what they were basing a so-so review on.

To put it mildly, the probability of seeing two reviewers giving a product the lowest possible rating based on an honest misreading of the label seems odd to me... like a probability of one in a million or so.

I have no connection to the Thompson supplement company, and it\x27s possible that if I ever fully checked them out totally thoroughly, I\x27d choose a different product for different reasons.

But I am a native English speaker, and I do know how to read a label. And if I never end up buying from this company, it certainly won\x27t be based on the previous two misleading reviews. The labels are posted online at Amazon, and available for anyone to read if you want to take the time to look for yourself; see the upper left of your opening window for this product and start clicking on all the pictures; you\x27ll see the entire bottle.

The Serving Size is listed as one capsule. The ingredients contents, listed as an equivalent to 2000 mg., means that one - only one - capsule (a serving size) must contain that specific equivalent amount, if the company\x27s label information is true.

As to the "Royal Jelly 3.5 X," that refers to the concentration of the freeze-dried product relative to a product that hasn\x27t been concentrated. That\x27s how the company can pack into a single capsule as much active ingredient of royal jelly as they claim.

Many other royal jellies at Amazon also use this same wording to explain their degree of concentration and the equivalency to a product that\x27s not concentrated at all. Thompson\x27s product has a slightly higher degree of concentration (3.5X) than the others I was looking at (3X) at Amazon. I didn\x27t see any postings by these fellows misleading customers as to the products of the others.

The idea proposed by the two previous reviewers (the only reviewers as of this writing) - that you are supposed to take a fourth capsule and split it in half to get to 2000 mg. equivalency might be accepted without thinking to a first-time supplement user, but it\x27s ridiculous on its face. The poor reviews only serve to influence customers who quickly scan for highly rated products and don\x27t even bother to open a webpage whose link shows 100% terrible reviews. I hope to change just a little that with this review. It seems the only decent thing to do.

I\x27m disappointed that Amazon is allowing these reviews to stand, just because the customers\x27 records show that they actually spent a small amount of money to purchase the product.

review_body: I use this for cleaning small engine carburetors in my repair shop.  You can use regular dish soap, like Dawn for example, but I went ahead and bought the 1 gallon of degreaser specifically for ultrasonic cleaners.  It works pretty good, however, it will not remove big chunks of dirt or grime.  For me it does a great job of cleaning out those small passages and orifices that I cannot get to with normal cleaning methods.  I typically pre-clean the part as much as possible and then put it in to finish it off.  The timer is preset to 3 minutes but I usually go for 15 minutes and set the temp to 35C.  If I had a complaint it would be on the temp not being in Fahrenheit and the depth of the reservoir.  The description of the reservoir is accurate, I just under estimated the size of my parts.  But, you can rotate the part in the reservoir until it is all done.  Any part of it submerged gets cleaned.  6-19-16  After a full plus year of use this thing is going strong.  I\x27ve learned to use the "Oil Eater AOD1G35437 Cleaner Degreaser" that I also get from Amazon.  What I\x27ve found is that heat is the key.  I still knock of the bulk of any dirt or grime first, just to help keep my cleaning solution lasting longer.  With the heat set about 45\xC2\xB0c to 55\xC2\xB0c and 15 minutes on the ultrasonic timer, the dirt and grime left comes right off with a brush.  I plan ahead and set my heat up on the machine 30 minutes or so before I use it.  Also, the heat has a timer built into it.  Not sure, but I think its set at about 30 minutes, then it shuts off by itself.  So, you have to keep an eye on it if it hasn\x27t gotten to temperature yet, you just have to touch the "on" button again.  I dilute the Degreaser at about 10 parts water to 1 part cleaner.  A gallon jug last me quite awhile.  It really all depends on how dirty/grimy your part is.    All in all, I couldn\x27t be more pleased.  It just took me a bit of time to dial in the settings for what I use it for.

review_headline: Love it. Definitely a game changer.. a must for women EVERYWHERE!
review_body:
After a friend and cousin raved about the Diva cup, I thought I would give it a whirl. I have a pretty regular cycle, however sometimes its kinda heavy and other months its quite light. So, trying to figure out which tampon I needed this month was a giant pain in my vagina. Literally, sometimes. I am 33 with no kids, I use the size 2.

The first time using it I was traveling, so I didn\x27t even get to practice with it in the comfort of my own home - but it didn\x27t matter. I figured if so many other people used them without issue, I could too. It took a few times to get use to inserting it and removing it, and sometimes it feels like you have to go in as deep as your elbow to remove it, as it can sit pretty high up. I mean, seriously once I thought it was lost up inside my body somewhere and I\x27d have to buy a new one because this one went MIA. Thankfully, there are a few tricks to removing it a bit easier, like squatting with your butt on your heels and letting gravity help, then you push (or bear down) like you\x27re doing a #2 to get your fingers around the base, then pinch and pull or give it a slight twist to release the suction. It should come out easily, and without pain. Just relax, because it really can\x27t get lost anywhere..

Once you find "your way" to insert it, it really takes no time at all. The first time I insert it at the start of my period, I run it under warm water to soften the silicone a bit. Otherwise, I do that when I remove and clean it - which for me is 2x a day, in the morning and then before bed. There have been times where I may not fully inserted it, so it felt uncomfortable until adjusted, which usually only happens if I am in a super mad rush. I can usually just push it up a bit and then I no longer even feel it.

The best part is that I can insert it the day I expected my period (since I\x27m quite regular) which means I am not longer caught off guard when it does start...and no more ruined underwear! I didn\x27t ever really experience bad cramps, but I do notice that even my mild cramps are even less with using the Diva Cup.

If you\x27ve been using Diva Cup and don\x27t like it, there are other brands out there with different sizes and shapes you can try. Some companies also donate menstrual cups to women in developing countries, with every purchased cup -- which I think is awesome.
Bottom line - It\x27s really a great product! If you\x27re not sure about it, seriously give it a try. It\x27ll make a huge difference in your life.\x27t ever really experience bad cramps, but I do notice that even my mild cramps are even less with using the Diva Cup.

The human body temperature tends to be close to 99F as a child and drops down closer to 98F as we get older (there is variability in this data). Also, when I contracted a nasty flu, I took ginseng 6 times daily and my symptoms hardly showed while I have noticed my body\x27s immune system working overtime. My flu completely disappeared in 10 days (the worst was over after 6 days).

Why Korean ginseng? In Asia, Korea is widely known to grow the best ginseng since the ancient days. Korea is a peninsula with lot of thick ocean mist traversing its mountainous terrain. Such conditions are considered ideal for ginseng.

review_headline: This should be a serious consideration for anyone purchasing a menstrual cup.
review_body:
I bought a Lunette size 2 sometime back and had it shipped to my brother for free when he was in the US. He brought it back for me, however, it went missing after 2 months. I was so devastated because it\x27s like a lifesaver compared to using pads. I almost wanted to purchase another Lunette but sellers on Amazon don\x27t ship internationally, or at least to my area. Other sites sell it at extravagant shipping costs (and the price of the cup is already at premium compared to the others). I thought, why not try other brands (and cheaper ones)? - Insertion and removal is easier with this cup than the Lunette. I think it is because the surface of this cup is very smooth.

- Best part is this: NO LEAKS. When I used Lunette (which I think was great anyway), I had to wear a pantyliner. To its credit, the leaks are minimal, but was spotting enough to have to wear a pantyliner. With Yuuki, I slept in all sorts of weird positions, and the next morning there were absolutely no stains at all. I emptied and cleaned it midday and at the end of the day, there was only tiny brown spot presumably due to process of emptying and putting it back. It really doesn\x27t leak in use - and I can get rid of using disposables altogether!

Conclusion: Yuuki is priced lower than Lunette, but no way inferior! If Lunette\x27s too expensive, just get a Yuuki.

review_headline: Really Works!  Teeth&Gums\x27 best friend.  Dentist was very impressed.
review_body:
I\x27m very happy with this Sonicare toothbrush. I had some tooth issues last year (molar extraction), and decided to try out a Sonicare toothbrush to curb any further issues as I\x27m getting older and my teeth are getting \x27long in the tooth\x27 (ha!). A co-worker mentioned the glorious check-up his Dentist gave him after he started using one, and I was sold.

My most recent dentist visit was my first checkup/cleaning in many years (beyond the aforementioned extraction and a few crown re-attachments). I told them about my past dental hygiene habits, and we both figured we were in for a 2-day long "deep-cleaning" and some very sore and bloody gums as a result.

Once I arrived for the check-up & cleaning, he and his hygienist were very impressed with my teeth and gums even though I don\x27t floss but once every few months (at most!), and I\x27m not fanatical about my dental hygiene by any measure. I credit this to the Sonicare and brushing twice a day with it. I had only been using the Sonicare for around 6 months at that time (preceded by a lifetime of marginal dental hygiene at best).

These things are powerful and can be a bit intimidating at first. When the plastic head hits your teeth, it seems like it will rattle your teeth right out of your gums! But you get used to that quick, and learn how to avoid the plastic brush-head from touching your teeth while brushing.

The 30-second quadrant timer is a nice feature I now rely on. I don\x27t really use the different "Modes" - I just use the standard mode and roll with it. Does the trick for me.

I like the 2-pack model as I keep one at home on the charger for at-home brushing, and the other stays in the carrying-case in my back-pack (take it to work everyday for after-lunch brushing). The neat carrying case can also hold a small tube of toothpaste if you slightly modify it (used a pair of wire-cutters to remove one of the two brush-head retaining clips - it now holds the Sonicare body, 1 brush head with cap, and a tube of toothpaste!). The one I keep in my backpack will go for 2+ weeks of once-a-day brushing with no problems (still has 2 battery lights on)! Then I swap the two bodies and heads when the battery gets a bit low. This prolongs battery life about as much as possible (reduces constant re-charge cycles as I rotate them in-and-out of the charger).

The UV Sterilizer built into the charger is a neat feature, but I can\x27t say I find myself using it all that often (maybe once a month). I figure if a standard toothbrush seems to do OK without UV Sterilization, then the Sonicare heads that I tend to replace bi-monthly should be OK.

The "Diamond Clean" heads have a wear indicator. I can get around 3 months from them, but generally replace them sooner (you can actually \x27feel\x27 a difference from a 1-month old head to a new one even though the wear indicator shows much life is left). Most brush heads are available on Amazon\x27s Subscribe and Save store (no brainer!).

This particular model does not have a pressure sensor, and that is about the only thing my dentist said might be an improvement for my dental hygiene needs (well that, and maybe flossing a bit more). I tend to be a bit aggressive when bushing, and the pressure sensor would likely be a good idea if you have similar aggressive brushing tendencies.

This was probably the best purchase under $200 I\x27ve made in the past 5 years. It\x27s not often that improving dental hygiene is this easy - but the Sonicare makes dental hygiene "cake"!
