product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_headline: If you believe the 1 star review, read this first!
review_body:
**** To the people who think this product is worthless ****

Straight to the point. Most of the 1 star review I see is the following:
1. In accurate heart rate reading
2. Do not work properly for certain kind of workout

However, these accusations are merely misconception toward the fitness tracking products. Any fitness tracking product is to provide relative progress over the day and relative heart rate monitoring. For those who wants the pin-point accuracy, they should get individual piece of equipment for different reading.

** The Good **
Here are the highlight of the fitness info I get from this band:

1. How long and how hard I\x27ve been active for the day:
Fitbit Charge HR is doing great job tracking my progress over the day. It is not that far off from what I\x27ve calculated with other source of information. One thing I really like is the ability to see how hard (heart rate) and how long I worked out. I can look at the log after a month to see if I\x27ve been staying active. The app also plots a curve of the resting heart rate, so that I can see if my cardiovascular condition is improving.

2. How long and how well I sleep
Remember, these information is relative, they are not pin-point accurate. There is simply no portable product can give all of those information like in the lab setting. Tracking my sleep is also a great feature. I tends to sleep a lot less than I should, so it is a good reminder to discipline my sleeping pattern (It is one of the requirement to stay strong and fit).

3. How much calories I\x27ve burned
I do not take this value seriously, because this should work with your diet. There is never a 100% accurate indication on how much intake vs how much burned. But overall, this is another number to summarize your workout progress for the day. If you believe the number 100%, your fitness plan most likely will fail, because a successful fitness plan do not work that way.

4. Price
With those feature and the price it offer, I can say this is a good deal. But if you are looking for a smart watch instead of a fitness tracker, get the Fitbit Surge or something else.

** bad (or not so good) **
Of course, Fitbit Charge HR is far from perfect (especially with people\x27s expectation). But here is the thing I found:
1. Design
I found that the design of the Fitbit Charge HR can get some attention. My wrist falls between S and L according to the sizing chart providing by Fitbit. When I put it on, the not flexible part seems a little bit too long and form a open space between my wrist and the band. Not that the band is sliding up and down my arm, but for people with smaller wrist, it may look funny.The flat bottom of the HR monitor also takes me a few days to get use to. It is not so comfortable for the first 2 days, but I got used to it later on.
I hope the next generation of fitbit HR can shorten the length of the non-flexible part and make it more curved so that the fit will be better.

2. Non-water proof
This really not an issue to myself, but I believe a lot of people in the water sport has to turn away from this band. I found no reason why the Surge is water proof while Charge HR is not. Unless the Surge R&D comes in a later time. Pretty sure losing customers who are into water sport is not Fitbit\x27s goal, just surprised that waterproofing was not something that Fitbit intended to do for all the bands.

3. The Fitbit App (good and bad)
Compare to MyFitness pal, Fitbit app is more fun to use. However, when Fitbit comes to log food, it becomes nightmares. I am so surprised that there is no generic categories for the food. Fitbit has to know not all food are from chain store, there are small business out there. I try to find the generic egg white omelette by weight, and it is not on the database. On the other hand, MyFitnessPal is doing much better narrowing down what I searched for. So this is one thing to keep in mind if you are looking for very strict diet plan.

** Conclusion **
I like Fitbit Charge HR overall. It meets or exceed my expectation mostly. I hope the band would be more flexible so that it wrap around my wrist better. The craftsmanship can use a little bit more attention to detail too, as there are a few rough edges here and there, but overall the band looks OK. I hope the next generation Fitbit will be more comfortable and tackle down all the negative points I\x27ve given. Given this is the first Fitbit band with HR monitor, Fitbit is doing pretty good.

product_title: Molly\x27s Suds Wool Dryer Balls (set of 3) - Natural Fabric Softener, Reduce Drying Time by 15-30%, Saves Money, Reusable, Unscented
review_body:
I\x27ve had wool dryer balls from Molly\x27s Suds for almost a year now and love them. I bought them mainly for economical reasons -- with a family of five, we go through so much laundry detergent and fabric softener. When I heard about wool dryer balls, I had to try them and was hooked immediately. My clothes dry noticeably faster and are just as soft as when I used fabric softener.

These dryer balls last 3 years and help laundry to dry faster, letting you run your dryer for shorter amounts of time. One thing to keep in mind is that the packaging for these balls says to use 6 of them for the best results. I only had 3 until recently and still found them to be very effective. I also love not having to buy fabric softener (I make my own laundry detergent now too, so our laundry cleaning bill is at a grand total of at most $40 a year).

Now that it\x27s winter, we have started to get more static with the clothes when they come out of the dryer. However, it doesn\x27t seem to last. By the time the clothes are folded and put away, then worn, the static is gone. I haven\x27t tried it yet, but I read that putting a wadded up ball of aluminum foil in the dryer will cut back on static. Or, a wash cloth with a few large safety pins can cut back the static. When the house is quiet, I can just barely hear the dryer balls bouncing around in the dryer. Our laundry room is in the basement, however, so if your dryer is on a main level of the house, it may be too loud.

I don\x27t plan to ever go back to fabric softener now that I\x27ve used wool dryer balls!

review_body: ADDENDUM TO PREVIOUS REVIEW: I was contacted by a rep regarding my review and they were EXTREMELY accomodating. They replaced the broken diffuser within days and emailed a free shipping label for the return. They were helpful, courteous and timely in their service. Since then, the new diffuser has worked fine! While this is not a big deal in the long run because I know which button to use, I would figure that the label would last longer than 3 weeks.  It is understandable that essential oils on the user\x27s hands could rub off the label which is why it should be embossed, not imprinted on the front of the unit.  If I had to recommend the unit for durability and warranty, I would give it a major \x27thumbs down.\x27  If the unit was still working, however, I would give it a big \x27high five\x27 because I liked the intermittent mist feature or the option for a constant mist.  When on intermittent mist, it would cycle for 20 sec on and off, allowing for a continuous aroma and the water in the 120 ml unit would last 8 hours through the night.  I also liked the cycling light feature, or the ability to select on color or the ability to turn off the lights completely.  For the money I spent on this Smiley Daisy Diffuser, I am not smiling! product_title: Lysol Disinfecting Wipes, Ocean Fresh, 160ct (2X80ct)
review_headline: Nice wipes; one sheet cleans a large surface area.
review_body:
I bought a ton of these wipes when I was going into a friend\x27s house to help him clean up after a fire. I used these to remove soot and even mildew from his belongings, and they worked well. The "ocean fresh" scent isn\x27t really that noticeable; however, these don\x27t smell strongly antiseptic (as some disinfecting wipes do), which was a relief since I used so many of them.

These are very wet and they do kind of leave a bubbly residue if you use them to clean very small sections of something. One sheet will clean a surprisingly large surface area. I ordered four of these tubs, and we only needed two tubs in total to wipe down over a hundred DVD cases, the surface area of a bed frame, a coffee table, a TV stand, a futon, four chairs, an armoire, multiple bookshelves, and any number of other items in my friend\x27s apartment. review_headline: Will help you know your true family.
review_body:
I was terrified. My 17 year old is attending Caltech and knows physics and genetics and biology. He didn\x27t know what his blood type is.

And he wanted to.

His dad and I know our blood types, me especially as a cancer patient. So we gave him this for Christmas, and I began to get nervous. What if some anomaly shows, meaning I wasn\x27t his mother?

I mean, that kid looks like his Dad. Same height, same build, same tendency to talk about directions or interesting license plates they see that day. (Caltech remember, he\x27ll make 90k out of school). But what of me in this boy? His eyes are blue, mine are brown. His hair light, mine dark. I\x27m crazy, he\x27s calm. I\x27m sarcastic and he\x27s intellectual. Where I am in there? I started to worry. Maybe he\x27s not my kid. Maybe I\x27ve been doing chemo after chemo to see him walk during his high school graduation, and he wasn\x27t mine after all. Maybe I tortured myself to stay alive to see some stranger\x27s kid walk!

Now I know where I\x27ve been, and it\x27s been at home, which means they would have switched him at birth in the hospital. Maybe my real son was out lost, wondering, looking for me, his mom, to also pay for his 40,000 a year college education.

Still, my soon to be ex-son wanted to know and its not time to be a coward. We set it all up. We read the directions three times, and got ready: I had to puncture his finger. Those same fingers that I\x27d use to kiss and put a band aid on before, I now have to stab and make blood appear. I pricked and he spread the blood in the proper areas.

The results came clear.

As usual, he got an A+. This means I am his official mother, as I\x27m A- Whew! Thanks Elgen, for saving the day.

product_title: Herbalife F1 Cookies and Cream Shake Mix, 26.4 ounces
review_headline: Don\x27t expect it taste like ice cream!
review_body:
If you\x27ve never had a protein shake or weight loss replacement before - first you need to understand what these things taste like. You\x27re not going to get something that tastes like ice cream or a candy bar. You are mixing 2 scoops of the shake mix with either milk (recommended) or water. Generally you shake it up in a blender ball cup, and drink it right away. If you do it this way - generally all these shake brands and flavors have the same texture. It\x27s always a little grainy no matter how much you shake that blender ball, and the more you shake it the more air and bubbles get added (and the warmer the milk gets).

We ordered cookies and cream because with other brands we always got vanilla, or berry - and this sounded good for a change. It\x27s not just cookies and cream flavor, in the mix are actual little tiny cookie bits. This is good and bad. It\x27s good in the shake mix because it\x27s something different, but it\x27s bad because (with milk) you just can\x27t ever get it all blended in the shaker cup no matter what you do. Also when you drink it, it tastes like your kids dunked a whole box of oreos in a cup of milk - and then you were forced to drink it.

The thing about these shakes is - some are great with water or milk, and others are better suited by making a smoothie with ice. From now on we\x27re going to make this shake mix with a cup and a half of ice and 8oz milk - at least then it WILL taste like ice cream!

review_headline: On the right track until side effects kicked in
review_body: After decades of full-tilt battle with my sinus allergies (countless prescriptions, natural remedies, and OTC formulas), I decided to give this one a try. I have no doubt that this product is very effective for many folks here, but if I\x27ve learned one thing about allergy meds, it\x27s this: nothing works for everyone, especially when something as strong as steroids are in play. If you\x27re not prone to medicinal side effects, then Nasacort\x27s certainly worth a try. Meanwhile, my recent switch to the lesser-known Nasalcrom, a steroid-free spray also now OTC, has given me some of the best relief I can remember and without side effects of any kind--so far. We\x27ll see how the long-term goes.    Good luck in your search, fellow sufferers. I wish there were one solution for us all.    Allergy relief after a week: 4  Side effects after a few days: 2  _____________  TOTAL: 3 stars

review_body: I tried these to combat my husband\x27s snoring--before I got pregnant, I just used the cheaper foam bullet kind and they were enough, but pregnancy\x27s turned me into a very light (and irritable) sleeper, so I wanted something that would block out the most noise possible. That brings me to the pros and cons of these earplugs.    Pro #1, they definitely block out more noise than the foam kind, though not all. #2, they\x27re pretty easy to put in.    Con #1, I found them distracting to have in. The material itself feels odd, warm and waxy, and when I sleep on my side, the molded shape sometimes presses uncomfortably into the folds and ridges of my ear. #2, unless you have a crew cut, hairs get stuck on them. #3, they\x27re high-maintenance--they only last a week, tops, and you can\x27t just pop them in and out like the cheapie kind--you have to clean your ear out before and after, and be careful not to handle the plugs with dirty hands, or they\x27ll lose their stickiness.    On the whole, these do win on the noise-reduction front, but they\x27re just too fussy for me, as a nightly earplug user. Lots of people love them, though, so I would advise you to buy a cheaper two-pair pack and give them a shot.

The third week we actually had a dry night and gradually we began seeing progress.  After a month in to the program, we went on vacation. My son, however, is a very sound sleeper and nothing wakes him up except, now, the urge to urinate. My son is a healthy, CONFIDENT, teenager.  THANK YOU, Dr. Sagie!

product_title: Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker
review_body: Gives me the motivation I need to get moving- I am amazed by the difference I can see in my activity during the week vs. weekends, and this helps encourage me to get moving on the weekends. Using this to help me not only get more active but also using the app to help with weight loss. The only downside is the included wristband for tracking sleep- I can\x27t stand to wear anything on my wrist at night. Instead, I\x27ve found that it\x27s still reasonably accurate when clipped to the collar of the v-neck shirt I wear to bed. I can generally get the battery to last over a week but tend to charge it once a week when watching a movie- no worries about missing steps then!  Edit: So, it\x27s been less than four months. While I still love the Fitbit One, I am not impressed by the included clip. About two months ago, the little plastic tab on the back of the clip broke off, although I was able to glue it back in place. Today, the little plastic clip cover completely disappeared, leaving 2 exposed metal prongs sticking out of the clip that are constantly poking into my skin, even through clothing. product_title: Nature Babycare Eco-Sensitive Wipes
review_headline: Not quite as good as Huggies
review_body:
My children are 18 and 12, so it\x27s been a while since I\x27ve had to change a diaper, but I\x27ve never stopped buying them. They\x27re a staple in our house. I keep a box in the kitchen for wiping down surfaces and general cleaning. They\x27re very convenient, and the ones I buy--Huggies fragrance-free refills--are cheaper than, for example, Lysol disinfecting wipes (though of course the baby wipes don\x27t claim to disinfect; I\x27m okay with that).

These Nature Babycare wipes, then, are competing with the Huggies wipes I usually buy. The caveat, of course, is that I don\x27t use them on babies, but I\x27m not sure that I\x27d have a different assessment of them if I were. After using these wipes now for a couple weeks, here\x27s what I found:

1. They are a bit smaller than the Huggies wipes and also a bit thinner.

2. They are stronger than the Huggies wipes. You can pull on them rather hard, either horizontally or vertically, and it takes a lot to break them. The Huggies wipes break very easily.

3. They do not seem to be as moist as the Huggies wipes. You\x27ll probably find yourself adding water to them frequently to get them as moist as you\x27d like.

4. Judging from Amazon\x27s prices, the Nature Babycare wipes are more than two times as expensive as the Huggies refills I buy.

My conclusion:

The dimensions of the wipes may not matter very much, so I discount the first point above. Perhaps surprisingly, I\x27ll also discount the second point: I\x27m not sure that the strength of the Nature Babycare wipe is an asset. The Huggies wipes are strong enough for the purpose. But points three and four above do matter, a lot. The Nature Babycare wipes are simply not as convenient as the Huggies because of the moistness issue, and I see no reason to pay more than twice as much for a wipe that doesn\x27t provide any particular advantage.

I gave the Nature Babycare wipes four stars because they do the job they\x27re meant to do for the most part: they\x27re not bad, they\x27re just not quite as good, and not as inexpensive, as the competitor\x27s product.

Update 4/17/2015: After using these for a lot longer I\x27ve downgraded my assessment by one star. Point three above, the moistness issue, is even more important than I had originally thought. It\x27s simply not convenient to use these, and I\x27m actually looking forward to being rid of them and being able to buy my old brand again.most part: they\x27re not bad, they\x27re just not quite as good, and not as inexpensive, as the competitor\x27s product.

review_headline: Great Water Pik but doomed by hard tap water? 2015 version is better!
review_body:
Update: Just got replacement Pik and it\x27s an updated 2015 version.

1) water is filled from bottom instead of top. In my old Pik I found rust-like spots inside top of Pik. Maybe bottom fill will prevent?
2) Old tips work
3) there is a rubber plug for the charger intake. I assume to keep water out of internals.
4) charger output is different. The new charger output is 5.0V 600mA. The old is 3.5V 0.5A (which is 500mA), so I\x27ll discard old charger.

The new Pik is stronger. The water supply is used up faster.

Original review:

I really like this water Pik but only 4-stars because it broke after one year (almost to the day!). That works out to ten cents a day since Pik costs $40. I just ordered another one. My review is to pass on what I learned from dis-assembling.

1) device is well made; internals were held together by tiny screws (I think stainless steel)
2) there is rust-like brown gunk inside
3) the batteries are AA 1.2v 1500mAH (when I tested battery after recharging, it measured 1.5v, so 1.2v maybe a typo)
4) there is a little electric motor that powers a plastic pump and pump was covered with brown gunk
5) Note: the two AA batteries are wired together with solder, so replacement is difficult

Water pressure was weak during last week of use, so I recharged. That is when Pik stopped working. Since batteries were charged and I doubt that wiring had broken, I assume internal pump failure. Since pump is partially covered by brown gunk, I will assume electric motor \x5C\x22burned out\x5C\x22 because it had to work too hard to overcome the gunk in the pump. And hard tap water is cause. I\x27ll use filtered or distilled water with next Pik.

review_headline: the dew drop is a better more reliable model
review_body:
I\x27ve been happy with my froggy I\x27ve been using it for 2 years now with distilled water and it does seem that it\x27s now dying the motor makes a loud growling noise when you first turn it on now and it\x27s getting a bit flakey in that some times the red light is on in the morning but there\x27s still water in the tank. I take the character face off, wipe it and then wipe off the top of the water container before trying to lift it out. By having a towel handy I haven\x27t had any problems. I\x27ve never had water leak from the water basin.

I prefer the adorable over the dew drop because I found the dew drop to be slightly louder and I didn\x27t like how the light in the dew drop one lit up the water and created a lot of light so we use that one in the living room.

Aside from thinking it shouldn\x27t have died already I will replace froggy with another I am overall very happy with the products.

product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_headline: Works great until you try to get your heart rate over 130bpm
review_body:
I held out on buying a fitbit product as I wanted to be able to monitor my heart rate. So when I saw the Charge HR I got really excited. I have been using a $50 hr monitor that I bought a few years ago at Walmart, along with its chest strap. The hr monitor worked fine, sometimes it was a little slow in getting readings until you warmed up. It was very accurate when using the chest strap, it matched my perceived exertion and pulses counted manually while touching my wrist. This was especially true when doing HIIT exercises such as P90X or Focus T25 (insanity jr).

I give this information to contrast it to the charge HR. The Charge HR fails MISERABLY when doing any kind of high intensity exercise where your heart rate is spiking/fluctuating very quickly.

I wore my chest strap and old hr monitor along with the Charge HR while doing a tabata exercise yesterday. While my chest strap monitor was reading a heart rate of 170 - 180, the charge HR never got above 130. Whaaaaat?! During a lot of the workout, the charge HR would just show two lines where the heart rate would usually be on the display, showing that it could not get an accurate hr reading. I\x27ve tried all the suggestions shown on the fitbit help website, such as not wearing the strap too tight, moving it up farther along the arm, stopping for 10 seconds or so to get a reading etc.

Nothing worked. I could never get the Fitbit to read accurately. Their heart rate monitor FAQ shows some different zones for workouts, and I\x27ve never actually seen my charge hr read a peak zone measurement. I\x27m starting to question if it even can.

Maybe they will release an update that can make this more accurate. I realize that a chest strap will probably always be more accurate due to its relative location to the heart, but fitbit has advertised this product as being able to replace all the older products that we\x27ve been using to track hr during any kind of exercise. Nobody likes wearing the chest straps.

Now, for the positives. It does great at reading my step count, flights climbed count, all day HR reading when I\x27m basically at rest or doing light activities, and sleep. The battery life is great. The band is comfortable once you get used to having something on your wrist for most of the time. The interface is intuitive and easy to use, the double tap custom feature is nice.

This product could be a 10/5 stars if the HR monitor actually worked with all exercises. Fitbit really would have a stellar product that would make me and others be a lifetime customer. But until they take care of this glaring problem with one of their new top of the line health products, the Charge HR will just be another mediocre hr monitor that distracts the user with lots of information and a snazzy app, but fails to deliver the real goods in the form of accurate hr readings.hest straps.

product_title: Stander Mobility Adult Home Bed Rail - Elderly Support Bed Handle + Swing-Out Mobility Arm & Adustable Legs Floor Support & Pouch
review_body:
After major spinal surgery I needed a bedrail simply to turn or get into or out of bed. While my need for it has markedly decreased, I left it up purely for convenience\x27s sake.

I don\x27t know if this Stander model was available at the time, but I surely would have chosen it, had I been aware of it.

The movable arm is a tremendous help to anyone who needs just a little bit more to manage getting in and out of bed independently. And let me tell you from experience, the ability to do things by yourself is a tremendous morale booster when you are recovering or just coping.

The product is well made, assembles easily and easy to use. The storage pockets may please some, but not all. I find them handy for holding a small tablet, eyeglasses and remote controls. Be sure that the legs are extended to the right length: you don\x27t want any gap between the end of the legs and the floor.

I had no need to contact customer support: the provided instruction sheet was more than adequate.

If you or a relative needs to consider adding a bedrail, I would strongly urge you so seriously consider the Standard Mobility Bed Rail. Also, they have a model with a folding table that looks interesting as well. Overall, I think Stander should be a first-tier resource for any mobility assistance needs. They have a very interesting and very useful product line.

Jerry

product_title: Fitbit Surge Fitness Superwatch
review_headline: I like the Surge, kind of (updated)
review_body: I have been looking forward to the Surge for months (like many other people). I was quite pleased when it finally got to me. I have had it for around 1 week.  Pros: feels great on my wrist, no issues there. Great watch face, easy to read. Navigation was unique, but I did get it and now I love it. Silent alarm is amazing, I use it every day now. When just walking around the heart-rate monitor seems to do great, and the only issue I had with it tracking my HR was when I was lifting weights. The GPS tracking on the watch is quite accurate. When I had an issue and the support finally responded, they were great and willing to fix my issues. Also, the app that connects to my phone is quite nice.  Cons: I emailed support and it took 2 days for them to get back to me. I know they are busy, but (as a support person) the average time it takes me to get back on a case is close to 2 hours. Huge difference. The Surge is said to last 5 days on a charge, but if you actually use it (E.g. workouts, notifications, tracking, classic Bluetooth controls) it lasts closer to 2 days. I\x27m not very bothered by this, as I have grown to accept that the battery life times of almost everything I have is "estimated" to be much greater then I will actually get. Also the watch face is scratched already which is a disappointment, I expected them to design the materials to withstand more abuse. I have uploaded a picture so you can see the scratches on the top edges of the watch.  Overall: I am happy with the watch, I just wish they spent more time on the materials chosen for the watch. It works great for running, which is its intended use, but has trouble with weight exercise. I would most likely buy this watch again. I will re-review this product at the end of a month with an update of my thoughts about it.  Update**  I have had the watch for over 2 years now and have a couple changes with my view of the watch. I got the watch replaced by Fitbit when the watch band broke (after a year). I had to pay for the shipping, which was less then desirable. I got the new watch and was happy again, for a bit. As time goes on, it find it unusable for anything but running. The bike tracking was terrible, and tracking while lifting was useless. I dropped it off my couch and onto concrete a couple days ago, screen cracked instantly. Wish they put more money into the screen material. I also found that it did not fit under my dress shirts when I wore my suit. The profile it too large. As such, it no longer is on my wrist. I keep it in the drawer, only to come out when I start running again (after the winter).  Overall, this is a underwhelming product. I feel they missed their target, again. sub-par materials result in sub-par product. Maybe the next product line the release will be better.I can only hope. I really want to like the product. One thing it for sure, I will not be per-ordering the next watch.

product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_body:
I had a Fitbit One and I was always forgetting to recharge it, or put it on for sleep, or activate it for sleep, or SOMETHING. I heard about the new Charge and upon read the other reviews and some of the comparisons, I was excited. I have really small wrists, but was right on the cusp between small and large. The Fitbit website says in that instance, GO BIIGGER! They\x27re right. :-) Bought the Large. I have found my Charge HR to be accurate, and being able to see the steps motivates me to move more. As my boyfriend said once when I told him "We can\x27t go to the grocery store, I have to go back to the house and get my Fitbit! (I had the One)," "You took the steps whether they are counted or not." I find that as someone who sits on the computer, moves my hand flipping pages of things I\x27m dictating, working my grad school retail job, my steps are fairly accurate. When it\x27s not as high as I want (625 on a lazy Sunday, YEESH!), I know I need to get out and move more.

Pros:
- I can see everything on my wrist - the One was hidden in my pocket, so all the nifty flowers, etc, I could never see. This also means it serves as a watch. :-)
- It tells me who\x27 s calling. If you connect it to your phone via bluetooth (which is what allows for syncing to the app), it will tell you who\x27s calling if the phones within range. It takes a second for it to buzz (I can hear the phone first), but I\x27ve already found this handy. No, you can\x27t answer the call, it\x27s just a notification.
- It automatically knows when I\x27m asleep. I\x27m trying to get sleep data and figure out sleep patterns, so this is helpful
- I can set it to default to whatever screen I want (this can be done at the fitbit website, in the devices screen)
- Splash proof. I\x27ve worn it doing dishes, and the websites states that you CAN technically wear it in the shower, but that they recommend you not in order to prevent anything from getting under the band and held against your skin. Because of the way the tracker sits against my wrist, it is nice to give it a little break (I\x27m actually going to set up a "charging station" in my bathroom so that I charge it while I shower, solving two problems at once).

Cons:
- It was a pain to figure out where the manual was. I only found an online manual, and it was a link posted in a forum I found after 5 minutes of searching. Perhaps some of the setup (like how to change what it defaults to) was intuitive for other people, but it didn\x27t occur to me that I would have to log in to the website and do it through there. If the set up software told me I would, I missed it when I turned to scold the cat. I found my One to be more intuitive to set up.

Overall: I love this tracker, I sprung for the HR model so that when I\x27m working out I can see my heart rate. I had the One, and I kept it so that when they add the ability to have multiple devices to one Fitbit account, if I\x27m going somewhere nice/fancy, I can use my One clipped to my bra instead of my Charge HR. The One is nice, and I like it. It\x27s great for people who don\x27t want something on their wrist, and don\x27t want/need to be able to see the data. I\x27m forgetful, and I needed something more in my face. Had the Charge been available last summer, I probably would have bought that. (it combines the things I wanted in the Flexx - being on the wrist, letting you see things - with the more numerous things I loved about the One - like counting all the stairs up to my apartment, ha). I also bought the Fitbit Aria scale, and thing that the Charge and Aria make a great combination.

And for anyone with questions about the step counting, here\x27s what the Fitbit website says:
"Fitbit trackers use a 3-axis accelerometer to understand your motions. An accelerometer is a device that turns movement (acceleration) of a body into digital measurements (data) when attached to the body. By analyzing acceleration data, our trackers provide detailed information about frequency, duration, intensity, and patterns of movement to determine your steps taken, distance traveled, calories burned, and sleep quality. The 3-axis implementation allows the accelerometer to measure your motion in any way that you move, making its activity measurements more precise than older, single-axis pedometers.
Fitbit trackers have a finely tuned algorithm for step counting. The algorithm is designed to look for motion patterns most indicative of people walking. One condition for a motion pattern to be recognized as a step is the motion must be large enough. The algorithm implements this by setting a threshold. If a motion and its subsequent acceleration measurement data meet the threshold, the motion will be counted as a step. If that threshold is not met, the algorithm won\xE2\x80\x99t count the motion as a step. Other factors can create enough acceleration to meet our threshold and therefore cause some over counting of steps, such as riding on a bumpy road. Equally, it\x27s possible for the algorithm to undercount (not meet the required acceleration threshold). Examples here include walking on a very soft surface such as a plush carpet."

So, I was huffing and puffing with my heart almost exploding out of my chest after 40 minutes of intense workout. I turn the Fibtit Charge HR on to see what my pulse was, and it shows "--". Okay, maybe I wore it the wrong way; I check tips on how to properly wear it.

I have a long way to go to get fit; I had never owned a device of this kind and was highly excited for the Charge HR, thinking all other activity trackers are nothing but fashion items and glorified pedometers. Finally a device that does continuous HR monitoring and compatible with my Windows Phone! In a sense, I considered a great motivation to keep going in my fight against belly flabber.

Alas... I am highly disappointed. Not only in the Charge HR but after looking at other, non-strap devices, which none seems to successfully monitor heart rate.

product_title: Weight Gurus Digital Body Fat Scale with Large Backlit LCD and Smartphone Tracking
review_body:
Picked up this scale to replace my aging, inaccurate, piece of junk $10 scale I got from a department store. So far after daily use for 3-4 weeks I can happily say this was worth every penny! It\x27s very accurate (I received consistent ratings over short periods of time) and is nice and large, yet sleek and low profile at the same time, with a nice big, backlit readout. The scale has some other nice little touches, like multi-user support. It automatically differentiates between my girlfriend and I (awesome), but there\x27s a 40 pound difference between us. For people closer in weight we had to manually select users ourselves, which is a little annoying, but no big deal.

There are two big features that attracted me to this particular product: the smartphone tracking and the additional metrics it measured (water weight, bodyfat, bone mass, and muscle mass).

Smartphone Tracking - A little awkward, but good. I incorrectly assumed that wireless meant bluetooth, but this scale actually uses a bar code system to sync with your phone. It measures you, gathers data, and spits out a code for you to hold your phone up to scan with its camera. Like I said, it\x27s a little awkward. However, it works great! It almost always read the barcode instantly and accurately logs my data. Aside from that, the logging is invaluable to me. In the time I\x27ve had this scale I\x27ve lost about 5 pounds, and seeing hard data presented in a nice little graph showing a downward trend in weight is definitely a nice little motivator to keep up with the diet/exercise regime.

Additional Metrics - Take it with a grain of salt. There have been many studies and reports run by professional companies that attempt to credit these types of devices, but many of them have found that absolutely no simple bathroom scale accurately measured factors like BMI. However, it is useful in the sense that you can use this information to gauge progress against itself. It\x27ll paint a very broad picture, but if you want accuracy, seek a professional.

review_body: I am pretty sure this stuff "works", but I would suggest caution if you have co-morbid conditions or are taking medications.  I am bipolar and have struggled with constipation dominant irritable bowel for most of my adult life.  The medications I take for depression/mood stabilizing can sometimes exacerbate the constipation and it has frequently been suggested that I take a probiotic.  I\x27ve tried a few with negligible results so figured I\x27d try something marketed as more powerful.  I started taking this and within a few days, I started having severe stomach pain, nausea, malaise and return of depressive symptoms that feel an awful lot like withdrawal from the antidepressant.  I stopped for a few days and things got better but, since I fancy myself an amateur practitioner/scientist (ha!) and found it kind of hard to believe something so benign could be doing this to me, I tried the experiment of starting again and immediately experienced the return of symptoms. I am not sure if it somehow interferes with the absorption of medication in the gut or exactly the mechanism of this response (there is some medical literature to support the idea that some people have an unbalanced immune response triggered by probiotics- quite complex if you are interested), but I suggest checking with a doctor before adding this to an existing medication regimen.

review_body: This stuff makes my stomach seriously upset almost immediately after taking it.  It doesn\x27t matter if I take it with food or without, shortly thereafter I experience something like harsh abdominal pains .  Now I\x27ve taken myriad different herbs over the past few years, reading about amazing benefits here and there and giving it a shot, and looked at this as a general tonic rather than a treatment for any specific symptom \xE2\x80\x94 this is the ONLY herbal medicine I have ever experienced adverse effects like this. I have seen it listed as a potential side effect in some places, granted, but it doesn\x27t appear to be common or one that people typically experience with it.  I am going to sample another variety of red sage (salvia) to see if it\x27s the actual constituents or the form/quality that is causing my adverse reaction, if I get the same result obviously it\x27s unfair to criticize this brand only.  I don\x27t feel one should leave a negative review on the basis that it doesn\x27t suit them specifically, our bodies are complex organisms and what works for others may not be the case for you.  However, this review is currently based on the suspicion this is a harsher, less benign, form of salvia.  I expect to find a more suitable variety out there that doesn\x27t punish my gut, if not, I will be clearing this review.

product_title: Sidekick - Deadline (A Virgil Flowers Novel, Book 8) by John Sandford
review_headline: Insightful synopsis of Deadline; good if you want to reflect on Sandford\xE2\x80\x99s newest novel. Worth $5? Questionable.
review_body:
Ever finish a really great book and wish you had someone to talk to about it? Here\xE2\x80\x99s Dave Eagle to lend some perspective. In this Sidekick Eagle writes to the reader rather than at him, as if he\xE2\x80\x99s having a conversation with you, discussing the book over a cup of coffee. He doesn\xE2\x80\x99t just robotically tell you what happened in the novel, but rather gives some insight into the events and makes you think. It\xE2\x80\x99s written in a way that doesn\xE2\x80\x99t spoil the novel for someone who may not have read it, but rather makes it more intriguing.

In the \xE2\x80\x9CThemes and Symbols\xE2\x80\x9D section, Eagle makes some good connections that may have been overlooked by the not-quite-astute reader. The \xE2\x80\x9CCharacter Analysis\xE2\x80\x9D section is perceptive, but I would have liked to see more on the subject. What about Virgil\xE2\x80\x99s relationship with other characters in the book? I would also liked to have seen more connections to other books in the Virgil Flowers series (for example how Virgil wasn\xE2\x80\x99t always such a one-woman-man).

That said, this Sidekick can be taken on two hands: On the one hand, if you absolutely loved Deadline and were sad to see it end, then this Sidekick is a great way to lend some food for thought and some closure. On the other hand, you have to ask yourself if you are the kind of person who will pay $5 to read a synopsis- albeit insightful- of a novel you just read and tell you things you probably already know.

review_headline: Surprisingly funny and endearing even if the romance was a bit lacking.
review_body:
Thank goodness I read this during the weekend. What was to be a chapter or two of light reading turned into my finishing this book at 4 in the morning. I did make a few judgments before getting into it and was really expecting some clique romance novel about some woman who\x27s life is magically transformed by some well endowed billionaire who\x27s rich, famous and great in bed. This story is thankfully not that.

Jennifer is a surprisingly intelligent woman who like many fresh out of college looking to make her mark in the real world and coming up short. Her story is something that just about everyone starting out can relate to. What happens next is a whirlwind of opportunity but grounded in reality. I liked that Jennifer had integrity and the common sense to leave a bad situation when things got uncomfortable with Alex. That was the turning point for me in this novel when I just couldn\x27t stop reading.

As for the romance it was slow building and I didn\x27t even mind the lack of sex. Actually I think I enjoyed it more without it. Strange as it may be I liked the tension and the building up to it. But more than that I liked that it wasn\x27t just about the inevitable love story of two people that we all knew was coming. I was enthralled and entertained by Ms. Blackwell\x27s character which came as an utter surprise because she was just a complete you know what at the beginning of the story. I imagine her as some Judi Dench type of sophisticated woman. I didn\x27t even care about the mysterious billionaire love interest because darn it the side characters were just such a joy to read about. I wouldn\x27t mind reading a side novel from just Blackwell\x27s point of view. Jennifer and Alex might be the face of the story but Blackwell she becomes the heart and soul of it. The story just lends itself to such witty humor and captivating characters the romance part was secondary to me.

product_title: NANOVISION: What Would You Do With X-ray Vision?
review_body:
Posted first to Blog Critics as Book Review: \x27Nanovision,\x27 A Technological Thriller by Paul T. Harry.

In Nanovision by Paul T. Harry, we are introduced to the subject of nanotechnology or nanomedicine, the medical application of that technology.

A devastating murder and betrayal leaves one person dead and a young teen without both his father and vision due to the fire used to cover up that murder. Daniel wakes up in the hospital with no vision and no memories. He doesn\xE2\x80\x99t remember his life before his pain and has nowhere to go.

Yet upon further search, an aunt that has cut off ties long in the past is located. She is involved in the field of Nanomedicine and works in research. Not sure she is capable of taking on such a tragic young man, she nevertheless does her best. Ethyl Santini is raising her granddaughter and leads a very busy life of research in a nanolab where she is at work on regeneration. The testing of animals has proved to be extremely workable, and she has been able to save many that would not have lived otherwise.

In her heart she knows that she must help Daniel, and while she had not been aware she had a nephew, she is up to the challenge. Armed with her granddaughter\xE2\x80\x99s approval she brings him into her family. Aware that while to the outside world he has been declared dead, there are concerns that he may still not be safe.

The fit is perfect and Ethyl is thrilled to find Daniel so likable and as he bonds with her younger charge life seems to be just right. Yet now her lab is in trouble and she is uneasy about her own research. Knowing she could be ousted at any time, she does the unimaginable. She puts together a new formula for her own nephew. With his agreement, they begin a series of doses to see if nanotechnology can help his eyesight. None of them are prepared for the changes.

As Daniel\xE2\x80\x99s regeneration begins, his memory resurfaces, as well as anger at the death of his father and the assault on himself. Heading back to his home he is after the very man who changed his life. Judy, The FBI special investigator that followed the crime and found his aunt is notified and she begins the hunt to find him, for she knows more about this crime then he understands. Can she locate him before he finds those responsible? She is very aware that if he comes upon them first, he will not survive for they have been in the business of death for a long time. With his sudden disappearance, can she find him before it is too late?

Harry has given us characters that are interesting and likable. His use of technology is an interesting foil and creates a plausible storyline. The action and undertakings seem very real and are much like some of the crimes we see reported in the news, yet he takes us on a rocky journey of home and nanomedicine.

His interpretation of the reactions as Daniel\xE2\x80\x99s blindness recedes is amazing and the action and interplay is sharp. You find the possibilities for exciting and strange. He has given us an intriguing thriller full of danger and excitement, and threaded it with the possibility of medical miracles.

product_title: His End Game (MMG Series Book 1)
review_body:
This is the impressive debut novel from RB Hilliard. Ms. Hilliard has a natural storyteller\xE2\x80\x99s gift, and she\xE2\x80\x99s able to capture her characters\xE2\x80\x99 emotions getting them on to the page in such a way that the reader cannot help but feel as well. Ms. Hilliard has given her readers a highly emotional story about young lovers, gut-wrenchingly torn apart, and their painful journey back to each other.

Ellison Davis, the product of a high school hook up, was unwanted from birth. Left by young parents who didn\xE2\x80\x99t want or acknowledge her, Ellie was raised by her father\xE2\x80\x99s sister. She first lays eyes on Max McLellan on the first day of her freshman year, but she knows immediately he is way out of her league. She loses her childhood best friend, Piper, when she is shipped off to boarding school before their sophomore year leaving Ellie very much alone. That summer, she meets and befriends, Joss.

Max McLellan is much older than his years. He may be in high school but in his short life, he has been dealt a tough hand that has forced him to mature quickly and step up for not only himself, but also his 12-year-old sister, Sarah. His father is a mean drunk who uses their home basically as a crash pad, leaving Max and Sarah to their own devices. Max has had his eye on Ellie for years, but he knows he\xE2\x80\x99s too angry, and she isn\xE2\x80\x99t ready for him. He bides his time with other \xE2\x80\x9Cdistractions\xE2\x80\x9D waiting for Ellie to mature.

\xE2\x80\x9DLife couldn\xE2\x80\x99t get any better than this.\xE2\x80\x9D

Max and Ellie finally connect, and it\xE2\x80\x99s that beautiful, all consuming, heart bursting, first true love with both of them falling fast and hard. They are inseparable; they are sharing their lives and pasts with each other and are planning their future. Joss has hooked up with Max\xE2\x80\x99s best friend, Kurt, and life is just good. Until one day, very suddenly and without a word to anyone, Max, Sarah and their father completely disappear, leaving behind a broken-hearted and confused Ellie. Her utter desolation was palpable, and I positively ached for young Ellie and the pain she felt.

\xE2\x80\x9DHe wouldn\xE2\x80\x99t just leave without telling someone.\xE2\x80\x9D

Ellie manages to move forward with her life, but she\xE2\x80\x99s never really moved on, she has never forgotten or gotten over Max. Kurt, nursing his own grief over the loss of his best friend, bonds with Ellie over their shared pain at losing Max so mysteriously. She leaves for college in Greensboro and plans to stay there, having secured a job after graduation. Unfortunately, life hasn\xE2\x80\x99t finished landing it\xE2\x80\x99s blows on Ellie, and she\xE2\x80\x99s called back to Charlotte for yet another tragedy. For a girl who was unacknowledged her entire life by both her parents and who lost the love of her young life in such a perplexing way, this latest loss is a huge blow to her already battered and abandoned soul, and she moves back to Charlotte, to her home and her friends, to deal with the aftermath.

\xE2\x80\x9D\xE2\x80\xA6all I could think about was making my way back to you.\xE2\x80\x9D

Ellie settles into life in Charlotte again. She is surrounded by memories of Max, but it\xE2\x80\x99s been five years, and she finally begins to accept that Max is not coming back and may even be dead. As she is on the cusp of opening herself up to the possibility of another man, Max reappears in their lives. He is determined to pick up where they left off, and he pursues Ellie relentlessly. His reason for leaving was surprisingly valid, and it was clearly a painful, heart-breaking decision for him. The author skillfully takes us through their reconnection, full of its ups and downs, its miscommunications and misunderstandings, and she lands us happily on the other side.

Max and Ellie\xE2\x80\x99s story was a rollercoaster of emotions, and I felt every single one, every single step of the way. This is where RB Hilliard\xE2\x80\x99s writing shines, in her ability to so expertly draw you in to what her characters are feeling and going through, while painting a rich story of young love lost and then found again. This was a remarkable first offering from this author, and I am truly excited about what the very talented RB Hilliard will give us next.h, while painting a rich story of young love lost and then found again. review_body:
I chose this one because it was touted as being a \xE2\x80\x9Cromantic comedy.\xE2\x80\x9D I have a weakness for romantic comedies, though I will admit, sometimes they can be hit or miss. In my humble opinion, this one is, mostly, a hit.

It is written in the first person present voice. Not my favorite, but this author did an amazing job of pulling me inside Charlotte Taylor\xE2\x80\x99s head. I felt what she felt. I saw things the way she saw them. I cried when she cried. I laughed with her, even when it was at herself. I felt invested in Charlotte\xE2\x80\x99s search for self, not to mention \xE2\x80\x9CMr. Perfect.\xE2\x80\x9D

This was a very well written journey of finding oneself in the make believe world of stardom as seen through the eyes of a newly discovered star. In places it was quite poignant. Something like this, being told in first person present could get rather redundant or cumbersome. I liked how the author solved that problem. She did excellent transitions through diary entries. Kept the voice, but moved the story along very nicely. I really liked that.

The romance \xE2\x80\x93 Blake Hudson was \xE2\x80\x9CMr. Perfect,\xE2\x80\x9D Charlotte\xE2\x80\x99s soul mate. I loved how that happened. It was fate. Predestined. Had to be. *sigh* Every romantics dream come true. So sweet. So \xE2\x80\x9Cperfect.\xE2\x80\x9D They way this was presented, they really were meant for each other.

The comedy \xE2\x80\x93 Charlotte seems to have this knack for getting herself into interesting situations. Mostly, it is just a lack of self-confidence, but to Charlotte, so much more. I adored her best friend Roo-Roo aka Rupert. He was a scream. Always there to lend his support to Charlotte. One of my favorite quotes in this book was from him.

\xE2\x80\x9COh, here we go. Are you going to go down Crying Crescent, take a left down Am-a-Failure Avenue then end up at the Heartbreak Hotel? Please. You\xE2\x80\x99re stronger than that. Get those big girl panties on and fight for what you want. Enough\xE2\x80\x99s enough, young lady. You\xE2\x80\x99ve been wallowing for far too long. Bounce-Back Boulevard is waiting for you\xE2\x80\x94if only you\xE2\x80\x99d grow a pair and run down it.\xE2\x80\x9D Isn\xE2\x80\x99t that just the kind of advice one wants to hear from a bestie? product_title: The Tesla Legacy (Joe Tesla Series Book 2)
review_headline: Cantrell raises an already lofty bar
review_body:
\xE2\x80\x9COur virtues and our failings are inseparable, like force and matter. When they separate, man is no more.\xE2\x80\x9D Nikola Tesla said this, and I think it captures the feeling behind the Tesla series by Rebecca Cantrell.

It\xE2\x80\x99s strange to say that I was looking forward to going back inside the mind of a man imprisoned by his fear, but if I could have run back, I would have. The Tesla Legacy takes us back into the world of Joe Tesla, a charming man blessed with a brilliant mind and sincere conscience, who suffers from crippling agoraphobia and a knack for finding trouble. Joe reminds me of Odd Thomas from the Dean Koontz series: a regular guy with an abnormal condition who\xE2\x80\x99s always in over his head. Rather than supernatural powers, Joe has to rely on his wits and his friends to find a way out.

I loved, loved, loved this book. It\xE2\x80\x99s awesome. No, it\xE2\x80\x99s AWESOME!!

Cantrell\xE2\x80\x99s virtues are her intimacy with her characters and her delicious sense of subtle details that bring out the characters and the scenes. Even legalese and neurology. It\xE2\x80\x99s hard to imagine that she isn\xE2\x80\x99t the one living in a house under Grand Central terminal. I still remember the image of the constellations in the ceiling, and the name of the color of the paint in Joe\xE2\x80\x99s house. She sharpens her eye when we\xE2\x80\x99re inside Joe\xE2\x80\x99s mind, giving us a fuller sense of just how smart he is. We take a walk through Joe\xE2\x80\x99s past by meeting Nikola Tesla himself and meeting his parents while Joe was growing up. Joe\xE2\x80\x99s mother is mindful of manners. His security consultant Vivian is quick-thinking, smart, and quietly, dangerously cool-headed. Ash, his nemesis, is almost as smart as Joe, but his conscience drives him to ruthless choices. Celeste, Joe\xE2\x80\x99s one-time love, whom we only know from telephone conversations, is unforgettable. And how can I forget Edison? Joe\xE2\x80\x99s best friend doesn\xE2\x80\x99t say a word, but he\xE2\x80\x99s beautifully expressive, and a wonderful, funny character.

Cantrell\xE2\x80\x99s failings are\xE2\x80\xA6 I have no idea. The only reason why I haven\xE2\x80\x99t told you about the story is that I don\xE2\x80\x99t want to give anything away, except to say that the end will look great in a movie (just sayin\xE2\x80\x99). The Tesla Legacy is a tight, fast-paced novel that\xE2\x80\x99s full of surprises. My only regret is that it wasn\xE2\x80\x99t released closer to the summer. Now what am I going to read sitting on the beach?

Who am I kidding? I\xE2\x80\x99ll read it again.

product_title: Kate & Alf
review_body:
ARC provided by Publisher in exchange for an honest review.

This was another book that I was looking forward to reading, based on the description on Goodreads and Amazon. I thought this was going to be a cute love story about a girl who is ready for the next part of her life to begin, that of wife, boy was I disappointed. Here is why:

Characters: The main story is about Kate and her boyfriend of several years Alf. Enter Kate\xE2\x80\x99s best friend Megan, her drug addicted brother, and Marcus, Alf\xE2\x80\x99s friend that moves in. Not to mention a whole cast of characters at the care home that Kate works at. Two old women that love to give Kate advice. These characters had the potential to be great, but they were a little one sided and had no real growth. Especially Alf, he spent a majority of the book clueless.

Plot: The story starts on Kate\xE2\x80\x99s 32nd birthday, where she is getting dressed up for a surprise party that Alf is throwing for her. A surprise she hopes ends with an engagement ring. The events of her birthday party send the couple on a spiral of hiding their feelings and making decisions without talking to each other. It is basically the beginning of the end.

Other issues with the story: One of the BIGGEST problems I had with this story was that the transitions from person to person in a chapter was not seamless, one minute your reading things from Kate\xE2\x80\x99s perspective and then bam your reading it from Megan\xE2\x80\x99s or Alf\xE2\x80\x99s. I felt as if there was no actual continuity of flow in this story. There was too much going on between all the characters and Megan basically did a 180 on her feelings halfway through the book, though I pretty much figured out who she would end up with quickly. Then there were Alf and Kate, who I had somewhat high hopes of seeing them learn to communicate with each other\xE2\x80\xA6but was disappointed in the end when redemption did not come. For me the end kind of sucked as well, it basically ended with Kate sittingon a bench in a new city looking towards her future, and the re-introduction of a character from earlier in the book, someone who answered one question, but basically left you with more questions that could constitute a second book. However, if a second book comes I will not be reading it.

I have to say that while the cover is cute, and the story could have been cute\xE2\x80\xA6.I was disappointed and would not read again.

review_headline: The writing itself is intelligent and the character and scene descriptions make it come ...
review_body:
This is the kind of book that I could not put down, that I thought about after finishing, that I did not want to end.
It is really 2 stories, one about a French girl and the other about a German boy during WWII. The novel flashes back and forth between the two main characters yet it is not confusing or hard to follow. They have to make a movie out of this book!

product_title: Summer Break (Summer Days)
review_headline: Good story...but could have been longer...
review_body:
From the first paragraph of this book, we\xE2\x80\x99re given the impression that Miles thinks of himself as a dork. 5 years before, Miles had a disastrous coming out experience. When he told his parents that he was gay at 19, they threw him out, cut off his college tuition and told him never to come back. Luckily he had a gay uncle, Steven, who took him in and put him to work to his gay campground, The Acres.

Miles suffers from a low self-esteem and doesn\xE2\x80\x99t know how to approach the hot men who come to the campground. Although he has seen some wild stuff since he came to the campground, he has always hung back and never tried to meet anyone. Now he has finally had enough and is ready to meet someone. He goes to the bar in the campground, but after an hour, the only contact he has had is one guy who smirked at him after looking him up and down, then just walked away without saying a word to Miles. Anyone who has ever had that experience will relate and feel really bad for Miles at this point. So Miles heads off to the bonfire, renowned for being the place the desperate go to find someone to hook up with. Still no one looks at him, until he stands up to go get another beer and runs smack into someone. While apologizing the guy says Miles name and it turns out to be Elliott, Miles old high school crush from when they were both on the swim team.

What follows is a sweet tale of two men getting to know each other, while dealing with drama; lack of self-worth; a huge secret on Elliot\xE2\x80\x99s part; and resistance to change on Miles part.

I enjoyed this book. It was shorter than I would prefer. I would have liked more detail on the characters, as I was never able to really picture any of them in my mind because they were not described well enough to get an image of them. Finally, I\xE2\x80\x99m not personally a huge fan of a two page Epilogue tying the loose ends up but the author did a good job with it. Based on this book, I will definitely search out and read the other books in her Summer Days series.

RATING: 3.5 Starsthe other books in her Summer Days series.

product_title: One Long Embrace (Eternal Bachelors Club Book 5)
review_headline: \xE2\x80\x9CLittle white lies can come back to bite you\xE2\x80\x9D
review_body:
One Long Embrace Book #5 (Eternal Bachelors Club) Tina Folsom

Right off the bat the read opens with Jay Bohannon waiting for a business associate. Tucked away in a booth he over hears a conversation from the next booth over. Women talking about prospective husbands. They were talking like it was a business, who had the most assets, who they would totally go for and who they shouldn\xE2\x80\x99t go for. Jay was in a relationship and was head over heels for Deborah. He was even contemplating taking their relationship to the next level. UNTIL he heard her voice. Paying a little more attention totally turned Jay\xE2\x80\x99s heart to ice. She was talking about him like he was some kind of investment property. Plus he found out she was actually cheating on him. Soooooooooo when he stood and approached the table Deborah didn\xE2\x80\x99t see him at first but when she did oh brother I wish I was a little fly on the wall. His response was priceless. That being said it still really put a knife in Jay\xE2\x80\x99s heart. How will he ever know if a woman was interested in him as a person and not his money and so the walls go up.
Tara Pierpont was born with a silver spoon in her mouth as the saying goes. But she was not like the rest of the rich women. Tara was a rebel, she hated the fact that her parents tried to rule her life and give her no say. Everything was a business proposition. What family could help how with a marriage arrangement. All about money that\xE2\x80\x99s all it was. Tara was sick of entitled \xE2\x80\x9CRich Guys\xE2\x80\x9D. So when she accepted an invitation to visit Paul, hang out for the weekend and attend his parents Anniversary Party, she thought this will be a nice break. You see Tara liked Paul, but not romantically, they were just friends. Unbeknownst to her the invitation was not from Paul but a set up between the parents. Last straw that broke the camels back. She was trying so hard to be independent and out from under her parents hold. But every corner she turned she was blocked. Turns out her father made it so she couldn\xE2\x80\x99t get a job.
During the party there was an incident that was ugly. When a drunken man was flattened by Paul and ended up in the pool Tara jumped in to save him since no one else was even attempting. And now the fun begins. Jay was standing next to the waiter as the big drunk was heading his way so of course Jay grabs the tray with the drinks. When Tara signals him over because she needs a drink thinking he\xE2\x80\x99s a waiter he immediately wants to clear up the misunderstanding until she opens to him about hating entitled rich boys. Jay immediately shut his trap. He\xE2\x80\x99s attracted to her and this would be the perfect opportunity to see if a woman could like him for him and not his money.
They end up on his boat and as much as he wants to bed her he doesn\xE2\x80\x99t. As hard as it was for him to resist her he does. The shower scene will make you melt trust me. His little charade almost comes to an end when Zach comes aboard the boat. Jay had to be quick on his feet with that one. He wasn\xE2\x80\x99t ready to let go of Tara. Honestly he didn\xE2\x80\x99t want to.
Jay was into Tara in a big way. She made him feel things he never had. It wasn\xE2\x80\x99t just the sex there was something else. Something emotionally binding. He liked it.
When Jay loses his designer he sends out the word to all his buddies in the Bachelors Club. When Paul responded with the perfect person Jay told him to set it up. And here\xE2\x80\x99s where the charade ends. Taking the advice of Jay, Tara has Paul use a different name so she can at least have a chance at the job and not have them call her father.
This is when his charade comes back to bite him. When Tara walks into his office for her interview she\xE2\x80\x99s shocked and Jay is numb. The Gig is up. After a lot of heated words by Tara and raised voices (their first fight) Tara storms out of the office leaving Jay with his mouth to the floor. He tried to explain but she wouldn\xE2\x80\x99t have it.
Jay was absolutely miserable. At Paul\xE2\x80\x99s wedding all his buds saw his mood and were riding him a bit. This didn\xE2\x80\x99t help his mood. But someone mentioned a party and they knew Tara was going to be there. He had one last ditch effort to win her back. Because he loved her.
When he shows up as a waiter again he rescues Tara from the Hosts son and takes her away to the dance floor to proposition her. He want\xE2\x80\x99s 4 days with her just 4 days so she can see he is what she wants. She agrees. This is the part of the story you start to really melt. Jay never talks about his past. But in a last ditch effort to win Tara\xE2\x80\x99s heart he\xE2\x80\x99s going to take her to the beginning. To what he was and how he grew up. How he wasn\xE2\x80\x99t born with a silver spoon in his mouth. How he worked for everything and with a little luck made it.
I absolutely loved this read. In fact it was my favorite. The sweetest love story between two people. You will fall in love with Jay and Tara. Tina this was fabulous, but I\xE2\x80\x99m a little freaked out. I didn\xE2\x80\x99t see the next title for The Bachelors Club. Will it be Hunter or Zach? 5* and can\xE2\x80\x99t wait for the next one.

product_title: Kyland
review_headline: Kyland is in my heart now...thank you Mia Sheridan for sharing your talent with us!
review_body:
Kyland\xE2\x80\xA6

First of all, let me just say that this is my first detailed review with some spoilers. I usually just say if it was good or bad and share a few reasons why I liked/disliked the book. This will be a long thorough review because this book deserves such a thing. (Some spoilers included in this review)

My first book from Mia Sheridan was Archer\xE2\x80\x99s Voice. I of course fell in love with Archer and his story. It immediately became one of my favorite books. The second book was Leo, again another fantastic book. I didn\xE2\x80\x99t get a chance to pick up another book from Mia Sheridan but I was planning on it. When I heard about Kyland I knew I would read it next. I had no doubt I would like it because everything I read by Mia Sheridan is excellent. I read Kyland in three days, but believe me, I could not put it down. It literally pained me to have to put it down to go to bed, to go to work, to get back to my life. If I could have spend an entire day reading Kyland, I would have. Maybe one day I will do just that, reread it. So with all that being said. I will explain why I am giving this book 5 stars.

Number one reason for giving this book 5 stars, simply because I can\xE2\x80\x99t give it more, if I could give it 10 more I would.

I don\xE2\x80\x99t think I have ever read a book that explained in such detailed the struggles of people who have very little. I\xE2\x80\x99ve read books before where authors explained poverty but Mia Sheridan not only explained it and described it in detailed, she made you live it through her words. I have always been fortunate enough to have what I needed, not always what I wanted but certainly all I needed. Fortunate enough to always have nice clothes and food in our refrigerator. I can\xE2\x80\x99t say I have ever experienced hunger like Kyland and Tenleigh endured. Mia Sheridan made me realized just how blessed I am. I thought I knew hard times, but you don\xE2\x80\x99t know suffering until it\xE2\x80\x99s explained like Mia explained it in Kyland\x1As story. Everything Kyland went through, everything he experienced is enough to break anyone, enough to cause even the strongest person to give up, but Kyland never did.

Tenleigh is also a very strong person. Her never ending love for Kyland made this book even more amazing. The way she cared so much for him, the way she understood him and encouraged him, the way she protected him. But most of all, Tenleigh\xE2\x80\x99s simplicity, her way of viewing life and being positive. Being poor didn\xE2\x80\x99t make her a bitter person, she was full of life and love and compassion for others. That made her an unbelievable and unique character.

When you love someone you think you are willing to do anything for them. Give up anything for that person. Do anything in your power to see them happy. But when that moment comes will we be able to go through with it, will we be able to give up so much for the person we love, can we sacrifice our own happiness for theirs? Kyland did. Kyland\xE2\x80\x99s love for Tenleigh was so strong that he did just that, he sacrificed himself, his happiness, his life for her. product_title: Worth the Risk (The McKinney Brothers, Book 2)
review_body:
"\xE2\x80\xA6he was a man who got what he wanted, and the longer he\xE2\x80\x99d stood there beside her car, the more he\xE2\x80\x99d wanted Hannah. Plus, she\xE2\x80\x99d said no. That alone had sealed her fate."

4.25 RATING+ It wouldn\x27t be fair to go into Worth the Risk thinking it was going to be fabulous just because Worth the Fall was one of my favorite reads of 2014. The type of book I sent to friends as gifts, turned into a fan girl with the author on twitter, and basically pimped all over Goodreads. Totally not fair. But I couldn\x27t help but go in with certain expectations. I\x27m only human, right? I did try to temper my expectations before starting Worth the Risk. I really, really did\xE2\x80\xA6

So, what\xE2\x80\x99d I think? Overall, Worth the Risk did not disappoint!

\xE2\x80\x9CI want to see you again. Tomorrow.\xE2\x80\x9D

Her stomach flipped with a new kind of fear. \xE2\x80\x9CI didn\xE2\x80\x99t think I was the kind of girl\xE2\x80\x94\xE2\x80\x9D

\xE2\x80\x9CI\xE2\x80\x99m sorry.\xE2\x80\x9D He closed his eyes for a second then opened them and pinned her with serious brown eyes. \xE2\x80\x9CI was wrong.\xE2\x80\x9D
\xE2\x80\x9CNo.\xE2\x80\x9D She shook her head. \xE2\x80\x9CI don\xE2\x80\x99t think you were.\xE2\x80\x9D

\xE2\x80\x9CWhy don\xE2\x80\x99t you let me be the judge of that?\xE2\x80\x9D

\xE2\x80\x9CBecause I can\xE2\x80\x99t.\xE2\x80\x9D But she wanted to touch him. Wanted to take his face in her hands and feel the rough shadow over his strong jaw. Wanted to stare into eyes so hot they melted her.

\xE2\x80\x9CHannah . . .\xE2\x80\x9D His hand came down to lightly circle her throat.

\xE2\x80\x9CDon\xE2\x80\x99t. Please.\xE2\x80\x9D She dropped her gaze from a man too used to getting what he wanted, too used to being wanted. \xE2\x80\x9CDon\xE2\x80\x99t play with me.\xE2\x80\x9D

\xE2\x80\x9CI\xE2\x80\x99m not.\xE2\x80\x9D

The writing in Worth the Risk is fabulous. Claudia Conner is an author whose writing style works for me. I love a vulnerable heroine and appreciate a strong, alpha hero. Hannah and Stephen filled both roles perfectly. While both characters suffer greatly from past events that were both violent and life altering, I thought the heroine worked hard to be strong and independent even with her many vulnerabilities. (Of course, I love a great damsel in distress story). I\xE2\x80\x99m especially excited that so many potential future characters were introduced in this book. Hannah\xE2\x80\x99s brothers seem like a dream team of possible heros! (Can readers expect a spin off series from this author focusing on these guys? I can only keep my fingers crossed!)

Readers expecting Worth the Risk to be a feel good romance like Worth the Fall was may be shocked. Worth the Risk is much darker. Both Hannah and Stephen\xE2\x80\x99s characters are damaged. Both have serious issues with terrible pasts, both violent and heartbreaking. Because of their pasts, there was some back and forth between the two characters, some mistakes made along the way but no matter what...I was totally hooked.

One small complaint I have is, I wish the read would have been sexier. On one hand, I understand the storyline and factors that contributed to this having a lower steam level. On the other hand, Stephen seemed like such a dominating hero, such a sexual character, I felt there was more potential between these two characters for things to get much hotter than they did.

Overall, this was a great contemporary romance. Darker than I was expecting but very well done. Claudia Connor cemented her status as a must read author for me. I can\x27t wait to see what she writes next.

**One note: I received an uncorrected copy of this book to review. The author did make changes to the story after I read the initial copy. I do plan to go back and read the revised version of Worth the Risk but did not read it when this review was written.

Thanks to Netgalley and the publisher for a copy of this book in exchange for a honest review.

review_headline: Fun romance novel from one of my new go-to authors!
review_body:
Review originally posted on my blog www.LivingLifeWithJoy.com

When I first heard about Tracy\xE2\x80\x99s novel Caching In, I was a bit mystified because I had never heard of geocaching and hadn\xE2\x80\x99t the slightest idea what is was. For those who have never head of it, geocaching is an outdoor game of searching for hidden objects by using Global Positioning System (GPS) coordinates posted on the Internet. It might be easier to explain that it\xE2\x80\x99s like a treasure hunt. You find things called a cache that other people have hidden to find; a cache is the treasure you find. You don\xE2\x80\x99t get to keep it, but you do get to claim that you\xE2\x80\x99ve found it and provide evidence that you found it. It sounds like a fun hobby and it\xE2\x80\x99s always fun and exciting for me to learn about something new through my reading.

Within the first few pages, I knew that Tracy was going to be one of my new favorite authors and had earned herself a spot on my list of go-to authors. I enjoyed her writing style and sense of humor and I can\xE2\x80\x99t wait to read all of her previous novels as soon as possible! The minute I finished reading Caching In I was inspired to read a short story she\xE2\x80\x99d written, Early Bird Special.

Ally has had a string of unfortunate events in her life from a failed romance to a dead-end job and she\xE2\x80\x99s at the point where things are so bad that they can only get better. Her only love interest is Harry Styles [yes, THE Harry Styles from One Direction] but she\xE2\x80\x99s completely happy with her fictitious boyfriend for the moment. When she decides to pick up a new hobby, she meets gorgeous Seth Hayes and it looks like things in her life might finally start falling into place.

One of the things I loved in the story were the strong family bonds and romantic relationships throughout the novel. I truly adored the story of Ally and Seth. It was intriguing, entertaining, and heart-wrenching and I loved every minute of it. I also loved the relationship between Ally and her brother Perry. It\xE2\x80\x99s so sweet to think that siblings that don\xE2\x80\x99t live close can still manage to stay in close communication over the years.

Caching In was not just a fun contemporary romance novel, though it was thoroughly entertaining. It was filled with important real-life issues like infidelity, being the other woman, recovering after divorce, death of loved ones and ultimately learning to move on and be happy with the life you have with the people that matter most.

Sometimes people act with selfish motives and don\xE2\x80\x99t stop to think that what they\xE2\x80\x99re doing will negatively affect the important people in their lives. Secrets. Lies. Backstabbing. When will it ever end? It\xE2\x80\x99s important to stick up for yourself when you know you deserve something like a promotion or a boyfriend that doesn\xE2\x80\x99t cheat on you. It\xE2\x80\x99s sad commentary that sometimes people get screwed over by the people they think they can trust most in the world.

I can imagine it\xE2\x80\x99s difficult when you\xE2\x80\x99re in a new relationship, to move past having been betrayed and not having a jaded sense of life. How can you ever fully trust someone new when you\xE2\x80\x99ve had your heart terribly broken in the past? When we\xE2\x80\x99re in love, we must allow ourselves to be vulnerable. We can\xE2\x80\x99t allow our fears to keep us from the possibility of love. Facing your fears and working through them is what ultimately makes you stronger.
