product_title: Hero
review_body:
Hero by Samantha Young \xE2\x80\xA6 Well, to put short: I was not overly fond of the reading experience.

I really do like romance: historical, paranormal and even modern new adult sometimes. But I like to read a good story with an interesting, forward moving plot, witty dialogue and three-dimensional characters. To be fair Hero isn\xE2\x80\x99t bad, it\xE2\x80\x99s just not good either. I might have enjoyed it more, were it not for some very incredible scenes. For example the whole preposition of the story:

The story starts off, with Alexa walking up to Caine the Billionaire during a photo shooting for the cover of a people magazine, telling him she is the daughter of the man who killed his mother. Believable much? She does this because she feels some kind of need to make Caine happy, as if she has to make up for her father\xE2\x80\x99s sins. This scene doesn\xE2\x80\x99t go well for her. Subsequently, she loses her job and walks into Caine\xE2\x80\x99s office a few days later in flip flops, tank shirt and shorts asking him to make things right again. And making things even more unbelievable he then offers her a position as his personal assistant with a small fortune as a salary (3x as much as she earned before). Yeah right, I so can relate to this. Having applied to more than my fair share of jobs and having had more job interviews than I can count, I can tell you this: No one, really no one not even a small sized company would give you a job as PA, with an annual income of 50k if you 1 walk in there looking like some tourist on the beach and 2 if the CEO has personal issues with your family.

description

But ok let\xE2\x80\x99s put the credibility aside and let\xE2\x80\x99s focus on the ensuing romance. It was kind of formulaic and honestly a bit boring. Caine is just a one dimensional billionaire hard boiled on the outside with a creamy core. We get treated to a few office scenes, which honestly were quite boring. Then of course she has to go to his apartment and gets introduced to the \xE2\x80\x9CFairy Godmother\xE2\x80\x9D, as I like to put it, the 70 years old, eccentric lady living next door who plays at matchmaking. From this point on I just started to skip pages. Alexa and Caine have a one night stand in the office, of course she then gives her notice to quit, but he won\xE2\x80\x99t let her go, because she is that outstanding at her job as PA. Phhhleeeeaaassse. What\xE2\x80\x99s so outstanding in making travel arrangements, or organizing conference calls? So he invites her on a business trip, including first class tickets and presidential suite in the hotel. *Insert eye-roll, here* From the business trip on they start a \xE2\x80\x9Csex-only\xE2\x80\x9D affaire which progresses fairly fast to a \xE2\x80\x9Cfriends-with-benefits\xE2\x80\x9D relationship and from there to a \xE2\x80\x9Cnon-exclusive exclusive relationship\xE2\x80\x9D. Hmpf, \xE2\x80\xA6 I was not drawn into the story. It seemed to me like Samatha Young had a list next to her laptop: Insert sex scene here, progress to new stage of relationship, yadayadayada.

So if you\xE2\x80\x99re looking for a billionaire romance with formulaic sex scenes, that aren\xE2\x80\x99t even hot, feel free to pick this up.iry Godmother\xE2\x80\x9D, as I like to put it, the 70 years old, eccentric lady living next door who plays at matchmaking. product_title: Blood Assassin (The Sentinels Series Book 2)
review_body:
After reading Born in Blood, I could not pass up an opportunity to read Blood Assassin and it was worth my time.

Serra and Fane\x27s attraction to each other is the worst-kept secret in Valhalla and even though Serra has has thrown herself at Fane countless times, he has never taken her up on her offer and she decides that she is done chasing after a man who would not acknowledge her or his feelings for her.

Fane is a highly trained and legendary sentinel and has dedicated his life to his duty as a guardian. Now that guardianship of his charge Callie has been transferred to Duncan, he has decided to return to the monastery as trainer. Fane knows that Serra is the only woman that will ever hold his heart, but his rejection of her is due to his responsibilities as a guardian. When Serra is in danger, he drops the barriers he put up against her and rushes to her rescue, but the constant rejection from Fane has affected her ability to trust him and he has a battle on his hand trying to convince her that his feelings are real.

If you love strong and spirited women, then you would love Serra. She is that and more - larger than life, gorgeous, smart, independent, bold but above all, she knows her shoes!!! Come on, you\x27ve got to love a woman that knows her designers! I loved that she lived life on her own terms and was no pushover. Fane is very much a protector- tall, strong, tattooed and lethal but against this enemy his hands are tied, which does not go down well with him. Fane and Serra together are just perfect - passionate sexual encounters mixed with very sweet moments.

In a first for me, I actually liked the villain and was rooting for him. Bas is a cunning criminal with a very broken moral compass and he demonstrates a chilling ruthlessness in the way he manipulates Serra into doing his bidding, but he is willing to use anyone and anything to save his child.

As usual, Ms. Ivy gives us dramatic, action-packed scenes that draw us right in and make us feel like we are in the thick of the danger and excitement. The teasers about other potential story-lines give a glimpse of what promises to be an even more thrilling addition to the series. Blood Assassin is definitely one to read.

review_body:
\xE2\x80\x9CBe happy while you\xE2\x80\x99re living, for you\xE2\x80\x99re a long time dead.\xE2\x80\x9D

Alex hasn\xE2\x80\x99t paid much attention to that Scottish Proverb. He is stuck in a major rut. He is working at a coffee counter at Edinburgh Airport in Scotland and is completely miserable. He hates his job, he hates his commute, and his relationship is a joke. Alex has finished his degree at university, but hasn\xE2\x80\x99t done anything with it yet. The only reason Alex is working at the counter instead of working for his father\xE2\x80\x99s prestigious law firm in Glasgow is Alex\xE2\x80\x99s evil stepmother. She also works for the firm and Alex feels she is to blame for breaking up his parent\xE2\x80\x99s marriage and his mother\xE2\x80\x99s subsequent car accident death. Alex has been in a \xE2\x80\x9Crelationship\xE2\x80\x9D with Rupert for 5 years, but Rupert is only in it for the position it gets him at Alex\xE2\x80\x99s father\xE2\x80\x99s firm and they haven\xE2\x80\x99t really been in love for at least 3 years. Most nights Rupert stays at the home of Alex\xE2\x80\x99s father and stepmother, and they seem to both like Rupert better than Alex!

One day, Alex looks up to see a handsome stranger standing in front of him. In blows Hurricane Jake, knocking Alex right out of the rut he has found himself in. Before he knows what is happening he is in a sleeping pod within the airport having some of the best sex of his entire life! And it goes on for a couple days!

Afterwards Jake has to leave, explaining he travels extensively and is on his way to London. Alex says good bye and figures he\xE2\x80\x99ll never see him again. He couldn\xE2\x80\x99t be more wrong. He continues to see Jake, and each time they have wild monkey sex and Jake asks him to jump on a plane with him and just take off for an adventure, leaving his dull life in a rut behind. Who is this mysterious man? Should Alex go one of these times, should he keep saying no? His life is very \xE2\x80\x9Ccomplicated\xE2\x80\x9D after all. Should he maybe get the guy\xE2\x80\x99s phone number?

This author creates very believable characters and story lines. The character of Alex was so well written that I truthfully was really irritated at Alex several times during the book because he reminded me so much of a couple 22 year old gay men that I know personally. I wanted to reach into the book and slap him up beside the head!

Along the way, Alex makes some decisions that left me cringing. I\xE2\x80\x99m happy to say he also made some good ones at times as well.

I very much enjoyed this book, and highly recommend it. I will be following to see what else Mr. Black writes.

We are introduced to the Prince, leader of the City of Florence, who is at once cold and calculating but beautiful in his own right. He cannot stay away from Raven and feels compelled to help her again and again. He sees in her virtue and goodness, and she awakens long-dormant feelings that he never believed he could have, even at his own peril.

"I\x27m afraid that trouble is not what you do. Trouble is what you are."

Raven is an unlikely heroine and I fell in love with her! She is damaged goods, inside and out, and her painful history is hinted at and then ultimately explained. She is an extremely sympathetic character and I cannot wait to read more about her in the next book. The Prince, too, is surprised at his attraction to her; might she lead him to redemption and true love?

\xE2\x80\x9CIn many ways, we are the most perfect match. We see each other as we are, but neither of us views the other as broken.\xE2\x80\x9D

product_title: The Perseid Collapse Series: Deadly Calm (Kindle Worlds Novella)
review_body:
I\x27d rate this closer to 4.5 out of 5 stars, if I could.

The pros:

It\x27s a fine story; I liked Blake\x27s portrayal of the main character as an average Joe who found himself in over his head, rather than someone who "just happens" to have everything figured out before disaster strikes. And I liked how quickly some of the side characters adapted to the situation, because I\x27ve recently read a number of post-disaster stories where one or more characters Just. Doesn\x27t. Get. how untenable anti-violence attitudes are when looters are actively threatening people. In particular, I liked Carla quite a bit; she\x27s no-nonsense and practical, and she\x27s got an excellent head on her shoulders. Also, the action is excellent and quite gripping.

The cons:

As with other stories set in the world of the Perseid Collapse series, Deadly Calm portrays EMP effects as all-encompassing, in the sense that almost all cars fail to work, almost all power grids are down semi-permanently, almost all cell phones are bricked... basically, once the EMP happens, there are universal and clear signs that the characters can use to figure out that they are in deep trouble and have to act immediately.

And that\x27s a perfectly valid trope, it\x27s just not all that accurate. One of these days I\x27ll stumble across a gripping, well-characterized story (which Deadly Calm is) that also portrays the widespread effects of an EMP more accurately, as affecting a fair percentage of cars but not 95+ percent of them, as causing many more temporary power grid overloads than permanently ruined transformers, and generally being ambiguous enough that the protagonists will have to deal with uncertainty over whether this is actually serious enough to merit fleeing elsewhere... but that day is not this day.

In short, if you want a fast, interesting read with a variety of characters stuck in a dangerous situation, this is a darned good read. Just be aware that it\x27sdoing what One Second After and many other post-EMP books have done, and simplified EMP effects in a way that heightens tension at the cost of accuracy. (Which, again, is a totally legit writing technique.)

product_title: The Alpha and the Omega: An absurd philosophical tale about God, the end of the world, and what\x27s on the other planets
review_body:
The Alpha and the Omega: An absurd philosophical tale about God, the end of the world, and what\x27s on the other planets was a very refreshing read. I like philosophically based books and this one is quite unique. It has a specific style yet a smooth narrative. I enjoyed the entertaining view on the after life and the overall playful approach to faith and religion.

The novel begins with the story of Zack and Lilly, two ordinary humans and atheists, who go about their lives calmly, before God enters their lives and invites them to heaven. The heaven seems like the promised paradise at first. One can savour his favourite meals ceaselessly, meet his deceased relatives and have all the fun he could imagine. However, it eventually turns out to be not as ideal and even God doesn\xE2\x80\x99t seem so perfect anymore. What follows is a rich, deep but also whimsical journey through different worlds, planets and an unfolding romance between Lilly and Zack with an amusing twist in the end.

What stood out the most to me was the philosophy behind the question that we all probably ask ourselves sometimes, and the answer it poses:
Why doesn\xE2\x80\x99t God do anything to change the world for the better?
But why don\xE2\x80\x99t WE do anything?
The novel also brought up the themes of duality, balance in life and responsibility, taking action instead of blaming the world, change the within if we seek change without, the concept of higher power and why humans have the desire to follow leaders, gurus, mentors or any kind of authority in general. This story really makes your mind spin but in a fun light mode and I enjoyed that.

But this one, The Troop, was so right on the money.  I read a lot of horror and books that claim to be horror--this one is horror and more. I was actually squicked out a couple of places. product_title: In His Keeping: A Slow Burn Novel (Slow Burn Novels Book 2)
review_body:
From the page one I was captivated by this compelling story, and was hanging on to every word.
The plot is set with skill and the tale flows like a river, as the history of Arial, and her parents, at the beginning of the book paint such a loving, touching and tender picture of the family.
The powerful and raw connection Ariel and Beau have, also has a history, and makes you want to believe in destiny and serendipity. This story proves once again, that the tougher they are, the harder they fall. Beau, the grouchy alpha male, talking about his feelings, taking tender care of Ariel, protecting her, and fighting for her, is nothing but adoring. The love scenes are nearly poetic in nature, filled with passion, true connection of heart, mind, and soul.
The action kicks the adrenaline going. The fear and threat are palpable, the psychic abilities interesting and intriguing, the fights against the evil villains energetic and merciless.
When the story makes you smile with the merry banter of the characters, sigh with the sweetness of the romance, shed a tear for the heartbreaking events, makes your heart beat rise with the fierce action, and at the end wish you could stay in that magic the tale weaved, it more than deserves
~ Five Spoons!!!!

product_title: Us: A Novel
review_body:
I found this book to be quite fascinating. It sort of poses two questions:

1. What would you do if your spouse suddenly and unexpectedly announces that he/she thinks the marriage has run its course and they might want a divorce?
2. How likely is it for two people from two different schools of thought to stay together forever?

The author explores both questions simultaneously as he takes the reader through the present time and the past. Douglas and Connie are soon-to-be empty nesters. Douglas tells us he is blind-sided by Connie\xE2\x80\x99s admission that she is unhappy in the marriage and is thinking about divorcing him. Despite her feelings, the family embarks on a European vacation \xE2\x80\x93 the last true family getaway \xE2\x80\x93 that forces Douglas to figure out how he got to this place in his life.

The themes that run throughout the book include science vs. art, how people grow apart, being a rule follower vs. being fancy-free, parents\xE2\x80\x99 dreams for their children and how it hurts or helps them grow, the importance of partners in life\xE2\x80\x99s journey, diligence and responsibility vs. living in the moment, and of course the famous nature vs. nurture and father vs. son themes.

A whole different discussion could be had about the \xE2\x80\x9Cun\xE2\x80\x9Ds or \xE2\x80\x9Cunder\xE2\x80\x9Ds in this book: unappreciated, underthumb, misunderstood, unfulfilled, unloved. Or perhaps what each character lacks in their lives: fun, understanding, compassion, appreciation. Oh the things that happen to us in our lives as we grow complacent!

Douglas is a scientist. Connie is an artist. Douglas likes structure and order. Connie lives freely and unconfined. After some time, this married couple naturally grows apart. Or was it not natural? Douglas wants to grow old together, but Connie doesn\xE2\x80\x99t want to age. Douglas does everything he can to lift up Connie, and Connie makes the ultimate sacrifice by moving to a place she doesn\xE2\x80\x99t fit in.

Douglas is not a very reliable narrator. He doesn\xE2\x80\x99t want to give away private, personal information, and he certainly doesn\xE2\x80\x99t want to go too deep into emotional feelings. He claims to have no idea why Connie wants to leave him and why his son hates him. The reader initially can sypathize with him. He paints himself as doting, caring, responsible, and having all the bases covered. However, as Douglas reveals more of his family\xE2\x80\x99s past, the reader discovers that Douglas begins to retreat and lose sight of what is important. He comes across as a real jerk. When Douglas slips back into present time, we lose a little of that notion but not enough to sympathize quite so much. Now, we just understand better. The ultimate irony in Douglas is that he sees things in his life only as he wants to see them. For a scientist, he is not very realistic!

I couldn\xE2\x80\x99t put this book down. I really wanted to know what had happened that brought Connie to this place of wanting to dissolve her marriage. I wanted to know if there would be a happy ending. I enjoyed the escapades of the Grand Tour: the train rides, the scandalous hotel, Douglas trying to let go\xE2\x80\xA6some really funny moments. The ending was half what I expected. Upon reflection, I see it more clearly now. When I initially read the book, it\xE2\x80\x99s not how I necessarily wanted it to end. But in hindsight the book couldn\xE2\x80\x99t have ended any differently. No spoilers here!

In all, a great book to read quickly. A little bit of a downer, so maybe not a book to read when you are looking for a pick me up. It did give me some great ideas for a possible European vacation, what not to do on family trips, and some new perspective on art. product_title: 3001 (Space Odyssey Book 4)
review_headline: Not to be missed after the previous three
review_body:
This final book changes some premises, and as Clarke himself had pointed out, doesn\x27t follow all the ideas/stories/concepts from the previous ones.

The context has the same base as the other installments but got a more material or worldly resolution for many of the philosophical/existential themes raised previously, specially on the first two books. For me it wasn\x27t a "deadly sin" as some had considered, and in this way Clarke was able to give a final conclusion to the series (nevertheless, the thoughtful questions raised on 2001 will keep resonating in my head).

Another reviewer said that "this book has inconsistencies that render it not a true sequel to the former novels, but an independent story that borrows many elements from the previous sagas". That\x27s basically true, but it doesn\x27t hinder the story as an entertaining and well thought option, and if you\x27ve read the other books in the series, I totally recommend this fourth one.

As a new novel I\xE2\x80\x99d give it 5 stars, but as part of the Odyssey series, 4 stars.

product_title: Sabotaged (Alaskan Courage Book #5)
review_body:
Reef McKeena has finally returned home. Accepting his family\x27s love and forgiveness hasn\x27t always been easy for him, but he\x27s working hard to make them proud of him. When he volunteers to do Search and Rescue for the Iditarod race, he finds himself paired with local vet Kirra Jacobs. Kirra was a goody-goody growing up. And she and Reef were always at odds for some reason or another. He\x27s the last person she wants to be partnered with, but he claims to have changed. When Reef catches her sneaking out of camp one night in search of her uncle, who has gone missing, Reef knows he has to join her. Soon the pair find themselves racing against time, and the race itself, to get answers and locate Kirra\x27s kidnapped cousin before disaster strikes. But as Reef and Kirra are pulled into more and more danger, neither can deny their growing feelings. Reef wants to show Kirra that he would never hurt her, but Kirra\x27s been hurt bad in the past and is afraid to trust this former bad-boy.

I think that this conclusion to the McKenna family saga is my favorite. I have loved each book in this series, but for some reason, Reef just climbed further into my heart than the other siblings.

True to Pettrey\x27s style, this book is an adventure ride to the finish. I actually found myself having to put the book down because I needed sleep. I love the family dynamics in the McKenna family. I love how they are willing to help each other out, no questions asked.

I also loved how Reef didn\x27t pressure Kirra to share her past. Yes he finds out. But he was willing to give her space. I also loved how Kirra had no other option but to trust Reef.

While I\x27m sad to say goodbye to this family, I\x27m excited to see what Dani has in store for her readers next.

review_headline: Now I wish Florida really did have fairies, dragons and witches!
review_body:
Stephen del Mar has written a contemporary fantasy set on the Gulf Coast of Florida that contains mythical beings, as well as every day humans. His writing is excellent, and even though there were a few word usage issues (i.e. waste versus waist), they were minor and easily overlooked. His characters were believable because they weren\xE2\x80\x99t perfect. I\xE2\x80\x99m so sick of reading books with the characters all having six pack abs, perfect lives, and cookie cutter romances. The characters in this book are not at all like that. I felt that if I got on my motorcycle and rode a couple hours north that I could actually sit down and talk with Dieter and the rest of the cast.

Dieter Reinhold has just lost his Uncle Wolfgang. Now he and his brother Paul are the last two surviving family members. His brother Paul ran off at the end of high school and Dieter isn\xE2\x80\x99t close with him at all. Dieter was very close to his uncle, but his brother Paul was not. Paul comes to the funeral and stops by the old farm for a few minutes, but says that Uncle Wolfgang was a \xE2\x80\x9Cnutter and a horder\xE2\x80\x9D and that the bulldozers can clear all the junk away when they sell the property. Only one problem. Dieter isn\xE2\x80\x99t that interesting in selling the property.

After finding a mysterious cold to the touch box with rubies inset in it, Dieter finds that he is the only one who can open it. (Well in truth, his brother can as well, but the brother isn\xE2\x80\x99t really part of the story, so we\xE2\x80\x99ll ignore him in this review because I personally didn\xE2\x80\x99t like him and I\xE2\x80\x99m the reviewer so it is my decision, LOL.) Inside the box is some dust, two fangs and a priceless ruby. It doesn\xE2\x80\x99t take Dieter long to put two and two together and realize, based on Uncle Wolfgang\xE2\x80\x99s having been confined in a death camp in Nazi Germany when he was a child, that the \xE2\x80\x9Cdust\xE2\x80\x9D is actually human ashes.

A few too many beers follow, and then Dieter calls his ex, Innes, who is a male witch (although Dieter thinks that\xE2\x80\x99s a load of crap). When Innes arrives and sees the box and what is written on it, he calls the witch living next door to the Uncle\xE2\x80\x99s farm. Dieter is told that the fairies have said that he must not ejaculate into the box and onto the ashes under the full moon or something bad will happen. Really. What are you thinking right now? I was thinking\xE2\x80\xA6.OK\xE2\x80\xA6.so why would someone masturbate into a box of what looked like human ashes anyway???

I probably don\xE2\x80\x99t even have to tell you that at some point there is masturbating and ejaculation into the box of human ashes. There are also fairies, witches, bears, a tease about some dragons living nearby, gypsies or Romani, a teenager who was actually born in the 1300\xE2\x80\x99s, an evil vindictive spirit and even some fairy bukkake! In between it all there is lots of well put together storytelling.

I really enjoyed this book. It was a fairly light read and I read the entire book in one day. Most of you will probably take a couple days unless you are reading fools like me. One note, the sex in the book is mainly \xE2\x80\x9Cfade to black\xE2\x80\x9D. You know the sex occurred, but it doesn\xE2\x80\x99t occur within the pages itself. So if you\xE2\x80\x99re looking for one of those sex on every other page, in full gory detail, type of books, this isn\xE2\x80\x99t it. Move on. If you\xE2\x80\x99re more about the story and characters than the sex, then give it a try.

I recommend this book to anyone who enjoys a good contemporary fantasy tale. While it set not that far from where I live in Florida, I\xE2\x80\x99m pretty sure my part doesn\xE2\x80\x99t have fairies, dragons and witches. Damn it! I would so like it to have all of the above!

product_title: Perfect Chaos (Unyielding Book 1)
review_headline: Good book, but needed just a little bit more development.
review_body:
Perfect Chaos was a perfect read for someone who is a fan of Nashoda Rose\x27s other books. Even though this is the first book in the Unyielding series, the book draws on characters from her other books. For the most part I could follow along but with other types of books like this, I felt like I was missing chunks of the characters\x27 pasts that would have made more sense for me to know in this book.

Anyhoo, we follow the story of the main female protag Georgie. She has had a troubled life. Her brother was killed overseas in the war, her parents are distant, and she has had some dramatic experiences with abuse in high school. But Deck, her brother\x27s best friend and war buddy and contracted killer, came back to look after her. He\x27s all hard and closed in. He keeps her at arm\x27s length even though they have a very heavy attraction to one another. Deck is honoring her brother, Connor\x27s, wishes. Stay away from Georgie.

But Georgie is hiding a sordid side of her from Deck. A side that reveals so much and all too much. She needs his help more than ever but it\x27s the help that finally brings Deck to his knees and he gives into temptation. BOOM! Sexy times!

The arc of the story is well-paced and I liked the introduction of the Kai character as the antagonist. I foresee more depth from his character in books to come. I also like Deck\x27s other coworkers (contracted killers). But what I would have loved to see was more focus on Deck and his band of brothers. Unyielding Riot the company that Deck headed up was essentially a hitman business or that\x27s how it sounded. But we never saw Deck or any of the others do anything. Deck was traveling but that\x27s it. Even in his POVs. I would have loved to see more of his hard life to feel for him more. A good chunk of the book was dedicated to sexy times with Georgie and Deck and the focus of the arc was kinda on the backburner.

So I felt like this book was missing something. I\x27m still interested to see what happens in book two and will be reading it for sure when it comes out.what happens in book two and will be reading it for sure when it comes out.

product_title: Mastering Leap Motion
review_headline: in addition to a few general best practices. 9
review_body:
This book Packt\xE2\x80\x99s Masterng series guide you to become an expert in making apps for Leap Motion using object-oriented programming through practical use cases. The author in 224 pages with a quick step-by-step guide to get you set up and an overview of the Leap Motion API. Then the book teach you effective techniques and innovative design processes that are ideal for creating and testing 2D and 3D applications.
In particular you will create a 2D painting application using only Java and the Leap Motion API and a 3D application using the Unity3D toolkit.
Featuring diagrams, screenshots, and code examples to guide you as you master Leap Motion, this book will keep you in touch with the future of technology.

In nutshell if you want to begin writing applications for the Leap Motion Controller or are trying to figure out how a Leap Motion device integrates with pre-existing technologies, this is the book for you!

WHAT YOU NEED FOR THIS BOOK
The author assumes that you have some programming background.
You should have a \xE2\x80\x9Cworking knowledge\xE2\x80\x9D of any object-oriented programming. In particular Java and C# (for chapters: 5, 6, 7) languages.
There are also few things you\xE2\x80\x99ll need:
- A Leap Motion Controller
- A Computer
- A Internet Connection

CHAPTERS OVERVIEW
1: INTRODUCTION TO THE WORLD OF LEAP MOTION
Shows you how to set up and test the Leap Motion device and a programming environment to use with it. Once everything is set up, the author review the API briefly.

2: WHAT THE LEAP SEES \xE2\x80\x93 DEALING WITH FINGERS, HANDS, TOOLS, AND GESTURES
The software and hardware side of any Leap Motion application. This includes basic tracking data such as hands and fingers as well as more advanced features such as tools and gestures.
The author will finish off with an overview of some of the limitations that you might run into when working with the API and the device.

3: WHATTHE USER SEES \xE2\x80\x93 USER EXPERIENCE, ERGONOMICS, AND FATIGUE
Covers the user side of any Leap Motion application.
This includes when and when not to make use of the Leap in an application, the importance of ergonomics, and the prevention of user fatigue.

4: CREATING A 2D PAINTING APPLICATION
Walks you through the creation of a two-dimensional (or 2D) painting application for the Leap.
You\x27ll start out simple with the basic framework and graphical frontend and then move straight into rendering user input onto the screen.

5: CREATING A 3D APPLICATION \xE2\x80\x93 A CRASH COURSE IN UNITY 3D
In order to prepare you for the next few chapters the author introduce you to Unity 3D.
This chapter cover the basic installation and setup of the environment, which is followed by the creation of a blank template project for use in the next few chapters.

6: CREATING A 3D APPLICATION \xE2\x80\x93 INTEGRATING THE LEAP MOTION DEVICE WITH A 3D TOOLKIT
Walks you through the basic steps of integrating the Leap Motion device with an external 3D toolkit.
You\x27ll learn how to render hands, fingers, and buttons.
The chapter will finish off by covering the detection of user input via the Leap.
In this chapter you need to utilize C# language instead of Java.

7: CREATING A 3D APPLICATION \xE2\x80\x93 CONTROLLING A FLYING ENTITY
Guides you through the completion of our 3D application.
You will create a 3D entity, retrieve user input from the Leap, and then use that data to control the entity.

8: TROUBLESHOOTING, DEBUGGING, AND OPTIMIZATION
Is devoted to the inevitable things that will arise during application development: bugs and problems and optimization.
This chapter will go over a few different things you can use to fix common problems with your device or application, in addition to a few general best practices.

9: GOING BEYOND THE LEAP MOTION CONTROLLER
Covers a variety of subjects that go beyond the Leap Motion device itself.
The author will talk about what you\x27ve learned so far, where the Leap Motion stands next to other emerging technologies, some concerns regarding the reliability and safety of the device in the industry, and even some ideas to control robots!

ABOUT THE AUTHOR:
Brandon Sanders is an 18-year-old roboticist who spends much of his time designing, building, and programming new and innovative systems, including simulators, autonomous coffee makers, and robots for competition. At present, he attends Gilbert Finn Polytechnic (which is a homeschool) as he prepares for college. He is the founder and owner of Mechakana Systems, a website and company devoted to robotic systems and solutions. As a home-educated student, he\x27s had the unique opportunity to focus his efforts on the fields that interest him. This has made him successful as the team captain for the FIRST Robotics teams: #4982 Caf\xC3\xA9 Bot and #1444 the Lightning Lancers. He has also served as a scientific research assistant to the Chairman of the Washington University Physics Department, where he wrote software to aid in the calculation of equations of state for dense matter in neutron stars. He has received numerous awards and accolades as a result of his involvement in various programs. Two of his most notable achievements are FIRST Robotics Competition Dean\x27s List Award and FIRST Tech Challenge World Championship Inspire Award.

ABOUT THE REVIEWERS:
Rudi Chen is a software developer from the University of Waterloo and has worked for companies such as Side Effects Software and Dropbox.

Lamtharn Hantrakul is an international student from Thailand who is double majoring in Applied Physics and Music at Yale University. His research interests include instrument acoustics, signal processing, and musical HCI.

Justin Kuzma is a freelance engineer and software developer based in Burlington, VT. He has experience in creating mechanical designs and digital art installations.

Maria Montenegro is a computer scientist and an electronic media artist. Currently, she is pursuing a Master\x27s degree in Entertainment Technology from the Entertainment Technology Center (ETC) at Carnegie Mellon University.

product_title: Sailing the Apocalypse: A Misadventure at Sea
review_headline: Irritating, preachy and predictable tale narrated by a 40 year old twelve year old
review_body:
I bought this book because I had heard it described as The Mosquito Coast for Sea Steader preppers, and the Mosquito Coast is an excellent story. I am an interested observer to the Sea Steading culture, so I thought this might be a safe bet. For a book intended to be narrated by a twelve year old boy, the biggest failing is that it comes across as a whiny monologue of the author\x27s views thinly veiled as fiction. I do not know any twelve year olds who have the self awareness to describe themselves as young and inexperienced, and generally you do not get the feeling of looking at the world through the eyes of a boy experiencing everything for the first time. Robbie is no Edgar Sawtelle, that\x27s for sure.

Within a few pages, I was irritated by Terry, the step father. I know this is intentional on William\x27s part, but there is no counter to this central irritation. It is not humourous, and the mild tension is never relieved or raised to a crescendo. "Terry launched into one of his rants...." is pretty much how every page begins. For a character like Terry to have such an informed big picture view but to be so bumbling and unprepared is too much of a stretch. The scene where Terry furiously throws away the throwable PFD was among the most contrived.

Too much of the story is given over to getting to the coast, and not enough is spent on describing life aboard the catamaran or the sailing of it at sea. There is a bit of plot given over to geting us thinking about Terry\x27s background; did he really sail around the Caribbean as a younger man, where did he get all his cash from, etc that may provide hooks to bring the reader back for book two, but for me there just wasn\x27t enough ground covered for a book about this topic.

A more relevant subtitle would be "a steady stream of irritating oversights and predictable misadventures on the way to sea"

Sorry people, but I think this is a mediocre novel, even though it will no doubt be popular with the doomers, particularly those of a Sea Gypsy bent. Rather, I can highly recommend the Aubrey - Maturin series by Patrick O\x27Brian for detailed descriptions of sailing, exciting action, satisfying character development and excellent use of humour, which, due to being set 200 years ago, are a very useful reference set regarding life at sea without modern technology.

Ho. Ly. Sh*t.

She refuses to allow him to prove her wrong in what she thinks has happened. Trace is determined to set Kylie straight and regain her love.

This book had me going back and forth for a while. I really was starting to not like Kylie for a while there. There are parts of the book she seemed like a child instead of a young adult... but then again, she kind of still is a child in her own rights. product_title: The Royal Palm
review_body:
The Royal Palm is a splendidly written tale of a that teaches young readers the significance of family and friends.

On a secluded island a lovely royal palm grew, however she was self absorbed and rude. She shunned her cousin palms and was impolite to any creature who dared to climb upon her palms. Thinking she was too good to be bothered by others, she spent her time alone admiring her own beauty.

When a violent storm rocks her island home the royal palm becomes weak and tattered in the wind. Her shallow roots struggle to hang on. Alone and scared she is on the verge of giving up...

Mrs. D. has created another incredible story that enlightens and inspires. I love the message the story conveys about being kind to others and how life is meant to be shared with others. The amazing illustrations are vibrant and engaging and readers will be drawn into the world that comes alive on each page.

I highly recommend picking up a copy.

product_title: River Oaks Plantation
review_headline: If you are a Gone with the Wind Fan...You will Either Hate or Love it
review_body:
I\x27ve read rave reviews on this historical romance and also read reviews saying it was horrible. I decided to read and decide for myself. If you liked Gone with the Wind then you might like River Oaks Plantation. It has a lot of the same characters such as the kind, over-weight mammy and even very similar dialogue and scenes. Some have called this plagiarism.

The jumping back and forth from the antebellum south to 2005 does make this story a bit different. Unfortunately, I couldn\x27t get into the story in either time period. The characters are one-dimensional and act contrary to the time period or their character.

This historical aspects needed to be better researched. I found myself skimming a lot as I got bored. Maybe this is one of those books you either love or hate.

product_title: Glitterland (Spires Book 1)
review_body:
Ash Winters has experienced some real ups and downs in his life. The author of best-selling novels, he now finds himself often struggling to deal with his depression and prefers to keep himself isolated from the rest of the world. But when he is dragged to a stag party and meets Darian Taylor, an energetic and outgoing aspiring model who almost seems to live in a completely different world, things change. There\x27s an attraction there, but it means Ash has to be willing to trust Darian and also trust himself. And that\x27s something he just might not be able to do.

If you\x27re looking for a fun romantic read, this is it. These two guys just crawl off the page and into your life and it\x27s simply a great experience. Alexis Hall has done amazing job with this one. The character of Darian is so incredibly well-written that if someone told me this was an account of a true story, I wouldn\x27t be surprised at all. (Even when Darian annoyed me, I was still smiling through it.)

product_title: Pink Shades of Words: (Walk 2015)
review_body:
Teasing Destiny by Melanie Shawn

This is an introduction to a new contemporary series, Wishing Well, Texas. It was enough to whet my appetite for this new series, scheduled for release in July 2015.

Destiny is the small town sweetheart who never left home. JJ is the small town golden boy turned pro baseball star. Destiny and JJ have a long history, one Destiny would rather not revisit. JJ realizes that leaving Destiny behind left a hole in his heart, something he plans to rectify.

This story has a a lot going for it. The emotional tension between Destiny and JJ is well established, early in the story. There are some fantastic secondary characters, including Destiny\x27s great grandmother, Grandma Dixie, who raised her. The story is told from both the hero and heroine\x27s point of view, with each chapter told from alternating perspectives.

I didn\x27t love that this was essentially the first few chapters to the book rather than a complete story on its own. Having said that, I can\x27t wait to finish the whole story! I\x27ll be eagerly awaiting the scheduled release so I can see exactly how Destiny and JJ\x27s story plays out, as well as the other characters in the series.

product_title: Wings of Arian (Young Adult Fantasy) (The Solus Series Book 1)
review_body:
This novel is utterly fantastic!\xC2\xA0 I\x27ve been waiting for a new author to make it to the top of my list of favorites and now I am eager to present to you: Devri Walls!

Paranormal Romance will always be my preferred genre, but finding a great story among it can prove to be a difficult task at times. Devri Walls nailed it! There is an\xC2\xA0 enjoyable prose, a flawless collaboration of more mythical creatures than I\x27ve ever read in one book, a delicious romantic atmosphere, and adventures galore.\xC2\xA0 The dialogue is filled to the brim with humor creating a light-hearted atmosphere. And one of the most important components necessary for "the perfect novel": the author took the time to build onto the prose.

How often is that we read books these days where trust, respect, and love are built over time? How often do we truly see a prose that tests these boundaries with creative and infallible story-lines, rather than rush it to immediately capture the reader\x27s attention? I have enjoyed my fair share of rushed relationships in stories and I believe those sort of relationships actually exist; however,\xC2\xA0 a great author will capture the readers attention using every element involved in a good book without having to leave other area\x27s lacking.

I love not only the balance Devri Walls provided in her book, but also balance in theory and in character traits as opposed to unrealistic standards. She allows her male and female protagonist,\xC2\xA0 along with the enjoyable secondary characters,\xC2\xA0 human qualities that I\x27ve seen unrefined in some books. They are allowed to feel and show fear just as much as courage, weaknesses and strengths alike. The characters are a balance one to another to depend upon, to test, and to motivate.
There\x27s also the meticulously written twist of how each consequence equally reflects an action.

I truly loved the characters, the romance, and the journey. At times I felt like a kid watching "The Never Ending Story" for the first time. So much took place to make it seem like a vast novel, but loved so well for it to end too soon.

Wings of Arian is a YA novel enjoyable for paranormal romance lovers of all age categories.\xC2\xA0 Enjoyable,\xC2\xA0 however, is quite the understatement.\xC2\xA0 I am thoroughly impressed by Devri Walls. I highly recommend her books and as a picky reader, recommending someone for others to invest in is always done with absolute certainty of quality.\xC2\xA0

product_title: City In Embers (Collector Series Book 1)
review_body:
I received this book as a gift

City of Embers is an unexpected thrill ride, packed with surprises that will throw and shock you into a serious adrenaline rush. Complete and utter captivation.

PROS:
Zoey is fierce. Her resilience is powerful and admirable. She\xE2\x80\x99s daring and beautiful, she wields so much strength. She fights tooth and nail for her life and those she loves. Her past is full of bad decisions made to survive and horror story foster homes. It\xE2\x80\x99s amazing how far she\xE2\x80\x99s come and with such confidence in her ability. Emotions are volitile and when Zoey crashes, it\xE2\x80\x99s brutal and hard. Zoey learns to trust and open her heart when she least expects it. Sarcastic, short-fused and prone to flying fists, Zoey is a take charge, risk-taker that shields her emotions with her words and dirty street fighting.

Zoey and Ryker have killer chemistry. The violent, explosive kind that leaps off the pages and pushes the story forward in a series of lust and unfulfilled desire. The angst is a drug that will leave you feeling tipsy and dissatisfied but thirsting for more. They\xE2\x80\x99re aggressive, angry, they throw punches and insults but the heat is constant. Despite a lifetime of learned hatred for their opposing species, their mutual loss and hardheaded tendencies bring them together.

Sprig is hilarious. The pervy little sprite is energetic, daring and completely adorable with his honey addiction and off-kilter TV references. It\xE2\x80\x99s easy to fall in love with his spirit and playfulness even though he\xE2\x80\x99s a constant source of disruption that effectively blocks the culmination of Ryker and Zoey\xE2\x80\x99s feelings. The frustration is INTENSE.

The violence is extreme. The bloodshed is extensive and graphic, deaths come fast and action scenes escalate so quickly it\xE2\x80\x99s hard to keep up. The story is fast-paced and moves even though here are lags the danger is ever-present.

The story does contain triggers. Zoey\xE2\x80\x99s past is dark, full of heartache and abuse but it is not really detailed, more suggestive than blunt. There are a few scenes that feature assault. I appreciated that the author included just enough without flashbacks.

Variety of fae and powers was quirky and inventive. Each character, no matter how small or fleeting has unique features and dominant traits. They\xE2\x80\x99re all memorable and that\xE2\x80\x99s quite a feat.

CONS:
Relationships and love, whether it be sisterly or sexual were a huge part of what made Zoey tick and yet, the back story was abrupt and felt insignificant to grasp their connection. Yes, you could feel the love and longing but it wasn\xE2\x80\x99t as poignant as it could have been.

Zoey\xE2\x80\x99s life as a collector and what they do as an organization was missing its history for most of the plot. product_title: His Secret Child
review_headline: Good if you like abusive women-hating jerks
review_body:
Jordan Silver is really all over the place. I\x27ve written 5 star reviews for her books and 2 star reviews. If I wrote reviews of her Pregnancy Affair series, they would be 1 stars. I don\x27t know what to make of her. Moreover, she repeats story lines. This plot is identical to her Deception book. So she plagiarized herself.
She can also step over the line to outright misogyny and that\x27s just not okay. The H in this book slaps and chokes the h. Cord believes it\x27s okay to be abusive because Zania left him years ago. Really? What are you, like twelve? How about asking, \x5C\x22Why did you leave me?\x5C\x22 before you smack her? And he\x27s abusing a woman who is obviously weak, desperate, and afraid. Geez, I cringed. Then he finds out that she was pregnant when she left him and they have a child together that is now sick. Apparently, that\x27s another reason for his unrelenting abuse.
Then there is the story line of having another child to save their first born. What doctor would suggest that? And why would they consider it without even thinking about the fact that they\x27re bringing another child into the world? Yes, later on Cord has a bit of a breakdown and a conversation with himself about having another child. But, why wouldn\x27t that have happened sooner and why didn\x27t Cord and Zania have this conversation together? Just creepy. And the angry sex just creeped me out further.
Cord really never redeems himself in my eyes. When he finds out the real reason why Zania left him, there\x27s not much of an apology for his behavior and he scolds her for believing his mother and not talking to him before she left. That\x27s it? No groveling? This is so not an alpha male. In fact, he\x27s a momma\x27s boy, an unfeeling, selfish, abusive, spoiled brat. Yuck.
The women in this book are not much better. They are portrayed as the worst sexist stereotypes: Zania is weak and acts like a doormat. Cord\x27s mother is a money-grubbing, controlling witch. Cord\x27s girlfriend, Camille is a clingy, pushy, social climber. There is no one to like here. To readers, I would say... pass on this.cial climber. There is no one to like here. To readers, I would say... pass on this.

product_title: Dungeon Code: A Fantasy Tabletop Role-Playing Game
review_headline: Unique Take on a Crowded Category
review_body:
I can\x27t speak with too much authority, as my experience with role playing games is mostly limited to good ol\x27 D+D, but Dungeon Code seems to me to be a unique take on the genera; in fact, it solves a lot of the things I didn\x27t like about D+D.

First, Dungeon Code doesn\x27t get bogged down in minutia. It\x27s not about players and GM\x27s citing rules. The system is based around FUN. The player and GM have a fair amount of latitude to make sure the game is fun and that the rules don\x27t drag things down. This is done more by creating a game framework to play from rather than an endless pool or regulations based on every possible situation.

Second, the combat system is something I\x27ve never seen before, but is kind of cool. You roll a lot more dice hoping to get certain numbers that "unlock" your opponent. This is more interesting than the "You miss." "You hit for 10 pts damage." "You miss." kind of thing you find in a lot of roll playing. I don\x27t want to say it\x27s like Farkle or Yahtzee, because it\x27s not, but it has that thrill because lots of dice can be involved and you\x27re looking to get certain numbers. It also has a kind of Risk thing going, whereby as you lose power you get less dice. Overall, I think it\x27s a lot more thrilling system than what I\x27m used to. It\x27s fast and fluid.

I\x27m not usually into magic user types, but the magic system is better in this game, too. Rather than have a "book of spells" to pick from, characters have a lot more flexibility to come up with unique spells that fall into broad categories. This way, rather than being limited, the wizard is limited only by his/her imagination. Of course, it gets harder to pull of some spells than others (which allows the GM to keep things in check,) and some spells even come with risk.

Overall, this is a good system for anyone who wants to quickly learn a great role-playing system and get playing right away. It favors people with imagination and the ability to tell a good story. It wouldn\x27t be as interesting to someone who is really into having everything spelled out for them, or having a bible of rules to refer to. Of course, I\x27m glad, because those aren\x27t the kind of people I\x27d want to play with anyway!

review_body:

When Donny and Kellen went to each set of their parents to give them the news, each set wanted them to get an abortion. Kellen decided tht she would never have anything to do with either set. Donny went to one last party, he said, but he also took OxyContin, which killed him. Kellen was devastated and thought she could never live with this. She got a job at the local hospital as a receptionist and had several girl and boy friends who worked there also. Donny\x27s buddy, Cade, decided he wanted Kellen to become his girlfriend and he would help to pay for some of the articles the coming baby would need, but Kellen was not attracted to him.
A new obstetrician, Dr. Brent, good looking, personable, took up residence at the local hospital, thereby meeting Kellen and became her physician. He was totally attracted to her, and helped her all he could, but took it easy because he didn\x27t want to frighten Kellen off. The story is filled with mysteries like stalkers, unknown callers, somebody writing obnoxious names about her on her apartment doors and cars. Kellen had a most difficult time attempting to decide how to live her life, especially with the new baby coming.
This was an interesting plot, it moved along fairly slowly, but the reader can\x27t help but empathize with Kellen and as she considered her choices. I was given a complimentary copy of the e-book for an honest review.

product_title: The Matchmaker: An Amish Retelling of Jane Austen\x27s Emma (The Amish Classics)
review_headline: The best of Sarah Price\xE2\x80\x99s novels to date.
review_body:
This is a wonderful retelling of Jane Austen\xE2\x80\x99s Emma- the plot of this classic novel seamlessly overlays onto Amish culture, ensuring a wonderful story for any reader.

Price\x27s Emma is, by turns, amusing and irritating, just as in the original. Her father is a great character- IMHO a better part of the plot than in Austen\x27s story. And Gideon is.... well, as wonderful as any of either Austen\x27s or Price\x27s heroes can be.

As with all of Ms. Price\xE2\x80\x99s novels, I do wish they were 100+ pages longer. I enjoy the characters so much that I\xE2\x80\x99d rather spend more time with them than we are given in her books. In particular, I do wish we could have spent more time watching the romance between Emma and Gideon unfold- or if not the romance itself, the awareness and jealousy start to build in Emma. The high point of the plot \xE2\x80\x93 Gideon\xE2\x80\x99s declaration- came too quickly for my taste.

Price\xE2\x80\x99s Harriet is both too confident and too diffident by turns, and is quite an amusing character. I missed the real buffoonery of the original Mr. Collins, but the softening of the character fitted the Amishness of the plot.

I eagerly look forward to the next Sarah Price novel- they are idylls in a kinder world, filled with friends I\xE2\x80\x99d love to have in my own life.

I was given a copy of this novel for an honest review for free. No money was exchanged. But I would have paid for it anyway-its really that good.

review_body:
I waited to write this review since I joined the Take Me With You blog tour. I was really hoping that after reading both books, that I would have appreciated and liked Take Me For Granted a little more. Sadly, that didn\x27t happen.

I am struggling with my rating of this book. I am disappointed in my disappointment in this series. Kyla has managed to write some great books in the past, but this series just isn\x27t her.

Take Me For Granted introduced us to Grant and Aribel. The elements are there. Rock Star. Bad Boy. Strong-Willed Female. In all honestly, the start of the this series fell flat. The characters were not likable or relate-able. I didn\x27t like either of them. Maybe it\x27s the character development, maybe it\x27s the characters themselves? I am not sure.

Take Me With You was no better. We got more of these characters. Neither character seem to grow. The story line itself isn\x27t really that attention getting. Maybe it\x27s that the rock star books are over told? Maybe this story itself isn\x27t original enough? I really am not sure.

Now you are probably wondering if these books didn\x27t do anything for me, why 3 stars? Well.... these books aren\x27t bad books. They are average for their genre. The writing isn\x27t bad. It\x27s average. Many seem to love these books, many are in agreement with me. I think I expected much more from these books since the author has delivered so much more in her previous books. Basically, for me, these books are just average books. I am not screaming over the mountain tops that everyone must read. I am not saying that they aren\x27t worth reading. I think these books are more subjective to being liked or disliked depending on what one generally likes.

product_title: Flawed (The Butcher Book 1)
review_body:
I am not even sure what to say. This is one f-ed up story, that\x27s for sure! I loved every second of it! I am still kind of trying to wrap my head around this one...

I will start with Lacey. She is one of those characters that you think you should maybe dislike on some level but should like on another level. She definitely is a strong and weak character in this story. It takes talent to create such a complex character. Between her being the glue always holding the family together no matter how they treat her and the power Knox seems to hold over, she is both strong and weak at the same time.

Then we have Knox. He is a no nonsense killer. He feeds off of the thrill and calm of butchering people. What\x27s not to love, right? But I find myself liking him. No matter what horrible thing he does, I still like him. He was trained to be the man he is. He knows nothing else. He allows nothing else. Somehow Lacey is under his skin in an instant.

I got lost in this story for a few days. I took my time with it. I am glad I did. This is one of those stories that you need to make sure you soak everything in. I was appalled, thrilled, sickened, angry, sad... I think I went through a whole rainbow of emotions while reading this book!

product_title: Written in My Own Heart\x27s Blood: A Novel (Outlander, Book 8)
review_headline: Better Than Echo in the Bone ***SPOILERS***
review_body:
First off; honestly I liked this book better than the last one (#7, Echo in the Bone? Blah...whatever), but that is kind of damning with faint praise. I should add here too, that I have spent a good third of my life nearly obsessed with Jamie and Claire, completely in love with them...until Fiery Cross, that seems to be the point where her editor must have lost his/her balls and decided that he/she no longer needed to tell Herself, Lady Diana Gabaldon to KNOCK IT OFF with the massive, and largely masturbatory descriptions of the minutest of detail! (Mark Twain is rolling in his grave along with Hemingway).

Brevity is the soul of wit Dr. Gabaldon -- do try to keep that in mind, I\x27m afraid we\x27ll have another Dark Tower Debacle on our hands if you don\x27t wrap this up soon (Remember when Stephen King almost died, and all of us Dark Tower fans nearly lost it because he\x27d die before he could tell us what happened Roland? No? No DT fans here then? Oh well.)

That being said: there were parts of the book I adored. In fact, it almost seemed like she had returned to form: the humor, the fleshing out of new characters (Mrs. Figg, Fanny, I enjoyed Claire\x27s relationship to His Grace, Hal as well. I love snarky Claire), I even liked the gross eyeball surgery. I love love love Brian Fraser and I especially enjoyed seeing Dougal again from a different perspective. All in all, I\x27d say that I loved a good 2/3 of this book.

Now, for the other 1/3...I agree with other reviewers, enough with the rape for the love of all that is holy! I get the feeling that Colonial America/Scotland/England was the equivalent of South Africa with the amount of rapes happening all over the place. Maybe it was, however, when it happens to every character in the story, it loses dramatic impact and I cease to care. (I found myself not really caring about Claire being gang raped in the last book, and later felt disgusted with myself for not caring.
That brings me to Captain(?) Harkness--Oh good gracious me! A Captain of His Majesty\x27s Dragoons! Is a pervert and a sexual sadist and a pedophile! Where have I heard that before?
Ahem
Then we have Brianna and Roger, being separated again...another RAPE ATTEMPT in the 20th century (at this point my eyeballs got stuck, and I had to have eyeball popping out surgery to fix it, just like Lord John because my eyerolling was acute). Chase Chase Chase, misinformation ... Chase Chase Chase ... Brianna is a strong woman ... la la la ... This reminds me of something...Oh yeah, it was written about ten years ago with the same exact characters!
And seriously, are the Scottish police that inept? I watch a lot of British television, and it seems to me that they take child kidnappings just as seriously as we do here in the U.S.
Or maybe the Inverness police department is led my Mr. Bean. He\x27s British.
But not Scottish.
Or should it be Detective Inspector Bean?
Let\x27s get back to Brianna shall we? I guess she whined and moaned for four 1000 page books about how much she detested living in the past. Bitched about it constantly. Fantasized about toilet paper.
Now she\x27s back!

Naw, I\x27m glad Jamie\x27s got his weans back. He needs his family. But only if Brianna will shut up. She and Willie are the bitchiest people in this series.
I want to smack their bums.

Honestly, I liked the way it ended. It could conceivably be an ending to the series "just in case" you know? In case I get hit by a car tomorrow, because George R.R. Martin doesn\x27t seem to care about me, or whether I get to see Arya grow up.

To wrap up, in summary, too much ego stroking sensory descriptions. I get it, move on. I liked that I wasn\x27t deluged with battle scenes, they stress me out. Too much rape. And I\x27m tired of men wanting to suckle on nursing mothers, I was a nursing mother once and that\x27s just unsanitary. I don\x27t want a nasty man\x27s dental carries in my baby\x27smouth thank you very much!
I did cry, twice. Rollo and Henri-Christian to be precise and I haven\x27t cried at these books since Drums of Autumn. (Why did she have to kill him though? Sometimes I think she\x27s got some prejudices or biases that she\x27s not aware of).

Better than the last one, but it doesn\x27t even rank with the first three. All in all, her original plan was for two trilogy sets: Old World Trilogy and New World Trilogy. I wish she would have stuck with that, because she could have wrapped up the entire revolutionary war and not lost a bit of plotting.

product_title: Nemesis: The Search for Orion
review_headline: A good enough story for the average 13-14 year old
review_body: This just isn\x27t a book suitable for an adult.  The book is based on two superhuman genetic constructs that become telepathic and able to regrow themselves from a single finger with all of their knowledge and memories completely intact.  They go from one totally implausible and completely impossible adventure where they defeat increasingly evil and unbelievably numerous enemies to get even more ridiculous victories over more and more and more even more powerful enemies.  In the end they live happily ever after and the entire universe is at peace due to their efforts.  The writers of the 1940-50 era would die of envy.  Those old writer\x27s couldn\x27t have even imagined such a ridiculous story line.  Oh well, I suppose it was at least vaguely amusing.  It must have been!  If it wasn\x27t I can\x27t think of a good enough reason that could explain why I actually read both books in the series. Two stars is so generous that I will never understand why I bothered.

product_title: LOL #3 Romantic Comedy Anthology - Volume 3 - 16 All-New Romance Stories by Bestselling Authors (LOL Romantic Comedy Anthology Box-set)
review_headline: Review for \x22It was Always you\x22 by Brenna Aubrey - a short, quick, sensual read.
review_body:
I received a copy of the anthology from Brenna Aubrey in order to provide an honest review.
Her novel was "It was Always you" a Gaming the System short story and when she said it was a \x27sensual\x27 read...boy did she mean sensual.

Michaela and Jeremy have been friends since they were kids, but circumstances have kept their true feelings at bay. Mac thought he had no interest and didn\x27t pursue him. But their friendship was soon rekindled when Jeremy came back to town to work for Draco. When Jeremy finally had the courage to ask his best friend\x27s sister out, he found out that she was with someone else. Now that Mac was out of a relationship, Jeremy had since then been scooped up by Mac\x27s roommate.

Tensions run high between these two friends who are trying SO HARD not to ruin their friendships. But Mac\x27s patience runs thin after being stuck with Jeremy and Tiffani during a trip to a cabin in the mountains. It must suck being in Mac\x27s position...trying so hard to move on and forget Jeremy. It was a delicate situation and not one to be taken lightly.

At first I thought Tiffani was really annoying and the sort of girl I wanted to punch in the face...
But later on she proved to be a strong, independent woman, who was actually a lot more grounded than I thought she\x27d be.

The romance scenes were DEFINITELY steamy and sensual and I loved every minute of it.
I hope everyone gives this anthology a chance, especially if you want something quick to read during this awful winter.

5/5 Hearts of Love

review_headline: A story of finding love, seeking revenge and great for a rainy day read...
review_body:

This is a great book for a rainy day or if you want to enjoy a quick read. It is a western romance like this author\xE2\x80\x99s other books I\xE2\x80\x99ve read. This is a story of romance, revenge, and some action and adventure. I didn\xE2\x80\x99t read Ms. Woolf\xE2\x80\x99s first book in the series but you can definitely read this book without having read the first book. It is a stand alone novel.
The characters in this book Sam and Cassie have great chemistry. Sam is a former Texas Ranger that visits his friends\xE2\x80\x99 horse ranch. Sam is looking for revenge in this story as he is searching for the man that killed his wife and two daughters. Cassie meets Sam while Sam is visiting his friends\xE2\x80\x99 ranch. Cassie and Sam both are widowed and seem to have instant chemistry.
Cassie needs a foreman so Sam helps her out on the ranch. Sam is tracking the killer and wants the killer to find him. Does Cassie open her heart to Sam to find love after losing her husband, does Cassie\xE2\x80\x99s children take a liking to Sam, does Sam find his wife\xE2\x80\x99s killer or does the killer find Sam first or does Sam get his revenge? Sam will never get back his family but maybe he will find love with Cassie and her children. Read this book to find out! It is a great read if you enjoy a western romance, action and drama. Ms. Woolf has done it again. I cannot wait to read book 3 in the series.

product_title: Never Too Late: Your Roadmap to Reinvention (without getting lost along the way)
review_headline: Been waiting for this one! Great references, help and encouragement!
review_body:
Claire Cook is amazing! This really is a great read no matter what part of endless middle age you are in! I have been reinventing myself for a lifetime as life as a single mom raising two boys on little money and the many moves required to sustain us. Now that they are grown I find I still have to do it as I feel I haven\x27t yet created the real me and/or some kind of lasting legacy that I actually was here participating in life. I am an overcomer, but the way she describes putting one foot (page) in front of another has somehow escaped me until this point. Survival seemed so crisis oriented and so urgent for so many years, long term goals never seemed to be anything but pipe dreams.
Starting a ministry for single moms and a support group to help them choose a road they want to travel toward a destination they want to see is a dream I want to realize in my lifetime. I loved how many of her reinvention stories offered that hope to single moms because they offer proof that many have done just that! Thank you Claire! I will be recommending this book to others to whom the road looks long and looming, as it offers a bright light to guide them. I couldn\x27t put it down and the insight and guideposts were many and specific. Bravo brave lady! thank you for finishing it. Makes me wonder if anyone is waiting for the book I haven\x27t written as I have been waiting for yours.
This one goes on my nightstand (even if it weren\x27t in my Kindle!).

product_title: Harper\x27s Bride
review_body: I just re-read this wonderful story and realized I hadn\x27t sent a review for the author. I loved the story all over again. My favorite genre is Historical Western Romance and this hit the target with the "western" being the Alaska Yukon gold era. It was different to be in Alaska and realize that was way before it was part of the United States. The late 1800\x27s were rough in those areas were the gold was sought and the men were not kind to women. Many family men left to seek gold and the family was left behind to struggle on their own. So often the father/husband never returned; either he was dead or shamed and often filled his life with being drunk. In this book, Melissa was abused by her father and then by her husband who hit her and starved her and the baby, Jenny.  Her husband had debts he couldn\x27t pay so he "sold" her to the local merchant who could see she led a harsh life. Melissa lived over the store with Dylan, raised her baby, cared for the house and did laundry for the local miners. She made money and worked unbelievably hard trying to pay Dylan what her husband owed and having money for her future. They all returned to separate lives in Oregon where they started new lives. It is a book worth your time and I\x27m sure you will love it.

The recipes are for TWO people (not sure if this was clarified) - so there were lots of leftovers.  Every day.  Also, some of the recipes required ingredient preparation the day before, which I didn\x27t realize and sometimes I had zero time to prepare, so I had to skip those. product_title: Moe Manifesto: An Insider\x27s Look at the Worlds of Manga, Anime, and Gaming
review_headline: \x22Mo\xC3\xA9 is Love, Mo\xC3\xA9 is Life\x22, explains this wonderful book.
review_body:
I really love the fact that a book like this exists, and is so well written out of passion. This is a topic that completely befuddles many of my anime loving friends because they view "true" anime lays only within the physical drama of a story. For me though, I had been seeing the word "Moe" show up even more frequently as of late. Early descriptions of its meanings lead me to believe that Dorthy R. from the anime, "Big O" was "Moe", but I didn\x27t know why. I couldn\x27t recreate the reasoning behind the decision.

I first saw this book during some tumblr scrolling and the cover caught my attention. There were a few lines of a review for it but it didn\x27t keep my interest long. Then, I finished watching Oreimo, and had also fallen in love with the pop idol, Hatsune Miku within the same year. While looking up manga here on Amazon it was suggested to me and I knew who Kirino Kousaka was this time and needed more of her in my life.

Waiting for Christmas to come, I added this wonderfully insightful book to my wishlist. I think my favorite part of this book is all the different view points on the same topic. By no means am I an anime historian as I was really late to the anime game, like Cowboy Bebop on Adult Swim late. By the way, Cowboy Bebop, great anime. Back on topic, this book really brings home my favorite type of writing, researching. Researching is where answer come from because it allows the reader to formulate their own questions to all the information being provided.

This book isn\x27t going to tell you what, "Moe" means, instead it shows you how time and personal experience can simply allow one find their own way of expressing and experiencing their own, "Moe". Though, that isn\x27t to say you won\x27t leave unable to explain to your confused friends just why you keep saying, "Moe" towards your favorite girl within their "serious" anime.

product_title: Love Letters to the Dead
review_headline: beautifully written, moving coming-of-age story with too much melancholy overload
review_body:
She writes about starting high school, navigating new friendships, falling in love for the first time, learning to live with her splintering family.

So maybe I am too old for Young Adult high school stories. Been there, done that. No need to relive the first day in a new school. I actually had quite a lot of them, as my parents really moved a lot through Europe. Not only staying in front of a new class uncountable times (which was always embarrassing), but also in a new city and sometimes even in a whole different country complete with having to learn a new language and adapt to a different culture. So this specific storyline did nothing for me. I just can\xE2\x80\x99t read any more about insecure girls trying to fit in.

My second misgiving with this book was that it was so damn depressing. First, you have all those dead people the letters are addressed to, like Kurt Cobain, Jim Morrison, Amy Winehouse, Janis Joplin, River Phoenix and Judy Garland which is all kinds of morbid. Laurel writes letters to deceased celebrities, people that died tragically, in most cases young, in some because of drug overdose. I was crying my eyes out when I read the letters to Kurt Cobain and River Phoenix. But all this melancholy when reading about River Phoenix and Curt Cobain combined with a tragically dead older sister, a tragically split up family and the perpetual feeling that something absolutely tragic happened that night when Mia died and you have the most miserable and sad book ever.

Even Laurel falling in love for the first time was drowned out by the myriad insecurities, her constant dealings with Mia\xE2\x80\x99s death and the consequences on her and her entire family\xE2\x80\x99s life.

Whatever misgivings I have because of personal reasons I cannot deny that Ava Dellaira writes beautifully. But there were also letters where I didn\xE2\x80\x99t feel any connection to, like the author put some name of a dead celebrity there because she had to. For example she leaves the century completely when she writes a letter to John Keats. Allen \xE2\x80\x9CRocky\xE2\x80\x9D Lane (Mr. Ed) is beyond my German upbringing (movies and TV series here are dubbed with German speakers). Amelia Earhart, American aviation pioneer, didn\xE2\x80\x99t ring a bell either and I never read anything by Elizabeth Bishop. And even if that is a minor point: but all those people she writes to are white. Where are all the black dead superstars like Tupac Shakur, Jimi Hendrix, Billie Holiday, Toni Morrison and even if he is not dead Muhammad Ali?

Next misgiving: This book is really slow going. This might have something to do with the epistolary stile in which the story is told as each letter describes only one small aspect of Laurel\xE2\x80\x99s life and is instead full of her childhood memories, reflections and of course always small hints as to what happened to her sister Mia. I have to admit I am not a big fan of this writing letters stile. Again depression overload.

review_body: If you do not like spoilers stop reading now!  If you are looking for a romantic story keep looking.  If you are looking for a story about a dumb wife and how she messed up her marriage you might like this book.  This is a story about a wife who is a self absorbed witch spelled with a capital B. review_headline: Maybe not Suflete Pereche...but definitely Prieteni Buni...
review_body:
A SOLID 3.5 STARS

When I sat down to read this book, I asked myself... Is this going to be just another vampire story? After finishing it, I would have to say yes and no. The author does offer us a slightly different take of the cliched creatures. The story is told from the POV of the protagonist, Anastasia Trent; a jaded, 50-something, married woman that works in IT and moonlights as a bartender. Faced with losing her day job, among other struggles of the human condition, Annie picks up all the shifts she can at the bar called The Exchange, where she meets our night-loving gentle man, Domn. This unexpected meeting sparks a series of changes that has Annie\x27s life apart at the seams.

First of all, I need to say that I love vampire stories. It really doesn\x27t matter what aspects of the myths are changed, I\x27m game. To me, the stories that humanize vamps are as interesting as the ones vilify or heroize. I liked the the overall concept that the authors gives us, not only the vampire side but the smothered mood of Annie\x27s quiet desperation.

With that being said, I didn\x27t really fall for the characters as much as I wanted to. The leading lady is older than I am, and while normally I can empathize with the characters that are very different from myself, I found it hard to do with Annie. I don\x27t fault the author for that really, I just found it hard to keep up the fluctuating logic and emotion she takes us through.

Then, there\x27s Domn. He is our 800-year-old \x27gentle man.\x27 In the beginning, I saw potential in his soft-spoken, antiquated manner and had hoped that he would develop into something swoon-worthy (even though his physical description didn\x27t do much for me...but hey, different strokes, right? I just imagined Johnny Depp and kept reading), but for me it just didn\x27t pan out.

The best parts of this book for me were in the fun and snarky tone the writer set throughout the story. I found myself chuckling at some of the quips and sarcasm Annie throws down. The worst part for me was the romance between Annie and Dom. It was hard for me to follow, since I didn\x27t feel the connection between the two. It was almost like Annie didn\x27t feel anything at all for him...but she kept letting him bite her? Didn\x27t quite add up for me. I kind of have the feeling that the age gap between myself and Annie has something to do with my feelings on the love connection here, it\x27s hard to say.

Despite my slight lack of swoonage, I really did enjoy this read. The author definitely has a gift for the written word and an awesome imagination. review_headline: Well-written crime thriller that just doesn\x27t stand out.  It\x27s okay.
review_body:
I sort of feel like the odd man out here. I did read one other three star review, but wondering why they gave it three stars, as they seemed to have liked it a lot. Don\x27t get me wrong. This is not a bad review. I just thought the book was okay. It was well-written and the characters were well-drawn. It\x27s just that, for a thriller, it wasn\x27t all that thrilling. The therapy sessions were authentic enough and the theme of post traumatic stress disorder a good one, and a device that gives reality to the story. But you knew the serial killer from the beginning of the book. I never found myself at the edge of my seat, or dying to get back to reading this. It was like a hundred other thrillers. You know who\x27s going to win in the end. That is a given. No surprises there. And when you find out the killer\x27s past that made him this way, that was not particularly surprising either. I must say, I was taken with Zoe\x27s gumption and feistiness. I\x27m sure it\x27s hard to write a thriller that is very different from all the rest. One way would be to keep the villain a mystery until the end and make it a real twist - someone you would never have guessed. This is a well-written crime story that, to me, just doesn\x27t stand out, save for the PTSD theme. If that is of real interest to you, add one star. The title was also a good choice.

One addition to my review. I was not happy with the less than adequate protection Zoe received from the police, for a clear victim and person in danger from a serial killer. Could they really be this careless?
