I didn\xE2\x80\x99t do that, I chose to think of here and now. The \xE2\x80\x9Cnormals\xE2\x80\x9D in the book don\xE2\x80\x99t know about the vampyrs so it could easily be here and now that this book is taking place.

The story revolves around the vampyrs, and special families of humans, known as the saborese. Certain children of the saborese are born with a special birth mark and are known as sabors. The blood of the sabors is coveted by the vampyrs and sabors are treasured. Vampyrs live on bagged blood, rather than hunting \xE2\x80\x9Cnormals\xE2\x80\x9D. The only exception to bagged blood for most of the vampyrs is the hope of sampling the blood of the sabors.

Tyrell Small is the fifth child born to his parents. The first four were all born saborese, but Tyrell is born not only with the birthmark, but also with a caul. The first sabor ever born with a caul in vampyr/saborese history. No one knows what it means. We quickly learn that Tyrell is the child of two saborese families, his father\xE2\x80\x99s family, the Lupescu family changed their name to Small when they immigrated to the US. His mother\xE2\x80\x99s family, the Dragomir family changed their name to Crist when they fled Romania, also settling in the US. There is a vast difference between the two families. The Lupescu/Small family embraces the saborese/vampyr relationship, the Dragomir/Crist family have been fighting it for generations.

When Tyrell is born, his mother flees from the \xE2\x80\x9Cmonster\xE2\x80\x9D that she sees him as, taking his brothers and sisters and disappearing with her extended family. Tyrell is left with his father, who raises him and eventually breaks the news that he is a sabor, along with all that that entails. When he tries to run away after hearing the news, he crawls out on the roof to find Adam Dasani waiting for him. Adam is a vampyr, the vampyr that has been watching over Ty since he was born.

It wouldn\xE2\x80\x99t be a vampyr story if there wasn\xE2\x80\x99t also a bad vampyr. In this book that bad vampyr is a \xE2\x80\x9Cmade\xE2\x80\x9D vampyr instead of a \xE2\x80\x9Cborn\xE2\x80\x9D vampyr. The guy thinks he should be the Rege (King) of the Vampyrs because he was a Duke in Spain before he became a vampyr. He has created some of his own vampyrs who he mercilessly controls. They are rogue vampyrs and think nothing of feeding on the \xE2\x80\x9Cnormals\xE2\x80\x9D. What will happen when the Duke comes chasing Ty because he feels Ty is his \xE2\x80\x9Cdue\xE2\x80\x9D as the rightful king? What will happen when the \xE2\x80\x9Cnormals\xE2\x80\x9D find a graveyard full of corpses from the rogues feeding?

I really enjoyed the way the story unfolded, and the characters. One note, there really isn\xE2\x80\x99t much sex in the book. Part of being a sabor is the necessity to stay a virgin so that the blood stays pure. That was the only part of the story that I didn\xE2\x80\x99t really like. Ty having to stay a virgin forever didn\xE2\x80\x99t sit that well with me. I would have liked at least a little hot vampyr/sabor sex thrown in along the way\xE2\x80\xA6but that is just my opinion. That piece is the only thing which kept me from rating it a full 5.0 because otherwise the book is great.

I can\xE2\x80\x99t wait to see where the author goes from here with the storyline. The author tells me that there will definitely be several books in the series, which I\xE2\x80\x99m happy to hear. This is a great start to that new series. I look forward to the next book and I highly recommend this current book. Consider picking it up today!

The guy thinks he should be the Rege (King) of the Vampyrs because he was a Duke in Spain before he became a vampyr. He has created some of his own vampyrs who he mercilessly controls. They are rogue vampyrs and think nothing of feeding on the \xE2\x80\x9Cnormals\xE2\x80\x9D. What will happen when the Duke comes chasing Ty because he feels Ty is his \xE2\x80\x9Cdue\xE2\x80\x9D as the rightful king? What will happen when the \xE2\x80\x9Cnormals\xE2\x80\x9D find a graveyard full of corpses from the rogues feeding?

I really enjoyed the way the story unfolded, and the characters. One note, there really isn\xE2\x80\x99t much sex in the book. Part of being a sabor is the necessity to stay a virgin so that the blood stays pure. That was the only part of the story that I didn\xE2\x80\x99t really like. Ty having to stay a virgin forever didn\xE2\x80\x99t sit that well with me. I would have liked at least a little hot vampyr/sabor sex thrown in along the way\xE2\x80\xA6but that is just my opinion. That piece is the only thing which kept me from rating it a full 5.0 because otherwise the book is great.

I can\xE2\x80\x99t wait to see where the author goes from here with the storyline. The author tells me that there will definitely be several books in the series, which I\xE2\x80\x99m happy to hear. This is a great start to that new series. I look forward to the next book and I highly recommend this current book. Consider picking it up today!

product_title: Spoils of Olympus: By the Sword
review_headline: A compelling story and convincing reason to delve into historical fiction...
review_body:
First off, let me start by saying that while I am an avid reader of books in general, I would not have described myself as a \xE2\x80\x9Chistorical fiction guy.\xE2\x80\x9D I was initially compelled to read this book by a good friend of mine, to whom I am now indebted for convincing me to do so. I may, in fact, now have to amend my thoughts on historical fictions altogether. To that I give my thanks to that certain friend, and for whom I will also probably now have to buy at least one round at our next night of debauchery and debasement (or happy hour as some like to call it). You know who you are\xE2\x80\xA6

Let me say that my fondness for this story is not in particular to the style of writing, but instead to that which all true attachment to stories is \xE2\x80\x93 namely the adventure of the story and the writer\xE2\x80\x99s ability to pull you along into the fray. This story did exactly that for me. As a former soldier and a man (by some estimate\xE2\x80\xA6), I can certainly relate to the coming of age and indoctrination into something larger than yourself. This story unfolds in a way that is both believable and yet incredible at the same time. While you start by experiencing the usual youthful waste and sordid indiscretions of a post-adolescent juvenile male, you transgress into a maturity that comes only with the weight of responsibility which is carried with ownership.

The story starts with the main character, Andrikos, who steps into a world where his fanciful delusions of grandeur meet a harsh reality. After overcoming the shell-shock of his new world, he strives to meet a standard which few can attain or hope to keep, and very realistically manages to barely keep his head above water. While the initial journey is enticing in its own right, the real discovery of this story for me comes somewhere midway through the book. This is where Andrikos is met and taken under wing by the spymaster of his age and that of the remaining Armies of Alexander the Great, a man by the name of Vettias. This turn in the plot propelled the story into a new realm of spy versus spy, of deceit and manipulation which surely has some semblance of truth given that the craft is the world\xE2\x80\x99s second oldest craft. The way in which the events unfold after the turn in plot breathe new life into the story and make clear its destination which turn this book into one which makes me question my taste in genre.

While I could go on with my review of the story-line, I will resist the urge since I want each reader to discover the story for themselves. I definitely recommend this book as a weekend read for those people who are 1.) historical fiction fans, 2.) for those who want to immerse themselves in the ancient world of Alexander the Great, 3.) people who find stories of the man behind the mask intriguing, 4.) Anyone who loves spy versus spy novels and lastly 5.) For those people who simply love a good read. I know my foray into the heretofore unknown world of historical fiction has now, and forever on, been favorably altered so that I will now seek out new adventures in the historical fiction genre. Cheers to both the author for writing such a story on his first published novel and my friend for convincing me of its worthiness.

There are a few books that deserve to receive every top prize in reporting that can possibly be given. \xE2\x80\x9CChasing the Scream\xE2\x80\x9D by Johann Hari is one of them.

I came across this book as a result of an article in Huffington Post that cited some of Hari\xE2\x80\x99s main points concerning the \xE2\x80\x9CWar against Drugs\xE2\x80\x9D, and was immediately convinced that the book would be well worth reading. It is much more than a \xE2\x80\x9Cgood read\xE2\x80\x9D; it is a MUST READ for anyone who cares about the current incredible tragedies that are occurring world-wide as a result of probably the most dangerous and destructive conflict that has ever beset humankind.

I feel compelled to give a bit of personal background. I am a non-smoker and a person who has only occasionally in the course of my life indulged in drinking alcohol. My only experience of being drunk, as a freshman in college, was so distressing that I knew I never wanted a repeat. My parents were both smokers, but I soon discovered a smoke allergy that led to devastating headaches, and therefore was delighted when the mounting evidence of the harmfulness even of second-hand smoke led to the popular pressure to prohibit smoking in restaurants and other public places. However, I know and care about both smokers and drinkers, am descended from and related to alcoholics, and have had significant contact with marijuana smokers. My elder son died in a DUI-related single-car crash just before his 32nd birthday; his blood alcohol level was over twice the legal limit, and there were also \xE2\x80\x9Ctraces\xE2\x80\x9D of cannabis in his bloodstream at the time of autopsy.

A few other things need to be said, however: I believe that all \xE2\x80\x9CWar\xE2\x80\x9D is wrong, I am against capital punishment, I consider our current penal system in the US a total travesty of justice, and I cannot conceive how rational and intelligent people, with the lessons of Alcohol Prohibition fresh in their minds, could ever have gone the same route all over again with Drug Prohibition. Hari\xE2\x80\x99s brilliant narrative proves this point; the fact that he traces it back to a single bureaucrat, Harry Anslinger, is a huge accomplishment. If one man (mentally unbalanced and completely obsessive) could launch such horror on humanity, surely other less unbalanced and obsessive people can undo it!

Hari documents exhaustively (his end notes comprise over 25% of the text) the way in which this totally misguided prohibition of drugs (from marijuana to heroin, and everything in between) was based on hysteria, false information and basic greed. He describes a wonderful experiment done with rats (that was almost totally suppressed by the drug-war proponents) that thoroughly debunked the idea that addiction is related only to the \xE2\x80\x9Cchemical hooks\xE2\x80\x9D of various drugs; in fact, it is much more related to the life circumstances of the potential addict. Rats caged in isolation rapidly became so addicted to cocaine that they drugged themselves to death, but rats allowed to be in community cages with other rats, toys, interesting food, and so on essentially ignored the drug; indeed, formerly addicted rodents, when removed from isolation and put into the \xE2\x80\x9CRat Park\xE2\x80\x9D setting, rapidly and voluntarily stopped \xE2\x80\x9Cusing\xE2\x80\x9D.

Besides being extremely important and a clarion call to end the abusive war on drugs, Johann Hari\xE2\x80\x99s book is fascinating, and describes alternatives in brilliant narrative. He doesn\xE2\x80\x99t gloss over real problems, and his reporting is painstakingly balanced. product_title: Saving Margaret (Vegas Mates Book 2)
review_body:
I read the first book in this series of novellas a few weeks ago and really enjoyed it. Tried another free download in a different series by Ms. Shannan and struggled with it. When I returned to this series I was relieved to discover I enjoyed it as much as the first one\xE2\x80\xA6so it wasn\xE2\x80\x99t a fluke. I am already well into book three and this continues to be a winner for this author, for me at least.

The series did take a surprising turn though. I thought it was going to follow the group of sisters from the first story as they all found their mates. Sweet, but not that complex. What is it they say about assumptions\xE2\x80\xA6 Anyway. The story switched to Margaret or one of the Maggies, a friend of the original sisters. The action picks up right where the other story left off and we get to witness the pairing up of Margaret and Scott, a wolf and a bear.

The world is actually pretty well thought out and complex for such short stories. Often in novellas we don\xE2\x80\x99t get the kind of meat that this world has. There is quite a large supporting cast of characters, which will hopefully mean that there are plenty of stories to come. Only criticism I have here is that it was difficult at times to keep the characters straight, especially when you have a group of women that all share the same or similar name.

I liked the tension in this book, the pairing up of a wolf and bear was fun to read about. I loved the difference in personalities between the two types of shifters. Most can appreciate two vastly different families blending together and the antics or drama it would create. I loved Margaret\xE2\x80\x99s family and hope we get a chance to get to know Scotts.

We still have the mess of Sam\xE2\x80\x99s mom to clear up and there was some sad moments in this story. There is plenty left to work out in this world and I look forward to seeing how things play out.

product_title: Bound by Flames: A Night Prince Novel
review_headline: A bit darker, but still great!
review_body:
While I loved this book, I found myself having trouble connecting with it in the beginning. Perhaps too much time had passed since I read the last two books, or something about this one made me hold off giving it five stars like the other two in this spin-off series. Don\xE2\x80\x99t get me wrong I still love me some Vlad, and Leila too\xE2\x80\xA6 I am thrilled that Ms. Frost has decided to extend this series into another book. This whole world is a favorite of mine and I would be fine even with another spin-off series with cameos from beloved characters of past books.

Like I said this one took me a bit to get into. This could be from the sudden switch in genres, too long between books, or that the first 100 pages of this book were pretty dark and disturbing at times. I often wondered if I was reading a chick-lit paranormal title, this book was so graphic and violent at times. Granted much of it was recounting of events in flashbacks, but still, Ms. Frost sure did challenge my comfort zone in at least one occasion. I\xE2\x80\x99m glad I stuck with it though, like that was ever in question\xE2\x80\xA6, it was interesting to see how Leila and Vlad handled the events of this book even though it shook their marriage quite a bit.

There were some fun, lighter situations as well, especially in the epilogue. But much of this books was one crisis after another. You could see their marriage and relationship growing stronger with each new obstacle they encountered. I appreciated how their dynamic changed. In the beginning we have Vlad almost using wrapping Leila in bubble-wrap and storing her in the most secure local he can find, but by the end they had truly become a team and were kicking ass together.

There were some familiar faces that popped up in this book, my favorites Cat and Mencheres played important roles in this story and I was happy with the closure that came about for Maximus. I am intrigued by the new \xE2\x80\x98bad guy\xE2\x80\x99 that was introduced at the end of the book and look forward to seeing what plays out with him. This was a great read, a little darker than the others, but wow what a ride.

product_title: A Very Levet Christmas (Guardians of Eternity Book 14)
review_body:
I received a copy of this book from the publisher through Net Galley for an honest review.

Perhaps a little early for a Christmas story, but hey I don\xE2\x80\x99t get to pick the release dates or when they show up on Net Galley. This is one of the authors I enjoy and own most of her books. This was a sweet little addition to the series and the novellas that center around Levet are always such fun. He is the much-needed comic relief in a world that could become much too serious and heavy with out his quirky personality.

As with the other novella centered around Levet, this in not a love story for him. The story is the bringing together of Damon and Gia. Ivy has cleverly shared this story as a tribute or in the spirit of the Christmas Classic by Charles Dickens\xE2\x80\x99 \xE2\x80\x9CA Christmas Carol\xE2\x80\x9D. This will be a lovely tale to read around the holidays on a cold winter\xE2\x80\x99s evening, perhaps when you are stuck at home during a storm. It is quite short, only 55 pages for the story itself, and I was able to finish it in a couple of hours. We get to see a glimpse of character\xE2\x80\x99s from past novels in this world and are there to welcome Salvatore and Harley\xE2\x80\x99s new family to the world.

The story while fun on its own, is probably going to be appreciated by fans of the series more than those who are new to the series. There isn\xE2\x80\x99t much back story, so new readers might not know much of what is going on or the context of the events taking place. Still a fun read, and I\xE2\x80\x99m thankful for having been granted to privilege to read and review it before its release.

product_title: The Secrets of Julia Hawke
review_headline: Not sure about Julia herself. Still worth reading
review_body:
Julia Hawke arrives home in Brisbane after a long journey from Europe. She is met by her adult son, who does not seem pleased to see her. We\xE2\x80\x99re not told why she has been away. We do learn that no-one knew where she had gone, except her partner; and that while she was away, he collapsed with a heart attack and is on life support.

Bit by bit, facts emerge. Her partner\xE2\x80\x99s wife and his two daughters are at the hospital. They are even less pleased to see her. Her parents don\xE2\x80\x99t seem too keen either. In her absence \xE2\x80\x93 which seems to have been for some weeks \xE2\x80\x93 the cafe she runs has hit a crisis. And before she went away, she quarrelled with her best (perhaps only) friend, Raz.

But to find out how all this came about, we go back to Julia\xE2\x80\x99s teens \xE2\x80\x93 and that\xE2\x80\x99s when the book really gets into its stride as we follow Julia through her early adulthood, her friendship with Raz, and her partnerships, and see her make some monumentally bad decisions that have led her to the life she has the day she gets off that plane from Europe.

Brenda Cheers\xE2\x80\x99s The Secrets of Julia Hawke is a well-crafted piece of fiction. It gets four and not five stars from me for a couple of reasons. One is that Julia\xE2\x80\x99s most important secret is revealed too early; there\xE2\x80\x99s still plenty of plot to enjoy, but even so, it could have been held back. The other is that I couldn\xE2\x80\x99t like Julia herself that much. The problem isn\xE2\x80\x99t that she\xE2\x80\x99s made some missteps in life; people do, and they are understandable in the context of the story. But she seemed a bit soulless (at least, as an adult), and I didn\xE2\x80\x99t get a sense of warmth or humour. This raises the question of how much we need to identify with a lead character and root for them (or if it\xE2\x80\x99s an anti-hero, hope for them to fail). For me it\xE2\x80\x99s quite important for getting into a story.

Despite that, I thought The Secrets of Julia Hawke was enjoyable. It does tell a pretty human tale. Moreover Cheers is great at characterization; although Julia herself is a bit weak, the others were very believable. Raz is particularly interesting (and maybe her story could have been a bigger part of the book). Julia\xE2\x80\x99s husband, and her later partner, were also highly credible. You may not be able to identify with the main character all the time, but there are other people to care about. Moreover Cheers is a good plotsmith; the whole book\xE2\x80\x99s well set out and properly paced, and things happen in the order they should. Some scenes are very well done, in particular a sexual assault that is very important to the plot.

review_headline: The side characters could have been better developed, as well
review_body:
Although I certainly have bones to pick with this book, it has an interesting storyline and characters, and the dialogue s is believable (although there were far too many "Kane--"s). It was a story that kept me reading and made me want to come back to it when I had to put it down. What kept me from giving it 5 stars was the descriptions I often had to re-read to tell what was going on and the paragraph and sentence structures that were confusing as well. Sometimes there were misplaced phrases within a sentence, and sometimes it was unclear who was talking. All that re-reading to figure these things out, took me out of the story. The side characters could have been better developed, as well. I know there is more to this series, but that\x27s no excuse for not giving book one\x27s characters more depth. I found Bridget to be completely unbelievable, and after such an out-of-the-box story, the author resorted to a typical romance device of having Kane push Beth aside for a time, because he felt less than adequate. That was disappointing. I also think that Beth\x27s panic attacks were solved a bit too easily.

With all these things that bugged me, it would seem I should have rated the book lower, but I enjoyed the main characters\x27 interactions very much and most of the storyline was exciting and fresh. I would definitely read the next book in the series.

review_body:

product_title: Death Pope: Vol 1 & 2 (Death Pope, Black Flame)
review_body:
When the hapless teen protagonist Roberto is crowned Pope Hadrian and finds himself dropped into a web of shadows worthy of an Escher painting, oily backstabbers and greedy nobles come out of the woodwork to puppeteer him to their own ends. As I plowed through John Oakes\x27s new alternate-history adventure, DEATH POPE\x27s deceptively dry beginning turned out to be the first clues that this novel would prove to be a very highly-researched and smartly-written thriller.

The characterization, as is customary of Oakes\x27 novels, is top-notch. Every character is a well-realized human unto himself, making the Vatican seem to crawl with activity. The three characters closest to the reader, Roberto, Petruccio, and Cosimo, begin the book as a trio of carefree Italian boys that could have stepped straight off the pages of Romeo and Juliet; their personalities made me feel as if I were reading a novel decades if not centuries older than their author. A few of the older characters, like members of Roberto\x27s new papal cabinet, are a bit interchangeable, but the Italian names are so colorful that they stand out well and it\x27s easy to overlook.

The Vatican itself is a Hogwarts of detailed passageways, choked with every opportunity to stage an interesting scene--honestly, I never knew it was so expansive and easy to get lost in. It\x27s a testament to Oakes\x27s talent that I feel like I\x27ve finally been properly introduced to it, even after years of reading Dan Brown.

Where DEATH POPE really shines is the dialogue scenes. While Oakes\x27s previous outing THE RIGHT KIND OF STUPID was no slouch in the quality department, DP\x27s dramatic scenes were a shocking step up in maturity and complexity. Besides the obvious point that Oakes has had more practice, I point a finger directly at the amped-up authenticity: where TRKOS was made of stoner coming-of-age humor and barroom conversation, DP absolutely gleams with intricate political thumb-wrestling and the cadence of 16th century speech. I have absolutely no complaints here--like Martin\x27s books, DP said, "Here comes the airplane!" and spoon-fed me a helping of Mafia diplomacy I didn\x27t even know I wanted. Oakes must have spent a lot of late nights poring over ecclesiastical references and protocol documentation.

I won\x27t spoil the catalyst that finally switches the story into high gear, but it culminates in a caper sequence that\x27ll have any fan of Tarantino cheering and cackling like I did. I thought the book ended rather abruptly--it feels like the pilot episode of an HBO series--but if Oakes has his way, this won\x27t be the last one, and I\x27m very much looking forward to the rest of the series.century speech. But Marcia isn\x27t happy to see him for the fear of him finding out her secret she\x27s been keeping from him.
This story deals with domestic violence, as Brock grew up in a bad family environment and his response to it is something he still deals with throughout the book. The fear of turning into his abusive father has Brock set in his ways that children are something he\x27ll never want in life.
This story is about lost love being found again. The romantic gesture of still being in love with someone five years after having no contact with them, is a sweet love story for me. Brock wooed me through the entire book with his love for Marcia and his attempts at winning her back.
Playing without Rules has a great storyline, good in-depth characters and a nice flow. The only complaint I had was the over use of baseball analogies in awkward situations. Other than that, very good read.

product_title: The Confession: A Novel
review_headline: Roller-Coaster Ride that Flattens Out Toward the End and Kills the Initial Enjoyment
review_body:
Like many reviewers on there, I loved the first two sections of this book and hated the last section for many reasons; one being that it just seemed to drag on and on. The first two sections of the book were thrilling, entertaining, exciting, and made it nearly impossible to put the book down. Donte Drumm was sentenced to death for a murder he may not have committed; in another state Travis Boyette a man with a long rap sheet admits to a minister that he is the real killer. The story then twists and turns in a heart pounding page-turning that leaves you hoping they make it in time to stop the execution.
The main plot of the story is great and I loved it; there are a few secondary parts to the story that were a bit annoying to say the least. The fact that in Texas the whites and the blacks were completely against each other. Donte Drumm being black had all the support of the black community while the white people all believed he was guilty and should be executed. Grisham makes the white folk look very snooty in comparison to the black folk; and although most of the black folks in town are responsible for inciting riots and car bombings; when some white police officers try to break things up they are ones who are made to look bad. Its hard to not put some of your own personal beliefs into stories that you read; but I find it hard to believe that every single white person would be against Donte Drumm and every single black person would be on his side. I don\x27t doubt there would be some racial discord for the simple fact that a black man is accused of killing a white girl and we all know how that normally plays out; however, I believe there would be some white folks who believed him innocent or at least not want him executed and some black folk who believed he was guilty.
A lot of the third section seemed so politically driven that it made the rest of the story more unbelievable to me. Whether you are pro-capital punishment or against it, whether you believe in the justice system or not; it seemed the story was a bit far fetched no matter what side of the fence you sit on. I\x27m no legal expert and I\x27ve only done a little research into capital punishment, but I found the death sentence based on a single confession alone to be reaching. I don\x27t want to give away anything from the book, but it lost some of its steam in the final section. I think the book would have still made its point and been a great read had things been wrapped up in a concluding chapter or two; instead of going on and on.

Overall the book was a good read. John Grisham seems to produce books I either Love or Hate; this one was just so-so.

product_title: Primal Hunger (Paranormal Fantasy Romance) (Guardians, Book Three) by Valerie Twombly
review_body:
I was looking forward to reading Seth\x27s story, and I sure was not disappointed! With the curse slowly driving him to insanity, you know there had to be a good story behind how he became the way he is...and how he could be saved.

Kaitlyn is a very strong and smart female lead, and a good match to Seth\x27s equally strong, cunning and stubborn nature. The two of them together don\x27t quite click all the way for me, I think due to just how overly strong both their characters are. But thankfully for me that didn\x27t really take away from the overall story.

Now that we\x27re into the third book of the series, most of the secondary characters we\x27ve been reading about for a while, so they are all becoming even more well developed. And as we learn more and more about all of them, it makes you want to know all of their own stories even more (honestly, this series has the potential to go on for quite a while-a big plus for us readers!).

The story itself flows very well, and really does draw you in-I read this almost straight through. Lots of drama, lots of action, plus I really like in this series that not only are we getting the story from the male and female leads\x27 POV, but also from other characters. This helps not only to add depth to the individual stories, but also to the overall series. And you\x27re also going to get plenty of hot and steamy here-especially since there\x27s a lot of sexual tension built between Seth and Kaitlyn since he is resisting so strongly against them coming together as he tries to stave off the madness that is slowly taking him over.

My overall rating for Primal Hunger...4 solid stars!

product_title: Kill Your Boss (A John Lago Thriller)
review_body:
My edition has the title Kill Your Boss but it\x27s also called The Intern\x27s Handbook.
The concept is a good one - that young trained assassins are pretending to be interns (young unpaid trainees) in major firms in order to get close enough to a major business figure to kill that person and make it look like an enemy - mafia boss etc. - killed them. The narrator John is twenty-five, on his last case, when he starts the story.

The book has to be taken as a comedy or satire, with a higher body count than just about any thriller you\x27ve read, gadgets, weapons and Kevlar galore. I don\x27t know how legal it would be in Europe for someone to do unpaid work for six months, as it just seems like exploitation and especially in a high-rent city like New York people would find it hard to live. The bosses are all apparent sociopaths - maybe that\x27s how they get to be on top of a business - and of course the boss of the assassin firm, HR Inc, is as bad as any.

John sets out some rules such as "be forgettable" and manages to break them, untypically falling for a girl at the same firm. Obvious lying and double-dealing is going on all around him and he gives us a story of his upbringing laced with pathos and unpleasantness. Not for the squeamish, but I am sure we can all learn something from the tale, even if it\x27s just to be kind to new staff.

If anything Mr Johnson becomes a little too close to his subject and perhaps shows a mild bias in favor of later characters in the account whom he has had a chance to meet and get to know personally. He is even handed in his treatment of the ties to the CIA where I think many would be tempted to turn it into a diatribe against CIA meddling.

review_headline: Lots of potential but too long of a wait for book 2
review_body:
~3.5 stars~ The synopsis on this one had me sold. While I found the story to be enjoyable for the most part, nothing about it really stood out as a one of a kind/memorable read. It had a similar feel to numerous other books I\x27ve read in the past. So, here is my breakdown:

Pros:
* I like that the heroine was independent and strong willed
* Each character had so much depth

Cons:
* I\x27m not a fan of love triangles and this read had a lot of that - 2 men swooning over the same girl throughout the entire story
* This was supposed to be a YA Fantasy genre but it never really had a \x5C\x22fantasy\x5C\x22 feel to it, only young adult
* There were a lot of times where very little seemed to happen - for instance, when traveling from one region to the next, they camped, they rode, they camped, they rode, day after day, it made for some slow spells in this book.
* The ending left much to be desired - while I wouldn\x27t call it a brutal cliffhanger, it wasn\x27t one of those reads that leaves you feeling satisfied upon completion
* Way over-priced at its current listing price of $9.99

Overall, the writing was good, and this series does have a lot of potential. I would like to say that I will continue this series, but I seriously doubt that will happen. Book one was released in July 2014, but book 2 won\x27t be available until July 2015. A year between book releases is just absurd to me personally. This book was pretty good, but not good enough for me to even remember what all played out a year later.

product_title: Into Shadow (Shadow and Light Book 1)
review_headline: Great YA story for all ages
review_body:
With the verbal brush-strokes of a Renaissance artist, T.D. Shields crafts a vivid picture of a world two centuries in the future. Thousands of books are given such a setting, but it takes a skilled author to immerse us in that world without weighing the story down in descriptions.

Set in heart of the former United States after decades of global war and economic change, Into Shadow pulls you in immediately as we are introduced to nineteen-year-old Poppy Walker, the First Lady and daughter of the President, whose life takes a turn for the tragic after a violent coup leaves her without a home and running for her life.

But Poppy is no soft, spoiled aristocrat. Possessing a toughness and a resilience that belies her diminutive height, Poppy not only escapes to but is able to survive on her own in the shattered remnants of the city of Denver, a land beset by nasty animals, lethal vegetation and vicious street gangs.

I love stories with strong female characters, and Poppy is such a character. She\x27s tough, fiercely loyal, and takes crap from NO ONE. But she also displays a shy awkwardness and vulnerability that teenage girls will easily identify with and root for.

I would highly recommend Into Shadow to anyone who loves YA fantasy. The second half of Poppy\x27s story, Into Light, cannot come fast enough for me.

product_title: Worth the Risk (The McKinney Brothers, Book 2)
review_headline: 4.5 Stars! No risk at all, definitely a safe bet! Claudia Connor brought her \x22A\x22 game!
review_body:
My eyes could hardly keep up with how fast I wanted to read! I got Kindle burn, I couldn\x27t turn the pages fast enough! While I didn\x27t care for one particular aspect in Worth the Fall, the first book in this series, I still enjoyed it very much, but, Worth the Risk was pretty close to a perfect read for me.

Stephen and Hannah were a great couple, with amazing chemistry, even though they couldn\x27t have been more different. She has trust issues and he is dealing with demons, both stem from tragic events in their pasts. This common thread of heartache and sadness is what I feel draws them together, and the need on both their parts, to uncover the other\x27s secrets and help them heal.

The family element, something I\x27m partial to, was very strong in this book, and Hannah\x27s brothers added an extra layer of testosterone...more like four layers...they are extremely protective of her, but they have good reason and the best of intentions, even though at times it was a bit much.

She loved her four brothers, and she wouldn\xE2\x80\x99t say they suffocated her, though the hum of their hovering could be deafening at times. FBI, Special Forces, firefighter, cop. It was like her very own big-brother protection force.

There was plenty of dialogue, appealing characters, a unique setting, some misunderstanding, suspense, passion, and it all leads to a beautiful ending! So the way I see it, the author\x27s proved herself twice over and is getting better with each story she writes. Now Claudia Connor needs to write a Walker Brother\x27s series too! Wow...what an amazing spin-off series that would make! McKinneys and Walkers...that\x27s enough to give me a heart attack!

* A copy of the book was provided in exchange for an honest review*

product_title: Town in a Sweet Pickle (CANDY HOLLIDAY MYSTERY Book 6)
review_body:
Its the bicentennial edition of interim editor, Candy Holliday\x27s news paper in the town of Cape Willington, Maine. All this farming town is abuzz with excitement for a cook off that Candy and her Community Correspondent, Wanda are organizing and putting on. All the villagers are very anxious to see celebrity cookbook chef, Julia von Fleming be a judge at the event and appear at a book signing for her cookbook.

The Community Cook off begins and there\x27s a jar of pickles on one of the tasting tables and it seems out of place because there is a label on it and the entries are not allowed to be labeled. Since the label is from the Sweet Pickle Deli a deli that has since closed down. Everyone thinks that the pickles the the best thing since sliced bread and can\x27t get enough of them .

Not being able to resist Candy\x27s father\x27s friend, Ned eats one of the pickles and soon falls to his death. Other jars of pickles begin showing up around town and it claims another victim and makes others sick. Julia is convinced someone is out to get her after she almost comes close to biting the deadly pickle. The town in convinced that Candy will solve the mystery to find out who is behind the perished pickles and suspects and the towns secrets start to emerge even after Candy becomes a suspect herself.

This mystery is filled with small town charm. It was my first taste of this series and it had me craving these pickles, deadly or not. The Community Cook off had me as a self professed foodie hooked into the story. I loved the inside look into all the characters that live in this town that have made their farms their life and the country feel but not all of the residents lived peaceful, quiet happy lives as a few did have secrets that also made this a page turner to also wonder who the killer among them would be. I hope Candy will be organizing many of the towns festivities and hopefully all relating to food for many, many books to come in this gratifying series.eries.

product_title: Caught on Camera (The Davenports Book 1)
review_headline: Everything you want in a book and more! Pure enjoyment!!
review_body:
Vega Zaragoza is haunted by her past. Shamed by falling in love with the wrong man years ago, she has doomed herself to a life of loneliness. No real satisfaction in her job or her private life. She stays behind the camera as a videographer for a television station, never putting herself out there, always hiding behind the camera, baggy clothes, little or no makeup and always wearing her long beautiful hair up. She can\x27t be noticed. People can\x27t find out who she really is.

JP Davenport, high profile business man. On the fast track in politics, following in his father\x27s footsteps, climbing the political ladder maybe to the White House. Playboy, rich and not much of heart.

These two meet while Vega is on assignment for her television station. The sparks of electricity fly immediately between them. Vega is instantly attracted to JP, who wouldn\x27t be? But she is there to do her job, hopefully get a one on one "day in the life of" interview with him and nothing else. Furthering her career is priority. JP finds Vega intriguing, beautiful and sassy. He is attracted to her and will use her job as a way to spend more time with her. Anything to get what he wants right?

Caught On Camera is a book full of laughs, tears, romance and heart warming friendship. Vega and JP go on a journey that will take you from being angry, to happy in a turn of the page. I experienced all of these emotions through the entire book. I laughed lots, got mad, cried a bit, and went aw. Kim Law has never let me with her books, she always comes through.

I would recommend this book to anyone that enjoys a great story, full of emotion, friendship, romance and of course love. You won\x27t be disappointed at all.
Can\x27t wait to read the next in this series.

product_title: THE MIRACULOUS RESULTS OF EXTREMELY HIGH DOSES OF THE SUNSHINE HORMONE VITAMIN D3  MY EXPERIMENT WITH  HUGE DOSES OF D3 FROM 25,000  to 50,000 to 100,000 IU A Day OVER A 1 YEAR PERIOD
review_body: Just look at the title- The MIRACULOUS results (for someone that is desperately ill these words are too powerful) of EXTREMELY HIGH DOSES (I can\x27t think of more dangerous words)     Well, a lot of these reviews simply focus on Vitamin D so I\x27m going to do the same.  Fat soluble vitamins were meant to be taken together, not in isolation, and especially not in mega-doses in isolation.  Recommending that strategy is horrifically irresponsible.  Taking too much Vit E on it\x27s own will push Vit K out of your body.  Taking too much Vit D on it\x27s own will push Vit A out of your body.  This is why whole-food sources of fat soluble vitamins always contain Vit D with Vit A together, in the ratio that you need.  So if you need Vit D, please get it from a very high quality cod liver oil.  This way you don\x27t end up doing more harm to your body.    Also, a lot of information is coming out now that supposed Vit D deficiencies are actually Magnesium deficiencies, and the Vit D level is fine.  Read books like The Magnesium Miracle and Magnificent Magnesium for the full scoop.      PS - This Tony Clifton thing is hilarious. product_title: Fatal Scandal (The Fatal Series Book 8)
review_body: Having read all the seven books which came before this new addition to the series,  I can testify that this novel once again ,comes through, so to speak, for all of us who absolutely love these characters and the rock\x27em sock\x27em quality to their lives, both independently of one another and together.  Sam is once again that complicated mixture of passion and vulnerability covered over by her fierce loyalty to those she loves and with whom she works and seasoned with her complete irreverence for the expectations of polite society.  Her bond with Nick is as enduring as the granite of Yosemite\x27s El Capitan, her love for Scotty as protective as any grizzly bear mom, and the depth of her sense of justice knows no bounds.  Nick is amazing as her husband, her lover, and the father every kid would want.  And as is the case in all the preceding novels in this series, the action is non-stop, the intensity is as consistent as one would expect in the life of high profile individuals, and the repartee between Sam and all her friends and family as sparkling and humorous as ever.  Sam\x27s life is already complicated but being the Second Lady of the land makes it even more so.  In the midst of all that, old enemies make new problems as it appears that Sam\x27s entire team and the police department is under fire and taking their share of political hits.  So be prepared for more of what makes all the \x5C\x22Fatal Series\x5C\x22 some of the best reading around.  Those who love hot romance mixed with humor, mystery, and political drama will love this novel.  If this is your first go around with Sam and Nick, please start with book one.  You owe it to yourself to experience everything about their relationship up to this present story.  All in all, this is a worthy addition to a marvelous series.

product_title: Comanche Moon
review_headline: Special snowflake meets blue eyed comanche

The major problem I had with it is the main character the oh so special snowflake Loretta, the one foretold, with hair the colour of honey who will save the Comanches. I have to say I feel indignation on behalf of all living Comanches for this book. Really, I don\x27t expect every native american to fall to his knees in insta-love, just because he sees a blond girl. But in this book not only Hunter but one of his friends as well sets his eyes on honey-haired and blue-eyed white girls as future wifes.

Loretta is special, specially stupid, if you ask me. She believes absolutely every lie or accusation told to her, except the one guy who always told her the truth. She rather believes her abusive uncle, who by the way tried to rape her, she rather believes the horribly scarred and therefore ugly/evil cousin of Hunter, but she won\x27t believe that Hunter isn\x27t going to hurt/eat/rape her. Somewhere along the line she should have realised that actions speak more than words for a persons character. But in my opinion it happens way to late.

I wondered why the author even titles her book "Comanche moon", when in fact Hunter is only a "half-breed" and looks like a bronzed, broad shouldered, well muscled "white man" with his brown hair and indigo blue eyes.

product_title: Prodigal Son
review_body:
I enjoy a good mystery and the blurb on Kathleen Lopez\x27s e-book, "Prodigal Son," sounded promising. Unfortunately, the book did not live up to the blurb.

Lopez\x27s idea for "Prodigal Son" is a good one with tremendous potential in the hands of a more polished writer. The plot contains the obligatory side stories in an effort to provide background to the setting and the characters. Unfortunately, it isn\x27t enough. The very clever plot idea develops as one might expect in a mystery and then suddenly fast forwards in the last 30 pages as if the author was on a timed assignment. Lopez\x27s failure to progressively build on the plot of her mystery ultimately leaves the reader disappointed. The too-quickly-condensed plot at the end of the book cheapens a good story into a grab-bag of disorganized tie-ins and finishing touches. A sidebar growing romance indicates the author\x27s greater ease with writing romance scenes than fleshing out multidimensional characters to race through her fast-forwarded mystery plot.

Finally, there were too many spelling errors, missed words in phrases and extraneous nonsensical words included in the text to assure the reader that Lopez\x27s manuscript had been adequately edited prior to publication.

I was provided with a free copy of this book so I could give an honest review.

review_headline: Jaguar shifters for fun and games!
review_body:
I am particularly fond of Ms. Spear\x27s Highland shifter series. While this one was steamy, and some of the shifter scenes were fun, it read like a PSA...for how bad it is to buy and sell wild animals. Don\x27t get me wrong, I agree that the trafficking of wild animals should be stopped, but I did get rather tired of hearing how bad people are. Not all of us fit that bill.

What I did like was that Melissa and Huntley are a team for JAG Special Forces. Don\x27t you love that name? Because they are also jaguar shifters. They are hunting for poachers and are looking at each other a bit differently. They\x27ve both recently stepped away from their significant others, for assorted reasons. Suddenly, it seems like becoming more than partners just might be fun. They are forced to pretend to be a couple anyway when they need to care for some temporarily orphaned cubs--cubs who shift to human every so often!

Once again Ms. Spear takes us on a shifting ride where we find steam, mystery, and romance.

*Thank you, NetGalley and Sourcebooks Casablanca for the opportunity to read this book.

product_title: Paper or Plastic
review_body:
Paper or Plastic is what I like to call "The Perfect YA Contemporary Romance". It\x27s sweet, light (with just the right amount of depth), totally swoon-ish, and overall, a fun read to lose yourself into. I can\x27t find a single bad thing to say about it, so forgive if I only gush about how wonderfully brilliant it is.

A few reasons why I loved it:

1. The feels. I had this goofy grin throughout the whole book and mostly because of our seriously handsome and endearing Noah. The guy immediately won a place in my list of favorite book boyfriends because he\x27s too.damn.awesome. He\x27s sweet, smart, loyal, a total gentleman and caring. He\x27s the kind of guy my dreams dream about. That perfect.

2. Interesting characters. Paper or Plastic has a wide array of personalities. From our sweet & special Ruthie to a beauty pageant obsessed mother and sister. I had a lot of fun getting to know each and every one of them, and I was surprised how everyone had an important role in this story, they weren\x27t just fill-in characters. Alexia, our main character, is great and I found her quite likeable, despite her initial foolishness. I loved her affection towards her grandmother and I liked that she outgrows her own prejudices and makes up for her mistakes.

3. The unusual setting. Who would have thought I\x27d fall in love with a place such as SmartMart? It\x27s far from being a romantic setting or even a cute one, but it totally worked. Not all the book takes place in the store, but most of the good parts, the ones that made my heart skip, happened in here. I had fun at SmartMart, and heck, I\x27d love to work there, especially if I had a handsome supervisor such as Noah!

But what I found even more amazing about Paper or Plastic is that, even though it is a light read, it deals with several issues that made this book feel much more real. My heart even had the chance to feel heavy, whether it was because of Noah\x27s family issues, or Alexia\x27s, or even just the events that were out of the character\x27s control. That thing that happens in the last chapters (the one that involves a bakery table and darkness) totally made me want to cry.

So yes, I only have high praise for this incredibly sweet book. I loved it and I\x27m so glad I had the chance to read it. It\x27s a book full of awesomeness and it\x27s very much worth the read (so read it read it read it!).r even just the events that were out of the character\x27s control. That thing that happens in the last chapters (the one that involves a bakery table and darkness) totally made me want to cry.

So yes, I only have high praise for this incredibly sweet book. I loved it and I\x27m so glad I had the chance to read it. It\x27s a book full of awesomeness and it\x27s very much worth the read (so read it read it read it!).

product_title: The Lincoln Myth: A Novel (Cotton Malone Book 9)
review_body:
I doubt if I\x27ll finish this book. I am 16 percent through the Kindle edition. While I generally enjoy historical fiction, this book so far has at least two major flaws that will likely cause me to abandon it.

The first one is a major lack of historical accuracy right from the start. From the book: "By 1862 both the railroad and telegraph lines ran straight through the Utah Territory to the Pacific." According to the book, this forced Lincoln to reach some important agreement with Mormon leader Brigham Young in order to keep the West connected to the Union during the Civil War. The problem is that the railroad wasn\x27t built until several years later. From the cover notes and other hints, this pact between Lincoln and Young is a critical part of the book. Berry can make up all the secret agreements he wants to make an exciting story, but he cannot create railroads in history seven years before their time.

The second issue is one I keep running into in a lot of mediocre writing--ambiguous pronoun usage. Several times already I\x27ve read paragraphs in this book which describe the actions of two or three men. The next paragraph then begins with "He" when it should say "Malone" or "Rowan" or "Daniels" or whatever. The first two paragraphs of chapter eleven exemplify this flaw. The first paragraph briefly describes Senator Rowan and how he doesn\x27t abuse his power, followed by a few sentences about his fellow senator from Utah who has suffered a fall from grace. But then the fourth sentence in paragraph two (the first sentence in it that is about one man) begins with "He\x27d". You have to read about three more sentences to figure out which senator is being referenced. Unacceptably bad writing, IMHO. Start that sentence with "Rowan had" instead of "He\x27d" and I\x27ll be able to pay attention to the story rather than trying to understand bad writing.

review_headline: Fast paced, lots of action, and an awesome storyline!
review_body:
**I received an e-book ARC from the author in exchange for an honest review**

Isabelle Richards exceeded my expectations with this story. I loved the plot line and how the action started almost immediately. I loved the different twists and turns, the friendships that were forged between Lily and the agents, and the comfortable banter between the characters. Most of all, however, I loved the romance that brewed up and the slow burn that eventually ignited into a full-blown flame.

Gavin caught my attention right away and it didn\xE2\x80\x99t take very long for me to fall in love with his character. (The British accent only helped matters, ha!) He\xE2\x80\x99s sweet and charming, and from the get go he has Lily\xE2\x80\x99s best interests at heart, which is evident by his actions. And of course some of the things he did are sexy as hell.

Lily is an amazing character as well. She\xE2\x80\x99s been through hell, but she\xE2\x80\x99s so so so strong, and when most people would give up and say \xE2\x80\x9Cscrew it\xE2\x80\x9D to everything, she keeps moving forward. She\xE2\x80\x99s determined to start over in a way that\xE2\x80\x99s healthy for her. I loved watching her transformation through the book, from a semi-grieving widower to this almost butterfly that\xE2\x80\x99s spreading her wings and taking flight and starting to do all of these things that she loves but was never able to do before.

There\xE2\x80\x99s chemistry between these two from the get go, but Richards doesn\xE2\x80\x99t just let things blossom immediately. She gives us a slow burn, and as these two go through ups and downs together, we start to see a romance budding between them.

There was a point in time when I got a little irritated with Lily\xE2\x80\x99s hesitation about Gavin. I got it and I understood the reasoning behind it, but it eventually seemed like it was just drawn out a little too much.

Overall, I loved this book. I got hooked on it, there was so much action, and it was very, very well written. I liked the characters, there was good development, the details between the back story and the present were consistent, and honestly, once I got to the big climactic part, I had to keep reading and didn\xE2\x80\x99t stop until I had everything finished. I love when authors write in a way that makes me feel like I\xE2\x80\x99m actually living in the story, and that\xE2\x80\x99s how Richards wrote this one. I would love to read more of Isabelle\xE2\x80\x99s work, and can\xE2\x80\x99t wait until the next book in this series drops. product_title: Somewhere With You: A Novel: With You Series Book 1
review_body:
This is definitely one of those stories that will stick with you for a while after you have finished it. The relationship, more like a ping-pong game, between Jack and Amelie is so frustrating and raw, it hits you right in the heart.

Jack is a no-nonsense person. He knows what he wants as an adult. And, most of the time, it\x27s Amelie. As a teen, he is much the same, except it\x27s harder for him to recognize.

Amelie is a free-spirit as an adult. She is more like a gypsy, never truly belonging with any one person or in any one place. She wants Jack, but just can\x27t come to terms with what that means. As a teen, she loves Jack. But at the same time, if he isn\x27t willing to give her what she wants, she will grab it where she can find it.

I wondered about Amelie throughout the book. The signs where there, if you knew what they meant. I did. I was right. Her resistance to not allowing her love for Jack to cloud her goals and other wants. Jack only has one thing on his mind. That is Amelie.

This story is more of love, loss, letting go, and re-welcoming what should have been. You could say that it\x27s about timing, but really it isn\x27t. It\x27s about two kids growing up, trying to find their place in life, and finding out just how strong love can be. Over coming serious and heart breaking obstacles is part of being an adult. And it is something these two have to find a way to accept everything and move forward with or without one another.

product_title: Callous (Senses Series Book 6)
review_body:
I received a copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.\xC2\xA0

(Possible spoilers and 18+ ONLY)

Being a huge fan of Neal\x27s "Senses series", I was more than a little intimidated by approaching C.J. and Erin\x27s story.\xC2\xA0 While a spin-off will immediately draw the attention of previous readers, there is always the chance of biased emotions interfering with the new story.

Obviously,\xC2\xA0 I had a bad case of amnesia and forgot who wrote the book! Expect all of the characters we love to love and love to laugh over to be present enough to Fan-girl over, but not so much that it dominates the attention away from Erin and C.J.\x27s love to hate you and love you to love me relationship.\xC2\xA0

I was more than a little intrigued from the very start of the book. Each turn of the page did not satiate my growing obsession.\xC2\xA0 As the story continued I knew it would be no more quenched than it was with Maxx and Logan\x27s story.\xC2\xA0 That would be never. There will never, ever be enough of these characters in my life. They\x27re not only loveable and realistic. Their dialogue and life stories embed themselves into your heart. They are home.\xC2\xA0

First, the anticipation surrounding C.J.\x27s unfortunate circumstances held me teetering in fierce denial. Once someone has joined the family, I\x27d rather see them held captive than walking away. C.J\x27s confessions to Erin kept me swooning long after the book ended. It left an ache for everything a woman needs, not wants, needs in a man. Swooning doesn\x27t justify this level of perfection.

Though I may have, sort of, wanted to pound Erin\x27s obstinance from her, where would the tension be? A character straying from her key character "traits" wouldn\x27t fair well or be of much use for the story-line.\xC2\xA0 As a reader,\xC2\xA0 I\x27m allowed to wanna slap and hug her at the same time. I wouldn\x27t change her quick-witted quips or snarky attitude at all. She\x27s hysterical,\xC2\xA0 confident, determined, and underneath it all she has a heart of Gold. Erin\x27s vulnerabilities introduced me to a new side of her to adore.

Moving on, we have the sexual attraction between the two and that alone was enough to drive me insane. Discovering\xC2\xA0 the sentimental side of CJ, via his point of view, melted my heart.\xC2\xA0 Understanding the complex, internal impact surrounding Erin\x27s life was heart breaking. The execution of unknown revelations pertaining to the\xC2\xA0 death of her parents added a broader element of intrigue to the picture. I thoroughly enjoyed the diversity of issues in the plot and the execution is written flawlessly.\xC2\xA0

The sexual content of Callous is delicious and utterly intoxicating. The scenes are steamy and explicit, but Neal also threw in such an intense level of passion it reinvigorate\x27s desires that make her former novels appear amateur. I am nuts over Max and Logan, but Neal showed so much progress as a writer that I was left riding a blissful high.

Callous is beyond extraordinary and the emotional effects have left me speechless. It\x27s perfect. I could search a thesaurus looking for synonyms to amp up the review, but perfect says it all. The story can speak for itself justifiably.

review_body: I did not like this book at all. I finished it, because I hate to leave books unfinished, but I did not want to.  I have to say that the story line left much to be desired. The main idea for the book was good, a billionaire that needs American residency and a girl full of debt that could use some money; however, it was not executed properly. And even though there is nothing good going on between them, and they act silly all book long, at some miraculous point they just fall in love. I never saw it coming, and I don\x27t know what happened, but suddenly they fit perfectly together.    The book goes on and on with awkward money conversation, and silly thoughts. We never find out why Daniel is so insecure and mean. We never figure out what happens to Maddy\x27s parents, or why she has no friends and absolutely no one to talk to. We never know what happens to the bad ex-girlfriend. After they confess they like each other, the author skips six months of the book, and now they love each other.    I will not be reading the rest of the trilogy. This was it for me from this author.

product_title: Second Debt (Indebted Book 3)
review_headline: Heart pounding, my stomach in knots, and my head spinning with emotions...
review_body:
Pepper Winters made my heart leap, so many times in this one, that I constantly felt my pulse pounding in my ears! Debt Inheritance was a vicious introduction between captive and captor. First Debt blurred those stark lines with raw temptation, a forbidden desire. And now...Second Debt changes everything! Who\x27s an ally? Who are the true villains? The game changes, the stakes go up, and you\x27re going to see Jethro and Nila in a whole new light.

Regal and in-control Jethro is stripped down, made vulnerable. A once weak and naive Nila has steeled over, built her own armor in order to survive. The layers to these characters and their relationship are so intricate. From book one, until now, I\x27ve loved watching them evolve. Pepper Winters grips those emotions powerfully and brings them to fiery life. Bouncing between lust and hate, I loved the tension and struggle, their contrast of fire and ice. They finally reached a point where they can no longer ignore the connection that\x27s developed between them. *highlights every filthy passionate thing*

--
Trailing my lips along her jawline, I murmured, "I\x27m going to make you moan...here." Baring my teeth, I bit her throat, filled with the primal need to mark. "I\x27m going to make you scream...here."

She shivered, letting her head fall back, surrendering to me.
--

This book pushed me over the edge right along with Jethro and Nila! They\x27re impulsive, visceral, and rough...but what they share is intensely passionate, and above all else, freeing. They give each other what they\x27re both ultimately craving: freedom. From obligation, from captivity. From tradition, from debts. Everything erotic and thrilling that I craved, I was rewarded with. Everything mesmerizing about this series was highlighted in this book. The foreboding. The ferocity. It\x27s all there! Pepper Winters orchestrated such an addictive, consuming ride!

--
I feel what you feel. Whether it be a kiss or a kick or a killing blow. I wished I didn\x27t, but you\x27re mine, therefore, you are my affliction.
--

I was wrapped up in all of the detailed layers, especially as more about the debts and the Hawk-Weaver feud were unveiled! Aristocratic families steeped in wealth and secrets. Torture devices. Secret passages. Secret caves. I fully embraced the medieval/historical vibe in this book! I loved this hybrid of lyrical writing, the historical tones, and the edge and grit that comes with modern dark romances. Elements from these two genres were blended seamlessly and raised the story to a whole new level. Pepper Winters has created her own dark kingdom, with Jethro as its tormented prince and Nila as a rising rebel.

Oh, but the moment we\x27ve all been waiting for? Anticipating? Dreading? The time comes to collect that second debt, and it\x27s akin to having the rug ripped out from underneath you! The panic, the anxiety. Holy. Crap. The author didn\x27t lie when she said the debts only get worse! (I am freaking out already for the next three still to come!!!) You think you\x27re spiraling in one direction, only to get twisted and turned unexpectedly!

--
Her forehead furrowed harder, her fists curled tighter, and she withdrew from me until there was no emotion left--just a tiny dying star that once had shone so bright.

Leaving me heartless and bleeding, she gave me nothing else to do.

I slipped into my role as torturer and began.
--

If you\x27ve been hesitant to start this series, or perhaps you read Debt Inheritance and wondered how could this possibly turn out well, I believe the journey has been worth it so far! Get in on this! I was hoping to go deeper with Jethro, and although there are still huge questions looming, his mask and calm facade are wearing thin. He gets a taste of happiness with Nila... Is this sympathy I actually feel for the devil?! ;) I wanted to see Nila\x27s claws sharpen, and while fear and uncertainty still haunt, she\x27s absolutely a different creature now.

My eyes were racing across the pages, devouring every word. This is the definition of a page-turner! I couldn\x27t stop. I couldn\x27t get enough. I fully expected Pepper Winters to hit me with something intense--to leave my heart pounding, my stomach in knots, and my head spinning with emotions--and Second Debt lived up to every single one of those expectations!

product_title: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl (Revised Edition) (Top Ten Best Fiction for Young Adults)
review_headline: Comedy Book Even Though I\x27m Promised Seriousness
review_body:
12700353

Amazon / Goodreads

Greg Gaines is the last master of high school espionage, able to disappear at will into any social environment. He has only one friend, Earl, and together they spend their time making movies, their own incomprehensible versions of Coppola and Herzog cult classics.

Until Greg\xE2\x80\x99s mother forces him to rekindle his childhood friendship with Rachel.

Rachel has been diagnosed with leukemia\xE2\x80\x94-cue extreme adolescent awkwardness\xE2\x80\x94-but a parental mandate has been issued and must be obeyed. When Rachel stops treatment, Greg and Earl decide the thing to do is to make a film for her, which turns into the Worst Film Ever Made and becomes a turning point in each of their lives.

And all at once Greg must abandon invisibility and stand in the spotlight.
Let me tell you this upfront.
I did NOT like this book.
But I\x27m not trying to offend the author.

It was a bit funny... I\x27ll say that. If there were cameras shadowing me, they would catch my laughing. This was a pretty funny book. But it was mostly awkward jokes. Not a lot of people might call it funny. I laugh easily...so it\x27s not hard to make me laugh. (But it\x27s hard to make me stop.)
The book made some nice jokes. Greg tried his best to cheer Rachel up with awkward jokes along the lines of pulling up his shirt and making his tummy rolls/fat rolls talk or making an on-going joke about alien barf. If you like these jokes, then you\x27ll laugh. But while they were funny, they were also immature. I felt a bit childish when I laughed at the book. These weren\x27t jokes that seemed sophisticated.
The thing is...the jokes suited the awkward Greg. I think that\x27s the more important thing. The author didn\x27t just slap in jokes. He tried to make them sound from the narrator.

The characters were hard to take seriously.
I couldn\x27t take Greg seriously. As a narrator, he has to be one of the worst I\x27ve read. He didn\x27ttake things seriously. He was a bit childish. He didn\x27t seem to have lots of emotions. He tried his best to stay on the outer edge. He never made true friends. (Earl makes great points about Greg.) I didn\x27t like him. Greg didn\x27t take his life seriously until the end. He didn\x27t take the world seriously. He slid by with average grades and an average attitude. People like him don\x27t try. They don\x27t try until they have to. But I\x27m happy he started to take his life seriously. He changed and started to rein in control.
And Earl... I know that teenagers curse and all, but Earl is too much. I can handle cursing. (I\x27ve learned to.) He kept cursing. And while I know of anger issues, Earl was something else. You\x27ll be surprised when you see Earl caring, in his own way, for Rachel. But Earl... He\x27s one of those characters who can be better. If he only applied himself to school. If he only tried harder. He would have been an A student, a bit busier, and maybe less mediocre.
Rachel...gosh. I don\x27t want to say anything bad. She isn\x27t the worst. But she isn\x27t developed enough. (As seen in Rachel the Film.) There isn\x27t much to say about her...

There didn\x27t seem to be a plot. Really.
What was going on? Jokes. Greg being idiotic. Anything else? Not really. There didn\x27t seem to be a set plot. It was a lot of ramblings. I understand that there was something underneath, but I didn\x27t see it. There were small peaks at the plot, but it was hard to follow. This book was mostly jokes.
I would have preferred if it had more on Rachel. Maybe if Greg learned about her more. (Though, him not knowing much is important to the story.) If there was something more than teenage antics, I would have liked it better. If I needed teenage antics, I could have gone to a high school.

The ending wasn\x27t the best. It wasn\x27t happy. Or sad. It just was...flat. I didn\x27t enjoy the ending. Nor did I hate it. I didn\x27t have questions. (That might be because the story didn\x27t raise questions.) I felt mildly done with the book when I reached the Fin. I felt like the ending could have been better if the plot was better. I guess this can be linked to the plot. I\x27m not entirely sure.

The book tried to deal with a serious topic, but it just made me laugh. I felt like the theme wasn\x27t there. We were talking about cancer. I thought it would be a different type of cancer story.
But it wasn\x27t.
This book danced around cancer. It wasn\x27t in-depth. It wasn\x27t detailed. We didn\x27t get Rachel\x27s point-of-view. We didn\x27t get anything about her struggle. Greg was an outsider to her mind. He didn\x27t understand her.
It was a comedy book. A light-hearted book. A joke book. Essentially, you can tell, I didn\x27t like that. As much as I needed this light-hearted book, I didn\x27t enjoy it. I prefer more tough and solemn books.
This book promised a cancer story. But Greg wasn\x27t close enough to Rachel to get a cancer story. I thought that it would be better.
(To be honest, \x27The Fault In Our Stars\x27 is a...how to put it...better cancer book. We get more of the emotional pain. But the uplifting romance as well.)

I couldn\x27t stand the way the book was written. Not in the words.
But in the script. In the format. There was movie script-style parts.
Let me say this first. I don\x27t like to read stories in other formats. I prefer the chapter-paragraph format. I don\x27t like straying.
So there is a reason the book\x27s format annoyed me. We had script-style. Chapter-paragraph. We even had bulleted lists. (What...) I can\x27t stand it. It was a nuisance to read. I could read it. I just didn\x27t like it. I didn\x27t want to read it in that format.

Cloudy with a 10% chance of rain
2/5

product_title: The Book of Strange New Things: A Novel
review_headline: Perhaps reminding us about familiar old things in a wonderful way
review_body:
OMG. There are no amount of words in any language that can describe how much I adore this book. It is fine as a stand alone book - but for me I\x27d love to see a sequel in the works. (hint hint dear Mr. Faber).

Sometimes I think my reviews are too long. People probably want to know up front if this is a good book or a bad book...if it\x27s worthwhile reading and/or buying. Well, okay then, you got it.

I\x27d say if you are interested in reading a story about a man who goes to a newly discovered planet far far away, to do a particular job that he was especially chosen for then this will be of interest to you. You will learn about the man and about the people he works with on the other planet. He is a Pastor. He has been sent to do Bible study with the aliens. You will also learn about the wife he leaves behind on Earth and how she copes with not having her husband there. You learn about the indigenous peoples/aliens on their planet - a world that is very different from our own. It\x27s not at all like Pandora (from Avatar) either. Not at all. It\x27s quite unique.

For me, this story was very believable. It didn\x27t seem like a sci-fi book either. Yet, it is. You just don\x27t have star ships zipping around the Universe involved with interstellar battles against evil sharp toothed dark slime dripping alien beasts. It\x27s more like an earthly explorer who found a lost tribe in the Amazon jungles and then missionaries go to share the joy of Jesus with these unsophisticated people. However, it\x27s not a religious book at all. Still it is filled with spiritual insights and lessons on love that are woven in and out of the book.

Make up your mind what kind of books interests you - if you decide on this one I bet you\x27ll be glad you did. Enjoy!

product_title: JOURNALS FROM THE EDGE
review_headline: \x22Yank on the ejection handle when there\x27s no hope left. Fires them out of the jet like a rocket.\x22
review_body:
Author/surfer/therapist Bill Boyum shares not only his life, his obsession with surfing, his bonding with his older brother Mike, and his global travels and drug abuse and so much more in this fascinating, deeply moving memoir that helps every reader understand the life of men who survived the wars and the effect that wars has on their families. One of the many reasons this book is so successful is the lucid writing style of the author whose compassion for his own sons encouraged him to write about his life with his brother, surfing, traveling around the world smuggling drugs, their affairs with women, living in Hawaii and even more exotic places to the dangers of being too close to death during the India/Pakistan war, the brothers\x27 struggle with an abusive father - a decorated WWII fighter pilot, post war test pilot and career Naval officer who suffered the consequences of what was then called shell shock, but now is recognized as Pos Traumatic Stress Disorder. The story is a coming of age story during the trying times of the 1960s and 70s and ends with both a personal tragedy for Bill but also a renaissance for living happy at ocean\x27s side having endured Gestalt therapy and the rigors of the drug and surfer wandering life.

Outside of the pages of this important book Bill Boyum shares his own quick bio. It is excerpted here for the reader: `Growing up, our family moved frequently because our Dad was a Naval Aviator. I continued to travel extensively as an adult until the last fifteen years when the wear and tear of jumping on airplanes finally got to me. Now I enjoy the rewards of staying in one place, near the ocean, Paia, Maui. But during the early 70s, while I had a home in Kula, upcountry on the slope of Haleakala, I traveled often to Indonesia in search of perfect waves. During those years if you picked one word to describe me it might be \x5C\x22surfer\x5C\x22 as in the old sense of the word that included all the lack of responsibility that categorized many surfers before the age of professional surfing. As such I was probably a good candidate for the various forms of `self-actualization\x27 groups and gurus of that time, like EST. But I always viewed them as fancy mainland hucksters selling psychological snake oil. What worked for me was high-grade Maui marijuana. In the late 70s, even with that cynical point of view, I grudgingly submitted to Gestalt therapy to make a weak stab at repairing a rapidly sinking marriage. The experience was confusing for me and in the back of my mind always seemed centered towards extending the expensive sessions into the future. The marriage was going under and it was time to abandon ship. Simple. But one request the therapists asked still sticks in my mind to this day. Tell us your deepest darkest secret. No way in hell was I going to tell anyone anything close to that. Exposing myself on that level just seemed absurd when I couldn\x27t even make sense of it myself. Trusting that they could was just too big a leap. Any time I had previously cracked the door to that dark closet, I couldn\x27t even see all that was there. Dark stuff needed to be kept in the closet where it belonged. So I blundered along through life, distracted by high adrenaline sports and recreational pot obliteration. The marriage did give me two strong sons and being a father saved me in no small degree from a complete marijuana lobotomy. But when my sons would ask me about my family and events from my past, I never felt adequate enough to explain to them or even myself, what it all meant. So whenever they asked, I changed the subject. Once the kids left home and I grew accustomed to the empty nest, little things would bubble up that made me edgy. I began to realize that smoking weed had really been a coping mechanism for something I didn\x27t want to face. So while I stopped smoking, I continued to pour as much energy as I could into adrenaline pumping sports, which worked to some degree but still left me troubled. After a surf trip with my sons in 2002, I began to write down a massive collection of memorable events. One would spawn another and soon my new pot free mind was digging up stuff I never imagined I would remember. It was exciting to use my mind but what did it all mean? And if I were to write a book, what was it that I wanted to relate? It came to me with a painful event in 2007. My two sons were living in Indonesia and had families. I was a grandfather and an empty-nester with a new favorite activity to keep my mind and body healthy. During that year at the age of 57, downwind paddleboarding removed me from all the contention of surfing in crowded line-ups while still giving me the in-the-moment focus I loved so much. I felt like I had it together. Life was good.\x27

A book of this quality, filled with photographs that mirror much o the narrative, a book that teaches us so much about PTSD and the effects on a family, should be on the must read for many reasons - not the least of which is because it is brilliant.
