product_title: The Congress
review_headline: Robin Wright makes up for the flaws
review_body:
The premise of this movie, that actors can be eliminated if their images are completely digitized is a little far-fetched. At least for today. And I\x27m sure that many actors are upset when movie studio digitize whole movie or certain scenes. But accept the premise.

Next, the plot of the mother\x27s search for her son is what is supposed to make the movie warm. But that\x27s what the emotion of this movie is. It is the incredible scene when Wright moves out of the animated world back into "reality". Her walk through the real people is one of the most upsetting dystopian worlds I have ever seen. The makeup, costumes, and actors expressions are heart wrenching. This is the way the world will end. Not with a bang, but a whimper.

Meanwhile for anyone who only knows Wright\x27s work as the cool woman behind Kevin Spacey\x27s House of Cards villain this is an incredible acting experience.

Wright totally understands Spencer Tracy\x27s comment "Concentrate, don\x27t embroider." She is so underplayed that her presence screams across the screen.

I understand how many people would like/understand this film. There is much I didn\x27t understand and much that just doesn\x27t make sense. But it doesn\x27t matter. Wright\x27s performance is breathtaking in its understatement.

product_title: Robot And Frank
review_headline: ... that shows Frank Langella at his shining and extraordinary best. What an actor
review_body: A lovely film that shows Frank Langella at his shining and extraordinary best.  What an actor!  The supporting cast is just as wonderful, if under-utilized--with the exception of the first-billed "Robot".  This film is a terrific story taking place in the near-future, showcasing technology believably based on current robotics research specifically as used within this film.  Ironically, robotics and artificial intelligence researchers are hoping that these "companions" WILL be able to learn and transcend their initial programming--as depicted in the film, though I suspect they would NOT be pleased with the direction this particular robot takes.  In this aspect, the film ably enters the realm of science fiction, but make no mistake, this is a film about humanity, and human frailty.  Wonderful film with a believable story arc leading the audience on an emotional journey towards a bitter-sweet finale.

product_title: Attic Door
review_headline: Finally saw it and it was very good!
review_body:
I\x27ve been wanting to watch this for a few years- after looking up Madison Davenport after her role on Shameless- and having read all of the good but mysterious reviews (had a heck of a time finding any spoilers!) I finally rented it from Amazon. It is a quiet and slow film but in a good and suspenseful way- I kept waiting for a jump scare so it kept me interested. I truly did not figure out the ending until it was upon me and even then, I was trying to wrap my head around it but it was a good ending. It was a sad one though because I felt for the kids who didn\x27t really get a chance to grow up. Not truly abandoned but left on their own indefinitely, always waiting for salvation that never comes. Reminded me a bit of Satre\x27s \x27No Exit\x27.
In any case, I really enjoyed this heartbreaking film and the young actors did a truly stellar job holding the film up. The \x27monster\x27 had me guessing until the very end and added a great mystery element without the gore and violence of most films. Deserves a second watch!

product_title: Alaskan Bush People Season 2
review_headline: Watch, Enjoy, and Accept it is a show :)
review_body: Ok to be fair it probably IS scripted - why would anyone watch it if it were boring? But lets be fair it is funny and entertaining and definitely better than some of the reality garbage available on television.  Also as to their lack of skills - this could be attributed to their lack of societal influence.  Most of us learn through what we see others doing or the resources/ materials available to us.  Honestly I think that Discovery should make sure they have all the tools that were available in pioneer days though.  Some on here have mentioned how they live without a proper job etc.  they do mention odd jobs to survive, they have also mentioned fishing/ crabbing etc as well.  Finally they do mention bartering.  I am very much a modern society girl and prefer all my technology in abundance, but I had a brother who thought it all useless and he lived off the land quite successfully.  I didn\x27t get why he would want to but he did, so it can be done.  Oh and I would imagine that to have cameras following them around they get paid for that too - why else would you subject yourself to the hassle? Overall watch the show the people are interesting and if nothing else the love this family has for each other is very obvious - that in itself is nice to see.

product_title: Sara Solves It
review_headline: Fractions are fair, and help us share!
review_body:
Brother/sister math/mystery-solving duo? What more could you ask for?

This is a seriously good show. Between Sara Solves It and The Stinky and Dirty Show, I\x27m immensely impressed with Amazon\x27s pilot offerings for preschoolers. I really hope both are picked up: my son keeps watching the only available episodes of each with the same sincere interest and enthusiasm as the first viewing.

There\x27s a lot to love about this show. I have a boy and a girl and I love the sibling concept of the protagonists. I also really appreciate the racial diversity of the characters. Having a strong lead girl is also an impressive attribute.

In terms of gimmickiness and the level of obnoxious/annoying: this does pretty well. It\x27s nowhere nearly as annoying as most other preschooler shows. The little musical numbers aren\x27t quite as delightful as Daniel Tiger\x27s, but they\x27re not too bad, and they\x27re So Much Better than most offerings, especially from the tragic LeapFrog shows. I don\x27t mind listening to this pilot, and there are several other educational shows that make me want to press my head between two pillows.

I\x27d really like to see where this show is going, and am hopeful that the series is picked up. My son usually likes only a certain type of show (builder/vehicle shows), but he liked this, which is immensely impressive. Well done, Amazon. Pursue it.

product_title: Twilight Syndrome: Death Cruise (English Subtitled)
review_body:
If you haven\x27t seen the other one, Twilight Syndrome: Deadly Theme Park, do yourself a favor and go watch it. If you\x27re a fan of that sort of campy, low-budget horror-comedy, you\x27ll probably like this one as well. I loved it! Much like the last one, it\x27s just so cute, like watching a high-school play. The acting isn\x27t great, some of the editing is a bit odd and the story occasionally makes sudden, illogical jumps. But despite all that, I found it completely endearing.

While I don\x27t think the characters were quite as cute at in Deadly Theme Park, I do think Death Cruise has a better story and premise. I love the idea of a real life game that you can reset whenever anyone dies. Of course, since players don\x27t forget, they still retain all their horrible memories of dying every time they reset. It\x27s a great premise.

These movies are cute and fun. I\x27m now hooked on Twilight Syndrome. If I see another movie in the series pop up on Amazon Prime, I will watch it in a heartbeat.

product_title: Impossible Choice
review_headline: FILM WITH A SOLID MESSAGE & BEAUTY OF CENTRAL NY CAPTURED!!
review_body: Excited to see this film on Amazon! I enjoyed watching it again for several reasons:  1.) I love films that show off Upstate NY and its natural beauty. From Skaneateles to Palmyra and Watkins Glen and scenes along the historic Erie Canal its fun to pick out places I recognize and see Central New York locations selected for this full length feature film!   2.) A storyline that deals with issues of tolerance, homosexuality, self love and acceptance and shot in a way that the characters are believable and could easily be your next door neighbor. In cities and more progressive locales homosexuality may be accepted but this film tackles how small towns and rural areas with less than liberal views still make people such as the teens in the film feel anxious, unaccepted, or unworthy and the film moves through how they navigate these issues through the lens of small town mindsets.  3.) I play Hannah in this film :) Although my speaking lines have been cut from this final edit and Im just briefly in 2 scenes I still feel strongly connected to it and appreicate having been part of a film that was developed with a solid message for the audience all while highlighting the beauty of central New York. It seems like so many films are made today solely for entertainment value so when I watch a film such as this one developed with the intention to have the audience rethink behaviors or belief systems or connect with characters on a deeper level I appreciate that!  4.) Im a lover of indie films and documentaries and encourage others to support independent thinking and film making. We each get to vote in life with our dollars towards whatever it is we want to support from what we eat and wear to what we watch. :)

review_body: I really like this show!  It reminds me of The Wonder Years, but mainly is focused on the family interactions instead of all aspects of the youngest son\x27s life.  These parents really love their kids, even if they don\x27t know how to show it all the time. I hope this boy and his siblings know how lucky they were to be loved so much!  This show makes me laugh joyously and cry from the tenderness; I love it!  Give it a try; let the Hollywood people know that feel-good innocent shows are appreciated and much needed in this world we live in. The family has problems, just like every family I think, but not in any kind of abusive way; and there is freedom to communicate between adults and children, no matter what the emotion.  I didn\x27t grow up with this freedom and am so jealous of how easy it is to just be able to express yourself freely. I also recommend The Middle.

product_title: The Man In the High Castle - Season 1
review_body:
The high concept of alternate, revisionist histories is the stuff of comic books (which I personally do love), but here it\x27s played as engaging as any premium HBO or AMC show like Game of Thrones, Walking Dead, or Mad Men. The world building and details are never presented in a clunky manner, but doled out subtlety through character details and plot escalations.

And the art direction is beautiful. Locations feel distinct and really help sell this world historically adjacent to our own. It may be too early to say, but I also get the sense that the trajectory of the story is headed towards a complete and satisfying conclusion, with plenty of twists along the way of course. I just hope I get the chance to watch it to that ending.

So, please pick up Man in the High Castle, Amazon!

product_title: The Man In the High Castle - Season 1
review_headline: Book is unfilmable, but this departure from it is riveting and beautifully produced.
review_body: I enjoyed this pilot so much I reread the book for the first time in thirty or forty years and realized the show isn\x27t nearly as \x5C\x22faithful\x5C\x22 to it as I had thought. The novel is wonderful, but unfilmable, taking place as it does mainly inside the heads of characters who are almost powerless to act in ways you could show on the screen. The setting for the novel seems to demand a story of action and intrigue, but that is just the first of the author\x27s head-fakes; its actual message, perhaps, is that the worlds in our separate minds right now are as different from each other as historical outcomes could be. (And the ending will always shake a lot of readers off, as it did my younger self.) The pilot is clearly for a series that _is_ mainly about action and intrigue, one that starts more than halfway through the novel and intends to keep going long after its events, with only a few characters from the novel and those barely recognizable. (Really, how could the novel\x27s heroine, for instance, an aimless, neurotic, not particularly bright, but big-hearted and deep-souled Beat-era gal, pass muster with a modern audience? They require a karate-chopping superwoman, and I suspect they will get her.) But these comparisons are not fair. The book cannot be filmed. A good series based on it must face that fact bravely and carve its own story from the same background, and they\x27ve clearly chosen that path. I can\x27t tell if their story will succeed or fail, but it is beautifully produced, with a look that is completely fascinating. I definitely want to see it play out.

product_title: Point of Honor
review_body:
I did not think it was very well done. Historically inaccurate is one point. That the war was fought over
slavery is inaccurate. It was fought over the state\x27s rights and more importantly as most wars over
money and power. I felt this did not depict the true history of the worst American war of all time with
more deaths of Americans than any other war. Interestingly when you look at the facts of the losses
on both sides it is noteworthy that although the northern states lost many more men, they prevailed.
My family fought on both sides and so this dilemma shown here was not new to me. It often tore
families apart and caused great pain which only worsened when the losses began to take their toll. I
also do not believe this is a time to bring up race and what it means. Most southerners never owned
a slave and never wanted to. They wanted the right to live as did the slaves. Upholding the Union was
a great and difficult task during that time period, but it was done at a greater cost than was needed.
Robert E. Lee was Lincoln\x27s first choice to lead the Union army, but he declined and Grant took over.
For this, General Lee\x27s plantation is now Arlington National Cemetery. Poor loser, Mr. Lincoln.
I think another pilot would be better than this one. I did not think the acting all that great and the daughters
all look like sluts. The touch of Chopin\x27s E flat Nocturne was nice. It is a hauntingly beautiful piece and fit
the time, but it was written just under 30 years prior to this portrayal of it being played. Possible, but
not likely due to Chopin writing it between 1831 and 1833 in Paris. Extremely low possibility it was available
in the Southern US as sheet music.

product_title: It\x27s Me or the Dog Season 3
review_headline: Not Cesar...but a class of her own. Thumbs up.
review_body:
I have been a Cesar Milan fan since I\x27ve discovered his show a few years ago. People kept telling me about Victoria Stilwell, but usually there was a jab against Cesar in the mix, and I didn\x27t like that at all. ;-)
I learned so incredibly much from watching and reading Cesar Milan, and that also made me explore other books about dog language, dog behavior, etc. (by now I\x27ve probably read 20). I volunteer at the local shelter, and I have been told that I am great with dogs, especially large and "scary" breeds. My own two dogs are not only happy but also very well socialized and have proper doggy etiquette... Without Cesar, I would never have gotten this far.
With that being said; I recently started watching "It\x27s me or the dog", and I have been quite enjoying it. Victoria\x27s approach is very different; she exclusively uses positive reinforcement, and it seems to work quite well. What I particularly enjoy is her personality, though. As a British lady, she is much less politically correct when addressing the owners. She is never rude, but she is so straightforward and honest...it just cracks me up. I am German, and I needed to get used to the extra niceties used in the US (no judgment here!). Victoria is very charming and pretty, but don\x27t judge the book by its cover...! LOL...!! If a dog gets treated poorly, she gets right into the owners\x27 faces and gives them a piece of her mind. It is priceless!
I am still a fan of Cesar, but it\x27s not one size fits all when it comes to dog owners. Some might be more comfortable with Victoria\x27s approach, and if it\x27s good for the dog...I\x27m all for it. Highly recommend this entertaining and educating show!

product_title: Triggers
review_body: A great show all around! One of the things that I find fascinating about it is how the episodes are put together. Knowing that the renowned cartoonist Garry Trudeau is the producer/writer/creator of this show, I can see how each episode is like a series of cartoon panels. Within each episode are a series of vignettes, flowing together, but separate in their own way. It is a lot like reading a collection of "Doonesbury" cartoons. This sort of style could easily go bad, but Trudeau pulls it off with flying colors. The result is that we\x27re presented with mini-stories that each stand up on their own merit, but carry the overall storyline along. I find this series wonderfully lighthearted entertainment, and in this day of hyper polarized politics, it is nice to have something like this to make us laugh about it all.

And while I love the actor who played Malcolm the way that storyline played out was a bust. Plus, what\x27s up with Jack? Once so likable although a constant complainer, he\x27s just dull and lacking any charm right now. I think the show is meandering and needs to step it up in a big way. Of course, I say that but I will keep watching anyway as I\x27m hooked in, but I don\x27t think I can stay tuned much longer if something bigger and more interesting doesn\x27t emerge.

review_headline: Segregation in housing coming to an end.
review_body: The politics of coming out of exile is in its last phase. We have ended segregation but in housing there are still neighborhoods that cling to this old obsolete standard. They want to live with "their own kind" and that in it self is a statement of hate and mistrust of the rest of the world. Breaking up these isolated ethnic areas is going to help end the politics of race. When integration into a mainstream society happens for these people they will not be able to cling to the old standards that " white people" are to blame for all their ills. It is not "white" people who have done anything. It is individuals who have abused others. When they claim whites are to blame- they collectively condemn all the good people who have helped them in thier emancipation. When these areas are transformed by mixing economic levels we will start to see the identity of ethnicity emerge as "American" first and not prefixed with ethnicity first. We are so divided with hate that to begin to see ourselves as Americans first is a step towards unity and peace in this society. This film is a lesson about learning to live with each other. product_title: Come Morning
review_headline: It will be all over in the morning
review_body:
Sometimes we grow up much too fast, and by the time the morning comes, ten year old D will have aged far beyond his years.

The movie starts with D\x27s mother attempting to persuade her father-in-law not to take D hunting. But D\x27s grandfather is a stubborn man, set in his ways, and despite her pleas, he takes D hunting. It\x27s a decision that all will soon regret because while out hunting, D shoots and kills a neighbor. D only wants to confess the crime. But because D\x27s family and the family of the neighbor have bad blood, D\x27s grandfather determines to cover the crime. What unfolds is a suspenseful as it is touching. D understands that his crime has gravity but perhaps not to the extent is should. All D\x27s grandfather can focus on is the potential impact to the family.

The movies covers one night in their lives. But it is a harrowing journey. And by its end, D is older and wiser. But we can guarantee that he will never be the same. Mornings tend to shed new light. But that light isn\x27t always a good light.

product_title: American Sniper
review_headline: Boundary value conditions, domain applicability and \x22American Sniper\x22
review_body:
Einstein\x27s general theory of relativity is a generalization of Newtonian mechanics which applies to large objects moving at high speeds that curve spacetime. Similarity, quantum mechanics is a generalization of classical mechanics which applies to very small objects like electrons and photons. Newtonian mechanics thus has a domain of applicability within which it works perfectly well even if it fails to work under the larger rubric of Einsteinian general relativity. Similarly classical mechanics has a domain of applicability within which it is golden. Both are perfectly comfortable within their own boundary value conditions - medium-sized objects and slow speeds for instance.

If you think about it, morality has similar domains of applicability. I was reminded of this comparison when I watched the Clint Eastwood-directed movie "American Sniper" over the weekend. The movie is about Chris Kyle, a celebrated US Navy sniper who over his four tours of duty in Iraq racked up 160 confirmed kills. The film has garnered some controversy for its supposed glorification of war and mindless patriotism. Kyle faced some gut-wrenching decisions in his sniper career in gunning down women and children who were enemy combatants, but by most accounts the decisions were quite simple for him and his conscience seemed clear. Personally, irrespective of where my political sympathies lie, I thought the movie was very gripping and well-made and enjoyed it, and Bradley Cooper was a revelation. After it ended I witnessed a kind of sustained and erie silence as the audience shuffled out of the theater, a silence that I haven\x27t encountered very frequently before.

Since the audience was based in Boston, MA, it is unlikely that the silence was the result of them being enamored and stunned by Chris Kyle\x27s sacrifice and patriotism. Instead I would like to think that the contemplative pause was provoked by a classic and highly problematic dilemma that mankind has faced since it acquired the ability to wage war: how can you vigorously oppose what you think is a highly unnecessary and immoral war and yet support the actions and decisions of individual soldiers like Chris Kyle who are putting their lives on the line with courage? It\x27s a question Americans of every stripe face: when a soldier appears at the airport after returning from a tour, do you condemn him or her or laud their courage?

It\x27s a very difficult question to answer, one whose answer is certainly not black and white and which we will almost certainly never definitively figure out in the foreseeable future. But a comparison with theories in science and especially in physics at least provides an interesting analysis in my opinion.

Here\x27s the point: When Chris Kyle was looking down the barrel of his sniper rifle and had to pick between the life of a ten year-old Iraqi kid carrying a grenade and the life of five American marines, he picked the marines. The choice still wasn\x27t easy but it was the best one to make under the limited parameters and boundary value conditions that he was operating under. The parameters were related to choosing between culpable Iraqi lives and American lives. The boundary value conditions had to do with the narrowly defined parameters of his mission or assignment. You could convince yourself that he had the right solution under those conditions even if you vehemently protested the war at large.

The fact of the matter is that moral decisions, as hard and endlessly unanswerable as they may be, still often operate within a limited domain of applicability. These domains of applicability have announced themselves in every war from the Mexican war to Vietnam. You can be for or against the moral decisions with some degree of confidence within those particular domains, even if you may be entirely opposed or in favor of them when the domains expand. It\x27s like being in favor of Newtonian mechanics when you want to send rockets to the moon while being vehemently opposed to it when you want to send rockets to a neighboring galaxy containing black holes. Or like being in favor of classical mechanics when you want to deal with large blocks of gold while denying the use of that domain of applicability while analyzing individual gold atoms and the energy levels of their electrons. You can therefore potentially consider the political leaders who orchestrated the Iraq war to be war criminals even if you agree with the difficult decisions that Kyle made in those few seconds when he was looking down that gun barrel in Fallujah.

There may be no answer to moral questions like those surrounding the Iraq war, and it is very likely that we may be forever divided into black and white bins when it comes to answering those questions. But I would like to believe that by dividing the conundrums into domains of applicability and at least agreeing that one\x27s answer may depend on the exact boundary value conditions that one is dealing with, we may possibly reach a consensus and reach out into that gray area that always bedevils the gut-wrenching implications of our morality in both war and peace. Perhaps then we can meet halfway across and reach some kind of consensus, even if that consensus may be occupying the kind of twilight netherworld that entangled electrons do.s to the moon while being vehemently opposed to it when you want to send rockets to a neighboring galaxy containing black holes. product_title: Dying Light
review_headline: Dead Island + Mirror\x27s Edge + Fun = Dying Light
review_body:
Just finished the game today. Really enjoyed it. It is pretty similar to Dead Island with the biggest difference being the vertical aspect of movement that Dead Island lacked. Parkour is a lot of fun and is similar to Mirror\x27s Edge. The world is huge and open. Just about every building can be entered and explored. Loot is everywhere. Combat is fun. Crafting is fun. The quests are fun. Challenges are fun. Movement is fun. Almost everything about this game is simply fun.

The storyline is really good as well and is lengthy. I logged 57 hours in the game and left out some of the stuff you can do although I feel confident that I covered almost all of it.

I really only had 2 complaints. The first is that my frame rate would dip when one of the spitting special zombies would hit me in the face with spit. Possibly correctable with tweaked settings and/or improved hardware. The other is the "water blur" effect on the screen any time you get wet. It\x27s super annoying and makes it nearly impossible to see anything for a good 5 seconds after you get out of the water.

All in all I really enjoyed this game. It\x27s fun just to run/parkour around the city. It almost becomes an art form after you get the hang of it. Well done, Techland!

product_title: Titanfall [Online Game Code]
review_headline: Flawed but can be fun for FPS buffs
review_body:
It\x27s a ton of fun for a little. It\x27s kind of a throw back to oldschool FPS games where fast movement and less realistic physics were a thing. Some stuff holds it back. I don\x27t think very high damage, high rate of fire hitscan weapons have a place in games where high map mobility is supposed to be a primary draw to the game. You end up doing the parkour tricks and then get autolocked by a pistol and killed in one burst by someone. Add in the Titans (which I think are in and of themselves very fun), and most of the time it felt like it was better to play at a crawl than to explore all of the different parkour routes on each map. Capture the flag changes this dynamic a lot, as you are forced to do the parkour routes for flag caps despite the dangers. However CTF is among the least played modes on PC and not really worth your time trying to play unless you have a dedicated group of people to scrim with.

The Titans are fun but I can see how they are divisive with people. Pilots (infantry) can get very easily killed by Titans, so you have to learn how to get your Titan out early and be effective at using one. You do stuff as a pilot like kill other pilots or get objectives, and you lower the timer on deploying your Titan. Titans are very mobile and kill infantry almost instantly, and they are hard to kill, especially for uncoordinated/new teams. Titan vs. Titan can be pretty fun as different loadouts change playstyle pretty noticeably (countering other Titans vs countering infantry mostly), and I think some of the best moments in the game are when both teams have their Titans out on the field.

Anyway, this game game goes on sale a lot and is probably worth giving a spin if you have time and are curious about it.

product_title: Dying Light
review_body:
Will you survive?

Terrifying. Heart-pounding. The fabric of nightmares.

Dying Light is in essence, FRIGHTENING. This is horror done right.

Harran has recently hit an economic boom thanks to the discovery of oil beneath its soils. With this black gold now within the governmment\x27s possession, development began and western influence creeped in and slowly took over. And then the plague hit. Rabies. No one expected someone to weaponize the virus...but they did.

Crane. That\x27s you. You\x27re him. GRE Operative working undercover between warring factions in the epicenter of the Rabies plague; you\x27re mission is to extricate a file containing delicate information in regards to the weaponization of this virus, pertinent to national security.

As you progress the game, your skills increase exponentially. Running up walls, using a grappling hook to fly from building to building, vaulting over enemies, and somersaulting to land high jumps all become routine. You are able to modify various weaponry found with a plethora of blueprints that add DoT effects and increased damage for crafted equipment that really feels epic.

Speaking of equipment, Dying Light has tons of it. You have plenty of melee weapons and ranged ordinance that are tweakable with blueprints to give you just the right amount of variety to keep the flow of the game engaging and never feeling stagnant.

Stale. That\x27s something you\x27ll never feel when playing. The ambiance of an infected Harran and the hyper-realistic quality of Techland\x27s Chrome 6 engine are to be commended. It is unbelievable what maximum settings do for atmosphere here. Everything is lush; movements have fluidity and polish while shadows, flames, electric currents, water, oil slicks, billowing smoke, flapping flags, and even birds in the air, all add to an intensely sinister and nightmarish reality that does an amazing job at mounting tension and giving you a jolt of terror.

The music has a very eerie 80s synth-pop slash modern era dubstep hybrid feel to it, giving the game itself this ever-present dark cloud that looms constantly, ever present and promising the player a carnival wrought with fear and blood. I can\x27t recommend highly enough the importance of playing this game with good audio equipment. The sound work on this game is truly topnotch. Playing at night in the dark with the volume cranked up really does induce goose bumps. Hearing a volatile scream echo in the hallways while walking through a multi-leveled abandon building is nerve wracking. The sounds of a Demolisher rounding his charge will make your blood curdle. And the infected toddlers in Sector 0..their cries will make you shutter.

Having enjoyed this genre since Resident Evil on Playstation, and with my all time favorite being The Last of Us, I would have to say that Dying Light is a serious contender for one of the greatest in the category. It is a superb experience, and it can truly be horrifying. The intense combat mechanics, the ominous music, the hyper-real visual effects and great voice work all make for one white-knuckle, high octane pulse pounding thrill ride. Remember: safety in numbers. Zombies are easy 1 on 1, but as soon as there is more than 1..the game changes, drastically.

Good night..and good luck./>

product_title: AmazonBasics Ultra Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_headline: Wow. It works. Just that simple, it works.
review_body:
This was my second attempt at using an HDTV Antenna and after utter failure the first time out I am thrilled with the Amazon Basics product. Prior to this I had tried an outdoor amplified antenna from another manufacturer with frustrating results. That system was mounted two stories high OUTSIDE and yet too often the channels I wanted to view were just downright un-watchable. We went back to cable, lasted for 6 months before the expense made me see red and I cut the cord again. Thought I would give antennas one more try and purchased the Ultra-Thin Amplified Indoor 50-mile model. I mounted this antenna on an interior wall ( not a window, not even a wall that was exterior on the other side) and about 12 feet off the floor. Soon as I turned on the TV, channels were showing up before I even had chance to run the Auto Select. After running Auto Select I have 36 watchable channels. After one week of use we have experienced no disruption while watching shows. Very happy.

Setup was super easy: Attach cable to TV, and hang antenna with double-sided stickers provided in kit. Plug power cable into inline-booster then plug into USB port on TV or use power adapter to plug into outlet(that\x27s what I did). Green LED on booster lets you know it\x27s on.

product_title: Sennheiser CX 2.00 In-Ear Canal Headset
review_headline: Great sound, nice price for Sennheisers.
review_body:
I normally don\x27t spend a lot of money on earbuds. I\x27ve been more than happy with my Sony Bumpin Buds [ASIN: B007BY3OTW]; which offer a great sound for the money. But I thought I\x27d splurge a little get something better, and something could be used with my phone for calls. First, don\x27t let the low reviews here dissuade you. If you check the Amazon UK site, the reviews are mostly positive 4-stars or higher. So it just goes to show different people have different preferences.

If you prefer boosted bass, then get a set of Beats or Skull Candy earphones. If you like to hear music the way it was intended, then consider these Sennheiser earphones. The sound is naturally flat. You an always use the sound settings or EQ on your phone to adjust the levels to your liking. Don\x27t have much else to say on the audio quality.

Other than for music or phone calls, these earphones can be used on laptops that have a combo earphone/mic jack. Pretty handy if you use Skype or other telephony applications. And the volume control on the chord works on the computer too!

One thing I don\x27t like about these earphones is the ear pieces. I think they\x27re made of silicone. They\x27re soft, but not soft enough. So they don\x27t quite stay in my ears too well. And they don\x27t quite block out environmental noises. So I did what another reviewer did, I swapped them out with some spare silicone ear pieces from my Sony earphones. Perfect. Now they stay in my ears and block out noises.

Highly recommend these. For the price, they sound great and look great. I just can\x27t justify paying more for the other Sennheiser earphones.

product_title: SMK-Link PS3 Blu-Link Universal Remote Control
review_headline: I bought one of these back when it first came ...
review_body:
I bought one of these back when it first came out (5 years ago or so) and just now finally replaced it with another. It did everything I needed it to do. I didn\xE2\x80\x99t care for the clickyness on some of the buttons, but that\xE2\x80\x99s a minor issue. The reason I replaced it was because some of the buttons started becoming unresponsive or difficult to operate. Even the \xE2\x80\x9CMenu\xE2\x80\x9D button lost its clickyness and almost felt collapsed. After I got my new one, I decided to tear down the old one to see if I could see what went wrong.

It was a simple matter of a single screw in the battery compartment and the two halves snapped apart. Once I took the rubber button panel off, I found a sticky slime-like substance. I washed off the underside of the buttons and wiped off the substance from the board and put it back together. After a couple of uses, it seemed to be working normally again. I\xE2\x80\x99m not entirely sure what this substance was, but I think it was some sort of adhesive that deteriorated over the years. There\xE2\x80\x99s a paper sticker/label on the underside of the remote and the glue that normally held it down also began to let go and become a similar sticky slime. Maybe it was the same material.

Hopefully if you run in to similar issues with your remote, consider taking it apart and giving it a cleaning before replacing it since no one else seems to make such a well-rounded Bluetooth remote for the PS3.

product_title: Orico PVU3-502U PCI-E expansion card 7xUSB3.0 (Blue)
review_body:
First, my qualifications. I am an electrical engineer with extensive design and programming experience. I have been building PCs since 1982, as a systems integrator and 3rd tier support engineer. I\x27m the guy people go to when they can\x27t get it to work correctly...

PC\x27s just don\x27t seem to have enough USB 3.0 ports to fill the need, so I looked around for a PCIe card to add some ports. The
Orico PVU3-502U PCIe adds 7 USB 3.0 ports, 5 external and 2 internal, which is plenty for most purposes. What is unique about this card is that there are 2 internal ports that use the standard USB connector instead of the 20-pin header found on most internal USB 3.0 ports. Since I had a front panel USB hub/card reader that uses standard USB connectors, this was an ideal choice. No need to route a USB cable outside the case to plug into an outside USB port!

The chipset is mature and bugs were worked out long ago. The driver is well-written, reliable and fast. I did not use, and do not recommend using the drivers provided with any card. There are almost always updated drivers available, so I usually download and install the latest drivers from the manufacturer\x27s web site. The downloaded driver installed without any problems. There have been no compatibility problems across a broad range of motherboards, running Windows 7, 8.0 and 8.1. I did not perform any benchmark tests, but have not noticed any significant speed issues.

I had no need to contact technical support, so I cannot attest to the card\x27s support, but you will most likely not need support. I liked the card so much that I ordered and installed more.

If you need an inexpensive and reliable USB 3.0 card, this is an excellent buy. I highly recommend it.

product_title: Klipsch RB-81 Reference II Two-Way Bookshelf Speaker - Black (Each)
review_headline: Amazing, large, loud, and a quality pair of bookshelf speakers
review_body: Amazing pair of bookshelf speakers. The first impression, that most would get as I would assume, is the surprise in its size.  These Klipschs\x27s are big, and I mean big.  I have yet to see many bookshelf speakers of this size.  However, with a big build means big sound.  The low end on these are great, I find myself listening to music with these a lot without the use of my subwoofer.  Though for movies a sub is always good to have! Never cheat out on a sub if you want a good movie experience no matter how large the speaker!  These are currently used in a 2.1 system (mainly used for music) paired with a 12\x5C\x22 Reference sub and they go together so well.  One thing I\x27ve noticed about these speakers, and a majority of Klipsch speakers in general, is that the treble is a bit harsh.  This is a pretty common criticism that Klipsch receives but that can be easily fixed by tweaking with the treble.  Before I purchased these I had the 5\x5C\x22 Reference bookshelfs and though they were great, but eventually I wanted something more powerful, and these deliver.  Great punch on the mids, shimmering highs, and astonishing clarity.  I can only speak for these on music because that is my main usage for them, but I\x27ve watched movies here and there with them and they sound amazing.  I cannot say these can replace floorstanding speakers, but they for sure have much greater output than many bookshelf speakers.  I got these at a crazy deal of $280 for both, but even at the current price Amazon is selling for, I would buy without any hesitation.  For those who are on the edge of buying these, I can assure you these will not disappoint for the given price.  However, do keep in mind of the size of these, if you are planning on using these in a small room or bedroom, these could be just too overpowering.  In the end, these speakers are wonderful.  When you listen to these and indulge yourself with your favorite soundtrack, you forget that these are made in China, you forget about their abnormal size,these offer you a fullness in sound that I have not experienced in many bookshelf speakers at this price point. Highly recommended.

review_headline: Finally an HDTV Antenna That Works
review_body: I live by LAX and have been looking for a while for an antenna that worked. I\x27ve gone through a Mohu Leaf, a Terk HDTVa Antenna Pro, cheap rabbit ears, nothing worked. I got the ClearStream 2V, put it together without the mount in about 15 minutes. Tied a strong piece of twine to the reflector and hung it up on a nail in my apartment. Now not even the airplanes flying over head interfere with the signal. I get about 20 more channels than before with a solid signal and of those 20 new channels about 15 I don\x27t really want to watch but I have that option now. No fiddling around with the antenna, the channels are clear the way they were meant to be. Only thing that might make a difference for someone else is that I live on the second floor of my apartment building. Not sure if the antenna being mounted high up on the wall makes a difference. I did have to find the sweet spot for "the nail" to hang the antenna from to receive the best signal. So far, I\x27m really happy with this antenna. Finally OTA HDTV the way it was supposed to be!

product_title: GForce GF-P1124-918 Heavy Duty Tilt TV Wall Mount For 26\x22- 47\x22 LED / LCD / Plasma Flat Screen TVs With Max VESA 400x400
review_body:
The mount works exactly as described. It will hold the weight of any TV less than 50". It really depends on the weight of your TV. I mounted a 32-inch, 25 pound TV and it handles the load easily. I would feel confident mounting a TV that was 2-3 times heavier. Your only real limitation here is the bolt mounting pattern on the back of your TV. Mine was 200mm x 200mm, and this one supports TVs up to a 400mm square bolt pattern. Just put a ruler on the back of your TV to measure the mount pattern before you buy.

The bubble level on my mount worked perfectly. I checked with my own level to be sure - I recommend anyone do that with any level they are using.
The tilt works exactly as described as well.

Also it\x27s worth noting that the base plate that mounts to the wall is long enough to reach two studs - allowing for four lag bolts to be used into studs that are spaced 18" apart. For those of us with the standard stud setup it is really great. Getting all 4 supplied lag bolts into your studs will guarantee your TV will not go anywhere once you hang it.

I am very happy with this mount and would not hesitate to buy more should the need arise.

product_title: C&C BK Amplifier Portable Headphone battery Amplifier
review_body: I\x27m using this with an iBasso DX50.  Awesome combination.  The directions for this unit are in Chinese so be for-warned.  The labels for the controls on the unit are quite criptic.  Best to learn the controls by experimenting.  I can say that "GC" is for Gain Control, "LF" appears to be a bass control, and "SF" appears to be a dynamic EQ setting.  With all three set to "ON"  the unit sounds fantastic.  I don\x27t have enough time for battery life but I have see other reviewers state of 40+ hours per charge.  The unit advertises 80+ hours so so your mileage may vary.  The unit is quite compact and manageable.  The fly in the ointment would be quality of construction. The case is either painted or powered code.  Out of the box there are pits and paint finish problems.  The construction as a whole is un-sightly as the Allen head screws don\x27t fit flush, and jacks are not exactly centered in the end plate holes.The rotary knob for the volume is also not quality finished.  I\x27m not a huge fan of the LED indicate which is old-school stoplight green or stoplight red depending on the unit\x27s operations state.  I have not seen these type of LEDs in years so perhaps refreshing for some, but not so much for myself.  I would also point out that if the Allen head screws are mild steel, which they appear to be rust problems may occur down the road if humidity is high enough.  Perhaps the fit and finish can be overlooked if the unit is user serviceable which I suspect that it may be although probably against the wishes of C&C.  However the end plates appear to be removable which would indicate that the unit could accept mods and the battery can be replaced down the road.  I will cross that bridge down the road.  All said this unit would still be a definite buy.

review_headline: my wife and I could not be happier! The installation is fast
review_body: This is the 10th Sonos component we have "invested" in. They are not cheap. However, my wife and I could not be happier! Apple should either buy SONOS or get with them on a solid iTunes integration. We find we need iTunes less and less. SONOS is our go to audio platform these days. I would buy an outside speaker if they had one. Using the bridge with third party speakers for weather proof speakers is sub-optimal. SONOS has great sound and certainly good enough for aging ears like ours. The TV interface and Surround sound is a pleasant surprise. We often put live sports from the TV Sound Bar as well on the speakers around the house to avoid missing anything while we move around. A GREAT solution and while expensive, meets the value expectations we had going in. Buy one and you will certainly add more and soon!

product_title: Brainwavz S0 In-Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones Clearwavz Remote & Microphone Stereo Headphone Headset For iPhone iPad, iPod & Android Devices
review_headline: Good Audio for the Price Point (4+ Stars)
review_body:
Although these Brainwave earphones are marketed as "neutral," I would say that there\x27s a slight tip to the bass and away from the higher ranges. Vocals aren\x27t as crystalline as I\x27d like, but they still sound good, if a little rounded.

These are best for rock and pop or any other music that doesn\x27t depend on the precise distinction of individual instruments, although female pop artists can sound less impressive than with quality, higher-end earphones. In classical music, the violins aren\x27t as sharp as they are in real life, and female jazz vocalists are not sharply defined. But rock and pop sound great with these, especially given their price point. (You aren\x27t going to get high-fidelity with earphones under $50.) These compete really well with other earphones with similar retail prices, outdoing many.

I love that Brainwavz always includes a case with their earphones and headphones. These comes with a good selection of tips for fit -- get the right ones before you judge the sound quality because they must fit snugly in the ear canal. The hard, zippered case has two pouches and a detachable Velcro strap for keeping the cord organized.

These offer much better sound than cheap earphones. For their retail price, these are excellent. Note: I received a sample for review.

-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann

product_title: Definitive Technology ProMonitor 1000 Speaker
review_headline: Def Tech Speakers are One of the Best!!!
review_body: I\x27ve owned Def Tech speakers since 2000 and they are by far one of the best speakers on the market today. They are equal to Totem, Revel, B&W, Legacy, etc. I used to be a big fan of the "Mirage FRX" series of speakers. Which back then were a phenomenal full bodied speaker. As a matter of fact I still have them hooked up to the home theater system in my living room and they sound as good as the day after they began their "break in time". The day I heard the Def Techs I bought a 5.1 system. BP7002 in front, C/L/R2500 center, SM350 for rears and a SuperCube II subwoofer and they sounded great. Since one of the owners of Polk Audio(forget his name)left in 1990 and started up Definitive Technology, he designed and mastered the sound quality. I now have the same BP7002\x27s in front and they still sound as good as new, the same C/L/R2500 center and same as new, the same SM350\x27s I have moved to be my front height surrounds and also sound as good as new. Since then in 2011 I bought a pair of ProMon 1000 for my front width surrounds, another pair as my rear surrounds, a pair of ProMon 800 as my rear back surrounds and added another SuperCube II subwoofer and with my Denon AVR 3311CI the system sounds incredible. You will not find a better satellite speaker than the ProMon\x27s no matter what receiver or pre/pro w/amps you use of quality. I hooked up Lexicon\x27s receiver to these speakers to see if a $13k receiver makes a difference over a $1300 receiver. Which both are a quality receiver and there\x27s no difference considering they have the same bandwidth. Lexicon is a higher end receiver over the Denon but, you won\x27t listen to them that loud to notice the difference. Besides, the Denon is a more popular brand that sells more so, they have cheaper prices than what they are actually worth. Also if you are a Marantz fan, as I am both, it doesn\x27t matter which one you decide on because they are the same exact receiver. I don\x27t want to call anybody out but, the someone saidthat they hooked up their ProMon\x27s to their SuperCube and use that crossover but, don\x27t have enough bass. Hooking it up that way is perfectly fine but the SuperCube subwoofers have a great deal of bass. When running that high-end of a sub it requires a higher end sub cable(not the most expensive, just something in the midline price) you should only have to set the level control to 10 to 11 o\x27clock and have plenty of bass. I use 2 and they\x27re perfect at that setting. One DefTech sub would be plenty when set up correctly. Make sure to go into your receiver\x27s menu and check that the sub frequency is set at 80Hz or 60Hz if that sounds better to you.

review_headline: The JungleConcert headphones are perfect if you love that deep rumbling bass ...
review_body:
Find yourself listening to Hardwell, Dmitri Vegas, or the likes of Martin Garrix? JungleConcert lives up to its name and captures that jungle beat, that bass that\xE2\x80\x99s sometimes difficult to find. Unless you\xE2\x80\x99re willing to spend some real money on headphones, you\xE2\x80\x99re not going to find an all-around sound ... the clarity, a perfect soundstage (love this one), an exquisite surround sound experience.

Listening to \xE2\x80\x9CTsunami\xE2\x80\x9D was a real experience to say the least. The leather ear cups and padded headband offer up a lot of comfort for hours of listening, and I\xE2\x80\x99ve been listening to a lot of music with the JungleConcert headphones. These headphones lend themselves to genres that grind out that deep rumbling, thumping bass sound. House and Hip Hop are just a couple of them.

The soundstage is really decent and I love it when the sounds move rapidly from ear to ear. I can easily pick out the instruments. One good example would be Diplo & GTA\xE2\x80\x99s \xE2\x80\x9CBoy Oh Boy.\xE2\x80\x9D The beat is heavy, but I can pick out those voices and each instrument as each is added or moving away. However, when you move into genres that add voices in the mid- to upper-range areas, some of that clarity is lost.

\xE2\x96\xBA User guide

As I stressed, the sound is excellent in the lower ranges and if I were looking for something in a decent price range, I wouldn\xE2\x80\x99t hesitate to snag the JungleConcert headphones. I certainly don\xE2\x80\x99t fancy myself to be an audiophile by any means, but if you do you\xE2\x80\x99ll probably wish to take a pass and move on up the line in price.

There\xE2\x80\x99s no buzzing, static, nor muddling in those lower registers. It\xE2\x80\x99s a tough sound to capture in Bluetooth-enabled headphones, but the JungleConcert has done it. The noise isolation isn\xE2\x80\x99t bad and I didn\xE2\x80\x99t hear much of anything going on around me in the room when I had them on. With 85dB it\xE2\x80\x99s almost a given you won\xE2\x80\x99t hear a lot.

The overall quality of the JungleConcert headphones is very good, but one end of the spectrum is sacrificed for the other. Just make sure you like that deep bass, lower register instrumentation and you\xE2\x80\x99ll love these headphones. Pairing was easy, comfort factor high, and for once there was a thorough, comprehensive manual.

product_title: Tecsun PL880 Portable Digital PLL Dual Conversion AM/FM, Longwave & Shortwave Radio with SSB (Single Side Band) Reception
review_body:
I am a radio junkie and have been eyeing this radio for some time. I finally bought it and I have to say I am impressed. The first thing I checked was the firmware version which is the latest, 8820. It comes with a nice carrying case, ear buds, battery, wire antenna for shortwave and a usb charging cord. It does not come with a wall charger but if you have a wall usb plug that comes with most cell phones these days you will be fine. You can also charge it off any computer that has a usb. The radio usb is a mini not a micro. I use a old Motorola cell phone mini usb charger and that works just fine.
The first thing I noticed was how nice the sound is. FM radio sounds great for such a small speaker. I also tried some DXing of AM stations and I was impressed. It ranks up there with my original GE Superadio. You can change the bandwidth so you can null out close together stations. I know its has a good AM antenna because when I used it in conjunction with my Tecsun AN 200 tun-able loop radio there was very little difference in the reception. This is a good thing.
I have only had this for a couple of days but I am impressed with the selectivity on shortwave. Being able to pick upper or lower side band is great. I can pick up ham stations at night. I haven\x27t hooked up the external wire antenna yet but am impressed nonetheless so far with just the attached antenna.
The radio takes a 3.7v lithium battery. This battery is actually becoming more common. I have a couple extra that I use in a flashlight. You should have no problem finding extra if you want a spare.
The page function is nice. You hold down the buttons and it stores to memory whatever stations are in range. It works just like the ETM button on my tecsun Pl-380
There are features that are not shown in the owners manual. Google "PL-880 hidden features" to come up with pages devoted to these features.

I can see this becoming one of my favorites.

I would definitely recommend them if you\x27re not in a hurry, there is no cheaper way to get these headers. As others have noted, if you intend to break these into smaller pieces via cutting, count on breaking one pin on each cut as well. product_title: HDTV Antenna and Amplifier, Liger\xC2\xAE 50 Mile Range Ultra-Thin Indoor Antenna Plus Antenna Amplifier, Antenna Booster - Receive HD Television Signals for Free - Includes Adhesive & Stand
review_headline: Impressive antenna, though you may want to get one without an amplifier
review_body:
Wow, I was sure this wasn\x27t going to work. I tried an unamplified HDTV antenna recently and got 0 channels. When I plugged this one in, it was about 7 feet too short to reach my window, so I just put it on the floor. I don\x27t even receive a cell phone signal indoors. So I start a scan for channels and it finds not 1, not 5, not 10, but 45 of them! Now, most of them aren\x27t usable and will probably improve when I change the position of the antenna, but I can actually see over half of them. About 15-20 are good enough to watch, and of those, maybe 4-6 of them I get clearly with no intermittent break up. Some are even in HD! I do live about 20 miles from a major city though, so if you\x27re in the middle of nowhere this will probably not work unless you have a station within 25 to 40 miles. The range is probably around 50 miles with a decent line of sight. I am probably getting a range of around 25 miles with the antenna indoors. One thing to note though is that I got similar reception with or without the amplifier, so I am not sure if it is actually doing anything despite claiming a boost from 30 to 50 miles in range. I did see one channel that has poor reception go from no picture to no picture + intermittent sound with the amplifier. I compared this amplifier to the Mohu amplifier and found that the Mohu amplifier was slightly better, but still not very good. With the Mohu amplifier, I managed to get intermittent picture as well as sound on that channel.

I compared this antenna to a Mohu Leaf Ultimate (now called Mohu Leaf 50):
The Mohu gets about 20% better reception but it costs about 40% more and is about 30% larger.
So this Liger antenna is much better value for the money, though it would be nice if the antenna was sold separately from the seemingly useless amplifier.

product_title: SVS SB2000 12\x22 500-watt Powered Subwoofer
review_headline: Everything I hoped it would be.
review_body: Wow! what a difference. No more booming bass. If you like booming bass that stands out from everything else, this sub is not for you. If you like very tight, controlled bass that sits in the mix like butter on toast this is your sub. I didn\x27t know what I was missing, the low frequency mud from my old sub was obscuring much more than just the bass line. Without those standing waves from the booming bass, the mid range is surprisingly better.  It takes a little getting used to hearing bass the way it is supposed to sound. The bass is never heavy no matter how loud it is. Listening to Nelly\x27s E.I. there are double hits on the electronic bass that it I didn\x27t know were there. The ship exploding in the beginning of Star wars episode 2 is visceral. This sub goes really low but its response begins to taper off below about 30 Hz. I have a Butt Kicker transducer under my couch that has a response that increases from about 30 Hz down to about 5 Hz. It is a match made in heaven. I put "Isolate It" isolators under the sub to prevent direct transfer to the floor and as a result the Butt Kicker and the SB2000 are tightly synchronized.  I use a Rolls bottom feeder to control the LFE gain, add a fair amount of sub octave synth and enhance the bass dynamics for the Butt Kicker.  I have digressed some but, the environment is important with a speaker review. If there is a better sub-woofer than this one, I am pretty sure it is not in my budget. If you dream of super tight bass like I did, don\x27t hesitate. Buy It.

Hook up was a breeze, though you may want to plan ahead as there are three connections to be made - the digital in, the RCA out, and the power.  I had to make a power strip more accessible.  I suppose longer digital or RCA cables could make it easier.  The product is very light so I have no issues with it simply hanging behind the furniture on which the TV stands.  The thing is light enough that a piece of velcro would easily hold it to the back of an audio cabinet or TV.  One day I will neaten things up a little!  Performance wise it does exactly what I needed it to do.  I was a bit worried about the different kinds of audio formats that may or may not come out of my TV digital audio out and the formats that the Orei may or may not handle (that\x27s what too much research can do!) but I decided to ignore that concern and I haven\x27t had a single problem.  Couldn\x27t ask for much more.

product_title: B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen4
review_headline: Sound, function and style.  Trademark B&O features shine with the H8.
review_body:
Right out of the box I noted the fit and finish of the H8 to be outstanding. I was impressed with how light they were for being cordless and with how classically simple the visual lines were. I also liked that the controls were paired down to one physical switch to turn on/off the Bluetooth and noise cancelling. I also appreciated the easily visible L and R symbols on the inside aspect of the ear pieces. Then, after breaking the H8s in for several hours, I test drove them for a day under different circumstance.

SOUND: Absolutely outstanding. The balance is amazing. Bass, mids and highs all combined to create a sound stage that made me feel like I was there. Across all genres of music I was impressed with the ability of the H8s to present unbiased and enjoyable listening. There is ample and full bass without being muddy or thumping. The highs are crisp but not harsh. Mids are full and not brassy. In short, nothing gets stepped on or washed out - making for an incredible listening experience.

NOISE CANCELLING: Again outstanding. While standing next to a noisy kitchen fan or sitting on a porch with cars driving by, the H8s virtually eliminated the extraneous noise with no music playing and made unwanted outside noise unnoticeable while listening to music.

CONTROLS: I found the controls to be very intuitive and very responsive. The surface of the right ear piece is touch sensitive and by touching or swiping I could easily change volume, change tracks, and activate and deactivate the noise cancelling. I especially appreciated how finely the volume adjusts. Each forward circle with my finger on the earpiece gently moved up the volume, making fine tuning easy and without sudden or loud surprises.

BLUETOOTH: Pairing was easy, as you would expect. All of the controls worked well with my Galaxy S5. A big plus was the synchronization of audio and video while watching an MP4 file was perfect. There was no detectable lag with the audio track that I have experienced with many other Bluetooth devices.

COMFORT: I am a hard sell for on ear headphones. I generally find them uncomfortable. The H8s however are quite comfortable for an on ear variety. I would say they hit the sweet spot for size and comfort.

Whether I listened to Strauss Op.30, John Coltrane playing sax, Adele singing or Metallica rocking, I was consistently impressed with these B&O headphones. The combination of style, comfort and - most importantly - sound is a real winner for these high end headphones. If you are at the point where you think life is too short for inferior music listening, you should check these out. I am taking these on a plane with me tomorrow and can\x27t wait to see who they handle that noise level.I have experienced with many other Bluetooth devices. product_title: Fosmon 3-Port HDMI Switch with Pigtail Cable
review_body:
Well, I don\x27t know if we got a defective product or if we just don\x27t understand how to use it. We cannot return it as we bought it in the US and brought it with us to Brazil to use. That being said, everything (except for the cable box) that we were trying to use this for is also originally from the States.

What would happen was quite bizarre. One port would pick up my AppleTV, but give an error saying that it wasn\x27t supported. Another port would pick up the Apple TV and work fine, and the other port wouldn\x27t pick up the Apple TV at all. This was the same for the cable box, except we could get picture but no sound. The only place we could get sound is the same port that the Apple TV worked. And our LG DVD player, gave similar errors as the Apple TV, and didn\x27t work fully on any port. We had to give up and just keep our current set up, instead of having all of our devices on HDMI.

I checked all over the internet to see if there were other problems like this, or to see if there was a list of supported devices for this HDMI switch, but I couldn\x27t find anything.

The only reason I am giving this two stars is because it is possible we simply have a faulty device, and if we were able to get it returned and replaced, it would work just fine.

product_title: Bluetooth 4.0 Transmitter, TaoTronics Wireless Transmitter for TV with 3.5mm Adapter & USB Dongle (High-Fidelity Stereo, Plug and Play via USB or AUX Input, Charging While Playing for TV & iPod)
review_headline: Useful upgrade to any audio setup
review_body:
The TaoTronics\xC2\xAE Bluetooth 4.0 Wireless Stereo Transmitter is a small audio transmitter which adds smart bluetooth connectivity to any audio device. This product was provided by TaoTronics for review purposes.

I am one of those people that hate wires especially when it comes to headphones. When lying in bed or walking around the room I really don\x27t want to have a long cable running through the room. This bluetooth transmitter allows to wirelessly send your audio signal to any bluetooth headphones or speakers.

The package includes the Bluetooth Audio Transmitter, 3.55 mm audio cable, 3.55 mm to RCA adapter, USB cable and a user manual. The sound quality is perfectly clear and I could not hear any distortions. The connection is is stable and the range is excellent. The built in battery is handy but in my scenario (connected to my receiver) not necessary. My headphones connect to it without issues even though it takes sometimes longer than I would like (1-2m). The build quality is good even though it\x27s made of plastic.

Overall I could not find any major negative points when reviewing this bluetooth adapter. For the small price you can upgrade any older device to todays standards. The only feature I would like the manufacturer to improve is the connection speed but other transmitters I have tested have the same problems. I can highly recommend this product to anyone looking to wirelessly connect devices to your audio receiver.

product_title: Asgard 2 Headphone Amplifier
review_headline: A warm friend on a cold day.
review_body: A warm friend on a cold day.  I just received my Asgard 2, plugged it in, and ... it\x27s better than I hoped.  I considered Schitt products because of a review by Linus Sebastian on Linus Tech Tips.  As I shopped Amazon, I was impressed by Asgard 2\x27s price, that it\x27s a Class A amp, and has outputs so I can run external speakers (I can\x27t wear headphones all the time).  I plugged in my DAC, put in a 1983 recording of Leonard Bernstein conducting Appalachian Spring at the LA Philharmonic - and it seemed new to me.  Warm.  Wide.  Intimate.  Deep.  On the same album, Samuel Barber\x27s Adagio for Strings is always moving had a sharpness that cut.  For a change, I put in Annie Lennox\x27s DIVA.  Lush.  Powerful.  Punchy.  Paul Simon\x27s GRACELAND is luscious, sweet, complex.  These descriptions are emotional and sensuous - and isn\x27t music supposed to be that and more?  I didn\x27t notice any coloring by the Asgard 2, so much as I experienced the MUSIC itself.  Is that Schitt?  Maybe.  Regardless, I love my Asgard 2 and won\x27t give it back.  I highly recommend the Asgard 2 for your consideration if you are looking for a headphone amp or pre-amp.

product_title: Jensen JTA-222 3-Speed Turntable
review_body:
I know.

You\x27re looking for a small turntable to play your old records on. maybe get some new ones - but don\x27t want to get a receiver, speakers, etc. "Small footprint" and all that. You looked at the Croselys and then saw this as the top rated turntable and desire to "Add to Cart."

Don\x27t. I have been living with this since Christmas. It skips over both new records and old-- clean or dirty. You can tape a nickel or dime to the arm and try to make it track right. It will fool you into thinking you somehow got it calibrated correctly with your dime, nickel and scotch tape on one record then skip like crazy on the other. The speakers are extremely tinny - but you can hook up ext. speakers which sound pretty decent.

Until the record skips again, after you just cleaned it and did your fifteenth nickel and dime trick with the arm.

Want a decent small turntable with a small footprint? Save your fifty bucks and get a Audio-Technica LP60 turntable and a set of Audioengine A2+ speakers. You won\x27t need a seperate reciver - the speakers are self powered and hook right up to the turntable. Together they run about 350 bucks, but it is well worth it if you want to listen to your music with having a nervous breakdown.

product_title: Emotiva XPA-2 Stereo Power Amplifier
review_headline: Good budget minded amplifier but certainly not an audiophile amplifier.
review_body: Update 2-6-2015: I had to update this to a 4 star as it sounds pretty good through my cheap Klipsch KF-28 speakers. Really brings out sounds I had not heard before. I guess they just needed the extra power. Also the buzz\x5Chiss I complained about is so minor even with these 98db sensitivity speakers that it is almost not worth mentioning. That is not the case with the XPA-5 gen 2 I have which has considerably louder hiss and buzz with 94db sensitivity speakers. This amp for me is a for sure buy now and has really brought my 7.1 system to life when watching movies.     I would have given this 5 stars if this was not my second one replacing the first one that had an issue with the cooling fins or something making loud pings every 2 hours or so. It was like someone hitting the cooling fins with a tiny metal hammer. Clearly sounded like a expansion issue causing the metal to ping loudly. I sent it back and got a new one after posting a question here to see if that was happening to others which it was not.    Now for the review. This amplifier is a good budget amplifier. So if you are looking for an amp that will give your speakers the power to play more of their full range on a budget this is the amp. My NAD T748 just didn\x27t have the power to push my front speakers properly. Using it as a pre-amp with this amp my speakers have now come to life. They will now play bass and their full range. I also have the Emotiva XPA-5 to power my surround speakers. That brought them to life as well.    Now for the bad. This amp is not perfectly quiet like my other power amps (NAD and B&K Components) though it is quieter than the XPA-5 even with more sensitive speakers on the XPA-2 than the XPA-5. If you run all Klipsch high sensitivity speakers like I do expect some buzz\x5Chiss. I am not even running expensive Klipsch speakers either. They are R-15M Klipsch bookshelves for the surrounds a Klipsch RC-52 II reference series center and KF-28 floorstanding speakers for the fronts. Just a cheap7.1 surround system so I was not willing to pay anymore for the power amps and not willing to buy used.    Pros  - Feels and looks well built  - Brings my speakers to life compared to my underpowered AVR. In fact I would be willing to bet it will make all AVRs sound better as their power ratings are always overrated and only rated with 2 channels driven. They drop significantly when all channels are driven so don\x27t believe ratings.    Cons  - Very large and heavy so you will most likely need a new cabinet to hold it  - Buzz\x5Chiss on sensitive speakers  - Build quality is suspect as my first XPA-2 was making loud clicking noises coming from the heating fins. Hopefully the 5 year warranty means that I just got a bad one and this will last.    I would still recommend this amplifier if you are looking for a budget minded upgrade to your AVR powered system.

product_title: Sonic Alert SB300SS Sonic Boom Loud Vibrating Alarm Clock with Large Display
review_headline: Loud Alarm Clock with one Minor Inconvenience and comparison to Sonic Alert SBD375ss Sonic Boom Dual Alarm Vibrating Alarm Clock
review_body:
My family is full of deep sleepers so we tried both this and the Sonic Alert SBD375ss Sonic Boom Dual Alarm Vibrating Alarm Clock. We like both just fine, preferring this model over the Dual Alarm model. The good thing is both do their jobs well with alarms that you can adjust so that they are optimal for waking you up.

But both have a slight drawback I wish they would change in the next model--they both are a bit inconvenient when changing the time you want the alarm to go off--with the SB300 being slightly less annoying than the SBD375ss.

For the Sonic Alert SB300 Sonic Boom Loud Vibrating Alarm Clock with Large Display, i.e. this model, the buttons for changing the alarm time (with separate hour and minutes buttons) are on the BACK of the alarm. Slightly annoying because you cannot look at the button you are pressing and see the time adjust on the clock at the same time. Also, since the buttons are on the back of the alarm, I always have to flip the alarm over to find the change alarm minute or change alarm hour button every single day.

For the Sonic Alert SBD375ss Sonic Boom Dual Alarm Vibrating Alarm Clock, the buttons for changing the alarm time are at the top of the device, so they are easier to find and see--but they only have a FAST and SLOW button for adjusting the alarm clock time, meaning it cycles through the times of the day either fast or slow. This is super annoying if you set your alarm for 8AM one day and then want the next day to be 7AM, because you have to cycle through slowly from 8AM for 23 hours until reaching 7AM, which is slow even on the \x5C\x22FAST\x5C\x22 adjusting button setting. Yes, you can set two alarms so you can have an alarm for 7am and 8am saved, but if you change the alarm time very often and have varying wake-up times throughout the week it gets to be quite a nuisance.

Since the SB300 is a bit easier to change alarm clock times, I prefer it. However, if there was an alarm that was just as loud with buttons to adjust time at the front or top of the clock, I\x27d buy that instead. Sadly, it does not exist.front or top of the clock, I\x27d buy that instead. Sadly, it does not exist.

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_body:
I purchased these after returning a pair of Audio Technia ATH-M50 I used for a month and then broke.

Initial impressions:
-Much lighter
-WAY more comfortable. I love the velour instead of the plastic ear cuffs. I typically use these in bed, listening to music or videos before going to sleep. So I fall asleep with them on. My ears would hurt in the morning with the M50s. Not these Sennheisers. Plus they are flatter which makes sleeping on my side with them against a pillow much better.
-The sound is warmer. Soundstage is way better.
-The bass is less. That\x27s a bummer.
-Sound leaks like crazy unless 1/3 volume or less. I knew this going in. My girlfriend hates it.
-Max volume is noticeably less loud
-I like the looks. It\x27s different.
-I don\x27t get much noise from the headphones themselves. My M50s made a lot of noise from the plastic parts twisting/moving/groaning.
-They come with the guitar style cord plug. Why?! I think that for the past 20+ years most people have only needed to use the mini jack. Why do so many headphone manufacturers insist on using the giant plug? And forcing us to use an adapter. These do come with an adapter, but it puts way too much mass on my iPhone and is likely to break (this is how my Audio Technias plug broke when my iPad fell off the bed, on the plug, bending it). I did buy the separate Sennheiser adapter which minimizes the problem some as it has a mini plug into the phone, a 4" length of cord, then the mini-plug to 1/4" adapter to headphone. But the best solution would be a "L" shaped mini plug going into the phone. Why do I have to do Quality Assurance for every company now-a-days? They should pay me...

I liked the sound, loudness, and bass of the Audio Technias, and their ability to fold up or lay flat. Other than that, the Sennheisers win.

I\x27m satisfied with these for now. I do feel that I need closed back headphones for some occasions. My earbuds will probably suffice for that.

*UPDATE* after 2 months:
The 1/4" to 1/8" adapter is bent from my iPad falling off the bed while plugged in. I suspected this would happen, and is how my Audio Technias broke.

I have these well broken in, and here is a review of how music sounds. I\x27m just hitting shuffle in my huge music collection:

1. Ensiferum\x27s self titled album. The headphones can\x27t keep up with the fast mid bass on most of these extreme Viking metal songs. Also, the electric guitars don\x27t "sizzle" the way I like, even at high volume. However, these headphones sounded great on the slower and acoustic guitar laiden "Eternal Wait" track.

2. "Do You Wanna Dance" by the Mamas & Papas. I\x27ve never heard this song sound this good. Lots of echo and reverb that I\x27ve never noticed before.

3. "Sharp Dressed Man" by ZZ Top. Wow! It\x27s like a remastered edition. I\x27m noticing details I\x27ve never heard before.

4. "Broom People" off the Mountain Goat\x27s Sunset Tree album sounds a little overcome by the bass.

5. "Summer of \x2769" by Bryan Adams sounds extremely clean.

6. "Danny Boy" by Celtic Woman. Amazing.

7. "Talkin\x27 Bout a Revolution" by Tracy Chapman sounds great, with a pronounced bass track.

8. "Goodbye Horses" by Q Lazzarus (LOL) sounds as good as it did in Buffalo Bill\x27s basement.

9. "Bold As Love" by Jimi Hendrix. Sounds like I\x27m listening to it on a hi-Fi stereo from the 70\x27s. In a good way.

10. "Jumble, Jumble" by the White Stripes. I never understood the pre-music background talking, but I can now tell you it is in French.

THESE HEADPHONES HAVE NEVER HURT MY EARS! Often, when listening fairly loud, my ears will crackle painfully. These headphones have never done that. Very smooth.

I don\x27t believe they reproduce bass well below 40hz. They suck for rap. They also do not do well with really fast bass beats, like in a lot of metal.

They excel at acoustic guitar, voices, detail, echo & reverb, and ambience.rb, and ambience.
