product_title: Koss KSC75 Portable Stereophone Headphones
review_headline: Fantastic for running but a huge design flaw.
review_body:
I have now purchased 7 pairs of these headphones. They are fantastic for running (or anything that gets you sweating) because they don\x27t allow sweat to accumulate in your ear the way plastic in ear buds do. They have a good sound for what they are and allow you to still hear what\x27s going on around you, to a degree. If I\x27m running, I want to be able to hear sirens, horns, someone yelling that they are passing me, or a dog getting ready to shred me to pieces.

So why 2 stars on such a fantastic running headphone? Because the wires constantly break down at the jack connection. as the wire moves around from your body moving, one of the two earphone wires eventually breaks down and you are left with one earphone. Not the worst thing in the world, except for one huge side effect. On most phone devices, when a wire is bad on a headphone, especially broken, the device reads the jack as either being lose or not in at all. So this will randomly shut off all sound to the headphones.

I\x27ve used many different style headphones on a daily basis for work and training and these have the highest rate of failure at the jack connection.

There is a lifetime warranty with Koss, however it will cost you $9, plus the cost to ship the headphones. So at $15 from Amazon, you are really only saving a couple bucks, but have to deal with the time of waiting for Koss to receive, process the return, and ship out another set. My suggestion is get a couple pairs and return when it breaks and use the back up. I return 3 at a time to save me on the shipping.

If it wasn\x27t for the faulty wiring and connection, this would be a superb 5 star product that should be owned by every runner, or active person.

product_title: Sony  Digital Media MP3 Player
review_headline: I expected much, much more from a genuine Walkman.
review_body: Sony provides two types of ear buds. One type for swimming and one for normal use. The swimming buds block water from entering a sound chamber in front of the driver and drowning out the sound altogether. Until you shake or blow any water out of that chamber, you\x27re not hearing anything. Unfortunately, the same "membrane" (it\x27s really just a thin rubber gate) that keeps the water out, also keeps much of the sound in. Consequently you\x27re hearing about half the volume you would if you had the regular buds on. This lower volume combined with splashing and the augmented sound of underwater breathing while swimming, makes these a poor solution for swimming. I want to love them, so, much, but the extra cost, slightly cumbersome fit, and poor swimming performance makes no sense. I would have thought Sony, the inventor of personal music devices, would have got this one right. Bottom line: they need a more powerful driver to push through the water in the sound chamber. I don\x27t need music for 8 hours in a pool. I need a sick beat for 90 minutes to get me through my workout, swim, and sauna.

product_title: Denon AVR-X4000 7.2-Channel 4K Ultra HD Networking Home Theater AV Receiver with AirPlay (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I upgraded my system with this unit and am happy I did. It took a while to figure out the very large amount of menu options and what they do. I had trouble with the "Audessy Equalizer" settings because most of the other menu settings will apply to all inputs when you set them but the Audessy settings will not, you have to set them for each input which snowed me for a while. My system is 7.1 with the Audessy set to manual equalizer and manual equalizer settings. The equalizer settings on the center and front speakers were set to -5db at 4KHZ and -3DB at 8KHZ to knock down the brightness of the Klipsch corner horns and Cornwall center. The sub (Klipsch RSW-12) and center channel set to LFE plus Center and the everything else in normal or flat position. The Dolby PLCIIx Music position was selected for a huge center stage presentation even in DTS. I drive the K-horns with another older Denon 2 channel receiver (55 watts per channel) because most of the newer receivers (politically fabricated power levels) just don\x27t have the balls for levels around 98 db SPL. This is the best setup I have ever had since 1965 for voice clarity and bass output which is basically indescribable. I am used to stomach rattling bass but this settup scared me at first.
All of my inputs (Bluray, DVD, CD, TV, D-VHS, HD-DVD, Phono, Betacam SP) route through this unit. I do have to use a magnifying glass and external light to read the print on the remote. A big button remote should be offered for old people.
I listen to the local FM-HD station every night at about 80DB SPL because I am fascinated by the voicing clarity of this unit. I have not tried using the automatic Audessy unit because I feel I don\x27t need to. This is the microphone that sets all your adjustments automatically to adjust for your room acoustics. This unit is warranted for 3 years which surprised me. This thing has bells and whistles that I probably will never use. My 1080P Sony TV (2006) passes through just fine with the HDMI cables.
I did have to buy some new cables, one for the sub which uses a one to two RCA connection and an optical cable for the TV input. It\x27s a lot easier to make adjustments for this unit viewing the 46" TV setup channel rather than the tiny viewing screen on the unit.
This is one of the best purchases I have ever made.
JJK

product_title: StarTech.com DisplayPort to DVI Video Adapter Converter Cable - M/M
review_headline: It really worked! But green line issues.
review_body:
I initially bought the Accell DisplayPort to DVI-D, and it would not work. My setup is:

- Sapphire Radeon HD 7950 3GB
- 3x Asus 25.5" 1200p 60hz monitors

My intention was to use it to run games such as Tera Online, Elite Dangerous, Star Citizen, etc.

After having struggled with the Accell, I was hesitant to see if the StarTech adapter would work, but it did! Almost immediately after plugging it into my computer, all three monitors popped to life. Using Catalyst to enable Eyefinity, then arranging the desktop playout properly, and I haven\x27t had any significant issues since. I can play all the games at respectable FPS (The 7950 is old, but still a lively beast) on medium/high quality, though I tend to stick to medium in order to ensure good FPS still.

One of the issues I\x27m having (not too huge an issue but hurts gaming immersion) is that on areas with perfect black (lots of those space sims have that often, if you can imagine!) my left monitor (the one with the displayport) and sometimes my right.. or all of them actually (but mainly the left), will have green lines flickering horizontally across the screen. This is for areas that are supposed to be perfectly black. If I switch out of the game or bring up something that has color (planet, menu, etc) the flickering stops, but will continue afterwards. I\x27m not sure why. But for now, the displayport is holding up marvelously. And at such a low cost!

Also, for those of you with my same setup (or approximately), I use Catalyst to boost my card. +20% power, 1200mhz OC, 1350 memory OC, 50% manual fan speed. Works like a charm, and significantly improves my FPS across all my games with minimal increase to heat.

product_title: Insignia NS-STR514 200W Stereo Receiver With Bluetooth
review_body: My rating is for an open-box (looks new) Insignia NS-STR514 with Polk Audio RT25I bookshelf speakers and a Sony SA-WM20 sub-woofer.  I have had the receiver for one week and am very pleased with it. At first I was going to give the receiver a 4 rather than a 5 because it looked like the unit did not have a dedicated speaker output for a sub-woofer. (So, I ran the speaker wires through the my Sony sub-woofer first and then back out to the L/R speakers, which is working well.) My misunderstanding was because the instruction manual first indicates that you can only select the A/B speaker switch for one pair of speakers at a time, but the remote allows you to select both at once, or one or the other, or none, which is very versatile.  The manual eventually describes those additional speaker options along with the remote control instructions. (My mistake for not seeing that sooner.)  In fact, the remote control offers many options that are not available (that I see) on the face of the receiver. For example bass and treble controls; display dimmer control and sleep timer among others. Bluetooth controls for connection, pause/play and skip back/forward are also on the remote; if that\x27s what you happen to have in hand rather than phone/tablet - it\x27s a great feature. The Bluetooth has excellent range and can detect my phone and tablet from 2 or 3 rooms away, which pleasantly surprised me. The Bluetooth finds and connects with devices rapidly and clearly. One thing to bear in mind is the quality of the source music. It makes a tremendous difference in sound quality when using poor quality mp3 or slow internet degrades Pandora/Spotify streaming quality. The other thing that is great about the Bluetooth connection is that it is not line-of-sight. This means that I can control the music from our dining room table which is around the corner from the room where the music is playing. Of course the most important issue is the sound quality: the Insignia does not sound as rich as myOnkyo receiver, but it was a third of the price. That being said, it sounds very good with the speakers that I have connected to it.  The receiver runs cool, which means it should last well. My favorite feature is the Bluetooth.

product_title: Nakamichi Wireless Speaker BTSP-70 Bluetooth Speaker Gray/White
review_headline: Great speaker with initial pairing issues for me & non-existent customer service from Nakamichi.
review_body:
I purchased this BTSP70 Nakamichi wireless speaker because of all its positive reviews. I had to also purchase a USB bluetooth adapter so that my non BT laptop and PC could pair with this speaker. I purchased the Kinivo BTD-400 adapter here on Amazon as well. Here is the review I\x27ve left regarding the Kinivo adapter which review would also apply here and should be considered if having problems getting this speaker to pair with your PC or laptop. It took me two days trying to solve my non-pairing issue using all the comments from Amazon reviewers on both this speaker as well as the Kinivo adapter.

So important to note that if you\x27re having problems pairing your device using this Kinivo BTD-400 adapter as I and several other reviewers did, the first thing you should do is to turn off the bluetooth settings on your nearby bluetooth enabled devices, like my Kindle HDX7 or Apple iPhone. My Namakichi BTSP70 speaker was "undiscoverable" to my PC when trying, for two days with all kinds of different suggestions, to pair because its signal was interrupted by my nearby Kindle\x27s BT "on" setting.
Kinivo has GREAT phone customer service. 1-855-454-6486 Pacific Time. Their rep was knowledgeable and very helpful and did succeed in helping me out. Nakamichi\x27s pathetic little manual, which, incidentally, is not offered online, gave no troubleshooting advice regarding my non-pairing issue. Since Nakamichi is located in Dubai, they have no customer service to offer at all except for an email contact address on their website. Two days after I emailed them, I got a response, saying they were unable to offer any help to me other than the information which appears in their manual under "Troubleshooting" and that they have nothing to do with Amazon or other vendors offering their speaker. If this was not satisfactory to me, I should return the speaker as "defective" and ask for a replacement. If I had returned the speaker, I still would havehad the non-pairing issue. I am amazed that their customer support rep would write such a thing without offering to help or realizing that the issue, which Kinivo discovered, was with the bluetooth settiing being turned "on" on my nearby Kindle while trying to pair the speaker, rather than with the speaker itself. He closed by saying "I\x27ve heard the speaker has amazing sound". His job is customer support and he hadn\x27t even listened to the speaker in question? Really pathetic, starting with the tiny non-informative manual and ending with non-existent customer service. However, once paired, the sound on the speaker is really great! I would definitely recommend it to anyone and hope the above comments will help anyone who is experiencing problems trying to pair this speaker with their adapter/PC/laptop. Just be certain that the bluetooth setting on your other BT devices nearby is turned off when pairing your new Nakamichi wireless speaker.

So, as a result, I give this product five stars! My speaker is working perfectly and wirelessly!

product_title: B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen4
review_body:
I have been a film editor and post-production sound engineer for many years so manufacturers often ask me to beta test and evaluate their audio and video products. When I\x27m editing video or audio I often have to wear headphones for 10-12 hours at a stretch so I take headphones very seriously... you might even say that I\x27m a professional headphone-wearer. Over the years I\x27ve product-tested close to a hundred headphones from $20 - $1000 and thanks to B&O I have a new favorite! My previous fav was the Senneheiser HD700 which is a remarkable pair of headphones, but these new BeoPlay H8 headphones have some features that elevate them to the top of my list.

First off, I generally don\x27t take packaging into consideration when I evaluate headphones, but the packaging for these is extremely sophisticated while being very efficient. The packaging really shows the headphones off to great effect... they are impressive from the moment you lay your eyes on them.

FIRST IMPRESSIONS:
* These headphones are beautiful - period. They have a graceful, flat leather band on top with firm padding underneath. The cans connect to the band with a brushed metal toggle joint allowing you to turn them to your chest when you aren\x27t listening to them. The cans have a slight toggle which provides comfort for a wide variety of head shapes. The leather ear pad is soft and gentle against your ears. While most of my high-end headphones cover the ear completely and are therefore, quite large, these manage to have an absolutely immersive sound without the size, weight or bulk.

* Right out of the box they are instantly usable, almost every feature is intuitively designed. Without even glancing at the manual I was able to pair the bluetooth with my computer and begin listening to music immediately. Turning the volume up or down took a minute to master - you place your right fingertip on the metal housing of the ear cup and make the \x5C\x22crazy sign\x5C\x22... you know, when you point your finger at your head and twirl it around to pantomime that someone is acting crazy. When you twirl your finger on the casing the volume slowly fades up and down as opposed to stepping up or down which never seems to put the volume where you want it. I didn\x27t have to do anything when a call came in - the music faded down and switched me over to my call. I tapped the left ear to hang up and it went right back to the music.

* The thing that really caught my attention with these is the bluetooth capability. This is the advancement I\x27ve been waiting for. I hate cables! Especially on headphones. I can\x27t tell you how many headphones I\x27ve ruined over the years when I\x27ve forgotten I had them on and walked away from whatever they were connected to ripping the cable out of them. (Luckily, I only tend to do that with lower-end headphones connected to video video cameras.) Regardless, any time I can cut a cable without losing quality I\x27m in! I\x27ve tried several bluetooth headphones in the past but the technology in Bluetooth 1.0 and 2.0 just wasn\x27t designed for audio. Even with Bluetooth 3.0 the compression that was used caused the sound to suffer in the transmission. I was very happy to read in the specs for these that they are using Bluetooth 4.0 and aptX compression which is the best that\x27s been developed so far and designed for an experience that is about as close to audiophile as you\x27re going to get wirelessly.

After using these I can attest to the shear pleasure of listening to music without cables. My high-end stereo doesn\x27t have bluetooth so I tested the bluetooth aspects of these headphones on my iPad listening mostly to tracks that were engineered for iTunes (better compression.) I also plugged them in to my stereo and listened to vinyl... shear brilliance! I\x27m currently waiting for my Pono player to arrive and I can\x27t wait to hear these plugged into a superior digital source.

SOUND QUALITY:
* You don\x27t spend this much on headphones if you aren\x27t extremely picky about the quality of the sound and these don\x27t disappoint. I started slowly - listening to Yo-Yo Ma playing Gabriel\x27s Oboe with the Rome Symphony and it was breath-taking. I could hear Ma\x27s barely audible breath as he played. The separation was almost infinitely nuanced. The highs shimmered with clarity and the lows were warm without even hinting at muddiness. I ran through a gamut of instrumental recordings from Joe Pass, Pat Metheny, Miles Davis, Keith Jarret, Gabriela & Rodrigo, Jobim Gilberto, the Amsterdam Guitar Trio, the London Symphony, and many more and with each one I was met with depth, clarity and warmth. Then I moved on to vocalists, Kathleen Battle, Frank Sinatra, Diana Krall, Andre Bocelli, Cesaria Evora, Ella Fitzgerald, Freddie Mercury, David Bowie, Pharrell Williams, Idina Menzel, and many more and found that these headphones support a wide range of vocal styles and dynamics without compromising the sound in any appreciable way. Even on bluetooth the sound is a delight to experience. (These headphones are so precise that I even heard flaws (grainy noise possibly from poor compression) in a Mimi Fox solo guitar recording of Wave that I had never been able to hear before.)

Warmth in an audio product is an important consideration - for work I use reference headphones that add absolutely no color to the sound allowing me to accurately add any nuance that\x27s missing or required to create a quality mix. While reference headphones are imperative for that kind of work, they are not generally pleasant to use for listening to music because they can sound too cold and crisp. On the other hand, audiophile headphones like these generally add a \x5C\x22little of this or that\x5C\x22 to the sound to enhance the listening experience - headphones for beats add varying degrees of enhancement (reverb, vibration, lower frequencies, etc.) to increase the feeling of the bass thumping in your chest, for instance. Flavoring the sound in this way is always a delicate balance - too much brightness, for example, and the music can sound cold, too much warmth and it starts losing nuance and clarity. The main reason that audiophile headphones are so expensive is because of the technology and expertise required to achieve something close to a perfect balance in the sound. These are one of the few headphones I\x27ve tried over the years that I couldn\x27t identify something a little off in the mix - something that I believe could have been done differently. These are about as flawless a sound as I\x27ve had the pleasure of hearing.

NOISE CANCELING
* The sound isolation on these is amazing for an on-the-ear design. The first time I used them to make a phone call I had to slip one of the ear cups off of my ear because I couldn\x27t hear my own voice enough to tell how loudly I was speaking! So even without B&O\x27s noise canceling filter turned on there is very little noise leak when you have these on. I can\x27t wait to try them on a plane.

CONCLUSION
I think it\x27s pretty obvious that I really enjoy these headphones. Even without Bluetooth capabilities these are extremely impressive headphones, but the ability to listen to music at this level of quality without wires is a real treat. The ability to switch between wired and wireless broadens the functionality of these headphones and allows them to be used for a truly audiophile experience as well as go-the-go.

I generally don\x27t \x5C\x22love\x5C\x22 products that I evaluate - I usually put myself in the mindset of a designer and look for the things I would have done differently to improve the product, but there is nothing that I would change about these headphones. There is, however, one thing I would have done differently in the overall packaging of the product - these come with a fabric bag to store or carry them in when you\x27re not using them or when you\x27re traveling - in this price range, on a productthat\x27s intended to be used on the go, I expected a more substantial case that would provide some level of protection when they are banging around inside a suitcase or bag.

I don\x27t know how it happened, but writing reviews has become a hobby of sorts for me, so I hope this review helps you in your assessment of this product. product_title: Audioquest DragonFly USB DAC Preamp Headphone Amp Version 1.2
review_body: I love good quality music. It is actually very difficult for me to enjoy music if the quality is lacking. I spend much of each day in my cube at work having my soul sucked out of me. Why not listen to good quality music as this is going on?  The work-issued business laptop, the HP Elitebook Intel i7 has a sound processor (yes...technical term) that [expletive] [expletive]. It\x27s so bad that if "IDT High Definition Audio" was a person I\x27d be groveling at its feet begging for mercy then pleading for Realtek to take me back! Yes...it\x27s that bad!  The DragonFly stick is about 2" long and constructed of a hard metal shell coated in a very soft, rubbery-like film. Great protection from any sort of EMI. For a little device it does have some weight to it. Using the DragonFly the sound is very powerful and clear and figuratively blows my on-board sound of said laptop out-of-the-water. However, swapping out listening between my Creative Sound Blaster Z at home and this I can\x27t really tell the difference. Because of my smarts I would wager that the "WOW" factor is much less or non-existent if you already have a good setup. For me this is OK because I just want good sound on-the-go. Speaking of "on-the-go", a little one-side open case is provided for storage and traveling. A last note, I have experienced zero static or interference of any kind.  So what I wanted was for good sound on-the-go and that is what I got. I wasn\x27t looking to replace an already good-sounding setup at home. If you already have a decent sounding setup then this may not provide the "WOW" factor you seek. It\x27s well constructed and relatively small making it convenient for travel. As others have stated, it pays to upgrade your headphones first THEN check out a DAC afterwards - I just already knew that my laptop sound was junk.  EDIT 2/26/15 - The shell is made of metal not plastic as I originally thought and still has the rubbery-like film coating; review has been updated.

It was a pain to loosed the moving arms, since you are always consciously thinking that if you loosen the nuts too much it may hinder the functionality of the mount. I had my wife assist me with placing the TV on the mount which was simple with the little knob they built into the plate. I made it loose enough for my wife to swing the TV and pull it out, angle it up or down. I actually placed this mount around an outlet and also made a cut out for wires to come up to the TV, to give the appearance of a "wireless" TV. I did not use the cable management system though just used zip ties in the slot to where the plastic covers would\x27ve snapped onto. At the end of the day I trust that this mount can support my TV even when I pull it out completely.

product_title: Sony MDRZX100 Headphones
review_body:
Long story short, these headphones aren\x27t very nice to look at but the sound quality is definitely there. I bought them as a spare pair to drag around with me to work in my backpack. The price was right so I figured I would give them a try.

I haven\x27t had mine for very long and they seem to be made of cheap plastic, but Sony products tend to last a long time, so I\x27m not sure about the life span of these. They are extremely comfortable and the ear pads seem to be well constructed. They are also very easily adjusted and can be changed around to fit your individual measurement. They are also extremely light weight and fairly compact so they can be easily transported.

The sound quality is good for the price; the bass is definitely there and the high notes sound just like they should. They leak sound like crazy so if you have a roommate, these headphones might make them want to evict you.

Overall, these are good for the price and make a very good back up pair of headphones to keep around the house. They are also good for toting around in a bag where they might get jostled a bit.

product_title: MOUNT FACTORY Articulating Swivel Full Motion TV Wall Mount Bracket for 22-42 inch TV
review_body:
This mount is incredibly strong. I was very pleased when receiving it. I had a mount previously from Walmart that had too much play in it and felt like it was going to snap. This thing feels like solid cast iron and is hard to move by itself without a TV on it.

Two things to be aware of:
1: When fully compressed, the mount is not centered on the mounting stud. If you plan on having the TV \x27pushed back\x27 against the wall when not pulled out or in use, be aware that it will be offset 5-6" to the left or right depending on which side you compress the mount to. In my situation, I have a stud directly in the middle of two windows with only 50 inchs of clearance. I was going to mount this dead center, but this would make my 40" TV have like 8" of clearance on one side, and very little on the other... I was in the middle of a remodel so installed a plywood backing board in bewteen the two studs so I could mount this offset so that it would be centered when compressed. Not everyone is going to tear their wall apart to do that, so just keep that in mind. The easy alternative to the whole "its not centered!!" situation is to pull the TV out just a little. At about 12" extended the mount will have the TV centered on the mounting stud (i needed mine flat though)
2: It comes with plastic shrouds to "jazz up" the look a little. You don\x27t realize it from the picture much, but these shrouds are very thin and cheap plastic. They aren\x27t really needed as they don\x27t make it look THAT much nicer, but just be aware that it\x27s probably best to CAREFULLY remove them prior to mounting. The middle shroud with 2 halves that has push to connect tabs can be broken easily.

Overall, it\x27s a great mount for the price and I wouldn\x27t remove a star for any of the things I\x27ve said.

product_title: B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen4
review_headline: Simply the best I\x27ve ever heard and customer service is outstanding!
review_body: The BeoPlay H8 headphones are wireless Bluetooth `phones with Active Noise Canceling and a built-in microphone making it possible to use them for iPhone voice and FaceTime calls. In short, they do pretty much everything I can imagine headphones doing.  I\x27m listening to Beethoven\x27s Third Symphony, Fourth Movement at the moment and the sound is phenomenal in its range and subtlety. The sound reproduction is what I would call "neutral" without the amped up bass so common with `phones aimed at the younger hip-hop crowd. These are headphones for grownups.  And I am a grownup.  The controls on the right ear pad are highly intuitive and it took me no time at all to navigate them with ease.  I\x27ve been a headphone junkie ever since my first encounter with a pair at a listening post in a Lafayette, Ind. music store around 1958. The ability to hear the music with proper dynamics and spatial imaging blew me away like no experience with speakers ever could.  I had a pair of David Clarks back in the late \x2760s and maybe a dozen pairs of various brands since then, but admittedly none in what I would call the serious audiophile range.  The Bang & Olufsen H8s are the best I\x27ve ever heard. They are showing me things in my music I never knew were there, which I consider the measure of great audio equipment. After a week of daily use, I continue to be amazed at the discoveries I\x27m making in virtually every piece of music in my library. It\x27s as if I\x27d never really heard most of the songs before - that\x27s how profound an improvement the H8s are over anything else I\x27ve used to listen to music.  The fit is comfortable enough to wear them for hours and the Active Noise Canceling is excellent. The materials and fit and finish are superb - exactly what you would expect from a $500 pair of headphones.  Mine came with a charged battery, so I was able to use them right out of the rather elegant box. They come with a carrying bag, USB charging cable and 3.5 mm mini-jack as an alternative towireless connectivity.  There was also an airplane adapter plug in the box. I don\x27t trust the bag to protect them, so I bought the GOcase F2 Headphone Case for Parrot Zik and Beoplay H6. The H8s are essentially the same shape and size as the H6s, but without an attached cable, so it\x27s a perfect fit and there\x27s a zippered pouch for the two cables that come with the H8 headphones.  Bang & Olufsen is a 90-year-old Danish consumer electronics company known for high quality audio products with distinctive design features. So far as I know, this is their first Bluetooth headphone offering and it sounds like they got it very very right.  The BeoPlay H8 headphones have an MSRP of $499, but I expect Amazon.com to offer them at a lower price eventually. It may seem excessive to spend this kind of money for headphones, but I can\x27t imagine anyone regretting this purchase.  At this writing, 17 of us have reviewed the H8 headphones and all but one reviewer has given them five stars. That speaks volumes about how impressive these headphones are.  *********************** June 29, 2016 - A note about Bang & Olufsen\x27s excellent customer service. My H8 headphones lost their Bluetooth connectivity a few weeks ago. After an exchange of emails with Bang & Olufsen\x27s customer service people, I shipped them to their repair facility in suburban Chicago. The conclusion was that my headphones should be replaced under warranty. The new headphones were shipped from Denmark a week ago today and arrived via UPS this afternoon. I can\x27t tell you how happy I am to get them. A special thank you to Betina U. Bertelsen and the B&O PLAY team their prompt assistance. The B&O customer service is first rate.  August 26, 2016 - Bang & Olufsen has created the Beoplay App for IOS and Android that lets your smartphone interface with your H8 of H7 headphones to tweak the sound. The ZIK Parrot headphones have had a similar, but somewhat more sophisticated app for several months. The Beoplay App also lets you connect with a pair of A2 Bluetooth speakers ($399 each) and assign left and right stereo channels to them.

product_title: Beats By Dr. Dre Solo HD 07400 On-Ear Headphone - Drenched in Black EA-MH9D2AM/A
review_body:
Beats are great headphones but are they worth $200?? Not really, at least in my opinion.. I have purchased several pair, few for me and a few for gifts.. I have always purchased mine on black friday for under $100.. For $100 they are amazing headphones!!! Few tips to keep an eye on

1.) Some reports speak of beats breaking.. Older beats did because they didn\x27t have a metal band inside the plastic to make them stronger.. At some point beats added this.. I believe it was right after the monster breakup but just to be sure I can promise all of the "Drenched" in color beats have this metal band!! This makes them very very very durable and premium headphones!

2.) Beats are designed for heavy bass music! Meaning they will sound better with rap, pop, and poppy rock. These solo beats produce no where close to "Premium" sound BUT for $100 - $150 headphones they do produce great sound for the price!

Beats are trendy, cool, colorful, and sound good.. this is why they are so popular but there are headphones that do sound much better and much lower cost than the standard retail of beats headphones.. If you can get beats on a good deal they are worth the price.. If you have a kid, friend, or anyone else who is asking for beats they probably want them for their cool factor.. I wouldn\x27t go cheap or even buy better headphones (Even if they cost more like Bose) if you are specifically asked for "Beats".. Again this is because of their cool factor and probably the majority of their customers want them because they are cool

The new drenched versions do not hold fingerprints! My favorite part!

Lastly, keep in mind that the cable that comes with them, while it works for android is designed for apple and iphone products.. The cable will work great for sound but the volume button and stuff might not work on android.. This is mentioned on the packaging!

All in all i would recommend beats as a premium headphone if you can find them at a good price.. the newer beats are very well made and they do sound great for $100 headphones.. If you have to buy them at full price of $200, they might not sound nearly as good as other $200 headphones but they are cool and trendyadphone if you can find them at a good price.. the newer beats are very well made and they do sound great for $100 headphones.. product_title: SOFTROUND Earpads, ear pads, ear cushion Replacement for Sony 211566803, Compatible with Sony MDR-7506, MDR-V6, MDR-CD900ST, Sony, etc. (Packaged 1 pair (2 pieces)) T018
review_headline: Fits and works as intended, but not as soft or high-quality as the original. Could be cheaper.
review_body:
I bought this to replace my Sony MDR V6 earpads, which had fallen apart from 3 years of use. The old pads started to flake off, and the fake leather covering had torn from the inside, exposing the yellow sponge inside. This actually made the headphones more comfortable, but at a severe cost to sound quality, where a lot of the low to mid frequencies were being attenuated by the exposed sponge.

I ordered these seeing the good reviews. These replacement earpads are definitely not original, and to be honest I was a bit disappointed with the quality. The material (for the ear) feels no more than a plastic material and definitely one step below the original. However, they looked ok, and I hope that they will soften after a few weeks of use.

As for size, I found the pads themselves to be a bit smaller than the original, but the fabric on the back used for wrapping around the headphone drivers felt nice and flexible, and they fit on the headphones perfectly otherwise. I found it easiest to use a small blunt tool (I used a blunt chopstick) to grab the fabric to hook onto the headphones. It takes a bit of practice but fits great otherwise.

Overall, definitely not as comfortable or as soft as the original, but works as intended at an affordable price (thought I suspect the other $3 to $5 alternatives on Amazon are probably better value than this $10 one). Regardless, the sound of my headphones went back to what I remembered them to be, with no more exposed sponge to attenuate the sound.

product_title: HD Frequency Cable Cutter Aerowave, Indoor Outdoor HD Digital TV Antenna (CC-17A)
review_body:
I reside in the suburbs of Adelaide, South Australia, located in the plains below the transmission towers on Mt Lofty, approximately 35km away as the crow flies. External antennae work very well in Adelaide, but indoor aerials do not. Over the years I have tried several different types of indoor antennae in a rented property with the usual mixed results of achieving some channels some of the time and other channels none of the time, all with fluctuating signal strengths and unstable pictures and dropouts.
Having reviewed the internet I discovered I was not alone virtually with similar stories from many countries; so I looked for reviews that were positive and the Cable Cutter HD Digital CC-17 stood out as a successful antenna in use in other parts of the world, but its performance was an unknown in Australia.
As it turned out, it was a gamble well worth taking as the CC-17 was an instant success and I achieved 28 channels immediately on the first TV scan and I have not bothered with subsequent scans as the channels I am interested in are all present, stable and crystal clear.
I scanned two TVs; first in a room with solid walls in the direction of transmission towers and second in another room with a window towards the towers and both worked brilliantly and flawlessly with only minor trial and error regarding the positioning of the CC-17.
To install the unit I needed an Ftype to coaxial adapter which I purchased on the net from Victoria Australia and received 4 adapters for A$6.
From my point of view I give the product 5 stars and recommend it for other applications in Adelaide and surrounds and I see no reason why it would not work successfully in other parts of Australia.

Verbatim seems content to sully part of their good name by getting into bed with CMC, as they keep outsourcing more of their media to them. Any Life series DVD\x27s or non DataLifePlus CD\x27s are CMC. Verbatim stopped making their own BD-RE\x27s and farmed them out to CMC.

If my memory serves me correctly, MCC 03RG20 is the same MID on Verbatim\x27s LightScribe DVD-R\x27s. I\x27ve been using them for 3 years without a single coaster. They play fine on the Playstation 3 and read data fine in my LG and Pioneer Blu-Ray burners. I\x27ve not tested these discs yet but I don\x27t expect an issue. However, because these are Verbatim inkjet, they may not properly burn in my Pioneer. Verbatim MKM inkjet DVD+R DL\x27s to burn the 2nd layer in the Pioneer, even though the branded, non inkjet Verbatim DVD+R DL\x27s of the same speed and the same MKM MID DO burn without issue in the Pioneer.

EDIT 02-12-2015: I burned one of these discs in my Pioneer and it burned, verified, and played fine in my PS3. It is probably the dual layer nature of the MKM discs that for whatever reason are the problem in my Pioneer.

review_headline: only one star for one very simple reason - Product ...
review_body:
only one star for one very simple reason - Product Description ! "Estone 5Ft 1.5m HDMI To 3-RCA Video Audio AV Component Converter Adapter Cable For HDTV DVD" ... note \x27Converter Adaptor\x27 . when I went to search for a way to hook up an HDMI blue ray player to my old school RCA input only TV , I accepted the description that this cable would \x27covert\x27 HDMI to RCA - of course this is not the case. I realize that now that I have bought it and hooked it up, it didn\x27t work. Then to search the web to find out I need a Digital to Analog converter.
I went back to the original PoP and noticed :
" Note:
1. The product conversion type is only HDMI to RCA.
2. The product is wire, not include chip.Only used for transport.
3. The cable HDIM to AV doesn\x27t have the conversion function. Only be used for the equipment that can output simultaneously HD digital audio & video signals,AV (CVBS) composite video signal and L / R stereo audio signals."

Even reading this - I would have thought it would work because of #1 (I don\x27t even understand # 2 and 3). That is because I took HDMI as being \x27Digital\x27 and RCA as being \x27Analog\x27 thus Digital to Analog Converter .. ANYWAY - bottom line - don\x27t buy it, in 99% of cases, this cable is not what you need. you need an HDMI to RCA converter - small box - costs about $15. plug the HDMI cable in one end and RCA cable in the other. Hope I have saved someone the time, trouble, and $7 with this review.

review_body:
Day 1 - my lovely new machine played only 2 out of 5 records without skipping - all brand new records just freshly opened with the amazon boxes still sitting on the kitchen floor to be taken out to the trash. Fine I\x27ll deal with it I thought, I know about the ghetto coin trick to add weight. I didn\x27t even do the coin trick yet, I figured I\x27d mess around with that tomorrow.

Day 2 - here\x27s where it went further downhill - records started slowing down, then going okay, then slowing down again - then eventually not spinning at all and the machine now rendered utterly useless. The tone arm being placed over the record no longer made the plate spin, so unfortunately it\x27s boxed up and had to return it. I tried screwing the mounting screw back and unscrewing it thinking it might not have been unpackaged correctly - but that was to no avail.

Overall I\x27m disappointed. I just wanted a nice all in one that didn\x27t have as many bad reviews that Crosley\x27s do for ruining records. I thought this might be the ticket. So I\x27ve reluctantly decided to spend more money on a better quality unit - maybe a Technics or Rega turntable and just get it setup with my sound system. I really wanted this to work and be done with it all, I loved the retro look and I was okay with an all in one type thing, and I didn\x27t want to spend more than this. I think I will be better off with a higher end unit anyways. If you manage to get one of these Electrohomes that works, great - its seems like it\x27s a possibility for many, but for me I don\x27t want to play games with multiple units shipping back and forth and hoping one works eventually. The radio worked fine, the CD player also worked fine, I didn\x27t have it long enough to try out the USB functionality. The speakers were very loud, not audiophile quality but loud and full sounding for a medium sized living room. I probably only had them cranked up about 30% and it was very loud. I was okay with the speakers when the thing worked. So goodluck - maybe you\x27ll get one that isn\x27t defective. I just don\x27t want to risk it and I want it to work from day 1.

product_title: B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen4
review_headline: Puts the Song in Your Head
review_body:
My previous experience with high quality headphones comes mostly from trying on family and friends\x27 \x27phones and testing random sets at demo stations at electronic stores. For the most part I\x27ve just been an ear buds guy - hardly a headphones connoisseur.

Even so, I know good sound when I hear it, and that\x27s what the H8s produce. Wow. When combined with the active noise cancellation, it\x27s just you and your music - crisp, crystal clear, rich, and absolutely in your head.

The active noise cancellation works well on its own. Loud noises are muted and softer sounds just disappear. You can\x27t help but talk in a louder-than-needed voice, and you\x27re rather at risk of being surprised by people who think you\x27ve heard their approach (this is especially true when you\x27re listening to music too!).

The H8s fit nicely and feel good on your ears. I have a large-ish head, and the \x27phones are comfortable on my noggin. On the other hand, my young daughters can wear them as well - the H8s smoothly adjust to fit them comfortably as well. The padded leather ear pieces are nice and soft.

Despite the comfortable fit, the H8s also feel solid. The metal components shift and swivel smoothly at the joints, and the span portion flexes nicely to adjust for various head sizes.

The Off / On / Bluetooth toggle is intuitive, and connecting the H8s to a Bluetooth device is straightforward (as is connecting to a device with the provided audio cable).

And now we reach our only complaint with these headphones: the aluminum touch interface isn\x27t flawless. The play / pause (just a tap starts and stops your audio) and the skip (swipe forward or back) work well, but turning on or off the active noise cancellation (swipe up to turn it on; swipe down to turn it off) and the volume control (spin your finger around the ear cup ... think old school iPod "spin wheel" that moved you through menus and such) don\x27t seem to be as accurate or as precise as we expected. That is, sometimes I swipe up ... and nothing happens. Sometimes I swipe up ... and I turn on the active noise control. Same for volume adjustments: something spinning my finger around the ear cup adjusts the volume ... sometimes it doesn\x27t. Obviously user error could be a factor; perhaps we\x27ll get better at these controls the more we use our H8s.

Oh - the wires (the audio cable and the USB recharging cable) and carrying bag are nice. They seem to be of decent quality (I saw reviewers complain about these for other Beo Play models). And the battery life appears to be good, though we haven\x27t yet timed exactly how much usage we get from a full charge.

Whether it\x27s a good value for the price, well ... these are clearly premium headphones. Bang & Olufsen have been making outstanding and beautiful audio products for a long time, and they knew what they were doing with the 8Hs.

product_title: Projector-Gear Projector Ceiling Mount for BENQ HT1075 HT1085ST MH630 MH680 MS612ST MS614
review_headline: A strong and easy to install ceiling mount for the BenQ HT1085ST
review_body:
I did extensive research on ceiling mounts for my BenQ HT1085ST projector. The most important features that fit my situation are: easy of use, simple/quick installation, flexible positioning, durable construction of the mount, and the ability to mount the projector close to the ceiling. The Projector-Gear mount met all of these requirements.

The item arrived with lightning speed and was well packed. The mount assembly is relatively lightweight, yet very strong. It is comprised of three pieces: a mounting plate that quickly attaches to the BenQ 1085 projector (this piece comes with three "risers" that elevate the mounting plate about a half inch or so above the projector, which gets mounted to the ceiling upside down - mounting holes are on the underside of the BenQ), a mounting plate that gets screwed into the ceiling (the plate has six pre-drilled holes that allow it to be attached to the ceiling using supplied wood screws for drilling into ceiling joists, and a set of toggle bolts to allow the plate to be attached to a drywall ceiling, and a short "neck" piece -- a section of metal about 2 inches long -- that attaches the projector to the ceiling plate via wing-nuts/bolts). The package includes mounting hardware (screws, toggle bolts, washers) and detailed directions with photos.

I cannot emphasis this enough: measure several times before drilling any holes into the ceiling. Mounting the projector in the precise position in relation to the screen is the key to success. I spent more time measuring and double/triple checking the placement location of the projector than I did assembling and attaching the Projector-Gear mount to the ceiling. The end result gave me exactly what I was looking for: a sleek, non-obtrusive mounting of my BenQ 1085 projector on my ceiling.

For those who need to mount their projector a bit lower from the ceiling, Projector-Gear offers optional extension rods on their website if needed (ordering information is included with the item). The seller has thought about everything to make mounting your projector to the ceiling as quick and easy as possible. Kudos to Projector-Gear for an excellent product. I could not be happier with this product. Highly recommended.

product_title: Sony MDR10RBT Bluetooth Wireless Headphones
review_headline: Great Wireless and Wired Sound Quality With Comfort
review_body: Sony makes good headphones as we use wired ones in our church contemporary service for accurate sound monitoring.  So, what do these Bluetooth Sony phones bring to the table?  First, accurate and pleasing fidelity in both wired and wireless modes.  The spectrum of highs to lows are simply well balanced while being fairly revealing (i.e. accurate).  The bass is really solid without any bloat or mid-range thickening.  Some may prefer a rising bass, but unless that is implemented only at the lowest octave I\x27d say it isn\x27t very welcome simply because it deviates from accuracy.  This is very close to the perfect bass as it seems natural and can even be authoritative if the music is mixed as such.  Across a wide variety of different music types, as well as piano and dialogue, there is a clarity of sound I find extremely pleasing.  As for the Bluetooth wireless reception/fidelity they shine.  Sony has engineered good range meeting the 30-foot distance staying connected as long as whatever transmitting device you mate them too is up to this.  So far I\x27ve never ran out of juice even after over 12-hours (the approximate time tested).  These are more comfortable and seal out more ambient noise than my previous Velodyne VFree phones (to be fair purchased on sale and at a far lower price which is fine as they\x27re not bad just all-around lesser phones).  The build quality is very good yet not the last word (i.e. more metal) as materials used are high-quality composites which provide the light-weight comfort with strength I believe Sony has aimed for. A Bose model I looked at recently while at Costco were less robustly constructed, noticeably less robustly built, and since they were on-ear types sealed out much less ambient sound (by design of course).  Overall, for the price I feel these are still as of late 2014 the wireless phone standard to beat, highly recommended.

product_title: Bose CineMate 520 Home Theater System
review_headline: * BOSE CINEMATE 520 REVIEW -- BAD PRODUCT PLANNING AND DESIGN *
review_body:
* BOSE CINEMATE 520 REVIEW *

Although I am (was?) a fan of Bose, this system truly disappoints. For the record, Bose customer service is very courteous and professional, but the problems with this product are beyond their control, unfortunately. I went through two CineMate 520 systems - original purchase + replacement unit - but the problems and shortfalls were the same. In the end, I\x27ve returned it. Here are its major flaws:

1. NO support for the high-resolution lossless audio formats - such as Dolby TrueHD, DTS-HD, FLAC, Apple Lossless, etc. Yes, mind boggling, but true. Yes, other sub-$200 surround systems support it, but not this $1,500 Bose. Yes, pretty much any $200-$300 surround and/or A/V Receiver support it nowadays, but not this $1,500 Bose system. Yes, such high-resolution audio formats have become very popular after being around for years. Yes, this is a brand new Bose system. No, you can\x27t even enjoy high-resolution audio produced by a simple $70 Blu-ray DVD player, Apple lossless music, or upcoming 4K content with high-res audio.

2. 4K video passthrough only supports 30Hz, not 60Hz. Again, this is provided by other very simple and inexpensive systems... but not this $1,500 Bose system. No 4K video upscalling either.

3. CEC feature (communication between devices connected by HDMI cable) is extremely buggy... before and after the latest firmware update (v 1.1.4 - up until December 2014). This could be fixed in the future, but until then, lots of frustration with communication issues between TV, cable box, DVD player, etc. Upgrading the firmware was painful too, both times I went through the process.

4. When playing multiple YouTube 5.1 surround audio/video tests, it seems that this surround system simply doesn\x27t work as it should. For instance, sound coming out of multiple speakers (i.e. 2 rights, or 2 lefts) when the test indicates that only one should be playing at a time.

5. Smart TV set to "Bistream Audio" (recommended for 5.1 home theater systems) doesn\x27t work properly... the audio gets chopped off. The solution is to turn TV audio output to "PCM", and not enjoy true surround sound - although this was already an issue, as noted above. In other words, your smart TV apps will suffer even more... Netflix, AmazonVideo, YouTube, etc.

6. There is no "back" button on the remote control. No, it\x27s not the same as the "last channel" button. Again, a major and simple flaw! That means navigating on AmazonVideo, YouTube, etc., will be painful, if only using the Bose remote control, since you can\x27t go back a single menu item. Therefore, adding this issue with the CEC issues, the idea of replacing all remote controls is not going to happen.

Indeed, very disappointing system overall. Certainly not the Bose standards, in my opinion. And by the way, as of 02/04/2015, Bose does not allow any reviews for this system in their website - hence is has ZERO reviews, after several months in the market.

review_headline: If you need technical support & good customer service.....DO NOT BUY THIS SONY AVR
review_body:
Firstly, I was a Sony audiophile supporter for many years, with purchases of several of their products including TV\x27s, AVR\x27s, DVD/CD players & recorders, phono\x27s, etc. , At least up until this defective AVR & terrible Sony technical support & customer service.

The only good thing from this experience was Amazon\x27s return policy & their good systems for making a return.

Sony had this AVR on sale just before this past Christmas at a competitive price with good options, if they work!
Right out of the box the second zone/surround back did not work, so the 7.1 calibration could not complete and in 5.1 setup there was no Zone 2, in either HDMI/digital or tuner/cd anaolg. I contacted Sony\x27s e-support who were untrained & knew nothing about how this new model worked. I continued chatting, emailing & calling Sony several times & was on the phone for hours finally working my way up to their level two technicians where I finally found someone who new this AVR, but they were not able to resolve the issue & were going to have their highest level technician call me back once they reviewed it. After no phone call from Sony\x27s technician I finally contacted Sony again, having to go through the whole story trying to get a high level technician who knew this AVR. The last tech agreed that the unit was defective & offered to repair this AVR, leaving me without any electronics for who knows how long. I told him this was not acceptable & asked him to transfer me to a customer service manager. He responded that he could not transfer me but would have a supervisor call me back in the next 3 to 4 days.

I was totally disgusted with Sony\x27s poor technical knowledge of their product & terrible customer service in not replacing this new defective AVR. This left me no choice but to return this unit to Amazon & start my purchase process again without Sony as an option.

(also the on screen setup would not show the HDMI\x27s were hooked up, although video was working... but not sure true surround sound was?).

After reviewing the other leading AVR producers & sellers I just purchased the Onkyo TX-NR 828, 4K, 7.2 AVR, from Crutchfield, an Amazon approved provider. I spoke to both Crutchfield\x27s technical & customer support teams in chat & by phone finding each of them fully trained & knowledgeable on all AVR\x27s.

product_title: HDE USB 2.0 Powered Battery Travel Charger for AA and AAA Rechargeable Batteries Adapter
review_headline: 75% of the power is purely wasted when you use 5V to charge 1
review_body:
This type of chargers work, but very inefficiently. My original plan was to use it to charge through the solar panel usb port so that I use some green energy. However, as someone pointed out, this is a direct bypass from usb to charge a 1.2-1.5V AA/AAA battery. As you can see, 75% of the power is purely wasted when you use 5V to charge 1.2V batteries.

A much better solution is to charge 3 AA batteries in series, or at least 2 in series. Assume the AA battery\x27s Voltage is at 1.25V and the USB is 5V. When you charge 2 batteries in series, only 50% of energy is wasted in conversion. When you charge 3, only 25% of the power is lost during the conversion (mostly in heat). The manufacturer would actually do a better job for the earth if they make the 2 battery slots in series, instead of in parallel.

It has a range of about 30 feet and I can listen to music on it outdoors with my phone or device indoors. In the summer I plan to stream music from the Amazon Cloud from my iPad indoors to the patio. The battery lasts just about 8 hours with a full charge. (I lost track of the exact time when I was testing it because of other things going on at the time.)

I like the sound. I tested it with classical music first because of the large range of instruments and tones. Brahms 2nd Symphony sounded rich and full. I also tested it listening to the album Title by Meghan Trainor, a country western playlist, and my Aerosmith playlist. All sounded great coming through this speaker.

The only thing I didn\x27t like about this speaker is that the port for the USB plug to recharge it and the 3.5mm audio cable connector are near the top, on the front, next to the volume and on/off and forwarded back buttons. I always use the Bluetooth rather than the 3.5mm connector, but I do often leave the speaker plugged into the wall and it looks kind of strange having the cables branching out from the top. It would look better having those ports on the bottom, in the back because with the brushed gold finish, this is a very attractive speaker.

product_title: Xpand 3D IR 3d Glasses single 1 pack (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: you may get something useful or something not-so-much
review_body:
If you order these glasses, you may get something useful or something not-so-much, depending on the seller you purchase them from. The item you *should* get it the XpanD Universal 3D glasses (Model X103), which are universal active shutter 3D glasses that work with most IR-based 3D TVs and projectors. And this is what I got when I ordered them from seller "Pioneer Distribution." But when I ordered the exact same item from seller "GG Global," I got glasses that looked similar, but were actually not universal.

The bad ones were labeled "HP" with an HP replacement part number of "622779-001" on the bridge. These glasses are also made by XpanD and look similar to the universal ones but they are specific to the HP Envy 3D laptop. They have no power/sync button on the bottom, or anywhere else, and they don\x27t work with any other 3D displays. I believe GG Global has mislabeled the product and is selling it with an incorrect description.

The correct item - *XpanD X103" - should work with most IR-based 3D displays. They didn\x27t work with my specific projector (a Panasonic PT-AE8000U) - they paired and created a 3D image, but there was excessive ghosting on the 3D image. So I\x27m returning them. XpanD also makes a Panasonic-specific version of the X103 glasses (X103-P2-G1) which I confirmed do work with my projector. But based on other reviews these Xpand Universal IR glasses do work with the first and second generation Panasonic plasma TVs and several others. According to the XPanD site (xpand.me), the glasses are compatible with select IR-based 3D TVs and projectors from B&O, HP, Hitachi, Epson Sim2, LG, Samsung, Sony, Panasonic, Toshiba and Philips as well as XpanD\x27s own IR emitter. Check the xpand web site for a full compatibility chart.

The X103 glasses are not rechargeable, but do come with a CR2032 battery inside plus a spare battery, each of which should last 40 hours, according to the manufacturer. The glasses also come with a cloth bag to store the glasses in when not in use. Be sure to look inside the small cardboard box inside the "egg" as that\x27s where the cloth bag, spare battery and extra nose pieces are hiding. It\x27s easy to miss as it looks like part of the packing material.

It\x27s important to note that most of today\x27s 3D displays use RF/Bluetooth to synch the glasses to the TV so these glasses will *not* work with 2012 model year (or later) TVs from Samsung, Panasonic, or any other manufacturer that switched to the universal Full HD 3D RF standard for 3D glasses. Be sure to check your manual or TV specs to make sure your display needs IR (Infrared) 3D glasses before you order these.

I\x27m including a picture which shows the two items I got when ordering this from Amazon. The correct item, which came from Pioneer Distribution is on the left in the egg-shaped packaging. Incidentally, I did a quick \x5C\x22reality check\x5C\x22 of some brand new cells...and--yes--new ones do test out as 1.6 V., so my educated guess about a full cell charge was correct. product_title: DSLRKIT 4AAA(LR03) to C Size Parallel Battery Adapter Holder (pack of 4)
review_body:
This product is just what I was looking for. It packs four AAA into a single C cell space. This particular format confers two main advantages that were important to me.

1. Capacity - One AAA has about 40% of the capacity of one AA. So four of them together is the equivalent of 1.6 AA batteries. That means it will last longer than adapters that are for a single AA cell.
2. Sizing - I\x27ve used Eneloop adapters before that convert a single AA. These are merely plastic housings that surround an AA. The original AA top and bottom are used for fit. Unfortunately, C cells must be ever so slightly larger because I have found that these adapters just did not work well. Contact was poor and they didn\x27t work in all cases. These adapters come with large top plates and bottom plates that give a much better fit for your devices.

I\x27m taking off a star because they did not work in one of my devices. The button tops are pointed domes. The device really needed a flat-top like you see on a typical C cell. If they could make that improvement to this product, I\x27d up it to five stars.

review_body:
I\x27m really torn between giving this headset two stars or three stars. I say three stars because it\x27s okay. It will do until I find something better. I say two stars because I don\x27t really like it; it will suffice until I find something more comfortable and functional. That said, this is why:
1. Mute fuction - being on conference calls most of my day, my major ask is for an external mute function (why, oh why can\x27t iPhone just give us a way to mute on the inline controller in the headphones?!). I thought this set would take care of that desire - BUT - once the mute function is activated (press the - button for 2 seconds until the tone is heard) there\x27s an annoying double beep every two seconds. I\x27d imagine this is to keep the user aware of the fact that they\x27re on mute, but it completely obscures the conversation making it impossible to hear what\x27s going on. Awful, awful, awful.
2. So uncomfortable - no matter how I adjust it, this thing presses the top of my earlobe into my skull. It\x27s like the center of gravity of the earpiece is off. My in-office headset is laid out similarly, but the pressure seems to center more on the center/bottom of my ear which, for me, is more easily handled. This thing hurts!
So - I\x27m still looking.

I got this as a Christmas gift and I use it quite a bit. It does the job I expected. However, I have two major complaints:

1. The default volume (which gets reset every time it is switched off and back on) is WAY TOO LOUD. Like, painfully loud. review_body: We recently downsized to a 2 bedroom condo. We brought with us an old Sony Bravia 40 inch LCD TV for the living room and purchased a new Sharp Aquos 39 inch model for the master bedroom. We had already successfully installed the Sharp with another full motion Sanus wall mount, but I was concerned about mounting the old Sony TV. First, it is much heavier than the newer models. Also, it is in a very constrained space, but needs to be viewable from a wide range of angles. Finally, we needed to mount it above a rather tall piece of furniture. I feared that I would not be able to find a full motion mount that could hold the weight of the Sony and tilt down enough for comfortable viewing. Following up on a tip given in a review of Sanus mounts, I used the Find-a-Mount tool on the Sanus web site and was able to get the perfect mount by searching on the TV make and model. I had a handyman install it. This TV is heavy and I would not have been able to mount it myself. He was able to install it in under an hour using the hardware it came with. It feels really solid. It is fully articulating. It can be rotated to any viewing angle we need and extended from the wall quite far to provide clearance for a large rotation angle. It also tilts down a good bit for perfect viewing. I highly recommend this mount for matching TV models.

product_title: SainSonic PAT-330 2.4G Wireless AV Sender Transmitter & Receiver 150M, Silver
review_headline: Good little set, beware of potential Wifi issues.
review_body:
These devices work well, however as others have mentioned, they do interfere with Wifi, as Wifi also interferes with them. I moved my router to a spot approximately twenty feet away and it did seem to alleviate the interference. Also there is not a lot of detail listed on setting the channel. The short of it is that the switches simply need to be set the same on both devices in order for them to talk. There are four dip switches on these devices giving a total of ten channels. Here is how it works: Switches are 1,2,3, and 4. add the numbers of the switches that are up and you get your channel number. e.g: 1, 2, and 4 are up. you get channel seven. This is important as the Wifi interference can be fixed by setting your router to use channel one or eleven and setting these to the opposite such as router on 1 and the sending/receiver to channel 10 as they both talk on the 2.4GHz band. Clearing this up in the manual would be a large plus. As a side note, if your Wifi devices and router support 5GHz, changing over to that will get rid of the problem completely. Unfortunately, not all of my devices are 5 capable. :( This aside, the devices run great and will serve my needs well.

I\x27d also like to note that I did receive RCA cables with mine, however, all of the wires are about four feet long, so these may or may not work for everyone.

I use these to play retro video games on my living room TV. The distance is about 20 feet apart between the TX/RX.

review_headline: Received a USED and damaged product when I paid for NEW
review_body:
When I took the VideoSecu television wall mount out of the box, it was covered in scratches and a couple of the screw packages had been opened. It was obvious that the bolts (which were stripped) and mount had been installed onto the wall and just put back into the box when the previous owner had decided not to keep the product. Very disconcerting - someone had returned the mount I almost wondered if the mount was safe or not to use. There\x27s no doubt I had paid for NEW not USED. It took almost a week for my payment to go through and then at least another week for the product to arrive so all I wanted was to put my television up. I had read so many good reviews about this product, I was so surprised to see that someone would return one. After thoroughly inspecting the mount, I decided it looked safe enough to install. There was no installation manual book in the box, just the mount and a dozen packets of screws (only a third of them you end up using and I had to buy new lag bolts). I was so anxious as to whether this mount would hold my 55" television that I left four 25lb weights to hang on it overnight and the next day. It\x27s been almost a week now and the television is still up. So other than the terrible delay for payment to go through and receiving a product that was anything but NEW - it seems I be a sturdy product.

So I take off two stars because I was deceived when I paid for NEW. If I wanted USED, I would have paid less and expected it. If USED constituted as NEW whenever you purchased something online, there would be no need for a section for USED products.

review_body:

Worth the price? Barely. Recommended, but not a slam dunk.

review_headline: Bohm BIG Wireless Bluetooth Stereo Speaker Review
review_body:
The B\xC3\x96HM Wireless Portable speaker allows you to listen to music, amplify your audio-visual media streaming, and communicate with callers by connecting your wireless Bluetooth device to it. I had no trouble pairing my iPhone and iPad to the B\xC3\x96HM wireless speaker. The instructions to get started were very easy to understand, which helped me get started by my first attempt. This alone deserves one star for its user-friendliness.

I used all the features that the B\xC3\x96HM wireless speaker offers and I enjoyed most of them. The first feature was connecting my iPad to amplify the streaming audio of television shows. I often turn on something on from Netflix while I prepare dinner, and usually watch it with the captions because I couldn\x27t hear everything. I enjoyed this feature because I could hear the content over the vent fans. This gets another star in my book.

The second feature, I tried out was streaming the music from my iPhone. Again, no problem pairing it to the device, and does not lag or skip. It comes out clearly and loudly. While I was listening to my music, I was able to try out the third advertised feature of being able to communicate with callers. I was able to connect to my call easily, but the caller had a hard time hearing me through the speakerphone. I had to disconnect the Bluetooth so they could hear me.

Another setback is that you have to adjust the volume through your phone. If you press the button on the B\xC3\x96HM device to make it louder, it does get louder but it sounds like you are going to blow-out the speaker. Make sure you adjust the volume through your wireless device. I will have to only give half a star for this.

The B\xC3\x96HM wireless speaker is aesthetically pleasing. It\x27s a simple design that is easy on the eyes and can blend into any household. I like how it is a classic look done in a modern simple way. When you look at it, you have no doubt that it is a speaker. One full star for this.

Overall, the B\xC3\x96HM wireless speaker is useful for someone who just wants to listen to music and amplify your audio-visual streaming. Not ideal for phonecalls. It is still quite affordable and a great gift to receive! You can\x27t complain about a device that will last 10 hours!!

review_headline: You get what you pay for.

I have mounted TVs in most of the rooms in my house with 3 in the basement alone. For $15, I decided to try this for my new bedroom TV. This product works ok for my 42" LED but I would not recommend it as this is the worst mount I have. The wall plate ships in two pieces that need to be screwed together. The mounting arms for the TV are shipped as three pieces that need to be assembled as well. All my other mounts are a single piece wall mount and arms. Why they designed it this way, I have no idea.

The instructions start with mounting the bracket to the wall. Since it says it "fits most TVs" I would think you would want to see it the arms work with the TV before you start putting holes in the wall. Also, the wall mount only spans the length of two studs (barely). In my case, I have one stud in the center of the wall. I had to use semi-high capacity drywall anchors (not provided) to secure it.

Anyway, like I said, it does work and is fairly inexpensive. It works fine for my bedroom TV as the LED is very, very light. I would not use it for a heavier LCD or Plasma TV. If I was purchasing a 42" TV mount again, I would definitely spend a few more bucks and get a better quality mount.

review_body:
If you love a stylish portable headphone, these studio beats are perfect for anyone who truly loves music and wants to appreciate through premier quality headphones. I just picked these up; so let me tell you what I love about them

Sound

Sound was the number one reason I picked these bad boys up. The noise-canceling feature is absolutely amazing; you can clearly hear your own pulse as soon as you put them on. I played 10-15 of my favorite songs with heavy bass and it sounded equally if not better than the system in my car. Sound quality is the best feature about these headphones for sure.

Comfort

The headphones are fit. Designers of Beats Studio headphones conducted a series of ergonomic studies to find the perfect lightweight, foldable headphone that always delivers a comfortable fit.

Durability

I\xE2\x80\x99ve had these headphones since summer 2013 and I can honestly tell you the sound quality, the speakers and the actual body of the headphones have stood the test of time. I use them pretty close to everyday as well in all types of weather conditions (absolutely essential for walking to class in the winter), and I haven\x27t noticed anything different.

Price

Do my Beats sound good? definitely. Do they sound great? Well, this is where things become debatable, but in my personal opinion no, they don\x27t. I can think of multiple headphones which can evenly match the Beats for bass quality and yet will cost you less than a third the price. Face it, these headphones are expensive. Do they offer the bang for the buck you forked out, though? No way.

Overall, I wouldn\xE2\x80\x99t trade my beats for anything. Although slightly overpriced, they serve a purpose that can\xE2\x80\x99t be ignored for any music lover.

review_body: After using these HDMI for 2 years, i was not impressed. The image kept blanking out from time to time and i would get a message on the tv saying, no signal detected. I would unplug and plug it back to see if the signal would make better contact, only to get the blank pictures between movies. I finally decided to switch out the HDMI for the ones that Dish Network provides on install. I no longer loose my picture. BlueRigger appears to be built nicely but it did not agree with my set up. So i will not buy this brand anymore for HDMI. P.S. i was running the BlueRigger 4.1 for 3D picture.    Second Update: 02-24-2015...After this review, immediately after the BlueRigger company provided me a quick response to address my concern, it was to my surprise since i decided to write a review aprrox 1 year after the fact. I explained to BRigger that i did not expect any compensation since i had purchased their 10ft HDMI 3d wires on 2011, only they were not tested, rather stored away for near future use since i was about to retire and move away from Florida. I had built a beautiful surround sound set up awaiting for me in Tennessee. Well, to my surprise they stated that their wires were lifetime guaranteed and would be happy to send me 2 10ft Bluerigger HDMI3d in effort to replace my defective ones. product_title: Little Dot I+ 6JI X2 Tube standard Hybrid Headphone Tube Amplifier
review_body:
It\x27s been a month with this amazing little amp. I\x27ve since replaced the stock opamp with a MUSES02 and the stock tubes with many different ones, and have settled on the Voskhod 6ZH1P-EV. All I can say is WOW! The amp with the stock opamp and tubes sounded great. But with the upgrades, it\x27s out of this world. Seriously.

Below are my earlier reviews that I\x27ve made since the purchase.

First night impressions:
Pros
-It\x27s got that glow! Don\x27t underestimate the glow. Probably biasing my impressions, but here goes anyway.
-Clear and clean. Crisp highs and mid range is very smooth. Alison Krauss & Union Station Live sounds as good as I\x27ve heard. No hiss or distracting noises. Just crisp and clean sound. Voice sounds great.
-3D imaging? Amber Rubarth "Hold On"; voice is front and center, first time hearing height in this track. Some instruments sound like they\x27re floating above others. Not distracting at all, just a very neat effect.
-Bass is present with stock tubes. KDrew "Bullseye" is a killer track if you like dub. Bass sounds thick, if a bit smeared sounding. I was afraid the stock tubes would be thin sounding, it isn\x27t. But it leads to a con...
Cons
-Bass is a little smudgy or loose sounding. It\x27s the first night with these stock tubes and I understand it takes 20 or so hours before tubes get comfy in their new homes and sing.
-Piano sound isn\x27t quite right. Smudgy bass makes the lower registers sound blurred.
-BRIGHT LED. It\x27s blue and it\x27s bright. Should be a soothing green or white. Such a contrast to the glow. I should put tape over it.

Two weeks later:
Pros
-Trying new tubes is fun! They glow and improve / alter the sound.
-Bass is MUCH improved. Rolling tubes, I\x27m a believer.
-Smooth smooth smooth!
-Overall an EXCELLENT amp.
Cons
-BRIGHT LED. Still haven\x27t put tape over it.t.

I\x27ve listened to this amp for about two hours now, so just the first impressions are shared. I\x27ll come back after rolling tubes (the famed former USSR Voskhod and Yugoslavia tubes) plus MUSES02 chip that I ordered in a few weeks for another take.

The utility lets you enter al the devices you have (have their make and model # ready). You can then start defining your activities. Everything is wizard based and makes the process very simple. If you don\x27t know the model number of your device, just type the name its popular with (Roku 3, Apple TV, Zeppelin Air) and it will find it for you. Pretty neat.

The remote works very well. No matter what state you leave your entertainment system in, when you trigger an activity, the remote will bring your TV (or AVR) to the right HDMI input, switch on the source device and will let you control the volume using your preferred speakers. I was really impressed when I was watching something on the netflix app of my smart TV and switched to cable and the remote actually simulated the exit button and even selected Yes for the prompt "Are you sure you want to exit Netflix?" on the TV. It then did the remaining chores of switching to the corrent inputs and powering on the source device. Pretty cool.

I prefer this remote to the more "advanced" touch screen based ones as I don\x27t have to look at the remote to press a button. After a while, I know where all the buttons are and I can use this like a power user.

Recommended for anyone who needs to clear up remote clutter from their coffee table.
