product_title: Sennheiser Headphones
review_headline: High End Sound for a Decent Price
review_body:
Switched over from 15 year old Grado SR125s to these Sennheisers. Loved the open sound of the Grados, but the ear pads were finally toast and one of the drivers developed an open. The Grados were never the most comfortable to my ears, but I did like the sound. I was looking for another open back design that has a spacious sound and would be more comfortable.

The HD598 cans have impressed me in many ways. First, they are EXTREMELY comfortable with the velour pads that fit entirely around the ear, rather than on top. These can be worn for hours without fatigue. Second, the soundstage and clarity are excellent. You hear whatever is on the recording. Even lower res music from Jazz Radio or iHeart sound fairly decent, but hi-res FLAC files sound amazing.

Compared these back to back with some Audio Technica M50X cans (similar price) and they both sounded great. The M50X have more bass impact and the clarity is also excellent. They were also more efficient than the HD598, so they were easier to drive without an amp. I would give the edge in comfort to the HD598, as well as the soundstage and smoothness in midrange.

Some things to note:
1. The HD598 hooked to an IPOD Classic are fine for low volumes, but they cannot reach high volumes due to their borderline 50 ohm impedance. Hooked to a Fiio E10K amp/DAC, they sound amazing, even in the low gain setting. In my opinion, the HD598 are acceptable without a headphone amp, but they really do need some extra juice to reach moderate to high volumes and to have more clarity and impact. You\x27ll likely not hear how good these sound without a decent amp.
2. Obviously, the HD598s leak a ton of sound out of the open back drivers. This is to be expected and what makes them sound so open. Just don\x27t expect to use these on a plane or next to your coworker without disturbing them.
3. The detachable cable is of high quality, but it is a bit much for desktop use. I may purchasea shorter cable to make the desktop a little cleaner without 6 feet of cable draped all around.
4. Some have commented on a "lack of bass". I wouldn\x27t say the HD598s are short on bass. I think they are very accurate. If you come from Beats, gaming phones or similar, then you might consider them "bass shy". But I\x27ve found them well balanced, not exaggerated, and don\x27t feel there\x27s anything missing.

Overall, I am extremely pleased with these cans. Comfort, smooth and open sound, clarity, and a decent price for the level of sound quality.

review_headline: Quality product that delivers.  Big bang for the buck!
review_body:
Got the antenna several days early - welcome surprise. The box was very wet and falling apart. Not the shippers fault. Luckily, all parts were in it and in good order. Prior to assembly, make sure you match both cross arms together to ensure you don\x27t end up with them mismatched. One side is shorter than the other side and mismatching them will make them bend incorrectly when you attempt to adjust. Also, remember to loosed the inner screws on the clamps to allow them to spread apart for assembly.

After assembly, I went up into the attic to mount it where I had a large antenna that I was replacing (space issues). After consulting an online antenna reference guide, I got out my trusty compass and proceeded to tune the antenna in. I needed to hit 295 degrees and 85 degrees. After some head scratching, I pulled one of the bays off the mount and turned it around to be able to aim it sufficiently in the correct direction. I have a home distribution box for my cable and CATV stuff where the lead goes into and to an amplifier that feeds the rest of the house. In the L/R, I hooked it up to the TiVo OTA DVR I just bought and dialed in 39 channels with ease! I am mechanically inclined and pretty adept at building things. The antenna is well thought out. There isn\x27t a problem with the wing nuts, they are great. They are a bit different in that they have a nut that is enclosed inside the wingnut part. Not an issue. The wiring was sufficient and no line loss experienced. This antenna is sturdy and not to difficulty to install. The negatives I read had me expecting a piece of junk, but I figured I would try it and fix what needed addressing when I got it. I am pleased with this purchase and really happy that it didn\x27t take the full shipping time quoted. It was 1/2 the shipping time :)

review_headline: I REALLY wanted to like these headphones
review_body:
I REALLY wanted to like these headphones, but I had to return them. I love the look and the features, but they just are not comfortable for extended use.

The GOOD: These headphones look really cool and are very good quality. They feel very solid and I imagine they would last a long time. The headphone cables are really thick and feel really substantial, and the controls worked flawlessly with my iPhone 6. The matte finish looks great.

The BAD: The noise canceling feature was really annoying. It\x27s hard to explain, but it makes a hissing sound and it feels like it puts pressure in your ears. It\x27s not a problem when there\x27s music, but between songs or during silent parts of gaming or watching a movie, it became uncomfortable.

The other problem is that after wearing them for an hour or so, they hurt my ears. I found myself constantly adjusting them to receive the pressure on different parts of my ears that were getting squished by the cups. Maybe if you have small ears this wouldn\x27t be a problem?

SUMMARY: If you don\x27t wear these headphones for more than an hour at a time (or if you have smallish ears) and if you\x27re listening to music with minimal silence, I think you\x27ll really like them. For me, I had to send them back.

I gave the unit to my husband because he was not happy with his portable speaker. He likes to listen to podcasts while he showers. That cord is very short, so in truth it needs to stay by the computer except for short excursions elsewhere.

Yosemite has a new version out, and it DOES work with this speaker. The sound is much better than the built-in sound on my MacBook (but not nearly as good as the sound on my 27-inch iMac). Looks as if my husband will have to get his own Alpatronix AX400.

I currently have the 450i\x27s that sound great but I thought I would try these thinking they would sound a lot better and because they are more premium. For the RHA 450s I found a "how to shorten headphone cables" video on YouTube which shows you how to make a nice Boy scout type knot that looks and works great. Unfortunately this does not work on the thick rubbery cable of the 750s so I had to use the black tie wrap. This looks bad and makes it more bulky. Also, due to the friction of the rubbery cable, I found them more difficult to untangle then the Nylon cable on the 450s. I have a nice little velvet pouch that the 450s fit in great but the 750s are really crammed in and tangle bad.

If RHA would shorten the cable by a good foot, use a softer Nylon or Kevlar cable I would keep these even if they only sound a bit better then the 450s. For now I will stick to the more user friendly portable 450s but will keep an eye out for future RHA ear buds.

product_title: Sony BDVN790W Blu-ray Home Theater System (2013 Model)
review_body:
Bought this product to pair with a new home theater system. Was particularly interested in the wireless rear speaker capabilities, the multiple HDMI inputs and the Blu-ray player, all in a single device.

The setup was pretty easy, and the program to auto-adjust the audio characteristics based on my room size was pretty cool.

Overall, it was decent.

However, over the next few months there were a few things that were really frustrating with this unit.

1) For some unknown reason, occasionally the volume will increase by itself up to the max. Using the remote, I try to turn it down, which it might for a 1/2 second before going back up again. It\x27s like having a volume fight with a ghost holding an invisible remote. Frustrating and annoying when watching movies or when guests are over.

2) I believe that switching inputs (or changing the channel when the input is from the HD Cable box) causes the output signal to \x27go black\x27. Like, if I change the channel, I lose the picture for about 10 to 15 seconds. Being a guy who likes to flip channels a lot, it really puts a damper on my style. I haven\x27t ever seen this with other setups.

3) I\x27m at a point now where I have to \x27jiggle the cables\x27. Seemingly every day now, I can\x27t simply turn on my XBox, Sony Home Theater System and my Projector and fire up a bowl of popcorn and enjoy a show. Instead, I turn on everything and hope it comes on. More often than not, there is no output detected from the theater system. I have to unplug/plug in/jiggle all of the HDMI cables, turn on and off my individual input devices (XBox/Cable Box) and/or turn off and then back on the theater system. The last one usually does the trick. But it\x27s getting old doing that all of the time. I\x27m now in the market for a new home theater system.

Pros: When it does work, it\x27s fine. Wireless rear speakers help declutter the movie room.

Cons: Ghosts in the machine, hacky workarounds for things that shouldn\x27t be problems.

review_headline: Good sub but it just didn\x27t \x22wow\x22 me
review_body: First off when I see a Martin Logan product. I expect it to live up to its brand name and offer everything that\x27s worth it\x27s value, as im sure many on you in the hunt for a subwoofer are. After recently purchasing large speakers with that pack a decent amount of low end. I decided that I was in no need of a 12" subwoofer anymore and was looking to replace it with a 8 or 10 inch sub that packed a punch. My main usage for my speakers are for music, and I figured a 10 inch good to give me some tight and accurate bass while enough to give me some good low end. My budget was $500, I was at a local Magnolia theaters and after test listening to many subs in the room I chose this one. Overtime with extensive listen I was a little surprised that this sub hits just as hard as some 12 inch subs I\x27ve had. However it didn\x27t hit deep enough for me, and even in the low end range (20-30hz) it didn\x27t deliver enough output. Now I might be crazy for having such high expectation for a 10 inch sub. But I did expect this to give a little more, it gave me that tight and punchy bass I was looking for in music, but the output just lacked enough to where I was unsatisfied with the price paid for this subwoofer. What else could I get with $500? An SVS PB-1000. A 10 inch sub which is rated to go down as low as 19Hz and has significantly more output in as the Dynamo 500. I am no way sponsored or paid by SVS to say this but as a fellow consumer that wants the best bang for their buck I want to let everyone that there are better options out there for the SAME price. Everyone has their own tastes in the end but I would urge you to check out other subs in the price range first.  This sub is by no means a horrible speaker. I just simply felt that it is not worth it\x27s value.

product_title: Abco Tech Water Resistant Wireless tooth Speaker with Suction Cup & Hands-Free Speakerphone
review_body: I bought this speaker planning to use it in the shower so I don\x27t expose my expensive iPhone to steam.    The pros:  -----------  The most striking thing about this speaker is that it\x27s so LOUD. In fact, the range of volume is incredible. This thing goes so loud I would have no problems recommending it even as a party speaker or general-purpose speaker overall (and easy to control the volume range, too). It\x27s that cool.    The cons:  -----------  Stopped working after 3 months. I was SO disappointed. :( :( :(    Especially disappointed because I took extra care of it. It wasn\x27t even exposed to water. I would keep it on the sink counter while I showered (cause the sound capability is that awesomely loud).    I made sure the cover to the recharger was always closed.    It just stopped working one day.    Before I purchased this, I read the reviews, and many other reviewers said this speaker had stopped working on them too. But these reports are scattered about. So I took a chance. I bought it even knowing these issues, figuring that I\x27d be a lucky one, maybe this issue wouldn\x27t happen to me.    Oops. It did.    Also, even before it stopped working completely, the power button was sticky on me. It wouldn\x27t shut off, even when \x5C\x22long pressing\x5C\x22 it properly. I would just never hear the descending tones confirming it was off while I pressed it. ARGH!    So while getting out of the house in the mornings, I would just have to leave it on and let it run out of juice since it wouldn\x27t respond to a shutoff.    So this speaker has inconsistent performance. If I\x27m going to buy a speaker I have to throw away every three months, I\x27d rather get the cheap $10 ones at Home Depot.    So, buyer beware. Is it a charging issue? This speaker comes with a specialized USB cable, but that\x27s it. I would charge it between plugging it into my Apple laptop or using a USB charger I had around the house.    Since the power button would be sticky and not respond, I had to let it run down a couple times and recharge it more frequently than usual.    Too bad. Outside of the inconsistent performance, this thing is a winner. I loved how loud it gets!

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 25 Headphones (wired, 3.5mm)
review_headline: Wearing Headphones Again After So Many Years
review_body: I chose these headphones from a list of items as a service anniversary gift from my employer.  I knew that Bose makes awesome products, as I have owned a set of their high end speakers for 30 years and I still haven\x27t found any that sound any better.    Took these on a recent business trip to see how they performed on an airplane.  I sat in the window seat right next to the wing near the engine exhaust to put them to the test.  When the aircraft started the takeoff roll, I flipped on the headphone switch and the roar of the engine faded away.  I could still hear it, but at a very low level (reduction of about 80-90%).  Started playing music through them and I could hear every note, even at a low volume level.    Later in the flight, the captain came on and made an announcement.  Even with the music playing and the noise cancellation in operation, I could hear every word of the announcement (although at a very reduced sound level).  Aircraft noise was still at a low level...thought this was good, where the noise was almost gone but I could still hear announcements in case of an emergency.  Throughout the flight, I was oblivious to the normal sounds around me (sneezing, mindless chatter, crying babies, complaining to the flight attendants, etc.).    As the title of this review says, I haven\x27t listened to music with headphones for over 20 years, because I haven\x27t found a set that did the music justice.  Now I have, and the headphones are part of my musical enjoyment once again....These headphones will be in my travel bag every time from now on.

product_title: GOgroove AirBAND Wireless Bluetooth Stereo Headphones with Microphone and Onboard Controls - Compact & Adjustable , Sleek Headband Design , & 8 Hour Battery Life
review_body:
I got mine for $20 on ebay because they were returned to the vendor with the box open.

First and foremost, I have to say the audio quality is excellent. I\x27m no audio snob, but the bass is warm & full, the treble is very detailed, and the channel separation is remarkable. Even when playing back medium-quality MP3s, I can hear individual horns and stringed instruments I\x27d never noticed before. My favorite genre is Argentine Tango from the Golden Age, and these phones bring it to rich, crystal-clear life.

I like the looks of the GoGroove. They are very plain and minimalist in gloss black--very modern looking. I have a larger than average head with normal sized ears, and the headphones fit me perfectly. I find them very comfortable with no tendency to slip off. YMMV.

They aren\x27t perfect though. I had a difficult time getting the GoGroove to pair with my LG G2 Android phone. I almost gave up and sent them back DOA, but after a lot of tinkering they finally connected. Since then, they have paired with my phone pretty easily.

Also, the GoGroove requires a special charging cable that is USB on one end, but micro coaxial on the other end. Why didn\x27t they use a standard micro USB connector? If I lose this special cable, the headphones will be worthless.

Overall I\x27m very pleased with my purchase. If I break these or lose them, I\x27m buying another pair.

Update: I\x27ve had a couple of phone conversations using the built in mic feature and it worked pretty well. I had to repeat myself a couple of times, but it was not a big deal. I think I can hear them better than they can hear me. In both cases I was walking outdoors, and even with wind and traffic noise, communication was no problem. The mic isn\x27t perfect, but it works.

product_title: Audio Technica ATH-ANC23 QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Cancels noise - but at a price
review_body:
Pros:
-The active noise cancellation works. I put these on the second I sat down on a 737, and the only reason I could tell we were taking off was from the movement.

Cons:
-The provided rubber tips are pretty stiff, and I found them to be uncomfortable after a short time and downright painful after a couple of hours.
-The tips are also harder to put on than any other brand I\x27ve used. If the mid-sized ones that they ship with work for you, that\x27s obvious not an issue. But you need to have pretty dexterous fingers and a bit of patience if you need to swap them out.
-Sound quality isn\x27t exactly great, due largely to the relatively quiet ambient noise produced by the cancellation system. But I\x27ll take that over the roar of a jet engine.

All in all: in a pinch, they do work for making air travel a quieter experience. But as I\x27ve got flights of over ten hours to deal with, these probably aren\x27t going to cut it unless I can find better rubber tips.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR626 7.2-Channel Network Audio/Video Receiver (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: easy switch between any audio (blue tooth) or TV sources
review_body:
I tried to use it due to its convenience. Single entry point to TV and audio signal, easy switch between any audio (blue tooth) or TV sources, managing volume output and data source with remote control .
For testing got only one Pioneer SP-FS52-LR - loudspeaker.

Testing results:
1. Onkyo was unable to work with my 3d blue ray player output
2. There is no protection from errors connecting sound system to Onkyo and from sound system failures - any error can break the whole device.
3. 20W (30$) Lepai was louder (with better sound quality) then 100W Onkyo on one speaker (may be due to some connection problems)

Details:
From the beginning did not like the quality of internal amplifier. It have THD > 0.07% for some channels > 0.1% for the rest. Lepai LP-2020A+ for 30$ have better output characteristic (THD<0.05%) but less powerful (10 contrary to 100).
So wanted to use something like BEHRINGER REFERENCE AMPLIFIER A500, and BEHRINGER monitor as sound system for audio - to be able to listen to good sound occasionally - using audio output from Onkyo.

Tests:
Onkyo was unable to work with my 3d blue ray player output. Was forced to use some devices to lower down quality - then it worked and I was able to hear some signal from cable and blue ray.

From cable box - got problem that not all signals were sent to front loudspeaker (voice disappeared) but this is fine the output is 7-1.
Output from blue ray player and cable box - was low, when tried to use 60% of volume - in 1-2 minutes of work Onkyo powered off, did not want to power on any more.
Investigating manual - understood that protection circuit has activated. There is no ways to trigger it off, have to return to manufacture only.
I explained this behavior - due to the fact that used only one loudspeaker, not two. Anyway, did not find any warnings that do not have to do it in the manual.
After failure I testedLepai amplifier (TV as audio source, Pioneer as sound system)- it generated better sound quality, output was louder then from Onkyo (quite enough for me really).

Was disappointed with my first design. Now I think that much better to use TV audio signal output as audio source, to connect to audio system of your choice. Audio signal generated by TV is as good as Onkyo. Will not have future problems that some data sources are not read by receiver but read by TV.

product_title: Aerb\xC2\xAE 4G Waterproof MP3 Music Player With Mono OLED Screen Display Support FM Radio / Pedometer for Swimming & other Sports (IPX-8 Standard)-Black
review_headline: Wanted to like this so much, but gave up on it after a month.
review_body:
I figured this was worth a try. I usually use an old Sanza for running, but recently started swimming a lot so I needed something waterproof. I knew the controls would be confusing at first and I would need petroleum jelly to get the headphones to seal around the speakers while swimming. But after a month of use swimming at least 4 days a week, 1 mile per workout, I tried to love this, I still really hate it. WHEN it works, it makes swimming laps for an hour a lot more enjoyable. Only time this should ever be used is swimming. Otherwise there are WAY better options for non waterproof mp3 players. My Sandisk Sanza I have had since 2008 still works great and is light years ahead of the Aerb player for non waterproof activities.

Headphones: They clip nicely to goggles and stay out of the way. They don\x27t sound to bad. Had a hard time getting the headphones to seal around the speaker (seals fine to the ear). Once i put a little petroleum jelly around the seal they no longer leaked. Except the plug would randomly now fall off the speaker, sometimes in my ear, which was very hard to remove. They are terrible for anything except swimming. Too short to clip to your shorts without pulling the headphones out of your ear while running. Tried using different headphones and song vocals would not play though them, no matter what equalizer setting I used. Very weird.

Controls: Yes they are terrible like everyone says. Sometimes pressing the volume up button shuts the unit off. Even when you press the very edge of the volume button as far away from the power button as possible. Annoying when you are in a workout and want to turn up a song and the unit shuts off. Sometimes when holding the unlock button, it will not unlock. Sometimes the volume will not turn up/down while holding the button in. It just cycles through songs. Sometimes the unit randomly stops playing a song and you have to stop swimming, unclip it from your goggles, hold the unlock button down and hope it unlocks. If it does, pressing the next track button sometimes doesn\x27t work, so you press it a few more times. Then about ten seconds later it jumps ahead to catch up to all the times you press the button. Then you have to make sure to lock it before clipping it to your goggles again, otherwise you will press a lot of buttons in the process.

I also had a hard time getting the shuffle feature to work. Learned that you have to create one folder with all the songs in it that you want to shuffle through. You can only shuffle in a folder. I first tried putting all the songs on the device without any folders at all and that didn\x27t work. Created one folder and put all my songs in it, then it shuffled correctly.

product_title: Teac Wireless Streaming Music System
review_headline: Retro looking design with modern blue-tooth function
review_body:
Out of the box I was pleasantly surprised at the build quality of this unit as I was afraid the plastic could have been on the thin and cheap side. The retro design is kind of a nice touch(personally I am not too crazy about it but can live with it). Comes with a handy little remote that can be used to set the time and control all the music player functions.

Pairing the smartphone with this unit is pretty quick easy and can be done in less than 10 secs. Aside from commercial CD\x27s this unit can also play MP3/WWA files via a CD-R. In my opinion the speakers sound pretty nice for this level of music player. The display is a bright orange color which makes it easy to see but the numbers on the display are a bit on the small side.

As for the radio you can program up to 20 AM/FM channels to memory(40 total). And with the USB slot you can charge any device that uses a USB connection. There\x27s a standard alarm function as well as a sleep mode. My main gripe is that it is a bit too pricey. Just under a hundred bucks would be more reasonable. But otherwise this is a capable little music player with several different ways to play your music.

product_title: Etekcity Mini AV Video Audio RCA CVBS to HDMI Converter Box with Power Adapter
review_headline: Works, just not through hdmi pass through devices (like google tv boxes).
review_body:
So over all this product works as advertised. It is very simple to connect. All you do is connect the RCA output of your old dvd player, cable box, old console and then attach the hdmi to your tv. The quality is great with a choice of 720 or 1080p. Comes with its own power supply as well.

The reason this is a 4 star review, is because it will not output video when going through a google tv box (hdmi passthrough). I tested this with both a logitech revue and an asus cube and on both I only get sound.

At first I thought the asus cube had gone faulty since It first had video and then lost it. I tested everything and then I pulled out the Revue from my drawers to test that. But the hdmi works when connected straight to tv but not when it goes through an hdmi pass through. I will have to research more into this and see if anything can be done, but the main purpose of this device, was to connect the analog cable box I was provided which cost 2.95 a month, to the hdmi input of my tv since I use an hdmi switch and that makes it a lot easier to use. The google tv option is the ideal scenario which I guess I can live without, since I rarely watch live tv. A digital box from my company is 5.95 a month so saving 3/mth is more important especially when watching live tv is a backup, not a priority.

So Generally it works, just not through hdmi passthrough devices (which will probably not be an issue for most).

product_title: Zinus SC-SBBK-14NT-FR Smartbase Bed Frame Metal, Narrow Twin
review_headline: Very affordable, platform bed foundation, no tools needed, this one is a winner. I bought a 2nd one!
review_body: I bought this frame to go with my memory foam mattress that I also bought on Amazon - see my review for that as well. This was one of the cheapest frames I bought and the main reason I bought it was because it said, no tools needed assembly and they were right.  The only "tool" I needed was a pair of scissors to snip the ties holding the metal frame together so it wouldn\x27t open during shipment.  The frame comes in two pieces, folded up in thirds. It\x27s all put together!  All you do is unopen the thirds, screw down the end legs ( you don\x27t need to do the middle legs), put both pieces side by side and clamp them together with the wing bolt sets included and you are done. I was postponing setting this up because I was afraid it would be much more difficult, but it was a dream. I bought a second one for the Twin bed I bought.  This is all that it is and more. And you can use it as a platform bed for your memory foam mattress, eliminating the need for a boxspring, saving you money.  I highly recommend this.

review_body:
The box it arrives in is the width of the queen sized mattress, so it can be a bit cumbersome to move it by yourself. The box itself is pretty heavy (about 80 lbs). I would recommend having an extra person available to help with set up. Our box arrived a little bit damaged, but the mattress itelf was protected inside the plastic wrap.

When it comes to setting up the mattress, you\x27ll want to make sure you have it positioned with the orange side facing down before you cut the plastic wrap. Once that is cut, the mattress begins to expand fairly rapidly.

We let our mattress sit for a few days to let it air out before we put the sheets on it. This mattress has a very firm feel, but it does a good job of cutting back on motion transference. You dont really notice the other person moving around a lot. I like that the cover is washable and removable. The cooling feature is not especially noticeable under sheets and blankets, but I do think it helps some.

product_title: Orchard Hills Bookcase Headboard
review_body:
It is possible we\x27ve assembled for ourselves and/or friends and relatives over 100 of these types of disposa-furniture over the years, and apples to apples - compared to other flat ship self-construct pressboard furniture, e.g. Ikea, Prepac - the Sauder stuff has definitely been cream of the crop in our experience (with the possible exception of the earliest US-available Ikea kits from the mid 1980s). The instructions are pretty good (in English, with diagrams, and in this case with a linked video on the internet) and have the advantage of having a few humorous asides to leaven the occasionally tedious experience of self-assembly.

This particular piece was heavier than we expected (a good thing for a headboard) and while we would have preferred a lighter finish option (maple, please, Sauder, or ash) ended up looking really good. The shelves are about the right widths and heights (adjustable) to customize putting alarm clocks, lamps, places for glasses, etc. on each side of the bed, and are heavy enough to support real books. The back board is just high enough you can sit up in bed with a pillow under your back without smooshing stuff on the shelves. The back panel is the usual cheap cardboard, and MUST be attached correctly to get good stability, so pay attention to that step. It looks fine once assembled but our experience with flat-assemble is that this is almost always the first part of a piece to take damage, and thus lead to the eventual collapse of a pressboard piece. There are pre-scored holes above each "compartment" on the back panel to pop out to run electrical cords as needed, in good spots, but don\x27t pop them out until you need them or it will be a bit unsightly.

Tip: A big plus are the mounting flanges/brackets, which are very heavy duty and have a variety of holes in them for attaching to various bedframes. However, in our case we had a wood platform frame and the brackets (utterly necessary to keep the headboard steady when you are in bed) did not fit anywhere. We were very hesitant to drill more holes in pressboard, but what we ended up doing was using the brackets to mount the headboard to the floor (where we had spots we didn\x27t mind drilling in), and then just positioned the bed accordingly. The headboard is very stable and level this way, and we can thus still move the bedframe around for cleaning, etc., without dragging the headboard.

We installed this on a queen, and it had enough space to fit over the end just so without swallowing the head of the bed or leaving gaps. For a full, I suspect the best strategy is to put it over the frame asymmetrically, so the "gap" is all on one side of the bed, where you\x27d have a little storage nook (put a hook on the frame, or maybe some ready-made stack organizers, for a little extra shelf/nook storage.)

One caveat: outgassing from the pressboard. Our manufacture date (US made) on our set was only about six weeks before we got it -- let\x27s hear it for drop-shipping -- but whatever process they make the wood product with, there\x27s a persistent (although diminishing) smell from the product that has ranged from distracting to a little nauseating. It did abate after a couple of weeks and has been disappearing, but is still there. So to Sauder - maybe "cure" these a little longer before shipping; for the consumer -- if you can wait, you may want to take the pieces out of the box and leave them out in a room you don\x27t sleep in for a week or two before assembling.

All that said, a pretty darn good deal - for a very low amount of money, a pretty sturdy piece that fits well and provides a nice space-saving alternative to side tables.en you are in bed) did not fit anywhere. product_title: Kawan Aloo Paratha 400 Grams, 4 Pieces (Pack of 2)
review_headline: more like a spread than an actual stuffing
review_body:
This is not the trad Indian Aloo Paratha you get at most Indian places but rather a Malaysian variant. The Indian versions are a fried in butter or ghee,a distinct golden brown, velvety textured, very thin whole wheat bread, stuffed w/about 2/3 inch of potato, peas and onion... or ground lamb, peas and onion,( aloo mutter or keema mutter) usually the only stuffed bread on the menu and pricey compared to the other breads.

This is a very thin nan or chapati bread stuffed w/potato, onion and green onion (the page contradicts ingredients, one place says peas, other says spinach, i got neither and the packaging was diff than illustrated)

The stuffing is ext thin, more like a spread than an actual stuffing.

While very tasty in this Malaysian version and i will prob re-order (hopefully get one w/peas) i\x27ll still be searching for the frozen *Indian* style one i\x27ve had at so many Indian places.

Like the reviews for their other "parathas" it arrived thawed (no dry ice) but refroze easily, wasn\x27t spoiled.
One star off for the above reasons, the taste did redeem it, just wasn\x27t an Indian aloo paratha.

review_body: I am a repeat customer of this coffee for 2 main reasons. Firstly let me say that I have tasted the most expensive coffees on Earth as well as many other varieties from all over the world. There are a few coffees that are standouts. I\x27m a firm believer that you can pretty much mask any taste, but unfortunately, you can\x27t mask texture. I managed to make the flavor of this protein tolerable in my smoothies with berries, some not-from-concentrate apple and beet juice, and a little squeeze of honey, but nothing I did could fix the texture. It is the consistency of fish food flakes and even pulverizing it in a blender doesn\x27t seem to help. The best I was able to do was add so much ice it basically turned into a sorbet, which is not really what I\x27m going for at 6 am.

I may have been able to stomach this every morning if I noticed a big change in appetite, but I didn\x27t. In fact, I often wanted something else to remove the "mouth feel" this texture left behind.

product_title: All Natural, Nitrate Free/Gluten Free, Dry Cured Pepperoni: 9oz. Pkg (2 Sticks Per Package)
review_body:
BridgeFord: 2/5
- Highly flavored, so much so that it seems like they are trying to hide some other flavor. But it does have the classic pepperoni flavor
- A bit on the spicy side, this has to do with the amount of flavoring in the stick but has a clear pepper flavor to it.
- Extremely oily. There is so much oil in this stick that it is just messy and nasty
- The casing is difficult to remove and tears easily like paper.
- Consistency of the meat isn\x27t good, and it is clear low quality meats are used in its preparation

Fortuna: 2/5
- Flavor is relatively mild, with a slight spice to it.
- Casing appears to be a slim plastic case of some sort and again not easily removed
- Meat quality again doesn\x27t appear to be great
- Several spots of mold on the casing
- This is certainly a serviceable pepperoni but not something I would consider great.

Battistoni: 3/5
- Flavor is slightly more than mild, with a good spice to it. Not enough to be a problem, but enough to add some flavor. It has a slight breakfast sausage flavor hidden behind the classic pepperoni flavor as well.
- Casing again appears to be some sort of slim plastic
- Meat is a slightly better consistency than the Bridgeford and Fortuna
- Another extremely oily stick, on par with the Bridgeford in how much oil is in it again making it messy to work with.
- The stick is a tad on the softer side compared to some of the others making it a tad easier to cut
- Overall again a reasonable pepperoni, but the breakfast sausage flavor underneath kinda throws me for a little bit of a loop. Not necessarily a bad thing as I enjoy breakfast sausage, but unexpected in a pepperoni.

Vermont: 4/5
- The flavor is a nicely balanced and well-rounded flavor with a little smokiness to it. There is not a lot of spice to it, just a hint so if you are looking for a spicy pepperoni this is probably not the one for you. However, the overall flavor is still very nice.
- The casing appears to be a natural casing, it is a smooth casing (not wrinkled like most of the others), it removes cleanly from the meat, and relatively easily.
- The meat has a nice consistency and appears to use higher quality meats than found in some of the other sticks.
- This stick is a little wider than some of the others
- This stick is pretty oily, not quite as bad as the Bridgeford and Battistoni, but not much better either.
- For some reason I found this stick slightly harder to cut than the others. I am not certain why that is.
- Overall a very solid pepperoni choice, an optional spicy version could be useful, and cleaning up some of the oil would be nice. This is a pepperoni I would recommend for those looking for a nice flavor with hints of smoke in it.

Boar\x27s Head: 4/5
- Flavor is a pretty classic pepperoni flavor with a little heat working its way in at the end. The heat appears to come on gradually and gets fairly strong near the end.
- The meat consistency is pretty good, similar to the Vermont in that regard.
- This still has a bit of oil to it (as all pepperoni likely do), but it is not nearly as bad as the Bridgeford and Battistoni.
- The casing is again round and smooth making it easier to remove than some of the dried wrinkled sticks. Though it tears like paper similar to what was seen with the Bridgeford casing.
- Overall another very solid pepperoni choice, particularly if you like a little heat in your pepperoni.

Margherita: 5/5
- Flavor is a very nice pepperoni flavor with depth to it. There is a little heat at the end, slightly less than in the Boar\x27s Head but it had a similar build-up near the end.
- The casing is similar to what was seen in the Bridgeford and Boar\x27s head where it tears similar to paper.
- This is again a round (not wrinkled) pepperoni stick so the casing comes off fairly easy.
- This is the least greasy of the brands I tried which I found to be a very nice change of pace.
- The meat is fairly consistent, one of the best brands for consistency if not THE best.
- This was one of the easiest pepperoni to cut into consistently sized slices.
- In my opinion this is the best of the pepperoni brands I tasted. It hit all of the right notes, was easy to work with, and not overly oily like many of the others. The flavor profile was very clearly pepperoni, but with a depth of flavor that most of the others missed, with a nice heat at the end that was not overpowering, but helped add to the flavor.

#1 - Margherita is a well-rounded Pepperoni that hits all of the right notes.
#2 - Vermont is another great choice, particularly if you are looking for a slightly smokey flavor.
#3 - Boar\x27s Head is a great alternate choice. It is similar to the Margherita, but I simply felt that the Margherita was a little better quality over all.

What should one expect from an "older, matured, stronger" Marmite? For me, it was more gooey, savory, spreadable ultra-umami, and that\x27s exactly what I got. The difference between this elixir and the standard stuff is subtle, but immediately apparent. Marmite XO delivers the familiar basic flavor, but somehow amplified, though not in the sense of being overpowering or too concentrated. In fact, I found the "XO factor" to be quite delicate, and easily overpowered in the presence of other flavorful ingredients such as, say, a sharp cheddar or onions. Accordingly, the simple but classic support of white bread and butter (or margarine) makes for the best way to enjoy this special treat.

Oh, and one more thing... those who\x27ve always felt that the classic Marmite is "perfectly horrid" will not change their minds upon tasting this variety, either.

review_headline: Best SCOBY around!!! No rehydrating needed!! YAY!!
review_body: First time brewer with amazing results!!!  I started my brew with some extra strong starter liquid (3 cups) that I got from my brother (to make the initial brew go faster). I could have used one of his baby SCOBYs but his look funky (to me - a novice) and I wanted to start off my brewing the right way...so I got this one.  I put my brothers starter liquid and one of Hannah\x27s (Kombucha Kamp\x27s) SCOBY\x27s in with the starter liquid that it came with.  I put all into a 2 gallon continuous brew vessel (http://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00BWC0E42/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o09_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) with a gallon of \x5C\x22nutrients\x5C\x22 --> (heated/blended/then cooled: c sugar/8 oolong tea bags/gallon of distilled water).  I used the Kombucha Kamp essential heating strip, bringing by brew up to 80-82 degrees (my house is frequently 62 degrees in the winter and the heating strip did all of the rest-temperature wise...also available on Amazon or on the Kombucha Kamp store website).  In 7 days I harvested amazing & fairly strong brew, perfect ph, and had a beautiful 1/4 inch thick, 8.5 inches in diameter, baby SCOBY on top.  I\x27ve never been more pleased!!  I did do A LOT of research before starting.  This is really going to save me a lot of money and will make it possible to drink kombucha daily.  I also look forward to sharing my brews and extra SCOBYs in the future with friends and family.  Thanks so very much, Hannah & Kombucha Kamp!!!

product_title: Barilla Collezione Pasta
review_body:
I do most of my grocery shopping at Whole Foods, so it\x27s been a while since I\x27ve eaten Barilla pasta. I received a free box through a Barilla promotion with BzzAgent recently, though, and I was pleasantly surprised by the Casarecce variety. I initially used it with a very traditional Tomato Basil Sauce, and I was pleased. The shape holds a good amount of sauce, but not an overwhelming amount. It does\x27t hold chunks very well, which is a plus in my opinion. I hate biting into a shell or some other larger, more open pasta and realizing there\x27s a chunk of onion or tomato in it. I like things smooth.

Where the Casarecce really shined, though, is with a white wine and cashew cream sauce I made. The creamy sauce was the perfect companion to this shapely pasta, and the cream coated the surface nicely. The best part, though, is that I tossed the extra in the fridge to see what it would look like a day or so later, knowing that pasta almost never makes for good leftovers - but this one held up. It didn\x27t even do that annoying thing where it absorbs all the liquid and leaves you with a dry, solid hunk of pasta and you have to rehydrate everything (only to end up with gross and soggy pasta).

I would definitely buy this pasta again, especially when I plan on making cream sauces.

product_title: Quirky Egg Minder Wink App Enabled Smart Egg Tray, PEGGM-WH01
review_headline: Batteries run down too fast - but now at the $9 price it\x27s worth it to just hold your eggs VERY good quality
review_body: I have purchased 5 of these, several as gifts and they all work well, until the batteries run down, which happens in a few days or less.   I have heard the the NSA is using these to transmit tip security memos they want to leak to the Russians.  But that is not verified.  This device is a real conversation piece,  The tray is very good quality and the whole system would work well if you have your own chickens and are routinely adding a few fresh eggs.  I know several people who know people with chickens and they routinely supply a tray to the chicken people to be filled with eggs.  This would be a great gift to friends like that.  I wonder if re-using old cardboard egg trays over and over to get eggs from undocumented chickens might be an E-coli risk?    The freshness sensor is only about the oldest items placed in the tray, in order, and it does not know the difference between a lemon/lime/egg/rock.  You have to install Wink on your phone by manually keying in your home WiFi info into the install - otherwise you will think you have installed it because you got it to flash but the Wink app still won\x27t talk to your eggs.  That done, the tray does not communicate well from inside the fridge, so it needs to be taken out to the counter  when you add/remove eggs.  It updates quickly, perhaps every few seconds.  BUT, the deal breaker is that fresh alkaline batteries run down in a few days and then your Smart Tray becomes stupid until you replace them - the batteries that is.  The real nice people at Quirky are very good and walked me through the installation.

product_title: Homebrew Lemon-Lime Soda Pop Concentrated Extract, 2-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 3)
review_headline: I find that this makes a good substitute for the sodastream diet lemon lime syrup
review_body:
I use this, homebrew lemon lime concentrate, all the time with my sodastream. Using an empty sodastream syrup bottle, I put in 1 tablespoon of the lemon lime home brew concentrate and, for diet lemon lime soda pop, 1 1/2 teaspoons of either liquid stevia or liquid nutrasweet sweetener, then fill rest of the bottle with water. I believe that other reviewers might have used the guidelines for mixing included in the homebrew box , which results in a bitter and much too strong mix. I sometimes also add 1 1/3 teaspoon of citric acid to my homemade diet soda mixture. I find that this makes a good substitute for the sodastream diet lemon lime syrup, which has become very expensive, and, where I live at least, difficult to find in the stores, and which is almost always very expensive when bought through Amazon.

As an aside, I have used other homebrew flavors, and find that the root beer recipe included in the concentrate box is pretty much on the mark for taste. It seems that it is only the lemon lime flavor that is much too strong when using their instructions...a good thing from my perspective, since it means that I get three or more batches from one bottle of the lemon lime flavoring.

product_title: Nutella & Go
review_headline: Tastes a lot like a slightly saltier Original Pocky
review_body:
Two of my sons are big Nutella fans so I knew they would love trying this.

This is a snack size treat that comes in a half-round plastic container. The container is then divided into two section with one side containing the pretzel sticks and the other side containing the Nutella for dipping.

The pretzel sticks are about 2\x5C\x22 long and have an average amount of salt on them. There is plenty of Nutella for dipping every single stick. My sons loved the combination of flavors and both said it tasted almost exactly like Original Pocky (a famous Japanese snack stick) except somewhat saltier. In fact, once they finished the sample I received from Vine, they went out to buy pretzel sticks to dip into the large jar of Nutella I already had in the pantry.

It\x27s important to note this is not what I would call a healthy snack. There are 270 calories in the small container and not much nutritional value. For that reason, I wouldn\x27t buy this as a regular snack food for my family. But it is highly portable and delicious so I might buy them in the future for day trips or other special occasions.

I often pack a lunch with a container of Nutella and some fruits like apples and strawberries to spread the Nutella on, but the idea of pretzels with Nutella has never crossed my mind. If your family likes these Nutella & Go Pretzel packs, try buying a big tub of Nutella and a bag of Rolled Gold pretzels for movie night or get togethers. It\x27s a tasty combo.

product_title: Tetley British Blend Premium Black, 80-Count Tea Bags, 7 Ounce, (Pack of 6)
review_headline: The perfect cuppa, hot or cold-brewed
review_body:
This is a fabulous, perfect tea. I pay approx $3 in Shoprite or a box of 80 (round) bags. I keep trying other teas (PG Tips, Twinings, Stash etc) because I can\x27t believe an inexpensive tea like Tetley is SO GOOD. Every time I try a different tea, it just validates my preference for this Tetley British Blend. For a large mug, I use 2 teabags and steep for 5 minutes. The price is low enough that I don\x27t mind doing that - I like really strong dark tea with a dash of sugar and milk. This tea also makes fabulous COLD BREWED ICED TEA - you do NOT need to purchase special "tea for cold brewing." I put 5 teabags in a quart mason jar with water, and leave in the fridge or 24 hours. The resulting iced tea is wonderful.
I will add that apparently tea can be prone to mold and bacteria. I used to use PG Tips and I liked it hot. However, when I made "cold brewed", I found ropey strings of bacteria. That has never happened with Tetley British Blend. It tastes like good tea - strong but not bitter, just a lovely cuppa.

Saw a recipe on the Pioneer woman where she took leftover Thanksgiving goodies and wrapped them up in a rice paper roll. It was a bit of a strange concept to me \xE2\x80\x93 but piqued my curiosity to the point I wanted to order and try some.

We didn\x27t follow her recipe, preferring something slightly healthier, so we julienned carrots, cucumbers, peppers, purple cabbage and tomatoes, and rolled them in the softened rice paper rolls. Also made a BBQ ranch ((it sounds peculiar, I was skeptical at first myself)) to dip them in....HOLY MOLY...they were unreal! These have become a new household favorite, making for a very pretty end product, that\x27s healthy and actually makes a nice treat if you have vegetarian or vegan friends. I\x27d be remiss if I didn\x27t mention these were a true crowd pleaser with my meat-loving brothers who are repulsed at the thought of frou-frou finger foods that are \x27pretty\x27 ;) We made extras for them the next day --they liked them so much.

The rice paper is SUPER easy to work with. Just dip one in a warm bowl of water and voilà -- you\x27re ready to roll. :))
Can fry, bake or serve raw. Did I mention they\x27re gluten free too...?

product_title: Morning Pep Pure Birch Xylitol sweetener
review_body:
I am always looking for ways to cut down on calories but I am also very wary of nearly all of the sugar substitutes out there because almost every single one of them has been shown to have a negative health risk associated with them. Xylitol is no different as it is toxic to some animals, including dogs, and has negative side effects in humans including diarrhea, bloating and gas. Reading the research that I could find online about Xylitol, something I think everyone should do before consuming a product like this, I found mixed reviews.

As I said I am very wary of consuming these types of products so I decided to test this product on taste alone (I didn\x27t swallow it) and when tasting it straight out of the bag it has a very strange aftertaste that made me feel like I just spit out a piece of sugar-free gum, which makes sense since Xylitol is used as a sweetener in some gums. Mixed in with coffee or tea I didn\x27t notice any of the aftertaste and it seemed to do a fine job sweetening the beverages.

My wife tested the product as well, but she consumed a teaspoon of it a couple of times as a coffee sweetener and while she liked the taste both times it caused massive stomach discomfort to the point to where she won\x27t use the product anymore.

I suggest everyone do their own research on the product, some people seem to have no issues with it and others cannot tolerate even a little without some kind of stomach or intestinal distress. It seems the "safe dosage" is under 3 teaspoons of this stuff a day according to the experts I could find an opinion from online.

Overall, the product is sweet but to me not worth any of the side-effects that may come with its consumption.

review_headline: OneCup Construction Good -- No spilled coffee \x22sludge\x22 as described in other reviews
review_body:
To address the latest batch (As of Jan 2015), the K-cup construction works fairly well. I did not have any issues with coffee grains at the bottom of my mug or in a mess on my Keurig machine. But... they are definitely different than regular k-cups. The OneCups are made with a finely weaved cloth instead of the complete plastic enclosure you\x27re used to, but they\x27re built well enough now to keep everything in the cup and not in your drink. I\x27m guessing their design previously had an issue with the Keurig piercer that pokes a hole into the bottom of the cups, but with the new version there\x27s no noticeable hole in the OneCups that would leak "sludge" into your drink.

My one issue though is the overall packaging of the product. I\x27m used to k-cups arriving in a cardboard box with a perforated corner that can be ripped off to allow a sort of dispenser style of k-cups. However, the OneCups came in 4 plastic bags that smelled strongly of coffee (that can\x27t be helped though since they don\x27t use plastic to encapsulate the coffee).

As for the coffee itself, it tastes fine and it\x27s a great steal at the price.

product_title: Smokehouse Soups & Spices Hatcher Pass Lentil & Potato Soup, 13-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4)
review_headline: Terrific soup, but BUYER BEWARE: Only 6.5 oz packages, not the 13 oz listed.
review_body:
Would give 5 stars, but be VERY CAREFUL about package quantities. Advertised and pictured as 13 oz (368g) clear bags on the website, have purchased this size many times. As of late 2014, they have changed the packaging to small boxes and cut the size IN HALF to 6.5 oz (184g). Thus this is clearly false advertising, as you only get half of the stated quantity paid.

Thus a 3/5 average score (1/5 for the bait & switch; 5/5 for the product). Wonder how many folks have been buying only to get half the product they paid for. Fortunately, amazon have a terrific return policy, but still it\x27s disappointing to only get 50% of your purchase on account of inaccurate listings.

As for the soup, it is very tasty, though a bit salty if only using the included ingredients. I recommend adding 1/2 lb carrots, 1/2 lb leek, 1/4 lb celery and more lentils to dilute sodium content. I also like to add a few fresh spicy peppers (jalapeno, poblano, habanero) for a nice kick. Thickens substantially overnight.

To Amazon: Please accurately list the product quantities in the listings, and update stock photos and prices to properly reflect the significantly smaller quantities being shipped.

review_headline: Great, if you know what you are getting into...
review_body: I will get to detailed opinions of Lavazza\x27s dark roast Gran Filtro coffee, but first here is the summary:  Fantastic coffee that is slightly over roasted.  It is GREAT but not perfect like the normal Gran Filtro.  I bought this 2 pound bag after having tried and LOVED Lavazza\x27s regular Gran Filtro coffee for my daily pour-over brew.  The regular roast hashints of caramel which are absolutely fantastic.  Overall, the flavor is an almost perfect balance of nuts, subtle spice, and wonderful sweet caramel.  These seem to be the same beans just roasted a little more. This dark intense roast has a slight burnt taste to it.  Much like you would taste in a *$ brew.  All this to say, do not over-brew this coffee.  Stick with a coarse grind which will allow for a shorter brew time.  Now, if you want coffee perfection, then go with the original Gran Filtro.  You cannot get any bitter taste no matter how fine the grounds nor how hot your brew water is.  That blend is coffee perfection!  On the other hand, if you are used to a darker brew and have a taste for some slight bitterness - then this dark roasted Lavazza will likely be a step-up from what you are used to.  I will be drinking and enjoying all 2 pounds of this coffee one cup at a time.  Let me know if you have any questions.

It was wrapped in paper and had string (kind of looked like re-purposed plastic bag) tied around it with a hand written \x5C\x22Thank You.\x5C\x22 It was really cute and added a little personal touch that was appreciated.    I highly recommend this product.  (I would even try the maple and coffee flavors even though the only thing maple flavored I like is pure maple syrup and the only thing coffee flavored I like is coffee).    Edit: I just realized each gum pack comes with little papers to use to wrap and throw away your used piece of gum! (The gum is unwrapped). This is wonderful and makes me love the gum more. I like to use the papers to wrap a piece of gum that I plan to chew in the future and keep it in my desk drawer.

product_title: Camano Island Coffee Roasters, Organic Papua New Guinea Medium Roast
review_headline: A very smooth, non-biting medium roast coffee with sweet overtones
review_body:
This is a review of the whole bean Camano Island Coffee Roasters, Organic Papua New Guinea coffee. I was provided a free bag of coffee for evaluation.

I love my coffee and go out of my way to make it the right way to maximize its potential. What that means is that I use a French Press, Pour Over or makes espress and add Hot Water (Americano.)

One of the keys to making a terrific cup of coffee is to use freshly roasted beans. The bag of coffee I received yesterday had a date stamp on the bag of 1/29/15. So I received this coffee within 4 days of being roasted. That\x27s fresh coffee.

When you use a pour over, after adding the coffee to the filter, you pour just a small amount of hot water over the grounds to let them \x5C\x22bloom\x5C\x22. Wow, this coffee bloomed beautifully... growing to a nice frothy head and the smell was wonderful. After about 30 seconds I add the rest of the water and let the filter do its thing.

The resulting cup of coffee was delicious. I normally prefer a more bold and slightly more bitter coffee (yes, I like Starbucks Pike) but the Papua New Guinea had the most smooth taste. I did not feel the need to add any sweetener to it at all. The aftertaste develops after a little bit of sipping and leaves a suggestion of toffee in my mouth.

Very nice and enjoyable coffee that is organic and fair trade.

product_title: Barry\x27s Tea Gold Blend 80 Count 2-pack
review_body:
Visiting Ireland throughout childhood, I became used to the stronger tea they drink over there. After pouring boiling water over this bag, you\x27ll notice right away how much darker the tea is compared to those typically sold in US supermarkets. I like the strength of this tea because it is robust enough for whole milk or half and half. (Personally, I never use low-fat milk in tea or coffee.)

The secret to making a great cup of tea with these bags is to use water right off the boil and directly from the kettle. You can brew individually in a cup or use a few bags in a teapot. If using a teapot, heat it first with boiling water because a cold pot will lower the temperature of the water too much. Be careful not to over-brew, because the taste completely changes if left sitting too long. Test different brewing times to get the strength that\x27s right for you.

review_body: The best.  (Update below)  My first review was simple, I simply said it is "the best," and gave it Five Stars.  Somebody did not find that to be a helpful review for the 10 pack of this product. LOL. I admit that was kind of short (and to the point). Although "the best" sums it up, I\x27ll expound on what "the best" means to me. If I could give this chocolate bar 10 stars, I would. I like this chocolate bar so much, after having purchased individual bars for awhile, I bought a 10-pack. And another ten after that...and another. I think you get the point.  Taste is very subjective, of course. If you like a Hershey\x27s type of milk chocolate bar, or even a Hershey\x27s Special Dark Chocolate bar (only 45% cocoa), you are likely not seriously considering this chocolate bar. It would very likely not be nearly sweet enough for you.  Getting that out of the way, if you like deep, dark, semisweet-to-bittersweet chocolate, you may like this chocolate bar very much. I have found the G&B 85% Cocoa Dark Chocolate bar is the smoothest, most satisfying, "best"-tasting dark chocolate bar I have ever had in my life. Nothing about it is bitter (to me). I think It is better tasting than Moser Roth and Lindt - both of which are fine chocolate candies. Again, taste is subjective. And, the fact it is organic is a plus (I have purchased other organic bars that didn\x27t taste all that great).  I also prefer the fact that G&B\x27s section their chocolate bars into more, smaller pieces than other chocolate bar manufacturers (30 rectangular sections). I apologize for the redundancy (that fact is already listed under the ingredients photo in the ad itself, but one must do some rudimentary math - 12 pieces X 2.5 servings = 30).  However, I only eat one to four pieces at a time - this chocolate is that rich and satisfying.  So, I never have a whole "serving" - and consequently, one bar can last me a week or two.    So, for my liking, it is not only the best tasting, but it is also the best sectioned bar. I also like the sturdy cardboard serving box that the 10-pack ships in; it allows the bars to stand up, like a retail display  - easy to grab the next one from the cupboard. I would miss this product if it were to be taken off the market.  So, there is my review of the Green & Black\x27s Cocoa Chocolate Bar, Dark 85%, 3.5 Ounce Pack of 10 - and the reasons why I think it is "the best." Of course, the "best" way to to know if this is the "best" chocolate bar for your taste, would to spend 3 bucks and taste one for yourself. ;-)

(It wasn\x27t until I received half of the qty of capsules that I realized something was amiss) And as it is well known that many vitamin buyers like myself, purchase several types at the same time by re-buying from our order history list. Re-ordering off this list prevents me (or the buyer) from re-researching a product and repeating a purchase quickly and easily.
The thing about ordering like this, is when a company realizes what\x27s going on and suddenly spikes the price or changes the qty of the product. They realize that many buyers are not paying close attention after the initial purchase, making it easy for something like a price inflation to slip by. I believe this was done intentionally to rake in new revenue from unsuspecting buyers, and I feel that it is an unethical way to conduct business. They could have easily have added another option for buying or created a new posting and deleted this one, but instead changed the entire headline description and price, making it look as if nothing had changed.

The product itself seems okay, but if the company is willing to be unethical by weaseling a few extra bucks out of people there\x27s no telling what they\x27re wiling to do to cut corners while making the product. I personally have no plans to invest any more into it.

product_title: Wool Dryer Balls - Best Natural Fabric Softener - 6 Pack - No Toxic Chemicals - 100% Organic - Deluxe Edition - Gift Bag - FREE Guide on How to Eliminate Static
review_headline: Helpful Instructions and Tips--Love these Balls!
review_body:
This is my first experience with wool balls and I am glad this company explains how to use them and why they work. Nice, clean wool dryer balls that come in a reusable cloth bag. Mine did not have an odor, which was a relief since some natural wool products do . This company is wonderful about giving instructions and tips. After 40+ years of doing laundry, I finally learned how to help remove static (without dryer sheets) and why some clothes cause static and some do not. Wonderful company and great communication! They are very honest about their claims, too, about what wool dryer balls do, and what they do not do.

I don\x27t use fabric softener on my towels, because I don\x27t like a "coating" on my towels that will reduce absorbancy and may cause skin reactions. With these dryer balls, my towels are softer and fluffier (although maybe not as soft as if they had fabric softener). The towels and clothes dry faster and more evenly. I use about 9 balls for an average load, and 12 balls for an extra large load in my extra large dryer. I probably don\x27t need that many, but I have them so I use them all!

If you want your laundry scented, you can use essential oils with these. Since scent is such a personal preference, I add a few drops of essential oils to a cloth that I keep with the balls. I add the scented cloth (after the oil has dried) with my clothes only, since my boys don\x27t care for the aroma of the "Jasmine" scent I use. I add the scented cloth after the clothes are dry, and set the dryer to the "no heat" setting for 10 minutes. I have a citrus scent that I may try on a cloth for the boy clothes. I would like to try Lavender, but haven\x27t found a brand yet that smells good to me in that scent. Every brand of essential oils seems to smell different in Lavender.

I previously used those blue plastic balls with nubs (mainly for blankets and comforters), but I feel these wool balls work better and are moregentle on the clothes. Also, I use a lot more of these wool balls because they are less expensive than the hard plastic balls. I always worried about the chemicals from the heated plastic balls, but with the wool balls--no more worry about that!

These dryer balls also bring humor to our household. Sometimes a few balls fall out when opening the dryer door, or when removing the laundry from the dryer and placing it in the basket. They also sometimes get "lost" in the leg of a pair of jeans or a bundle of towels. My older boys grin when I tell them I am missing two of my balls and ask if they have seen my balls anywhere. In all reality, I probably get a bigger kick out of just saying that, but I\x27ll take a laugh wherever I can get it.

product_title: Neilmed NasaFlo Neti Pot
review_body:
Bought this at my local pharmacy for 9 bucks, FAR cheaper than here on Amazon.

I\x27ve never used a neti pot before, hell I\x27d never even *heard* of a neti pot til I got sick a few weeks back. I caught a cold, that rapidly turned into a sinus infection. Doctors were seen, medication given, and absolutely nothing improved. Took my mom to an appointment with her GI doc, one of the ladies in that office mentioned she had chronic sinus infections, and the only thing that helped was a "neti pot". I asked a lot of questions, and even though it sounded gross (cause cmon, it does), figured I\x27d give it a try. Super awesome lady at my pharmacy hauled out this box, said it had everything I needed, just grab a bottle of distilled water and go.

Today is the first time in 3 weeks I can breathe without coughing, gagging or feeling like the front of my face is going to fall off. It comes with really simple instructions (even has pictures in the book that comes with it), and LOTS of premixed soloution (tiny packets, you fill the pot, empty a packet into it, cover the holes and give it a good shake to dissolve).

review_headline: A rebuttal to MidWestGuy: Tangy Tangerine is not anymore toxic than water, is organic, and is good value for money
review_body:
This post is a rebuttal to MidwestGuy and his somewhat disingenuously-titled post \x275 day supply, overpriced, full of cadmium, thorium, strontium, and sugar?\x27 Please see my rebuttal here on my blog: http://chipstero7.blogspot.co.uk/rving of Tangy Tangerine. Let us put some numbers on it. There is around 250 grams in one glass of water and let us assume the water contains cadmium at a concentration of 5 \xCE\xBCg/L, which remember, is considered safe. Tangy Tangerine contains around 15 grams per serving with a cadmium concentration of 30 \xCE\xBCg/L. Therefore even though the water contains 3 times less the concentration the fact that it contains a higher number of grams (17 times higher) means that you will be swallowing almost 3 times the total amount of cadmium by drinking the one glass of water. Hence it is not anymore toxic than a glass of water.

Additionally, the concentration of strontium in Tangy Tangerine is 1 mg/L and the acceptable concentration of strontium that has been measured in drinking water in different parts of the United Sates by the EPA is 1 mg/L (3). So absolutely nothing unsafe there. And considering people would obviously be drinking more water by volume than Tangy Tangerine, you\xE2\x80\x99ll be getting a vastly greater amount of strontium from drinking water. And that is not counting the amount you\xE2\x80\x99ll be getting through food either. Thorium, another element you mentioned, is also naturally-occurring and replete throughout nature (though it can be artificially-produced) and is present in Tangy Tangerine at a concentration of 0.0025 mg/L (i.e. 2.5 \xCE\xBCg/L). A paper by Richard Betty titled \xE2\x80\x98Determination of Thorium in drinking water\xE2\x80\x99 (3) found that at a concentration of 4.76 \xCE\xBCg/L (almost twice the concentration present in Tangy Tangerine) natural thorium had a radioactivity of 11.25 pCi. To put that into perspective the average banana has a pCi value of 520. Hence a banana is almost 50 times as radioactive. So, all in all MidWestGuy, as far as I can see your comments amount to little more than uneducated fear-mongering and if you had any intellectual integrity you would retract your comments or at the very least substantiate them scientifically, which you have completely failed to do. Aggressively labelling anyone who disagrees with you as a propagandist affiliated with Youngevity is ridiculous. It is not their fault you have failed to substantiate your claims.

As far as the price goes, considering the very high concentration of the various minerals and vitamins each tub contains, it is really not such a bad deal. I purchased a \xC2\xA323 non-Youngevity bottle of plant-derived minerals from Amazon a while ago and as far as the concentration of minerals go, Tangy Tangerine blows it out the water. For example the non-Youngevity bottle contains 12.3mg, 3.7mg and 4.9mg of calcium, potassium and magnesium respectively per serving while Tangy Tangerine contains 50mg, 100mg, and 20mg. I usually take only one scoop per day. Given its high concentration I feel one scoop per day does me fine and lasts about 2 months. If one Tangy Tangerine is lasting you only 5 days then are obviously overdosing because the recommended dosage as stated on the tub is 2 scoops per day for a 2000 calorie diet. Unless you are eating like a horse. It is certainly cheaper for me than going down to Holland & Barrett and spending \xC2\xA3100+ to get the same concentration of minerals and vitamins from their synthetic, non-organic products, which I might add, cannot be absorbed as easily by the body. Furthermore the sugar-content of Tangy Tangerine is about 1 gram per serving. Within the ingredients the Tangy Tangerine 2.0 tub that I buy also notes that it is organic (5).

product_title: Asthmanefrin Starter Kit
review_headline: It\x27s a start but still needs work
review_body:
I have had asthma all of my life. I have been dependent on rescue inhalers just to get me through any given week. Primatene mist was a low cost alternative to prescribed albuterol inhalers. A few years ago, in an effort to cut down on CFC emissions, Primatene inhalers were taken off the market and asthma sufferers were left with a choice of forking out over $100 if you did not have insurance for the prescribed inhalers or purchasing something like the Asthmaneferin EZBreathe automizer.

The starter kit is not cheap. You are still going to fork over between $45 and $60 for this unit. You must follow the instructions to clean it after almost every use, because the medicine itself will cause the unit to clog and eventually fail. Never touch the mesh inside the delivery cup with anything - not your finger, not a Q-tip or even a bit of a tissue to clean it. Do not immerse it totally in the recommended water and vinegar solution. Deposit it in the cup, let it run for a few minutes. Rinse and be sure to keep the little blue protective cap that covers the delivery end with the nebulizer. If you don\x27t you will end up replacing this unit very soon after you buy it and will have to purchase another.

While the product inserts claim that you can expect 6 months to 1 year of use for this unit, I have yet to have one last me for more than half of that period of time - even if following the instructions to the letter. Futher, no one carries just the nebulizer cup alone, so you are going to have to buy another whole unit all over again. Asthmaneferin needs to offer just the replacement cups so folks with asthma such as myself don\x27t have several bases and no cup unit for medication delivery.

As for the medication itself, it is an epinephrine based medication. It can give you heart palpitations, make you feel almost dizzy and jittery. Pay careful attention to how your body reacts to it. The doses are fairly small, but they really open up your lungs very quickly. I have used this unit with albuterol solution used in my electric nebulizer when traveling, and it works fairly ok. For whatever reason, the albuterol saline in standard prescribed nebulizer dose is less likely to clog the unit than the medication that comes with it. In any case, always be sure to mention using the product to your doctor.

Please note, that a couple of years ago with earlier versions of this product, the units were recalled by the manufacturer. This was because the mesh in the delivery cup came loose and posed a potential choking hazard. Since the recall, this has not been an issue reported. product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_body:
I was first introduced to the FitBit about 1.5 years ago.

I loved the concept but I wasn\x27t that excited about it. Fortunately, I\x27ve received a FitBit Flex one year ago as a gift and yes, it changed my life. But this is not about the Flex, it is about the Charge HR.

This is my sixth day with the Charge HR. I won\x27t go into detail of what a FitBit does. I\x27m going to say my pros and cons about this device alone, compared to the Flex and to my general needs.

Pros:
- Very good feel, the bracelet is a huge improvement.
- It is actually a good watch.
- Accurate tracking of steps UNLESS you are running on the treadmill. Based on how you run, it may lose some steps.
- 95% accurate HR sensor. Tested against a professional one.
- Not having to sync all the time to see my progress is a good thing. My iPhone\x27s battery is grateful to the fact that it has a display.
- FAR BETTER charger. It resembles an USB connection and it seems far better built. One of my main complaints with the Flex was the charger.
- The same dongle as the Flex. I haven\x27t used it so far.
- Auto sleep tracking. This actually works. I don\x27t know how it works but it tracks when I go to sleep and when I wake up with 99% accuracy. It even knows the difference between lying in bed vs. actually sleeping.

Now the cons:
- Battery life is not 5 days with the HR sensor on. With it off and without syncing often, it may even go for 7 days. But with the HR sensor and active use of the device, it is about 4 days.
- Altimeter gets easily confused in the subway.
- It is not water proofed anymore. I\x27ve kept the Flex even in the pool. I need to take the Charge HR off when showering or in the sauna, not to mention any form of bath / pool.
- Not very effective on the treadmill. I estimate that it tracks about 70% of the steps. However, this is ONLY if you keep your hands in front of you. If you move them, then it works.
-No more replaceable bracelets. It is not a huge downside but I have like 5 for the Flex. I guess I\x27ll put them for sale.

Conclusion: Do I like it? Yes.
Do I suggest it? Yes.

Are better trackers out there? Maybe. Jawbone looks interesting. But I\x27m in this eco-system and I don\x27t see a reason to change. The only tracker that is more advanced (tracker, not smart phone) in my knowledge is the Surge. The Surge is a bit too much for my needs. The JawBone (the latest version) also seems interesting, with a few more sensors. The downside on that device is that you may lose it with ease.

If you judge the Charge HR as your first purchase, it may or it may not fit you. The best competitor is JawBone but there are at least a dozen brands on the market. If you judge it as an upgrade from the Flex or One, it is a great choice. It is like upgrading from an iPhone 4 to an iPhone 5S. It is the same thing but it does everything better.

Would I have bought this if my Flex was still functioning? Maybe, but not right now. It wasn\x27t urgent. But since I had to buy another tracker, I\x27m proud of my choice.

review_headline: Pills don\x27t make you lose weight! There\x27s only one way...
review_body:
I took this product exactly as directed. I did not experience any weight loss whatsoever, and I\x27m an active guy. Putting this pill aside, however, people need to know that the only way to lose weight and get into shape is to exercise and eat properly! You hear it all the time because it\x27s true. People need to stop trying to find some alternative to that; this is none. If you\x27re not willing to eat properly and exercise, fine. It\x27s your choice, and that should be respected. However, I believe that you should get real and simply accept that your weight will remain the same until you can start doing what you need to do. Stop wasting your money on these fads and just be honest with yourself. If you\x27re not ready, you\x27re just not ready. I think buying pills like these is actually a form of denial, but let\x27s not get into psychology right now.

When you *are* ready, make a *real* commitment; one in which you decide to actually do the work. Just do the best you can. A little is better than nothing. My advice is to take the money you would have spent on this product and buy a PEDOMETER (it counts how many steps and the distance you walk). Walk around very single day at first. I don\x27t care if it\x27s just to the corner and back. Establish that habit right away.

There was a time in my life that I\x27d become tired if I walked three or four blocks. Now, I walk for HOURS at a time. I kid you not. I live in NYC and my walks are now extremely rewarding to me. They can be this way for you, too.

I worked up to those distances block by block, one step at a time. It took me a year to start walking long distances with ease. I learned the appreciate the walk along the way, and not to hope that it concludes as quickly as possible. THAT was a big key. The right ear is 25% less proficient. I have problems at restaurants and other places with noisy backgrounds cupping my ear with my hand to hear table-mates. I then moved the Soundhawk to my better left ear. The experience has improved. The ability to adjust the volume, full/bright and boost functions works well.
