Now to the points I really like: The remote microphone is a great addition. Lay it beside the TV speaker, on a table or attached to a person you want to hear, it is very helpful. In addition, I would suggest maybe laying it on a small piece of  cloth or foam so that the hard table surface does less projection of reflected table noise. The hands free phone capability is also very useful. To summarize, the rating is 4 out of 5 due to the loop but the functionality is a five. The Soundhawk is a great interim step to a full blown hearing aid system which I hope Soundhawk is working on. If people ask, I have no problems telling them it enhances my hearing.

product_title: Afunta High Quality Genuine Somic 7.1 Surround Gaming Headset Stereo Headphone Powerful Bass Earphone with Mic USB Plug 2.9m Cords (Black)
review_body: Ok, right off the bat, I am and have always been a headphone freak. I have a dozen or so sets ranging from $4,000 Stax electrostatics to $200 custom earbuds. So with that in mind, here are my impressions of these AFUNTA gaming headphones. They are actually a SOMIC 7.1 Sound Effect Gaming Headset. Usual Chinese revolving door company name changes (to protect the innocent?) makes trying to get a proper description difficult.  They arrived in a white ziploc bag with a manual (all in Chinese!!) and a mini software CD. These phones are attractive, mine came in gloss black with red accents, and fit over ears completely with good comfort. The headband is nicely padded and promises to be comfortable for hours of gaming, time will tell. There is a neat lighted volume control puck on the cord to control volume and mic usage Overall impressions so far are quite good considering how inexpensive they were on Amazon.  The software installed with out any drama and despite the manual being in Chinese, you should have no problems if you have any computer skills. In addition to the driver, you get a nice control panel, in English, to play with and configure your preferences.  With everything set to flat frequency response, I sampled various music types to profile the overall frequency bias. Most headphones have a particular frequency emphasis, some are bright, some are bass loaded like those junk Beats phones that all the cool people wear. These phones are slightly midrange but with fairly bright highs depending on source material. I went in to the control panel and set up for gaming surround sound. I launched Gears of War and was very much aware of an enhancement of the game environment. A definite sense of 360 sound environment. I look forward to playing pc games with these headphones based on first impressions.  I have not played with the mike as I do not have time for multi gaming so I cannot help you with any impressions. My experience with single player PC games has been quitesatisfactory.  These phones are strictly USB connected. There is no option for 3.5 connection so be aware of this before you buy. My built in sound card took a crap so I needed a set of PC phones with USB connection to give me access to my new sound card. These headphones are exactly what I needed. Reliability is an unknown factor at this time but I will update in future if there are issues. I would very much encourage you to try these headphones if they meet your needs. The price is right and the performance is surprising. A bargain, worth a buy.

review_body: My wife received her Fitbit Flex from her children for Christmas.  I am not sure if they bought it through Amazon or not.  However, in the interest of getting the word out about this product I wanted to offer this review.  She loved Fitbit and has been using is it faithfully to track her activity and sleep.  The interface with her apple phone was very convenient and helpful.    The problem she has had was while skiing at Copper Mountain ski resort  the Fitbit fell off of her wrist somewhere on the Mountain.  I seems rather ironic that a product made for activity has a wrist band where either the clasp breaks or the band breaks under normal physical activity.  To make matters worse it is impossible to find a contact number to call customer service at Fitbit.  We would not recommend this product, unless Fitbit would be willing to replace the lost item.    Update February 14, 2015:  I am updating the Fitbit Flex from 1 star to 3 stars.  The reason for this is the outstanding customer service that we received from Fitbit.  We emailed our complaint to Customer Service through the Help function on their webpage.  Within the hour we received a followup email concerning my wife\x27s lost Flex.  Upon verifying her account the Fitbit team promised to replace her Flex and within a week my Wife received her replacement Flex.  I can not be more pleased with Yuri and the Fitbit Team.     The only reason that I have given the Fitbit Flex 3 stars and not 5 stars is because the clasp design is flawed and allows the Flex to either break or come undone under normal activity.  There are third party vendors that have created solutions to this flaw but I believe Fibit should address this problem directly. Until they do this my rating will only be 3 stars.

review_headline: It messed with my hormones, in a good way.
review_body: I started taking these because I have borderline Hypothyroidism. At the time I started taking these I had ran out of my Levothyroxin prescription and recently switched doctors and my new doctor didn\x27t agree I had Hypothyroidism. So, I sought a more natural approach to increase energy, lose weight, and manage my intolerance to cold. So, I\x27ve been taking it for over half a year now, and even though I was re-prescribed Levothyroxin a couple months ago I\x27ve continued to keep taking it. I decided to take one pill a day instead of two, because I wanted to play it safe, especially now that I\x27m back on Levothyroxin. It actually works very similar to Levothyroxin for energy. In that it gives a tiny boost of energy, barely enough to notice, but just enough to feel like, yeah, I feel a little better. I didn\x27t notice any major differences with weight loss, but I didn\x27t notice that with Levothyroxin either. My cold tolerance is a little better, and, I have been checking my temperature every so often and now instead averaging 96 or 97 something, I\x27m now more likely to be 97 or 98 something. Now, here\x27s the weird part, my bra size before starting these vitamins was 50C, which I always felt was a somewhat small cup size for my body type, and small compared to my sister\x27s breast size, but as of today? It is a whopping 48DDD! How am I sure it was the Thyroid Energy vitamins? Well first of all I started taking them at 23 and a half years old, too old for a growth spurt. The growth didn\x27t start until after I began taking them. I didn\x27t gain any weight in the time span. I saw my doctor and had my hormones checked(which were all in the normal range), and had pregnancy ruled out. I became suspicious of the Thyroid Energy vitamins because they were the only new thing I was taking at the time, so when I ran out at one point with a cup size of 48DD and didn\x27t get a new bottle for another month, it was the perfect opportunity to see what would happen, and my breasts stopped growing, shortly after starting up on the Thyroid Energy vitamins, they started growing again! Now at 48DDD my bra is starting to feel snug but I think the growing has finally stopped. I\x27m not totally sure why they stimulated breast growth in me, when obviously most women didn\x27t have that side-effect. Apparently L-Tyrosine and Folate can both increase bust size. Although from what I gather they don\x27t cause very much growth, maybe I\x27m special, but I believe the reason these vitamins increased my breasts so much was because my hormones were off due to my Hypothyroidism and PCOS, and these vitamins regulated and normalized my hormones so I could have the breast size I was meant to have. It was annoying to keep having to buy new bras, but I am a very large woman and now my breasts finally look like they fit in with the rest of my body. I will continue taking these vitamins, because I feel like they\x27re doing something good to my hormones.

review_headline: really wanted to like this product
review_body:
I really, really wanted to like this product. I\x27ve been slowly moving toward more natural health and beauty products and am interested in reducing waste. The Moon Cup seems like the perfect product for me and I was really attracted to the thought of a reusable product that wouldn\x27t disrupt my natural internal balance and wouldn\x27t contribute to landfill waste. But... BUT (there\x27s always a \x27but,\x27 isn\x27t there?), I found the Moon Cup to be so uncomfortable as to be unusable!

The first day I tried it I was only cycling lightly, and it felt fine. Insertion was easy, I didn\x27t feel it all day, and I was even able to sleep with it in. The problem started when I tried to remove the cup in the morning. I couldn\x27t! The cup suctions into you and attempting to "break the seal" as the instructions stated was impossible for me to do! My hands just couldn\x27t reach that far and I wasn\x27t able to get a strong enough grip to remove it myself- I had to ask my boyfriend for help... TWICE! I continued to use the Moon Cup that day, which was much heavier, flow-wise. That\x27s when I started to notice the cup more. It was uncomfortable and needed to be removed more frequently, and even though I was able to remove it myself by this point, it was, quite literally, a bloody mess. I probably spent a good 20 minutes in the bathroom at work trying to wrestle this thing out of me and was covered in sweat and looked like I had just murdered someone by the time I got it out! It felt like a victory every time I removed it but a huge disappointment once I realized it was just going back in to be wrestled and painfully removed a few hours later.

This product is probably going to be a really great thing for a lot of women, and congrats to them. But I found the product to be uncomfortable to wear, difficult to remove, and just plain painful in a sensitive area of my body. It\x27s just not for me. I will be switching to organic cotton tampons in the future.ton tampons in the future.

I ordered a bottle of these and it\x27s clear that they are NOT enteric coated as claimed (it\x27s just a gelatin capsule), nor is the oil molecularly distilled. Why the original retail price of $59.95? For comparison I purchased a bottle of Now Foods Ultra Omega 3, Fish Oil Soft-gels, 180-Count (retail $44, Amazon $23). NOW is a reputable company (unlike Manga Naturals, which mostly makes trendy diet supplements). The NOW fish oil is molecularly distilled (to ensure there are no heavy metals) and truly enteric coated (to prevent fish burps after ingestion). I would not waste my money on the Manga Naturals bait and switch product.  p.s. It\x27s my opinion that many of the 5-star reviews of this item appear to be canned, written by ringers who make silly and questionable claims about fish oil in general and this product in particular. Click on the reviewer names and you will find that for virtually ALL of the 5-star reviews, this fish oil is the only product ever reviewed by that person. Click on reviews with fewer stars and you\x27ll see that those people have reviewed other products on Amazon, leading me to believe that their reviews are legit.

Not so much taking it apart, but reassembling it was a nightmare. And it felt like every time I "re-loaded" it, the material got damaged. Luckily, I recently came up with a way to make this process a breeze:

1. After cleaning, put the bottom of the sleeve into a clean sock
2. Insert socked sleeve back into the top of the plastic case, bottom side first
3. Unscrew bottom of the plastic case and grab the end of the sock.
4. Pull through until the top of the sleeve is in place with the plastic casing.
5. Gently work the sock though the rest of the way and pull off of the sleeve.
6. If the bottom of the sleeve is exposed, gently shake the device until it falls back into place.

Hope that helps someone. Turns a 10 min job into a 2 min job.

All said and done, I am very happy with my purchase.

review_headline: Don\x27t waste your money. These oils likely have no therapeutic value, and are potentially dangerous
review_body: I had been using a popular, "main brand" essential oil, but for curiosities sake, I decided to try a few other brands. People kept telling me I was over paying for oils, and there were cheap brands out there that were "just as good", "same quality", etc. I know that with the loose laws and stipulations that the government has in place for essential oils, companies can pretty much say whatever they want about their products (100% pure, therapeutic grade, etc.) without it being true at all. The only way to know for sure was to try other stuff. I had a very open mind, because if there really is something out there that\x27s as good as what I\x27m using, but cheaper, I\x27d like to know!! The Kis website said all the right things, and was very attractive, and user friendly, but the oils were not available to purchase yet through the site, so I came to good ole\x27 Amazon. Being somewhat familiar with the process of essential oils, I was pretty unnerved by how cheap they were.. They came fast, the packaging was nice. I opened them all up and gave them all a good sniff. Put a drop in my hands.. Continued to really experience the. I have been using essential oils for quite some time now, so I am pretty familiar with how they are supposed to smell, work, feel, etc. The aroma was pretty "off" on most of them, and the consistency was more oily that I am used to. Nothing so obvious that a brand new essential oil user would catch on to though. Well, 15 minutes later I had a throbbing headache, and was very nauseated. I am very sensitive to scented things, and synthetic fragrances. I knew without a doubt at this point that these oils are absolutely adulterated. I have never.. EVER had an essential oil cause a headache. It\x27s quite contradictory to how an true EO is supposed to work. Anyway, since a bottle of essential oil only needs to contain a minimum of 5% PURE, UNADULTERATED essential oil in order to legally be labeled "100% pure", it is no surprise to me that these oils are adulterated. Likely containing synthetics, chemicals to enhance the fragrance, cheaper oils to make it stretch.. Don\x27t waste your money. My favorite brands are HealthForce and Vibrant Health - so if you know anything about these 2 companies, you\x27ll understand that I only use the best of the best. I\x27ve been in the health food and supplement game for over 20 years and have sorted through the junk and the gems.

I\x27ve also been teaching nutrition and health sciences for over 15 years. In these 15+ years, I continually see again and again that what most people consider \x5C\x22healthy foods\x5C\x22 I consider better than most, but still poor nutrition. So I\x27m writing this review to see where I set my health food bar and to help you raise your bar, if you want to. I posted my recommendations at the bottom of this review.

So where does this Vega Sport Recovery Accelerator fall into my lineup for post workout nutrition? Near the top, but still with room for improvements.

First off the taste is pretty similar to Gatorade or any standard sports drink. It\x27s not a bad flavor, but it doesn\x27t taste like any tropical fruits that I\x27m aware of. In fact the ingredient label has zero tropical fruits on it. Natural flavors, stevia and some (awesome) herbs give it it\x27s flavor. In the flavor department, this drink could make some improvements, in my opinion.

Does it work? Yes, it does. All of the ingredients serve the purpose of body recovery post workout. Some reduce inflammation, some repair muscle fibers, some boost energy levels, and other support the immune system. I\x27ll go over each ingredient here to show the purpose of what\x27s in this Vega supplement.

1) The magnesium and potassium act primarily as the minerals for inflammation reduction and muscle soreness recovery. Turmeric and the curcuminoids are the herb-based method of inflammation reduction.

2) A range of amino acids, along with the pea and rice proteins create the muscle repair.

3) Ginseng, maca and the B-vitamins act as energy boosters.

4) Astragulus and cayenne red pepper are for immune system support - which is important for recovery because the immune system reduces the inflammation post workout.

So the ingredients are excellent for post workout recovery. I can clearly see why so many people are benefiting from this product. If you have a basic or even no understanding of health food science, then this supplement is a very easy way to support your body and accelerate workout recovery. I would recommend it. But if you are more scrutinizing of what you put into your body and want only the best of the best, there are better choices - such as building your own recovery drinks - which is what I do.

Here the products that I feel offer similar or even better post workout recovery, and have a higher quality ingredient list. I created this structure to give the body exactly what it needs in the order it needs it: First, carbohydrate and electrolyte replacement to continue the fitness benefits without reducing muscle mass. Second, protein to repair and increase muscle. Third, complete meal-based nutrition with all carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals that body needs - all 100% vegan.

Here is my recovery drink / drinks:

1) The first thing post workout I ingest is 100% natural (no additives or preservatives) coconut water. Here I get my immediate carbohydrates, electrolytes and some vitamins and minerals. The biggest are: potassium (19% RDA and 150% more than a banana), calcium (4% RDA) and magnesium (4% RDA). The coconut water restores the calories I burned, the salts (electrolytes) I used and released (sweat), and the minerals my body needs to repair muscle. There is no better sports drink on the planet in my opinion. This takes about 10 minutes to drink and digest.

2) Within 30 minutes of the end of my workout I use an easy to digestand assimilate protein supplement / food. There is a 2 hour window to get protein (amino acids) to the muscle for optimal recovery, repair and building. This 2 hour window includes digestion time, so don\x27t wait longer than 1 hour or the amino acids won\x27t make it to the muscle in time. For this I use one of the following (and often rotate my schedule):

- Vibrant Health Puregreen Protein, Vanilla. This is 100% vegan and organic or wild harvest. 20g protein and lots of vitamins and minerals

- HealthForce Nutritionals Warrior ForceTM Elite Green ProteinTM Cool Green. 100% vegan, organic or wild harvested. Uses spirulina and chlorella (algae) as the main plant-based protein sources.

- Nutrex Hawaiian Spirulina. 100% vegan. Spirulina is considered by many vegan health experts to be the highest quality vegan protein because it\x27s 100% whole food based and a complete protein (amino acid set). Most other vegan proteins (rice protein, pea protein, hemp protein, soy protein, etc.) are highly processed partial foods.

- BlueBonnet Whey Protein (from Grass-fed New Zealand cows). Whey is whole food protein from dairy. It\x27s a whole food, but it\x27s not vegan.

- Mt Capra Whey Protein (from grass-fed goats in the USA) combined with Mt Capra Mineral Whey (low in protein, but high in minerals for immune system health and muscle/bone recovery). This combination is not vegan, but is whole food based.

2) I wait 30 minutes after my 1st protein drink to then supplement with minerals, vitamins, carbs and more protein. For this I use:

- Vibrant Health Maximum Vibrance Digestive Supplement, 24.9 Ounces (My #1 favorite supplement and 100% vegan and organic or wild harvested. Gives me 100% RDA or more of nearly every vitamin and minerals. It\x27s truly the best meal replacement supplement out there

I\x27ll also add:
- 1 tsp organic turmeric powder (not the curcumin extracts because the whole turmeric roots shows better research)
- 4 TBSP organic hemp seeds for the Omega 3 fatty acids
- 1/2 cup organic blueberries, 1 packet organic acai or other high antioxidant fruit
- 1 apple for carbohydrate calories
- 2 TBSP organic cacao powder for antioxidants and magnesium
- 1 tsp maca powder for hormone and immune support

If I am exercising at a gym or not at home within 1 hour of ending my workout, then I\x27ll use the Maximum Vibrance powder alone with water. I may also eat an apple to replace my glycogen stores (carbohydrate fuel) if the workout was intense and the cocount water not feeling sufficient. Or I\x27ll skip the apple and drink another coconut water with the Maximum Vibrance. Then I\x27ll try to eat a whole food meal as soon as possible, waiting for the Maximum Vibrance to digest in the stomach (about 25-30 minutes). It is important to replace the carbohydrates post workout to avoid using the muscle as fuel.

Vega\x27s ingredient quality -2 stars

Unfortunately Vega uses zero organic or wild harvested products - which means that Vega\x27s supplements will likely include the residue of pesticides, herbicides and chemical fertilizers, as well as potential GMO ingredients. This low quality ingredient list is my biggest gripe with Vega. Otherwise they are using good nutritional science.

All in all, this Vega Sport Recovery Accelerator is a good formula for the average Joe or Jane wanting to support their body\x27s recovery post workout. review_body:

I have never been able to find a scented candle or air freshener that helps, without smelling strong, artificial or overpowering. This diffuser, combined with the peppermint oil, emits a light, fresh, natural aroma.

review_headline: Tests indicate that the product contains little Saw Palmetto
review_body:
The attorney general of New York tested Spring Valley Saw Palmetto from multiple store locations. Only one sample tested positive for Saw Palmetto. Here is a link to the report:
http://www.ag.ny.gov/press-release/ag-schneiderman-asks-major-retailers-halt-sales-certain-herbal-supplements-dna-tests

From the AG\x27s press report:

Six \xE2\x80\x9CSpring Valley\xE2\x80\x9D brand herbal supplements per store were purchased and analyzed: Gingko Biloba, St. John\xE2\x80\x99s Wort, Ginseng, Garlic, Echinacea, and Saw Palmetto. Purchased from three geographic locations with representative stores in Buffalo, Utica and Westchester.

None of the supplements tested consistently revealed DNA from the labeled herb. One bottle of garlic had a minimal showing of garlic DNA, as did one bottle of Saw Palmetto. All remaining bottles failed to produce DNA verifying the labeled herb.

Of the 90 DNA test run on 18 bottles of herbal products purchased, DNA matched label representation 4% of the time.
Contaminants identified included allium, pine, wheat/grass, rice mustard, citrus, dracaena (houseplant), and cassava (tropical tree root).

review_body:
The FitBit Charge HR is awesome!! However, when I first bought it I ordered a small, but I received it and according to the directions it should be at least an inch away from your wrist bone. The positive to this situation is that it still is monitoring your heart rate, so if your goal is to track calories burned... it is extremely accurate in this scenario!

Lastly, the app is great and it\x27s so so easy to sync! I love reaching my goals.. which is obviously the point to making them. The only problem with the app thus far is the accuracy when logging the food. Most of the generic food items seem extremely incorrect. Also, since it\x27s a new app there are still not a lot of brands added into the database. What\x27s great is that you can help out fitbit and submit pictures to the database to be processed and added for your food brands of choice.

I use one until it shows it age.  When washed and dried immediately after use, a single spoon lasts at least 2 months (and even longer if oiled), so a bagful of these can go a long way.    If there\x27s a need to disinfect beyond the capability of dish soap and water, I give the bamboo utensil a good wipe down with Seventh Generation Disinfecting Wipes, which kill 99.99 percent of germs botanically and are completely food-safe.  Once the disinfectant dries, I wash the spoon with soap and water, anyway, for good measure.  Bamboo is actually a grass, not a tree, and it\x27s very renewable.

product_title: VisionQuest Organics~ Dream Herb Tea- 28 grams (1 oz)
review_body: I don\x27t normally write reviews, but because this stuff gets such mixed feedback I thought I should add my thoughts to help anyone looking for information prior to purchasing. This covers my own input as well as addressing some of the reviews I\x27ve seen.    1. \x5C\x22Is it really bitter?\x5C\x22 -- Yes. It is. I\x27m not a botanist, but I suspect it\x27s a different kind of bitterness than you would find in, say, a lemon. You can make sweet lemonade that counteracts its bitterness. You can\x27t counteract this bitterness. It almost has a different, almost oily, texture to it that is near impossible to mask. That said, I have to say, it is tolerable, and you can get used to it. If you can handle an India Pale Ale, you can get used to this. Personally, what I do, is to go half-and-half with the calea and lavender, three tsp sugar, and a dollop of honey. I\x27ll be the first to admit, I didn\x27t like it much at first. But I\x27m stubborn, and I stuck with it, and I can attest that it is possible to get used to the bitterness.    2. \x5C\x22Does it work?\x5C\x22 - Scientifically speaking...I dunno. Let me explain that. For me, personally, if I make tea out of about 1 tsp. of this stuff, it\x27ll affect the quality of my dreams about 50% of the time. But I often have weird dreams anyway, and the expectation of possibly having altered dreams because of this is a potential primer for said dreams, if not an outright placebo effect. As you might guess, I\x27ve been trained in research psychology, and the biggest problem from my standpoint is that I have a sample size of one. To get back on track: in my estimation, the calea works for me approximately 50% of the time, given a large enough dose in the tea and ideal sleeping conditions. Your mileage may vary. From what I\x27ve read, traditionally one is supposed to smoke some of this stuff in addition to drinking it in tea form. I haven\x27t tried that yet. When I do, I\x27ll write another review.    3. \x5C\x22Is this worth my money?\x5C\x22 - That is entirely subjective, but for the purposes of an admittedly subjective product review, I\x27d say: probably. I just bought this stuff for the second time, from the same seller. It\x27s good enough for me that I went ahead and bought some more. All told, that was less than $20. I spend less on beer each week, and the last batch of this tea lasted me a year and a half (and the dreams were a lot more fun than stumbling around the apartment).    So, if you can handle a little bitterness in the pursuit of wisdom (or an IPA, at the very least), and can spare $20 for at least a year\x27s worth of tea, this is quite possibly the best recreational, consumable plant product available for easy purchase. Now, everyone\x27s brain is different, so you might get different results from other people, but I think it\x27s at least worth a try, based upon my own experience. Seriously, try lavender and honey.    To address other reviews I\x27ve seen:  Yes, it\x27s bitter. It really is. Why are you surprised by this? You have read reviews, and you have done your research at least as far as Wikipedia. Right? You do read this stuff, right? Yes, it\x27s bitter! Don\x27t give a bad review on the product for being no more than what it is! Seriously, you buy a dried plant product with an Aztec-y name, put it in your teapot, and then complain about the taste like you didn\x27t know what to expect? Do your bloody research!    Yes, there are bits of woody stems in the mix. Do you take exception to finding roots in your dandelion root tea? Do not automatically assume that the most useful parts of the plant are in the leaves alone. It could be in the bark. I don\x27t know. Do you? Does aspirin come from the leaf or the bark of the plant of its origin? (look it up) That said, the bag I\x27ve just received appears to have a lot more leafy bits to it versus woody stems, compared to the previous bag I purchased in 2013. Maybe they do read the reviews. Either way, I don\x27t think it\x27s a problem.    Bottom line of a too-long review: I think this stuff is worth trying at least once. And I mean an honest try. Finish the bag. Dreams are an awesome part of life, and for me they are one of the best parts of life. For me, that alone makes it worth a little bit of bitter tea. I guess I almost think of dreaming as an art form that might require a little bit of sacrifice on the part of my taste buds. But if that\x27s not your thing, there are always other forms of entertainment.

When I called fitbit about the problem with the tracker deciding to put itself in a nonresponsive coma - I asked if the replacement they would send could be an XL band. Nope - won\x27t do it.  Fitbit you are making me unhappy once again. review_body:
[[VIDEOID:ac36f9585418362455d2fd635ef76031]] The creators at BACtrack are considered heroes for some. They have been working diligently, for more than a decade, on enabling individuals to check their own blood alcohol level. BACtrack was the first FDA approved personal use breathalyzer, and was featured on shows like The Doctors, Dr Phil, and Mythbusters to name a few.

BACtrack Mobile, Why You Should Buy It?
The BACtrack Mobile breathalyzer, or any BACtrack breathalyzer in general, is a very practical item to own. Having the option to connect it to your smartphone enriches the awesomeness, and the ingenuity of this valuable gadget.

PROS:

- Good visibility -Once connected to your smartphone BACtrack Mobile is no longer restricted to a small built-in screen (which might be hard to see when you are under the influence), but instead will have big, bright, and easy to see results.

- Countdown to sobriety-I love that the app gives you the ability to see your past results, and uses that information to determine your ZeroLine, a patented technology by BACtrack which determines how long it takes your blood alcohol level to drop to 0.00%. This feature knows me better than I know myself. ZeroLine predicted an accurate time frame for me to reach sobriety almost every time I used it. If at any time the prediction was inaccurate it was most likely because I didn\x27t drink enough water.

- Small and rechargeable- This device is truly mobile. It is small enough to fit in your pocket and the included carrying case makes it even more mobile. Recharge it using the included micro-USB cable (battery life varies depending on usage)

- Sanitary - It comes with three mouthpieces so you don\x27t share it with people (don\x27t be nasty!) and you can buy more mouthpieces here. Past users have shared that you can use a straw, and it works equally well.

- Accurate - Thanks to some friends who work in law enforcement, we were able to compare the BACtrack\x27s results to a device commonly used in public safety. We got the same results! This is because, BACtrack Mobile uses Police-Grade Xtend\xC2\xAE Fuel Cell Sensor Technology (A fancy way to say it\x27s accurate). To learn more about this technology check out this page.

IMPROVEMENTS:
One drawback that I was able to find with BACtrack Mobile is that if your phone dies, you\x27re out of luck. This breathalyzer is practically useless without a phone. However, it is really easy to borrow someones else phone and install the app. It takes literally less than one minute to connect the breathalyzer to any phone after installing the app. Maybe including a built-in screen that can be turned off when the breathalyzer is connected to the phone to preserve battery could fix this.

In Summary:
The accuracy of BACtrack Mobile is astonishing. The features, the design, and the app are like a team that complete each other. review_headline: You can\x27t light it,you can\x27t smoke it, it doesn\x27t work. Grrr
review_body:
-- Doesn\x27t light
-- Doesn\x27t smoke
-- Doesn\x27t light

I spent 20 minutes trying to light it and couldn\x27t. A few weeks later got it lit by plugging up all the air gaps that exist around the little metal pan the pipe uses to hold the tobacco. As they have made it, so much air flow comes down around/under this metal bowl that you can\x27t get the flame to draw DOWN through the tobacco. I suppose if you attached a machine to the mouthpiece that drew down a huge amount of air, rapidly, you could get the tobacco to light. But for humans, can\x27t even light it. And I\x27m an experienced pipe smoker.

Finally I got it to work by putting chewing gum around the pan (required unscrewing some screws) to plug this asinine massive air leak. But soon the chewing gum melted from the heat. I did not feel like going to the hardware store to buy heat resistant caulk to make this pipe smokeable.

Really the most absurd excuse for a "pipe" I have ever encountered. The makers of it (Chinese likely) obviously never tried to even light their product to see if it could be smoked.

This would only be worth buying as a prop in a play but only if the actor didn\x27t actually have to smoke it. Completely ridiculous. Complete waste of money. Pissed me off, too.

product_title: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband
review_body:
Design: window could be bigger; and should be in the middle of band instead of near the top. Color: picks up dust, lint, dry skin. Maybe with another color this wouldn\x27t be as noticeable. I live in Central NY and we all have dry skin, this shows it. Would be great if it could be rinsed off, but it can\x27t!
Working: syncs nicely most of the time. Battery: I am getting a day of solid power, then it drops to half and I charge it. Seems very short. Sleep: not too impressed with the stats- vs my original Jawbone. I actually liked pushing the button on the Jawbone - it really was more accurate and more visually pleasing on the app- easier to read. Speaking of the app, my daughter and I are pals but all I can seem to find are accumulated steps for her. With Jawbone, you can see everyone\x27s stats on most everything. Hate to keep comparing, but that\x27s what I have to compare it to! Step accuracy- while wearing this band at the same time as a Misfit Shine- on same arm- Misfit has counted up to 4000 more steps. I sort of average the two. Note that I just had back surgery, need toe fusion, and back fusion- so I mostly walk around the home and have been very disabled due to my back since Nov 2013- so I am not a very active person. Weather prohibits walking outside with a Canadian Crutch! Heart rate counter- appears relatively accurate. I have a finger HB/O2 Sat monitor and accurate while sitting. It can jump up to 80\x27s-90\x27s while walking around house doing menial tasks. This seems correct to me- since I am quite outta shape. Once in a while it will give a wacky reading of 115-150 or so, incorrect! For my purposes, it works fine. Stairs: only one time did it give an incorrect reading- credited for some I did not do; but on the whole, very accurate. Ease of use: easy to set up, easy to use app. Viewing window- mine has a distinct click when I push it; my daughters does not. Nap- yes, I sleep pretty awful so I nap. It has only picked up one napping event so far, which is disappointing. Pep peeve- besides the low battery, the lint grabbing and the low battery, the strap holder is a bit annoying. When you choose your correct hook- watch hole- you then have to secure it with the watch band holder-,not always easy to slide it up the band since it is the same material!
Overall-, I am pleased with this item but not thrilled with it for the reasons listed.
This is a review after using this for 6 days. I really hope there is an update to see your competitors entire data and not just steps. If I am wrong and you can, correction would be great!
Would I recommend it- at this point I would say yes. I am purchasing a Jaybird Reign in addition to this one. Waterproof- swimming and bicycling with the attachments you need. Sad that you need to purchase 2 to get the features you want. My kids both have the Misfit Shine and it feels like wearing nothing.... I had one, not working quite right but decent for the price point. Thanks for reading this, I hope it helps someone like me!

review_headline: Not a miracle for severe reflux, but a huge help
review_body: In my quest to get off omeprazole, which has caused me a significant magnesium deficiency (and heaven knows what else), I decided to try these out. I\x27ve been taking them fairly consistently for about a month and a half, and while they don\x27t get rid of my reflux completely, they have helped me drop another notch with the omeprazole, from 20mg every other day or two to 10mg (this is down from 40mg/day a year ago, so I\x27ve made progress!). Taking them on an empty stomach, as I\x27d seen suggested elsewhere, didn\x27t work well for me so I now take them with or after a meal. Sometimes it takes two instead of one. The standard dosage is twice what\x27s listed on this particular brand\x27s bottle, and if I had the money to spare, I\x27d take that much per day. But alas, I don\x27t right now. The effect, at least for me, doesn\x27t last like omeprazole does...if I don\x27t take it multiple times a day, I will have issues, so it\x27s been a little bumpy, but tolerable. Keep in mind, my reflux is very severe, and it is constant...if you don\x27t have severe issues, or just have problems after meals, this may be an ideal solution for you, and just may get rid of your reflux entirely.

product_title: Maternity - Probiotic Enzyme Digestive Support - Nutritional Supplements and Prenatal Vitamins - Multivitamins - Enhance Your Immune System To Decrease Your Baby\x27s Risk of Allergies
review_headline: Convinced a skeptic probiotics really work though needs a more readable label
review_body:
While I received this product free of charge, this review is my own personal thoughts on the product. First about me: I am not pregnant, but was assured this product works well for those of us not expecting as well. I have not used probiotic products in the past but have always been curious if I would notice any difference. And frankly, I will also be honest and say I\x27ve been pretty skeptical about all the recent hype about probiotics.

First things first - the packaging, which is the only reason I deducted one star on the review. The instructions are reverse printed - white on the dark green part of the label and the combination of type font, small print and dark background make them very hard to read even for those of us that do not needing reading glasses. Since directions are critical, I hope the vendor will consider a redesign of the label and font to make these directions more readable. Especially with the price of this product, spending a bit more for a higher quality label should be a given.

Directions say to take 1-2 with partially cooked meals and 3 with fully cooked meals. I have to admit even with web searches I am not sure why they give this advice. Most recommendations on probiotics are to take them on an empty stomach so stomach acid will not destroy the probiotics. Perhaps this is pregnancy related and that is why I don\x27t understand the reason?

The pills themselves are clear capsules about the same size as most standard capsules - in other words not small, but not so large that they are hard to swallow. Dimensions are approximately 3/4\x5C\x22 long by 1/4\x5C\x22 diameter. Inside the capsules is a fine light brown powder that does have a bit of an aftertaste if you do not swallow them correctly. In other words - do not take them with a carbonated beverage - a mistake I only made once, because it did dissolve the shell before I swallowed it (oops).

I have now taken the product daily for three weeks. The first week I took just one a day and then I upped it to 2. I have been taking mine without meals, and other than once, without carbonated beverages. The first week I can\x27t say I noticed any difference. Not that I have much stomach or intestinal discomfort anyway.

Now unfortunately the review will get into the nitty gritty or perhaps TMI for some people - so if such things bother you, fair warning to stop reading. However, with this type of product, nitty gritty is what it\x27s all about. I have always tended toward the constipation end of the spectrum and have issues with gas when I eat the wrong foods and/or eat late at night. product_title: CT Mask for Adult Small/Youth
review_headline: Amazing product.  Keep your toddler safe in freezing temps.
review_body:
This mask works and fits great on our 3 year old son. He has a narrow airway, so colds and runny noses give him a croupy cough. We wanted him to safely get from place to place when the winter days can drop down in the negatives. We also wanted him to be able to go and play in the snow when it was warmer outside, without worrying about getting sick. This mask does the job well for both.

I was really curious if the mask warmed the air as well as it claimed. I took the mask outside in 15F cold and held it against my face for 5 minutes or so (obviously wouldn\x27t fit over my head). I was impressed! My uncovered skin was bitter cold, the skin behind the mask was warm and my breath felt like room temperature. After the first test run with my son, he confirmed every few minutes that his breath was not cold. No runny noses after many successful commutes in the freezing cold and several times out sledding.

I was initially worried it was not going to fit him well since he is only 3 and on the small side, but I was surprised to find it fit him perfectly. It goes on nice and snug and he said it\x27s comfortable. It also slides over his head easily. It has a strap that goes around the back of the head and one that goes over the top, so it keeps the mask securely on his head. Another plus is that it covers his ears and keeps them covered under two layers with a hat.

The material is soft polar fleece but holds its shape with a little stiffness in some sections. It flexes/ folds in all the right places. Overall, I think the design was very well thought out for comfort and function.

When mine arrived, the filter part had been folded and needed to be flattened out before it fit correctly in the pocket that holds it inside the mask. The inside of the filter is copper screening and you can feel that inside the foam covering. I had some brief concerns if this would be a safety issue such as poking or cutting my son\x27s face. I handled the filter for a few minutes, flexing and squeezing and decided that as long as it was flat and inside the pocket, there is nothing at all to worry about. If the foam were to rip, I would replace the filter.

I can only think of a few small negatives, but none of these would prevent me from purchasing again. First, the filter had a strong odor when it arrived that is common to foam and some synthetic materials. I let this air out on the counter for a day, outside of the mask\x27s pocket. By the next day it was noticeably better, and by the 2nd day the smell was gone. Second, the mask does tend to ride up a tiny bit as my son moves and it will start to get in the way of his eyes after some time, so I have to adjust it down every so often. Not so much that it\x27s an annoyance, but if I forget to check, my son gets frustrated, as it\x27s hard for him to adjust with mittens on. I\x27m not sure if anything can be done to prevent this, and I don\x27t see it as a big deal.

The mask does not cover the neck, so you should make sure your child has a scarf or a neck gaiter. It\x27s also tough to hear my son talk with the mask on since it is so well insulated. If I don\x27t hear my son he pulls up on the bottom so he can talk a little.

I think this is an amazing product and I\x27m really happy I gave it a shot. I\x27m thinking of getting a couple in adult sizes for my wife and I. I\x27d recommend this for any kid for outdoors in the winter, and definitely for anyone with breathing or health concerns.

product_title: GermGuardian AC4010, 3-in-1 Table Top Air Cleaning System with HEPA, UV, and Odor Reduction
review_body: Too bad this beautiful design is so badly made (in Asia, you know who).  Right out of the box the thing had a low pitched vibration sound at all speeds, so it is clear that the fan cage is out of balance.  So after 3 nights of use, it also developed a high pitched whine, likely because the motor bearings failed due to the fan being out of balance.  Also, the UV light is intermittent (sometimes takes a while to come on, but then stays on).  Seeing all of the bad reviews, especially about fan problems, then my experience is sadly quite common.  Thought about buying another one, but since several folks have tried this already with the same sad results (sometimes taking a month or two for the fan to fail), I\x27m just returning this for good (bought this from someone else, but reviewing here).    I also tried their newest AC4020 desktop unit in the hope that they have resolved their quality problems by now (the AC4010 has been in production for several years, and evidently they have not made any manufacturing changes for this one over time).  Well, even on low, it has a high pitched whir right out of the box.  There is no way that someone could use this on a bedside table while sleeping.  It didn\x27t seem to be broken, just designed this way.  So returning this as well.    As far as I know, GermGuardian makes the most compact desktop designs on the market that have True HEPA filters (not just the \x5C\x22HEPA-Type\x5C\x22 filters that will not filter much at the sub-micron levels required for allergies), perfect for allergy sufferers that want an unobtrusive bedside or desk unit that gently blows True HEPA filtered air right at us.  So it is sad that they don\x27t spend the effort to make the quality better, since most of us would gladly pay TWICE as much (or even more) to have this.  The cost of the True HEPA replacement filters is what drives the long term use of this unit anyway, not its initial price, so GermGuardian would do itself a big favor if it made this a high quality unit at a higher price.  I\x27m sure its sales are being crushed by the poor build quality, as most folks buying air purifiers will indeed review them before purchase.    Also, I think that for all of their tabletop models, GermGuardian is trying to move too much air through too small of a unit.  This requires then a small fan to be used that runs too fast, making it too loud and resulting in premature failure (unless a lot more effort is put into the fans).     Consider then the Holmes desktop units, though they are somewhat larger than the GermGuardian ones (which may be what is required to produce quiet and reliable units).  Note that they only come with a HEPA-type filter, but Holmes makes an entire line of \x5C\x22AER1\x5C\x22 filters that go in all of their newest desktop units, with two types being True HEPA filters (with or without baking soda added for odor control).  They similarly supply True HEPA filters for their older models as well (some of which are sold here at Amazon).  They have about the same price point as the GermGuardians, but seem to have a better build quality based on the reviews and longer warranty (3 years vs 1).  If what you want is a horizontal outflow to blow right at you, make sure to get one that alternately stands in the vertical position (see the holmesproducts.com website for their full line of latest greatest), as their units ordinarily outflow vertically (in their usual horizontal position).  Unfortunately, only their white colored units will do this.

I finally went to a natural doctor who listened to my giant list of symptoms and said, "You have B12 deficiency." I thought, "It can\x27t be that simple." I began researching it on my own, and discovered that just about every symptom I\x27d been having over the years, from neuropathy to the digestive problems, were symptoms of B12 deficiency. Even lying on my side became problematic. Bizarrely enough, it didn\x27t occur to me that I wasn\x27t taking enough B12, despite my past. Then it finally DID occur to me, and I started taking it faithfully again. Within a few months, my neuropathy was completely gone. It felt like my legs woke up and realized they were alive. No more odd sensations of warm water pouring over my feet when there\x27s no warm water in sight, etc. Every year, I\x27d be miserable when winter came around. I had a very low tolerance to the cold and was prone to depression. I no longer loathe winter, thanks to the B12.

I\x27m never going to stop taking B12, and I so hope this company keeps making this one. It\x27s the ONLY one I could find with just three ingredients, and is a good price.

review_headline: When it arrived I was very happy with it
review_body:
About 6 months ago I purchased this brush. When it arrived I was very happy with it. Such a nice thick full soft brush and the handle was of nice solid weight. It lathered nicely and was wonderful to use. I don\x27t shave every day and the first month or so everything was wonderful. But then things started going badly which is causing me to write one of the very few reviews I have ever written. The bristles started coming out. At first it was maybe three or four every shave. I stuck with it thinking that shedding a few bristles is ok maybe even normal and that it would stop. But it didn\x27t. In fact it is much worse. The past few weeks have seen it lose 10-20 bristles every shave if not more. Pretty soon there is not going to be any brush left! Not only does this take away from the shaving experience but it is causing me to go look for a new better brush.

I am writing this hoping to help others save their money on this brush. Had it held together it would have been easily a five star review given the price. I guess the old adage you get what you pay for is true. I can only guess that the many raving reviews on this brush were written in the days and weeks after receiving it as I would have given a positive review then as well. Buy at your own risk.

I could experience a more complete splendor of the natural environment than I could have otherwise, thanks to these WoodyKnows nasal filters. Suffice it to say that these filters made this past weekend\x27s transcendentalist excursion into the woods a much more pleasant and fulfilling experience ^o^

The filters themselves fit snugly in my nostrils, which correspond to III-S (Medium adult nose, slotted nostril). It felt physically strange at first to breathe in and out through the filters, but I got comfortable with them fast--I barely notice the structure now after just under a week of use.

And, holy cow, WoodyKnows customer support is prompt, polite, and magnanimous. WoodyKnows customer support contacted me a few days after my order for these filters was delivered, inviting any feedback about the product and offering further support as needed to make my experience with their product superb. Major thanks to them for making my shopping experience a pleasant one, and for making such an awesome product. I\x27ve already referred this product to a few friends of mine who also suffer from hay fever, and I couldn\x27t recommend it more--it allows me to breathe comfortably again!

product_title: #EDOAP-3104-10 Panel Instant Dip Drug Testing Kits - Test for 10 different drugs
review_body:
I am sorry to say that a drug problem in my family makes these necessary, but I am very pleased with this product. They test for ten drugs and the cost is very reasonable -- I don\x27t think you could find a better price anywhere. On one or two occasions, out of dozens and dozens of tests, we\x27ve had a possible false positive -- a very faint red line. That\x27s not a huge problem. If you\x27re testing frequently, wait a few hours, or a day, and test again. If in doubt, you can always test your own urine, as a reality check.

Cheap, accurate multi-drug tests like this are a modern miracle. They are very difficult to manufacture. Don\x27t expect perfection. Having tested the same person every day, more than 200 times, I can say with confidence they are accurate 98 or 99% of the time. That\x27s as good as it gets.

My only regrets about drug testing my loved one are that I didn\x27t start sooner, and I didn\x27t test every day, at first. Addicts will lie and manipulate. If you don\x27t test every day, they have more opportunities to like and manipulate.. My story ended well. My loved one entered a methadone program, slowly tapered down to a zero dose. He\x27s been drug free for many months now. When addicted and using, or withdrawing, he was a monster. Now he\x27s a very pleasant and reasonable person. Don\x27t give up on the people you love. Don\x27t be afraid of tough love, either. I made my loved one live in a tent in the back yard for over a month, until he agreed to daily testing, without lies or arguments. We still test every day. Now, he welcomes the tests and reminds me if I forget.

Recently, I had a few questions and problems with this product. Telephone support was excellent. The manufacturer graciously shipped replacement tests, even though that wasn\x27t really necessary.

There are too many shills and fake reviews on Amazon. Not me. I\x27ve reviewed all kinds of things, for a long time. Look me up.

product_title: Air Lite - High Density Urethane Foam Sheet - White
review_headline: This foam is not High Density as the weight is only 1.2 lbs per cubic foot!
review_body:
I measured a piece of this foam and weighed it. A cubic foot of this foam only weighs 1.2 lbs! For an education, go to foambymail and look at their foam under foam mattresses, and the data sheets for each kind under the resources tab. You will see that they sell 1.3 lb foam under the name Poly Foam, and the description has \x5C\x22Poly foam is a fair-quality foam with a medium feel\x5C\x22. This is one of the lowest quality foams they sell and has an ILD (Indentation Load Deflection) of 36 lbs. This foam won\x27t last very long if used for cushions, but might be OK for light duty applications.

I was lucky to get the 2\x27 x 10\x27 x 3\x5C\x22 thick piece for only $28.17 and free shipping from Amazon as a Prime customer, so I am not complaining. Amazon does have some incredible deals at times!

I bought a Full Mattress from foambymail which is 4\x5C\x22 thick and made of LUX-HQ foam for $109.99 with free shipping, and it is very good high density foam which weighs 2.8 lbs per cubic feet, has an ILD of 50 lbs, and is rated to last from 12 to 18 years. It is much better than this foam. I wish sellers of foam on Amazon would list the Density and ILD rating so buyers would know what they are getting, as the words High Density don\x27t really mean anything.

product_title: Singer Studio Machines
review_headline: Great For Even A Beginner Like Me
review_body:
I\x27ll start off by saying that I\x27m pretty much a sewing novice. I\x27ve had sewing machines over the years but I have only used it on occasion. The Singer S10 Studio Embroidery Machine was easy enough to use even for someone like me.

Setting up the machine was fairly quick, it took me about a 1/2 hour to set up and run through the quick-start guide to get it ready to start. The instructions on the other hand was a bit more in depth so reading up on how to use the machine took some time, it took about an hour for me to feel comfortable enough to give it a go. I started with a simple, single color monogram on a handkerchief and the Singer S10 went through the stitching without a hitch. The small 2"x2" monogram using my initials took just a few minutes to complete and looked great. I did a few more practice projects on a couple of pillow cases which also turned out great. My next project will be a set of bath towels as a gift so hopefully those will turn out just as good. I should add that I used a water soluble fabric stabilizer and embroidery thread when doing these projects.

Some of the features I like about the Singer S10:
The machine "looks" like a sewing machine so it mentally made my introduction to embroidery less intrusive.
Numerous built-in set and editable designs that are included in the machines memory.
USB port so you can import your own fonts or designs.
Large, easy to read touch screen display.
Solid build quality.
2 different hoop sizes for larger or smaller designs.
Nice dust cover.

With the few projects I\x27ve done so far, the Singer S10 was very user friendly and had fantastic results, and was also loads of fun to use. I\x27ll be creating many more projects during the year to give away as gifts. 5 stars.

product_title: OK to Wake! Alarm Clock & Night-Light
review_headline: Awesome product, but wish it had an AC adapter instead of just batteries
review_body:
I love this item, can\x27t say enough great things about it. Only really have two minor annoyances / complaints about it.

I initially bought this for my 4 year old daughter who kept waking up at 4 o\x27clock in the morning asking if it was morning yet and if she could get up. We tried putting a clock in her room and telling her she couldn\x27t get up until 6am, but that was confusing for her. She\x27d come in if ANY of the numbers on the clock were a 6. A family member suggested this clock to me and said it worked great for her daughter so I thought I\x27d try it out. After buying it for my 4 year old my 2 year old insisted on getting one of her own also. Both LOVE it!

It is really easy to set the "OK to wake" time and choose if it should use light only, alarm only or both. The nap mode is brilliant. You set how long the nap should be, then when it\x27s time for nap you just hit the nap button (on the back behind the panel) and it does a count down on the front instead of showing the current time. Nap mode also allows you to choose light only, alarm only or both for "OK to wake" time. When it is "OK to wake", it plays a cute little animation and you can choose to snooze by hitting one of the toe buttons, or turn it off by hitting the other toe button. You can choose how long the clock stays green past the end of nap or OK to wake. The first few times I used it my kids napped longer than I expected and slept through the Green OK to wake light, so when they woke up they didn\x27t know if they could get up or not. I changed it to stay on for 2 hours past the end of nap and that worked great. There is a night light also that is independent of the "OK to wake" functions. The clock glows yellow for the night light and glows green for OK to wake.

PROS: Works great! Love the nap setting. Easy enough for my two year old to use.

CONS: Battery operated only, I would love for this to have an AC adapter so we wouldn\x27t haveto go through so many batteries (we\x27ve started using rechargeable ones to cut down on cost). Keep the instructions handy. It was easy enough to set up with the instructions, but when the batteries run out after only two months of use it\x27s somewhat confusing getting it all set back up if you don\x27t have the instructions. They are now just taped to the bottom for future use.

All in all, this does everything that it claims to do and even though it is expensive for a kids clock it has been worth every dime for us.

Since there is no fan, the heat just rises, also it doesn\x27t really combat the cold room temperature because it doesn\x27t put out the heat fast enough.

review_body:
The first day I owned this: broken. I had to call customer service and order a new piece. But I was committed to loving this vacuum. One of my admitted faults is sometimes valuing form over function.
After receiving the replacement part, which you replace yourself (no problem), I have spent the past 5 years making excuses for it, like a beautiful but continually drunken boyfriend at family holidays. Small pieces(pebbles, crumbs, petrified tears, etc) are ignored and I have to say it\x27s the noisiest vacuum I\x27ve ever met. At this point, the warranty has run out. The function of switching from upright to attachment mode is now impaired. It now requires me to pull on the hose and manually push the flap near the base all of the way shut.
On the bright side, it\x27s light, easy to maneuver and very handsome. It also does an adequate job cleaning the rugs and sucking up pet hair tumbleweeds.
The point: if I hadn\x27t spent $430 to marry that drunken boyfriend I would have broken up with him already and moved on to a more satisfying relationship by now.

review_headline: Break the code, win the war...
review_body: \x5C\x22Imitation Game\x5C\x22 is a dramatization of the vital British code-breaking operation at Bletchley Park during the Second World War, built around the life of Alan Turing, the genius who built a pioneering computer (in the 1940\x27s!) to aid in the code-breaking. This poster shows Benedict Cumberbatch (BBC\x27s Sherlock Holmes) who provides a heartbreaking performance as the well-meaning but literal and almost unlikeable Turing, a world-class mathematician upon whose shoulder some terrible moral decisions will be placed. Keira Knightley co-stars as Joan Clarke, the rare female mathematician who is Turing\x27s co-worker. The supporting cast is excellent, especially Mark Strong as Sir Stewart Menzies, the ruthless head of MI6, who sponsors Turing. Rory Kinnear is surprising sympathetic as the policemen who investigates Turing after the war. Turing\x27s co-workers at Bletchley Park manage to be individuals in spite of their smaller roles. An \x5C\x22Aha\x5C\x22 moment late in the movie is especially priceless, as a seemingly casual remark in a bar has the crew running back to their place of work. \x5C\x22Imitation Game\x5C\x22 the movie and the poster are highly recommended.

[[VIDEOID:7de42114693fc0068958966e0a7bc788]] Included with the 20 feet set of multicolor lights are the instructions, the solar panel with off/on switch, mounting hardware, plastic mounting ground stake, plastic wall mount, and approximately 10 feet of wiring from the solar panel connecting to the 20 feet of lighting.

Brightech sent me several different sets as samples for review (each I will review separately). This multi-color set is approximately 20 feet in length with small LED lights spaced about 2 inches apart approximately. This set of lights has a large solar panel approximately 6 inches by 5 inches which contains a replaceable rechargeable battery. The lights are surprisingly bright but are meant to be decorative and not an illuminating type of lighting but they look very colorful and nice. The wire is bendable and pretty durable for a thin wire. Like all solar lights, the length of time they will stay on is dependent on the amount of sun the panel gets during the day and the rechargeable battery life. These lights come with a 3 year warranty. I will update my review over time if I have any issues with long term durability.

Overall these are nice looking decorator lights at a reasonable price that have the flexibility of being mounted practically anywhere with the two different mounts and long cabling.

product_title: Hidden Valance Clips - 6 Pack, 10 Pack, and 20 Pack!
review_headline: Valance clips -- what can you say?
review_body:
Let me begin by saying that I have replaced the valance clips on my horizontal blind valances at least 5 times. The blinds are Levalor, so they hold up like nobody\x27s business. The valance clips ---- not so much.

Now: These clips are just as good as any others that I have purchased. I bought the package of 20, and I\x27m quite pleased with my purchase. They were easy to install, and they clipped onto the carriage of the blinds with absolutely no problem.

Anyone that purchases ANY brand of these clips and expects them to last more than a few years is in for a major disappointment - especially if you live in a hot and humid climate.

My only recommendation is that if you need valance clips, make sure they match the ones you are replacing. If you only have access to one that is broken, glue that puppy back together to get accurate measurements.

product_title: Queen Boyd Specialty Sleep 920 Natural Flex Natural Latex Mattress
review_headline: Awesome bed! Wish we had bought it sooner!
review_body:
My husband and I first tried this bed in a local store about a year and a half ago and we loved it in the store. But I was bothered by the fact that it wasn\x27t natural latex. I wanted a natural latex bed. So, I held off in hopes of saving up enough to get an all natural latex bed. I was eyeing the ones on Habitat Furnishing\x27s website. This last couple of years, my old bed was starting to really cause me a lot of pain and I think I started spending more time on the couch than the bed, because my pressure points flared up so bad on my old bed. So, I went back online to the HF store in hopes they had a sale, and well, to my surprise they did! Only it wasn\x27t for an all natural latex. It was for a new line, a latex hybrid. I realized that with the level of pain I was experiencing from my old bed, it was time to compromise. I rationalized that it was almost the same thing, because the side you lay on is all natural, real latex, so we bought one of the hybrid beds, but it wasn\x27t right for us, so we got a refund. I posted a review on that bed as well if you are interested in looking it up. My husband and I then visited the store where we first tried the Boyd 920 to give it another look. Now that I had gotten to try a natural latex (hybrid), I wanted to give the Boyd another chance, since I was now willing to compromise on natural vs. synthetic. It was just as comfortable as we remembered it to be so we bought one. We almost bought one from an online store to save some money, but the local store was willing to price match. In the end, we did pay more because of sales tax, but it turned out to be worth that, because the first one was defective and had to be exchanged. Since it was a local purchase, exchange was simple. Had we bought it online, we would have had to pay for return shipping, shipped it back and waited for the new one. But through the store, we were able to keep the defective one and use it while we waited for the new one to come in.

Now for the actualreview of the Boyd Specialty Sleep 920 Natural Flex. It comes in a box, rolled up in plastic. You simply, carefully, remove the plastic and gently unroll the foam on your foundation. We bought a sprung slat foundation from Amazon.com, http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B002KQ5KQG/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o07_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 . It takes a few hours for this particular mattress to rise, and could take up to 2-3 days to reach it\x27s full size. The reason we had to exchange ours was that the first one didn\x27t ever reach it\x27s full size and it\x27s thickness was inconsistent throughout. The one we kept reached it\x27s full size within 36 hours. The weather has been cold and we were told that some foam beds take longer when it is cold. This one is consistent throughout. And it is so comfortable!

My husband likes fluffy soft beds, and I don\x27t mind that, but I want to at least be able to feel supported under that fluff. Well, this bed is not fluffy, but it is a perfect combination of firm enough to feel the support, and soft. And when you add a topper like this one, http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00FX0QYNY/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o06_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 , you can have that cloud on top and still feel the support. At first, I didn\x27t personally like the extra fluffy, but I got used to it, and now it\x27s very comfortable, and my husband is in love with our new bed. The nice thing is that we can compromise and sometimes I can take the topper off if I want the firmer feel, and he is okay with that because the bed is so comfortable even without it, even for someone who prefers the feel of a fluffy topper. Without the topper, it has a buoyancy similar to real natural latex. This is engineered latex, designed to feel and act like real latex. With a topper like ours, you can still feel some of that buoyancy, but depending on your topper, it may not feel the same, because you are likely to sink into your topper, unless you have a latex topper.

This mattress was designed with stay cool chambers in the foam, and they really work! Sheets and toppers can make a difference in the temperature too, so if you try a bed that seems too hot or too cool, try changing those things first. We do have one sheet set that does tend to trap the heat, so my husband doesn\x27t like me to use them unless it\x27s below zero outside. But otherwise, we have been quite comfy as far as the temperature of the bed goes, thanks to it\x27s design.

I think that the price for this bed ... for the level of comfort and support that this bed provides, you can\x27t beat this model! I will never go back to spring beds again. If I never save enough to buy a real all natural latex bed, and if I ever need to replace this one, I would definitely buy another if they are still making these at that time. It doesn\x27t bother me at all now that this is not an all natural latex. I think the reason I was so worried about buying a new bed was that I was afraid of chemicals. I don\x27t do well with chemicals and odors. There was a slight odor at first, but I just opened my bedroom windows during the day the first two days, and the odor was gone after that. I did sleep on it the first night, and I could smell it if I was on my side, but it wasn\x27t overpowering and I didn\x27t experience any allergic symptoms. By the third night, all I could smell was the smell of my laundry detergent on my sheets. Definitely not worth all the worrying and pain I put myself through while trying to decide what to do while suffering on my old mattress. Seriously, we put off buying a new bed for several years, because I was more afraid of the toxicity of new bed materials, than I was concerned about the physical pain I was already enduring on our old worn out spring mattress that was causing me trigger point pain. If you are suffering with an old bed causing you pain because you are worried about the toxicity of a new bed, don\x27t do like I did. Don\x27t let other people\x27s stories of how a toxic bed made them sick, scare youfrom trying a new bed. It\x27s not worth it! Keep your old bed until you try the new one just in case it does bother you and you can\x27t keep it, but at least try a new one. You may be pleasantly surprised like I was! I totally recommend this bed to anyone who wants the feel of a latex but can\x27t afford one. We LOVE this bed!

product_title: file holder
review_headline: hung it on some command hooks, the compartments could use more space between the two, nice look
review_body:
I bought this specifically for some paperwork I like to keep close at hand, but off the counter it always ends up on. Here is how it worked out:

1. The paperwork will fit in both slots, but it does not come out, or go in, the bottom compartment easily. So it just isn\x27t practical for the purpose I had in mind. That said, I decided to file all of the paperwork on the top slot and use the bottom for mail, as it is smaller.

2. Hanging it up was fairly easy. There are 2 spots (in in each top corner) to screw it into the wall. I opted to hang it on a pair of command hooks. I hate putting holes in the wall when I don\x27t have to. This file holder slid onto them easily. And the product isn\x27t heavy, so I am not worried about it pulling the hook off. So far it has held for 2 days no problem.

3. There are slots on each compartment to put a label or tag. Had I used it as originally intended I definitely would have utilized them. Since the way it used now is pretty self-explanatory I have no need for them.

Overall I like the way it looks and how easy it was to put up and use. I am disappointed with the space between compartments. It made it impractical to use the bottom one with letter size (8.5x11) or larger. I felt like it is a bit over-priced as well.

review_headline: Better than alarm clock but still wakes us up sometimes
review_body:
We have young children who through some magic or skill usually end up sneaking into bed with us. Husband goes to work very early and the alarm he needed to wake up was waking us all at 5 am, and once kids are up, they\x27re up.

This vibrates much like a cell phone. My husband had no issue setting up, the other reviews are pretty helpful in pointing out problems to avoid. He usually keeps it under the pillow as he says it is not comfortable to wear. The first few times it woke me up but not the kids. After awhile though, I got used to it too. Now, it will wake me up if he leaves it on a hard surface. Even in another room, if this vibrates against a hard surface, it is loud enough to hear while asleep.

Otherwise I would recommend this. But definitely read the other reviews if you have set up problems before trying to return.

product_title: Premium PEVA Shower Curtain Liner Non Toxic Environmentally Friendly, White, Mildew Resistant, Heavy Duty, Magnetic Weights
review_headline: No More Throwing Away My Shower Curtain Liners! This Is A Keeper!
review_body:
I have thrown away so many shower curtain liners, and have spent so much money on buying them constantly. Why? Because they constantly harbor mold, odor, stains and rust on the metal parts that hold the liner. Some other liners that I have tried harbor less
mold and mildew than others. But mold and mildew are disgusting, and they should not belong in the shower!

I have been using the PEVA Shower Curtain liner for about 4 weeks now, and I am so impressed with the quality of this liner! Not only is it sturdy and strong, but I have not seen any mold spots on it at all so far. This is quite impressive because if I had used my other shower curtain liners that I have thrown away, by now there would already be few spots of mold. But the PEVA Shower Curtain Liner has surpassed my expectations!

I also love that the metal grommets are rust free. The PEVA Shower Curtain Liner contains a weighted magnetic hem that allows the bottom to stick magnetically to the tub without the shower curtain sliding off. It is made from Eco-friendly materials and is certified PVC free.

The only thing that I wish the PEVA Shower Curtain Liner had was to be able to stick it straight into the washing machine to simplify the cleaning process. I know how easy it is to wipe down and clean, but it would eliminate the need for me to wipe the entire shower curtain, and just be able to throw it and let the washing machine do the rest of the work for me.

I am so impressed with the quality of the PEVA Shower Curtain Liner, and I definitely recommend it to anyone who is sick of mold and mildew in their shower, and wants a nice Eco-Friendly shower curtain liner that is of great quality!

product_title: Wesco Star Wars R2D2 Projection Alarm Clock
review_headline: My son says it\x27s the coolest alarm clock ever
review_body: My 8 year old son is MAD about Star Wars.  This gift has him excited.  When visitors come, I ask myself why he has taken them into our kitchen walk-in pantry.  Turns out it is a window-less room and perfect to demonstrate the light-up time on the wall or ceiling.    The noises are cool.  There is a button to press to hear the noises on demand.  R2 has a little repertoire that we all enjoy.  He beeps once softly on the hour, every hour, he tries to wake you at the alarm-set time.  There is an option to have the alarm off.  He looks great on a bed-side table.  Or anywhere.  Good for collectors, too.    So he is a clock, and not much use except for telling the time and waking you. And looking good.  It\x27s not a toy, and having accepted this, my son loves it.  R2 is a great novelty for my son and he compares the digital time on R2 to an analogue clock also in his room.  The screen for reading the time is small, so you won\x27t be checking out the time from across the room.  But on the bedside table, my son finds the numeral sizes are not an issue for him when he is in bed.    He\x27s had it since early December 2014 and I\x27m waiting for the novelty to run out.  Hasn\x27t happened yet.

product_title: Adjustable King Pillow - SmartSOFT Memory Foam - Original Bamboo Pillowcase - Hypoallergenic - Supports Neck Back & Head - Shredded Design
review_headline: keeping my head elevated in relation to my chest is pretty darn important
review_body:
First, I am a side sleeper with Acid Reflux. So, keeping my head elevated in relation to my chest is pretty darn important. That said, I\xE2\x80\x99ve tried at least a dozen various \xE2\x80\x9Cextra firm / side sleeper\xE2\x80\x9D pillows in the past with disappointing results. Basically, all of them started out pretty good, but then \xE2\x80\x93 at varying speeds \xE2\x80\x93 lost their stiffness / firmness or whatever you want to call it and I started having problems again. The Bamboo pillow sounded pretty interesting and had good reviews. Besides, it was competitively prices, so I gave it a whirl.

You will notice a few things when it arrives. First, it\xE2\x80\x99s quite heavy compared to any other pillow. Second, it\xE2\x80\x99s packed tightly into a special shipping tube to save space. Third, when you pull it out, it doesn\xE2\x80\x99t look all that impressive \xE2\x80\x93 pretty flat in fact. But, if you let it sit for about 24 hours without slipping it into a pillow case, you\xE2\x80\x99ll be amazed at how much it grows. And it will feel impressively firm too. Yes, this might finally be the pillow I\xE2\x80\x99d needed.

Well, it\xE2\x80\x99s been about two months. How do I feel now? First, it\xE2\x80\x99s still the heaviest pillow I\xE2\x80\x99ve ever used. (That did not change.) Second, it\xE2\x80\x99s still reasonably firm, but nowhere near as firm as when it was first delivered. Third, it\xE2\x80\x99s flattened out considerably compared to when it first arrived. Is it flatter than the other pillows I\xE2\x80\x99ve tried? No, not quite.

Chalk could also be used, but you would probably want to use a sealant to keep the chalk from migrating off of the card surface.
