product_title: MASTER 1/6 hp Airbrush Tank Compressor with Air Hose & Training Book to Get You Started, Published Exclusively by TCP Global
review_headline: Very good, could\x27ve been the best, but...
review_body:
I bought this for my wife for Christmas as she just started to pick up the hobby of building model cars and wanted an airbrush.

The pros:
Quiet doesn\x27t even begin to describe it! I\x27d say it\x27s about as loud as a pot of boiling water, if that. You can hear a conversation, you don\x27t have to try to talk over it, it\x27s wonderful. And that\x27s with it sitting on the table!
It never seems to run low on pressure for airbrush use, even when it has to turn on again, so you always have enough air.
The tank ensures no pulsing of air, so it\x27s a steady flow of air, so a steady flow of paint.

The cons:
As has been mentioned probably hundreds of times, the moisture trap doesn\x27t sit vertical. You have to either wrap the threads with many layers of teflon tape (it took me about 12-15 wraps), or shim it with thin washers. Either way, not the best design.
The auto shut-off pressure seems to be very low, because you can\x27t spray for more than about 45 seconds before it turns on again, then it only runs for a minute or two then shuts back off. I\x27m spraying at about 20-25psi.

Overall, a very good piece. I\x27d give it 5 stars if they upped the turnoff and fixed the threading so the moisture trap would align without a pile of tape.

[[VIDEOID:21e73159717fa23f84f481fff6fdc93a]] Oh where were you Shefko fire starters when I had a fireplace in our house? These would have made the job of starting a fire so easy and painless. Instead I had to deal with fatwood (black sooty smoke) or those Duraflame slabs that never lit right. Oh I love these fire starters.

This is a brilliant product. They used some kind of scrap sawdust. Then blended that with some kind of wax that doesn\x27t burn black or sooty. Then they made a hockey puck with a cross hatch on the puck. That cross hatch is to make it easy to split these up into smaller pieces for smaller or easier to start fires.

Seriously, this stuff doesn\x27t stink when it burns. It doesn\x27t give off a lot of black smoke. And it lights in a heartbeat. I love these.

I even managed to start a fire with totally soaking wet ancient firewood, on a blustery cold Chicago winter afternoon. That\x27s how good these starters are.

I was provided a review sample.

review_headline: Beautiful, bright, Easy to Hang, Solar Lights
review_body:
Bright lights work great! In the box is the string of lights on copper wire, 6 feet of cord, and solar panel (with battery) and steak to secure into ground. Upon opening, I unwrapped the lights carefully as they feel delicate, but had no issues with breakage or twisting. I could not remove the film over solar panel (and still have not removed it). I turned the solar panel switch to ON as instructed (you can not charge it without it being turned to on). Once outside, I chose my balcony for these colorful lights - wrapping the strand around the wood beams easily. The strand stays in place and I did not need any additional tools. I placed the end, the solar panel, against a wood beam where I knew it would get the most sunlight throughout the afternoon. We live in So Cal and have solar panels on our roof, so I\x27m familiar with the best areas. The lights worked right out of the box and stayed lit through the night.

The small, pretty lights are bright. They are green, red, blue and purple. Not pastels, these are more like primary colors. Distinct.

I have monitored these lights for review for a month. In that time, they come on by themselves when it gets dark and stay on all night. I\x27ve had to turn them off a few times around 3am because it was too bright for me to sleep (my balcony is outside my bedroom). They have withstood wind, cold temperatures around 40 degrees (doesn\x27t snow here), and very, very light rain for a brief afternoon.

I\x27m impressed with these lights and am glad I had the chance to review from Brightech. I will update with any concerns over time.

review_body:
Despite much talk and disagreement as to who contributed what to it, REBECCA is definitely an Alfred Hitchcock film. Producer David O. Selznick hands-on approach to producing definitely is evident, yet the film does not look entirely like your typical Selznick movie for that period. I would think this is director Alfred Hitchcock\x27s doing. Yet again, it does not resemble the style that Hitchcock employed in his first American film, FOREIGN CORESPONDENT.

I think a lot of the success of this film should be given to the performances of Joan Fontaine as the young woman who becomes the second wife of Laurence Olivier as the brooding aristocratic widower Maxim de Winter. Laurence Olivier performnce and screen presence as is Maxim de Winter is one of a dashing figure, yet aloof and seemingly enigmatic. Judith Anderson as the stern housekeeper, Mrs. Danvers is the real protagonist of the film and her unsettling performance opposite Joan Fontaine is mesmerizing.

review_headline: I thought I\x27d take a chance and put it in water that was hotter than recommended on the container
review_body:
I got this item, under the impression that when placed in hot water (around 140 degrees, per instructions on container) that it would actually melt after a few minutes. This was not the case for me - always staying in its "white pellet" form. The instructions also say to never put in water with temps above 150 degrees due to possible burns.

Due to my growing aggravation with these non-melting pellets, I thought I\x27d take a chance and put it in water that was hotter than recommended on the container: each "trial" consisting of an increase of 5 degrees, and waiting for the InstaMorph to change. It did not begin to change and take on that "clear" color until about 160 degrees - quickly cooling and hardening within SECONDS of kneading.

After what equated to hours of my time wasted, going back and forth from the hot water, to molding, to reheating the water to soaking and remolding... I was actually angry, realizing too late, that I would never be able to make anything out of this stuff. I realize that ambient temperature is a factor - but I live in Florida, and it was warm.

I\x27m going to send this crap back, and find something else that hopefully works and melts as stated in the instructions. As far as I\x27m concerned - this crap is defective and doesn\x27t work as promised.

product_title: Laser Disc, Laserdisc of Alfred Hitchcock\x27s Notorious With Cary Grant And Ingrid Bergman and Claude Rains.
review_body:
NOTORIOUS is Alfred Hitchcock\x27s wartime romantic thriller. Ingrid Bergman as the daughter of a Nazi spy living in the United States. Her father has been convicted of treason as we see from open doors outside the courtroom. Bergman an amorous and promiscuous playgirl who is reluctantly conscripted by an enigmatic American espionage agent Cary Grant, finds herself in more peril than she bargained for on her assignment in Brazil. This has always been considered one of Hitchcock\x27s better thrillers. NOTORIOUS is absolutely intriguing and deliberately paced. As an Alfred Hitchcock enthusiast it took me some time to realize the power of this film. I even watched this film again before I wrote this review. For me it no longer seems out of step from his other films. In a strange way it jumps ahead to a style Hitchcock employed in 1969\x27s TOPAZ. For me the romanticism combined with Cary Grant introspective performance rank this among Hitchcock\x27s best.
Despite much talk and disagreement as to who contributed what to it, REBECCA is definitely an Alfred Hitchcock film. Producer David O. Selznick hands-on approach to producing definitely is evident, yet the film does not look entirely like your typical Selznick movie for that period. I would think this is director Alfred Hitchcock\x27s doing.

product_title: 28oz Circle E Candles Birds of Paradise, Our Most Popular of All Candles! This Sweet Intoxicating Smell Will Make You Get a Sweet Tooth If You Don\x27t Have One Already!
review_body:
I purchased a large number of candles from Circle E before the Christmas holidays and planned to give some as gifts and keep some for myself. I didn\x27t purchase through Amazon, but from the company itself, however I am compelled to tell as many as I can about my experience with the candles and customer service.
One night while my husband and I were watching TV, one of the candles we were burning made a loud pop. We looked closer and saw that the side of the glass jar had broken, and a piece of glass had popped out across the table. Upon inspection, the wick appeared to have burned over to the side of the jar causing this dangerous situation. Although this caused us concern, we chalked it up to a fluke in that one candle. The next one we burned resulted in a similar situation although we caught this one before it broke the glass, but not before it melted the plastic around the top of the jar.
I contacted customer service 2 or 3 times by email with no response. I then called and was told they were behind on emails due to the holidays. The young lady I spoke to listened to me and then began asking if I trimmed the wick properly. Yes, I had. She did not admit that it could be a faulty candle, that it was more likely user error. She then told me that customer service would be in touch. I experienced much the same with this lady. She asked for pictures, front, back, and side views. I sent them, showing the off centered wick and blackened glass, as well as the melted plastic. Her response was that it did not appear to be a faulty candle and that there were things I should have done. Her instructions were so ridiculous. I am 56 years old and never had a problem with any other brand of candle. I didn\x27t find anything special about these candles anyway, and I really wasn\x27t interested in getting replacements, but I did feel like I should be compensated due to their cost, and I knew it was very unlikely that I would get a refund. I was all but told I would not get replacements. Then I got two in the mail, so I am satisfied with that, but I still want to tell others to be cautious and watch these candles closely. I am betting these candles I ordered were stored in a warehouse laying on their side and got warm enough that the wick shifted. That said, customer service was unbelievably bad. I will never purchase Circle E candles again.

Our neighbor has the Bissell Little Green Cleaner and it did a great job on the stains we had from puppy stains and other stains mainly from our messy 5 yr old. This machine had much less suction power and some other faults that I will explain. The holding tank was insufficient; on one small stain it  took three times to empty the dirty water to complete the task...but since the suction was not that good, we had to use a towel to get the carpet sufficiently dry. Another issue was the spray pattern of the nozzles. They say to keep the attachment in contact with the carpet at all times; the reason is that the nozzles spray in all directions. I see the logic here, but it prevents you from pre-spraying the area to be cleaned without spraying everything else in the area you are spraying. I am only giving 2 Stars because the people at Amazon are so good about returns of bad products; the machine only gets 1 Star. We will likely order the Little Green Machine by Bissell instead.

But it\x27s exactly what was advertised and was hand-painted, as I can tell, and even the frame was made at home - not well, but sturdy enough to hang on a wall for years. It\x27s light and easy to hang.
It came wrapped in plastic, protected at the edges in cardboard, put in a box, protected with tons of wrapping paper, and then put in another box. Arrived safely.

It\x27s nice! Everyone\x27s freaking out because they expected crazy perfect art. It was 30 bucks when I bought it. That\x27s what 30 bucks gets you.

product_title: Frigidaire Aroma Fresh-50, 3-Stage Anti-Allergen Desktop Air Cleaner / Air Purifier FRAP05A6OB
review_headline: Good product, but not the best value
review_body:
I like Frigidaire products in general and have been buying them for years. I was not that impressed with this Frigidaire Aroma Fresh-50, 3-Stage Anti-Allergen Desktop Air Cleaner / Air Purifier however and was intending to give it 3 stars. I have raised the stars to 4 only because the price has been lowered to $28 (current listing as of this review date).

As a preliminary matter the first thing you will need to do when you get this product is pop off the bottom, where the filters are located, and remove any shrink plastic wrap from the main filter. If you fail to do this the unit simply is not going to work as air will not be able to get through the filter.

I like the following. The unit is well designed and nice looking. It sucks dirty air in through the bottom and expels clean air out of a hole in the back (not visible in the only product photo currently listed). The unit is very quiet and has 2 fan speeds. It appears to have a CADR (Clean Air Delivery Rate) of 50. This is important as the only way to clean or purify air is to get it to move through the filter. The higher the CADR the more air being moved. According to the user manual it has an air flow rate of 14 cubic feet per minute. This unit is 12 volt DC and an adapter is included with the unit. This unit should not require much electricity to run. The outer case is plastic and easy to clean. There is a lighted circle around the on/off speed dial but all it appears to do is tell you whether this unit is on or off. The unit comes with no included scents or fragrances. You instead add your own using a small fabric like strip that pops out the back. You can run this unit with or without any scents or fragrances as they are optional. The pre-filter is washable. The main filter cannot be washed but can be cleaned and re-used using a vacuum cleaner to pull out dirt and dust. The manufacturer recommends cleaning both filters once every 3 months and replacing them once per year.

One thing that should be emphasized with this unit is that it is for very small rooms, like small offices or bathrooms. I put this unit in one of our bathrooms (my office at 2,000 square feet is way too big for this unit) and it works great. But we have to keep the door shut as otherwise there is too much unfiltered air coming in for this unit to be effective.

So why was I considering 3 stars and end up with 4? First, I found nothing in the product description or user manual that says this unit provides HEPA filtration. I prefer HEPA filtration to get the smallest particles of dust or whatever out of the air. Second, the unit has no ionizer. Third, I find the Holmes HEPA Type Desktop Air Purifier, HAP242-UC also available on Amazon to be a better value. Currently listed at $34, it has a 3 speed instead of 2 speed fan, HEPA filtration, a CADR of 70 (instead of 50), an ionizer, is suited for up to a 10 x 11 foot room, and is currently the #1 best seller on Amazon in Electrostatic Air Purifiers. Products rarely get to be #1 best sellers on Amazon by accident. They get to be #1 best sellers usually because people buy them, write great reviews on them and recommend them to others. The Holmes unit however may not be as effective with scents or odors. So I was thinking 3 stars. Then however there was a price cut on the Frigidaire unit that made it less expensive instead of more expensive than the Holmes unit. That takes me to 4 stars. product_title: We R Memory Keepers Evolution Advance Die Cutting/Embossing Machine
review_body: This machine is a big piece of junk!  It sounded like a good idea: rather than switching around between different plates and making different sandwiches, this machine has a dial on the side that adjusts the space between the rollers, with different settings for diecutting, embossing, and letterpressing.  So, in theory, you would always use the same plates and just adjust the dial according to what you\x27re doing.  Sounds quick and easy, right?  Not!  The reality is that this machine isn\x27t at all as good as it sounds.  The dial settings that they suggest don\x27t really work.  For instance, the embossing settings that they suggest do not emboss very deeply.  And fiddling around with the different dial settings, trying to find the right one, is annoying and is a waste of my time and my paper!  Maybe mine is defective, because it doesn\x27t diecut properly no matter what setting I try; it only diecuts half the image, so then I have to flip the sandwich around and run it through again for it to cut the other half of the image.  And it does the same thing with the embossing; the embossing is deeper on one half than on the other.  The rollers do not seem to be putting even pressure across the whole die/embossing folder.  Plus the handle keeps falling off.  (Gee, maybe that is defective too.)  There is a little button that you slide to lock the handle in place, but the button somehow keeps sliding back to the unlock position and then the handle flies off while I\x27m using it.  I thought this would be a good replacement for my Cuttlebug, but I was sorely mistaken.  Good thing I didn\x27t get rid of it because it looks like I\x27ll be sticking with my Cuttlebug!  That I have NEVER had a problem with!

review_headline: Well made, but chemical smell never went away, and finally too thick for me
review_body:
It was time to get new pillows after using the same thin miserable ones for years and years. After several hours of pursuing reviews as you may be right now, I decided on this pillow, for a combination of price, reviews, and material.

Let me say that this is a very comfortable pillow, and I\x27m sure this would be great for certain people. Not for me, however.

I had no problem with the material\xE2\x80\x94it is breathable, incredibly soft while remaining supportive, the cover it comes with is probably the softest thing I\x27ve ver touched, etc. etc. Needless to say, when I first took it out of the packaging, I was delighted!

The first night it was hard to get used to. It was incredibly thick feeling and even on my side, my heart felt like it was tilted up, putting pressure on my neck. I assumed this was just transitioning from a thing junky pillow to a thicker, more serious memory foam. Also, as every other review states, there was a chemical smell. But I assumed that I would get used to the pillow thickness and that smell would go away. After 3 weeks, neither of these are the case. Finally, after trying really really hard to love the pillow, I\x27m back to sleeping with my ancient, super thin, "junky" pillow. I tried endless different positions with my head and left it out of the pillowcase every day to try to relive the smell. Still, 3 weeks later it stinks (it is quite unpleasant!) and my neck hurts every morning that I used it.
I\x27m sad to say, this didn\x27t work for me.

Its quite possible that the smell would disappear after more time (so many other reviews seemed to say so) and perhaps my discomfort was just a matter of taste (again, there are so so many positive reviews in this regard! not to be ignored).

Still, if you are looking for the perfect pillow, it may be smarter to go to a store and test them out. Or purchase a few from amazon and return the ones you dislike (they do have an excellent return policy!). No matter how many good reviews there are, I am here to tell you, that it might not be comfortable for you!!No matter how many good reviews there are, I am here to tell you, that it might not be comfortable for you!!

review_headline: Be aware of warranty pit falls with Brother sewing machines!
review_body: I purchased the machine in April 2014 and it has seized up.  The first time it did this I took apart the bottom plate to clean the well.  After that we blew it out with an air compressor.  The second time it happened we could see dust in the top part so we removed the front top panel to blow it out again.  It worked for another day and seized up again.  The sewing wheel will not turn.  You can tell it seems to be catching on something.  I called the Brother service center and was told my warranty is void because I opened the top front panel.  It seems to me if you don\x27t want something removed you would put a hex screw in it not a Philips head screw.  I am going to order again because the price to fix it will end up being around 60 - 80 dollars and that\x27s if they don\x27t have replace anything.  I asked if they could look at it just to assess it and they said yes for 32 dollars. product_title: OSKAR Humidifier - White
review_headline: Quiet, classy, and most importantly, humidifies really well!
review_body:
Creating my first Amazon review (after YEARS) because I\x27m so happy about this humidifier!

I\x27ve had lots of humidifiers over the years, from cheap (Vicks) to expensive (Air-O-Swiss). Why this one makes me so happy:
- Looks classy and modern (swiss design)
- Can be refilled with a jug of water ie NO LUGGING THIS TO THE BATHTUB TO REFILL. Yay! (I use distilled water with this, I don\x27t know if you have to but I\x27ve heard it\x27s healthier in general with a humidifier). You just pour the water in a little side spout. Note to the people that are saying it\x27s hard to see the fill line: that\x27s true if the power is off. You can refill it with the power on which illuminates the fill line. Problem solved.
- Very quiet operation - no glugging sound
- Operational lights can be dimmed or turned off, perfect for people like me who don\x27t want a glowing light in their room at night
- Has an auto humidity sensor, so you can just leave it plugged in and set the sensor to your desired humidity level (they recommend 45%)
- Doesn\x27t leave surroundings wet with water. This uses evaporation, so you won\x27t see steam coming out of this. Which made me worried that it wouldn\x27t humidify enough, but according to my external humidity gauge, if I run it at full blast my bedroom reaches 67% humidity during the night. Which is great, as I\x27m dealing with dry mountain air which really dehydrates me.
- Most importantly, humidifies really well! (see above)

In the past two weeks I compared this model with a Vicks model (didn\x27t humidify AT ALL) and the Roolen humidifier, which, while it also looks nice like this Oskar model, has a lot of issues: goes through water quickly, small tank, makes slight gurgling sounds all night, has a bright light, and leaves surroundings wet, without upping the room\x27s humidity very much. So Oskar for the definite win.

review_body:
First, I\x27d beg you to not discredit my opinion simply because I own a futon--the most maligned of all couch-like furniture. We keep the thing around purely out of lazy cheapness. I give it a week before the zipper bursts open once and for all and I chuck the whole thing to the curb.

product_title: Elizabeth Craft Metal Die, Gifts
review_headline: Cute die cut but a bit of a gluing challenge
review_body:
This die-cut set yields a cute present that measures about 1.5\x5C\x22 x 1.75\x5C\x22 when all of the pieces are glued together. I use the assembled die cut both inside and on the outside of my birthday and Christmas cards. You can face your present with polka-dots, hearts, or stripes, depending on which die you use. You will be gluing four pieces of paper together, and I often add glitter to the bow.

The only problem with assembling the four pieces of paper is that there is no really good way to glue the package top onto the package body. I tried gluing the bow to the package top, and then gluing the bottom of the bow onto the package body, but had trouble lining up the top with the body. What seemed to work better for me was to glue an extra piece of paper behind the package body, with a little strip sticking up over the top. Then I glued the package top to that exposed strip of paper. That gave me a nice, tight fit.

review_headline: Worst consumer product I\x27ve ever seen
review_body: This is the worst consumer product of any kind that I\x27ve ever seen.  It is a very poor design and the tank is made of very cheap, soft plastic that makes it very difficult to seal the cap after refilling.  Even when it does work, it puts very little moisture into the air.  The main problem is that the filter just sits in the machine, with nothing to hold it in place to ensure air moves through it.  Very often, the filter will fall over and the air will just move around it, instead of through it to evaporate the water.  Even when it stays in place, the unit doesn\x27t put out much moisture, because the filter is quite small and the fan is pretty low volume.  I bought two of these last winter.  One lasted about a month before the fan quit.  the other lasted a year, until I threw it out for being useless.  I think someone else already said it, but I wouldn\x27t take another one of these if it was free, with a lifetime supply of filters.  It\x27s not worth the electricity it takes to run it.

product_title: Amaze Heaters Wall Mounted Electric Heater, Heat Reflector, 250 Watt
review_headline: Chemical odor for months, no end in sight
review_body:
I have been using this heater since early November 2014 for my infant daughter\x27s 70 sq. foot room. I thought this heater would be the perfect solution to heating this teeny room that has no floor space for a heater. We turn our heat down very low at night, and the house hear never seems to reach the nursery anyway. This heater definitely does not make the room warm, but it takes the freezing edge off as long as we have the door completely closed and the window insulated with that plastic "shrink wrap." My baby\x27s hands often feel icy cold when I feed her in the middle of the night, but the cold doesn\x27t seem to bother her, so I guess the heater is doing its job well enough.

More concerning, however, is the odor. I kept the window cracked, the door open, and a fan on for the first couple days. The instructions say off-gassing should be done after 24 hours, and the heater has tested as no-VOC. After nearly 3 months of nightly use, the heater continues to give off a terrible chemical smell that overpowers her teeny room. Because it is winter and temps are so low, we can no longer leave her window and door open. I am very concerned about my daughter breathing in these fumes. For this reason, I am not sure I can recommend this heater for a baby\x27s space, let alone any space where people will be breathing these fumes. The company is definitely misleading in its statement that the fumes will be gone after 24 hours, which makes me very concerned that the "no-VOC" claim is deceptive as well ...

review_headline: Exactly as pictured, high quality, beautiful!
review_body:
The colors in the photo are very true to life. The package shipped directly from Japan, and arrived in perfect shape - no wrinkles in the curtain, so I could hang it immediately no need to iron or anything. I ordered a standard American-style spring-rod, and the pocket was easy to slide through. It was up and hanging within 5 minutes of opening the package.

One note - these curtains are not opaque in general... if you want something to totally block view or light, this is not it - from the top of the door jamb, they fall to around 18-24" off the floor, and if there\x27s a light source behind them (a window or bright light), you\x27ll be able to see shapes through them. That wasn\x27t a problem for me - this was a decoration for a party, rather than an everyday use thing, but some people are surprised when it comes and it\x27s not totally opaque due to the open weave of the fabric.

We put one up in the doorway to our kitchen for a Japanese style dinner party to add some ambiance, and it\x27s perfect. I think it\x27s also a great option for a teenager who is having friends over, and you don\x27t want them to close the door to their bedroom, but want to give them some privacy.

product_title: Holiday Trims Tree Removal Bag (1 Bag), 144\x22 Circumference x 90\x22 Tall (0.75 Mil)
review_headline: Imperfect but the best I\x27ve found
review_body:
I don\x27t know why the images on the packaging indicate you can put this on from the trunk up, but as other reviewers have noted, you have to cut a special hole in the bag for this. I think this leads to tearing. The plastic is pretty thin, but I haven\x27t found that to be a really big deal. This is what I have done:

Put the bag over the top of the tree
slowly move it down the tree, pushing branches up (think of how the tree came before its branches fell into place)
get the bag as far down as it will go, gather the bag at the bottom (use the huge twist tie they include to help)
remove the tree from the stand
tilt on the ground
use a plastic shopping bag to put around the trunk and pull it from there

I\x27ve had pretty good luck with these. They do form small rips where the branches poke out, but I haven\x27t lost many needles that way. In all, it\x27s not a flawless product, but I buy them every year. I will say, though, what Amazon is charging now (~$7) is pretty high. I buy mine for $4 at the tree lot.

product_title: La Crosse Technology
review_headline: Depends on whether the weather matters to you...
review_body:
After 20 years my simple La Crosse station stopped correctly reading the remote, and no amount of tinkering, batteries etc fixed it. Time to modernize. I picked this model because I wanted something fairly straightforward to operate, easy to read as I strolled by, but with min max and indoor-outdoor humidity. The animation was unnecessary, but OK.

It has a big bright display, is fairly easy to set up, and the temps are reasonably accurate. End of pros.
The display is hard to read from off-angles or in brighter light.
I\x27ve had to coax (prolonged button-holds) it to reconnect with the remote every other day. (Remote is maybe 35-40 feet away through 1 outer window and 1 inner wall, never had a problem with the old station.)
The cartoonish animation is not only unattractive, but is completely incorrect- it was pouring rain, 85% humidity, and it showed sun. It\x27s been sunny, 30% humidity for 3 days, and it consistently shows rain. I mean, in Arizona!
It really requires being plugged in to run; my old one ran a year on a set of batteries. That\x27s ok, but limits where I can put it.
Overall I\x27m disappointed enough that I\x27m probably going to replace it and give this one to my grand kids. (They live in the Pacific Northwest so the cartoon being stuck on rain won\x27t be a problem.)

product_title: Whitmor Book & Magazine Organizers, Set of 5, Multicolor
review_headline: Looks Great, Gets the Job Done
review_body:
Despite the many negative comments, I went ahead and ordered 25 of these because of their looks. They are GORGEOUS. The colors are vibrant and the hardware adds a delightful touch of bling. Some here have complained that they are difficult to assemble, flimsy, and won\x27t stand up on their own. My college-sophomore son assembled them while I filled them with magazines. He had all 25 assembled before I could even fill the first eight. Judging by some of the complaints here, assembly is not fool-proof. So if you are a fool, don\x27t buy these. If you are not a fool, you should be good to go.

As for these organizers being flimsy and falling down, yes, they are light weight, and you could knock them down if you are clumsy, or a strong wind could blow them over. You shouldn\x27t use them to hold your magazine while you are on the deck of an aircraft carrier, guiding in fighter jets. (If I were you commanding officer, I would have a discreet word with you about reading magazines on the flight deck.)

I am attaching a picture of how they look in my home. Oh, look--there\x27s one standing up by itself!

Fold them, fill them, and shove them into the book case. They\x27ll be great.

product_title: Lask0 755320 Ceramic Tower Heater with Digital Display and Remote Control
review_headline: Safe and reliable heater for small to medum rooms!
review_body:
I\x27ve had the same Lasko ceramic element heater for over 10 years. It has served me reliably and safely in that entire time. I still have it and it works perfectly fine. You just have to remember to blow out the dust lint that collects with constant use. I just needed an extra one for my two story home.

I was a little concerned about a few of the negative reviews that reported fire and hot plugs. I researched the issue and most of the evidence points to loose plugs or faulty outlets. The warning tag on the power cable warns of this and is typical of any high current draw appliances. I\x27ve been monitoring the heat on the plug and it has not felt warm to the touch at all. I think that if you follow the recommended guidelines that come with the product, you should be fine. I also read in another review that the handle was not well designed for a person with small hands. I would have to respectfully disagree. I have small hands and I find that this models design is easier to carry around the house compared to my old one.

Now on to the fact that I love this little heater! Compared to my previous Lasko, there is half as much noise from the blower. It is very quiet! I love that I can now fine tune the temp down to a specific degree. My last one only had 5 degree adjustments. So either I felt it was too cold or too warm. Now it\x27s Perfect! It also shows you the current temperature in the room which is another nice little feature. I did notice however that the remote is basically the same as my old one and both of them work on my new heater. I guess if it\x27s not broke, don\x27t fix it...

review_headline: Response to Review - Misinformed About Latex Densities
review_body:
To the reviewer above who made claims about this not being the correct density as advertised because \x27it didn\x27t hold their weight\x27 as the buyer thought it should...

The \x27thinner\x27 Latex is, the less supportive it is... Latex slabs naturally come in 6\x5C\x22 thicknesses which IS ideal for supporting a body; BUT at 4\x5C\x22 thick, it would NOT be expected to fully support probably even a toddler. THUS is why it is called a \x27topper\x27 and not a \x27mattress\x27.

A Latex mattress should support you at this ILD - but not a topper. I have one of these on my solid Latex ILD 32 bed. It\x27s a great sleep & support system.

review_body:
We had another brand of Indoor/Outdoor thermometer and relied on it. The digital readings were accurate when checked with a conventional thermometer. When the sending unit on that one \x27died\x27 after several years, we tried this product.

After setting it up, and before mounting the units, I noticed that the indoor and outdoor temperatures displayed differed by several degrees, even though the parts were right next to each other! I left them for several hours, in different locations around the house, and found temperature variations from 1/2 degree up to 5 degrees F, between the indoor and outdoor displays.

The Atomic Clock feature sounds like it should be super accurate and automatic. But we had to set it up manually, and the owner\x27s manual describes all kinds of things that can interfere with reception. Like daylight.

Because of accuracy issues, and lack of confidence in the readings, we sent it back to Amazon. Might be OK if you just want a rough estimate of time and temperature.

product_title: Lacis Bead Loom Hardwood Purse Bead Loom, 11-Inch
review_body:
This loom is very, very sturdy, and very, very well-thought-out. It\x27s based on Indian looms (open or box looms) that have been found in the U.S. (particularly in the southern part of the country), but it\x27s even more flexible, because you can adjust the tension at any time. At first, I was baffled as to how this would work, but then I found a YouTube video (just keyword \x5C\x22Lacis bead loom\x5C\x22, or even \x5C\x22Lacis\x5C\x22- you\x27ll find it!) ordering, and now I totally get it! The parts go together easily, and the inner screw-ins on the outer knobs are lined with machined metal, so they won\x27t wear out anytime soon. It\x27s also larger than I thought it would be- assembled, it\x27s 20\x5C\x22 x 14\x5C\x22 outer dimensions (20x16, counting the knobs), and the wood frame is thicker and heavier than expected. It\x27s also rather pretty- mine has some knots in the wood, but any weak spots have been filled in with what appears to be epoxy, and well-sanded to a smooth finish, so it\x27s got character, but is still strong. It\x27s such a pleasant surprise, to have gotten such a lovely loom at such a great price! I\x27m thinking about making permanent spacer strings for this, with something permanent (like Beadalon or SoftFlex & crimps) with all of the different sizes of seed beads- the holes for running the string through appear to be wide enough to accomodate finished crimps. The video shows how to hook your spacing string up using paperclip hooks, rather than tying the string to the elastic. Also, I\x27m thinking that finishing a project (tying off) will have to be done as described by Shoopy McMeerah (look for him on YouTube, too- just copy & paste the name, and you\x27ll find his stuff)- the booklet that came with this doesn\x27t really get into that, but it doesn\x27t seem like it\x27ll be all that hard to do. I\x27m very happy with this loom, and would recommend it to anyone who wants to try looming, but I would also strongly recommend that you watch the YouTube videos, both the Lacis instructional one, and Shoopy McMeerah\x27s videos on open / box looms- it\x27ll make it much, much easier to understand how this works. Overall, this was a score, and I\x27d recommend it. :)

UPDATE: In the video made by the Lacis folks, they demonstrate winding the loom using a small-diameter wooden dowel. I would recommend, instead, getting a 1/4\x5C\x22 non-threaded metal rod/dowel, instead! Picked up a zinc rod at a local hardware store for two bucks, and it works much, much better than the wood- less friction, and the metal doesn\x27t bend and bow like the wood did. Still really, really pleased with this loom. And very pleased NOT to have had to buy a floor stand to make winding easier! :)en / box looms- it\x27ll make it much, much easier to understand how this works. We use this vacuum on a daily basis, really like the swivel head and it can get into much tighter spaces than the Dyson ball. The attachments are all easy to use and the included mini turbo attachment works great to remove pet hair from your furniture.

If you are looking for a vacuum that can handle pet hair, look no further than the Miele S7260 Cat & Dog Upright.

product_title: Whitmor 50-Pair Shoe Tower, Chrome with Wheels
review_headline: Design could definitely use some improvements.
review_body:
This rack just so happened to be the perfect size to slide into our under-stairs coat closet. I wanted something on wheels so it could be pulled out from time to time to access the storage space in the back of the closet. This was the perfect solution.

The construction is pretty sturdy and assembly is pretty easy, though a little time-consuming with all the screws that are used.

Shoes regularly fall off of this when being moved, though. I find that the gritty bars just don\x27t do a good enough job holding onto the shoes. It\x27d honestly probably work just fine if the bars were not as angled to help keep shoes in place. Or having a lip at the bottom to stop the shoes from sliding off would be even better. If you\x27re going to put wheels on something, to me, that goes with the assumption that it\x27s made to move around from time to time. If the shoes are going to fall off whenever it gets moved, that kind of defeats the purpose.

Even still, the size of this thing is perfect for a big family with lots of shoes if you need the vertical storage space.

product_title: Essick Air 5D6 700 4-Speed Mini Console Humidifier,White
review_headline: I maintain 40% humidity (shown by an external hygrometer) and refill them easily just once a day
review_body:
980 square foot, single story house. I bought 2 and set them to run continuously on fan speed 2 (extremely quiet), and they each put out about 2-3 gallons of water per day. I simply fill them up once a day and forget them.
Prior to using these, my house\x27s humidity was about 20% in January and February. The way I use them, I maintain 40% humidity (shown by an external hygrometer) and refill them easily just once a day.
I have tried using them on fan speed 3, and I can attain 55% internal humidity throughout my small house. Fan speed 3 is noticeable to me but not irritating if run continuously. Fan speed 4 is annoying to me. I do sometimes use fan speed 3 as white noise while I sleep.
I believe this is about as simple a humidifier as you can get. Extremely easy to maintain and clean and refill. I\x27m completely satisfied.

product_title: Bucilla Counted Cross Stitch Bookmark Kit, 2.5 by 8-Inch, 45709 Inspired By Nature (Set of 12)
review_body:
I am so disappointed with this kit. For starters, all the threads are wrapped around each other in a wad of floss the size of a softball. It took me four hours to untangle and match the threads into groups. None of the threads are labeled so it\x27s a huge guessing game to sort out the difference between pink, pale pink, light pink, dark pink, coral, pale coral, light fuchsia, pale periwinkle, etc. There are so many colors that are almost indiscernible from one another that the only way to determine what color they were was to count how many yards each color had and hope they didn\x27t both have the same amount. It took me another two hours (with help) to sort out what color each thread was named and label them. Even now there are two or three colors that I am not certain are labeled correctly. I am not a novice and I expect there to be a certain amount of prep work for any project I start, but six hours is just ridiculous and it has sucked the fun out of this project before I\x27ve even made a single stitch.

After all of that hassle I unfolded the included fabric to iron out the creases and found that there was a giant bug smashed between the folds which resulted in a stain. Unfortunately, it was in the middle of the fabric and will most certainly mean I won\x27t have enough to complete all twelve bookmarks.

Overall, I am disappointed with this kit in a big way. I will not purchase another Bucilla product in the future and would only recommend them to someone who preferred arduous activities over enjoyable ones.

First of all, if you are looking for heavy wood with an old time feel, this is not the clock for you. In fact the only way to obtain a clock with that substantial old time feel, and deep sound, is to buy an old vintage key wind clock. They are readily available.
This clock is light because it has a quartz movement.
The Amazon price for this clock is really good. I bought mine 3 years ago from a large clock store and paid $100.00 more for it.
This clock, hanging on the wall is lovely. It does not in any way appear cheap.
The glass covering the pendulum compartment is thick and decorative . They describe it as seeded.
The glass covering the face and dial is convex.
Both features give this clock an elegance.
I don\x27t normally like Howard Miller clocks, but I like this one.
Mine is set to a simple bim bam chime.. The chime is in tune. The volume can be controlled. It offers three different chime patterns, and it can also be turned off.
The clock keeps perfect time, and gives warmth and a delicate elegance to the room.
I love clocks, particularly old key winds; however there is something to be said for a clock that is lovely, does not have to be wound, keeps exact time, and adds character and warmth to a room.

review_body: I don\x27t know if I have a dud or if I\x27m doing something wrong, but I can\x27t get this thing to cut. product_title: InterDesign Orbz Bath Shower Tote
review_headline: Versatile, multipurpose lightweight plastic tote whose uses are limited only by your imagination!
review_body:
This is a nicely made medium-sized plastic tote that can be used in many ways depending on your needs. We\x27ve tried it out as a tote for bathroom essentials for guests (we load it up and leave in the guest room so guests have toiletries to easily take to bathroom, but don\x27t have to leave them in bathroom, which has NO space for more stuff!); we\x27ve used it to tote laundry supplies to the basement laundry room. We use it to store newspapers and magazines until we read them. We also use it to store the abundance of daily mail before we sort it. We use it to carry multiple items from one room to the other in a single trip.

If it were less rigid and wider (or of a material with more "foregiveness"), we\x27d use for many trips to the local shops to pick up fruits, veggies and small items. It\x27s a perfect size when you\x27re just picking up a few things. It worked well for us when picking up flowers from our corner fruit/veggie stand. They tend to leak no matter how well wrapped and having a washable tote was helpful.

Pros:
>Not too large, not too small. Easily stored.
>Lightweight
>>Like the rigidity (but it can be a "con" based on what you want to put in it as well)
>Seems to come pretty clean (yes, it might get easily stained depending on how you use and what it\x27s exposed to but so far, stuff washes off and anything that sticks has come off using a Magic Eraser.)

Cons:
>>Personally, I am not in love with the little circle design on the sides with openings between them. I\x27d have preferred solid sides not just for design purposes but to keep what\x27s inside intact and not exposed.
>>Handle opening: Could be larger so you could more easily sling over your shoulder (If your arms are short and/or on the thin side, it will fit but very snugly)
>>Wish the handles could be locked together

product_title: Sengoku HMN-110 HeatMate 10,000-BTU Portable Radiant Kerosene Heater
review_headline: Big heat from a relatively compact unit, for a great price
review_body: This item has helped extend the time we can use our trailer in Northern Minnesota.  By October, it\x27s getting too cold to heat the place with electric heaters, and propane is expensive and refilling the tanks a hassle.  This heater worked right out of the box, and is small enough to fit in most rooms of the trailer.  It has a convenient removable tank so we can refill it outside without carrying the entire heater up and down the steps.  One tank of kerosene kept the bedroom warm for a couple of nights.  You can find jugs of kerosene on sale at Menards or any home improvement store, and they are far easier to carry than the propane tank.  A drip-free siphon is included which makes filling the tank much easier.  I think this heater is perfect for places like trailers and fish houses, where you don\x27t have a lot of space.  I would "break it in" by running it outdoors for a few minutes to an hour; after that, you will notice minimal smell compared with the kerosene heaters of the past.  These new models really do operate with relatively little kerosene smell.

product_title: Neato XV-21 Pet & Allergy Automatic Vacuum Cleaner
review_headline: The next step in domestic revolution!
review_body:
What the washing machine did for my grandmother, and the dishwasher did for my mother, the robot vac has done for me! Keep in mind it\x27s not perfect, it\x27s not a maid, but it does what it\x27s meant to do which is to simplify housekeeping in an efficient and relatively cost effective way.

I do not have carpet in my home which means I can see every dust spec, crumb and fur clump on my floor. With active kids and 4 animals, you can imagine the floors get messy very quickly each day. Running "Jaws" (as we lovingly call him) each morning has kept us from going insane trying to keep the floors clean on top of everything else we get to do in our free time lol! It keeps the mess to a minimum so all i have to worry about is a weekend spot cleaning with a broom and dust mop.

An added benefit is that Jaws taught us to leave nothing on the floors which shouldn\x27t be there, so the house is even tidier!

I can\x27t speak to the lifespan, Jaws has only been on the job since Christmas. He vacuums just as well as my regular vacuum, and does it (mainly) independently. If that\x27s what you are looking for, that\x27s what you will get.

One star off for him getting confused sometimes and missing a spot but since I run him daily it\x27s no big deal to me - he will get it tomorrow.

product_title: Hoover Max Extract 60 Pressure Pro Carpet Deep Cleaner, FH50220
review_body:
I\x27ve cleaned four rooms with my Max Extract. It works. I had a few problems, but they were the result of operator error, not machine malfunction.
What attracted me to the Max Extract was its promise of a shorter drying time, and I\x27m happy to say that the promise was kept.
Let me offer a bit of advice for the shoppers out there: Read the product description, read reviews and watch some You Tube videos of the product in use. Whatever you purchase, Read The Instructions! Follow The Instructions!
The machine is large, heavy, and noisy, though it rolls and pushes easily. The hot air it blows out helps to dry the carpet. Have a towel handy; a lot of water is involved, there are bound to be spills. The upholstery attachment seems fragile.
It comes with a small bottle of soap which I used up on one room. That was fine by me because I didn\x27t like the smell. I ordered the Bissell Allergen Cleaning solution: Virtually NO odor! Yay for those of us who are sensitive to fragrance.
I like this product. I gave it four stars, though, because the fifth is for longevity and I don\x27t know how long the machine will last--it is almost all plastic and made in China (like everything else).

product_title: iRobot Roomba 780 Vacuum Cleaning Robot
review_headline: Much better on carpet than hardwoods...
review_body:
I am a bit disappointed with the Roomba for MY uses. I know these things sell like mad and get good reviews, but I am in a position to judge them based on two very similar models. I ordered the 780 for my wife for Christmas and purchased the 770 for my mom for Christmas. The big difference between these two is the accessories, lighthouses and walls.

Otherwise they appear virtually identical.

At my mom\x27s house, she has a large family room with mostly carpet and a small entryway and a medium size study with hardwoods. We used her Roomba over the holidays and were fairly impressed. It cleans carpet very well and seemed to be getting the small entry and study fairly well.

Then we came home to our larger house with a large first floor of hardwoods and area rugs. We set up our Roomba and it woke me up at 3:00am and so we set it up for 8:00am.

So now we are able to see it in action some days. Watching it in action is disappointing. It\x27s really disappointing to watch the Roomba in action. It goes over a lot of stuff that isn\x27t picked up. I have cleaned the tray out and watched it with a fresh clean tray. The little white brush swipes the garbage in front of the Roomba, It runs over the trash and most of it is still there afterwards.

It simply does MUCH BETTER on carpet than hardwoods.

So my suggestion is that if you have hardwoods, this thing is not doing what I would expect a $500+ device to do. The tech is neat, but the vacuum isn\x27t quite what I would hope for on hardwoods.

product_title: Moda Flame Cavo Table Top Bio-Ethanol Fireplace
review_headline: Great Winter Christmas or Birthday Gift- Can someone buy me one too?
review_body:
I bought this as a Christmas gift for someone "who has everything they need." In this case for someone who owns a condo but doesn\x27t have a cool fireplace with it. They LOVE it and uses it regularly.

Packaging: Came in a box disassembled, with Ikea like assembly instructions, fire snuffer, and one wool wick within the fireplace insert. (Don\x27t throw away the insert). Doesn\x27t include fuel. Some people complained about that but its like asking a toaster to come with electricity. Please plan for it.

Assembly: Wasn\x27t difficult at all. If you can assemble Ikea furniture or legos, you can easily handle this fireplace.

Pros:
- Beautiful, Modern design.
- Portable and compact - move it to any room you want
- Smokeless - doesn\x27t need to be vented
- Does put out some heat to warm up by. Can warm up a small space.

"Cons:"
- Doesn\x27t last super long due to its small fuel insert. (Its a trade off to having such a portable little fireplace)
- Real Fire = Danger Zone~ It looks so cool that you may forget you are playing with fire. Read safety manual.

Fuel Tips:
- Fill up to the recommended amount- no more. My friend doesn\x27t put in much fuel (half the max amount) and complains about fire longevity. Its also because he isn\x27t sure how much he is pouring. A dedicated measuring cup may help.
- Buy the fuel in bulk packs: You will save money on the long run and you get to enjoy the fire without worry about fuel. At the time I purchased the fuel and fireplace: the Moda Flame 6 pack was only $10 more than the 3 Pack. Get the six pack.

review_headline: Works as advertised but don\x27t expect any tech support
review_body:
I have had several La Crosse products over the last 8 years and I agree with previous post, as lone as you don\x27t spend much money, there worth it but their tech support has gone from poor to pitiful to non-existent over the years.

I placed this in my motor home with the outdoor sensor zip tied to the ladder on the back. I was worried about the sensor being exposed to the rain and snow so I placed it into a Ziploc bag. The bag slows the temperature response time down a little by blocking the air flow but within half an hour it will stabilize and read the accurate temp. I placed lithium batteries in the main unit because of the low temperatures in the motor home when it\x27s not in use will kill alkaline batteries. I have another La Crosse whether station in our house that picks up the outdoor temp from the same outdoor sensor. The distance from the outdoor sensor to the base unit is greatly affected by walls or other objects so don\x27t plan on the 330 ft they advertise. Mine works at a max of about 40 ft.

After about 3 years the batteries in the outdoor sensor died and I replaced them with AAA rechargeables it\x27s working fine now.

review_body:
This took about 1 1/2 hours to assemble and another 30 minutes trying to move through 2 doorways and around a corner. The screws for the rear shelf were too long and popped through the laminate in one spot, but that shelf is hidden from site anyway. The storage drawers work well for small items like pens, pencils, sharpeners. I didn\x27t even know there was a 3rd shelf along the back of the desk when I bought it. I originally thought that I would never use this, but I\x27ve been putting small canvases and drawing paper on it.

I am left-handed, so I would prefer to have the horizontal surface on the left side, but that is minor considering the use I\x27ve already gotten out of this desk. Overall, this is a wonderful item for drafting, art projects, storing items, and even a conversation starter.

product_title: Frigidaire Aroma Fresh-50, 3-Stage Anti-Allergen Desktop Air Cleaner / Air Purifier FRAP05A6OB
review_body:
I feel this is an "okay" product, but I am not overly impressed in the short time I have been using it. To be fair, I would think that you would really need to use the product for a couple of months to get a real feel for how well it filters the air, but in the few weeks I have had it in operation, here is what I think:

1) It is quiet - remarkably so. Many portable air filter devices aren\x27t, so that is a plus if you are looking for quiet operation. I don\x27t mind the noise of a fan or air purifier in the bedroom since it is a "white noise" that I find helps me sleep. But if you\x27re looking for quiet, you\x27ll have no issue with this device.

2) The area around the air speed control is illuminated with a green light that I found too bright for me when I am trying to sleep (I am using this on a nightstand by my bed). Not a big deal, really. I just covered it up with a square of cloth to block the light.

3) I was completely unimpressed with the scent pad option. I added eucalyptus and lavender oil to the pad, but neither I nor my husband could tell that the air leaving the machine had any fragrance at all. I doused it pretty good, too. Others users say they felt it worked great, so not sure why we couldn\x27t smell anything.

4) I am not convinced it is doing a whole lot to filter the air. I ran it and another purifier side by side in my bedroom for two days, then opened them up to take a look at how much debris the filters had collected. My other device had evidence of dust and dog hair in the filter. This device\x27s filter still looked like new - no debris collection at all. I was running it on its highest speed, too. I\x27m not sure how effective the fan motor is in this. In my old device, if I hold a tissue up to the air intake area, the fan is strong enough to hold the tissue in place in front of the intake. This one will not hold the tissue in place. It just falls off as if there is no suction at all. That probably accounts for the difference in the amount of air "junk" collected in each.

I have not completely written this purifier off, and will give it another 30 days or so and check the filter again. But at this point, I am unimpressed.

The filter plugs up very easily, so I bought some filter fabric for a window air-conditioner.3/16 thick foam filter fabric, & cut ten disks 4 1/2 inch diameter & replaced the original filter with all ten disks. Now it is a much better vacuum cleaner. The suction is good, the motor should stay cooler with more air flow. It cleans the carpet much better now, & there is very little dust filling the air, but as I look at the filter, some dust must escape through the filter as even the last disk contains some dust, it just is not notice-able when using the vacuum. So if you are having problems with this machine, this is how I solved my problems, & now it is as good as any other vacuum cleaner that I ever appreciated before. product_title: Dyson Ball Multi Floor Upright Vacuum
review_headline: No regrets in buying the Dyson D65
review_body:
Lovin\x27 this beast!! I was pretty confident that my house and carpets were well cleaned before - I\x27m not a clean-aholic but I do dust and vacuum at least once per week and vacuum sometimes more often. I did the suggested "test" I heard about; vacuum with the old machine and then redo with the Dyson. I thought that was just a gimmicky thing but OMG!! I was truly shocked at how much more pet hair, dust, crumbs, "stuff" the Dyson sucked out of my floors and furniture.

What I love about it: (1) the hose is attached right in the machine so you can easily go from vacuuming a big area to "spot" sucking stuff up by simply pulling out the hose and attaching the tools - kept on board the unit body, (2) easily adjusts from carpets to hard floors with the push of a button to turn off the beater brush (actually, you could probably leave it on - I have and it works just a fine.) (3) it is SO damn easy to empty the canister cup. Just watch the YouTube videos on how to operate the unit but this feature alone now is what I really sing the praises of - -that and it\x27s awesome sucking capability. (4) for it\x27s power, it is not as loud as I thought it would be.

What I which were better/different (but is not a turnoff nor should it be a deal breaker for you - just some design items I wish were different. After all, it\x27s a vacuum cleaner and not the answer to all life\x27s problems!) (1) the "cord management" is a bit awkward; I wish it had a retractable feature (2) the tools don\x27t attach very well and fall off. I finally stopped trying to wrestle with it and just left them off - why fight this; life it too short! However, for the price, this part should be way better than it is. Overall, however, fairly minor inconvenience. That\x27s it! Otherwise, so far, no regrets in this purchase.

It is a bit heavier than I expected but this is the D65 which is their biggest model, I think. I may have been able to go with the one size smaller but I got the D65 at a crazy good "Black Friday" deal of over $200 off the list price. The smaller size down (D50, maybe??) would have cost me more in the long run because the $$ off was not as generous at that sale time. (PS - I have 2 cats in the house so being able to pick up pet hair is important to me. Also important, being able to easily and cleanly empty the dust cup. This product does an exceptional job with both. I\x27m very glad I made the investment. I recommend it to my family and friends.) product_title: The Amazing Musical Rainbow Birthday Candle
review_body: The entertainment factor was over the top.  The product didn\x27t work as it was supposed to but I guess we got our money\x27s worth considering how much we laughed.  Most definitely NOT a candle for inside a building.  The sparks shower everywhere and open flame shoots from the top.  It is pretty impressive to watch, but do it outside!!  The packaging is a scream if you are amused by poor attempts to translate directions from Chinese to English.  The candle did not play Happy Birthday when it first opened but after about 10 minutes it did start to lamely play the song.  After about 20 minutes it played the song correctly.  And then it continued forever!  We followed the direction to cut the wire to make it stop playing and promptly threw it on the garbage.  Later in the evening the trash can mysteriously started playing happy birthday so I checked it out and the wire had apparently not been cut all the way through.  I cut the wire again, making darn sure I cut the copper wire.  Two days later I was walking past the outside dumpster and guess what - the darn thing had started playing happy birthday again!  So I cut the wire in another spot.  Not sure if it was some sort of alien communication device or merely possessed by a poltergeist, but that things was still playing 3 days later on garbage day.  That was in December and I wouldn\x27t be surprised to hear it still playing Happy Birthday out in the landfill.  For sure it was $5.00 of fun but use this outside!!

product_title: Brother(R) VX1435 Mechanical Sewing Machine
review_headline: Before you go jumping to conclusions, based on the reviews, look around the internet.
review_body:
Wow, my mom got me this for Christmas. I started making puppets and wanted to get a sewing machine. Lots of bad reviews. 100% different on another site I saw. This thing works perfect for me. I am using another site, that has classes, some of which are free, and I\x27ve learned a lot of neat stuff about it.

It is easy to learn with this thing. There are not that many settings, so that you will get overwhelmed. You can take the needle out simply, as well as the bottom bobbin. I have made a bunch of pieces of fabric, just showing the different types of stitch. They are all 100% straight and worked very well. The only problem I had was, I was using felt. It got caught on the hole that the needle goes through. I switched material and everything worked great.

I made my first button hole today. It took some figuring out, but I did not give up. I have like 15 puppet arms sewn. The things works great.

It is easy to take the needle out. You just turn the little screw. You can easily take the thing that holds the fabric down off. You just push something in on the back. Taking the bottom tray off is easy. You just pull it out. The top part, just above the needle comes out easy. You just unscrew a simple screw. I have no problems doing anything on the machine.

I emailed the company and asked which type of oil to use. I shall try to oil it when I find out. The instructions easy show you which few spots to oil. Could not make it any easier.

I am 100% happy with this thing. For someone just learning, it is great.

Update 6 - 13 - 15:
Ok, well, I got this for Christmas 2014. It is June 2015 and it broke. Well, it DID sew, but the stitching was off. It was far pulled from the fabric. I could not get it to sew correctly. I tried different settings and nothing would work. My mom connected the place she got it from. They said they\x27ve had problems with this machine. They gave her the money back, plus %50 off another machine. So, I picked a different one. I did use some thick stuff. Tarp kind of stuff and thick, fur stuff for puppet skin. So, it did work great for a bit. Also, it is because of this machine that I learned, at least the basics of sewing.

If you want to learn to sew, I would not recommend this machine. I\x27ve not used it in a while. I was learning to make a shirt and pants for a puppet. product_title: SterlingPro Double Wall Stainless Steel French Coffee Press
review_headline: Produces Stainless Steel Powder You End Up Drinking. UNSAFE.
review_body:
First off, wow. I\x27ve never had so many people use the unhelpful rating to let me know they disagree with me. You guys really love this thing. I never read reviews of items I already know I love so that is some genuine consumer loyalty. So, from that alone, people reading this, you\x27ll probably love this thing.

That having been said, I tried this at a friend\x27s home recently, along with several others in two stores, and found the same flaw on all models. If the plunger base (where you find your fine mesh filter on all French Presses) comes in contact with the inner wall of the stainless steel unit at any point, which it will, the ring/rim of the mesh portion of the plunger will scrape the side and take tiny flecks of stainless steel with it, a fine powder of metal that you will be drinking with your coffee, as it is so fine as to easily pass through that metal mesh filter. Cancer, liver failure, dementia, take your pick. You\x27ll be poisoning yourself if you use this or any other stainless steel unit that is not glass lined (and glass linings can crack or break).

For the record, the Sterling Pro, along with Bodum, among other presses, produced a fine powder of steel particles when tested and are not safe to use.

Note: All of the French Presses I tried were units that had been plunged again and again and, as a result, had at least one point of contact resulting in scraping and the production of the fine, stainless steel powder. The safest version of the metal I found was a chromium and nickel mix, both of which are toxic in higher than very low milligram doses and are not intended to be ingested as metal shavings. If you have a stainless steel French Press, please check it before each use to make sure it has not developed one or more points of contact where the metal inside is being shaved off into the cup. My old Il Mulino press has been retired to non-food use because, as it turns out, it has a point of contact. The worst offenders, with 100% of the surface of the interior being scraped in this fashion by the mesh/plunger assembly, were the Bodums and the Frielings that I tested, possibly because they are the most popular brands.

I was asked by a manufacturer to be clearer on the circumstances of my trying of their unit. While some were tried in home, most were tried in store. To be clear, I found that my Il Mulino was shedding this fine steel dust. I asked two friends, both of whom manage local coffee houses to post a sign asking people to bring in their metal French Presses on specific days. A number of people showed up at each house on each day and we tested all of their units and wrote down the names of the units tested at the time. All units had the same flaw, as all had been used enough to develop it. None were reported to be over two years old and nearly all were reported, by the owners to be less than one year old. Reports of use ranged from \x5C\x22once in a while\x5C\x22 to \x5C\x22daily\x5C\x22. Not all units had names on them but they were matched based on owner report and pictures on Amazon to the units I have reviewed. I have not reviewed any units that were not seen in person and will not, though I suspect they suffer the same flaw. I will not retract my reviews due to the inconvenience it may cause some manufacturers because this is an issue of the health of the consumer. I only looked at my Il Mulino press because I tested positive for heavy metal poisoning and my doctor specifically asked about sources of Nickel in my home. That press was a source and, very possibly, the source. However, I will reiterate that none of the presses I examined were brand new, all had been used, and all were tested simply by inspecting the carafe, making sure there was no steel dust, pushing and retracting the plunger ten times, then removing it to see if steel dust had been deposited. All units inspected (including many duplicates of two Bodums that I can only review once) had the same steel-dust production problem. Ihope this clarifies the issue and puts an end to the not so pleasant messages.

As an aside, if you are still reading reviews of stainless steel presses, you may be interested in Kamerod, Hobbie and Anderson\x27s, \x5C\x22Stainless steel leaches nickel and chromium into foods during cooking\x5C\x22 from The Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry (J Agric Food Chem. 2013 Oct 2;61(39):9495-501. doi: 10.1021/jf402400v. Epub 2013 Sep 19.) Or perhaps Dan and Ibong\x27s, \x5C\x22IMPACT OF COOKING UTENSILS ON TRACE METAL LEVELS OF PROCESSED FOOD ITEMS\x5C\x22 from Annals. Food Science and Technology. These are just two of the more recent articles on this issue. It is well known that the FDA allows higher levels of toxic chemicals in everything from household cleaners to make-up than most developed countries. Unfortunately, this extends to our cookware as well.

Good luck with your search and please don\x27t send me hate mail if you own this and disagree with me. My opinion of this item is not meant to offend but to inform.hope this clarifies the issue and puts an end to the not so pleasant messages.

product_title: Willert AirBoss Keep It Dry Activated Charcoal Closet Deodorizer - 8.46 oz
review_headline: Great closet deodorizer, a little pricey
review_body:
I discovered this product at Wal-Mart when my mother was selling her house. She had mothballs in every closet, and neither my sister nor I could ever convince her to stop. But then we got feedback from an Open House that a client loved the home, but was sensitive / allergic to many chemicals / odors and was afraid she would not be able to get rid of the strong smell of mothballs and cedar out of the house. That finally did it - she was willing to purge all mothballs and some of the worst smelling linens that had been stored enclosed in mothballs. I searched online for what to do to get the residual odor out and found that dry activated charcoal had worked for others, in addition to airing out the house which we had been doing. It does take time - this is not an overnight fix - but these did the trick.

I bought out 2 Wal-Marts and still needed more, so I found and ordered more on Amazon. These were about twice the price I paid at Wal-Mart. That\x27s the only reason I give these 4 stars instead of 5. You may be able to find a better deal locally.

review_headline: I was disappointed to see that this vacuum performed almost same as ...
review_body:
I had a very high expectation and hope for this vacuum cleaner and I wanted this to work because after reading many reviews, I thought this is THE vacuum one should get. Got it from walmart for 299, hooked up everything, started vacuuming. After close to an hour going back and forth on every single room, I was disappointed to see that this vacuum performed almost same as my 14 year old hoover (bought from costco) bagless. This is a brand new vacuum, not a refurbished. Man, over 5 years of design (and over 5k? prototyping), if this is the best they can come up with, this is just a pure marketing hype.
Went to walmart, bought the bissell bagged vacuum ($48), went through the rooms. Went back with dyson to see if I can pickup some more dirt from the carpet. I wanted this dyson to work and somehow justify the purchase. I probably picked up may be 1/2 spoon dirt (real fine powder).
I don\x27t think i got a lemon because there is good suction from the accessory wand and also from the bottom (almost same as the bissell).

My bottom line:
From a pure performance point of view, I wouldn\x27t buy this vacuum if the price is anything over $100. I have no problem with the feel of the vacuum, set up, pushing around etc but if it is not going to pick up more dirt than a $50 vacuum, why would you want to spend 6 times more?
This review is not an endorsement to hoover or bissell, but looks like dyson, shark etc are running fine marketing campaigns rather than quality products. I am wondering how so many people rated this product so high, yet I couldn\x27t find that performance in this brand new vacuum. What am i doing wrong here?

There are over 1000 engineers working in dyson R&D (written in box), I would love to know how many are working in bissell and hoover etc :)

product_title: La Crosse Technology WS-9080U-IT Wireless IN/OUT Temperature Station featuring Atomic Self-setting time & MIN/MAX records
review_body:
I\x27ve both been through, and currently have many wireless thermometers in use, LaCrosse, Oregon, AcuRite, etc, including this one, which is overall the best of them all. Each has their strong and weak points.

This unit has the best range of most, LaCrosse generally does, most of theirs do 330 feet, other brands often 100 ft, these are line of sight ranges, expect less through multiple walls.

The auto-resetting daily low and high temps are displayed full time without pressing buttons. Also all four long term min/max-in/out temps since the unit was powered up can be accessed with time and date of each of them by pressing a single button.

Pairing the receiver and transmitter is slightly more demanding than others, but simple if done right, and the connection is not randomly lost like others, not until the battery wears out. Pairing is easy with fresh batteries, put them in transmitter first, then receiver quickly after. Never fails.

Most all signal loss between transmitter and receiver, and pairing issues, are due to low batteries in either or both units, in both this and all brands of wireless thermometers, even if the low battery icon is off.

The transmitters aren\x27t meant to get wet! Place them under an eve or on an open porch. Sub-zero -20F or so temps sometimes stop the transmitter but return when temp rises. Lithium batteries are said to hold their voltage in very cold temps, though I haven\x27t tried them.

The atomic clocks in many of them are hard to get a signal with as the time stations are far away for most of us. Location in the house, topography around you, and other devices nearby all can effect receiving "atomic time". Fortunately time can be manually set in all of them.

Hope this helps. Cheers!

product_title: Vktech Swift Yarn Fiber String Ball Wool Winder Holder Hand Operated New
review_headline: Inexpensive, but not as simple to use as I\x27d hoped.
review_body:
Overall the product is about what I expected for the price. It has kind of a flimsy feel to it and isn\x27t as \x27pretty\x27 as some of the more expensive winders. I was able to just barely make a 3.5oz hank of bulky yarn into a ball.

Maybe I was trying to wind the ball too quickly, but my yarn keeps getting tangled in the gears. I\x27m hoping maybe it\x27s just my inexperience with yarn winders...I\x27m going to possibly invest in a yarn swift and see if that helps.

As others have notied, the metal yarn holder needs to be pulled as far out as it will go in order to lock into place. I didn\x27t realize this at first, and it was moving back and forth. I had to pull harder than I expected to get it to snap into place.

I give this product 3 stars. The price is good, and I won\x27t be using it on a daily basis so I think it works for my needs. I\x27m going to keep practicing and will update if I have better luck with the tangling as time goes on.

product_title: Weiman Glass Cook Top Heavy Duty Cleaner and Polish
review_headline: Effective Polish - Particularly if Used Before the Stove Gets Too Grimy
review_body: Though I try to keep my glass stove top clean with frequent use of glass cleaner, eventually a bit of cooked on grime seems to accumulate around the outer circles of the cooking rings. Sometimes it appears as just a subtle off-color ring rather than uniformly shiny glass; then I know it\x27s time to use the Weiman polish. I wipe on a small amount, let it dry then rub vigorously with a microfiber cloth (not paper towels since they aren\x27t strong enough and leave a fibrous residue). Even when the discolored ring is barely visible I know I\x27m removing residue when the cloth becomes discolored. If the ring-around-the-ring is still visible after polishing, I give it another coat of Weiman\x27s. The secret to keeping the stovetop clean is to never let it get too dirty - cleaning after every use and scraping off any chunks of spilled or burnt-on food is very important.
