product_title: ADDI Lace Turbo 60\x22 Circular Knitting Needles by SKACEL
review_headline: You can\x27t beat ADDI Lace Turbo Circular Knitting needles for knitting.  Period.
review_body:
I\xE2\x80\x99ve tried many needles, including bamboo (straight, DPN\xE2\x80\x99s, circular), even the ADDI lace turbo interchangeable set. When I was first starting out, I liked the friction that bamboo provided \xE2\x80\x93 it helped me build confidence as stitches were less likely to fall off the needle accidentally.

Then I started knitting a sweater with a beautiful thick/thin mohair yarn. I used a mosaic stitch pattern to combine two colors (you only knit with one color at a time for 2 rows, and you slip periodic stitches to create the color pattern). This resulted in a beautiful pattern, and a nice warm dense knit. Slipping stitches means you get a tighter denser fabric. Translate that to friction across the needles. It took a lot more work and effort when I was using bamboo circulars \xE2\x80\x93 even just to slide the stitches down progressively to continue knitting was a chore. I ended up getting a longer pair of Addi Lace Turbos from a local yarn shop and was hooked. The knitting slid effortlessly across the needles. Instead of battling with every slide of stitches, these were a joy to use.

I tried to increase my stock and save money by purchasing an interchangeable set of Addi Lace Turbos, but there is a small catch where the metal needle slides onto the interchangeable cords. It doesn\xE2\x80\x99t catch the knitting when sliding down the needle onto the cables, but it did when sliding the stitches off the cable and back onto the needles. This ended up felting my mohair yarn together in places. Not a problem if you are a perfect knitter, but I sometimes have to tink or unkit. This was a problem for me.

Once I found Nena Galati\xE2\x80\x99s \xE2\x80\x9CHow to knit socks on 2 circular needles\xE2\x80\x9D DVD, I started using that technique for sleeves instead of DPN\xE2\x80\x99s. You don\xE2\x80\x99t have to worry about dropping stitches or having them slide off a DPN this way.

Although I mostly knit on size 7 needles, once I am committed to a yarn that needs a different gage, I invest ina set of ADDI Lace Turbos. This typically means two ~24 inch circular needles for sleeves, and a longer ~60 inch circular needle for the sweater body (for cardigans, extra length is not a problem). For me at least, knitting is an investment of time and creativity. It is worth the investment in good tools if I am going to invest a significant amount of my time (and also money in yarn). But I am thoughtful about the needle sizes I use. I do create my own sweater patterns or adjust other patterns for the gage and yarn I am using. So I have found I don\xE2\x80\x99t need every size needle there is. I can be selective.

review_headline: Deceiving descriptions and lousy customer service
review_body:
If I could give a rating of zero stars I would! This is NOT a shadow box! While the company claims it is, in both their product name and description, they are telling a big fat lie. This is a frame that has the glass deeply set at the back of a deep border. There is no way you would be able to place any item, other than a piece of paper or a picture in this "shadow box" for safe keeping. Don\x27t bother buying this item. Not only is the item not correctly and honestly advertised the company has lousy customer service. Once I saw what I ordered (which unfortunately, was outside of the 30 day return period) they were unwilling to work with me and deny that they misrepresented their items. They claim they sent me frames which is what I ordered and they claim they clearly describe that is is not a shadow box in their description. After many emails back and forth, I noticed they slightly changed their description trying to cover the butts. However, the name and description are still misleading as they use the words "shadow box"

Here is what they originally used in their verbiage to describe their product. I believe you should all beware of their shadiness before deciding to purchase any items from them!
The item description was listed as this:
"With a slim, simple black frame and stylish, shadow box display, this 5x7" photo frame is perfectly modern. It is equipped with an easel stand for portrait or landscape table top display, and also includes hooks for vertical or horizontal hanging. Smooth lines and basic black make this frame suitable for any room or style. It is a great birthday or wedding gift and a fitting addition to the existing decor of your kitchen or living room."

And the item\x27s name:
"2 of Adeco [PF0035-3] 5"x7" or 7" x 5" Shadow Box - Picture Frame For Wall Hanging & Table Top - Single Photo Decoration"

As you can see, they do not specify that thisis NOT a shadow box, rather then continue referring to it as a shadow box hoping to take advantage of people like myself that believe that is what this is. BEWARE!!

review_headline: Box was smashed - Edited review - Company responded
review_body:
****NOTE***** See below for edited portion of review.

I wasn\x27t terribly thrilled with this purchase. You get what you pay for I suppose. The very small box arrived mangled and smashed but the device seemed to be intact and unharmed in the bubble wrap. It\x27s rather odd because you are able to move the eyepiece up and down to focus on the object you are viewing. However, everything I\x27ve looked at so far (I\x27ve been using mostly to check the nibs on fountain pens) you simply have to put right up against the clear guard at the bottom of the device and the eyepiece just stays bottomed out at the very bottom of it\x27s range of travel. I don\x27t know if the problem is on the inside of the lens or the outside but trying to clean it has had no effect. I do like the unit as the LED light is nice and bright and really helps. I don\x27t know that it\x27s really 45X (I sort of doubt that) but it does offer a fair bit of magnification. At it\x27s current price, it is nothing I\x27d bother to send back since the shipping would obviously be more than the cost of the item. I think I most are probably fine, I just got one that was extremely dirty for some reason.

Edit: 1/29/15

product_title: iRobot Roomba 650 Robot Vacuum
review_headline: Better than doing it yourself.  Better than paying for a cleaning person.
review_body:
We purchased our iRobot Roomba 650 about a 6 weeks ago. My husband and I are transitioning to our second home, so our primary residence was looking a bit dusty due to my lack of time there. I decided we either needed a cleaning company or a Roomba. So far, it has been really helping us keep our place looking neat and tidy. True, it doesn\x27t clean stairs )-: or get into the corners, but if used as a twice weekly touch up after a great cleaning, it is amazing how good it works. I didn\x27t expect much and told my husband to use it as much as possible when he was there in case it was a bust and died after a few uses, but so far so good. I think the way to use this is to move things like cords away from the floor and it will be smooth sailing. During Christmas, it kept knocking our candles off the windows until we raised them a little. It just makes it easier than getting an error message. I have not noticed any marks on furniture or woodwork, but I will look for that. I think a flannel bumper should be included on the Roomba if people are having damage. Wouldn\x27t it be wise for the company to eliminate this problem. Now hoping it has a long life. I will try to remember to update in a few years if it is still working. I have had many brands and other than my current vacuum, my experience is that they have a very short life.

Pros: I don\x27t have to spend all my time at my temporary residence making up for being away so much. I can do other things while it is vacuuming. It can be programmed. It is very small and you can even hide it under furniture if you want to. It does a great job on wood, carpets and tile so far.

Cons: Noisy, but no where near as noisy as my regular vacuum cleaner; not even close. Doesn\x27t do stairs or corners. It can get stuck under things even though it got in there in the first place. It must be cleaned after every use or I see a short life.

product_title: Sizzix 656850 Vagabond Cutting/Embossing Machine, Inspired by Tim Holtz
review_headline: Tim Holtz/Sizzix Vagabond can cause accidents.  Also, if jammed Sizzix says it can\x27t be repaired!
review_body:
My friend and I used her brand new Vagabond and, due to the manufacturer\x27s use of poor color coding of a shim and another piece, she made a sandwich that was just a hair thicker than the machine could handle, resulting in the Vagabond propelling the sandwich pieces from the machine with such force that if either one of us had been in the line of fire we would have ended up in the emergency room. NOWHERE DID IT MENTION IN THE LITERATURE THAT AN ACCIDENT LIKE THAT COULD HAPPEN. A machine of this cost SHOULD have a safety feature as well as better customer service.

Still, due to my own physical disabilities, I ended up buying my own Vagabond because I didn\x27t think I could handle a manual. I figured I was forewarned so would steer clear of the line of fire, and be exra careful. Recently, however, I used the wrong platform. Although the thickness was within limits, the whole sandwich jammed the machine. Almost two hundred dollars down the drain, since neither Tim Holtz nor Sizzix will stand behind their product enough to make a machine that can be repaired even at the customer\x27s expense. No wonder Tim Holtz\x27s YouTube video on the Vagabond doesn\x27t allow comments or ratings. I\x27ve learned my lesson.

By the way, I tried a Cuttlebug, and was relieved to find out that even with three abdominal hernias and arthritis, I was able to use it without a problem. Another pleasant surprise was that it worked easily with thin and intricate dies, whereas my Vagabond could never seem to cut through an entire intricate die. It seemed as though there was always uneveness with the rollers on the Vagabond, even with the use of new cutting plates and experimenting with shims.

product_title: Winsor & Newton Professional Water Color Compact Set
review_body:
The packaging has been updated so it\x27s not exactly as shown, but after double checking with Winsor and Newton, everything is in order and the package arrived in perfect condition! Note that the packaging it comes in is now silver and white instead of green and is labeled "Professional" watercolor instead of just "Artists\x27 " watercolor. The pans do not have individual foil labels on them as shown, they arrive individually wrapped in clear plastic. Winsor and Newtons customer support confirmed that this is all correct.

It\x27s such a perfect watercolor set. The included waterbottle, with the amount I use, usually lasts me three paint sessions if I pour the cup out afterwards (Since then I\x27ve gotten better at cleaning with the sponge instead of swishing in the water and can reuse the water). The sponge is a great addition, you use it to both clean pigment from brushes and dab the paper to lighten areas and its better than a paper towel in size and cleans without issue. If its full of water, just squeeze it out into the grass or cup if you\x27re indoors.

The pigments are vivid and go a long way with just a little paint. They mix well. The brush is very tiny, so I\x27d recommend getting a Da Vinci 1523 Russian Red Sable Round size 5 portable brush or something to carry along with it. The included brush is maybe a 2, give or take. It works well but is best used in conjunction with a 5 or 6. I use a 5x8.25 moleskine watercolor album [EDIT: I don\x27t like my moleskine as much as my plain Strathmore 400 series watercolor sketchbook. The paper is super thin in moleskine, good for light washes but not layers at all] and those two brushes work for just about everything, but I use more when I\x27m at my desk.

If you\x27re new and wondering whether you should spend twice the money of the Cottman colors, get what you can afford but lean towards these ones. I haven\x27t compared them in depth, but the professional quality ones seem to be a better and the pans last a bit longer. Get yourself a good watercolor sketchbook too, and perhaps some sakura pigma micron pens and a gelly roll white pen and you can do anything. Don\x27t be afraid to use up your supplies, you learn a lot from using them often.

Overall this is a perfect set for doing watercolor on the go. I got them so I wouldn\x27t have an excuse not to watercolor wherever I went. I do it in class, too. product_title: Seville Classics 40-Bottle Birchwood Wine Rack
review_body: In three different orders. I now have four units of this rack. FedEx is the mode of shipping. All the parts were in perfect condition.  There was never any damage due to manufacture or shipment. The quality of the unit is very high.  The birchwood that the unit is made of is completely without any blemish.  The pieces are straight which helps the assembly without additional stress on the way it comes together.  The unit is about 20 pounds each.  It is pretty heavy because birch is a hardwood.  The assembly is nearly idiot proof.  Make sure that the vertical pieces have the counter-sunk screw holes facing out and that the bottle slatts are all facing up.  The screws are massive and very long.  My electric drill-style screwdriver was not able to take all the screws all the way in so I had to touch up with a large high quality hand screwdriver.  My units did not come with a bit that is supposed to be the tool for the screws and supposed to be included.  I have the right bit in my drill set so it didn\x27t matter to me.  It took about 20 minutes to put each one together.  The strength is very good.  The strength of birch gives the needed strength and rigidity to the over 30" of span across.  There are also screwed in feet on the bottom of all four of the vertical pieces so the unit could be leveled.  The unit also comes with four pins that may be screwed onto the bottom of the vertical pieces for the unit to sit on top of another one.  It is recommended to not stack more than two units in total (one over another).  Overall, I like this unit for the quality of the wood, the design and how it fits together and the compact profile.  One final comment is that the slots are large enough for up to Burgundy bottles (or standard Chardonnay and Pinot Noir).  These placed one next to another will work but they will pretty much touch each other.  Anything larger will not work.  That includes Champagne and the larger specialty Burgundies, Chardonnays or Pinot Noirs.  Also, the bottome upon where this unit will rest would be open and tall enough for miscellaneous storage including another layer of bottles.  That will work for your larger bottles but they will just be resting on the open space.  Of all the units of this style, I have found this to be the best.

review_headline: A fun DIY solar ventilation kit.
review_body: Solar ventilation:  This is a small DIY kit to add solar powered ventilation.  I received a solar panel, wire and a fan. At the very least you will need a soldering iron, solder and a wire stripper to build your kit. I decided to take it a bit further than that and add crimp on connectors between the fan and solar panel. I also added Velcro to the back of the solar panel so I could move it to follow the sun if needed.  The outlet on the fan is 5/8\x5C\x22 by 1/2\x5C\x22.  I like to both craft and refurbish small parts and items yet I do not like to breathe the chemicals that can be involved in that process like solvents and glues. I had the idea to build my ventilator into a plastic storage organizer so I could put small parts and items in it while they \x5C\x22off gas\x5C\x22 solvents or glues and such. For example, I can glue two parts to each other, place the newly glued/repaired item in the plastic organizer, and take the organizer outside or put it on a window sill and let the glue fumes all vent outside.  The repaired item is protected in the organizer from wind and such and I am protected from the fumes. I used a large grommet to line a hole I drilled in one side of the organizer for the fresh air inlet. I made a rectangular hole for the fan outlet. The solar panel is attached with Velcro to the outside of the organizer.    All in all I am happy with the kit.  Being that the fan outlet is 1/2\x5C\x22 x 5/8\x5C\x22 I am a bit skeptical about its use to ventilate a large structure like garage or attic (although I have not tried it yet)  but it is very nice for small projects. Either way, I figure with it mounted to the organizer I can move it to any window sill for testing, venting fumes or for venting whatever space the organizer is in.  I had fun building my kit.  I received my kit free in exchange for doing a review and I was absolutely free to write anything I wanted.  My pictures really tell the story...

product_title: Prolux LED Upright Sealed H-Grade HEPA Allergen Pet Vacuum
review_headline: Solid choice that could be even better
review_body:
Even though this isn\x27t a well-known brand, I took a chance on this vacuum based on all of the reviews. It\x27s a good vacuum though I think the reviews are slightly overrated. Overall it\x27s a good machine, but there are definitely some flaws to be mindful of.

Pros:
- Very well built / solid / sturdy. Definitely not plasticky and junky like other vacuums
- Color & finish are gorgeous
- Good performance on carpet (suction, agitation, fluffing)
- Metal components where it counts
- LED headlights are bright and should last a long time

Cons:
- Poor performance on hard floors. I mostly have carpet in my home, but this was pretty ineffective on my kitchen tile. Didn\x27t suck up well at all. Brush roll on/off switch would help.
- Limited range of recline. Couldn\x27t get it underneath my coffee table which isn\x27t especially low. Like most vacuums, you can use the foot pedal to recline it more than the first stop, but it barely went much lower until the power head started to lift up.
- Bulky head made it difficult to get all the way under kitchen cabinet baseboards
- After only a few times vacuuming, I could hear the belt start to slip on the back stroke. Doesn\x27t bode well for long-term.
- Wanted the cord to be longer

Neutral:
- Noise level is decent. Well-controlled, but not the quietest vacuum I\x27ve ever heard like some reviews lead you to believe
- Weight is in the middle. Certainly not light, but not too heavy either. And a little weight doesn\x27t bother me considering the build quality.
- Filtration was one of the big selling points for me. Seems to do a good job filtering, but my allergies would still act up a bit when vacuuming with it. The HEPA filter is pre-motor, and I think that a post-motor HEPA filter is better for allergy sufferers. Less sensitive folks should be ok.

product_title: Ultimate Dreams Shredded Talalay Latex Pillow
review_headline: knowing that I would probably like one better than the other
review_body:
This pillow was not at ALL what it appears to be in the advertisement, nor in many of the positive reviews. I don\x27t have much to add that the negative reviews haven\x27t already said, but i will reiterate it, and affirm them, as, I spent a lot of time reading reviews of various pillows and finally settled on this one AND the "Simmons Beautyrest Authentic Talalay Latex Foam Firm Support Queen Pillow", knowing that I would probably like one better than the other. I liked the IDEA of the shredded latex, but that is where it ends.

First, the pillow is ridiculously under filled for the case it is in. we are talking less than half full. When laid flat/spread out evenly inside the case, it rises less than 2 inches. To give you an idea of how under filled it is, when received, it was rolled up and stuffed in a plastic bag with a diameter of less than 5.5 inches. THE ENTIRE PILLOW. I think for a shredded latex pillow to work, it needs to be filled tightly for the case it is in. That doesn\x27t mean over filled. It means don\x27t put that amount of filling in a "queen" sized case. When rolled up/the filling pushed together to make an appropriate loft for anyone, it was mildly comfortable. But i wanted a "queen" sized comfortable pillow, not a loaf of bread sized comfortable pillow.

Oh, on another note, as said, i also got a different latex pillow that had virtually no smell, while this pillow most definitely had a very distinct rubber smell. I honestly probably wouldn\x27t have cared if it was filled appropriately. I would certainly like to try another shredded latex pillow, but now I\x27m afraid to buy online because of this.

Also, luckily, I am happy with the other pillow i mentioned above that I purchased at the same time. I was turned off by some of the reviews that were saying it has too high of a loft and is like sleeping on a balloon. Although it is "bouncy", it is not as dramatic as you might be thinking. I\x27d go with a "solid" piece latex pillow, unless you can trust a properly filled shredded one.

product_title: AcuRite 01121M Vertical Wireless Color Weather Station (Dark Theme) with Temperature Alerts
review_headline: A real eye catcher of a weather station.
review_body: I\x27ve waited a few weeks to review this so I could comment on the forecast abilities.  I really like the display, layout, color and the information provided.  The indoor AND outdoor min/max on both the temp and humidity have come in handy on several occasions and the direction of change I use regularly.  I paid a little extra to get a model that had the actual barometric pressure reading displayed and not just the pictorial forecast and I\x27m glad I did.  I find the accuracy of the pictorial forecast to be questionable and I\x27ve even reset/restarted the "learning" mode to see if it helped.  Not so much, but hey, it\x27s probably as accurate as the weather people.  The pictorial forecast does follow the changes in the barometric pressure, so it is useful in that regard.  The display is fantastic and is really an eye catcher with the color scheme they use.  One thing to note is if the display is sitting above eye level, the brightness is lower than if you are looking at a down angle to the display.  This is not necessarily because of the Autodim or the brightness setting, but does make it a little difficult to see if you have it located above eye level and it\x27s either Autodim/low or you keep is set on low.  This wouldn\x27t be an issue at all if you were able to adjust the tilt of the display.  I have mine leaning slightly forward to resolve this.  It does what it is suppose to, I use it many times a day and would gladly buy it again.

product_title: Honeywell Cool Moisture Console Humidifier
review_body: Received the humidifier yesterday and the item arrived well packed and without container damage.  This is a good size humidifier and the wheels are quite handy.  Upon taking the packaging from the humidifier I read the instructions and soaked the filter in cold water as the unit was assembled.  There isn\x27t much to do except to put the wheels on the base and unwrap the electrical cord.  One thing that did concern me was that the fan motor/blower side of the humidifier, with the controls on top, just sits on the base and doesn\x27t feel solid to me.  The two water containers, when filled and in place, help to keep things in place but I feel the design is lacking in solidity in this area.  The containers are easy to fill but you have to hold the container where you want it in the sink throughout the fill process of the container will fall over.  If you forget to put the water treatment in the container before you fill it...well, let\x27s say that is interesting.  One other thing:  I had read that this humidifier can be noisy and mine is, especially on medium and high fan speeds.  Last night the unit was run on low fan speed and, along with an ongoing "rising bubble" sound each time the water container released water into the base, the unit was irritating at times due, I feel, to the motor/control filter cover moving on the base.  I could place my hand on the filter cover at various locations and quiet the unit down for awhile.  Eventually the noise would become louder though; just loud enough to draw one\x27s attention to the humidifier.  I would think the humidifier, set on Low fan speed, should emit little more than a moving air sound.  If not for the rather flimsy filter cover to base design and the noise I would have given this unit a much higher rating in my review.  Nevertheless, I\x27ll run the humidifier for awhile and see how the unit performs over a week or so.  Almost forgot:  There is no digital humidity readout on this unit so you will need of obtain a hydrometer if you want to obtain that information.

review_headline: Doesn\x27t work, pilot won\x27t stay lit
review_body: I\x27ve been using a Mr Heater for years in my shop as an adjunct to the expensive electric wall heater in the winter. I decided to upgrade to this newer model because it is larger but mainly because it also has a fan to circulate the heat. I unpacked it, hooked it up the the 15\x27 hose and filter from the 20lb bottle outside, pushed the knob down to light the pilot, held it 30-40 seconds and released the knob - the pilot went out. I repeated the sequence, holding for varying lengths of time, until finally taping the knob down for 15 minutes to completely purge the hose of any possible air and to make sure the thermocouple was heated sufficiently - pilot went out as soon as the knob was released. I removed the filter and repeated - still went out. Tried a portable bottle in place of the hose - still went out. I re-installed the old Mr Heater and it worked immediately, and, since the hose had been disconnected I expected I might have to hold the knob down and repeatedly use the igniter while the air was purged but it lit right up and stayed lit, showed some signs of air burning off (slight orange flame among the predominately blue) for only a few seconds. Returned the \x5C\x22new, improved\x5C\x22  item. It\x27s possible this is just a defective model and a replacement might work fine but that level of quality control (they DO test each one before shipping, right?) makes me think I\x27ll just settle for a refund instead.

I have not knit with those tips, but logic tells you the yarn is going to slip into that little opening and snag. review_headline: Privacy for apartment dwellers, easy to install
review_body:
I bought this to cover the sliding portion of my first-floor apartment\x27s sliding glass door. It\x27s a real pain to adjust the blinds to exit and enter the apartment, so I leave them pulled and closed over the stationary part of the door and now I\x27ve covered the other half with this translucent film. During the day, passers by can\x27t see into my apartment at all, whether the lights are on or not. At night, people can see shapes and colors, but nothing distinct. It\x27s safe to do streak from the bathroom to the bedroom with no one the wiser.

I recommend taping the plastic over the window before installing it. Leave it hanging for a few days so the pastic relaxes after having been tightly rolled for shipping. Don\x27t obsess about cutting the plastic perfectly before installation. I taped the top left corner of my window and made sure the left side and top of the plastic were square in the window frame. Keep in mind that your window might not be perfectly square. Mine isn\x27t. Once I had it taped in place, I ran a Sharpie down the right side of plastic, tracing the wood window frame, not the glass. In other words, I purposely made the mark wider than the glass. Do not worry too much about straight lines. Make an effort, but don\x27t obsess. Then I took the pladtic down, removed the tape (packing tape), and cut the pkastic along my Sharpie line using regular ol\x27 scissors. I cleaned the inside of the window (I recommend pre-moistened Windex towelettes for glass because the cloths are lint free.) I filled a spray bottle with water and added a drop of Dawn dish detergent. I sprayed the inside of the window very thouroughly (well coated, but not dripping). Then i peeled back the thin protective film on the smooth side of tbe plastic, but just the first 18 inches or so. I placed that top left corner of yhe plastic into the top left corner of the window and made sure that the entire top was flush with the window glass. Again, don\x27t worry about the overhang on the right side. Once I had that area how I wanted it, I removed the next bit of protective film. Just leave it hang; no need to cut the protective film. I worked my way down the window and had to lift up the plastic a few times to make sure it was still flush with the frame on the lefy. It\x27s fine to reposition the plastic and also to respray the window with tge water/Dawn mixture if it dries out. OnceI had the plastic how I wanted it, I grabbed a plastic pancake turnet (spatula) from the kitchen and worked the bubbles out from under the plastic, starting from the top left and working my way to the bottom right. I still have a few bubbles under the plastic. They\x27re not easy to spot and if they bug me, I just use my fingers to guide them to the right. To deal with that overhanging edge, I carefully ran a razor knife down the plastic, using the window frame as my guide. I havea coulple of areas I want to clean up a little, so I\x27ve kept the razor knife nearby to make small cuts. It\x27s obvious to no one but me that the edge coukd be straighter.

I\x27m glad I bought plastic with a small geometric pattern, and nit the large sqare pattern I\x27d been considering. As I mentioned, my window isn\x27t quite square and my installation method is partly free form. Any small mistake would have been magnified if I\x27d chosen the large squares. I recommend choosing a pattern with a small repeat, like this one, or else a randomized pattern so any installation errors aren\x27t obvious.

My husband runs warm and I\x27m always cold with this blanket we both sleep comfortably regardless of mild or cold weather. Our toddler is also sleeping better with the wool blanket and I like that it is washable.

My one complaint is the plastic storage bag. Pendleton is appealing to eco conscious consumers with the eco-wool blanket\x27s cradle-to-cradle certification. I wish a little more care was extended to safer, quality packaging of the product itself. The blanket comes in a thin, zippered blanket bag made of #4 plastic with a large warning sticker: "This packaging may contain a chemical known to the state of California to cause birth defects or reproductive harm." One blanket bag we received is not functional because the seam where the fabric and plastic meet came undone. This is a minor issue but I could see where it could be problematic to someone seeking natural products due to chemical sensitivity or concerns.

product_title: Vornado Evap3 Whole Room Evaporative Humidifier
review_headline: Take it for what it\x27s worth, but this was my choice
review_body: Spent the weekend researching humidifiers to replace the \x5C\x22White Powder Ultrasonic Humidifier\x5C\x22 that I had previously.  Although the ultrasonics appear to be putting out a lot of moisture, the dust that they create (especially on my TV screen and stand) was very annoying.  I was looking at the disc type \x5C\x22Air Washer\x5C\x22 and the Steam type, along with the Wick type (as this vornado evaporative model).  I couldn\x27t justify spending $250 on a humidifier, even though they promise low energy usage and no replacement parts (as wicks).  I watched the YouTube video on cleaning one of the air washer models and it seemed like a major process.  The steam type model (also $250) uses about 450-800 watts! Yikes!  Although I\x27ve only had the Vornado for a couple of weeks, It appears to be very easy to clean, it only uses about 18-50 watts while running (Less than a Kilowatt/day, Set at 45% humidity with the fan set to \x5C\x22Auto\x5C\x22.  I verified the wattage using the Kill-A-Watt metering device for 2 days).  The hygrometer control is consistent with 2 standalone hygrometers that I have.  The fan sound doesn\x27t bother me at all as I have it set up in my living room/kitchen areas (I have a forced hot air heating system, you should hear that fan).  It took a day or 2 to come up to low run times, but once the humidity evened out the fan has been running on low, or shutting off as expected.  You don\x27t actually see any moisture coming out of the unit as with the ultrasonics, but the hygrometers and the water usage verify that the unit provides the desired humidity levels.  I fill it once daily and use the bacteriostatic water treatment. I only expect to have two wick changes per season (based on previous reviews). I\x27m looking at a total operating cost of less than $50 per heating season (Wicks $25, Water treatment $5, Electricity $15). I think that is a low price to pay for comfort.  I\x27m very happy with my purchase.

product_title: Hopewell Lace Kitchen Curtain
review_body:
I so badly want to leave a 5 star review for these. I love them! They are soft and the off white color is the perfect shade. I bought two 63" panels and as other reviewers have stated, the length is somewhat inaccurate. My panels differ in length by about 1.5 inches.

They were wrinkle free and ready to hang right out of the package. I wanted to hang them inside my window frame as privacy panels since I have room darkening curtains as my full length panels. I wanted curtains that I could still see out of and these work perfectly since there is no mesh between the lace detail. You cannot see through them from the outside during the day which is what I wanted. I purchased 1.5 inch tension rods to initially hang these with and the pocket was too small for them. If you are using a tension rod, I wouldn\x27t get anything larger than 1".

Overall, I would recommend these to anyone even though the length is wonky. With a basic stitch in the sewing machine it was an easy fix.

review_body:
Makes a robust, flavorful cup of coffee that rivals my Aeropress. Easy to use and easy to clean. Worst part of the process is waiting the 5 or 6 minutes for the coffee to finishing brewing.

I was concerned about any french press letting a large amount of coffee grinds through, but this press has done a fantastic job filtering. I use a coarse coffee grind, as suggest by most of the online French Press tutorials. The grind size is often described as breadcrumb like. The grind of typical grocery store pre-ground coffee is too fine for you french press but is ideal for your counter top drip coffee makers. They have a much shorter steep time and paper filters.

I\x27m only giving the product 4 stars because it arrived with a portion of the metal screen bent the opposite way as the rest of the screen. I was able to bend it back, but there is still a small crease that allows unfiltered liquid through.

product_title: Tzou Cube Wood LED Alarm Clock - Time Temperature Date - Sound Control - Latest Generation
review_body:
Let me begin by saying I loved this clock the first two weeks I had it. It was cute and little, and it wasn\x27t backlit by an annoying, colored light. I wasn\x27t even bothered by the fact that the power cord was three feet long, or that it didn\x27t come with a USB adapter. I even ignored how annoyingly bright it was at night. I was evenconsidering buying another one for another room.

And then, I woke up one morning to see that the clock read "9:00" instead of "8:00". What? At first, I thought daylight savings time had crept up on me, but my phone said "8:00". A power outage wouldn\x27t have explained it either, as the time would have just reset back to "12:00", not skipped an hour. When I went to manually change it back I realized it hadn\x27t changed at all. The internal clock was still set to the right time, but part of the light had stopped displaying. It had only been two weeks. It has sat safely on my dresser the whole time, and without kids or pets, I know it hasn\x27t been damaged. When I bought this, I was wary because it had few reviews. I have learned my lesson. I guess something can be "cheap", even if you end up forking over twenty dollars for it.

product_title: Testors Complete Airbrush/Compressor System
review_headline: Not Bad for an Intro Unit
review_body:
I\x27m writing this to balance out the ratings a bit, because my experience is completely different than the other reviewers. I don\x27t show up as a verified purchaser because I didn\x27t buy mine through Amazn, but I used one successfully for years. My kids use it now, and it still works fine. Contrary to what some cynics are thinking, I have no affiliation with either Testors or RPM, it\x27s corporate parent.

So let\x27s get down to it. First off, dare I suggest it, some negative reviews are probably the result of purchasers not having the faintest idea how to actually use an airbrush. I had to take a class -- six hours -- on how to operate one, how to clean one, and how to paint with one. Trust me, it\x27s not intuitive. Testors includes a double action airbrush with this set, which is a questionable decision (one reason for the one star deduction). Yes, you can get much better control of your paint flow with a double action, but they\x27re harder to use. But such basics as frequent wiping of the nozzle tip and periodic cleaning / purging while in use are fundamentals that greatly improbe performance of any airbrush. When using acrylic paints, I run a cup (the paint cups thst come with it, not a measuring cup) of soapy water through it for every two cups of paint. Just like painting with a bristle brush, keeping your brush clean is an essential part of producing good results. I\x27ve never had the compressor overheat and shut down, even during sessions lasting half an hour or more, and trust me, that\x27s an eternity with an airbrush.

My only other marks against this system involve the bundled equipment. The nozzles that come with it are poorly selected and not labelled at all, so that I had to go to the Testors website to figure out what was what. And the set needs to include more paint cups. It only came with 3, one large and two small, and since you need one per color, plus one for cleaning, you basically have to go buy more cups immediately if youintend to use more than one color at a time. And this is one reason to love this set. To change colors, simply remove the cup with the first color, wipe the nozzle, run some soapy water through it, and inset the cup with the second color. The inclusion of a cleaning station is a definite plus. You don\x27t want to airbrush without ine.

review_headline: Works OK...but read the directions and use COMMON SENSE
review_body:
Bought 2 queen sets after asking about putting them on adjustable beds since we have Sleep Number beds on adjustable frames.....come to find out that the instructions recommend NOT USING ON ADJUSTBLE BEDS. Reason is obvious as adjutables usually have a metal post at the end to keep the bed from sliding off....well it is right were the electrcal cord attaches to the mattress pad. So if you do use it on an adjustable DO NOT ADJUST THE LOWER PORTION and only raise the top portion enough to sleep comfortably but not up enough to scrunch the wires in the pad. Instructions worn agains scrunching or bending internal wires both for the pad, throws, and blankets. An alternative is to switch the pad and put the electrical section on the upper section but make sure you don\x27t rub up agains the wall as you will tear the cord out as the clipps are only pastic.

Also, the instructions tell you the pad is machine washable but warns against spilling liquids on your bed. I assume the the bed warning is because you have the thing hoooked up and plugged in. Have not tried washing it yet....but as a veterance of electroncis for over 40 years....wash and test BEFORE you put it on the bed for use would be my advise....

Finally I bought this as I hate to sleep with blankets and quilts on but living in Alaska can get a little chilly in the winter or very expensive in heating....so I bought it to sleep on so that I get radiate head to back and muscels with only a light sheet.....it works very good and i use setting 2 or 3....if you do like quilts and blankets then unless you like to sweat....it is an old trick to just use a light blanket, place it under your top fitted sheet, and let your body heat keep your down side warm.....

product_title: Kirby Sentria Upright Vacuum
review_body:
I\x27m in the process of starting my commercial carpet cleaning business with about 80-hours of learning under my belt. Kirby came by to offer me a demo and I wanted to see what it was capable of so I accepted!

Needless to say I was a little worn out by the sales process that has been mentioned before. I got an abbreviated version by instructing the gentleman to not waste his time instructing me on how carpet cleaning works.

That being said, this vacuum is AWESOME! Holy cow, it picked up a disturbing amount of dirt after I ran my personal vacuum. I would recommend the vacuum to anybody looking for the best on the market. This thing blows Dyson away with no question!

But please, seriously, do not buy in to the temporary lightening and fluffing of the carpet left by the shampoo mechanism. The shampoo feature is a complete joke. About an hour after the sales guy left I stuck my nose to the floor and it wreaked! It obviously left a ton of residue but, more importantly, seemed to revive the smell of previous stains. I had to fire up my commercial equipment to do a rinse cycle in order to soften the fibers back up and get it fresh.

I didn\x27t buy the machine as I take the sales pitch seriously that Kirby\x27s tend to out-live their owners. I found a refurbished Kirby vacuum with vacuum attachments, previous model, for $250 with free shipping on e-bay! It will perform just as well for 1/5th the cost of a new one. Do I have the warranty? No. But I\x27m expecting a baby and can\x27t affort $1,000+ for a vacuum cleaner!

product_title: Hoover Vacuum Cleaner WindTunnel Air Bagless Corded Canister Vacuum SH40070
review_headline: Good with a powered Brush Head
review_body:
Vacuums, amiright? So many to choose from, so many compromises, so many gimmicks, and all for something I don\x27t even want to use anyway... and they never last!

I want what everybody wants - something that makes cleaning easy, and that means it actually cleans, and cleans as many surfaces as possible as easily as possible. AND, I\x27ve decided not to go for broke and buy one of the ridiculously expensive models because they seem to break just as often as the ordinarily expensive ones. Also, I want a bagless model, as the last thing I want to do is EVER run out of bags.

Enter the the Hoover Wind Tunnel Bagless Cannister...
REASONS TO BUY:
1. Price is right
2. Cannister style (preferred by my housekeeper and easier on the arms than a heavy upright)
3. Bagless
4. Powered Bush-Head (and other useful tools)
5. Wind-tunnel design with HEPA filters.

The early results are in and I think this is a pretty great vacuum. The power-brush-head is something that seems to be harder and harder to find, especially in this price-range. A lot of other models and brands feature a carpet-head, but it spins the brush with only suction-power and I have found that inferior to a truly mechanized brush that really beats the dust out of your rugs.

Everything works well and is very ergonomic - the extension wand is sturdy and the the whole unit seems well-made. It took me a few minutes to figure out how to dissemble the dust canister (you need to empty the inner filter as well and it\x27s kind of hidden in there), but once it was back together it snapped right back into place.

I have yet to have a problem with overheating as a few other people have mentioned (which worried me), but I do agree that the extension cord is shorter than I would like. However, the auto-rewind works very well. I really like that the rewind and power buttons are both foot-operated (big buttons that you step on) and that saves my back a bit. Also, there\x27s a notch that lets you stand the wand up when you\x27re not using it and saves the thing from crashing to the floor. There\x27s a strange three-way attachment for corners and curtains that is a little odd - you flip it around and pull it open to use different features. I\x27d rather have separate tools, but these work fine.

I hope this is the last vacuum I ever buy, or at least it lasts long enough for the next revolution in cleaning to come along.a bit. product_title: AcuRite 00613 Humidity Monitor with Indoor Thermometer, Digital Hygrometer and Humidity Gauge Indicator
review_body:
OVERVIEW:
After receiving the Honeywell Germ Free Humidifier (http://www.amazon.com/Honeywell-Germ-Free-Humidifier-HCM-350/dp/B002QAYJPO/) for Christmas, I needed a way to see just how much humidity was being pumped into my apartment. Apparently that\x27s known as a hygrometer, and the all signs pointed to this little device.

PROS:
\xE2\x80\xA2 Price -- At $9, this is easily the most affordable hygrometer on the market. I never thought I\x27d be looking for an affordable hygrometer, but here I am
\xE2\x80\xA2 Features -- Not only will it tell you how much humidity is in your place, but it will also tell you the temperature, and show you the high / low humidity / temp for the past week. Plus, it gives you an easy low / OK / high rating for the level of your humidity in relation to the temperature
\xE2\x80\xA2 Magnetic Stand -- You can either stick this thing to a magnetic surface (i.e. your fridge) or just have it stand like a picture on your table / counter / other flat surface
\xE2\x80\xA2 Size -- It\x27s shorter & a little thicker than a standard deck of cards. Pretty nondescript

CONS:
\xE2\x80\xA2 Build Quality -- The clip on the back of my unit wasn\x27t connected all the way, and when I tried to snap it in place, it broke. It still stands, but it would not be flush against a magnetic surface if I used it that way.
\xE2\x80\xA2 LCD Screen -- It\x27s easy to read if you\x27re looking at it straight on in a bright room. From any other angle, you\x27re better off picking it up and putting it front of your face.
\xE2\x80\xA2 Minimum Humidity -- The instructions said the minimum humidity it could read was something like 18%, so if your place is less humid than that, you\x27re probably living in a desert cave and don\x27t need a device to tell you that your place is less humid than 18%

BOTTOM LINE:
Again, for the price, you\x27re not going to find an easier, more full-featured device to measure the humidity in your domicile. The build quality feels cheap, but at under $10, I\x27ll take those trade offs.

product_title: Dyson AM05 Hot + Cool Fan Heater
review_body:
Well now thanks to Dyson I have a solution to my hot and cold office, the Dyson AM 05 hot + Cool fan. I cannot say enough about how much I love that I can have just one small sleek product to solve my crazy weather problems in my office. With just a flip of a switch I can stay cool in the Summer and warm in the Winter.

Features:

Energy efficient - 30% less energy is used to heat the whole room than other fan heaters and it can lower energy bills by 20% when used with air conditioning.
Precise temperature control - You can set the target temperature to exactly what you\x27d like in heat mode (an intelligent thermostat will even keep it there) and the airflow, oscillation and temperature can all be adjusted with the remote.
Remote storage - The remote can be stored on top of the machine via magnets so you don\x27t loose it if you don\x27t need it. I love that there is a spot for the remote since I don\x27t really need it but don\x27t want to loose it either.
Safe - this is a huge plus for me since fast-spinning blades freak me out with my kids around. This fan does not contain any blades or visible heating elements and it even automatically turns off if its tipped over.
No burning smell
Easy to clean - since there are no blades or grille plate it is easy to wipe down any dust off it.
2 year warranty on parts and labor.

The problem I have had with other heaters I have tried is they shoot in one direction only so I have to position them just right in order to heat the area I\x27m in. I absolutely love how this heater can be oscillating so it can blow the whole right either hot or cold. This way if I move about in the room it still works and it is also nice so I don\x27t have it consistently blowing on me if I don\x27t want. The design looks great in my office and its lightweight enough I can easily move it as needed. It is super easy control as you just push a few buttons for the temperature, power level and if you want it to move or not. Yes you can stick your hand through it too, no blades! I would recommend this for anyone looking for an amazing fan + heater all in one, especially for parents who are worried about their kids little hands!o move or not. review_body:
I make and sell greeting cards to benefit our local libraries and these two embossing folders add a nice dimension to the background of my A2 (5.5\x5C\x22 x 4.25\x5C\x22) card faces. They are both non-thematic, so can be used with any type of card. The \x27burlap\x27 folder embosses a pattern that looks like lizard hide.

I create the raised pattern on cardstock by running the cardstock and embossing folder through my Cuttlebug machine. I either leave the raised pattern uncolored or else use a cosmetic sponge and an ink pad to dab color on the raised portion. Chalk could also be used, but you would probably want to use a sealant to keep the chalk from migrating off of the card surface.

product_title: Kurt Adler 1-Light Metal Star Treetop
review_body:
This is a very nice and solid tree topper; all metal. The edge is a golden wire and the flats are some kind of very fine metal mesh decorated with glitter and more golden wire. Very pretty!

I am not a big fan of plastic or cold led light. I was very happy to find this star. It give me a warm feeling very time I look at the tree top.

The size is 7.5" wide and 11" tall measured from ray-tip to ray-tip. I have a 6\x27 narrow tree and the star\x27s dimensions are just perfect for it. The star has a clam-shell design with identical back and front pieces, light up by a single light bulb in the center.

The power cord is a design flaw to modern standards. This might have been a typical design 100 years ago - I am not sure.
It is a white cord and plug, so it does blend in with the tree. The plug is polarized and does not fit into a regular light chain plug. It is too short to reach any outlet without an extension cord.

I could have taken a point off for the power cord, but the star is so pretty that I am simply going to overlook it.

product_title: Handmade Indian 54\x22 Square Tablecloth - Red, Green and Yellow Floral Cotton
review_body:
So, this was a gift for my mother, who has not had a new tablecloth in years and is incredibly hard to buy for during the holidays. Most of these are her observations as the gift recipient:

*The product does not look at pretty in the package as it does opened up. I called her the day she opened her gift to make sure she liked this tablecloth design so I could exchange/return it if she didn\x27t. I bought this particular design because it had some of the MANY colors she has going on in her dining room. Apparently when the item is folded, it gives the appearance of a somewhat less appealing design? Her first response was a bit non-committal and a little confusing... "it\x27s ok...did YOU like it?" Not so reassuring for someone who wanted to wow my mom with something I thought was a creative gift. I finally had to send her a picture of the product from Amazon to show her why I had thought it would work for her. She finally opened it after that conversation and said flatly, that it was "pretty." I\x27m not convinced by her tone, but will take it at face value.

*The material is quite "delicate and by delicate, I mean thin." She said it wasn\x27t your typical thicker tablecloth that isn\x27t see-thru. She likened the material to the thickness of the lightweight scarves she used to purchase from Asia. She wasn\x27t completely disappointed by the thin material, but mentioned she planned to buy a piece of white cloth from a fabric store to put underneath to really "protect" her table.

*A big positive, in my book, is that this company seems to be one of the very few that offers a smaller square tablecloth. So many companies quit at just producing a 60" square, which leaves some seriously long overhang on small tables that are becoming more popular for apartment living. Kudos on offering an alternative and this is one big reason I considered this tablecloth. My mom said it has a perfect length of overhang on her small table...not too long, not too short. I believe her table is a 38 or 39" square.

*From my personal experience, I can say the item was received quickly and that the seller is very good about following up to ensure you are happy with the product...once purchased. I DID however, ask a question on the item prior to purchase and never received an answer. You might have better luck with questions from someone who has reviewed the item, rather than trying to contact the seller prior to purchase.

*The price on this particular color combo was nearly twice the price of many of the other "tablecloth only" sold in this size by this seller (many of which were just as "decorative" but not in the colors I was looking for). I have no idea if that had to do with the specific color(s) or what. Knowing what I know now about the material, I would have definitely bought one of the ones that was $17 or $18 and bought her two for some variety AND for the fact that thin material often wears more quickly, had color not been an issue. Just a thought for future orders.

Overall...I wouldn\x27t say the purchase was a complete loss, but a non-commital "just so-so" gift is just OKAY at this price...thus the 3-stars. product_title: Modern Bamboo Weighing Body Scale 2016 Product 400 Pounds Wood Decor for Bath, Kitchen and Living Room
review_headline: Pretty, but the number is more what you call guidelines, than actual measurement
review_body:
Looks lovely in my bathroom - doesn\x27t show footprint smudges or dust like a glass scale. Looks like something you would find at a spa. Not particularly great construction - the feet of the scale under the wood platform are plastic. Not sure how it would hold up to heavy strain. So far so good, but ... the point of a scale is to give a measurement and I have to take the numbers with a grain of salt. How you stand on this thing makes a difference. If you shift your weight forward or backward you can easily tweak your number + or - a few pounds. Now I find myself stepping on it and trying for my "thin" weight, which is super silly. "No no, I stood on it too forward, let me try again ..."

If you are maintaining your weight it probably won\x27t bug you to see your number vary a little. If you are trying to lose weight it may frustrate you very much. I would not recommend it for recording weight loss.

I kept mine because I am more or less okay with a roundabout measurement. It is pretty.

review_body:
Let me just say, "I had eight black cotton or cotton/poly blend shirts with underarm sweat and deodorant stains that were hard and crusty."
Needless to say they were unwearable. I liked the shirts so I kept them.
Thought I\x27d take a chance and try Deo-Go.... After a couple applications I figured out a process that worked for me.
Apply liberally on stain, scrub vigorously with a stiff bristled brush, let sit for at least 30 minutes and make sure the areas do not dry up. Reapply as needed but keep them moist. then wash normally.
Now I had to do this a couple of times, remember the stains were "crusty and hard"!!!
Ended up with three shirts that were wearable again, no sign of the stains. The others are so close I could probably get away with wearing a couple, but decided to just order more Deo-Go and finish the job!!!
Very happy with the outcome!!!

review_body:
I move around in my sleep a lot, so I wake up in the morning with MAJOR bed head. I will go to bed with neatly combed hair and wake up looking like a beast. I researched various methods to combat bed head and one of them was sleeping on silk or satin pillowcase. Since I started using this pillowcase, I no longer wake up with crazy hair!

With a normal cotton pillowcase, when you move your head, your hair doesn\x27t move with your head, so you end up with bed head. With a silk or satin pillowcase, your hair glides with your head, so you don\x27t get bed head.

I recommend this pillowcase to anyone who wants healthier hair and no more bed head! If you\x27re used to cotton pillowcases, this pillowcase may feel strange to sleep on at first, but you\x27ll get used to it very quickly.

product_title: Welland Chicago Floating Shelf
review_body:
This shelf is a piece of crap.

Now that this is clear, here are some specific problems:
1) It is probably made of MDF, but it is hollow inside. This is useful if you plan to use it as a musical instrument.
2) The plugs for the bottom screws are stickers. Stickers! I gave them to my son.
3) The veneer on the shelf is bad quality, and it is glued on very crudely; This is evident from the side if there is any natural light in the room.
4) The anchors provided are crap, even for a drywall. Recycle them with the plastic and make sure you get some solid anchors, unless you plan to use this shelf only for towels or picture frames.

The good things:
5) It has not fallen off the wall, yet.

So overall, the shelf has not fallen off the wall. Which is good thing, but that in itself, I think, is not worth $50. I believe you can find equally crapp shelves for much less on Amazon. I would have given it 1 star, but the sticker plugs gave me a really good laugh, and we had some fun banging rhythms on it before putting it up on the wall.

review_body:
These humidifier filters are not as nice as the ones that are more expensive, but I am still not sure how to judge them against one another. These don\x27t have the reinforcing metal throughout, but there is no physical strain put on teh filter that would require such reinforcement. . . I am really at a loss.

I bought a four-pack to save money, and I still feel gouged for such a simple and seemingly low-tech item. If you like humidifiers, and you want a clean filter, buy a bunch of these and be prepared to change them constantly because they just sit in a small pool of water day in and day out. product_title: Dyson DC59 Animal Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
review_headline: Far better than I\x27d hoped - Excellent vacuum system!
review_body:
I looked at the Dyson DC59 off and on for months before I finally purchased it. I was influenced by the good price available on Amazon and took a chance. I\x27m glad I did! For what I wanted the machine to do, it is exceeding my expectations. I have a large German Shepherd who considers it his duty to fur-coat my house. During the peak shedding seasons it can be really bad - if you\x27re a dog owner you know. So, I needed something for the quick \x5C\x22once around and get the hair balls\x5C\x22 daily cleaning, but also wanted versatility to do stair runners, area rugs, and even entire rooms. The DC59 delivers in fantastic form.

In regular power mode (there is a Turbo mode that I rarely use, because regular power is quite good), you can get every bit of 20 minutes of vacuuming done. And if you get the hang of letting off the trigger when not actually cleaning, you can stretch that for a lot of jobs. The powerhead for floors/carpets is nice and does a great job of both cleaning and grooming the rugs and carpets - even fussy wool area rugs. The bristles in the powerhead seem delicate enough that I have used it on spots of my hardwood floors without much fear or abrasion, but would rather add a bare floor attachment later on for that. The smaller powerhead is ideal for little jobs, curtains/drapes, harder to reach areas between furniture - but it rocks for stairs! Cleaning the stair runners can be a real chore when you don\x27t have the right tool. This tool is perfection for it. Therefore, I do it more often and keep them much cleaner.

I\x27ve never previously owned a Dyson but I have had the bagless type machine in the past and didn\x27t like how hard and messy it was to empty the bin. I won\x27t blow smoke here - there is always mess and hassle with this design, but this Dyson is far better than the previous machine I had. It empties rather easily and has a removable filter that you should clean monthly. I will admit that I like seeing all that dog hair and dust in the clear bin and knowing it\x27s not filling an expensive bag in my other vacuums.

The attachments provided are a great start and for many, all you may need. The powered floor head is awesome, as I said, and small enough to go many places. It\x27s easy to steer and so low you can vacuum under a snake without waking it up. The small powered furniture and stairs head is equally good though rigid in one position. You also get a long extension tube, a crevice tool, and a brush attachment (where the bristles retract if preferred). It also comes supplied with a wall mount that will also charge the unit.

I find that the battery charges fairly rapidly, and even after 15-20 minutes of use, I can plug it in and be ready to go again in an hour or two. The DC59 has much more power than I\x27d have expected for a cordless - and that is without using Turbo. With the Turbo on, you get corded-machine type power - though you will obviously discharge the battery faster.

I had high expectations for the Dyson DC59, and it has met them all and exceeded most. I strongly recommend this Dyson, but it is also important to note a few drawbacks to this (and similar) systems: 1) Canister capacity is small, so you will be emptying it a lot. 2) Suction is not as powerful as corded machines, and sometimes it won\x27t pick up little objects without turbo; 3) Attachments are proprietary and expensive, this comes well equipped - but to add more attachments will cost you; 4) Emptying and cleaning out the canister is a dirty job. If you have allergies don\x27t even think about it. I empty mine in the garage because you will get a dust cloud. Just know that about this type of vacuum.

Lastly - \x5C\x22Can this vacuum replace my plug-in unit for the home?\x5C\x22. In my opinion, no. I love the D59 and use it several times a week for small jobs and to make some hard jobs much easier - but there is still a need for a full corded vacuum system unless you have a small apartment, no pets, or something like that.

review_headline: Hangers for Women, Not for Men
review_body:
So if you are a woman, please feel free to add a star to my rating.

The purpose of the velvet covering is to keep slinky, sleeveless dresses and tops from sliding off onto your closet floor, at which it works extremely well, according to the women I have conned into testing it for me. But if you are a guy like me, used to hanging up his t-shirts the wrong way by sticking the hanger down through the neck opening, the flocking is a problem. I actually had to resort to hanging my t-shirts up \x5C\x22the right way\x5C\x22, by sticking the hanger up through the waist opening, and it still took longer to work the shirt on than it did onto a smooth plastic one.

Otherwise, these are strong, thin profiled (take up less closet space), well made hangers with movable metal hooks that should last quite a while and are so far shedding no flocking despite my manly misuse of them.

review_headline: Top notch airbrush, even for a first internal mix brush
review_body:
Without much to compare it to short of a cheap plastic external mix Testors, I can only give my impressions.

This is the first top feed, high quality airbrush I\x27ve owned. I bought it for my wife in addition to the Master tank Compressor for Christmas and we have both used it quite a bit since getting it. I haven\x27t used all the combinations, but I don\x27t seem to need to. For painting 1/24 scale models it has been very even, very smooth painting. It\x27s easier to operate than I thought it would be. It feels very well made, is easy to take apart and (mostly) to clean.

Cons:
I haven\x27t found any cons yet, other than there\x27s a couple spots that can be a bit tricky to clean if you leave paint in it. I also haven\x27t been able to find the best techniques yet for fine lines vs. wide sprays, but I know it\x27s possible.

product_title: Captive Cables | Desktop Cable / Wire Organizer and Management Solution | Best Value 9 Pack on Amazon!
review_body:
When looking for similar products on Amazon, I found there were a few companies that had similar products. The prices were all pretty much the same but these had good reviews so I thought I would give them a try.

I have only used a couple of these, but so far, they do exactly what I wanted them to do. I have stuck one just on the back edge of my and my wife\x27s nightstands to keep our iPhone/iPad charging cables from falling onto the floor when they aren\x27t in use. I noticed that the adhesive used is a 3M product (can\x27t go wrong there--they feel like they are sticking very well. It should also be noted that I am not using these with the standard Apple brand Lightning cable. Instead, I am using a slightly thicker cable that has a woven cable cover instead of a standard soft plastic one. This makes the cable\x27s diameter slightly larger than Apple\x27s cables, but it still fits fine in the cable holder--not too tight and not too loose so when you pull on the cable, it does not get pinched my the cable holder.

So far I\x27ve only used them for my iPhone, but I am sure I will find other places in the house that these would be useful for.

review_body: I have a 10 yr old version of this model, and after 10 years, it is still going strong.  I have many dogs and many kids running in and out of my house non-stop. I guess after being washed so much, it finally fell apart.  Also, the end pieces that hold the roller on went out, those were cheap and easy to replace.  I also use this vacuum to clean other houses for income, so it has been abused being loaded in and out of my vehicle.  My kids use it often and it holds up to their abuse as well.  Can\x27t say enough good things about this vacuum.  Still works like it did when I first got it now that I\x27ve replaced a few things on it from wear and tear.

product_title: Miyuki Delica Seed Beads Size 11/0 Colorful Super Mix
review_headline: A good mix and a good value. Perfect for doing a lot of small projects or trying out different Delica styles.
review_body:
These are the usual high-quality Delica beads, not culls. I recived them in little resealable bag with a little plastic tube packed to the brim with beads.

I dumped them out onto a plate to get an idea of the proportions of the mix. The picture shows mostly opaque with many AB (aurora borealis), and a few metallic, foil-lined, matt, clear, two-toned, and clear color lined. The proportions where different with mine: many AB and foil-lined, some opaque, a few mat and two-toned, and a very few clear, metallic, and clear color lined. Not bad, I just was hoping for more opaque, clear, and matt ones as they\x27re my favorites. The balance of colors is quite good, though very few browns but it\x27s not a very popular color so I\x27m not surprised.

Sometimes a mix like this will be mostly one or two types with just a few others thrown in to justify calling it a \x27mix.\x27 But this has true variety. It\x27s not a perfectly balanced mix but it is a good one and I\x27m satisfied with it.

As a side note, usually I don\x27t like foil-lined because they\x27re too gaudy for my taste, but the Delicas are less flashy while still being very shiny. I kinda like them. It\x27s also won me over to Delicas: the consistency of size, shape, and quality even between styles and colors is really impressive!

product_title: BLACK+DECKER BDH2400FH 2-in-1 Lithium Stick Vacuum with ORA Technology, 24-volt
review_body: This is a powerful and useful cordless vacuum that gets the job done.  I generally use a Dayton portable hand vacuum cleaner for small jobs as it has a strong motor, good suction, and a nice variety of attachments.  (My only gripe about the Dayton vacuum cleaner is that, over the years, the quality of the storage bags seems to have deteriorated and they are harder to put on as the attachment rings on the bags are less flexible than they used to be.)  My Dayton vacuum cleaner, however, is not a cordless model.  Sometimes, you do need to use a small, cordless vacuum cleaner where it is inconvenient (or impossible) to use one that needs an electrical cord for power.  This Black and Decker unit fills the gap nicely.  It is more powerful than other cordless units I have tried in the past, there is no loss of suction even as the battery runs down (until, of course, kaboom it just runs out altogether with little or no warning like most things powered by lithium batteries), it is lightweight, it comes with a lot of useful attachments (especially the extension wand), and it is easy to empty the debris canister (which is self-contained and does not use a bag).  The only drawbacks, although somewhat minor depending on your personal needs and usage, are the debris container could be a mite larger, the battery does not seem to last that long without needing to be recharged (something less than an hour of use per charge in my experience), and the unit does not stand by itself when the extension wand is attached (perhaps because you don\x27t really need the vacuum cleaner to stand by itself when you are using the extension wand).

review_headline: 30% less noise than a Dyson Vacuum cleaner or what?!
review_body:
So I really needed to do something to bring up humidity levels in my large apartment. Therefore I chose this Honeywell unit. It says on the packaging Quiet (30% less noise). Well I guess that means 30% less than a Dyson Vacuum. This unit is indeed very loud. I could not sleep with this unit in my bedroom. Even on low you can notice it running. On high and medium you have to turn up volume on TV.
I guess I kind of expected that higher noise level because of the pure size of the unit. So far the Cons on this unit.
The unit works perfectly in regards to bring up humidity. Within 2 hours I had the room from 18% up to 38%. I love the capacity and how easy it is to refill. So I will keep it and let it run higher while I am gone and turn it on low while I am home. That should keep the level around the 40%.

product_title: InterDesign Orbz Bath Shower Tote
review_body:
This is a heavy-duty plastic tote bag, suitable for carrying a variety of small objects. The sides of the bag measure approximately 11x9x4\xE2\x80\x9D, with 2 large looping handles whose opening measures 7x4.5\xE2\x80\x9D. The bag is made of heavy duty plastic which has some flexibility, but is generally rather stiff. The bag weighs just under 1 lb when empty. The sides of the bag are composed of circular shapes that touch each other on 4 sides. This leaves diamond-shaped holes in between the contacts that are about 1/2\xE2\x80\x9D across. Being solid plastic, the bag is fully waterproof. There are 4 small (1/4\xE2\x80\x9D) holes on the bottom of the bag to allow any fluids that might fall into the bag to drain. The bag was made in the USA.

I am impressed with the quality of this bag\xE2\x80\x94it really feels like it will hold up to heavy use. I\x27m using the bag in my garden. It is just the right size and shape for carrying my garden hand tools and packages of seeds. It will stand up to the elements like dew and rain showers much better than my former bag, which was made of reeds, or the old standby plastic shopping bags that always seem to get ripped to shreds by the end of the day. Other suggested uses for the bag include a shower tote, a lunch bag, or a magazine holder. Basically, this bag will hold a lot of stuff and it won\x27t mind getting wet. The big handles are great, not only for carrying the bag around, but also for hanging it on a variety of hooks. Overall, this is a handy, well made little tote.

product_title: VicTsing 140ml Essential Oil Diffuser Humidifier with 7 Color LED Lights for Office Home Room
review_body:
I have been provided this VicTsing Aroma Diffuser from the distributor in exchange for a review. However, this in no way obligates me to write either a positive or negative review. I do hate dishonest reviews and lazy hyperbole and refuse to provide it. If a product is poor, I have no compunctions about saying so.

My wife was especially thrilled about seeing this diffuser arrive here and we attempted to set it up. No manual is obviously included and other than lifting off the top piece we weren\x27t quite sure where to go from there. We looked in and could see what appeared to be an instruction manual underneath the white cover but couldn\x27t figure out how to get to it. I went on line to see others of this type and learned that you had to twist the wooden base which has a very thin seam so that the two parts of the wooden base would unscrew. The first time I did it took some strength and I was afraid of breaking something which did not happen. My suggestion is that the instructions should be included inside the box and not inside the diffuser or, at least, to start, on the box.

I found the manual to be somewhat confusing, especially in the areas of what the W & P designated buttons on the sides of the diffuser were to mean. There are two charts and after awhile, I figured out that either of these buttons should be pressed multiple times to create different color effects.
Especially important you are instructed not to fill the diffuser with too much water, no more that 160 millimeters. You can add 2-5 drops of scented oils to add a pleasant scent to the air. Once plugged in with the supplied AC cable, the Aroma Diffuser begins to do its job and it has been running steadily for over 8 hours now emitting a steady stream of humidifying steam and whatever scent my wife put in there. She loves it.

The base of the diffuser does not get too warm but you are advised to keep the diffuser on a flat plain as tilting it might spill the contents and cause a problem.
The single LED changes colors and looks especially cool in a dark room. With the unobtrusive and tiny buttons on the bottom part of the base you can set the diffuser to either keep one color or constantly but slowly change colors. As advertised this diffuser is extremely quiet and will shut itself off if there is no water left in the well. The water and oils do not run out quickly, it will easily run for about 12 hours before any refilling is necessary. The steam generated by the diffuser is supposed to help in the relief of colds, flu and general congestion. I cannot attest to this since I am currently feeling healthy but it certainly can\x27t hurt. The diffuser will work for about 8 minutes and then temporarily shut down for 3 minutes and start again. I believe that this is done to prevent heat build up. The unit is definitely safe, however, being paranoid about leaving devices turned on while out of the home, my advice is to shut if off if you intend to leave the house for work or whatever.

You are advised to gently clean the inside of the water well with a few drops of dish soap and a soft cloth...do not hold it under the spigot of your sink.
This VicTsing diffuser really works well and looks just as good, very classy in its own way and would fit in with really any decor.

While this is a 5 star product, I do wish they had placed the instructions somewhere where you didn\x27t need instructions to get to them.
I do hope that this brief review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase.
Thanks for reading.

UPDATE 1/25/15....My wife has been using it every day for many hours at a time. No problems at all and the rooms smell quite nice. She really likes that the unit safely shuts itself off should the water/oil levels get too low.

Update 5/2/15 ...It is in continuous use with no issues or problems at all. I have been asked about the lights and whether you can shut them off..the answer is \x27no\x27 but the top part which glows and changes colors is really quite subtle and no glaring or overly bright at all and the two LED lights at the base of the unit are very small and non intrusive. If you want, you can turn the unit to face a wall and you won\x27t see them at all. So far, this unit is working perfectly each and every day.tle and no glaring or overly bright at all and the two LED lights at the base of the unit are very small and non intrusive. If you want, you can turn the unit to face a wall and you won\x27t see them at all. So far, this unit is working perfectly each and every day.

product_title: Sling Media Slingbox 350 (Old Version)
review_headline: Slingbox is the best thing ever
review_body:
Slingbox is the best thing ever. I travel a lot for work and use this religiously in hotels to catch up on DVR\x27ed shows or just to watch live HDTV when the cable sucks in room.
My biggest drawbacks with this thing is the web interface, both on iPhone and on the computer. The TV guide function is terrible! Every time I close the tv guide and reopen it, it goes back to the very first channel in the lineup. It does not remember where you left off, nor is it smart enough to follow the channels you tune to. It does however tune to the channel you click on. It is too slow and frustrating to use the cable box\x27s guide through sling box because of the video compression delay as well as the delay to transmit IR to your cable box.
Another thing to note is that the iPhone app is not free at around $8 from what I remember. I guess its the price you pay for a subscription free service from Slingbox. They recently started adding advertisement videos to the web app that pop up when you launch the streaming of your cable box.
All in all I think Slingbox is the coolest thing ever despite some annoyances. I traveled to Peru last year for vacation from U.S. and was able to stream my Slingbox! Unfortunately my Netflix does not work outside of the U.S. but this thing will stream anywhere in the world!
