product_title: Samsung 5203 with F355 Soundbar Parent
review_headline: Good TV with a few minor flaws
review_body:
I purchased this TV as a gift for my boyfriend on Cyber Monday. I was looking for a smart TV with good image and sound quality at a reasonable price. For comparison purposes I own a 32" Sony Bravia 720p non-smart TV and I would say the overall quality is at a similar level - albeit higher res on the Samsung. We do not have cable but have an antenna and an Apple TV hooked up - both work fine. We do not have Samsung devices so have not used the mirroring feature.

Pros:
-Easy setup
-Excellent sound and picture quality - the sound quality is much better than my Sony
-Easy to access and use apps
-Overall a good value

Cons:
-Base is not sturdy - the base for this TV is much more flimsy than the base on my Sony. The screws were also not included in the package and it was too much hassle with the 3rd party seller to obtain them. I think manufacturers are anticipating that the majority of people will mount their TVs on the wall and have started cutting costs here.
-Initialization takes a while - we have to wait 5-10 minutes to be able to use any of the built-in apps
-Video and sound cut out intermittently - this hasn\x27t been a huge issue but it does happen, especially when using the smart TV features. It can usually be resolved by going back a step and restarting playback or turning the TV off. This has never happened with my Sony and I\x27m hoping it doesn\x27t become a more serious problem.
-Limited browser functionality - We wanted to be able to stream live video from websites since we don\x27t have cable but the browser they use is proprietary and doesn\x27t have the necessary plug-ins and playback capability for most sites. Not surprising but annoying considering how many people use streaming services now. Hopefully there will be an update to fix this.

Overall a good buy, especially if you can get it on sale. I might have gone with an older, lower-res Sony if this hadn\x27t been on sale.

product_title: Samsung UN F5000 1080p 60Hz Slim LED HDTV
review_body:
I had purchased a Sceptre 19\x5C\x22 TV and was a little disappointed with the picture quality when not viewing the TV at eye level. I returned it and bought this Samsung instead.

The Samsung was more expensive but definitely worth it. The picture quality is very sharp and bright right out of the box. There are many adjustments to make it even better including a \x5C\x22leaning back\x5C\x22 setting which also compensates for different viewing angles (i.e. if the TV is positioned a few inches higher from where you are watching).

The TV is exceptionally thin and the right size for the kitchen or other area where space is limited. There are 2 HDMI inputs which is all you would really need for a small TV.

The only improvement that I can suggest to Samsung is fixing the unnecessary difficulty associated with attaching the base. The screw holes are recessed several inches making it awkward to fasten the screws. What should take 30 seconds or so took quite a bit longer. review_headline: Good soundbar, but some lessons learned with it.
review_body:
Bought this soundbar as a way to upgrade sound on my HDTV. After some tweaking, it works as advertised. Overall for the price, I think it\x27s worth it. Is it audiophile quality sound? No...but it\x27s good, and it enhances everything. I also purchased it because it had a subwoofer out. After some use in our medium to large room, I realized I really didn\x27t need it because my sub would just overwhelm it, and the unit actually puts out quite a bit of bass. The bass is somewhat tuneful, but not tight by the way. Also, I have a built in made of wood, so that does amplify the sound since the soundbar is above the TV and in the shelf area.

I would recommend a few things for people who get this soundbar to maximize your experience. First off, READ THE MANUAL. It will help you understand the features of the soundbar before you attempt to play it. Next, let it "break in". Don\x27t play the sound too high to start, I just set it up with "TruVol" off, and let it run at moderate volumes for say, 12-24 hours. Then it will loosen up, sound better, and you won\x27t run the risk of blowing out a speaker. Next, disable the "Energy Saving" mode. It sucks, and it actually causes the unit to increase/decrease volume as well as causes a delay in sound once you activate it or turn your TV on. Next, use the Optical (TOSLink) or PCM (Digital RCA) inputs to get the best sound. Next, understand what TruVol and TruSurround do. TruVol mode actually nearly doubles the sound. This is definitely the mode you want to use this soundbar in after your break in period. TruSurround is kind of a gimmick, as most of those types of processing really are with a single speaker array. I\x27d just skip it and enjoy the 2-channel.

If you are going to use a subwoofer, tune it, and adjust your gain and volume settings to blend in with the soundbar. The manual recommends turning bass to the "0" point, but that\x27s subjective. My sub is so powerful that even barely turning it on overwhelmed the soundbar. I gave up and just set the Bass setting on the soundbar to the lowest it could go and tuned my sub from there.

Finally - some people have asked if they can control the sound from the TV. If your TV has a variable audio out, then yes you can. Just use RCA cables (good ones) to connect it and leave it on and in "non Energy Star" mode.

Overall, I like it, it does add a lot of extra sound and good vocal clarity to the TV audio and movies. The bass performance is acceptable, but if you like your bass I would get a powered sub. If you are just using it for average TV watching, it should do though. And the small footprint is really nice!

review_headline: VIZIO S3851w-D4 38\x22 5.1 Channel Sound Bar Review
review_body:
I purchased this sound bar through a national retail chain to replace my existing 5.1 surround sound system. I\x27m giving it 4 stars for now as this is a first impressions review and will update after further use.

Let me first explain why I decided to go with a sound bar and ditch my 5.1 system. We recently moved into a home where the main living space had vaulted ceilings and the acoustics in that room were poor to say the least. We have a Panasonic Plasma TV (TC-P42s1) with a Yamaha Receiver (RX-V375) just for reference and I will be talking about some compatibility issues later in this review. One of the reasons we wanted to ditch the system we had was audibility issues, especially voices, with the acoustics or set up we had. It could have been my fault for how I set it up but I tried everything and voices were always being drowned out by the action or music in the movies or shows we were watching unless we had the system turned all the way up. Regardless, I wanted to try something new and at the price point of this system it was a great intro into sound bars for us to give a try.

I love the looks of this system and will not get into the ascetics of it. When trying to set this up my initial plan was to keep the Yamaha receiver as a glorified HDMI switch for all of my entertainment devices (4) and run an optical cable (supplied) from my TV to my sound bar. This was my first hiccup with the Vizio system. When I ran my optical cable from the tv directly to the sound bar I would get audio for one half a second and it would go out. When I changed the volume it would cut out again after a half second. After doing some research online for about an hour it seems some TV\x27s do not export audio in the proper format that this sound bar recognizes. I read that there were some firmware updates for the larger units like this but did not want to try that at the time since it was late on a Saturday and figured I would not get ahold of any rep at Vizio that could help me. So, instead I decided to hook up my PS4 directly to the sound bar via the Optical cable provided and my cable box with the coaxial cable since those are the two that I swap from the most. I will be buying an optical splitter from Amazon in the near future if I decided to keep this set up to connect my PS3 and Apple TV down the line. For now, I have the cables attached but resting near the sound bar to switch over when I want to use those devices. And for note, my receiver did not have an optical out or coax out.

After getting that figured out I started to have issues with the remote changing the input. I don\x27t know if we have interference in the house stoping the signal but I cannot change the audio input from my couch (only about 8 -10 feet away) I have to get about half way to the sound bar for it to recognize the inputs. I will look into this more and update if I find out what is going on with this.

All that aside let\x27s talk sound. Out of the box this sounds great. There will be some adjusting needed depending on your room and set up and I will probably be tweaking the sounds levels more after I write this review. From the factory the sound bar itself is a little mid-tone heave, in my opinion. You can adjust the bass on the sound bar and sub separately and I will be doing more adjusting as I listen to more movies and music on this. The rears are a little low for my liking but I am going to have to test more movies before I make a determination if it needs adjusting. Also with the rear speakers, the audio cable supplied will not run through my existing rear speaker stands. The connectors are too thick to go through the holes on the stands. I may drill into it to make it work or just look for a different stand.

All that being said this is a great unit and worth the price. If you are just getting into home theater set ups and want to give something a go the sound on this is awesome for the money. Plus the addition of 2 rear speakers and a sub is well worth the price tag. And since this has been out for a while now you can find good deals as well.ar speakers and a sub is well worth the price tag. And since this has been out for a while now you can find good deals as well.

product_title: LG Electronics 65UB9800 4K Ultra HD 240Hz 3D LED TV
review_body: I spent a great deal of time researching 4K TVs, stereo AVR units, and 3D Blu-ray players. I read many reviews on many sites. I read plenty of reviews commenting negatively on the 3D quality of this LG 79 inch TV. I never had a 3D TV before this one, and our previous TV was a 720p Panasonic from 2005. This was a big change. Here is what we settled on for equipment and how it is plugged together:  New Oppo103 3D Blu-ray>single HDMI into new Onkyo838 THX AVR>single HDMI into new LG 4K 3D TV (79 inch, 2014/2015 model). Typical installation most audiophiles would attempt to use. I have all NHT speakers. All firmware updates, all HDMI 2.0 cables, all HDMI 2.0/4K ports (except AppleTV and cable box). Very picky about sound and video, but accepting of technological limitations as will be apparent below.  My LG TV is mounted to the wall using the Sanus XF228 mount, which swings and tilts. You really must buy this mount for this TV. Flat mounts will not work properly for 3D viewing. You must tilt the TV down several degrees to have center of TV generally pointing at center of where you sit. We sit a typical 8-10 feet from TV and up to four people across the room, so not all are straight on viewing.  Viewing: cable TV is amazing as is standard DVD and regular Blu-ray. Upscaling is amazing. Low quality commercials look bad, yes. But 720 or 1080 broadcasts look amazing. AppleTV movies look awesome. Our previous set was a plasma 50inch Panasonic. I held off buying LCD for so many years because plasma was a very high picture quality relative to LCD. I wanted bigger and 3D. Blu-ray 1080 upscaled is amazing. Audio and video are in-sync with all of the above.  3D viewing: You must tilt the TV, especially if you mount it such that bottom is 42 inches off ground like mine. It is the physics of the design and how 3D is projected at home. The 3D is simply amazing if you tilt it properly and have the correct mount. Is it perfect, no. There is slight double imaging in certain parts of the screen if you do not have the proper tilt or sit too slouched in your sofa. But most of the scenes are simply amazing. Have watched Avatar, Guardians, and Jurassic Park in 3D. The 3D video is being shown as 1080p/24hz in each eye as passive. It is a home experience that is awesome, but not perfect. We truly feel it is better than the theater 3D experiences, aside from maybe IMAX. Guardians even changes aspect ratio for dramatic experience, and is essentially their IMAX version brought into your home. Be careful believing the strongest negative comments about this TV regarding 3D. You will miss out on a rare home 3D experience. I bet most people get cheap flat mounts and then it won\x27t work.  3D audio sync issue: The Oppo and TV and Onkyo have trouble syncing audio to video only on 3D movies. Very strange. I never bothered contacting LG. Figured that would go nowhere. I did contact Oppo (not that I blame them, it\x27s hard to assess where the issue is). They are going to study it, but as a resolution for those with similar set-ups to ours and have audio issues (audio comes slightly before video), here is what pretty much solved it: in the Oppo set the audio to delay being sent by +200ms. It\x27s in the settings. The TV 4K and 3D processing must be demanding enough that the audio just arrives quicker. There are plenty of others on the internet with this issue, and different ways to solve it. Slowing the audio helps a lot, and we set the TV to Photo or Game mode to alter the processing enough that video comes closer to audio. Standard and vivid settings make it a bit out of sync, so those processing choices may be more taxing. Again, Oppo may figure out something later with a firmware fix anyway.  We have beautiful 3D Blu-ray in 1080p passive with no headaches and expensive glasses, awesome DTS-MA or DD5.1 sound, and amazing 4K upscaled normal TV viewing.

product_title: VIZIO S3821w-C0 38-inch 2.1 Home Theater Sound Bar with Wireless Subwoofer (2014 Model)
review_body: UPDATE: The first one failed almost immediately (see below). The free replacement failed after 2 years. OK, this isn\x27t high end, but it should last longer than 2 years. This time the bluetooth failed - Vizio tech support tried everything they could - well, that was only one thing, a reset. Nada. It won\x27t pair with anything - and bluetooth definitely works on all our other devices, some of them much older than 2 years. We were taking a chance on Vizio - it\x27s fairly new, doesn\x27t have a long track record, so we didn\x27t want to invest in a TV. I\x27m glad of that - no more Vizio for us. It\x27s not worth any amount of money, no matter how little. I mean, this thing now has to go to the dump? Who can fix bluetooth? Major fail for Vizio. ***** Not high-end sound by any means, and controls are rudimentary, but for the money...  This was a Christmas present. Had no problem getting it up and running - simple instructions. As other reviewers have noted, some TV program voice are a little muddied, so usually we save it for movies and music. Also - the sound volume goes by distinct steps rather than a smooth ramp up or down, so it can be hard to get exactly the volume you want. Still, the Bluetooth for the subwoofer works as it should; it paired with my phone flawlessly (you have to remember to push the Bluetooth button on the remote and hold for 5 seconds, plus of course selecting the unit on your phone).  And today it stopped working after less than a month - no power, wouldn\x27t turn on by remote or power button. I tried everything - unplugging/replugging, etc. Nothing worked. Called Vizio - tech had me unplug, hold power button down for 30 seconds, plug in, and turn on. It\x27s working again. That\x27s how you reset it.  BUT - she said you shouldn\x27t have to reset it at all and that there was a manufacturing defect. They\x27re going to send us a new one without the defect. So we won\x27t be without for a while, Vizio is putting a pending charge on our card, and when we get the new one with freeshipping label, we\x27ll pack up the old one and send it back.  IOW - Vizio made it real easy. Props for that.

product_title: Google Chromecast HDMI Streaming Media Player
review_headline: Use a supported Android device and you\x27ll be fine
review_body: For screencasting, Google supports a limited number of Android devices. Make sure your smartphone/tablet device is Android 4.4.2+ compatible and is on this list (click on the Supported Android Devices button):    https://support.google.com/chromecast/answer/6059461?hl=en    When it comes to iPad support, forget it. Its a waste of money. Google support for iPad versus Android devices is not the same. You cannot screencast from your iPad to your LCD TV. You cannot tab stream either. You can only stream from Google Chromecast apps available in iTunes.    I bought this to use my iPad as a remote control and screencast device for websites. It fails in this regard.    I have a 2nd Gen Moto X smartphone that works flawlessly with screen casting. But its not very useful to me as the user agent rendering is mobile specific defeating the purpose of displaying a desktop web page view onto a large screen. You can download the Opera browser onto your Android smartphone and then set the user agent from mobile to desktop. That will get you a desktop web page instead of a limited mobile looking web page on your LCD. Also a disadvantage of using a smart phone is that typing in a tiny virtual keyboard is error prone. This is why I preferred to use an iPad with a larger screen surface and bigger virtual keyboard because its easier to input and click on page links in tightly designed navigation menus.    Attempting to get another Android tablet to work was sproradic. Screen casting was unreliable even with the Display | Casting | Enable wireless device set. When it did work when launching Chromecast apps, there is quite a bit of fuzzy rendering and laggy performance. This, with my wireless router being just 10 feet away. Based on this, I would not recommend using Chromecast outside those screencast supported Android devices listed above.    Chrome tabbing works well from a Windows PC. I am able to screen cast to it without a problem.    Outside of screen casting, regardless of actual h/w device, there is heavy reliance on the existence of Google Chromecast apps. There\x27s a good selection here - https://www.google.com/chrome/devices/chromecast/apps.html    For $35, its a good deal but only if you have the right supported Android device.

review_headline: OK, but my search is not over....
review_body:
I have had a ton of problems with Blu-Ray players. Cheap players just don\x27t get it, but higher cost doesn\x27t seem to matter. I have tried several different brands between $50 and $125, but none have remained in service. Even cheap players have all kinds of gewgaws that you may or may not want for Internet connection. Some can be annoying. That said, this Sony player has been doing nicely for several weeks. It has played without issues, and by all accounts, will continue (fingers crossed). There are a few distractions. The power and open/close buttons are almost invisible on the top of the player and have a triangle shape. Hard to hit the right option. Also, I don\x27t like the navigation menus, which are confusing and take time to load. The primary reason is the desire by Sony to integrate on-line services with the player, whether you want them or not. It\x27s a way to sell Sony, and not much else.

I\x27m happy with this player, but it\x27s not perfect.

product_title: ANDROSET MINI PC
review_body:
Sounds like a good idea, but technology was not ready for average consumer.

I am a software engineer and after much fiddling with flashing ROMs and puttering around I was able to get it working.

Full 1080p video stutters and chokes depending on codec. 720p does better, but again depending on codec may also stutter and choke.

If you want this for netflix, amazon video, or google video forget it, I have not been able to get this to reliably work for either.

480p or countless in between codecs below 720p work great. I was able to get XBMC (Kodi now) to work with some success using external SD card to store videos.

Biggest issue I have with this device is that the WIFI chip is VERY VERY SLOW! Glaciers move faster than this thing sometimes. Some folks have had luck soldering new antenna on the board... but if you want to go that far just buy a newer device with 4 cores.

My best results were from Finless Bob\x27s v2.1 ROM.

product_title: Samsung 40-Inch 4K Ultra HD 60Hz Smart LED TV
review_headline: This T.V. is for someone who desperately wants the newest tech, but cant afford the good stuff (ME!), and it shows
review_body:
This T.V. is bottom of the barrel regarding quality. The bezel is cheap and the T.V. feels flimsy. Let me start this review off by saying that I am not an audio/videophile. I didn\x27t run comprehensive tests, calibrate the monitor with software, etc. My only knowledge of displays comes from being a photographer and using calibrated monitors, and my past experience with Samsung T.V.s, which is the only brand I have owned since flat panels became a thing.

When I walk into a big box store to buy a T.V., the first thing I do is stand back and look at all the displays. You can usually tell from here, where you want to start looking. Whatever is most comfortable for your eyes. I prefer good contrast, rich colors, and smooth motion. Not the fake smooth that the software in the TV does (Auto motion plus) This is how i bought my last Samsung, about 5 years ago. It was the last of the LCD style TVs, and has a better picture than this T.V. in every single aspect.

This T.V. shows digital noise and screen tearing in the few tests i threw at it. It just was not pleasant to watch. Like I said, my old TV runs circles around it.

This T.V. is for someone who desperately wants the newest tech, but cant afford the good stuff (ME!) and it shows. I learned my lesson and returned the T.V. and "settled" for a 7150. Its not 4K, but its a top of the line Samsung HD TV and looks amazing. You get an awesome 240hz native refresh rate. Its performance and image quality is impressive to say the least. The form factor and build quality is rock solid compared to the 6950. Its like comparing a Mercedes to a 20 year old Toyota. If this TV defines your price range, I would highly suggest checking out a 7 series and waiting for the 4k tech to catch up in the lower end models.

product_title: Frigidaire Professional FPID2495QF Fully Integrated Dishwasher
review_body:
...OVER MY INSANELY LOUD DISHWASHER!

It\x27s loud. Insanely loud. My wife\x27s Honda Civic is quieter. Seriously. It has a \x5C\x22delay\x5C\x22 feature that lets you set it to run at night while you sleep, but it ends up being more like an alarm clock that wakes you up at 2am and sends you frantically running around your house in your tidy-whities with a baseball bat, hunting down potential burglars while stepping on porcupine shaped cat toys in the dark. It even frightens my cat -- the one that I have to move out of the way with my foot while vacuuming. It\x27s that loud.

Worse than that is the design. If you put a standard 12\x5C\x22 diameter plate in the bottom rack, the spinner blade gets stuck and mockingly shoots water at the door seal, flooding your kitchen floor, as if to say, \x5C\x22How dare you put a standard sized dish into my Pro grade belly! Here\x27s what I think of your filthy proletarian dish!\x5C\x22

There\x27s also a \x5C\x22Sahara\x5C\x22 drying feature, which just straight baffles me. It heats up a coil in the bottom of the dishwasher, which basically just makes a bunch of steam. But since the designers apparently forgot to add vents, the steam doesn\x27t really go anywhere. It just circulates inside the dishwasher until it shuts the element off, then it condenses into water and voila! you once again have wet dishes. They should have named this feature \x5C\x22broccoli\x5C\x22 instead of Sahara as it appears better suited to be an industrial grade vegetable steamer rather than a dishwasher.

Longevity, you ask? You\x27d think, that at this premium price, this thing would outlive your youngest grandchild, but wait! Think again! The door sensor failed about one month after the warranty expired. It cost me over $100 to get it fixed.

Final conclusion: buy a Bosch. They\x27re cheaper, quieter, and clean better.

product_title: VIZIO S3821w-C0 38-inch 2.1 Home Theater Sound Bar with Wireless Subwoofer (2014 Model)
review_body:
This is a great sound bar, without question. I purchased it to go with my 55" TV, and although the recommend the larger one for tv\x27s this size I think this size compliments my tv perfectly. The wireless subwoofer came already paired out of the box and has great bass response. Being omnidirectional and wireless is great so it can be placed out of view wherever it fit the best. The bluetooth function works great and I have paired it to many different devices, the range however is not as great as I expected, unless it is the walls of my house interfering. Volume Control and Simulated Surround Sound are neat features, I generally leave both turned on, however sometimes I turn off Simulated Surround Sound to improve vocal clarity.

I have a TV without a master audio output, so I had to use the digital audio input from my Cable/DVR and the optical audio input from my Amazon Fire TV, this means that I need to switch the input on the sound bar when I switch the TV input, but I knew this would be the case when I bought my set up. The input selection is read with a series of little lights on the front of the unit, which takes a little getting used to, but I have no complaints about this.

The reason I gave this only four stars is in the 6 months I have owned this sound bar a strange thing has happened three times. With the unit off the remote stops communicating so it cannot be turned on with the remote. It is not an issue of dead batteries but rather whatever processes the IR receiver in the unit freezes. The solution is simply to unplug the unit, wait 10 seconds, and plug it back in so no big deal except that it is hard to do without lifting the bar off of the mounting hooks.

review_headline: Good value, just not quite what I needed
review_body: For the money, I think this projector is one of the best out there. The picture is quite good at its native resolution of 1280x800. Images appear pretty crisp and sharp, and the colors are good once you play around with the settings. While it does have speakers and they do work, I would recommend using a receiver or something similar. The cooling fan is a touch loud, but it never bothered me. The brightness of this projector is very good, but I would still recommend using it in a light controlled room for the best quality. The only thing that significantly limits this projector is its manual keystone and focus. If you do not use the keystone feature, the picture is easy to focus and looks very good. However, once you start using the keystone feature (i.e. if you are mounting it on the ceiling) it is impossible to focus the entire picture. Overall this is a very solid projector, especially given the price, but it is difficult to work with the manual keystone and focus.

I\x27m pretty sure those result were from moving the TV and having it off and not the reset itself. The flickering is still a problem and now I\x27ve learned if the TV shacks at all it flickers. I live near train tracks.... So now I know it is a physical problem. I contacted TCL again and they demanded I send a video as proof. So I recorded it and emailed them the video. I then got a random call days later from them on a Saturday night while out at dinner from TCL support. Not knowing the number I did not answer, but they left a voicemail to email them what time I\x27ll be home. I did and have not heard back form them since. This has all been going on for months now and I still have a broken TV that TCL doesn\x27t seem to want to believe is broken and doesn\x27t want to fix. This will be my first and last time buying a Chinese brand I don\x27t know. At least I can get it replaced when my extended warranty kicks in.

product_title: Seiki SE22FR01 22-Inch  1080p 60Hz LED TV (Retro TV)
review_body:
This TV is everything I wanted out of it.
+ SMALL AND PORTABLE
There\x27s a little carrying handle on the back of this TV, which makes toting from a car to a tournament or house easy. The TV is also a great size and I personally decided not to attach the legs just to keep it small- it works perfectly fine like that.

+ NO GAMING LAG
I primarily bought this TV to bring to Super Smash Bros Wii U tournaments and friends houses, and it hasn\x27t let me down. There\x27s no noticeable input lag, so everything runs smooth and everyone is happy. I have yet to test this with older consoles (SNES, N64, Dreamcast, PS2, etc...), but I\x27m very happy so far.

+ IT LOOKS SUPER SPECIAL AWESOME
I\x27ve already brought this to a few Smash Wii U tournaments and gatherings and everyone always compliments it and says how awesome and unique it is. I personally love retro/mid-century designs, and this TV fits right in with my mid-century thrifting finds. The red is a bit bright for me (I\x27m considering painting it), but it\x27s a great glossy finish and very fun to look at.

+ SURPRISING SOUND
I wasn\x27t expecting this TV to sound all that great, but it certainly puts out some great bass and treble. I feel no need to attach any external speakers, thankfully. I usually keep the volume between 6-8 for gaming while not disturbing others.

- VIEWING SWEET SPOT IS A BIT SMALL
I have this TV set slightly higher than my bed, and I\x27ve noticed that the screen is darker when viewed from low, high, and side angles. It\x27s not a huge let down, considering I only paid a little more than a hundered dollars for it, but it\x27s a bit annoying when trying to watch shows or play games that are dark in color. And on that note, the black are not incredibly black, so don\x27t expect a ton a contrast from this TV.

Overall, I would definitely buy this TV again if need be. My friends and a few tournament goers were considering getting their own as well, but unfortunately Amazon no longer has any in stock as of this posting.nfortunately Amazon no longer has any in stock as of this posting.

product_title: Sharp HT-SB602 2.1 Channel 310W Bluetooth Sound Bar
review_body:
I bought this for my husband as a Christmas gift. The unit itself is sleek and looks great. it fits perfectly for our 60 inch TV. It does NOT interfere with our remote for the TV, but our TV is a SHARP as this bar was made for a Sharp TV. We rarely use the TV remote anyway as we can use the provided remote for everything.

The setup for was a little cumbersome since our Sharp TV is 4 years old and doesn\x27t have some of the stuff the newer TV have. My husband got it all figured out though, so it does work as it is suppose too . The sound is great when sitting in front of the sound bar and the bass puts out a nice even sound but it will definitely shake you walls if you keep turning it up! . The wireless subwoofer is a great thing as who wants more wires? The remote works well and is easy to operate. You can leave the sound on with the bar and the TV on a different port (i.e. camera system, game system) So you can still listen to the TV if you choose. The wireless features work well and Bluetooth. If you are looking for an upgrade and do not want to go the surround sound way, this is your best bet. We had an older Sharp sound bar and it worked good but didn\x27t have the subwoofer. This bar is a great upgrade and works well for us. The sound is crisp and clean and you have several playing mode options. My husband is very pleased with this and loves it!

review_body:
Listen up folks: Frame interpolation is automatically turned on. To avoid the "soap opera" effect when watching films follow this advise:

Click menu, picture settings, scroll down to the Advanced Settings option at the bottom, scroll down again to the bottom to click on Film Mode. The TV comes with the setting on. For any kind of film based material you will want to turn it off.

Yep - turn off "film mode" and it will actually look like a film (24 frames per sec and not interpolated to 60fps). You will thank me later.

Keep it on for sports and live news. Anything that you want to look like "real life".

product_title: VIZIO S3820W-C0 38-inch 2.0 Home Theater Sound Bar with Integrated Deep Bass
review_headline: Better than built-in TV speakers on Vizio p-series
review_body: Edit: after using heavily for a day, sound opened up considerably (speakers breaking in?).  They still require a subwoofer, but now sound good enough music listening (classical is a little flat).  Remote functions initially appear overly complex.  A little practice solves that however.  Particularly switching between TV and bluetooth usage.   Upgrading to 5-stars.     ------    While significantly better than my anemic built-in Vizio p-series TV speakers, this sound bar will not wow you with awesome sound.  It is no substitute for a decent set of speakers.  To my ears, it DOES require a separate subwoofer for adequate effect.  So either repurpose your existing sub or buy the soundbar (on sale) with at least a 2.1 subwoofer setup.    I would not recommend relying on the soundbar as your primary means of listening to music (via Bluetooth from phone or via TV app).  The sound is loud, but not rich enough.  If music listening is an important function, definitely invest in a model with subwoofer and additional speakers.    Finally, the soundbar is tall and will block the IR port on the Vizio p-series TVs if both rest on a flat TV stand, soundbar in front of TV. review_headline: Not perfect, but a steal at this price!
review_body:
I\x27ve had this for a few weeks now, so I\x27ll share my impressions...

Set-up:
Pretty simple. Plug it in to the TV (with or without the included dongle), plug in a USB input device (a mouse, or like me, you have a keyboard/mouse combo that terminates with 1 USB connector, use that), and finally, connect it up to the wall wart, and you\x27ve got picture.

Configuration:
It\x27s pretty watered down, so there aren\x27t many things to tweak. The process was pretty self explanatory after setting up Wifi and device language.

Using it:
It\x27s perfectly good for 720p video. I don\x27t have any 1080p videos to test, and that\x27s partly the reason why I took a gamble with this device. I just needed something to play DVD quality content. The UI is pretty responsive. It has tabs for videos and music from a connected USB storage device, but I stream stuff off my NAS so this wasn\x27t applicable to me.

Notes and tips:
- Enable the Google Play Store from the settings.
- Download XMBC/Kodi for your video viewing. It hasn\x27t failed me yet.
- With regards to Wifi. Others have mentioned that Wifi speeds were spotty. I\x27ve noticed that too. What I found out was quite interesting, speed test would show me less than 1Mbps downstream when I had the dongle spitting out a 1080p resolution. However, after I changed it to a 720p resolution, my downstream jumped up to 11Mbps. Since that was all the throughput I needed, I didn\x27t tweak it anymore. My wifi access point is about 50ft away on the main floor, and the device is in an upstairs loft.
- All in all, a good bang for the buck. It does what it\x27s supposed to and nothing more. Don\x27t expect this to solve all your problems, and if you go into it with that mindset, your relationship will be much better. :)

product_title: Cree 30/60/100W Equivalent A21 3 Way LED Light Bulb, Soft White
review_headline: Read the reviews before you purchase this bulb!
review_body:
The bulb performed great for three months, but then it flickered once and gave up the ghost. Admittedly, I did not read the reviews on Amazon before purchasing this bulb. Shame on me! However, I did read CNET\x27s article, \x5C\x22LED there be light: We pick the best bulb upgrades for your buck,\x5C\x22 and they rated Cree\x27s 60-watt replacement LED a \x5C\x22no brainer,\x5C\x22 based on its cost and 10-year warranty. I took a gamble on Cree\x27s 3-way LED based on CNET\x27s remarks. I should have done more research before I made the purchase. Cree\x27s 10-year warranty sounds good in theory, but the buyer must return the bulb to Cree at their expense, plus provide a copy of the receipt and proof of purchase. JEERS to Cree for charging nearly $30 for a single bulb and then making the buyer eat the cost of returning it. Not a very good way to garner customer loyalty. I would like to note that on Cree\x27s Facebook page, someone posted a comment about the burnout rate on the Cree LEDs he purchased for his home. In that post, the writer stated he purchased his LEDs at Home Depot, and that they replaced them for him, rather than him having to return to Cree. It you plan to purchase any LEDs in the future, it might be worth a trip to Home Depot. Nice to know there\x27s a brick-and-brick-and-morter store you can return the LEDs to instead of sending to the manufacturer. I would love to see Amazon spearhead a replacement program for LEDs that would make it easy on the consumer to receive replacement and/or refund. If an on-line retailer giant like Amazon complained to manufacturers like Cree, we might have a better chance of seeing product improvement in the future.

From a consumer standpoint, we are venturing into the unknown with respect to the longevity of LED bulbs in our homes. Hopefully in time, the price will go down and the quality will go up. Until then, I\x27m stocking up on incandesencent bulbs while they\x27re still around.

review_headline: While this is not the forum to debate the values of the bidet- I have been very satisfied with the product
review_body: We were in the process of building a new house and decided to use bidets along with high efficency toilets in each bathroom to be green and hygienic! While this is not the forum to debate the values of the bidet- I have been very satisfied with the product. It is reasonably priced and easy to install. The way it works after install is that there is an easy to use knob on the right side which can be turned up like a dial thus increasing water pressure. The water from the jet comes out in an arc so that it can target the "right" areas.The water pressure even at the lowest setting is good and we have not felt the need to go to any of the higher settings. It is effective and easy to use- even our 6 year old is using it now and we feel is much cleaner than with the use of TP. Now, I believe options are available wherein you can either get warm or cold water but this particular model is just cold water which I feared initially, but have found not to be uncomfortable even in winter. review_body: A few years ago I switched a number of incandescent floodlights in my house to flourescent and was never really happy with them.  I recently bought 6 of these Bioluz BR40 bulbs to replace some of the fluorescents and am quite pleased with them.  They do seem a bit brighter than the "120W equivalent" fluorescents they replaced and are marginally brighter than some similar Feit LED BR40 bulbs.  I like how they come on instantly to full brightness, unlike fluorescents.  Only time will tell if they last as long as they are advertised to, but even if they last only half as long as expected, I will be happy.  The surface barely gets warm so I don\x27t anticipate any problems with overheating.  They are a bit heavier than fluorecent or incandescent bulbs, but not alarmingly so.  My only complaint is that they are a bit whiter than incandescent bulbs and I would guess the actual color temperature is closer to 3000K than the stated 2700K (but then again so are the Feit bulbs I bought for comparison).  I also wish they would give a CRI index to compare with other bulbs (the high the number, the more true-to-life colors appear).  Overall, very good.  These LED floodlights have now reached the price point where they are worthwhile.

review_headline: Beautiful lamp at a bargain price, but not a significant source of \x22negative ions\x22.
review_body:
These lamps are really great - beautiful too look at, and perfect for a mood light, night light, or TV light. A real bargain for the price.

However, I docked one star off the review because of the claim that these emit healthy negative ions. Here is a review from a site that lab tested salt lamps with a sensitive ion detector:

"Salt lamps are indeed beautiful. But do they emit meaningful levels of negative ions? Having personally tested a popular brand of rock salt crystal lamp in our lab, we can attest that it was all but worthless as a generator of negative ions. After measuring the negative ion output level from the salt lamp, we took our sensitive negative ion detector outdoors and measured a far higher lever of naturally occurring negative ions than the salt lamp emitted."

Summary: If you want a really beautiful mood lamp at a bargain price, buy one of these -- you won\x27t be disappointed. But don\x27t be fooled into thinking that it will be a significant source of "negative ions".

review_headline: This is been one of my favorite purchases in the last year
review_body:
This is been one of my favorite purchases in the last year. I knew I needed a C wire for the thermostat to work so this was motivation to run the third wire and finally get remote thermostat control. One I figured that out it connected to the hub and was showing in the app in under a minute. the lamp modules basically add in a second after you hold the button on them and the app will find them right away. I got hooked and had to by the First Alert SA521CN ONELINK Hardwire Wireless Smoke Alarm that communicated with the INSTEON 2982-222 Smoke Bridge perfectly, and now I\x27m getting smoke and CO alerts from ANY smoke detector in my house. The Nest cannot compete with that because I have 9 smoke detectors linked to my Insteon hub with alerts for under $100. I also put in a leak detector near my hot water heater for informational purposes/alerts but I do plan to link it with a main shutoff valve now that I see how easy this stuff is.

I feel this is well worth $200 and I know Insteon is growing and is now going to work with Siri and Apple HomeKit soon with their new Hub.

My one complaint so far is that they offer alerts for Door and Motion sensors but there is no easy way to turn off the alerts for all your sensors at once when you get home, it will just keep alerting you unless you turn off alerts on each individual sensor. You would need a computer controlling it or an ISY to do this as it stands right now. This product is still amazing for what you pay and what you get at your fingertips once it is set up. You will be happy with it

review_headline: Nice look. Two persons required for installation.
review_body: These pendant lights really improve the looks of a kitchen. Very classy.   In retrospect, not a very difficult installation if one pays attention to a few details:    The 3/8\x5C\x22 screws provided are too short for a convenient attachment of the canopy over the mounting plate. They are difficult to grip while holding the pieces in place. Use 1\x5C\x22 screws (#8-32) until the attachment is complete and then go back and change out your 1\x5C\x22 screws with the provided brown screws.    If possible, attach the mounting plate to a ceiling joist instead using wall anchors in the sheet rock. You may have to drill some new holes in the mounting plate, but that is no big deal. Be sure to drill pilot holes into the joists or you will eventually strip the screw heads.    Secure the extra wire in the canopy with tape. This will keep the wire from migrating to the edge where it will interfere with slipping the canopy over the mounting plate and subsequent screw hole alignment.    Use large wire nuts to connect the bundle of 4 wires to a pigtail. Connection of the pigtail to the power supply is simpler than trying to connect 4 x 3 strands of wire.    Clean the globes before installation. Try to avoid leaving fingerprints during the installation.    The attachment of the canopy to the mounting plate is a two person job. One person will find the installation frustrating.

review_headline: Flawless Performance and Ideal for Temporary Outdoor Lighting
review_body:
The purpose of the Wowtou Solar Motion Light is that it utilizes the suns daily solar power which charges the inside battery for an outside area after dark; it illuminates an area when it detects any motion. The Wowtou is a motion sensor light, it only illuminates when the sensors detect movement, just to be clear, it is not a night light that remains on.

The Wowtou is approximately 7\xE2\x80\x9D X 5\xE2\x80\x9D X \xC2\xBD\xE2\x80\x9D, and it is hung horizontally so that the sun is able to charge the top solar panel. The Solar area of the panel is large approximately 5 \xC2\xBD\xE2\x80\x9D X 3 \xC2\xBD\xE2\x80\x9D, which is the largest solar panel of any solar light that we own. It comes with its own bracket, a couple of smaller screws, two larger screws with plastic anchors to insert into the drilled holes, and small one-inch pin with a round loop at the end. On the underside of the solar panel are 3 pinholes. The small one-inch pin is for insertion into the on/off hole and then removed. This is a one-time activation; the Wowtou Solar Powered Motion Sensor is ready for placement on the bracket.

We have installed the Wowtou outside our backdoor, right around the corner on the east side of the house. This side of the house has no electrical lighting down the alleyway, until the very front. This is where my husband\xE2\x80\x99s large outside grill area is located, and since he barbeques in the evening and after dark, he has always had to fumble with a flashlight, which is inconvenient, and gave poor lighting. The installed Wowtou provides a large area of illumination, and now he can actually see to barbeque. The Wowtou is so sensitive to motion, that as soon as we step outside, the light detects the motion and immediately goes on. The convenience of the motion sensor is that it stays on the entire time he is working. About 15 seconds after he leaves the area, the light goes out. This is convenient for us, because we live in close proximity to our neighbors, and we do not want the light to stay on and shine through their windows. This is also a perfect location, because there is a single step down from our patio, and in the dark, we are unable to see the step.

The Wowtou Solar Motion Light is encased in a metal body, it is waterproof and heatproof, and the light is bright without any glare. It only takes a short time of sunlight to charge the battery, and the battery remains charged for days because it does not remain lit during the night. We have had a week of rain and overcast skies, but the Wowtou still works every night due to the short time of use, which is only when it detects any movement.

The Wowtou is an excellent product and the performance is flawless, the set up only takes a minute, the soft lighting illuminates a large area, and we like that the light turns off automatically within 15 seconds rather than staying on all night. In addition, if the Wowtou is hung low enough to reach, the light panel can be slipped off the bracket to serve the purpose of a bright flashlight in the dark. This is an ideal illumination for any outdoor dark location, where temporary lighting is required.

The black plastic fan part was also rubbing on the motors coil as well. The old inducer motor shaft could me moved back and forth about 1/2 inch which was allowing rubbing to occur. I removed the old motor and replace it with this one. Took less then 30 minutes to mount this new motor. Turned unit back on and its even more quit then it was new from the factory. Saved myself a $350.00 service call by installing myself! This motor is used under several part #\x27s and is a perfect replacement for several furnace brands.

One note: the large side jam is solid wood, but also has a veneer surface applied. Do not be alarmed, this is a good thing. They apply a very nice pine grain veneer over the stabilized subsurface. product_title: Waste King Legend Series 3/4 HP Continuous Feed Garbage Disposal with Power Cord - (L-3200)
review_headline: It\x27s easy to install, good quality, and has a great warranty.
review_body:
The shipping was incredibly fast despite not being Prime eligible. I ordered it on Friday and was expecting to receive it Tuesday. It arrived Saturday afternoon and had it installed that night. Installation was a snap with one exception. I was replacing a Badger 1 unit. The 1-1/2" drain from the Badger used a compression washer and threader collar whereas the Waste King uses a flanged pipe, rubber gasket and bolt on metal bracket. The Wast King kit includes a flanged angled drain pipe for use in a configuration where it drains directly into the pee trap. However, in my configuration the disposal drains into a tee connection from the second sink and then into the pee trap. This required purchasing a flanged straight drain pipe from Home Depot for a couple of bucks. The extra time was the only inconvenience. Installation was quick and easy.

The quality appears to be high. It\x27s about as noisy as the Badger, not really quiet. It handles all the same stuff we threw at the Badger just as well. The 8 year warranty is awesome and worth the few extra bucks as the Badger only lasted 2 years and cost nearly as much.

product_title: Gold Flexible Glue Gun Sealing Wax - 7 Sticks
review_headline: Used these on over 100 invitations, very fast, high quality
review_body:
I have had zero experience with glue gun sealing wax. S I was able to seal around 113 event invitations -- even with all of the glue gun dripping -- in about 45 minutes with one pack of 7 sticks. About half way through, I discovered a dime sized worth of wax is more than enough for a seal, so with proper technique, you can squeeze even stamps more out of a pack (but get more than you just in case!). I was using the standard wax seal stamp that you probably see all over amazon. It\x27s about an inch in size.

This wax has a very nice, classy gold finish. I have some other gold wax from a kit (the kind you melt in a spoon), and this glue wax was much higher quality. Don\x27t be scared about putting it into a glue gun. It comes out nothing like hot glue. The wax has the correct amount of fluidness and does not stick to the stamp. The wax sticks very well to the paper envelopes I was using. I sealed them anyway, but I am sure the wax would have probably held the paper.

I used the "Surebonder L-270 Low Temperature Standard Glue Gun" and it was a perfect fit.

I have used sealing wax the old fashioned way with a spoon -- this is probably 100x faster with more consistent results. I did not have to deal with any messes or burnt wax.

review_body:
so i read back through some of the reviews, and i must say they\x27re interesting. one person was upset about shipping (1 star review); so why not review the SELLER and not the product.

a couple of things to note: hopefully this will be helpful for those on the fence about this product. the clarity is on purpose; i wish that people understood why, and they would probably give this thing better reviews. it\x27s purposely textured because this further prevents someone from seeing in via the reflective mirrors contained in the unit. you are supposed to apply a very thin coating of patroleum jelly to give that "dry" look a bit more clarity. it\x27s actually a pretty nice lens, but the "dry" look is not only easily reduced, but it\x27s on purpose.

another reviewer said that the image was upside down. wow! it\x27s flipped vertically because it\x27s using a prism/lens method for projecting the image on a textured surface. think of a much, much, MUCH clearer version of a shoebox sun viewer. just rotate the lens a 1/4 turn and you\x27re looking at a picture right-side up, but (like i said) flipped vertically. why give the product a poor review because of your lack of understanding?

one more thing is about night vision...yes...it will be a bit harder to see than a normal peephole...will it work? yup...look at my photos. you can see just fine in normal scenarios and i\x27ll go a step further and say that it works really well if you have a porch light. now, if you don\x27t have a porch light...you should make that your FIRST purchase anyway. move on to that before you get this....

lastly, there\x27s one thing that got me, although i\x27m not going to take away a star (although I probably should). the outside cover is chrome. this is perfect...exactly what i needed to match our door handles etc. the other parts are more like....brushed aluminum. why not make them the same all around? maybe corrosion? i guess i should try to understand this before docking the review, because there could be a good reason for it. over all though, it\x27s really barely noticeable...this is a negligible gripe.ng the review, because there could be a good reason for it. over all though, it\x27s really barely noticeable...this is a negligible gripe.

review_body: Just installed the Nutone EZ80N fan in our master bath and installation had it\x27s ups and downs.  On the good side, the fan housing installed easily.  Using the provided cardboard template I enlarged the opening without much fuss, removed the old unit, and slid the fan housing into the opening.  Since it\x27s employs "old work" style screws with wings, a simple turn of any screw was enough to hold it into place before securing the housing to the ceiling drywall. If you have access to the attic it would be wise to take a look a the old fan from above before you start to make sure that both the current electrical and exhaust hose will reach the new configuration and that no obstacles are blocking the unit.  It was a close call on my wiring, but I had just enough to comfortably make the connections to the new unit.  Our exhaust hose was never installed by the builder, unless you count the 4 inch long piece that terminated in the insulation, so I had to purchase a hose and connect it to the exhaust pipe the was there. Additionally, we had a short piece of 2X4 nailed between the joists that had to be removed because it interfered with the installation of the hose to the housing.  Probably just a rare occurrence but it\x27s best to take a look before you start if possible.  Now for the bad.  EZ it ain\x27t. The fan unit itself does not have any way of temporarily securing it to the housing before permanently attaching it.  This means that you have to hold the unit in one hand and press it over your head into the housing while trying to line up screws with the holes in the housing using the other hand.  It is nearly impossible.  The screws do have some plastic washers to retain them to the fan unit; however, these can be easily knocked loose as you try to line up the unit with the mounting base.  Have fun picking them up off the floor or out of your sink trap if you don\x27t close the sink stopper.  What moron designed this I do not know? product_title: SimpliSafe Wireless Home Security Command
review_body:
I have had Simplisafe for 1 month. The system was easy to install with most items using the 3M strips for easy removal if needed. The extra siren, smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detector could also be mounted with bracket and screws. I did need to call customer service and they were very helpful and took their time with me until the issue was resolved. Testing the system was easy and the base station can easily be moved during the testing process. I have had 2 alarms go off (as they should have) and the dispatch centers response time was impressive - they also did their best to ensure I was not in any danger. I love the iPhone app to be able to turn off and on my system, see any events and to call SimpliSafe or the dispatch center. You can personalize your set up using your online account such as naming each device and indicating if you want that sensor on while the system is either in away mode, home mode or both. You can also indicate if a sensor is an instant trigger rather than delayed; set up text messaging or e-mail for system status and events. It really makes me feel like I am in charge of my system and I can modify it at anytime should I need to.

I have had other alarm systems and companies and I never felt like I was in control of my system - Simplisafe gives me that sense of control. I also feel like this system, compared to others, allowed me to include so many more sensors at a fraction of the cost and by adding sensors it did not cause my monitoring fee to increase. I have all bases of my home covered; windows, doors, motion, glass, fire, carbon monoxide, and water. It also uses a cellular service and a hardline for back up if needed - to add cellular service to an existing system would have been over $400! I look at this as an investment and I can take my equipment with me if I move - I think I made a wise decision and don\x27t have any regrets.

product_title: Best Choice Products SKY1421 25 gal Bench Top Air Sandblast Cabinet
review_headline: Actual Item improved over one in picture & many reviews.
review_body: I ordered one of these online from Best Choice Products and received an improved, updated version of what is pictured, which I am very happy about!  The design pictured was the main reason I considered other blast cabinets.  DIFFERENCE #1__ is in the shape of the floor of the cabinet where the sand falls to and collects. In the picture, it is a "V" shaped trough. Reviews of this design from Amazon, YouTube, & Tractor Supply site this as one of the major flaws, causing a disruption in the flow of media where a user has to stop mid-project to manually pile the media up around the end of the pick-up tube. The one I received has a conical 4-sided triangular floor with a pickup mounted at the lowest point in the center! The main reason I was considering paying significantly more for another unit was to get the Triangular floor with center pickup that this one ended up coming with anyways! Cool! It seems as though Best Choice is paying attention to reviews and making small improvements in the product over time to satisfy their customers. I really appreciate that!  DIFFERENCE #2__Mine also arrived mostly pre-assembled with the seams sealed with silicone--another sign of improvement from leaks reported in early reviews.  DIFFERENCE #3__A brace was mounted to the bottom of the screen in the one I received to help keep it from bending excessively under the weight of heavier parts--also a fix of complaints from previous reviews.  The only other improvement I can think of would be to paint it a lighter color--at Least the Interior. This would reflect the light around the inside work area better to make the most of the lower wattage bulb that is included with the unit and improve visibility. I plan to spray the inside of mine with a glossy white enamel, but it would probably be yet another practical affordable improvement if you are reading this, Best Choice.  Inside dimensions of the blasting area of this are 23"W x 19"D x 12"H(top of floor grate to top of glove wall). Keep in mind, however, that some of the 19" depth will not be usable to factor in the size of parts you are blasting, as your hands inside the gloves will be taking up some of that space. Thank you.

product_title: Hangman Anti-Tip Kit - 400 Pound Falling Furniture Prevention Device (TK-400)
review_headline: Easily Installed, Strong Device Can be Quickly Detached
review_body: This is a well-made product.  My application is a tall and narrow glass curio cabinet that could easily be tipped a lateral force were to be applied.  The cable is easily attached and disconnected from the brackets supplied to secure it to the wall and to the piece of furniture.  This is done simply by pulling the spring key and then removing the pins that attache the cable end loops to the brackets.  Once one has the furniture repositioned, reattaching to the flexible cables is just as easily accomplished.  In both cases, the brackets used to secure the top or back of the furniture piece and to the wall have two mounting screws which appear to be adequate to the task.  It is important that the wall bracket be screwed to a stud, so locating it with a stud finder or by some other method is essential.  A hollow wall (drywall) anchor would not be sufficient to secure the device to the wall given the torque that might be created if the furniture piece would become unstable.  Likewise, it\x27s important to anchor the other bracket to the furniture one is attempting to stabilize by attaching it to a strong component, not the flimsy plywood backing that is used on some furnishings.  \x5C\x22Common sense\x5C\x22 should always be observed, though it\x27s been my observation that \x27good sense it\x27s so very \x5C\x22common\x5C\x22 after all.\x27  Just exercise abundant caution when considering the locations with which to attach both ends of this device.

review_headline: Works perfectly with LEDs and Vera if you can get it installed
review_body:
Even though it says "incandescent only" right on the side of the switch, this works perfectly with both Philips and Utilitech Pro dimmable LED bulbs. It was EASY to pair with my Vera (just press the on switch to make it pair).

Installation was a bit strange. First of all, you have to use pliers to break off some metal bits if you want to make it fit alongside another switch. The manual says doing so reduces the amount of power it can control from 500 to 300 watts, though with LEDs that\x27s hardly a concern. Then you have to find your "neutral" wire. My house came with 3-wire switches, but I eventually realized there were 4 wires. They were all capped together and shoved in the back of the box.

MAKE SURE YOU HAVE ALL 4 WIRES BEFORE YOU BUY THIS! You need BOTH the ground (bare) wire and the neutral (white) wire in addition to the normal line and load wires.

The manual also says how you can reconfigure everything down to the LED blinking behavior using a Z-wave controller - but for most people it should do just what they want right out of the box.

I have mine set to slowly brighten my bedroom in the morning to wake me up. It\x27s sweet! Highly recommended!

product_title: Ecobee3 Thermostat, Wi-Fi, Remote Sensor, 1st Generation, Works with Amazon Alexa
review_body: I was really excited to get this thermostat; we bought a house and were looking to make it as efficient as possible by using the schedule feature. I considered Nest, but didn\x27t like the \x5C\x22learning\x5C\x22 curve. I considered Lyric, but it just seemed too buggy. Besides, both my Thermostats (upstairs and downstairs) are located in hallways and I really like the remote sensor idea. After some trouble with the installation (due to the house wiring, not the thermos), I was unpleasantly surprised to see the temperature readings several degrees off from what another independent thermometer read. Other articles suggested it took a couple of days for Ecobee to \x5C\x22settle in\x5C\x22--well it never has. The remote sensors have proven pretty accurate, but the temp sensor on the thermostat itself is sometimes as much as 9 F different than the thermometer! When trying to regulate the temp, a 9 degree difference is huge! It seems like the unit runs slightly warm from the continual power, and that may be influencing its temperature reading. I\x27ve deactivated temperature reading on both thermostats--but now I\x27m back to the 1 sensor for each floor; that\x27s a buzzkill seeing as the averaging temperatures were the main appeal and differentiator.    Also, it seems like the temperature reading \x5C\x22falls asleep\x5C\x22 once my comfort level has been reached. My Thermostat will heat the room to 67, and continue to read that, even while the room gets cooler. I\x27ll turn on the thermostat by increasing my temperature level, and as air starts moving again, the thermostat\x27s temperature reading begins to fall. It\x27s like it \x5C\x22wakes up\x5C\x22 and remembers it is supposed to actively be reading the temperature. This happens multiple times a day.    Additionally, I\x27ve had one thermostat (2nd floor) freeze on me and need me to cut the power and start it over again.    Finally, a lot of people have raved about the Customer Support--I\x27ve called once and left a message, and emailed a couple days later, and I have yet to hear back from either medium. So, color me less than impressed.    I\x27m more patient with technology than my wife, so I\x27m willing to see if any updates are coming out. My wife is ready to return them. I\x27m actually beginning to consider the other offerings I referenced earlier...    I\x27ll update this as it improves or gets worse. For my sake, I hope it gets better.    UPDATE 2/6/15:   Ecobee support finally got back to me. They suggested (while the commenter) to use Plumber\x27s putty in the hole of the wall. I did that, but still the thermostat read (on average) 4 F higher than it should. Well, Ecobee support told me how to make a temperature adjustment in the installation settings. That worked like a charm. Now it works much nicer, since the temperature reading is more accurate.    I\x27ll hold off on giving it 5 stars because I would like to see Ecobee work with other companies more. Like I\x27m not thrilled with Nest, they are doing many things to open their APK up to other products/companies to really create a connected house. For instance, is ecobee worked with Ecovent Systems closing registers, it would be a home run product.    I would still suggest this product.

review_body: I have bought a total of 25 of these bulbs.  Every one of them works PERFECTLY! product_title: Kohler 81996 Replacement Switch Assembly,
review_headline: When you need your best friend back
review_body:
As this could be the most expensive switch most people ever buy (and it is made out of plastic), I have a hard time leaving 5 stars. However, if you have one of these power flush toilets, your only alternative is to scrap the toilet and switch to a regular toilet or or pay a plumber to diagnose the toilet and replace the same three parts you can replace yourself with ease (since many plumbers do not see this type of toilet often, misdiagnoses even from a professional plumber is possible as well) The switch is very simple to change this switch out yourself and Kohler has excellent customer service reps that will walk you through it if you are hesitant.

In my particular case, the fill valve over time had corroded and would squirt water out of the top into the switch. Eventually the switch was damaged by the water and stopped working. The first step is to lift the cover off and inspect the inside of the switch connector for corrosion. Then adjust the fill valve (press down on the float) so the fill valve opens and fills the reservoir. When it fills, if any water leaks or sprays from the top of the fill valve, you must replace the fill valve. This valve (when functioning properly) should fill the reservoir from the bottom only and not spray water at all from the top. The Kohler fill valve is expensive, but regular fill valves (the kind you can buy at Home Improvement stores) cannot be adjusted down to a low enough fill level (I believe this toilet reservoir tank has an overflow level of less than 5") and regular fill valves cannot adjust below 5.5" (yes, I tried to save $80 and failed miserably!).

If you replace the switch and the fill valve and you still have a problem, it is very likely the pump. The pump is the most expensive part of the power flush system and costs around $450. It is best to decide if the toilet is worth it to you if you suspect pump failure before you buy this switch.

This switch is expensive for what it is, but my best friend is worth it!

product_title: OMNIFilter OT32-S-05 Drop-in Undersink Filter OT32
review_body: Bought this newer (\x5C\x22Series E\x5C\x22) version to replace a 2002-era OT-32, which was functioning fine/not leaking or cracked, etc - but I was tired of trying to figure out Omni\x27s frustrating filter cartridge \x5C\x22version\x5C\x22 numbers (often not on labels) in trying to fit the newer, slightly larger CB3 filters AND, it turns out, Omni recommends changing out earlier units based on reports of units \x5C\x22cracking\x5C\x22 or leaking - although, as I said, mine was fine.     Initially just tried to spin the new canister on the older upper mount but the threads were different- so I ended up replacing/replumbing the unit. Original model used a saddle-valve, which I retained as the supply point (since it had already made a hole in the pipe...). As other reviewers have noted, plumbing is simple (and I have had no leaks) with the supplied 1/4\x5C\x22 flex tubing and push-connectors, but will be more complicated if you\x27re trying to use copper. Since I installed the original unit I have redone the upstream plumbing (old farmhouse now on city water), so I have no real rust/dirt filtration requirements, so I took one filter offline (removed the canister and plumbed the \x5C\x22out\x5C\x22 line into the first canister)  - so now using a single canister with a CB3 (which you can also buy elsewhere). Having said that, we DID have a significant filtration problem for years and the dual-cartridge unit worked like a charm - I generally had about a 2-3 to 1 lifespan ratio for rough/1st-stage filters to the final CB3. You can, of course, use CB1\x27s in the unit but I have found the CB3s make the water taste noticeably better than the CB1s do.     Although the Omni (confusing and outdated (see my review of the CB3 filter) website indicates the older (slimmer) CB3 is the correct filter for this \x5C\x22series\x5C\x22 housing, I called Omni Tech Support and verified that the \x5C\x22Series E\x5C\x22 (latest version, and the one I received from Amazon)) OT-32 WILL, in fact, accept new/current (slightly larger) versions of the CB3 filter - and, in fact, it does. Works great and provides good tasting, allegedly clean water.

product_title: AC Smoke/CO Alarm
review_headline: that way if they go off again I know where in the house to look for fire or find the dirty one. To clean with canned air
review_body:
I replaced eight old interconnected detectors with these Kidde KN-COPE-IC combo PhotoElectric/CO2 detectors. Over the last year three of the detectors would not stop alarming. I tried using canned air to clean them, but the Kidde web sight was not clear on where to spray. I finally called their support line and a very friendly and helpful woman told me exactly where to spray the air. That fixed all three alarms. These PhotoElectric alarms are very sensitive to dust particles. This is not an issue with these Kidde ones, just all PhotoElectric ones. PhotoElectrics are required for use near bathrooms and kitchens in the state I live in, so I am going to have to clean these things out every once in a while. I wish that you could add a location on the alarms, that way if they go off again I know where in the house to look for fire or find the dirty one. To clean with canned air:

1. Disconnect the detector and open the battery door
2. Turn the detector so that you can read the the text on the back
3. Look through the open space around the edge at around 11 o\x27clock (the left side near the top. Locate the round black sensor.
4. Spray the canned air at that sensor, aiming to spry through the fins on it, parallel with the text on the back of the detector. You can also gently shake the detector up and down while doing this.
5. Close the battery door and test the alarm, it should stop after going through its test.

product_title: Aquasana Shower Filter
review_headline: For the tall person with a BIG shower area, not for the average height person with normal space to shower in.
review_body:
Two stars is due to how this product sits on the shower arm. If you are a tall person with plenty of room in your shower area, then this may be for you. If you are average height, with normal space to shower, then you may be inclined to look else where. I have had this for several years now. I do like this product, however, how it sits on the shower arm is absurd for the average height person with normal space to shower in .

So, I have to have it sit sideways so to speak, and then it leaks galore. Just as someone else stated how it leaks unless you get it JUST right. If you move the filter any so that it sprays on you not across the tub/shower area, then expect leakage.

I\x27ve tried dealing with it, with all of the maneuvering, but I\x27m tired of trying to fight it. I think FOUR YEARS of testing is enough testing!?!?

For the expense of this it surely is NOT worth it. As much as this is, and it does fairly good filtering, looks like this company would make a short stem part for height adjustments on the arm, verses just long arm it attaches to.

If you have a BIG shower area then this may work for you. If you live in a normal house normal shower area, trust this review, or you may regret the price you paid for something to be so annoying and not work as you wish.

-The dial for different pressures seams to be useless since it ultimately comes down to the water pressure coming out of the faucet

-The clip on end that comes with the unit is a little lacking but it still gets the job done.

product_title: Honeywell RCT8100A 7-Day Programmable Thermostat
review_body:
We have used this thermostat for several years. It has been great for us. It is easy to program, turns on and off as scheduled. The only issue we have had is that the heater tended to cycle on and off several times per hour. I think this happened for 3 reasons 1) our ducts leaked like sieves allowing more cool air into the house making the heater work harder than necessary, 2) the heater was really old (30-40 years), 3) I think there might be a setting on the thermostat that only allows the heater to cycle on 4 times per hour and I think this was not set to on and I was too lazy to try to change it.

The 7 day program is nice because every day can have a different schedule if wanted. And the program is very easy to override, just increase or decrease the temp as needed.

I cannot say how it works with a/c since we didn\x27t have it only heat.
Only reason we changed it was the HVAC co that installed the new heater also included a new programable thermostat.

review_headline: Keep your scraps until you are done
review_body: We were looking to keep the water as hot as possible to prolong showers in the morning. This product went on fairly easily as described. The double sided tape makes it a bit hard to slide it around the back by the wall but I figured out how to do it pretty quickly.  I have an 80 gal heater and with all 3 strips ( 2 x 24" and 1 x 15") I ended up with about a 5" gap at the top not covered.  I kept and used the cut off ends from each piece and had enough to fill in the gap.  DON\x27T THROW AWAY THE SCRAPS FROM CUTS UNTIL YOU ARE DONE IN CASE YOU NEED THEM. Because I had to fill in the space I used more tape than provided and had to go buy a roll at Home Depot. The end result looks fantastic and hopefully the power bill will go down a little. It is too soon to tell yet but I noticed immediately that I cannot feel any heat transferring to the outside everywhere that is covered.  Showers seem to last a bit longer now as we don\x27t have to turn the hot water on as high.

product_title: KOHLER K-72218-CP Sensate Touchless Kitchen Faucet
review_headline: looks great, works as described, DIY install went well.
review_body:
Got this installed January 2015 so we only have a few weeks of experience with using this faucet, but so far, it is great. The Kohler seemed like it might fit and clear the limited space we have between the faucet hole and the back splash.

Why we chose the Kohler Sensate Faucet. First, this touchless faucet only needs a wave of the hand in the crook of the neck. Unlike some other choices, as there is no touching the faucet at all, there are no transfer of skin oil, no water spots, etc on the faucet ever. The pull-out spray head has a nice magnetic docking feature to it seats back onto the neck for a nice fit when done using it. This magnetic feature wasn\x27t so obvious when unboxing the faucet, but it is noticeable after the installation, perhaps helped by the weight on the goose neck tubing under the sink. The water spray is in a fan shape, not a round spray, so it seems effective in sweeping liquids and particles down the drain. When not in the Spray setting, the stream of water from the faucet is very smooth with no aeration it seems. It is actually a nice flow of water and at 1.8 gpm, it is adequate. Our old faucet was rated at 2.2gpm so I was concerned about the loss of flow, but with the fan spray, cleaning is still effective and the non-splash flow of water in non-spray mode it great also. The faucet head has a two position manual selector on the backside to switch between spray or no-spray. The last mode selection remains even when the water is turned off/on until you switch it again. The faucet also has an auto-off feature that only kicked in once when filling a large pot. I don\x27t expect this feature to be a nuisance the way we use our faucet for cooking & cleaning and I suppose it can save water if there are times when the auto-off feature is invoked by the faucet being on for an extended period.

Installation - Installation of the Kohler went smoothly with well thought out fittings and design of the hardware. The instructions for the Kohler could have been slightly more detailed e.g. explaining that the supply lines had built-in washers that are concealed. Took a chance that there were would be a water tight fit by attaching the hoses and turning on the water slowly. Well, it didn\x27t leak. Overall, I would say it was only a moderately difficult install because I have a very crowded undersink cabinet.

Once I had hooked up the faucet, no fine tuning was needed - it just worked! I had prepared myself for fiddling and trouble shooting but the concern was unnecessary as the faucet worked perfectly. As you can see from the photo, the clearance between the faucet neck and the granite window sill is about 1/8" (32mm) so I was very relieved about that since the neck isn\x27t round, but oval in shape. This oval shape of the neck is attractive and is another aspect that sets this faucet apart from others.

The faucet has an LED on the handle to show that power is on and it is in touchless mode. If the LED is unlit, then the faucet is in manual mode so don\x27t bother waving a hand.
