product_title: Everpure H-104 Water Filter Replacement Cartridge (EV9612-11)
review_body:
Great filter! I had 1 that my plumber installed and it lasted over a year. The water still tasted fine but I was a little concerned after the 1 year mark so I replaced it. Removal and installation of the filter were relatively easy. The price does seem like a lot at first glance but if you divide it over 12 months, it\x27s more affordable than bottled water or Pur filters.

FILTER REMOVAL/INSTALLATION TIPS
Several notes on installation: 1) Put a bucket or a large towel under the filter to catch any water drips from the filter when removing the old and installing the new filter. 2) Push the filter fully into the housing and then turn it counter-clockwise until it locks. (Judge the amount of twist based on how much it took you to untwist the old filter.) Be sure to click on the latch before turning on the water. I did not twist the cartridge enough and had a little flood after I turned on the filter. Make sure you run the filter for 15 minutes to flush out any trapped air and residue. Put a label with the installation date so you remember to change the filter before 12 months have passed.

I also have trouble removing the filter from the housing. I was advised to use a strap wrench to have more leverage and add some silicone-based o-ring lubricant around the threads to reduce the friction and prevent o-ring from bunching up. The strap wrench worked and I was able to remove the old filter. We were concerned about using a non-food grade silicone lubricant so we used a bit of vegetable oil instead. Hope these tips will help you.

NOTE ABOUT THE CHEAPER BUT INTERIOR S-104 FILTER - AVOID AT ALL COST!
I initially replaced my H-104 filter with the S-104 to save $10. According to the specs, the only difference is the H-104 reduces lime and scales but all of the filtration specs is the same for both filters. THIS WAS A MISTAKE! 6 months later, the water tasted worse than unfiltered water. So, I called Everpure to trouble-shoot. I was told that I need to replace the filter as it is likely "full" and thus not filtering properly (eventhough there is no change in the flow). How is that possible since the old H-104 had lasted over a year with the same water usage pattern??? So, I asked whether there is any warranty for this issue as the filter is supposed to last about a year and it\x27s non-operational after 6 months. I was told there is no warranty for the longevity of the filter. So, in saving $10, I wasted $50. This is a raw deal for a seemingly more economical option. product_title: Luxe Bidet Neo 120 (Elite Series) - Self Cleaning Nozzle - Fresh Water Non-Electric Mechanical Bidet Toilet Attachment w/ Strong Faucet Valves and Metal Hoses
review_body:
When I first tried a bidet over a year ago in Japan, I knew I had to have one. However, the one I tried in Japan was a top end model, with electric, hot water, and all sorts of settings. Those models demand a high price that I was unwilling to pay. When I found this model, I was skeptical something so relatively cheap could be a good product. However, after over a year of putting it off, the positive reviews steadily mounted and looked entirely legit. I finally bit the bullet and ordered. I am glad I did.

As many others have pointed out, installation is a breeze. Just make sure you measure your seat and surrounding area to ensure there is physically enough space before you order. Additionally, the water pressure is indeed very high. I wouldn\x27t even put this past the halfway point for risk of creating a new hole back there. If you have lower pressure or buy a regulator valve, you won\x27t risk this. However, I can live with it because I really have no need for a wide range of settings.

I would also recommend this model because of the little door that shields the spray nozzle when not in use. This is a nice feature to help keep it clean, and probably well worth the slight bump in cost over the model one step down. There are also no issues with seat gap, unlike some other similar models seem to have. You can buy seat bumpers to prevent possibly cracking the seat if this does happen to you, so I wouldn\x27t worry too much about this. Also, I agree that the cold water is not an issue at all. Even if you hooked another model up to hot water, the water in the pipes between uses wouldn\x27t be warm anyway, so don\x27t bother with that.

product_title: Honeywell 7-Day Programmable Timer for Lights & Motors
review_headline: Well made hard wired timer.  Easy to install and program.  Great value.
review_body:
When I purchased my home I needed to have a radon fan installed as the radon level was just slightly above the advised limit. The fan, like any fan, makes some noise/vibration and the vent pipe goes right by my bedroom on the outside of the house. As a light sleeper this drove me nuts. All last winter I went to the basement and shut off the breaker to the fan each night. It wasn\x27t an issue during the summer thanks to open windows, crickets, tree frogs and other night time noise makers. Then it was winter again...

I started shopping for a hard wired timer looking at several variations. I kept coming back to the Honeywell and finally pulled the trigger on it. It arrived quickly thanks to Amazon Prime and I soon went to work. $6 in parts from the big box store bought me a place to mount it in the basement. I shut off the breaker and cut the electrical wire to the radon fan. New box installed and when I went to mount the Honeywell I found it wouldn\x27t fit in the metal faceplate. I needed to trim the mounting tabs on the timer to make it fit. This would have happened to any brand and is not the fault of Honeywell. Once the tabs were trimmed the timer mounted beautifully. Electrical connections were simple.

Programming the Honeywell could not have been easier. Set the time, set the day, set when you want it to come on and off. My program was simple and repeated each day. Off at 11p, on at 6a. It works wonderfully and there is now silence when I sleep (except when my kids wake up)

I highly recommend this timer and my only complaint is a lack of a backlight on the display. Certainly not a show stopper but it would make the timer even better.

As stated above, my radon level was just at the threshold for a mitigation system and I am comfortable shutting it off. Consult a radon professional before shutting off your mitigation system.

review_headline: Cute looking lantern, but could have been better if LED was placed inside the fake candle
review_body:
This solar lantern is made of all plastic body, including the 4 transparent walls. It has solar panels on the top and a 1200mAh Ni-MH rechargable battery located at the bottom compartment, which is removable, therefore battery is also replaceable. There is a ON/OFF switch located at the bottom. Once it is turned ON, the lantern can work automatically. It charges using sunlight during day time and then automatically turns ON the light during night time. It uses a standard white LED bulb that flickers like a candle glowing inside a lantern. Since it is a single LED bulb, the light glows pretty much all night, provided there is enough sunlight during the day, for charging.

The lantern is not water proof, so make sure to remember it when placing it on patio or your garden. I liked the flickering effect of the lantern, and almost resembles a real candle effect But there is a drawback, the LED light is located on the top, and not at the bottom fake candle, therefore the unit has to be placed at head level or below, because positioning it up will expose the LED light, and spoils the experience. There is no need to turn ON and OFF the lantern every night, a sensor in it takes care of it automatically.

review_body:

The only reason I dinged them one star is that there is no seal for the top of the unit - I went to the hardware store and got a o-ring myself to create a watertight seal.

Originally I tried to adapt the larger outlet back to 1/2 inch, but doing so caused water to spirt out the top three holes. I realized that the reason the outlet is larger is that the water from the dishwasher is under pressure, and so a passive drain of the same diameter will not work. I am now going to move the drain from a second sink pipe nipple to the disposal (which has a 3/4" nipple for this purpose).

The top rotates easily so you can install it with the 3 holes facing backwards if you want - for aesthetics.

review_headline: Great night light for when the power goes out.
review_body:
This is a great product. I was able to setup the main control in my kitchen which is center to all the locations I wanted to light up. I successfully setup a couple lights in the hall and stair well upstairs and a few on the main floor all while still getting two in the basement. If you unplug the flashlight from the outlet, everything turns on as well as there is an on switch if you want to manually turn them on. I feel very safe my kids will make it down the steps in the event of a midnight power failure and one needs to go to the bathroom or something :)
I\x27ve had the same batteries in them for several months now, regardless that they are not turned on that often, but the batteries are still strong. Just a few very bright LED\x27s wont kill batteries very quickly and I expect they last through the year or more.
My only warning is to make sure that you attach them with the included screws. Even after cleaning the walls, the sticky stuff on the back will eventually come loose and scare the hell out of you in the middle of the night :)
I already recommended this to a few friends and would continue.

product_title: Aprilaire 500 Humidifier, 24V Whole House Humidifier w/ Auto Digital Control Bypass Damper .5 Gallons/ hour
review_body: Fairly good instructions and easy to install, even in old furnaces. Runs a lot the first 24 hours (which concerned me as this was not noted in the paperwork). But this seems to be the system \x5C\x22learning\x5C\x22 the house b/c humidity is maintained without a lot of runtime (Midwest, January) after the initial 24 hours. One thing that is not clear that I found on a Youtube video for the install of the 700 model is that the 24 volt transformer has a 24v terminal and a 10v terminal. The instructions do not say how to hook these up to the solenoid/control module. It may not make a difference, but according to the Youtube video and my installation, the unit works properly when the 24v terminal goes to the solenoid before going to the control module. The 10v terminal goes directly to the control module.    Needed items not included:    18-5 thermostat wire, used to connect the control module to the furnace. TIP: Use the green in this new wire to connect to the green tsat wire previously running to the G furnace terminal (disconnect completely from furnace), then use the new yellow to connect Gf control module to G on the furnace.    18-2 thermostat wire, used to connect the outside temperature sensor to the control module and to connect the 24v transformer to the solenoid and control module. TIP: run the red wire from 24v transformer to one of the yellow solenoid wires. Then use the same red wire to continue on to the second H terminal on the control module. Run the accompanying white wire uninterrupted to the first H terminal on the control module.    Electrical box to mount the transformer inside the furnace. You may need a small amount of romex to connect the transformer to the electric before it reaches the furnace.    Small bag of 1/2\x5C\x22 sheet metal screws.  Two, 3/4\x5C\x22 sheet metal screws for the control module.    Wire mounting brackets.    PVC pipe for drain line + 1/2\x5C\x22 ID clear flexible drain line.    Thin copper water line (not sure of specs b/c my line was already ran to an old humidifier).    My bypass install required two, 90 degree 6\x5C\x22 elbows; one, 6\x5C\x22 starter collar; and a couple feet of 6\x5C\x22 duct. All round. I also needed some spare sheet metal, duct sealer, and aluminum duct tape to patch holes from the old humidifier b/c its openings were different than the Aprilaire 500.    I\x27m pretty handy, not scared of electrical work, and have a basic knowledge of HVAC. This install took me about 3.5 hours, most of which was cutting out the sheet metal on the return and supply plenums. I used a hand tool for most of it, which took a long time. Halfway through I switched to a metal cutting blade on a reciprocating saw (this was much faster and would have \x5C\x22cut\x5C\x22 my time at least in half had I done it from the beginning).    In short, the only problem with a DIY install of this unit is that it supposedly voids the 5 year limited warranty.  A real shame because this is very easy to install.

product_title: Brightech - The Original Starry Solar String Lights by Brightech - 20ft LED Light String Set with Solar Panel
review_body:
Included with the 20 feet set of warm white lights are the instructions, the solar panel with off/on switch, mounting hardware, plastic mounting ground stake, plastic wall mount, and several feet of wiring from the solar panel connecting to the 20 feet of lighting.

Brightech sent me several different sets as samples for review (each I will review separately) and this set quality is essentially the same as the other 20 foot sets. This warm white set is approximately 20 feet in length with small LED lights spaced about 2 inches apart approximately. This set of lights has a large solar panel approximately 6 inches by 5 inches which contains a replaceable rechargeable battery. The lights are a nice warm (red hue) white light and make a nice decorative light. The wire is bendable and pretty durable for a thin wire but like all wire lighting like this you have to carefully bend. Like all solar lights, the length of time they will stay on is dependent on the amount of sun the panel gets during the day and the rechargeable battery life. These lights come with a 3 year warranty. I will update my review over time if I have any issues with long term durability.

Overall these are nice looking decorator lights at a reasonable price that have the flexibility of being mounted practically anywhere with the two different mounts and long cabling. These look nice but my personal preference are the multi-color set.

4 Stars

I was provided a sample for review and I do not promise a good rating in return, nor am I affiliated with this company or compensated in any way. I am just a regular Amazon customer who shops a lot on Amazon.

The adjust a gate system is easy to work with and I installed the whole thing solo. 2. Flexible - this is the real power of this gate. I had to have my gates to a precise width and height. I had a top rail cap on my fence and I wanted the gate to match the fence; therefore I had to be precise. If I had something fabricated instead of this product and my measurements were off by a hair:; it would all be a waste. This gate served this purpose beautifully. 3. Comes with everything you need. review_body: Bought this unit to replace a Kohree\xC2\xAE Wireless PIR Motion Sensor Super Bright 10 LED Light for use in a semi-dark closet.  This particular closet apparently receives too much light for the Kohree motion detector/auto-on to work consistently, and I couldn\x27t locate the light sensor to cover it.  Rather than return the Kohree, however, I moved it to another (darker) closet, where it is working quite well.  The Fulcrum seems to be somewhat less sensitive to light and is working flawlessly in the first closet.  However, I also note that the Fulcrum: 1) is noticeably brighter than the Kohree; 2) has a multi-function switch that allows it to operate manually or automatically with the built-in motion detector; 3) comes with a bracket that allows the light to be angled downward rather than just flat-mounted to the wall; and 4) easily pops out of the mounting bracket for battery replacement or use as a flashlight.  My only complaint is the same one mentioned by other reviewers - the template for the mounting bracket is \x5C\x22off\x5C\x22 by about half an inch.  Irritating though not a deal breaker, but, seriously, how did they get that so wrong??  In summary, the Fulcrum is more expensive than the Kohree, but for my particular need it was worth the extra cost.  FYI, I would note that the Kohree appears to be the same wireless light marketed under various other brand names on Amazon.  One final note: I do not yet know how quickly the Fulcrum (or the Kohree) will go through batteries, but I use Panasonic eneloop rechargeable AA batteries, which have been proven cost savers in all my remote controls and other portable devices.

product_title: K5Q9 11\x22 warm white under cabinet LED dimmable light
review_headline: Excellent replacement for 120v hard-wired under-counter fluorescent lighting.
review_body: I gave this a 5-star rating because it combines fluorescent task light replacement ease with price, and scores well in both categories. I used four of the 22\x5C\x22 fixtures and two 14\x5C\x22 fixtures (in the 2700K Warm White color) to replace my 8 watt and 16 watt fluorescent under-counter lighting in our kitchen.    These fixtures were direct replacements for my hard-wired 120v fluorescent fixtures and were fairly easy to install. These fixtures come with a standard wall socket power cord that plugs into the \x5C\x22input\x5C\x22 side of the fixture if you want to just plug them into the wall rather than hard-wire them. The power transformers are inside the fixture.  To accommodate hard-wiring, they have six knock-outs (3 on the back, 3 on the top) through which you can attach a Romex strain-relief connector and run 120v power into the fixture. (A Romex connector is supplied, though the quality is average.)  There is plenty of room to make 120v wiring connections on the inside of the 22\x5C\x22 fixtures, but less so on the 14\x5C\x22 fixtures.  I did manage to run three 14/2 romex feeds through a 14\x5C\x22 fixture ( two as a daisy-chain from the wall, and one going to another nearby fixture).  It was very tight, but it all fit. I used the internal input-output pass-through wires to make my 120v connections without having to make my wire-nut bundles huge.  Doing so disabled the plug-in cord option, but since I was hard-wiring, I didn\x27t care.    There is also an \x5C\x22output\x5C\x22 side to these fixtures so that they can be daisy-chained together using either a short plug (supplied) that connects the output of one fixture to the input of another, or a cord (not supplied) that connects the fixtures.  Of course, you can also daisy-chain them using Romex via the knock-outs.  The fixtures only draw 0.1 amp, so the instructions tell you to not daisy-chain more than 50 fixtures (5 amps).  50 fixtures?! You could pretty much light an entire house with 50 of these fixtures!  They are very bright for under-counter lighting and I could have easily used one 14\x5C\x22 fixture to replace each of my 16W under-counter fixtures.  However, they are also dimmable and the instructions include a list of compatible dimmers.    Mounting them involves using two screws 9.5 \x5C\x22 apart (for the 14\x5C\x22 fixture) and 15\x5C\x22 apart for the 22\x5C\x22 fixture.  (2 pan head screws and plastic inserts are supplied.) They use the pop-and-slide mounting method since it\x27s difficult to get to the screw holes with the access panel open.  However, it can be done since in one of my installations, I couldn\x27t slide the fixture to secure it, so I had to tweak the plastic cover, apply oversize screws, and then slap the fixture shut.  It was tricky, but it worked.  The pop-and-slide was much easier, though, especially when you tighten the mounting screws snugly then turn them out 3/4 of a turn.  The fixtures snapped right on. If you\x27re using romex through the connector, then you\x27ll need to set your screws at least 3\x5C\x22 away from the backboard.  Total depth for mounting needs to be at least 5.5\x5C\x22 to accommodate the fixture and the Romex connection.    Overall, I am vary happy with these fixtures and the bright warm light they give.

review_headline: Cyberstat. Met expectations, great low cost device to test this new category of home electronics
review_body:
It provides the basic functionality at a reasonable cost. I was looking for something with a standard preprogrammed schedule which I could change upon demand from my cellphone (i.e. to arrive home early to a warm house). Remote access set up easily but appears to be dependent upon Motison staying in business to keep the web interface running. Possibly they may offer a low cost option with additional features to create a revenue stream for the web services they provide.

Installation was a little challenging since all three of my existing sites only used two wires (no power connection)---but, in all three cases I had extra, unused wires and with some furnace schematic studying, found the required 24v "C" to add in the basement to one of the free wires.

Motison provides their installation manual on the web do prospective users and see what the Cyberstat requires before they order.

With electronics, most consumers are not really in a position to evaluate what they are buying until they have owned "it" for six months. The Cyberstat is a low cost way to get that experience---and after 6 months or a year, it is often the case that the price of the full featured devices have dropped to the point where the Cyberstat cost you nothing.

product_title: Whirlpool 8194001 Door Balance Link Kit for Dish Washer
review_headline: Double-action pulleys screached and squeaked in a KUDS01FLSS3 dsihwasher
review_body:
I have a KUDS01FLSS3 dishwasher. I\xE2\x80\x99ve gone through several door balance kits and springs in the products 11 years of service. I generally replace parts in pairs. When one spring broke, I replaced both springs. When one cord broke, I replaced both cords. This time, a plastic tab broke that holds the pulley assembly to the dishwasher broke. I bought this kit not remembering I had leftover spare parts. The new plastic pulley system came with 2 rotating pulleys. The old system had one rotating pulley and one fixed pulley. I installed the new pulleys on both sides and vaselined the new cords. After it was all put back together, it screeched. Maybe the grease is not needed with two rotating pulleys. Hard to take off the grease once it\xE2\x80\x99s been put on. I always used the vaseline on the cords to quiet the cords. I found the old style pulleys and installed them. The squeaky screeching went away. I also tired installing the double-action pulleys on the different tensioning holes. That didn\xE2\x80\x99t make a difference.
I\xE2\x80\x99ve seen 2 cord plastic-end connector types. One type is a straight plastic hook that attaches in-line with the cord. That\xE2\x80\x99s what is pictured on Amazon. The other type attaches at an angle. The dishwasher came with the angled plastic attachment. That failed after a few years. No complaints against either design. Just noting the cord parts that arrived in the mail don\xE2\x80\x99t look like the cord parts in the picture. I didn\xE2\x80\x99t measure the lengths as some others have noted receiving shorter cords than the originals. I didn\xE2\x80\x99t have a problem with the lengths.
Bottom line, the parts fit and seemed to be high quality. For some reason I couldn\xE2\x80\x99t get them to install and operate quietly on my dishwasher.

product_title: iSpring RCC1UP-AK 7-Stage Maximum Performance 100 GPD Under-Sink Reverse Osmosis Drinking Water Filtration System with Booster Pump, Alkaline pH+ Remineralization Filter and UV Sterilizer
review_headline: Excellent product and fantastic customer service!
review_body:
****UPDATE****
After I posted the initial review, the manufacturer contacted me and informed me that the UV stage of the product has been redesigned. The new UV ballast now includes a water flow sensor, and the UV bulb will only turn on when the water is flowing. Therefore the water does is not heated. The only flaw in this device has been completely remedied.

The seller/manufacturer sent me the new, upgraded parts FREE OF CHARGE, even though I had purchased the unit almost 2 years earlier.

I can\x27t say enough about this level of customer service. As stated in my initial review, everything has worked perfectly with this unit for the 2 years I\x27ve owned it.

UPGRADED TO 5 STARS and Highly recommended.

****ORIGINAL REVIEW****
I\x27ve been using this daily for 2 years with no issues, except one small thing- The first couple of cups of water that comes out of it during each use is HOT due to the ultraviolet bacterial-killing stage. That is the only reason for the 4-star rating instead of 5. This is only a minor inconvenience in most cases, but...

I installed a \x5C\x22T\x5C\x22 fitting and a pair of on/off valves from the local home improvement store so I could feed the output both to the sink faucet and my refrigerator\x27s icebox. Worked fine at first, but the very high water temperature at the output damaged the O-rings in the aftermarket cut-off valves after only a couple of months.

However, I still recommend this unit overall. It would be nice if they had a thermal cut-off switch on the UV. Then it would be perfect for its capacity and price.

review_headline: AVOID - Lasted 3 months  stopped working - Terrible Support - Geofencing is a joke
review_body: I had the unit professionally installed. It worked well enough for a about 3 months although the geo-fencing feature never worked and compared to the Nest it was lacking many features.  After about 3 months the unit stopped working in the middle of the night. Of course it happened on a night where the temperatures were below zero. Luckily I was able to get a serviceman out the next morning. He tested the furnace and the voltages and determined that the Lyric wasn\x27t working correctly. He then installed a basic digital thermostat which has been working fine.  I contacted Honeywell. They have a separate number for the Lyric which I called. It has two options. Option 1 is order status, option 2 is support. After the usual elevator music and annoying pre-recorded messages every 10 seconds for several minutes it puts me back at the beginning where I had to choose either option 1 or 2. I hit option 2 again and went through the same thing bringing me back to the touch tone menu after several minutes of annoying messages and music.  I gave up on that and used the online chat feature ...after a long wait I finally ended up in a chat with a support person. I asked if we could talk on the phone and she agreed. She was friendly but unhelpful. They wanted me to contact a professional to come to my house to troubleshoot with them over the phone at my expense. I explained that a serviceman had already done that though not on the phone with Honeywell and that I was unable to reach a person via the phone through their support. At no point did they offer to send a replacement unit.  Needless to say I am completely unhappy with this massive waste of money. I would never recommend this to anyone. AVOID this product and probably Honeywell in general. They do not stand behind their products.  I also contacted the reseller (Mystic Direct) to which they said "I really appolgize about this. But there is nothing I can do considering that this was bought four months ago." I\x27ll obviously be avoiding them in the future as well.

review_headline: Best made switch of its type on the market
review_body:
This type of switch is usually associated with controlling the power of holiday tree lights, and is usually sold as a convenient foot switch that you step on to turn the lights on and step on it again to turn the lights off. Another popular use is to assure an \xE2\x80\x9Cabsolute off\xE2\x80\x9D to certain appliances that don\xE2\x80\x99t have a power switch or those that have touch-sensitive switches that may be accidentally powered on by a child.

I have used many of these switches, both for control of power only and also those that incorporate built-in dimmers. I\xE2\x80\x99ve never found a brand or model that didn\xE2\x80\x99t work \xE2\x80\xA6 it is an inherently simple design that operates exactly like the common wall light switch. There is really very little that can go wrong with them. There is one exception to that rule and that applies to the push-on/push-off foot switches that have a little round enclosure. They work but don\xE2\x80\x99t last very long, which I suspect has to do with the fact that you operate them by stepping on them. The spring-loaded switch ends up being too delicate for long-term use.

I found this Stanley model and liked the design \xE2\x80\x93 I could hide the switch itself in an inconspicuous place because of its small size. I included a photo with this review to indicate exactly how small the switch itself is compared to a U.S. quarter dollar, it is much smaller than I expected.
In operation the switch is very definite in its on/off motion, operating with a firm click. I like that. And you can visually see if the power is on or off, unlike the foot switches.

I almost didn\xE2\x80\x99t buy it after reading the reviews that claimed it was defective because in the \xE2\x80\x9Coff\xE2\x80\x9D position a string of LED holiday lights still had a faint glow. But I\xE2\x80\x99ve had that problem since LED lights became popular with all kinds of switches and dimmers so I suspected that this switch was not the culprit but the way LED\xE2\x80\x99s work. A quick online search revealed that it is not the switch at all that is at fault because almost all switches only interrupt power on one of the two wires, and LED lights have a weird characteristic that they suck up an insanely small amount of power from the unswitched wire and \xE2\x80\x9Cglow\xE2\x80\x9D from it. There is no really appreciable amount of power being used (like it may cost 1 or 2 cents over an entire year) and the seepage doesn\xE2\x80\x99t affect anything, Some brands of LED lights are labeled as far as being compatible with certain lighting controls. So what might have been a deal-breaker turned out to be a complete non-issue. Maybe future LED lights will be made someday that are more compatible with common standard light switches like this one.

review_headline: great product but worried about long term life of bulbs
review_body: Review on A19:  great product but worried about long term life of bulbs.  I ordered 4 of these to try them out (planned on ordering many more if I liked them).  At first I was in love, yes they cost double the budget LED bulbs but when placing these in bedrooms its worth it to avoid flickering and buzzing noises.  The previous 3 brands I tried had both issues (if not at first they would develop the issues after a few weeks).  These bulbs were perfect, no buzzing, no flickering, great color rendering, what was not to like!  and since the life expectancy of LED is so long the extra cost up front was easier to swallow.  well about 6 weeks after installing, one bulb (out of 4 in an open ceiling fan with a dimmer) started flickering, no problems before that even with the dimmer being used everyday.  about a week later the bulb just went out, after turning the light on and off a few times the bulb came back on, tried a different socket and the same thing happened.  For a $13 A19 light bulb I expected much better quality control.  I was hoping a premium LED would be better than CFL bulbs that had high fail rates, I guess not.  This also makes me wonder what the actual life on the other 3 bulbs will be, what good is advertising long life if they fail.  And no one wants to take the time to mail in light bulbs under warranty.  I have upgraded my review to 4 stars as G7 did send me a replacement bulb and they do have excellent customer service.  Review on BR30:  So I had to drop my rating again to 3 stars on this product since I purchased 2 BR30 versions of this bulb, both of mine came scratched (light cover), which as another reviewer stated makes you think they are shipping out bulbs returned by other customers!  I never had this happen when I could order direct from G7 Power, its still sold through them but now the only way to buy them is shipped through Amazon.  Bad decision G7.  I hope these are not returned/refurbished bulbs, they send them in over packaged boxes but this may be where its getting scratched, might want to look into a package change for the big bulbs, spend less on the graphics and more on lens protection.

product_title: VIGO Zurich Single Handle Pull-Down Spray Kitchen Faucet
review_headline: Updated many times - Great but leaks but fixed and breaks rinse and repeat.
review_body:
I bought this, but with the soap dispenser which is the VG02007STK2. My review is posted there but I thought I should add it here.

I am very happy with this faucet, it would be 5 stars if the spring issue was fixed. Yes I bent it, and most of the time it holds it in place but I have to bend it again every so often. The sprayer is powerful but not overly so that water bounces back out all over the counter. The faucet is heavy and solid. It feels good in your hand while using it. Even the soap dispenser is solid metal, not cheap plastic. I have no use for it, but I wish I did since it is so nice.

Installation was simple, although for someone not familiar with installing faucets they could easily need a few attempts to get it right. Just make sure the triangle shaped washer fits flat up against the underside of the countertop. It is not mentioned in the install sheet. Also the metal sleeve just above the sprayer head comes with a piece of plastic around it. I believe this is just to protect the metal as I see no use for it, but again the instructions don\x27t mention it. Do use plumbers tape, that is important to prevent leaks. Also don\x27t over tighten, hand tighten and then one complete turn of the wrench. Four stars

I will update this in a few months with further thoughts or sooner if issues arise.

Update 01/12/14: Leaking at the sprayer handle. First it leaked at the top underneath the rubber so I tightened it (it does not come apart to fully tape and tighten). Then the leak moved to the bottom, same type of connection. Leak slowed but then showed up on the metal ring towards the top that locks the sprayer handle in. No way to fix that and since both spouts are always receiving water it leaks every time the other is used. Vigo is sending me a replacement, all I had to do was email them a copy of the receipt. I will update again after installation. Changed to three stars

Update 01/20/14: New sprayer arrived quickly and has been working great. The old spray would turn at the top and bottom, and this one does not. Hoping there are no more issues. We still love the faucet and are very happy with it. We also no longer have the issue with the sprayer not staying in the holder. When I called to get the new sprayer he said to give it a good bend and make it look like a question mark. Well I did and it stays put now. Changing back to four stars.

Update 03/29/14: I fixed the spring issue and it has been fine since. The way I fixed it was actually putting some force to make a good bend. It has been working flawlessly. We love this faucet.

product_title: Maple Tree Tapping Kit \xE2\x80\x93 Includes 5/16\xE2\x80\x9D Tree Saver Taps Spiles + 3-Foot Drop Line Tubes (Pack of 5), and 80 Page Fully Illustrated Guide to Maple Tapping Book
review_headline: Product Review: Maple Tree Tapping Kit Plus How-To Book #mapletapper
review_body:
Disclaimer: I received this product/service at a reduced price or for free. All opinions are my own and are my honest opinions based on my own experience with the product.

It\xE2\x80\x99s still several weeks too soon here in Indiana to start tapping our maple trees but when I saw this new Maple Tapping Tree Kit plus the How-To Book, I wanted to check it out. The taps are what sets this kit apart from other similar kits. The taps and tubing are all food grade.

The tubing runs from the tap to your bucket carrying the sap with it. As long as the bucket you use is sealed well this means no more ants or tree debris falling into your sap.

The light blue tubbing is highly visible against tree bark. It is also easy to see liquid through it and draws less sunlight than what a clear tubing would.

The book \xE2\x80\x9CGuide To Maple Tapping\xE2\x80\x9D by Julie Fryer is 80-pages and even though I have been tapping maple trees for years, I found lots of good advice in it. The book covers some basic information about maple tapping, the process start to finish, how to make syrup, recipes, additional resources and some final notes. The book is clearly written, the photographs and drawings are very helpful and I feel this is one book every #mapletapper should have on their reference shelf! I encourage you to check it out.

product_title: USAutomatic Sentry 300 Commercial Grade Automatic Gate Opener
review_headline: The unit is very solid, but accessories are too pricey
review_body:
Purchased in Dec 2014.
Few initial thoughts:
Swing-Arm is much larger than i thought it was. Very big and sturdy.
Battery is MUCH larger than i expected. BIG, very BIG for this unit.
Instructions were a bit lacking. Wish the details were more evident and less ambiguous (specifically around mounting hardware). A little overwhelming at first, but not as bad as it seems when you take it one step at a time.
EXTREMELY unimpressed with the solar panel options... both in size and price. System is a 30W system, why only offer 5W (have also seen 10W panel) option? Found 20W alternative option for under 75% of the price of the 5W and it works perfectly!
Not as impressed with the accessory costs: auto exit sensor and keypad offerings are a bit expensive.
Made in America: used to mean a very high quality product. Initial thought is that this meets expectations.
battery not included. +$70
On to Installation:
Installation was a little of a challenge. The "universal" mounting brackets are built for just about any fence setup out there; however, that also comes at the expense of being simple and easy to install. Instructions don\x27t really help here. If you continue to work with it, it does become evident how you should set it up.
Big complaint in mounting between the gate and the fence: it required you to drill into your gate to install the gate connector. I really don\x27t like this as it\x27s an ornamental gate and holes like this tend to promote rust. I engineered some U bolts and a solid metal flange to allow me to install the gate connector without involving a drill. Holds very solid.
As with the gate, i refused to drill into my fence to mount the control unit. I again engineered a piece of 5/8 plywood and attached it to my fence with radiator clamps and then attached the unit to the wood. Overall, very happy with this. I didn\x27t use treated wood and will probably be replacing in the next year or 2, but will be good for now.
Installation of the wiring, battery, and such are very easy and straight forward. Yes, that HUGE battery fit perfectly. The system fired right up and began operating with no issue... some minor adjustments but no issues.
Setting the sensitivity was simple and easy, configuring the opening and closing settings were pretty simple but did take a few opens/closes to get everything just right. Configuring the remotes was super simple and when i programmed one remote the other seemed to automatically be programmed too. One issue I have with the remotes and programming is that I have the gate set to "auto-close" after about 40 seconds. P2 can be configured to open the gate and keep it open (over-riding the auto-close). I\x27ve spent 2+ hours trying to get this programmed right and just can\x27t seem to make it work right. But a really small problem in the scheme of things.
Solar connection. The alternative solar panel came with only wire leads. I had to find a wiring connector that matched the input the unit was expecting and having a lot of spare computer parts/power-supplies and such laying around it wasn\x27t real difficult. I spliced the solar leads to the connector and plugged in. The lights all came on and everything looks good.
In operation for about a month now and all i\x27ve had to do was to tighten the mounting bracket screws a little as things have settled in. I\x27m very happy with the unit and it has played well with my "engineering" alternatives as well as my alternative solar panel. I would recommend to friend/family as i feel it\x27s a very solid unit. Family has a mighty-mule system and I feel this unit is superior to that model in both quality and durability.
Pros
High quality, Durable, very well built, easy program
Cons
$$$ accessories, poor solar opts, instructions

product_title: G7 Power Tahoe LED 15 Watt (75W) 1100 Lumen BR30 Recessed Can Light Bulb, Dimmable 4000K Bright White
review_body:
I am a techno geek when it comes to my light. I am a software engineer and amateur photographer. I understand and care about the kelvin temperature color of my lights. I don\x27t understand why people romanticize and wail about the loss of incandescent tungsten light. I find 2700K "warm" light abysmal for most tasks. This G7 is 4000K, which was a major selling point for me. It is plenty warm for my tastes and produces great quantities of light. I use it in a torchiere lamp in a room that lacks any built in fixtures. I do not have it on a dimmer, but I like that I could. Non-dimmable is a major beef I have with CFL (compact fluorescent) bulbs... that and the fact that every CFL I have starts out dim and slowly brightens. I want my light NOW, not later. This G7 satisfies my LIGHT NOW demand. But back to my color rant... people: do yourselves a favor and learn a little about the kelvin light scale. It will save you grief later. It can also help you take better photos by adjusting your white balance correctly. 4000K = YES. I\x27d really like a 5000K option, but 4000K is magnitudes superior to the dismal 2700K reddish yellow lights.

Aside: I bought some color changing HUE bulbs for when I want to geek out over color. That is a light toy. I love it, but this is the real workhorse light in my apartment living room.

product_title: Piper Piper with Door Sensor and Smart Switch
review_headline: You Have to Pay the Piper -- But Only Once
review_body: (2015-02-02 update:  I\x27ve changed my score from a 5 to a 4.  There is at least one flaw:  the backup batteries.  If you install them, and the device crashes -- as mine did as the Seahawks were losing a Super Bowl in which they should never have been playing -- the batteries must be removed to reboot.  If you remove the batteries permanently, and there is a power outage, it appears the device will not boot up on its own when power restores, as the power button on back must be then pushed.  This is a huge use-case design flaw that must be fixed, if true.  Comments?)    If you\x27ve lived in enough places, you know that rats will always come sniffing around, trying to make off with your stuff.  Or at least steal your cheese.  And while you don\x27t want to lose that stuff, you don\x27t want to have to pay a monthly fee to keep that stuff protected either.  And with just this idea, this new little device will surely be music to your ears.    My wife and I own a house, and with that house, we gladly paid for a full ADT Pulse system and its monthly fees.  While there are certainly flaws, it is mostly good as well, as you can monitor your home while you\x27re away, but also feel assured that someone else is paying attention as a backup, just in case.  Yeah, I will admit, both BTK and one of the Hillside Stranglers worked for ADT at one time or another, which is certainly disconcerting.  And sure, Dennis Rader once configured a \x5C\x22back door\x5C\x22 into a company\x27s system so that he could come visit anytime later if he wanted; and sure, Kenneth Bianchi even killed two people during an installation one time in Bellingham.  But still, you have to figure that those guys were outliers.  Most of the people at ADT seem to be fairly trustworthy, at least in comparison.    But we\x27re renting a place too.  Now, while that place is in a city that is surely safer than Hamelin ever was, the city still has some crime.  After all, it is in California, and Californians think that crime is OK -- \x5C\x22Criminals arepoor, they\x27ve been downtrodden, and so they deserve to steal,\x5C\x22 would be the \x5C\x22logic\x5C\x22 in liberal California.  So, I wanted to be able to check up on that rental from time to time while not having to Pay the Piper monthly, so that\x27s where this thing came into play.  Plus, I didn\x27t want to ask the landlord for permission to do an installation, and this hardware is sleek -- and sneaky enough -- to slither into town without almost anyone noticing.  Even maybe the criminals.  Or rats.  Or landlords.    So, I bought this package from Amazon, and configured it in less than an hour, faster than you can play Chopstix on the flute.  The setup is really easy, and it automatically downloaded and installed a firmware update itself, without missing a note.  So many systems lose their place just doing this alone.  The video image is really good -- although I wish it had night vision -- and the light-switch works as designed as well.  And the software is fairly intuitive; I will say that I\x27ve seen much worse and I\x27ve rarely seen better.  I will admit that I still have to add the Z-wave door sensor -- I need to bring some double-backed tape, as I don\x27t want to damage the door with the default drill method -- but my guess is:  this system won\x27t miss a beat while doing it.  Stay tuned.    If you have some pets -- such as mice or rats, perhaps -- to keep an eye on during the day, this system might be just for you.  Or if you have some children that you worry about, worry about wandering off to God only knows where following God only knows whom, this system might be just for you as well.  Just remember:  you have to pay the Piper, but with this version, you\x27ll only pay once.

review_body:

I accidentally left a small puddle of canola oil on my granite counter overnight and woke up in the morning to find a dark stain where the oil was. The reason I give this product 4 stars is because of the smell. It has a very fragrant citrus smell that really smells toxic. I tried to stay out of my apartment for much of the time that the product was on and I had to open the windows for some ventilation when home (in the winter). I don\x27t think it smells bad -- I was just genuinely concerned about breathing it in. I would do a second application to get out the small spots that remain of the stain, but they look natural enough that I dont think it\x27s worth breathing in this stuff. I would recommend doing it when you will be out of town for a few days, or at least do it during the week when you wont be home all day! review_body: I have been purchasing LED household lamps for about eight (8) years now.  Although I have seen an overall improvement of the products, over the years, my finding is not consistent with all of the LED products I have seen, even amongst the top brand names.  However, the Philips products seem to be very consistent with their improvements and with their quality.  Some brands appear to advertise certain specifications, such as color temperature, incorrectly.  This item, on the other hand, emits a very warm color temperature.  Let us consider one thing, however.  As with all "dimmable" LED lamps, be advised that color temperature of LED lamps *REMAINS THE SAME* as you dim it.  In contrast, incandescent lamps get warmer when you dim them.  Therefore when you dim an LED lamp it will probably appear to your brain to get "cooler" as you dim it, only because your brain is trained to think that a lamp should get "warmer" when you dim it.  Maybe someday the dimming technology will improve.  However, specific to this particular lamp, it still emits a smooth warm-ish color temperature even at 25% dimmed.  Enjoy!

product_title: Rust-Oleum Hammered Metal Finish, 1-Quart
review_body: I have used this product on numerous occasions. I really like it. I have bought it on Amazon and from a home center on line.  If you read the reviews, you will see some people who say that 1 coat will work and other reviewers will say that 2 coats are needed. That depends on what you are painting. I have painted bare wood, and previously painted metal. One coat would just not work for bare pine boards. If you would like to extend coverage, I suggest "priming" your project with glossy gray Rust-Oleum enamel paint. It is cheaper and can be found in stores in most areas. One coat of gray enamel followed by one coat of gray hammered metal works for me. If money is no object, definitely go for two coats of the hammered metal paint. For large flat areas, I would suggest using a roller, otherwise brush marks might show up. If you have not used this paint before, no amount of stirring will get you a uniform color in the can. Don\x27t even try. Your project will turn out just fine anyway. The paint dries fairly quickly. If you continue to work it as it dries, you will get really fine, angle-hair-like "strings". I don\x27t know how else to describe them. I have never seen these with any other paint. I have used the spray can version of this Rust-Oleum project. It is similar, but not the same. The spray product has a "finer" hammered finish. The paint from the can has a "coarser" hammered finish. They are both nice. The coarser finish hides more flaws. The attached photo shows an I-beam in my basement. Previously, the I-beam was ugly brown and had a lot of mud on it, which I washed off before painting it with the gray hammered paint from the can using a roller. It came out near perfect. I highly recommend this product.

review_body:
This works exactly as stated.

Installation was all of five minutes. Lift off the tank\x27s top, hang the device, remove one hose, attach two, insert the cartridge, put the top on, and you\x27re done. Bingo. There is an odd smell that\x27s not quite bleach-like, for several flushes. It dissipates fairly quickly. It was slightly annoying but easily tolerated.

This Sparkle hangs on the rim of the toilet, under the lid, and above the water line. The bleach or blue stuff is in separate circuit so it doesn\x27t get into the tank. All the internals are safe, unlike using tablets in the tank. Because the Sparkle hangs on the edge, the tank lid will not sit flush. This should be no surprise to anyone, but if you didn\x27t know, now you do.

After two months, it\x27s still working on the first cartridge. There is a slight bleach odor right after a flush, but it doesn\x27t last long. The bowl stays very clean below the water line. Because the water from the device fills from the bottom of the bowl and doesn\x27t run down the top, you still need to clean as appropriate, above the water line. Tablets in the tank would reduce that, but they tend not to play well with the rubber stopper (not a big deal) or a Fluidmaster Fill Valve (which is kind of a big deal)

I bought a couple of bleach refill kits, but will make the suggested modification to use up the rest of my tablets, and then buy the spa tabs.

There has been no downside for me. I\x27d buy it again and wish I had bought one sooner.

One last mention- this apparently does not work with low-flow and/or Toto toilets, so if you have either you may want to do some research before you purchase.

review_body:
This is not a secure lock; you can side a 3" nail long inside the case and push back the tongue to open the gate.A 10-year-old can open it with a nail or straightened paperclip. The manual key to unlock the latch is a tiny, hollow metal barrel, more like a suitcase key than a door key. The knuckles on the bottom of key fit snugly into ball-bearings inside the lock. The key operated the lock smoothly for the first dozen times and then began to scrape and drag as it turned. The knuckles are a soft metal and wear down after 50 or 60 turns of opening the latch. I would like something more secure and a more rugged, dependable design.

This is the second lock I have purchased. The first was installed on the gate for about 2 weeks before I connected it to power. After opening the latch 6-8 times a day with the key for about two weeks, the latch failed to open with the key. The key wouldn\x27t turn in the latch to retract the tongue; the mechanism was stuck. I used a small nail to push back the tongue( takes about 5 seconds to defeat the mechanism) and open the gate. On examination, the key showed a lot of wear; the silver paint was worn away. I thought the mechanism might have rusted; oiling it didn\x27t help. I bought a second lock. Hopefully the replacement will last until the opener is installed and powered.

product_title: Hot ! Thunbird New 12v 4 Channel Wireless Remote Control Receiver Momentary Switch
review_body:
Received this in two days! Works great but...You need to read the other posts on how to program it. I received the unit that uses a jumper.
As shipped the jumper is on pins 3 & 4, this is the monetary setting. Pressing a button operates the corresponding relay. Releasing the button and the relay returns to it\x27s off state.
Putting the jumpers on 1 & 2 puts it into latching mode. When you press a button that relay latches and stays latched until you press the same button to release it.
Removing the Jumper puts it into a interlock mode. in that case what ever button is pressed latches that relay and all others remain off. Pressing another button causes that relay to latch and the latched relay turns off and all remaining stay off. so in essence you get the realy that you press a button for and all others are off, now once yyou do that the only way to release all of them is to power cycle the unit :(. I suppose someone could use this.
lastly power draw, when the unit is powered up all relays are off and at 12.8 volts the unit draws 10.2ma. Each relay draws 30ma. So if you have all for on the total power draw is 130.2ma.
So far the remote control battery seems like it\x27s in good shape. But I\x27m going to pick up a spare.

review_body:
Included with the 20 feet set of cool white lights are the instructions, the solar panel with off/on switch, mounting hardware, plastic mounting ground stake, plastic wall mount, and several feet of wiring from the solar panel connecting to the 20 feet of lighting.

Brightech sent me several different sets as samples for review (each I will review separately) and this set quality is essentially the same as the other 20 foot sets. This cool white set is approximately 20 feet in length with small LED lights spaced about 2 inches apart approximately. This set of lights has a large solar panel approximately 6 inches by 5 inches which contains a replaceable rechargeable battery. The lights are a nice soft (blue hue) white light and make a nice decorative light. The wire is bendable and pretty durable for a thin wire but like all wire lighting like this you have to carefully bend. Like all solar lights, the length of time they will stay on is dependent on the amount of sun the panel gets during the day and the rechargeable battery life. These lights come with a 3 year warranty. I will update my review over time if I have any issues with long term durability.

Overall these are nice looking decorator lights at a reasonable price that have the flexibility of being mounted practically anywhere with the two different mounts and long cabling. These look nice but my personal preference are the multi-color set.

4 Stars

product_title: SmartThings Hub, 1st Generation
review_body:
I have this installed in my home for the past 4 months. Use it to control 8 light switches. Some switches are just on the hub so I can control them when on vacation (to mimic people being at home) while the other switches are programmed to turn lights on and off with the sun (for exterior illumination applications). So my use requirements are pretty basic.

Pros:
- it is white like Apple products, if you\x27re into that
- relatively easy to set up

Cons:
- it is flaky - i.e. it intermittently does not work! (more on this below)
- SmartThings iOS App is confusing to use (you name switches/devices twice, etc.)
- it does not work "off-line" and depends on the SmartThings servers for the brains (more on this below)

This gets one star because it intermittently fails to work for me.

Like all hubs without a battery backup, this does not work when the power is down - that\x27s ok, because my house lights don\x27t work either.

Like all hubs that do *not* have an off-line mode, this does not work when your internet is down - that is ok for me because my internet is relatively reliable.

This hub fails for me when the power is on and the internet works fine. It fails by not activating the switches (lights) based on the set schedule. In the past 4 months it has failed at least 3 times by either not turning on the lights or not turning off the lights - it may have failed more often than that, but these are external lights that I sometimes don\x27t notice when I leave the house.

The frustrating thing is that one day it may not work and the next day it works and I haven\x27t done anything different - I didn\x27t go in and reset things, I didn\x27t go and change the schedule, my internet is fine for both days, my power is fine for both days. Intermittent problems are a hassle to deal with because you can\x27t track down the cause of it.

My guess is that the cause is on the SmartThings (ST) server end of it - maybe their servers have an occasional hiccup right around the time of my scheduled activity so my hub does not get the message from the ST server to turn on or turn off the lights.

The unreliability of this hub makes it a product I will resell on the \x27bay, the \x27list or throw in the back of the closet. I\x27m using this on a low stress case - turning on the lights when the sun goes down; I can\x27t imagine what the failure situation would be if it was used to monitor water leaks (a use case advertised on SmartThings\x27 site) or other more valuable situations.

I\x27ve contacted ST\x27s customer support each time I\x27ve had a failure - first time the response was \x27let\x27s see if it reoccurs\x27; second response \x27I\x27ve updated your firmware, so install that\x27; third response \x27maybe you could try uninstalling and reinstalling your GE z-wave switches, and you only have a 30-day return window so that has expired\x27

So basically I feel I\x27ve been told that I should turn it on and off again and if that doesn\x27t work (it didn\x27t), then I\x27m SOL. I\x27m buying something else instead, and so should you.

review_headline: Bright Light, Mounts Easily, Beam throws illuminates a large area, PERFECT LIGHT FOR OUR FRONT DOOR!
review_body:
I\x27ve been using this for several months now and so far it is exactly what I was looking for! What was I looking for? A light to kick on when we walked up to our home at night so we could find the keys and unlock the door. It works great, is extremely bright, has a wide beam throw, and activates from about 10 ft away so it easily lights up the walking path to the door so we don\x27t trip over any packages. I ended up using the adhesive to stick the light mount to the top of the metal front door. So far it hasn\x27t fallen off but I am very concerned I will come home one day and see my light, broken, on the ground. If it does happen I will definitely update this review. The only real negative I have is that it slides off the mount very easily, so it is possible that someone could easily take your light with little effort. Now, on the flip side, i have on several occasions slide the light off the mount and used it as a flash light while looking for something in the yard, as long as you keep moving it will stay on.

Overall, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! Works great, and I hope the batteries last a while.

*** UPDATE 6/18/2015 ***

So it has been about 6 months since my last review and I wanted to say that I AM STILL ON THE ORIGINAL SET OF BATTERIES! The light is triggered probably twice a day, staying on for as long as we need to while unlocking the front door, and then shuts off. To be fair, it has gotten about 50% dimmer due to the decreased battery capacity but it is still very much useable and I will not be changing the batteries for probably a few more days. So honestly, you can get a full year out of two sets of batteries, this is well worth it in my book!

product_title: Prime Line Products U-9842 Patio Door Lock, Self-Adhesive, Clear
review_headline: Works as a basic child-safety device
review_body:
First of all, the product is a TWO PACK. Amazon has it INCORRECTLY listed as "Item Package Quantity: 1" when it actually contains 2 of the adhesive locks which affix to the glass surface of the sliding door thereby preventing children from opening the door - as long as they where placed high enough to remain out of reach of a child.

I noted some reviews which said the purchaser considered it a theft-deterrent. However, older sliding-glass patio doors often merely lift up-and-out of the groove - even from the outside. Hence, this hinge-style lock product won\x27t serve as an anti-theft device on older door models.

My only complaint is the plastic spring-loaded pull-string that is intended to be pulled on, prior to attempting to disengage the lock. It\x27s often overlooked and, as a result, the plastic pull-string is easily bent and forever rendered useless. This damage results in the lock opening and closing with minimal effort. While the lock still performs as intended, preventing the sliding doors from being opened by a child, the pull-string should be a metal material that resists bending, so that the user cannot disengage the lock without first pulling the mechanism.

UPDATED:  The GE 45600 can be set up with a Wink hub by using the Wink app\xE2\x80\x99s \xE2\x80\x9Cadvanced Z-wave controls\xE2\x80\x9D function.  1) First, bring up the \xE2\x80\x9CZ-Wave Controls\xE2\x80\x9D panel.   2) Second, on the GE remote, press and hold SETUP until both the red and green LEDs blink twice. 3) Enter 967 on the GE remote.  (You may press either the on or off half of each of these buttons; they function equivalently for this task) 4) Press \xE2\x80\x9CINCLUSION MODE\xE2\x80\x9D on the Wink app. 5) Both remote and hub should be blinking quickly; do this as quickly as possible. 6) Bask in the glow of technical success.  To add devices to the GE remote: 1) Hold \xE2\x80\x9CSETUP\xE2\x80\x9D 2) Press \xE2\x80\x9CAdd\xE2\x80\x9D 3) Press \xE2\x80\x9CLIGHT\xE2\x80\x9D 4) Press a number key you want to associate with the device 5) Press the control button on the module 6) Gloat as you gain magical powers to control devices with a gesture at a large distance   OBSOLETE - this was my original review, preserved for posterity, and is no longer factually correct:   Can\x27t be added to Wink hub as a secondary controller. review_body:

I used this unit primarily to measure actual wattage used by various space heaters, and it confirmed to me that the ones that were making less heat were indeed using less electricity. This means there is no worry about using a lower power heater, it will still operate at the same cost, just more slowly. I wish I could measure the power being used by my 220v heat pump, but cannot... what do I expect for twenty bucks? I can get a good estimate by watching my daily graphs from the power company and subtracting the power used by other appliances.

review_headline: Works great but needed to buy a speed controller.
review_body:
This review is for the Dual 120 unit. I bought this for use in an enclosed entertainment center where an audio receiver, satellite box, blu-ray, and ps4 are located in a space just wide enough to accommodate them. Before installation of the fans the devices were hot to the touch and hot air would accumulate in the space. After installation there is no discernible heat radiating from the electronics or when touching the devices themselves when I open the cabinet door. I installed this with the fans pulling air out of the cabinet , and have a large cut out at the bottom of the cabinet for wires that allows cool air to be pulled in and sucked up though the cabinet to the fans at the top.

My only complaint with this unit is the sound they make at full speed. It\x27s not terribly loud but was enough to annoy me as I could detect it during normal TV viewing. A USB speed controller allowed me to reduce the speed of the fan and eliminate the noise without reducing the effectiveness of the cooling.

The hardest part of the install was taking the electronics out of the cabinet and cutting out the back of the cabinet. The template was a little flimsy but it was helpful and I\x27m glad they included it.

product_title: Culligan FM-15A Faucet Mount Filter with Advanced Water Filtration, White Finish
review_body:
This thing is beautiful!
I\x27ve been using a Pur Plus for years and finally decided to try a Culligan.
Here\x27s the key differences that stand out right away.

1) The Culligan has metal threads that attach to the faucet.
The Pur Plus has plastic threads.

2) The Culligan is smaller than the Pur Plus.
The Culligan extends 1 3/4 inches below the faucet.
The Pur Plus extends 4 inches below the faucet.

3) The Culligan turns on by pulling a small metal button, and turns off automatically.
The Pur Plus turns on and off by rotating the entire filter.

This Culligan is much more compact, gives me more room underneath and is easier to operate.

The most noticeable thing however, is how attractive it is.
The faucet attachment is metal and the filter housing is plastic, and both are chromed to match my faucet perfectly.
It really looks like it belongs there.
Just writing this review got me to shine it up again!

product_title: Culligan / Pentek OR-34 for HF-360A, HF-150A Water Filter Housing O Ring made by PWF
review_headline: Best value, appears to be exact replacement for OR-34A
review_body:
I have the HF-360A and have heard rumors that the "A" version o-ring "OR-34A" is not the same diameter as the OR-34 for the older housing. I don\x27t know if this is true but Culligan sells an OR-34A set with two sizes one of which you will not need. This product appears to be the proper size for the "A" housing as advertised, 4 1/8" diameter measured by me, and looks exactly like the original o-ring. It is the best value I have seen. I ordered four and was charged the same shipping rate as for one and they came in a single zip lock bag. Nice to have spares in case you pinch one with a misaligned installation.

The o-ring appears to belong on the step above a circular groove in the housing that is smaller than the o-ring. My first attempt to screw on the housing resulted in the o-ring falling down into this groove causing leaks and possibly being damaged. I urge you to use a silicone grease like Dow Corning MOLYKOTE for several reasons: it will hold the o-ring on the step as you install the housing, it provides lubrication, it slows down leaks.

product_title: Buttons and Scissors (Pro)
review_headline: Fun for the casual gamer that likes puzzle type games
review_body:
Fun for the casual gamer that likes puzzle type games. Good for killing a few minutes here and there. Interface is well thought out and implemented - just drag across the buttons to cut a group from the cloth... It couldn\x27t get much simpler. The puzzles vary in difficulty but so far, I haven\x27t found one that I couldn\x27t solve, some just take longer than others. You have the option to undo moves and reset the board, so if you realize you made a mistake, you don\x27t have to completely close the puzzle and go back in to start over.

Note that resetting the puzzle does not seem to reset the "time to solve" clock. Your time to solve is the total time of all your attempts, including time from any restarted games. If you\x27re a "beat the clock" kind of player, that may make the game seem more stressful. If you\x27re just into solving puzzle and not as concerned with the time it takes you, it probably won\x27t matter to you either way.

product_title: TouchUp Pro - Photo Editor
review_body: [Added] I was browsing the Play Store just now, and found that this app has not been updated for two years! So, I suspect it has become abandonware meaning the developer no longer works on it. If you are considering buying this, please keep that in mind & check the latest development.    [Original]  As others have said, this is a basic photo editor. If you want only the basic functions, it\x27s solid enough. All the available functions are shown on screen, neat & tidy. Its code is pretty clean too; it does ask for full network access although I can\x27t see why (it doesn\x27t access cloud storage, nor does it seem prepared to download any extensions or add-ons), but it runs fine offline anyway.    You should note that the maximum save resolution is only 2600x2600 which is not good enough for newer devices. In fact, even a 8MP camera will capture at 3264x2448, so its limit is pretty outdated.    There is also the question of not exiting cleanly (even after you\x27ve saved the photo you\x27d been working on). The practice of letting the system terminate apps is debatable, and frankly I\x27m against it, but I digress. The key issue is whether these apps just sit idly in memory, or still uses up CPU cycle. Unfortunately, this app belongs to the latter.    There are a lot of photo editors out there - both free & paid - that offer more. TouchUp Pro is worth a look while being FAOTD, but certainly not worth $2.99.

product_title: Elevation Moon
review_body:
If you\x27ve used Ripside\x27s "Elevation Mars" app, you\x27ll feel right at home with "Elevation Moon," since both apps use the same mechanics. The app features some very detailed mapping of the Moon\x27s surface, including mountains, valleys, craters, "seas," and landing sites or impact points for manned and unmanned probes that have reached the Moon. Think of "Elevation Moon" as sort of a lunar equivalent of Google Earth, since there are a number of similarities. Zooming in on terrain features gives a 3-D look, and you can adjust the vertical scale to exaggerate the relief if you like. Clicking on the "W" in an information box brings up a Wikipedia article about the feature. The app allows you a 360-degree look at the Moon, including the so-called "dark side" that we can\x27t see from Earth. One unusual feature is the ability to add surface water and see the effects as the water level rises.

For me, the most fun was to expand the surface to a large scale and start the surface slowly scrolling by. It\x27s mesmerizing to see the surface of the Moon from the vantage point of an astronaut in low orbit.

The developer has done a fine job with this informative, fun to use app, which ran perfectly on my Kindle Fire HDX 7" tablet.

product_title: Paradise Island
review_body: I installed the game "Paradise Island" in June 2014 on my Kindle Fire, because I was looking for a game similar to "Coconut Queen," that I play on my computer, and the game "Paradise Island" was suggested to me by an Amazon Kindle representative. I must have started to play it a little and then stopped for some reason, because I don\x27t remember a Tutorial or experiencing any glitches as mentioned by some reviewers. Then, in the first week of January, when I noticed the icon picture of the game & wondered what it was, I was pleasantly surprised.  I began playing more often, and I started to build accommodations at once.  I have built on all the space of the 1st half of the island, and I am now on level 15 & that\x27s where I will stay until I get 2300 more XP (experience points) to advance to the next level which will take forever to acquire.  I honestly enjoyed the game UNTIL I realized that the objective of the developers of the game (and Amazon) is to make you SPEND REAL MONEY on virtual reality.  < I DON\x27T LIKE THAT hence the rating of 2 stars.  Not only do you have to spend real money buying these "Piastres" in order to progress, but the game is slow-moving and takes hours to repair and upgrade buildings, and to accumulate enough game money, pearls, golden rings, and energy bars to accomplish the set tasks.  Someone said you could play it without spending any money at all, yes that maybe true, but it would take you SEVERAL MONTHS, EVEN YEARS to get enough money to buy more land i.e. those Regions, in order to make progress because the prices they set are ridiculous. Sadly, one day, I was so frustrated at waiting on the game to accumulate money to buy Regions, that I bought some Piastres. I got a deal that doubled my Piastres but still, that was not enough. I was about to get suckered a second time into buying a triple Piastres pack deal when I decided to do a search for the availability of this game for the PC, but the game is only available on Android devices and Apple products. My search led me to the developer\x27s webpage, Game Insight, & they said the game was "free to play" & I laughed out loud.  In conclusion, if you game-players have a lot of real money to spend or several years to play a game, then by all means, Paradise Island is for you; but if not, I strongly recommend the game "Coconut Queen" which has the same theme & setting as "Paradise Island" but without the high costs and after your initial purchase of $19.99 will be truly "FREE TO PLAY."

product_title: Brave Frontier
review_body: GREAT GAME! BUT!!!!! The tutorial falls extremely short of anything I\x27d call useful. I\x27ve played for over a year and I\x27d like to explain a few things to all who will listen.  First you need to understand that this is a freemium game and is mildly pay to win(play galaxy legend if you want to see what a true pay to win game looks like, cuz it looks like many thousands of dollars requiring hundreds spent at a time for ANYTHING GOOD). Next, every unit that has ever been in the rare summon gate is still there so don\x27t feel pressured to summon just because they have something new. There are hundreds of units you might get from that gate and most have a value in some form or another, some are worth having 2 or 3, and a handful are worth getting 4 or 5(high hit counter for metal parades). NEVER get rid of something before you Google it, forums are the best for this. There is a lot to do in this game and no one squad is going to do it all. A LOT of people complain about this and I was one of them for a bit, but there is no reason to try for every unit, new units are not and never will be &#34;unstoppable&#34;. Another thing to keep in mind is this is very much a strategy game, the first bit of the game is just to get your units lvled and you comfortable with them. Eventually the boss fights get extremely challenging and it is just a much how you play, as who you bring with, do some research if you get stuck and don\x27t be afraid to lose and not spend a gem to continue. Yes this game is kinda boring at first, don\x27t worry because it does get heartbreakingly challenging, but not impossible. And finally, my last thought, I love this game for one major reason. I have watched people dump 100s of gems into an event and lose to someone who was just smarter about what they were doing(some gratification for all the free to play users out there)

product_title: Machinarium
review_body:
This is a gem of a game! I play many point and click games, but this one is both unique and thoughtful, and really in a category all its own (although it did remind me of \x5C\x22Shapik the Quest\x5C\x22). In this story, you guide Josef the robot to save his girlfriend from the Blackcap Brotherhood. The gameplay is standard point and click: you pick up useful objects as you explore each scene and use them at the appropriate time. Unlike other games, the objects do not go into an inventory banner, instead, the robot eats them. There is a sense of humor throughout the game.

The graphics are stunning with hand drawn artwork, and really set the mood for this steampunk adventure. The music is great. I found the game to be a challenge, and really had to think in order to move forward and solve the puzzles. There are no easy actions here (like find a key and open a chest), you must consider the whole scene and what the robot can do - for example, his body can extend up or squish down. At times, I could clearly see what needed to happen, but simply couldn\x27t figure out how to get it done. The game offers help, but even that was difficult to figure out, and I overlooked the whole help guide the first hour I played. Alternatively, there are many walkthroughs available online.

I recommend this adventure for those who have the patience to figure things out and want to take their time. I was actually very frustrated when I first played it, and sent it to the cloud. However, on my second (or third) attempt, the game clicked, and I found it captivating. This is not a game to rush through, or one you play when you\x27re looking to waste a few minutes. It requires attention and some degree of concentration. I recommend this one, as it is very worthwhile.

product_title: Paper Monsters
review_body:
This game is pretty fun, fun enough that I got through the first three worlds. It\x27s a 2.5D side actor a bit like Mario on the Wii U. Graphics are simple and blocky, like N64, but smooth. You collect collect buttons for points, and paperclips for bonus points (what??). Too kill bad guys, you jump on them (usually).

There are a few annoyances that prevent this from getting four stars for me.

1. Checkpoints don\x27t always work. Sometimes I get through 2 checkpoints, only to die and be reset to the first checkpoint.
2. Enemies are not always intuitively dealt with. Monsters can be jumped on, but not walked into. Fine. But snakes cannot be jumped on at all? Spikey lizards cannot be jumped on, fine. But green monsters in the fourth world that look almost exactly like previous monsters can\x27t either? Having no way to kill half of the enemies is annoying. And out of nowhere, there are suddenly cannons back in the 3 dimensional plane shooting at you, when previously all interaction had been 2D.
3. Since there are unlimited lives, I can\x27t figure out the purpose of collecting buttons.
4. Graphics are sometimes glitchy, seams between elements are often visible.

It has a lot of potential, but there is something missing (like the power ups and brick bashing in Mario).
