product_title: Five Nights at Freddy\x27s
review_headline: This game may make you be more careful with your electric bill.
review_body: Five Nights at Freddy\xE2\x80\x99s is one of the best horror games to come out in the last 10 years. Somehow, they were able to take a game with such simple gameplay, and make it suspenseful. The game was a smash hit once it came out, and it\xE2\x80\x99s gotten a huge following, with a rabid fanbase wanting more. I first got a glimpse of the game when watching Rage Select play it a few months ago, and I was very impressed by what I saw. This is a game that I can\xE2\x80\x99t stop thinking about, especially now that my daughter is hooked and wants to know the full story. I gotta admit- I\xE2\x80\x99m in the same boat.  You play as a security guard at Freddy Fazbear\xE2\x80\x99s Pizza, a family pizza place similar to Chuck E. Cheese\xE2\x80\x99s or Showbiz Pizza. During the day, the animatronic characters sing and play music for all the kids to enjoy, but at night, once everyone is gone, they get a little\xE2\x80\xA6restless. The characters roam through the building, trying to get at you. Why? It\xE2\x80\x99s not exactly known yet, but if they get you, they\xE2\x80\x99ll think you\xE2\x80\x99re an endoskeleton without a costume, and will force you into once. How do you defend yourself against them? You don\xE2\x80\x99t, really. All you can do is stay in your office and close the doors to keep them out, checking on where the animatronics are via the security cameras on your screens. There are 4 animatronics out to get you: Bonnie the rabbit, Chica the chicken, Freddy Fazbear and Foxy the pirate fox. Foxy is actually supposed to be out of order, hidden behind a curtain in his area. But if you check the area, he\xE2\x80\x99ll start to peek, and before you know it, he\xE2\x80\x99ll take off to come get you. To make matters worse, there\xE2\x80\x99s a golden Freddy costume that may or may not be a hallucination. And on top of that, it turns out that several children went missing while at Freddy\xE2\x80\x99s a while back, and one person almost died during an event referred to as \xE2\x80\x9Cthe bite of \xE2\x80\x9987\xE2\x80\x9D.  Yeah, this sounds like a great place for families.  Playing the game is easy; all you do is check cameras, open and close doors, and turn on lights if you need them. The problem is, you have limited electricity, and it goes down very fast if you have more than one thing going at a time. It seems like it\xE2\x80\x99d be easy to just close the doors and wait for 6am to roll around, but having just one door closed drains a lot of power. Having both of them closed will make you a sitting duck in no time. To make matters worse, if Foxy comes up and bangs on the door, it\xE2\x80\x99ll take up even more power. You need to be very careful when you check the cameras too, as one of the animatronics could be in the rooms right next to your office, and as soon as you put the screen down, they could get you. See, not every room has a camera in them. There are many areas with no surveillance, so it\xE2\x80\x99s not like you know exactly where someone is at all times.  The game\xE2\x80\x99s biggest strength is how it manages to be suspenseful with what\xE2\x80\x99s essentially a game where nothing moves (save for Foxy). When you see Bonnie or Chica, they\xE2\x80\x99re just standing there, looking through the window or looking at the camera. You never actually see them walking around. Before you know it, they could be right outside your office, when you just saw them a couple of rooms away when you checked the cameras. Having the limited power supply helps the suspense, since you need to be careful with everything you do. You\xE2\x80\x99re completely defenseless- no gun, no knife, no way out. It\xE2\x80\x99s a breath of fresh air in a time when most games like this would give you a weapon of some kind to take them out. Just the idea of these machines with happy faces, and two sets of teeth, coming at you relentlessly, not stopping until 6am or they get ahold of you, is pretty freaky too. They\xE2\x80\x99re not going to rip you apart or bite you- they want to cram you into an animatronic costume, full of gears, wires and mechanical parts. Yeah, think about how THAT would feel for a second, all the while this thing smiling at you and Freddy\xE2\x80\x99s theme is playing. That\xE2\x80\x99s way worse than some stupid zombie biting you.  Try the game out. The demo gives you the first 3 levels, and there are 3 more with a custom mode to play after that if you buy it. This is the kind of game I\xE2\x80\x99d love to see more of, and I can\xE2\x80\x99t wait to see what happens in part 3.

review_headline: Here how to print documents without having to purchase the Pro version for $9.99
review_body:
If you don\x27t have Google Chrome on your PC, then please download and install it. You need Google Chrome to add available printers to your Google account to use for Google CloudPrint.

Steps 1 through 3 are for your computer. Step 4 through 9 are for OfficeSuite Professional.

1. Login to Google chrome with your Google account
2. Go to Settings>Show advanced settings, locate Google Cloud print and click on Add printers
3. All printers (local or network) should appear

4. Start the OfficeSuite Word document that you want to print.
5. Tap Menu>File>Print> Add Printer>Add account
6. Login with the Google account you have added the printers to in Google Chrome.
7. Select the account after you have logged in and tap on Allow access button.
8. A list of the printers appears, select the printer you want to use and tap on Add.
9. Tap on the printer to submit a print job.

product_title: TouchUp Pro - Photo Editor
review_headline: Simple, Yet VERY Effective Filter/Touch Up Editor - Cannot Change SAVE Location (Default Camera File Folder)
review_body:
Oddly enough, this app is not compatible with my Samsung Tab 3 10.1\x5C\x22 - which is an utter shame as if I were to use it regularly, it would be on that tablet. It could be the wonky chipset choice made by the Samsung engineers when it comes to the Tab 3 10.1\x5C\x22 (it\x27s not the first time I have run into brick walls over it... oh, the stories I have about trying to mirrocast on that tablet...), so I won\x27t ding TOUCH UP PRO over it.

The first thing I noticed, before even downloading, was the minimal permissions. Camera apps run the gamut when it comes to permissions, from LOL WHUT?! craziness to pretty minimal, like TOUCH UP PRO, so we are already looking good. Code is clean as well - no analytics again! As for Network Access, there is left-over, inactive \x5C\x22Google Play In-App Billing\x5C\x22 code for those who may have gotten this off the Google Play store as a freebie and wanted to upgrade. I have the feeling the Network Access is also a concomitant left-over from this. Does run OFFLINE without issue.

Installed at 50MB with automatic moving to my Internal USB Storage, leaving 17.51MB on Device Memory. The app does NOT exit with the back-key, but remains running in the background until Android\x27s own Resource Manager kicks it out (or you manually \x5C\x22optimize\x5C\x22), but as this is how Android is meant to work, this isn\x27t a hit but a neutral observation.

I must say this does have one of the better filter applications - sometimes you get a camera app that makes a pixelated mess when applying certain filters. In fact, this is the first one I can recall that lets you layer multiple filters at once, such as \x5C\x22Sepia\x5C\x22, \x5C\x22B & W\x5C\x22 and \x5C\x22Vintage Photo\x5C\x22 (the combination really does look like an old photo now!). The \x5C\x22Color Saturation\x5C\x22 is pretty bang-on as well - this may be the app you want if you have a device camera that takes rather washed-out looking photos (many of the economy priced tablets have this fault).

And yay for crop and rotate (it\x27s surprising how many camera apps don\x27t include so basic, and for me, needful tools).

In the end, there isn\x27t actually that much to this app. No crazy filters, no stamps, no borders, but there is also no social media links or intrusive permissions or code modules. The save option gives a choice of size, but not a choice of where to save it (although it did save automatically under my own device\x27s camera photo folder). This could be considered the only drawback, and I do suggest to the dev to at least add in an option to designate a location for photo saves. I do have to ding on this aspect as I well know how this could well be the deal-killer for a great many folks looking for a camera editor.

So yes, an overall simple \x5C\x22touch up\x5C\x22 photo app compared to other more fluffy apps... but if you are looking for something that is completely safe to download and fix otherwise mussy device photos, this may be just up your alley. This program doesn\x27t offer that, instead it offers a few verbal selections (classic Road, Modern Racer, Dutch City, French Randonneur, and Obsessive/Custom). Not sure what the last 3 bikes equate to, so only the first 2 choices are realistic for MOST riders.

I can say the numbers are quite different than the other calculators I\x27ve used. For Example, I only weigh about 145 on a \x27heavy\x27 day, riding a 15lb bike w 23mm tires front and rear. It gives a reasonable 100 psi for the rear, and the front is quite low @ 63psi.

The other calculator I used has my rear at 102 and the front at 72psi, which I have upped to around 80 typically, and even that seems almost squishy when I do ANY out of saddle exertions. I can\x27t IMAGINE 62psi...it would be quite scary! Can you visualize a high speed descent and hitting the brakes HARD with pressure that low? I\x27d think I\x27d be a sure candidate for pinch flats at that low pressure, or even blowing it out and rolling it off the rim.

And then my other road bike is steel and a few lbs heavier (19lbs vice 15). On this bike I actually weighed myself sitting ON the bike in full gear with 1 full water bottle, with first just the rear on the scale and then the front (the other wheel sitting on 2x4\x27s at the same height as the scale). This actual weight per wheel yielded 108lbs on the rear wheel and 73lbs on the front (hands in the drops). Yet this app gives me a massive 127psi rear and a quite reasonable 82psi front. That seems like quite a diff...the rear would suddenly be over the 23mm pressure rating (not to mention SUPER hard). SO I just can\x27t figure out how it calculates. I\x27ve been riding w/ 102 rear (which the other calculator used my actual weight on the front and rear) and around 80 front for a few years now with zero pinchflats, a very comfy ride (even on my aluminum 15lb race bike), yet never felt too soft as to be scary. I think I\x27ll stick with those numbers and ditch the numbers from this app.

Good luck, maybe it will work for you.

product_title: Spotify Music - for Fire TV
review_headline: With connectivity issues, bluetooth streaming is generally a better option
review_body:
I\x27ll preface by saying that I\x27ve only been using it a few hours at the time of this review. Will update if I get more experience that changes my rating.

As other have said, it\x27s better than nothing. The Chromecast has no native app, and all solutions are ugly and unreliable.

My Vizio TV has a native app that works, but it is...really simplified. It doesn\x27t support nearly the number of features that the full client has. So that\x27s nearly useless unless I only want to listen to my own playlists.

So then, we have this app for the Amazon FireTV Stick. Discovering it actually gave me a reason to really start using the stick itself (since my TV and Chromecast have all of the other apps I need). I\x27ve been trying to use it all afternoon, and the results have been...mediocre.

As has been discussed, it\x27s just a destination for streaming audio from your phone\x27s own Spotify app. You can\x27t just log into the Spotify app in the Amazon interface, log in, and start streaming music. You have to do all of that from your phone. Which is kind of how I\x27d like it to work, since it gives me a better keyboard and touch navigation through the menus. So that\x27s cool.

But the main problem I\x27ve had is that it doesn\x27t stay connected to the Spotify app on my iPhone 6. Local wi-fi network is strong. When I stream directly via bluetooth or use other apps from phone-to-tv, I have no problems. Music keeps playing for a while, but I think since it loses sync with the phone, that must cause it to start repeating songs. And the song and time shown on the TV are all wrong (likewise on the phone). I reconnect to Spotify Connect within the phone app, and it syncs up and keeps going. But I just don\x27t want to have to keep doing that.

I haven\x27t figured out exactly where the problem is. In the phone app, the network, the Amazon stick, or the Spotify Connect app. Like I said, since all of the others work independently, I think it\x27s Spotify Connect. So, that\x27s why I give it 3 stars for now. It\x27s somewhere to start that\x27s marginally better than the other options I have for getting Spotify on my TV.

But really, the best solution is to just connect my phone via bluetooth to my A/V receiver and stream audio that way. product_title: Beats by Dre Pill XL Speaker Titanium, One Size
review_headline: both will define your speaker life as well as how good it sounds
review_body:
I have been using Bluetooth speakers for a very long time. I have used some cheap and some so obese in cost it would blow your mind. The thing with a Bluetooth speaker is the importance on the battery as well as the design, both will define your speaker life as well as how good it sounds. The speaker itself is important but less important than you might think.

Considering the size of the speakers on these there is actually less difference on 98% of them than you might think, the position and design of the front grill ( build quality in other words ) will have more of an effect than anything else you throw at it. a over powered speak will give you more distortion than a under powered who will have less distinct sound. so in reality the battery who also gives you longevity and the circuitry that delivers the power source in what really drives these not the speakers.

I have used a JBL that cost over $175 less than this and sounds 1000x better but then again if you care more about looks than sound then this is the option for you. Everything from the low end tweaker speaker\x27s to the top end old iHome IDM8 will work great for most people. This is a Obscenely over priced company who tries to toss around marketing terminology to justify the over priced hardware.

And has successfully made a fool out of many people who like to spend money for a status symbol without ever shopping around or reading. Given that a Tweaker Speaker will produce what seems like a more distorted sound that is muffled and that is because of the design and aiming of the speaker. review_headline: A solid dash-cam for your vehicle.
review_body:
There are so, so many of these dash cams out there, and they\x27re becoming more popular in the US, so I figured I should get ahead of the game and try one out in my car.

The device comes well-boxed with a car charger (cigarette lighter with a long, long cable (about 4 feet) to micro USB), a regular micro USB cable for your computer, a suction cup, and that\x27s about it. It\x27s a very through-the-motions packaging experience. Nothing fancy, and the camera itself is a little plastic-y. The buttons on the camera have a very satisfying click to them, and my sample\x27s regular LCD screen looked just fine (if not HD), with no stuck/dead pixels or other screen anomalies.

Setup was a little trickier than I\x27d have liked, - it\x27s not a touch screen, and the button layout is not instinctively intuitive. Once you have it set up (date/time etc), it all becomes a lot simpler as you\x27ll likely just be hitting the record button.

Getting a micro SD card into the unit took a bit of finagling. I ended up using a credit card to push it in all the way as I don\x27t really have any nails to speak of. In a positive sense, at least it won\x27t be popping out by mistake!

Image quality is actually quite decent. There\x27s a slight fish-bowl look to things, a result of the extremely wide lens in there to capture everything very close in front of you (in the event of a collision, for example). Cars come out pretty well defined, and you\x27d have no trouble reading license plates when the car in front is reasonably close to you. This is important, so I\x27m glad it works.

Curiously, while you can zoom in and out, you cannot do this while the camera is recording. However, to be fair, it\x27s just a digital zoom (there\x27s no physical lens movement that I can tell), so you don\x27t gain any extra detail by zooming in anyway. If you have some basic editing tools at home, you can always zoom in as necessary, after the fact.

The GSHOCK option in the camera menu I found quite interesting. You can set it to low, medium, or high sensitivity, and the camera will record if it detects any sudden shock to the device. This could be particularly handy if someone crashes into you when you\x27re parked, although if they ram the back of your car, you might well be wishing you had another camera in the back window! At the highest sensitivity (my recommendation), it did a pretty decent job when I tapped the camera mount itself - starting recording immediately, though I\x27ll wait till someone reverses into my car to test that feature out extensively!

There are a few software quirks (e.g. to turn the device off you have to hold down the power button for a second or two... and then let go. If you don\x27t let go, it never actually turns off! Weird), and the interface definitely takes a little getting used to, but, you know.., the Esky 2.4\x5C\x22 Full HD car camera does a pretty decent job - doing basically what it sets out to do, and it works.

Overall, 4 out of 5. Certainly recommended for those in need of a dash-cam fix!

product_title: DBPOWER 13.3\x22 Portable DVD Player,2 Hours Rechargeable Battery,Swivel Screen,Supports SD Card and USB, Direct Play in Formats MP4/AVI/RMVB/MP3/JPEG (Black)
review_headline: A Solid DVD Player, But the Remote Control Disappoints
review_body:
I tried to purchase this product from Amazon three times because the first two times it arrived damaged. To add insult to injury, every time I asked for a replacement they wouldn\x27t honor it (thought they did give me a full refund and paid for return shipment) and when I reordered the price would jump around $10 each time. I waited until the price dropped to an acceptable level before I ordered it yet again. This time it arrived undamaged.

Now on to the product: The size is as advertised and the casing of the product is not a sturdy as it appears. Nor is the product is as heavy as you would think it would be. But it\x27s solid enough. As for the picture, I don\x27t find it as bright or sharp as you would expect. It\x27s not bad, it can be adjusted, and it depends on the angle of the screen to the viewer, but overall the quality is okay. Another review commented on how short the length of the power cord/adapter. The reviewer is right: the player must be practically on top of or next to the power socket.

So far I\x27ve tested the machine by playing four types of mediums: music CD; a purchased movie and TV show; a burned DVD, and a DVD containing shows copied from TV and recorded on a disc with a DVD recorder. So far the machine has played all the discs without any difficulty, which is surprising. The disc does have to be almost flawless, as the machine will have a problem with playback if there\x27s considerable smudges and scratches (but many machines will have that difficulty). One issue is that normally when a portable DVD player is on but at rest, the screen will either go into screen saver mode or the machine will simply shut down. This machine won\x27t do either; it will remain at the DVD factory screen. There could be a way to reset this, but I haven\x27t found it yet. Also for some reason when I turn on the machine from standby mode and play a purchased movies or shows, the subtitles will display when the event starts. This is very annoying because I have to go to the menu and turn off the subtitles. And the subtitles display on the TOP of the screen. I find this very odd. But I\x27m sure there\x27s a way to prevent this from happening; I just haven\x27t figured it out yet. I will write an update to this review to discuss the other options of product (TV, USB, WiFi, etc.).

The buttons on the machine for basic functions (skip, fast forward, stop, menu, etc,) is prominently displayed and I find the layout pretty solid and sound. But there is a slight lag when you press a command. For example, there seems to be one second lag between when you press the pause, skip or other functions during play before the command takes effect. It\x27s very different from other DVD players where the commands are achieved almost instantaneous. It\x27s not a major issue, but it\x27s just odd.

By far the biggest drawback is the remote control. It\x27s about the size of a post-it pad: it\x27s very small and easy to misplace. But a greater drawback is the layout of the button. One has to use their fingernails to press most of the buttons because they are so small and close together. In addition, with a few exceptions the buttons are in the same shape and size, resulting in a lack of differentiation between may of the most commonly used functions. And I swear there must be forty buttons on this tiny remote: thirty of them are exactly the same shape and size. I\x27m definitely considering getting a low-cost universal remote control (a learning remote) to use in place of the one provided. And the remote must be pointed directly in front of the sensor, otherwise it won\x27t work.

If this player was any more expensive, I would consider it a bust. But given the price of the product and the basic quality, this was not a bad purchase. I know other reviewers have mentioned the machine breaking down after a short time. But after several months use the it\x27s still operating quite well. There\x27s definitely better options out there, products of higher quality and less expensive. But for the options this one provides with the low price, this is a solid buy.

review_headline: Very good cables which actually draw about the same current (~2.0) as original Apple Lightning cables.
review_body:
I purchased a Zeus 4-pack Lightning cables. ( http://www.amazon.com/Certified-iPhone-Charging-Lightning-Connector/dp/B00OOM2DTQ/ )
Upon receipt, I tested all 4 cables to see what current (amps) it can draw from a 20w power supply adaptor.
I tested it against the original apple cable. The test was performed with an Apple Air 2 iPad.
The original apple cable drew up to 2.03A. The Zeus cables at most drew up to 1.42A MAX. They varied between 1.13 and 1.42.

I also purchased IXCC Lightning cables ( http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00QERR5CY/ ) and they worked better than Zeus cables. They were NOT perfect but drew higher Amps than the Zeus cables. They drew very close to 2.0A. One of the two IXCC cables drew around 1.91A MAX. The other one was able to draw 2.0A MAX.

IXCC doesn\x27t sell 4-packs. I purchased a 2-pack for $16.99. I wish the price was less or that they sold 4-packs -- like Zeus does -- but given the higher current supplied with the cables, I am very satisfied with the IXCC cables.

The Zeus cables should be sufficient for any of the iPhones which only draw 1.1A max. But for iPads, which draw 2.0A max, these Zeus cables won\x27t provide full current to charge up iPads as quickly as possible. They do charge up eventually.

Also of note, ALL 4 of the Zeus cables had an error message the very first time I plugged them into the iPad Air 2. ALL 4 of them. But after the first connection, there were NOT any further error messages upon future connections. It\x27s as if the cables needed to initially pair/synch with the iPad before it recognized it as a certified Apple cable. At any rate, the Zeus cables did/do work after the initial pairing.

Also of interesting note, the IXCC cables did NOT have this quirky need to pair with the iPad the very first time I connected the cables. Both started charging with NO error msgs the first time I connected them to my iPad Air 2.

My recommendation would definitely be to purchase the IXCC cables if you have iPads which can utilize the 2.0A faster charging current. If you will use these cables to charge an iPhone only, then Zeus cables should suffice. I can\x27t attest to the longevity of any of these cables. I am only attesting to the current that can be drawn through the Zeus and IXCC cables.

I was NOT provided with any free samples. I purchased all cables with my own money. This is a TRUE fair, balanced and objective review.

Lest you think I\x27m here on behalf of IXCC to promote their cables, I will state that if money is no issue, purchase the original Apple Cables. Apple Cables are the best, period. review_headline: This disc contains the least satisfactory..
review_body: ...Brendel Mozart concerto #25.  Best I think is his Vox/Turnabout version with Paul Angerer at which time he  was not committed to excessive ornamentation, primarily in the second movement (not by accident, it is paired with an   almost unadorned 22nd concerto which is equally impressive).  With Neville Marriner,, he ornaments the second movement excessively but Marriner/ASMF are quite good in it. Brendel\x27s best adorned version, though, is a live version on Golden  Melodram  (titled \x5C\x22 Great Conductors at the Piano\x5C\x22) with Eugen Jochum and the Bavarian RSO .  Jochum provides a reading matched  only by George Szell with Rudolf Serkin/Sony, filled with poetry and verve despite Brendel\x27s cluttered second movement.  Mackerras, I am assured by a good friend who sang with him at the Met, was constantly experimenting and experienced  a brief infatuation the HIP orthodoxy.  It mars both concerti here, but #9 is considerably plainer, especially in the second  movement. I still prefer the Brendel/Marriner and Janigro versions, but if one doesn\x27t mind the interpolations, another star might well  be added.  I would select  alternative Brendel versions of these concerti, or non-Mackerras readings, however.    Peers:  #9-Larrocha/Davis/RCA, Haebler/Rowicki/Philips, Gulda/Bohm/Orfeo, Brendel/Janigro/Vanguard, Goode/Orpheus/Nonesuch    #25- Serkin/Szell/Sony; Fleisher/Szell/Sony; Goode/Nonesuch; Kovacevich/Davis/Philips; Moravec/Vlach/Supraphon; Larrocha/Davis/RCA; Haebler/Galliera/Philips; Foldes/Sawallisch/Golden Melodram

product_title: Only To Rise
review_headline: Hard, ballsy, haunting, tasty, perfect, melodic ... so uh, pretty much PERFECT !
review_body:
I could not love this album more! I have listened to it from front to back now about 10 times ... and it is quite simply the best album these two have ever made. There are melodies, hauntingly sick leads as only George Lynch can deliver, bluesy tracks, love, passion, and everything you would have wanted from these Pillars of Rock. Yes, you can hear Stryper in parts, you can certainly here Dokken in parts. That\x27s what makes this so beautiful. Come on, didn\x27t you ever want to know how amazing Dokken could be if they had a better singer? Or how much better Stryper could be if not held in the confines of forcing every song to deliver enough blatant Christianity so as not to lose their fundamental base? Well, here you go. This is it ... the album of albums. You will love how much you can hear each part fantastically well.

The drums are recorded perfectly as you feel the bass drum, not just hear it. You can hear every time Tichy hits the cymbals - oh it\x27s just sooooo good. Tichy is such a masterful timekeeper. The double bass right in the pocket. Bands wish they had someone this in the zone, but they don\x27t. Brian should be talked about among the greats every time they are mentioned. He doesn\x27t take over the song, although he so easily could, he just just lays this seemless, steady, luscious, emotive, and essential drum line.

James Lamenzo is so absolutely ROCK solid on the bass lines. He\x27s always moving and accentuating every little inch of each song. This is a bass players delight right here. So nice to have a rock album not afraid to kick that bass up right along with everyone else and not try to hide it. It\x27s beautiful, every note, and run better than the one before.

George Lynch ... come on ... George Lynch killed it on this thing. Every lead just sings through each tune. Nothing out of place and hoards of stretches and vibrato that is so signature Lynch. Wait till you hear the song Me Without You and that tap sequence he plays.It\x27s pure silk. Oh, I could just die in that song. Then listen to his scorching riffs in Divine - they are nothing short of the songs title. He plays with so much testosterone in parts it makes you wanna sit up and adjust yourself! The blues, the heart, the ferver ... yes it is all there.

And Michael ... what I love about this disk is he doesn\x27t overdo it. Sometimes less is more dude. But, on this disk, tasteful and perfectly executed. I love that in a Rock and Roll album as amazing as this one that you can have a man sing as pure as he does. There is no growl in his voice, which is fine, there is plenty of guitar doing that. I love the harmonies, the melodies, and just the fact that he is singing, not screaming or growling, enhances every fiber of this recording.

Seriously, it has been too long since I have had the disk spinning. I am already having withdrawls ... I need to hear Hero-Zero and Only To Rise really badly. And then, Rescue Me slide into Me Without You. This disk is not going to leave my car for months. DANG !!!!!!!! It is off the charts good people. THIS IS A MUST HAVE !

review_headline: Good album, but not their best
review_body:
I love Alter Bridge; in fact I\x27d say they\x27re my favorite band at the moment. However of their 4 albums that have currently been released, this is my least favorite. This album just lacks the memorable, hard rocking sound of the other 3. I don\x27t know if it\x27s the lack of production value that others have mentioned or what, but I just don\x27t get the same feeling from most of these tracks as I do from the tracks on their other albums. That\x27s not to say there aren\x27t some really good tracks. But in an album with 16 tracks, which is more than on any of their other albums, there are only about 3 songs I\x27d consider really good or great (Isolation, Still Remains, Coeur D\x27Alene). Whereas on their other albums there are at least 5 or 6 great songs out of 11-13 tracks.

Finally, what\x27s the deal with Amazon and Spotify, among others, stating that all of the tracks on this album have explicit lyrics? As far as I can tell none of their songs are explicit, on this or any other album. It\x27s one of my favorite characteristics of the band, actually.

product_title: The Phosphorescent Blues
review_headline: such as with the brilliant \x22Who\x27s Feeling Young Now
review_body:
I preordered this album 2 months ago, as I\x27m a rabid PB fan. Receiving it Tuesday (the first day of it\x27s release), I\x27ve listened to it about 4 or 5 times in my car so far.

This band has gradually gone from the heavily eclectic (Punch) with their 4 movement 45 minute "Blind Leaving the Blind" to a more short song format over the years, perhaps becoming more accessible to ever more music fans, such as with the brilliant "Who\x27s Feeling Young Now?" from 2012. This album continues that trek, with a cleaner studio vibe reminiscent of 2010\x27s "Antifogmatic", I\x27m sure partly due to being produced by T Bone Burnett. As great as all the cuts are, I would say the tour de force this time around is the first composition, "Familiarity".

These guys are easily the most creative bunch of virtuosos you will ever hear on their respective instruments. As a serious fan and musician in both the classical and jazz worlds, my introduction to PB 2 years ago left me feeling this is the freshest and most inspiring group in the world of music today. I drove 8 hours both ways to the Savannah Music Festival last year to see them live, and it was worth every mile! (PLEASE come to South Florida, fellas.)

I can confidently say that Punch Brothers will never make a bad album... they\x27re that good. This album was worth the 3 year wait. My only peeve is that a deluxe version with extra songs is being released on vinyl only next month. Awh, come on, guys! I\x27ll probably get it, like when I gave my "Antifogmatic" to a friend and bought the deluxe of that (to be richly rewarded, such as the absolutely burning "When in Doubt" - blue grass meets heavy weight jazz?). Vinyl\x27s cool, but I like the flexibility of CD.

product_title: Exposure: Deluxe Edition /  Expos\xC3\xA9
review_headline: Booklet Comes With *LYRICS* And Additional Info! Great *DEBUT* Album! *Expanded* On 2 CDs!
review_body:
It\x27s about time that Exposé\x27s debut album be given the deluxe treatment. I loved EXPOSURE and so I was overjoyed when I found out that Cherry Pop in the UK was releasing this 2-CD expanded version of it. I\x27m amazed that it\x27s usually Japan or the UK that does these lovingly expanded re-issues of older soul/disco/r&b music from the USA (look at Universal Japan\x27s reissue of the original Donna Summer "Live & More" album or Big Break Records UK expanded edition of The Pointer Sisters "Break Out" album for example), while the US record companies just keep putting out the same stuff just repackaged (I\x27m still waiting for a Janet "Miss" Jackson\x27s CONTROL album to get an expanded makeover).

I only know the original album (I actually had it on cassette) and the old CD, so I don\x27t know if many of these remixes have been released before, as another customer stated, and I think I have two remixes that are on a "Free-Style" compilation, but I\x27m not sure if they\x27re the same as on this edition, so mostly all of these extra tracks are new to me.

On track #6 "Point Of No Return" from the original album, the track listed here on CD 1 is the extended version and runs 6:08-minutes. I no longer have that old cassette tape, but on the previous CD version of EXPOSURE this track is only 3:29-minutes, so that\x27s one difference that I found, but that might be because the CD version had an edited version of the song -- I can\x27t remember if the track was longer on the original.

The remastering sounds fantastic and I think Cherry Pop did a great job.

EXPOSURE DELUXE EDITION comes with a booklet featuring the lyrics to all songs, track annotations by the song-writer Lewis Martineé who talks about the inspiration for each song and how it came about, liner notes by Bill Pitzonka written on Aug 2014 that includes interviews with Jeanette Jurado, Gioia Bruno, and Ann Curless discussing how the group was formed etc., discography, some publicity pictures from back then, and single/album sleeve pictures.

According to the liner notes there was a different group of singers who initially recorded "Point Of No Return" and "Exposed To Love" and featured lead vocals by Alé Lorenzo, who sounds exactly like Jeanette Jurado, and in the credits on lead vocals in the booklet it lists Lorenzo as the singer of both songs that feature the 1985 mixes. Jurado --once the group was formed with the lineup of Bruno, Jurado and Curless -- went back to the studio and recorded her own vocals on the two songs and Lewis Martineé says that if you owned any of the first 125,000 pressing of the EXPOSURE album you have Lorenzo\x27s vocals, and any after are Jurado. I didn\x27t know that so the liner notes were very informative.

However it should\x27ve been mentioned that Gioia Bruno was diagnosed with throat cancer (I think that\x27s what it was), which caused her to drop out of the group and be replaced by Kelley Moneymaker, while she recovered, and eventually she rejoined the group. I learned all this when I saw them perform at an LGBT Pride Festival back in either late 90s or early 2000s and Bruno was back in the group, and all were in fine voice.

Another interesting tidbit is the group\x27s performance at the famed Apollo Theater in New York, which you can find on Youtube, when they were touring. They brought the house down and I remember watching this on TV.

Anyhow, if you were a kid in the 80s and went out clubbing you\x27d know this album and so I definitely recommend picking it up. If you like "High Energy/Free Style" music from the 80s then EXPOSURE is what you need.

Normally, I don\x27t really care for remix versions of songs, but in this case all of the additional tracks are based on the strong hits from the album and the remixes are extended mixes that doesn\x27t change the song around too much.rmed etc., discography, some publicity pictures from back then, and single/album sleeve pictures.

product_title: VOLDA
review_headline: Expensive, obscure, and really worth having
review_body: Peter Br\xC3\xB6tzmann\x27s recordings are so numerous, and in their various formats -- duo, trio, tentet, bands with electric bass, etc. -- oftentimes so similar that it\x27s easy to overlook any number of them, especially if they\x27re pricy imports. What\x27s more, though I am an enormous admirer of Br\xC3\xB6tzmann\x27s work, I will confess to wishing him to show more often the multidimensionality he clearly possesses: a little less face-flaying, a broader range of emotion. (This is not to suggest he never displays a wider emotional palette; only that he doesn\x27t do so often enough.) Both of these considerations lead me to endorse this particular release, which features enough screaming sax and tarogato to please the Br\xC3\xB6tzmann-as-human-cheese-grater connoisseur, but also a good deal of subtlety, refinement, and gentleness. Br\xC3\xB6tzmann deserves some of the credit for this, and not only insofar as he knows how to lay out. But what\x27s great about *Volda*, for me, is the versatility of Michiyo\x27s koto work (both the 21-string koto that provides moments of real lyrical beauty and the 17-string \x5C\x22bass\x5C\x22 koto that gives this recording a surprising amount of bottom end, particularly as the third piece builds toward its final, and remarkable, climax) and her interplay with Paal Nilssen-Love, who must surely be numbered among the best living drummers by now. Br\xC3\xB6tzmann is, at times, his overpowering self -- as well he should be! -- but he is also clearly listening to Michiyo and Nilssen-Love, and he gives them ample room to develop intricate interplay between their strange-bedfellow instruments. The result is a deeply satisfying record that balances ferocity with lyricism.    Jazz is full of hybrid forms these days; indeed, it was from its nineteenth-century inception an assimilative and hybrid medium. But this records smacks not at all of the soppy blandness sometimes connoted by the phrase(s )\x5C\x22[one] world music.\x5C\x22 Here one really must give Br\xC3\xB6tzmann\x27s indelible musical identity its due: even as he pursues musical interactions with musicians from all over the world, who play any number of instruments, he never compromises his own utterly distinctive voice. My claims about the subtle interactions the koto and drums should not be mistaken for allegations that this recording does not bear the stamp of Br\xC3\xB6tzmann\x27s sui generis brand of European free jazz (or whatever one might choose to call it). He is an assimilator, not a chameleon, and this record\x27s distinctive qualities could never lead anyone to mistake it for any other musician\x27s work. *Volda* is as purely Br\xC3\xB6tzmann\x27s as \x5C\x22India\x5C\x22 was Coltrane\x27s.    That said: Michiyo Yagi\x27s solo record for John Zorn\x27s Tzadik label -- [[ASIN:B00000G4SY Shizuku]] -- is highly recommended to anyone who enjoys the (relatively) softer moments that make *Volda* a subtle and attractive recording.

product_title: Popov: Symphony No. 1, Op. 7 / Shostakovich: Theme & Variations, Op. 3
review_headline: The Popov is a major discovery, and performed well
review_body:
Revival discs such as this Telarc release have a pretty mixed track record with me, but this is one of the winners. I had never heard any of Gavril Popov\xE2\x80\x99s music before \xE2\x80\x93 not surprising because he took the condemnation that this 1st symphony received in 1935 to heart and wrote \xE2\x80\x9Csocialist realist\xE2\x80\x9D music for the rest of his career \xE2\x80\x93 but his 1st is one of the best 20th-century symphonies I\xE2\x80\x99ve had the pleasure of hearing. All of fifty minutes, it is a long work and very taxing for the listener. Although tonal, the outer movements contain spiky dissonances and material is rarely repeated in its original form, always subject to variation and alteration, often reworked thoroughly.

The symphony is cast in three movements, with two dramatic, dynamic outer movements and a soulful, contrasting central Largo about twenty minutes in duration. The ambitious opening Allegro energico is actually my least favorite of the three. It has a faked ending \xE2\x80\x93 the music deceptively fades out before starting up again several times out of the silence, finally dying away. The limpid, central Largo, with its beautiful and memorable oboe melody, is a masterful midcentury example of modernism, attractive and complex and idiosyncratic all at the same time. About 10 minutes in length, the finale is the shortest of the three movements and is written in a similar idiom as the opening Allegro but I think more coherently. That said, the sheer difficulty of the music and its complex organization may make me re-evaluate that opening Allegro on more listenings. And there will be more listenings, because this is a top echelon creation. To set a \xE2\x80\x9Cquality level\xE2\x80\x9D, I\xE2\x80\x99d rate the Popov as better than any of Sergei Prokofiev\xE2\x80\x99s 7 symphonies excepting the 1st and 5th, and on par in achievement with a major effort like Dmitri Shostakovich\xE2\x80\x99s 10th. That\xE2\x80\x99s good company to be in.

I have heard Leon Botstein conduct live a couple of times and always thought the results worthy of a talented amateur rather than a professional. Both the Popov and Shostakovich performances here are very strong, though, which suggests that if you give Botstein a world-class orchestra like the London Symphony and I assume sufficient rehearsal time, the results will be very successful. Their performance is precise \xE2\x80\x93 so important to a score like the 1st symphony \xE2\x80\x93 and lively. The recording\xE2\x80\x99s sound quality is excellent, important because the dramatic outer movements of the Popov are taxing to any stereo reproduction.

The disc also contains a juvenile variations set from Dmitri Shostakovich, written in an appealing and heartfelt late romantic style. If you\xE2\x80\x99re a committed classical fan, you\xE2\x80\x99ll absolutely want to hear the Popov. Strongly recommended.sults worthy of a talented amateur rather than a professional. product_title: Rock or Bust
review_headline: No Iconic Song But Still a Great Album
review_body:
This is a pretty good new album that will satisfy fans. When I was in primary school Razors Edge came out with Thunderstruck that gained the band a new generation of fans who as they got old enough to have their own money tracked down their older albums as well. To be honest I don\x27t hear a song on here that will dominate the charts and do the same thing, although perhaps if the track Play Ball is officially used as the theme song for promoting baseball, basketball or some sport where they use that phrase it may well achieve that. I can see a lot of people adding Sweet Candy to their Candy Crush playing soundtrack on their Kindle Fire and other devices. Although there may well be no chart dominating hit on here the songs on the album are all as good as most of the songs on their previous albums, there\x27s certainly no fillers on here. The voice and sound of AC/DC is still very present on this album. I\x27ve listened to this a few times now and haven\x27t noticed any swearing on the CD either which will either be a plus or a minus for some people. My only complaint is at only 34 minutes perhaps we could have had a few more songs.

The album cover artwork of course deserves every accolade and ideas like this are something other artists need to come up with for their fans who still like to buy physical CDs and to give those who buy it more than those who obtain burnt copies.

product_title: Black Halo
review_body: This is a different type of music for me.  I am the Megadeth, Metallica kind of person but I also range to Savatage which is what this kind of resembles.  The best way for me to sum this album up is that it\x27s a combination of Queensryche and Savatage.  It tells a story and has a heavy metal opera feel to it.  It has lots of power and some of the songs like Memento Mori are just incredible.  I would call this album a metal opera of sorts if you will.  I ranked it a 4 because it has very great sound quality and delivers.  Some of the songs are slow but when the power rolls it is unstoppable.  When the lights are down is the fastest song on the album and I wish they would have done a few more like that one but all in all a great addition to my collection.

product_title: my lover 45 rpm single
review_headline: One Of Two Failed Stax Singles By Barbara & The Browns Appeared In 1965
review_body:
Barbara And The Browns (Barbara, her sisters Betty and Roberta and brother Maurice Brown all from Memphis) are in some books as a One-Hit Wonder for their May 1964 # 97 Billboard Pop Hot 100 Big Party b/w You Belong To Her (Stax 150). It originally emerged as Wil Mo 101 but after it began attracting some considerable local interest it was leased by the much larger Stax. Unfortunately, not only were they running head on into the British Invasion in terms of the Pop charts, which had been shoving all but the best North American artists off the upper regions of those charts since The Beatles arrived in January, but Billboard had also suspended the R&B listings in late 1963, something that would last throughout all of 1964 and to the end of January 1965. And you just know that Big Party would have scored much higher on the R&B charts had they been in effect and, who knows, that publicity may have, in turn, helped the Hot 100 results.

In any event, neither of In My Heart b/w Please Be Honest With Me as Stax 158 later in 1964, and I Don\x27t Want Trouble b/w My Lover as Stax 164 in 1965 - and the 45-rpm you see covered here - went anywhere. They would go on to record at Cadet, Atco and the MGM Sound Of Memphis labels (without any further sides making any charts) and that aspect of their recording career is well covered in the 2007 CD \x5C\x22Can\x27t Find Happiness - The Sounds of Memphis Recordings\x5C\x22 from the Ace of London subsidiary Kent Records.

Finding those Stax sides in a quality CD setting is, however, currently impossible.

Barbara apparently quit recording after 1972 and passed away in her 70s on February 3, 2010.

product_title: Millions Like Us: The Story of the Mod Revival 1977-1989
review_headline: The reality is this: most of \x22mod revival\x22 music is pretty mediocre.
review_body: The reality is this: most of "mod revival" music is pretty mediocre. The Jam were fantastic (but they\x27re not included here) and there were a handful of other bands that had at least a few good songs, but the majority of it was pretty sub-standard power-pop. Most people who got seriously into Mod through the revival of the late 70\x27s/early 80s quickly moved on from revival sounds and dug deeper into the 60s stuff, which was FAR FAR better anyway.  In truth, the mod revival bands had more to do with punk and very little to do with the sounds that the original mods listened to.  I understand the desire to include as many different bands as possible, but if the more mediocre tracks had been omitted this could easily have been a 2-cd set instead of 4. product_title: Berlioz: La damnation de Faust
review_headline: There are better recordings to be had.
review_body: There is no argument about the late Colin Davis being one of the major champions of the music of Berlioz and his many recordings demonstrate that commitment; that does not mean I personally care for the way Davis presents the music -- no particular reason, to me he just sounds too stiff and uninteresting.  My preferences for Berlioz in general are for those conducted by Munch and Dutoit (the more limited number of recordings made by Monteux and Martinon also stand out).  Being myself a major fan of Berlioz, I do listen to Davis recordings when wanting a different "take" on something in particular; all a matter of taste.  The winner and still number one for "La Damnation de Faust" remains Markevitch on DG, from all the way back in 1959 (very early stereo, but it still sounds better than this one).  If you want Davis in this work, find the earlier (ca. 1973) version on Philips.  The main fault with this one is the sound; rather recessed, dim even, and, when the volume is cranked up, still nothing to be wowed about.  There  are really no other particular faults to be found with this LSO release, but those in search can do better (Markevitch, Dutoit, or Ozawa even).

product_title: Tchaikovsky: Swan Lake, Op. 20 (Recorded 1982)
review_body:
This recording, from April/May 1982, by EMI, is, in my estimation, the version of choice; tops in overall quality of performance and sound (in music like this, both qualities must be high!). This is complete on 3-CDs, none of that compromising stuff where a movement here and a passage there gets hacked out so the whole thing will fit onto 2 discs. This includes the Act III Pas de Deux which often gets left out because it was lost for a long time, and was only included after-the-fact in the first place, not part of the original score (but, if you\x27re accustomed to hearing it, you\x27ll miss it). Lanchbery also recorded Tchaikovsky\x27s other ballets (Sleeping Beauty and The Nutcracker) about the same time, all are absolutely excellent and the collector with an interest in this music should seek them out (all were released by Musical Heritage Society, as well as original EMI). Nothing here is overdone, nothing too fast nor too slow, no histrionics nor banality, powerful where it needs to be, lovely everywhere, in short, near perfect.

One word of warning! The serious collector should attempt obtain the CD versions of these released by Musical Heritage Society. In the case of Swan Lake and Sleeping Beauty, these will both be on 3-CD sets. EMI has also released them, but, in both cases, they were gotten onto 2-CD sets by making a few cuts in the music here and there.

The earliest recording of the "true" Swan Lake score was that of Antal Dorati/Minneapolis (Dec. 1954, for Mercury Living Presence, available on a 2-CD set, mono only, no Act III Pas de Deux - it wasn\x27t published yet - complete, but reported that some repeats were cut). An early (stereo?) recording by Ansermet (Decca) was quite good, but it is of a older, highly corrupt (and heavily cut) score, which does represent the performing version in use for many years and still used in some productions. Probably the best sounding release was that by Dutoit/Montreal (Decca), which is also a very strong performance which appears to be favored by many, has the Act II Pas de Deux, but ALAS is fitted onto 2-CDs by 3 of the above mentioned hacks and chops (albeit minor ones, BUT I want this score complete!). A 3-lp set conducted complete by Previn is also among the better ones ever made, released on 2-CDs with same kinds of minor cuts. The only complete version I am aware of which was squeezed onto 2 CDs was that of Wolfgang Sawallisch/Philadelphia Orchestra (EMI), an outstanding performance, but falling just a hair short of Lanchbery, probably due to the excessive tempi needed. An altogether outstanding offering is made by Mark Ermler/Royal Opera House Covent Garden (on Conifer, 2 CDs), no Act III Pas de Deux, most tempi are slower, therefore being more "danceable", with full luscious sound and great poise. A version by Evgeni Svetlanov/USSR State Symphony (1988, Melodia, 3 CDs) is rough in delivery and sound, has no Act III Pas de Deux, but is also engaging and visceral and offers an interesting complement to the more sublime Lanchbery. Everyone needs at least one recording of "Swan Lake", there are many good ones out there, but I must place Lanchbery at the peak. [Important Note: DO NOT confuse this recording with one of 1967 Lanchbery made with the Vienna Symphony! That was for a film score and was of an older performing version, with many cuts and re-arrangements of movements.]formance which appears to be favored by many, has the Act II Pas de Deux, but ALAS is fitted onto 2-CDs by 3 of the above mentioned hacks and chops (albeit minor ones, BUT I want this score complete!). product_title: Ja, vi elsker (Ceremonial Versions)
review_body:
The 1st review of this SACD & BD combo pack here at Amazon lacks a certain something.
I\x27m now 1/3 of the way through this and could not wait to verify some website reviews that this is a delicious production.
Sound of the band is clear and up front without any congestion or aggressiveness. The chorus sings on all odd-numbered tracks (8 of the 15) and sounds right there with you. Most tracks are respectable length for folksy and/or patriotic numbers, between 3 and 12 minutes for a total of about 80\x27. Halvorsen has two transcribed items here; Boyars march (I was hopping!) and the 1st Norwegian Rhapsody (not as great).
The SACD sounds so warm and alert; I can\x27t imagine that the Blu-Ray could sound even better.
The drawbacks are:
1. The producers assumed we all speak and read Norwegian; texts without translations!
2. Some of the music has a parochial feel - not likely to grip most of us.
3. The extensive notes use paragraphs dealing with guilt about enjoying a band playing patriotic music, and find almost no space to discuss the music itself.
If you want to hear a band and chorus march through your living room playing music mostly unknown to you, here you go.

product_title: Storm the Gates of Hell
review_headline: Another very good DH metalcore album
review_body:
Demon Hunter just keeps on clicking. And they keep the goods coming. Storm The Gates of Hell is the last album that Don Clark, brother of lead vocalist Ryan Clark appears in, and the band sends him off with a heck of a record. Not quite as consistent as some of the band\x27s other top albums, Storm The Gates does benefit off of Carry Me Down, possibly the best DH track out and definitely the top ballad from the band. In fact, its one of the best ballads in metal history imo.

When I said that it isn\x27t as consistent, I mean that there were a handful of tracks I really loved, and a couple I couldn\x27t care for at all. review_headline: Excellent 1960s/70s Bernstein Columbia recordings live again!
review_body:
I recently ordered Sony\x27s Leonard Bernstein Album collection, and it arrived in just several days to Michigan from Z Overstocks in the UK! The shipping was prompt, and the 80 CDs in the set were in great condition and perfect order; absolutely no complaints about the quality or shipping of this CD mega set!

I will have a great time in the coming weeks with this musical encyclopedia, a real feast of listening pleasure. I have so far listened to the CDs of Bernstein\x27s "West Side Story" Symphonic suite, "Candide" Overture, "On the Waterfront" and "Fancy Free", and find them to be excellent early 1960s stereo, with alot of bass and "Punch" where needed. Bernstein\x27s "Prelude, Fugue and Riffs", with soloist Benny Goodman, and "On the Town" are also excellent.
I also checked CD 80, "Great Marches", and liked the Sousa items, Rule Brittania, Le Marsellaise, Battle Hymn of the Republic, and Star Spangled banner. I had read a review of this in it\x27s "Bernstein Century" release of ca. 1998, and did not find the bass (Booming bass was their complaint) a problem. Some of Lenny\x27s tempos seem a bit spritely for Sousa marches, but they work, and the end result is enjoyable.

I know many of the recordings herein from individual releases, and believe the Falla CD will be terrific, for example.

This is one of the best value/dollar deals in the Classical music world right now. Consider it an investment, and GO FOR IT.

product_title: Gangster of Love: The Early Years
review_headline: EARLY WINTER  BEFORE HE BECAME AN \x22OVERNIGHT\x22 SENSATION.
review_body:
For deep fans of Johnny winter this is worth hearing if you want to hear his formative work. This reissue is almost the same as the 2003 2 CD set on the Fuel label except that the earlier set collects four more tracks not found on this new one.

This has recordings beginning in 1960 with Winter\x27s first band, Johnny and The Jammers ("School Days"/"You Know I Love You") and continues with a number of singles Winter recorded for very small labels (Dart, Frolic, KRCO, Pacemaker, Diamond Jim, Todd, etc.) in the early/mid \x2760s. If you\x27re thinking all these tracks have Winter\x27s scorching guitar front and center you may be disappointed. Winter was still finding his own style and sound which is evident across these tracks. Consequently some tunes are better than others as far as guitar work. You\x27ll hear strains of "Gatemouth" Brown, Freddie King, Little Richard, Guitar Slim, Jimmy Reed, and several others throughout this set. But it is pretty cool to hear Winter before he exploded onto the scene in the late \x2760s playing in different musical styles--especially r&b style songs. There\x27s a number of cover tunes from different genres which are pretty interesting to hear Winter tackle, along with the help of a number of different sidemen from different regions (Texas, Louisiana, etc.) of the South. Not every track is a vocal--also here are some instrumentals that show Winter\x27s early sometimes incendiary style of playing.

This set is for fans who are very familiar with (and already own) Winter\x27s best albums--both studio and live efforts. It\x27s fascinating to hear him working out his music and bringing different influences together into what would be his own style of playing.

product_title: Nielsen: Symphonies Nos. 1 & 5 / Helios Overture / Flute Concerto / Clarinet Concerto / Maskarade; Schultz: Serenade for Strings
review_body:
Fabulous historical recordings, but these are early Decca\x27s which still sound fine given their age. Symphony No. 1 is by Thomas Jensen/Danish State Radio Symphony, recorded June 1952, first commercial recording of the work (and, I think, the earliest one in existence); very fine, I have found none of the Nielsen recordings by Jensen have ever really been bettered, though some have come close. If one wishes to search long enough, a complete series of the Nielsen Symphonies by this conductor, some commercial others from concerts, may be acquired. Most of the rest of the items on this 2-CD set are or have been available elsewhere, but I think this maybe the only source currently available for the Symphony 1.

Symphony No. 5, Jensen/Danish Radio, recorded April 1954, is the second commercial version (following Tuxen for EMI in 1950); Helios Overture, Tuxen/Danish Radio, recorded June 1952. Flute Concerto, Jespersen/Jensen/Danish Radio; Clarinet Concerto, Erikson/Woldike/Danish Radio; and Maskarade excepts, Jensen, all recorded April 1954. Jespersen was the dedicatee of the Flute Concerto, and this was the first recording of it. All are among the earliest made. Unbelievable that it took so long for Nielsen to start becoming "popular" as it was the 1970\x27s before recordings of his music were released on a regular basis. The Danish conductors Thomas Jensen, Erik Tuxen, and Launy Grondahl all had first-hand knowledge about how Nielsen wanted his music to sound and this shows through in their various releases. Those with an interest in this wonderful composer should investigate.

product_title: Heaven & Earth
review_body: Here is one question for the (at this point) one hundred different five star reviewers of this album: How many stars would Fragile get? Seventeen? How many for Close to the Edge? Thirty two? Folks who throw five star reviews around willy nilly need to take a breath, and realize they are not really reviewers, but cheerleaders. And hey, that\x27s ok. I love Yes. Seen them every tour since 1977. But if this is a good Yes album, I am apparently stone deaf. I saw Jon Davison twice on this past tour, and he is a very nice replacement for Jon Anderson-gauzy shirts, ethereal voice, cosmic references. But as long as Jon Anderson is on earth and breathing, it is hard to take this band seriously. The last tours were full versions of Close to the Edge, The Yes Album and Going For the One. Davison acquitted himself respectfully, more Jon Anderson than Benoit David\x27s take on Drama was. Yet the previous vocalist managed to get some life out of these guys, where on this record, the band literally sleep walks through a mind numbing embarrassment of stuporific elevator music.  The list of the guilty is large. First up-Roy Thomas Baker, of Queen fame at the production helm. Those Yes fans who are hard core will remember him as the producer of the failed follow up to Tormato in 1979, an album that wasted months of time, thousands of dollars, and miles of recording tape better left untouched. Some of that ended up as a blueprint for a wispy Jon Anderson solo album, but the main result of this collaboration was a hugely acrimonious break up of one of the most legendary prog bands of the seventies, and no album. The production here is demo level and sounds hurried and murky-drums in the background, Squire\x27s bass varying from inaudible to middling, but always on cruise control. Howe is hard to gauge, more a background coloring than the forceful disciple of Chet Atkins and maniacal fretboard wizard of the seventies that topped \x27best guitarist\x27 polls on both sides of the pond. Downes has a distinct lack of imagination in his keyboards, although he may be trying to inject some 70\x27s authenticity and sacrificed the rest to the gods. Davison sounds as bright and excited as anyone who just joined his dream band would. But inexplicably he has co writer in credit on most of the album. And though vocally a fine performer, lyrics are not his strength. Subway Walls has flickers of the Yes we knew and loved, but is written by Davison and Downes. Squire and Howe have nothing to say musically any more? Seriously a sad state of affairs for such a beloved band. Yes, we may have unreasonable expectations, but this falls off a cliff and drags everyone with it. Safe, saccharine, pop soft rock cliched trite unchallenging slow tempo poorly produced AOR bland unambitious easy listening. This is a compendium of various comments on this site. Does that sound like a Yes album you cannot wait to hear? If Open Your Eyes was a two star affair, let me be clear: this would rate a zero on that scale.  One reviewer put it this way-if Starcastle was several degrees away from Yes, this album is several degrees away from Starcastle. If you are a long term Yes fan, let that last sentence guide you.  In summation, this is the worst album they have ever released, by a longshot. If you enjoy watching disasters unfold, jump aboard. If you love Yes as much as many of the reviewers here do? Mourning is upon us. The gates of delirium have slammed shut.  .

product_title: in my heart 45 rpm single
review_headline: One Of Two Failed Stax Singles By Barbara & The Browns Appeared In 1964
review_body:
Barbara And The Browns (Barbara, her sisters Betty and Roberta and brother Maurice Brown all from Memphis) are in some books as a One-Hit Wonder for their May 1964 # 97 Billboard Pop Hot 100 Big Party b/w You Belong To Her (Stax 150). It originally emerged as Wil Mo 101 but after it began attracting some considerable local interest it was leased by the much larger Stax. Unfortunately, not only were they running head on into the British Invasion in terms of the Pop charts, which had been shoving all but the best North American artists off the upper regions of those charts since The Beatles arrived in January, but Billboard had also suspended the R&B listings in late 1963, something that would last throughout all of 1964 and to the end of January 1965. And you just know that Big Party would have scored much higher on the R&B charts had they been in effect and, who knows, that publicity may have, in turn, helped the Hot 100 results.

In any event, neither of In My Heart b/w Please Be Honest With Me as Stax 158 later in 1964 - and the 45-rpm you see covered here - and I Don\x27t Want Trouble b/w My Lover as Stax 164 in 1965 went anywhere. They would go on to record at Cadet, Atco and the MGM Sound Of Memphis labels (without any further sides making any charts) and that aspect of their recording career is well covered in the 2007 CD \x5C\x22Can\x27t Find Happiness - The Sounds of Memphis Recordings\x5C\x22 from the Ace of London subsidiary Kent Records.

Finding those Stax sides in a quality CD setting is, however, currently impossible.

Barbara apparently quit recording after 1972 and passed away in her 70s on February 3, 2010.

product_title: Is There Anybody Out There? The Wall Live, 1980-81
review_headline: The Last True Performance Of All Four Band Members
review_body: As I was born in 1995 and have never had the chance to see Pink Floyd in concert, especially when they were in their prime with albums such as Dark Side of the Moon, Wish You Were Here, Animals, and The Wall, This album actually makes me feel like I\x27m at that show that took place in Earls Court back in 1980 and 1981. There were some versions of songs on this album that I liked better than the original studio version that came out in late 1979. A few examples are the live versions of In The Flesh, Mother, Another Brick in the Wall pt.II, Run Like Hell, and Comfortably Numb. This version of the wall also captures the last true performance of all four band members (Roger, David, Nick, and Rick) playing together, making it a sort of bittersweet to listen to as well. This album should be owned by anyone who loves Pink Floyd, it is not only a great live rock  album, but is probably one of the best Pink Floyd recordings out there. I highly recommend it.

review_headline: Bless my little 16 year old heart.

I was going through some older purchases on Amazon, and I found this one, right at the end of the year in 2006. I was going through a big pop punk revival during that period in my life. Listening to all the happening and pop-hoppining bands around. I had All Time Low, Panic! At the Disco, Mayday Parade, The Starting Line, The Maine, A Rocket to the Moon, etc. on my constant rotation. I\xE2\x80\x99m giggling a little at the thought of it all.

I bought this CD because Valencia was playing a show at the local downtown hangout spot where bands played (since closed down), it was either with Mayday Parade or All Time Low. I generally tried to get a handle on other artists that were playing with bands I saw since I felt like they deserved the love too.

Well, I was pretty much obsessed with this CD back in the day. Even now, 8 years later, I\xE2\x80\x99ll get a hankering for Valencia and I\xE2\x80\x99ll play it, purely for nostalgic reasons. Though it\xE2\x80\x99s been years since I\xE2\x80\x99ve ever seen them live, they must have had enough of a presence for me to continue to listen to their CD. I would have remembered it if they sucked live (I\xE2\x80\x99m looking at you, The Secret Handshake). At any rate, the songs are beautiful, catchy, and well-written. I think my most listened to tracks were The Space Between and Tenth Street.

And though this band may have never truly become \xE2\x80\x9Cthe next big thing\xE2\x80\x9D, I\xE2\x80\x99d rate this 5 stars because it\xE2\x80\x99s still a CD I enjoy listening to.

product_title: Luxury Liner
review_headline: One of the best in a career of bests
review_body:
One of the best albums in Emmylou\x27s considerable catalog, helped along in no small part by an incredible crew of musicians from James Burton, Rodney Crowell, Ricky Skaggs and Albert Lee to the background voices of Nicolette Larson and Dolly Parton. Her musical dream team is given a cherry picked batch of songs to jump in on that must have satisfied everyone in the studio. Two Gram Parsons cuts (the title song and the chestnut "She") remind us of Emmy\x27s enduring emotional and spiritual bond with the departed Country Rock icon. But wait, there\x27s more. We\x27ve got selections from A.P. Carter, The Louvin Brothers, Chuck Berry, Rodney Crowell and Townes Van Zant sitting comfortably side by side with Emmy\x27s own "Tulsa Queen"\xE2\x80\x94as good as anything on the record.

It\x27s a thoughtful mix that runs from the uptempo, hurtling power of the title song to the quiet, wistful "Making Believe." And as always, Emmylou\x27s voice seems the perfect vehicle no matter what she chooses to sing.

The band is tight and focused, the arrangements are memorable and clean, Emmylou\x27s voice is strong and clear and the whole thing works together seamlessly\xE2\x80\x94a very playable, listenable musical experience from one of Country Rock\x27s founding proponents \xE2\x80\x94 and one of it\x27s classiest, most enduring talents.

Red\x27s rise is pretty remarkable for a christian modern rock band, and their third outing should not disappoint the majority of fans. Though a lot more straightforward than both the previous two albums, Until We Have Faces gives fans the crunchy, flavorful alt rock that they expect out of Red, with even higher volume that before. There are a couple more ballads than before, and that can either be a positive or a negative depending of what kind of fan you are. Red still executes the album with good vocals and a high level of energy though, and that alone keeps the album from falling on its face. Boasting a generally hard sound (though not enough to be classified as hard rock or alt metal), Until We Have faces is an exciting listen.

I think this album vies for "top album" honors with End Of Silence. If you liked Pieces off of that record, this release is a good one. If not, its still a quality addition to Red\x27s resume.

product_title: All Things Must Pass
review_headline: A great milestone and accomplishment - that has not aged very well
review_body:
George Harrison, as a Beatle, always seemed to hold the promise of having great music within him, which couldn\x27t all come out within the confines of the Lennon/McCartney partnership. And that was probably best, since it was John and Paul who really led the band and whose music gave The Beatles their distinctive and incredible range of styles.
But after the band\x27s breakup, George finally had his chance to bust loose and make his own statement. The results were instantly recognized as a modern classic, a milestone in the post-Beatles era for each member as a solo musician. To this day, it is probably the greatest album any of The Beatles released as a solo act.
It did not hurt that having been a Beatle, George commanded a lot more attention than the typical singer-songwriter would have gathered in the early 70\x27s. Recalling that period, soon after I graduated from HS and was listening a lot to FM radio and buying albums, it seemed every month Rolling Stone magazine was proclaiming the latest, greatest new artist to hit the scene. Carole King, Joe Cocker, Leon Russell, Steve Miller, Maria Muldaur, Todd Rundgren, Bonnie Raitt, Eric Clapton, Van Morrison, Paul Simon, and of course the other ex-Beatles John Paul and Ringo, all were making distinctive music and stealing a significant chunk of the music market from the traditional rock band. George had a lot of competition, and for him to establish his own career, he needed to make a big entrance.
All Things Must Pass satisfied that requirement extremely well. It was several things all at once: it was a magnificent opus, a body of music by itself; it covered a wide stylistic range; and at the same time it bore the stamp of George Harrison\x27s personality through a consistent overall tone or texture inside the songs themselves.
Above, I state that ATMP has not aged very well. I put it on recently for the first time in over 10 years, and it took me several listenings to begin appreciating it again. Pop and rock music has undergone so many changes, nobody would ever record an album like this again. So you have to listen to it for the absolute, or timeless, quality of the music.
The album\x27s greatest asset is its range of styles which still mesh because of the hand that wrote them. Some songs are sweet and uplifting, some moody, some rocking. George infuses them all with a touch of melancholy and thoughtfulness, the dominant tone of All Things Must Pass. Much of it is beautifully recorded, especially the rich 12-string and mixed guitar strumming you hear in songs like I\x27d Have You Anytime, My Sweet Lord, and If Not For You, the steel guitar solos on Behind that Locked Door, and the horn sections in What Is Life and Beware of Darkness. Eric Clapton provides some beautiful accompaniment on the second version of Isn\x27t it A Pity, and he injects a lot of energy into the Art of Dying. George the songwriter was everything people hoped he could be. He expresses emotions deeply without excessive self-indulgence, which is the biggest problem with most writers in the 21st century. Hear Me Lord, at the end of the two "studio" LPs, is particularly effective to end the album, with an elegiac tone that emanates from a deep devotion to God, also unlike the unthinking surrender found in (some, not all) current Christian rock. George as a singer is often weak, but his years as a Beatle made him very precise, and he compensates with careful intonation and pitch. God Bless him for that alone!
But It has some negatives. There are a couple of throwaway songs like I Dig Love that could have just as easily been left out. (It seems George was determined to release a 3-LP set and so they were included.) I also do not care for the two jams you find at the end - almost musically worthless, just a chance for the guest stars like Clapton to strut with George at his side.
The worst thing to modern listeners will be the echoing sound in almost every song. Apparently this owes to producer Phil Spectre, who had produced some Motown music with a similar sound. Unfortunately, this lush effect goes too far, and songs like Wah-Wah, Let it Down, and Let it Roll sound like they were recorded in an ice rink. Sadly also, most music today is frantic and caters more to dance than listening, so ATMP will not appeal to that audience either.
For anyone who loves The Beatles or who wants a comprehensive collection of great early FM-oriented rock, All Things Must Pass is a must-have. But as the title says, for most others, its time has probably passed.

product_title: Essential Chick Bullock 1932-1941
review_headline: Decent sampling of a fine 1930s-era singer
review_body:
Whenever I hear others compare all male singers of the 1930s to either Al Bowlly or Bing Crosby I think to myself "thank goodness not everyone sang like them." I like Crosby and Bowlly just fine, but how *boring* and tiresome it would be if all the era\x27s singers had tried to sound like them. Crosby and Bowlly made enough records to keep today\x27s collectors chasing after them with little hope of ever finding them all. Fortunately for those of us with fairly wide tastes, there were plenty of others on the pop music scene, and Chick Bullock is one of my favorites of those "others." His distinctive, friendly voice is pleasant and "comfortable." It\x27s like pumpkin pie: it may not top many people\x27s list as a standout favorite, but few will go out of their way to disparage it either. (JJA\x27s obvious hatred notwithstanding!) Just because Bullock didn\x27t distort rhythms or melodies "far enough" from the composers\x27 intentions to satisfy certain jazz aficionados doesn\x27t mean he had no rhythmic sense or personality. Bullock may have sung more "straight" than Crosby, but whenever he does alter rhythms or notes, it\x27s always subtle and tasteful. No self-aggrandizing interjections here! Bullock steps into the spotlight when it\x27s his turn to sing, then steps out again to let the instrumentalists shine. And what instrumentalists he always seemed to have! Bunny Berigan, Benny Goodman, the Dorsey Brothers, Glenn Miller, and so many others.

The production values of this CD are top-notch: excellent transfers, a decent booklet, and helpful discographical information. Of course, with Bullock\x27s prolific career, boiling down a single "essential" CD is tough. Still, with so much good material out there to choose from, I\x27m left wondering why we needed so many alternative takes? I\x27ve got several hundred Bullock sides in my 78 collection, and to my ears, these are in no way the "essentials." (Where are the Vic Berton Vocalion sessions?) There are some mighty fine selections here, but I think a far better, more listenable compilation could have been assembled deserving of the "Essential" title. Still, for fans of 1930s-era pop and jazz, this is an excellent CD worth picking up.
