product_title: Exactly As We Are
review_headline: Exactly as They Were: Country Girls Reaching for the Big Time
review_body: This is the first of two albums that the band "Honey Pig" released. According to the band\x27s original website the band was started by Debi Derryberry, Laura Milby and Eliza Jane Schneider, and at first they played clubs and restaurants. This first album "Exactly as We Are", was released on August 28, 2001, although they seem to have started the band about 1999. Difficulties arose about 2002-2003, and as Eliza tells it "Honestly, I just want to belong. That\xE2\x80\x99s why I\xE2\x80\x99m always trying to sing backup and play fiddle in somebody else\xE2\x80\x99s band. Invariably, I end up taking focus and the lead singer gets mad at me.\xE2\x80\x9D --{San Diego Reader. October 16, 2013.} This also happened to be the time at which Eliza was also performing as many of the female voices for the television show "South Park", which also ended around this time.  Eliza was replaced by Melissa Sills, who was later replaced by Corrie Shenigo, after which they made a four song EP album called "Clueless You" released on August 31, 2004, before they eventually broke up.  Eliza however went on to do her Blue Girl musical appearances, and released a album called "Gypsy Grass", with her western bluegrass band called Eliza Jane & the Barnyard Gypsies.  The cover art of the album shows the original three girls in cut-off blue jeans, and wearing bras, while with their hands, they feed pigs. A second picture on the back of the lyric sheet has another image of them in the same clothes but this time leaning against a pig. Besides the lyrics for every song, there are credits for all the musicians that played on the album. Debi is the only one of the girls listed as playing an instrument on the album, other wise the girls are listed as \x27Vocals\x27. Debi wrote most of the songs on the album, while two were written by aura, and two by Eliza. There is a special Thanks page, and below the second picture, there are "Did you know" facts about each of the girls. It mentions Debi\x27s pregnancy while recording, Laura\x27s running a marathon, and Eliza\x27s traveling the USA in a ambulance to record dialects. The back cover of the album shows a parody of the front cover. Instead of them feeding the pigs, the back cover shows the girls, now fully clothed sitting at a dinning table after eating a big meal with many dishes, presumably the Honey Pig{s} from the front cover.  01, Cost of Love The first song is about a woman longing for her ex-lover, and sings about how much would it cost her to reunite. She then tells about how she now knows the Price/Cost of Love.  02, So My Man The next song is about woman who has fallen in love with a guy, and he leaves her, but she is still in love with him. She talks about the things he did for her, and during each chorus she says "You are so my man", meaning that he is perfect for her, even though they aren\x27t together. There is a 1950\x27s style rockabilly guitar solo, at the middle of the song.  03, Exactly as We Are Here is a song about a woman and her man, she sings about how happy they are, how long it took her to find such a man, and hopes that they will stay \x27Exactly as They Are" forever. This song is a slower ballad.  04, You Got Style In this song a woman is at a bar, and a guy is trying get her to go home with him, she says "You Got Style, but you can\x27t take me home tonight." It has a jazz piano, type quick tempo, with drums.  05, Beautiful Creature This is the first of two songs that Laura wrote for the album. The song begins by the singer comparing herself to a small fish, that needs time to grow before being caught. She then explains she has a broken heart and isn\x27t ready for love. Alternately she says she is a "Beautiful Creature" that is incomplete, and that the person trying to love her is a "Beautiful Creature" that just can\x27t compete with how she is feeling. The song has a harmonica, and guitar, in a melancholy type blues style song.  06, Mile a Minute Continuing the bluestype feeling, this next song is about a woman who wants to take time out, and stop working at a "Mile a Minute" type pace. She then gives credit to another un-named person for helping her slow down. There are a few hints in the song that it could mean that a child helped her slow down, as lyrics about a "house full-a-toys", "the need to split me in two", and "they all get so small". Might mean the baby that Debi was pregnant with while recording the song.  07, Backyard Train This is the first of two songs written by Eliza on the album. It is about a girl finishing her chores, and rushing out into the back yard to ride the train. The song\x27s lyrics are arranged in such a way that they could mean a toy train, or one that passes by behind her house. Because of the lines such as "The World goes by again, and again, and again" and others that say, "You\x27re giving your daddy a heart attack! If he knew what you do", if it was a model toy it probably wasn\x27t meant to be ridden on, or other wise he would already know about her riding it. She describes traveling through the yard, and the song ends with her getting ready to jump on the train. The song features a harmonica, violin, the pedal steel guitar, and tiny bit of what sounds like a mandolin, or banjo. While on the television show Beakman\x27s World, Season 2, Episode 06 {S2E06}, Eliza helped explain how trains work, with a model train for visual reference. In S2E09, after Beakmania, Liza sings a country and western style song about Oil and its by-products. {This track was later retitled "Runaway Train", and rerecorded for Eliza\x27s solo album, "Eliza Jane: Gypsy Grass", a Rythm & Blues, Soul, Blue grass, Country music album, with the word "backyard" replaced with "runaway".  08, Nose The song begins as a solo song, and after the first verse, the words are matched by the other girls. It is about a woman and a un-named person about to go to sleep, she describes the preparations for the night, and then she explains that she can\x27t get to sleep because her nose gets cold. She then describes various ways she wishes she could keep her nose warm. The opening of the song\x27s guitar riff sounds a bit like the Beatles "Here Comes the Sun", while the vocals are a bit more like those from the Bangles song "Eternal Flame".  09, If This is How it Feels This is the second of two songs that Laura wrote, this time as a co-writer with Larry Treadwell. The song describes the drifting apart of two people. How the guy has a "fragile shell around him", and can not let the girl in. It tells about how the \x27feeling\x27 they have of being together, something she needs, and he "can\x27t grasp a love so strong". The song ends with her drifting on, while he wishes he could have let her in. The lyrics mention "mystical energy", that "she crashes into her soul" while waiting for another love, and "not letting spirit guide them.\x27 The vocals seem to be a cross between Cher and Bonnie Taylor.  10, Credit Card Blues In this light hearted song, a woman describes how she was given a credit card, and she began charging lots of things to it. She then explains that "I like plastic money, honey, too", and at one point asks ""Where\x27s my Visa". The song starts out as a classical country and western style of banjo and violin, then later changes into a rockabilly theme slightly before the end.  11, Never Enough This song begins by describing a girl that doesn\x27t have enough to eat, and that in her world there is Never Enough food. They then describe how the world would be like if there was plenty for everyone. It then describes a boy who\x27s parents don\x27t have time to spend with him, and that there is Never Enough time. They then talk how they should raise a noise to help find "love for all the girls and boys".  12, Sugar & Spice A woman describes her lover as \x27Sugar and Spice\x27, and that she wants them to "Lay me down and love me tenderly." She tells how she is thinking of them, and can\x27t get too sleep. The words "Love Me Tender" are probably a reference to Elvis song, while the "Sugar and Spice and everything nice" is from a nursery rhyme which describes what girls are made of.  13, The King and Queen of Hollywood This is the second of two songs Eliza wrote for the album. In the song a woman in Hollywood is going about her daily life, when a religious man tries to get her involved with his religion. She then describes the strange scenery, and people around her. She also talks about a lingerie model being the Queen of Hollywood, with the King of Hollywood being the founder of that religious group.  The girls sing a three part melody on every song, however here and there a lead part will be solo for a verse or two. Although Eliza plays violin, she sadly does not play on the album, and most of the music is played by other people, with the girls providing the the songs and vocals only. The songs are professionally recorded with many country and western standard instruments, including the classic; guitars, Pedal Steel guitar, banjo, harmonica, violin {fiddle}, along with others such as the mandolin, viola, accordion, and Dobro. They give the album an almost symphonic feeling at times. Sadly despite the lyrics to the song Credit Card Blues, I don\x27t think they ever reached their goal of "I\x27m goin\x27 Platinum". If they would have released more albums and they were this quality, and had a hit single here or there, they may have gotten their wish, and become as famous as the Dixie Chicks. But the follow up EP loses that symphonic feel, and seems to have more of a feeling of all vocals and instruments being recorded in a single room, all at the same time.

product_title: The Spy Who Came In From the Cold (Original Soundtrack)
review_body:
Martin Ritt\x27s highly acclaimed film adaptation of John Le Carre\x27s cold war espionage best seller "The Spy Who Came in from the Cold" contains an extra bonus: an excellent score by one of the lesser known composers of the time, Sol Kaplan.
A bleak, realistic black and white depiction of the ruthless world of secret agents operating in Britain and East Germany at the height of the Cold War certainly debunked the popular James Bond world of glamor. sex and excitement. Ritt assembled a superb cast with Richard Burton, Claire Bloom and Oskar Werner topping the credits but the supporting cast of Sam Wanamaker, Peter Van Eyck, George Voskovec, Rupert Davies, Cyril Cusack, Michael Hordern and Bernard Lee was truly exceptional.
Sol Kaplan, a noted concert pianist, began film scoring in 1942, working on some forty films including "Niagara" and "Titanic, until falling victim to HUAC in 1953 and being blacklisted for most of the next decade. Hired by Ritt (another blacklist victim) for "Spy", he created a moody, melancholy score which works perfectly. To quote Jeff Bond in the excellent liner notes: "With his history as a concert pianist, he seemed eager to showcase the instrument and its capabilities in unusual ways ..... features a library of extended piano effects, created by striking, brushing or plucking the strings in various ways to create resonant, highly atmospheric sounds. These effects permeate the score, swamping the cues in mysterious, nocturnal textures and adding to the feeling of gloom and uncertainty." There are also variations of the main theme, usually performed on sax and even some pop-oriented pieces.
Although this is a sparse score, just 27 minutes in the film, the fine people at Intrada have included both the 1965 soundtrack album as well as the original film soundtrack on this CD release, totalling some 65 minutes of superb music. And after many listenings, I can say that I loved every moment ofthe music and heartily recommend this Sol Kaplan composition as a worthy addition to your film music library.

product_title: Celloverse
review_body: New songs and a DVD of videos; how lucky for the fan who likes to watch them play as well as listen to them!  Anytime the cello is used to play a strong melody line, you know the song is going to tug at your heartstrings.  It is especially true for their version of Street Spirit (Fade Out) and Shape of My Heart.  I liked the piano/cello balance in Live and Let Die better than their versions of Clocks from their previous album.  If you listen to songs like Mombasa and They Don\x27t Care About Us, you are left scratching your head at how the cello can make those sounds.  (See the video for Mombasa for help with that.) There is just enough classical music to remind you of their roots, and to demonstrate their skill at combining said music to classic rock-and-roll. Their original track Celloverse is a welcome addition to the album for those fans who have been wondering what Luka and Stjepan hear in their own heads. No one else has put out a CD that combines classical music, classic rock-and-roll, pop, film music, and rock alternative, so prepare yourself for an emotional ride.  Pick up the CD/DVD, see them live if you can, and encourage everyone you know to venture into the Celloverse with you!

review_body: I have had the pleasure of listening to Amy Robbins-Wilson\x27s Lullaby and Goodnight CD.  She has the voice of an angel, perfect for soothing babies and gently singing them to sleep. product_title: Schumann Edition
review_body: 3.5 stars    The Schumann cycle of Gerard Schwarz and the Seattle Symphony will appeal to those seeking a very lush, relaxed, romantic view of these works. These are arguably the fullest, most languid, plush versions you will find, big and grand. While tempos are mostly moderate, phrasing is the issue with this cycle. If your preference is for more chiseled, sharper edged or muscular Schumann, you will likely find Schwarz\x27 take to be quite soft. You can think of Schwarz\x27 Schumann as the polar opposite of David Zinman, whose Schumann is tight, fast, hard and sharp. The lushness is appealing on the slower movements, which are beautiful, such as gorgeously indulgent treatments of the largo of the First, the third movements of the Second, and the third movement of the Rhenish, which Schwarz does as a langorous adagio.     What I find frustrating is Schwarz\x27 use legato phrasing throughout these renditions. I have heard no other interpreter do this. The scherzo and fourth movement of the First and the finale of the Rhenish stand out for slidy, odd legato. The Fourth symphony, which should be dark and forceful, is mushy throughout. So this legago tendency, and the overall approach, are the main issues that determine whether you like this set or not. The recorded sound is a bit cavernous and distant, but acceptable.    Although not a standard-bearer among Schumann cycles, and not the place that I would recommend as a start to a Schumann collection, this set has a definite point of view (not to every taste) and interesting moments. When I adjusted my expectations (forget \x5C\x22correct\x5C\x22, and accept the legato and strange tempo choices), this set became oddly appealing to me.  It is more interesting than many faceless new Schumann cycles of recent years, and an upper middle-of-the-pack alternative.

product_title: big party / you belong to her 45 rpm single
review_headline: The Only Charting Side For Barbara & The Browns Appeared In 1964
review_body:
Barbara And The Browns (Barbara, her sisters Betty and Roberta and brother Maurice Brown all from Memphis) are in some books as a One-Hit Wonder for their May 1964 # 97 Billboard Pop Hot 100 Big Party b/w You Belong To Her (Stax 150). It originally emerged as Wil Mo 101 but after it began attracting some considerable local interest it was leased by the much larger Stax. Unfortunately, not only were they running head on into the British Invasion in terms of the Pop charts, which had been shoving all but the best North American artists off the upper regions of those charts since The Beatles arrived in January, but Billboard had also suspended the R&B listings in late 1963, something that would last throughout all of 1964 and to the end of January 1965. And you just know that Big Party - the 45-rpm covered here - would have scored much higher on the R&B charts had they been in effect and, who knows, that publicity may have, in turn, helped the Hot 100 results.

In any event, neither of In My Heart b/w Please Be Honest With Me as Stax 158 later in 1964, and I Don\x27t Want Trouble b/w My Lover as Stax 164 in 1965 went anywhere. They would go on to record at Cadet, Atco and the MGM Sound Of Memphis labels (without any further sides making any charts) and that aspect of their recording career is well covered in the 2007 CD \x5C\x22Can\x27t Find Happiness - The Sounds of Memphis Recordings\x5C\x22 from the Ace of London subsidiary Kent Records.

Finding those Stax sides in a quality CD setting is, however, currently impossible.

Barbara apparently quit recording after 1972 and passed away in her 70s on February 3, 2010.

review_headline: Second Of Two Decca LPs For Late 1950s/1960s Country Singer Margie Bowes
review_body:
Country singer Margie Bowes (born in Roxboro, North Carolina on March 18, 1941) is another whose music has largely been ignored since the advent of the CD in the early 1980s. By 1954 she was good enough at age 13 to be a frequent guest on local TV shows, including the popular Virginia Barn Dance out of Danville, as well as radio shows. At age 17 she won the nationwide talent contest sponsored by The Pet Milk Company which led to a recording deal with the Nashville-based Hickory Records, launched in 1954 by Acuff-Rose Music. Her first two releases in 1958 failed to crack the national Country charts, but both Wont\x27cha Come Back To Me? b/w One Broken Heart (Hickory 1084) and One Time Too Many b/w Violets And Cheap Perfume (Hickory 1087) did well enough on a regional basis to get her a shot on the prestigious Grand Ole Opry towards the end of 1958.

Then came her breakthrough hit, Poor Old Heartsick Me, which reached # 10 in March-April 1959 b/w Blue Dream as Hickory 1094, followed by the Aug-Sept 1959 # 15 My Love And Little Me b/w Sweet Night Of Love as Hickory 1102. It certainly appeared that she was on her way, but when the next three releases failed to chart in 1960 (Make A Wish b/w They Just Don\x27t Know You - Hickory 1112, Day After Day b/w Don\x27t Turn On The Light - Hickory 1124, and Are You Teasing Me? b/w Judge Not - Hickory 1135) she and the label parted company.

Her next stop was Mercury Records and things there got off to an encouraging start when Little Miss Belong To No One managed to reach # 21 in July-August 1961 b/w Bitter Sweet Kisses as Mercury 71845, but when that was followed by three straight failures (Lonely Pillow b/w Always Remember - Mercury 71897 in Oct 1961, Hammer And Nails b/w You\x27re Still A Part Of Things - Mercury 71971 in May 1962, and Think It Over b/w Within Your Crowd - Mercury 72090 in Feb 1963) Margie was again looking for a new recording deal.

That came later in 1963 with another giant of the industry, Decca, and as with Mercury it began reasonably well when Our Things peaked at # 33 in Jan 1964 b/w There\x27s Gotta Be A Way as Decca 31557, and the follow-up Understand Your Gal, an \x5C\x22answer\x5C\x22 song to the Johnny Cash hit Understand Your Man, topped out at # 26 in May-June b/w You Can Be Replaced as Decca 31606. But that would be it insofar as national hits were concerned as none of her next 9 Decca singles into 1969 could get her back on the charts, nor could two releases at Stop and Brite Star in 1970 do the trick (see the list in the Comments below).

Even so, Decca did give her two LPs, one in 1966 and the other in 1968, and the second was the one you see covered here titled \x5C\x22Today\x27s Country Sound\x5C\x22 (Decca DL-75023) containing: A1. product_title: Live at the Main Point 15th August 1973
review_body: I am from Philly. I grew up here. There is not a day that goes by that I don\x27t think of THE MAIN POINT. Those were the days, let me tell you. The Point was very small and very intimate. The number of performers that became successful as a result of THE MAINPOINT is in my opinion, WAY TO LONG to list. Performing there was a singer songwriter\x27s delight indeed. Then there was the WMMR, and Philadelphia factor. \x5C\x22MMR\x5C\x22 was instrumental in bringing forth and supporting these artists. WXPEN a local college station in Philly, should also be mentioned as a pivotal catalyst for many of these artists. Something about Philadelphia usually always inspired these acts to \x5C\x22Up Their Game\x5C\x22, even to this day. The Main Point practically became my second home. I Loved It There! So, onto the CD. This was a \x5C\x22classic\x5C\x22 radio broadcast. Wmmr was always trying to provide Philly with Live Broadcasts to increase awareness of the upcoming talent in the music industry. Jackson was no exception. His sidekick David Lindley was no slouch either. He could play the stuffing out of any instrument you put in front of him. He played like a Madman, a real treat to watch. Jackson\x27s songwriting along with Lindley\x27s musical talent is a huge reason to get this cd, if nothing else. I jumped on it as soon as I saw it. Keep in mind these are the \x5C\x22early days\x5C\x22. The east coast was pretty much just being introduced to Jackson. It was performances like this that made the first impressions for most of us. As far as I\x27m concerned, the sound quality is excellent! No complaints here. This cd really takes you into The Point, bringing forth a fine intimate performance from one of the greatest singer songwriters of our time. 5 STARS for this one! A must have if you are a fan. Don\x27t miss out, you will love it. Thanks for reading my review. ->(There is a fantastic 3 CD 1975 Main Point release out there also. Try Importcds website for both. Like I said, Don\x27t miss out!)

review_body:
I wept hearing this CD, especially "Xizi She Knows," because it\x27s just SO. FREAKIN\x27. GOOD, and it blows my mind that music this good is even allowed to exist. I\x27ve loved every one of Imogen\x27s albums (except I Megaphone, which I believe is her first, when she was quite young) and feel they\x27ve gotten progressively better, and this one ... wow. I can hardly imagine how anything could be even better than this, but I sure as hell am eager for all her future albums to see if and how she does it.

I LOVE that she included an instrumental version of all the tracks, as well she should, because the instrumental versions are just as magnificent in their way. Her voice is otherworldly beautiful, but so is just the instrumentation in this case. I feel like I\x27m seeing someone shoot through the stratosphere and escape Earth\x27s gravity. I give it all the stars.

product_title: Phaedra
review_body:
Why I didn\x27t buy this when it was a new album on the recently established Virgin label I don\x27t know.

(Virgin Records was formerly a mail order operation with only two retail outlets in the world, in London and Birmingham, but now a chain of shops had opened in every major city and they had a label of their very own)

A very good friend had a copy and shared my taste for \x5C\x22music without words\x5C\x22 - the terms New Age, Ambient and Electronica had yet to be invented so we just called it \x5C\x22music\x5C\x22 and got on with life. The seventies were a hive of invention in the music scene, and people didn\x27t freak out as easily as they sometimes do today when confronted with something not to their usual taste.

In the goodole daze, when you owned this you had one long track on side one and two shorter tracks and then a really short track on side two. Now, of course, \x5C\x22sides\x5C\x22 is an alien concept to most on the planet.

How to describe it? I\x27ve heard it called \x5C\x22head music\x5C\x22, \x5C\x22electronica\x5C\x22, \x5C\x22ambient\x5C\x22 and \x5C\x22New Age\x5C\x22, all of which are as good as anything else and as inadequate as some here would declare those terms to be. The music varies, sometimes being like a fog over a river of sound textures inside which themes can sometimes be heard as they bob to the surface, sometimes being more structured. Some will delight in this. Some will find it tedious and won\x27t give the music the time to show itself to them. Their loss.

There isn\x27t really a comparison I can give. Tangerine Dream were forging a new path here, and though there are probably many imitators this is a type of music I don\x27t collect. I bought Phaedra because I\x27d always intended to, one day. It just took longer than I expected. I wish I\x27d grabbed it 40 years ago. All that pleasure missed.

But with digital downloads instant gratification is possible, and the price is right for you to find out firsthand whether this stuff is for you.

And think what you like, with a back catalog the size of theirs, Tangerine Dream *must* have had something going on, no?catalog the size of theirs, Tangerine Dream *must* have had something going on, no?

product_title: Paul Kelly presents - The Merri Soul Sessions
review_headline: Merri Soul is Soulful with Magnificent Voices!
review_body:
I have to admit that I was unfamiliar with Paul Kelly\x27s body of work and that the draw for me was being very familiar with the music of Clairy Browne and The Bangin\x27 Rackettes as well as Kira Puru. That said, I was more than pleasantly surprised with the quality of the other singers that Mr. Kelly brought together for this album. They all have powerful voices and really make Kelly\x27s songs their own!

The standout tracks are Clairy Browne\x27s "Keep On Coming Back for More", Linda Bull\x27s "Smells Like Rain", Kira Puru\x27s "I Don\x27t Know What I\x27d Do", and Paul Kelly and the Bull\x27s "Hasn\x27t it Rained". The funny thing is is that Kelly must like rain as four songs have "rain" in the lyrics and two songs feature "rain" in their titles.

The bottom line... the whole album is great and not a clunker in the list!

product_title: Lindsey Stirling
review_headline: No reason not to add this to your collection
review_body:
I am not sure what I could say about this CD that you don\x27t already know. If you know Stirling\x27s name and have come to Amazon to buy the CD, chances are you\x27ve already made up your mind and aren\x27t looking at the reviews.

Her music isn\x27t revolutionary, but it is charming and easy to listen to. It isn\x27t slow, and has that dubstep/techno lightly strung into the music enough that it makes the song catchy, without overpowering the sounds of her violin. It\x27s not really an easy genre to find a great quality of: mostly when you look for this type of music, it\x27s an MP3 of violin or other strings music that is in no way prepared to have their music bred with dubstep/techno, and someone adds it to the music anyway. They can sound good, but generally aren\x27t.

Lindsey composing her music with the intention of adding the extra noise is what makes the music palatable. If you like strings music, but don\x27t need it to be slow and melancholy, YouTube her music and then buy this CD.

review_body: If you are a fan of the Robert Rodriguez\x27s \x5C\x22Mariachi\x5C\x22 Trilogy films than you will love this disc. It is not just for fans of \x5C\x22Mariachi\x5C\x22 the film but for anyone that loves genre bending Spanish guitar or just cool Spanish music. Most of the guitar work is original and electrifying with a frenetic pace. It is cutting edge flamenco inspired if anything, but not Mariachi music. This is not, let me say it again, this is not Mariachi music by any means. I have a library full of music that is Mariachi and believe me this is not Mariachi de Tecalitlan [[ASIN:B004N09KCC El Mejor Mariachi Del Mundo]] or anything like it. The song by Chingon, love the name which also happens to be the name of my favorite breakfast sandwich up the coast in Carlsbad at Mas Fina Cantina, \x5C\x22 Malaguena Salerosa\x5C\x22 is a case in point. It is a hot number reinterpreted on an old Spanish theme. All the music is amazing, conjuring images of Rodriguez\x27s film and old Mexico. As the title says it is music from the movie and inspired from Rodriquez\x27s trilogy, El Mariachi, who was a character, the main protagonist.  The DVD is also very good and informative but unfortunately ii is much too short. I really did like the DVD but I would have just liked more behind the scenes and more footage of the concerts. All in all it is a disc worth adding to your library, just don\x27t file it under Mariachi music, unless you have a sub category for film than it would be El Mariachi. Did I say this is not Mariachi music? This is a highly entertaining CD/DVD combo and worth having, como se dice en Mexico, vale la pena.

review_headline: First Of Two Decca LPs For Late 1950s/1960s Country Singer Margie Bowes
review_body:
Country singer Margie Bowes (born in Roxboro, North Carolina on March 18, 1941) is another whose music has largely been ignored since the advent of the CD in the early 1980s. By 1954 she was good enough at age 13 to be a frequent guest on local TV shows, including the popular Virginia Barn Dance out of Danville, as well as radio shows. At age 17 she won the nationwide talent contest sponsored by The Pet Milk Company which led to a recording deal with the Nashville-based Hickory Records, launched in 1954 by Acuff-Rose Music. Her first two releases in 1958 failed to crack the national Country charts, but both Wont\x27cha Come Back To Me? b/w One Broken Heart (Hickory 1084) and One Time Too Many b/w Violets And Cheap Perfume (Hickory 1087) did well enough on a regional basis to get her a shot on the prestigious Grand Ole Opry towards the end of 1958.

Then came her breakthrough hit, Poor Old Heartsick Me, which reached # 10 in March-April 1959 b/w Blue Dream as Hickory 1094, followed by the Aug-Sept 1959 # 15 My Love And Little Me b/w Sweet Night Of Love as Hickory 1102. It certainly appeared that she was on her way, but when the next three releases failed to chart in 1960 (Make A Wish b/w They Just Don\x27t Know You - Hickory 1112, Day After Day b/w Don\x27t Turn On The Light - Hickory 1124, and Are You Teasing Me? b/w Judge Not - Hickory 1135) she and the label parted company.

Her next stop was Mercury Records and things there got off to an encouraging start when Little Miss Belong To No One managed to reach # 21 in July-August 1961 b/w Bitter Sweet Kisses as Mercury 71845, but when that was followed by three straight failures (Lonely Pillow b/w Always Remember - Mercury 71897 in Oct 1961, Hammer And Nails b/w You\x27re Still A Part Of Things - Mercury 71971 in May 1962, and Think It Over b/w Within Your Crowd - Mercury 72090 in Feb 1963) Margie was again looking for a new recording deal.

That came later in 1963 with another giant of the industry, Decca, and as with Mercury it began reasonably well when Our Things peaked at # 33 in Jan 1964 b/w There\x27s Gotta Be A Way as Decca 31557, and the follow-up Understand Your Gal, an \x5C\x22answer\x5C\x22 song to the Johnny Cash hit Understand Your Man, topped out at # 26 in May-June b/w You Can Be Replaced as Decca 31606. But that would be it insofar as national hits were concerned as none of her next 9 Decca singles into 1969 could get her back on the charts, nor could two releases at Stop and Brite Star in 1970 do the trick (see the list in the Comments below).

Even so, Decca did give her two LPs, one in 1966 and the other in 1968, and the first was the one you see covered here titled \x5C\x22Margie Bowes Sings\x5C\x22 (Decca DL-74818) containing: A1. Big City (2:03); A2. Get Your Lie The Way You Want It (2:26); A3. Making Believe (2:44); A4. It\x27s Enough To Make A Woman Lose Her Mind (2:55); A5. Over Night (2:19); A6. Look Into My Teardrops (2:16); B1. Understand Your Gal (2:36); B2. That Completely Destroys My Plans (2:39); B3. Look Who\x27s Lonely (2:14); B4. There Goes My Everything (2:42); B5. Our Things (2:25); B6. I\x27m Living In Two Worlds (3:06). The contents of the second are also shown in the Comments. In this same period she also appeared in the 1966 film The Gold Guitar.

In terms of CD coverage, you\x27ll find Poor Old Heartsick Me, Violets And Cheap Perfume, Are You Teasing Me? and Wont\x27cha Come Back To Me? in the B.A.C.M. release Country Music Ladies Of The 1950\x27s. product_title: No Prayer For The Dying [Enhanced]
review_body:
When I bought this album and re-listened to it for the first time in five years, I asked myself was, "Does it deserve it\x27s reputation as a complete flop?"

Yes and no. It\x27s not bad enough to get smashed with a hammer or used as a coaster. But it\x27s not a good album, and it\x27s still one of their worst.

One of the goals of No Prayer was to return to a stripped down sound after the proggy Seventh Son. Bruce Dickinson adopted a harsh, scratchy singing style. If the band was going for the Di\x27Anno era, this totally didn\x27t work, because No Prayer sounds nothing like that. It doesn\x27t sound like the classic era either. It sounds like stuff thrown together without cohesion.

The opener, "Tailgunner" is a B-grade "Aces High." "Holy Smoke" is one of the only Iron Maiden songs with profanity, and it\x27s an enjoyable tongue-in-cheek number.

Enter the three "No Prayer" songs, tracks 3-5, which have similar composition, lead styles, and lyrical themes. These songs are unique to this album, and I\x27m indifferent toward them.

In high school, I had a dream where "The Assassin" played on repeat for about an hour while some assassiny guy creeped around my house. Since then, I\x27ve kept my distance from this track. "Run Silent, Run Deep" and "Hooks in You" are two of the worst Iron Maiden songs ever.

Then, there\x27s "Bring Your Daughter...To the Slaughter." It\x27s a Dickinson solo production remade for this album. It\x27s about humanity\x27s obsession with female virginity and Freddy Krueger. "Mother Russia" is the epic finale, except it\x27s short, and thus, not very epic. No Prayer is the only Iron Maiden album without a song exceeding six minutes.

Some good songs, some okay ones, and some bad ones making an okay album.

**Unlike the other remastered Iron Maiden discography, finding No Prayer with a slipcase is difficult. The album still comeswith a greatly expanded booklet and case art. The cover picture was edited to remove the guy that Eddie is strangling, because Derek Riggs didn\x27t like it. The disc picture still has it though.

product_title: Strauss: Eine Alpensinfonie (An Alpine Symphony), Op. 64
review_headline: A Public Announcement from the Australian Kna Association
review_body:
Look, I don\x27t care how bravely he fought at Khe Sanh or those missions into Cambodia, the fact remains that Colonel Harland Sanders was a genocidist and his legacy endures in the evil empire that is KFC. Last week, it announced the release of its latest atrocity - the Double Down Dog (a hot dog wrapped in a cheese-stuffed, deep-fried chicken breast). The \x5C\x22dog\x5C\x22 follows the infamous Double Down Burger (bacon and cheese between two deep-fried chicken fillets) which cut a swathe through Australia in 2011. Worse still, KFC has been using the Philippines as a dumping-ground for these monstrosities to the delight of the locals. Have care for judgement.

Reader, this 1980 recording of the Alpine Symphony is this most synthetic, glare-ridden compact disc ever made by Deutsche Grammophon - and that\x27s saying something. While the performance itself is a world-beater, it\x27s amazing that it was ever released. Trust me: it\x27s safer to eat a raw Double Down Dog after a quadruple bypass than listen to this horror. The 20-bit Gold remaster worked wonders on this early-digital monster ([[ASIN:B000001GK2 Eine Alpensinfonie (An Alpine Symphony)]]) - and the latest remaster is an improvement still ([[ASIN:B00JEPZVYM Strauss: The Analogue Recordings Deluxe Edition]]).

Come the New Year, Gwyneth Paltrow is determined to evict \x5C\x22marriage regrets, heavy metals, fire retardants, pesticides, Double Down Dogs and old copies of the Alpine Symphony\x5C\x22 from her life. Even as you laugh at her, heed the example. You are mortal. As things stand, there\x27s already enough malfeasance in the world. Add not to it!

product_title: Richter: Complete Decca, Philips & DG Recordings
review_headline: RICHTER DISCOGRAPHY FOR WESTERN RECORD COMPANIES updated October, 2017
review_body:
After a false start due to World War II, Sviatoslav Richter\x27s public career lasted fifty years - until his final concert in 1995.
The first fifteen were spent behind the Iron Curtain - It wasn\x27t until 1960 that he was allowed to visit the West.
Once the dam had broken, Western companies rushed in to record Richter.

-- Deutsche Grammophon was first: They actually jumped the gun by sending DG engineers to Prague in 1956 and Warsaw in 1958.
-- In 1960, RCA and Columbia documented Richter\x27s first North American tour:
Thirteen CDs recorded over a ten week period. The most thorough documentation we have of Sviatoslav Richter in his absolute prime (seven recitals were recorded in their entirety).
For the bizarre story of that tour, see my review of [[ASIN:B00NFLVFFK Complete Album Collection]]
-- In 1961, Richter visited London - Philips recorded him in the Liszt Concertos, and EMI recorded him at their Abbey Road Studios.
-- Decca waited until 1970, though later on they issued some 1960\x27s recordings from Benjamin Britten\x27s Aldeburgh Festival.
-- Between 1970 and 1983, the small German company Eurodisc (Ariola) recorded twelve studio LPs.
-- Teldec made a few very late recordings with Richter in 1993-1994 (he retired in 1995). Bach, Mozart and Schumann - all new to his recorded repertoire.

All of Sviatoslav Richter\x27s recordings for Decca, Philips, Deutsche Grammophon, EMI/HMV, Teldec, Eurodisc, RCA and Columbia have been released in five inexpensive mega-boxes:
--- DECCA = [[ASIN:B00N9MWVVW Richter: Complete Decca, Philips & DG Recordings]] 51 CDs
--- WARNER = [[ASIN:B01JDODEEW Complete HMV & Teldec Recordings (24CD)]]
--- EURODISC = [[ASIN:B01AVPVT58 Eurodisc Recordings]] 14 CDs
--- SONY = [[ASIN:B00NFLVFFK Complete Album Collection]] on RCA & Columbia 18 CDs
Then Sony complicated matters by issuing a 13 CD box of only Richter\x27s 1960 Carnegie Hall recordings.
11 of the 13 CDs are identical to CDs in Sony\xE2\x80\x99s "Complete Album Collection" box (marked with an asterisk in the discography)

product_title: Son Of The Morning
review_body:
Call this a 3.5, but I\x27ll give them the benefit of the doubt because I was really surprised and impressed when I first heard this album. It doesn\x27t measure up to the follow up, Children of Fire, but the album is still quite good in its own right. Oh Sleeper boasts a very aggressive sound, with lots of energy. Kind of a raw band, they really bring it with the kind of effort you can appreciate from your favorite sports teams. Lead harsh vocalist Micah Kinard is particularly aggressive, and his screeches will excite and chill you.

The album is a bit of a concept album where it portrays the war between God and Satan, and almost like a rap record, Oh Sleeper writes some hard hitting lines for God. Its really impressive for a metal album. If you dig Christian (or any) metalcore, pick this up.

product_title: Children Of Fire
review_body:
I\x27m was not much of an Oh, Sleeper fan, until now. Their previous albums were really derivative of the better metalcore bands that came before them, and I often felt a little bored as the tracks rolled by. This album is much better though, and the band does a really good job as they once again recreate what good metalcore sounds like.

Children Of Fire is without a doubt darker than the previous release, and a little bit heavier too in sound. The harsh-clean vocals dynamic is still there, but the harsh vocals aren\x27t quite as sloppy as they were with Son of The Morning. Standout tracks include Means to Believe, The Family Ruin, and Hush Yael, all featuring nice clean vocals, and satisfactory aggression in the instrumentals.

Oh Sleeper isn\x27t near the top of my list for metal bands, but this album is among the best so far I have heard this year. Give it a go.

review_headline: Powerful performance of a classic score
review_body: This is a powerful performance of this classic score. Yes, the movie soundtrack is amazing and we all grew up on it. It remains definitive but Tilson-Thomas wrings out so much beauty and lyricism in so many parts of the score that it surpasses the soundtrack in many places (\x5C\x22One hand, One Heart\x5C\x22 is breathtakingly beautiful here - I mean it - it literally took my breath away for a moment). There are a few moments when the vocalists don\x27t match up to the originals (\x5C\x22Something\x27s Coming\x5C\x22 is far better on the soundtrack), but this is not to be missed, no matter how much you may think you don\x27t think you need to hear WSS again.

review_headline: Absolutely at the top of the list thanks to Pentatone\x27s engineering
review_body:
Given all the enthusiastic reviews of this remastering, I\x27ll just echo the praise. The Davis/Concertgebouw recording was a success in its original Philips issue, but this Pentatone version, made from experimental quadraphonic masters, takes it several notches higher. Now the listener can experience the feeling of being in a good seat midway back at the Concertgebouw and hearing all the range and color of this astonishing score.
It\x27s all here: a legendary orchestra, at home in an acoustically attractive setting, playing a romantic masterpiece under the direction of an authoritative conductor. While everything came together in Amsterdam in 1974, this impeccable re-release reveals even more detail and atmosphere. Fire up the Blu-Ray player and see for yourself.

product_title: J. S. Bach: Toccata & Fugue in D minor, BWV 565 / Passacaglia in C minor, BWV 582 / Fugue in G minor, BWV 578 / Concerto in A minor, BWV 593 / Fantaisie & Fugue in G minor, BWV 542
review_body: I received this as a gift. This CD has low volume and needs to be played at full volume. "The" Toccata BWV 565 is good. The mysterious hall has great reverberation. The country in which the hall is located is not given. The stereo effect is good. The rest of the CD is not good, and the Passacaglia is very bad: there is no deep bass. ERATO\x27s address is not given. The origin and name of the recording company is also not given, although the sound engineer is listed as Yolanta Skura; never heard of her. The notes are skimpy and thereby emphasize the lack of care given to the production of this CD. The lousy performance of the Passacaglia may be due to Marie-Claire Alain\x27s possible perverse francophilism that leads her to make Bach\x27s non-French music uninteresting. If you buy this CD, you will need to buy another to get a proper performance of the Passacaglia; so, why waste your money?

review_body: I just could not let a 1 star review be the only review there was for this great piece of music. It is a variation on a theme but the variations are what make this piece so amazing. The whole thing clocks in at just over an hour and what an awesome hour it is. Slow building brass with drone and bells thrown in as a bonus. The droning bass is my favorite thing about this masterpiece and the digital noise is mesmerizing. It slows down almost unnoticeably and the last track takes 20 minutes to wind down. This and Miners Hymns are my favorite works by Johann and I know I will be a fan my whole life long. A++

product_title: Gibson USA LPNSTDEBCH1 Les Paul Standard 2016 T Electric Guitar,
review_headline: VERY POOR QUALITY...BUT, A GREAT GUITAR IF YOU CAN FIND ONE W/QUALITY CRAFTSMANSHIP.
review_body:
I just dropped this off at UPS this morning & I debated whether I should actually do it or not. This was advertised as a 2012 but, wound up being a 2013. I initiated a return but, started to really like it despite the year difference. I planned to keep it in spite of this. This particular guitar has VISIBLE & blatant blemishes in finish. Gibson quality is severely lacking. At least on this one! Spots on the headstock like blotches & minor scratching. This is probably why it wound up on Amazon. Again, I was willing to overlook these. I give it 5 stars for playability & comfort and a 0 for quality. The nut was cut ridiculously low. Another quality issue. How does Gibson, using the Plek, come up with a nut like this? After repeated efforts with a tech who personally owns 30 LP\x27s, we could not get this guitar to play well. I\x27m talking about a dozen trips to the tech in 40 days. And I was not paying to replace a nut on a brand new Les Paul even though they are notorious for this. The G string constantly dropped out of tune. Either after a few minutes of light strumming or ANY kind of bend. A string always sounding out at various points on the fingerboard when playing power chords yet, the neck was perfect. Action was perfect. Maybe bad tuners? For the life of me & my tech, we couldn\x27t get it right.

I will continue looking for a new one. These instruments, if you can find one that reflects quality in craftsmanship, is hard to pass up. This one was simply a dud. I am just a hobbyist who was sick of the foreign made junk. I wanted a quality instrument that put those to shame. My Floyd rose equipped Indian made Jackson holds tune better than this guitar did. I\x27m not a basher, just a normal person looking for high quality guitar after years of just getting by with whatever. For the price tag, it\x27s not even close. Not when a $500 Jackson plays & sounds better.

The one thing it does have going for it is the software included that you can use by itself on your computer or inside of a DAW. Unfortunately even that software isn\x27t the best. It\x27s somewhat CPU intensive which wouldn\x27t be a problem if it didn\x27t crash so often (and not because of it being too CPU intensive). product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-M50x Closed-Back Professional Studio Monitor Headphones
review_headline: Want an honest review from an everyday consumer? Look here.
review_body:
Have you ever been told that you have big ears? Do you feel your ears are larger than normal? If that is the case, DO NOT BUY THESE HEADPHONES. I bought these headphones because reviews had said "Ohhhh don\x27t worry! Once you break them in they are AMAZING!"..well...after 2 weeks of wearing them about 6 hours a day (not in succession) my ears hurt and I feel that if I were to have broken them in I would have done so by now. If you have "normal" sized ears this may not be a big concern for you.

To be completely honest with you, I feel these headphones are not worth the price tag. Are they worth the price tag compared to other headphones? Possibly. Are they worth the price tag compared to Apple Ear Pods? Absolutely not. First off, I was listening to music imported from Vinyl and CDs so the whole "You probably were listening to YouTube ripped music" can be thrown right out the window. The sound quality is 6.5-7.0/10.0. I did not feel the WOW factor that I expected dropping $160 on headphones. Other reviewers REALLY sugar coated the bass being "good"; I would say the bass is atrocious. I listen to all types of music: from Mozart, Kanye West, to Taylor Swift, and everything in between. If you listen to multiple types of music (this includes/emphasized modern day Hip Hop, pop music, EDM etc.), the bass will leave you severely disappointed...to be honest...the Apple Ear Pods probably have better bass quality. Do you listen to music where bass isn\x27t a concern? Then these headphones may be for you.

Something that most reviews haven\x27t touched on, these headphones are not too bad for PC gaming. I would not recommend these for FPS, but playing games like Witcher 2 and Far Cry 4 they are surprisingly good.

If you have made it this far in the review, I would give this headset 3.5 stars. The sound quality is good, not great. The bass sucks. If you do not have large ears AND you do not want to drop $300 on a pair of headphones but at the same time you want slightly better quality than $100 Beats in-ear headphones, these are for you.dphones but at the same time you want slightly better quality than $100 Beats in-ear headphones, these are for you.

review_body: Good practice/small studio amp.  This allows you to amplify electric guitars, basses and acoustic/electric guitars.  It\x27s versatile has a built-in tuner. If the outlet has the ground and power swapped or if it is used with an extension chord which is incorrectly wired the amp suffers from a horrendous AC hum. There\x27s a lot to love about this, but the first thing you have to do is consider the price.

Mixing four tracks on-site is very nice, and having analog controls to change on the fly is a joy to use. Being able to use "real" microphones is wonderful. The ability to manipulate and control sources is almost unheard of at this price. And, adding features like the ability to mark record points (and have Premiere understand them) is jaw-dropping.

On the other hand, this isn\x27t really built.as a take-along accessory. It\x27s not built to last long if it gets moved often, and it\x27s too heavy to carry along independently. The learning curve is also probably pretty steep for people who aren\x27t familiar with mixing or audio engineering. Chances are, you\x27re not going to want this to capture your kid\x27s third birthday.Of course, if you want to learn, this could be an incredible tool.

product_title: Smart SI-922 Irish Whistle Black Key of D Tin Whistle Penny Whistle ABS
review_headline: Quite good, but the Susato is better, and by enough to justify its higher price
review_body: I\x27m a professional musician, and teach whistle.  My preferred high D pennywhistle is the Susato Kildare S series.  I purchased a Smart whistle to compare, and see if it is a viable substitute for the $50 Susato.    Almost.  The Smart whistle arrived with the name \x5C\x22Woodi\x5C\x22 on the head.  It appears that Woodi is another brand name for the same whistle. The Smart / Woodi\x27s appearance is nearly identical to the Susato, but with a matt black finish compared to the Susato\x27s gloss.  There are also some subtle differences in the shape of the windway.  The heads are not quite interchangeable - the Smart / Woodi will fit loosely on the Susato body, so not vice versa.    The Smart / Woodi is tunable and has excellent intonation, including an in tune cross-fingered C.  The volume and tone are solid.  Those features make it better than any comparably priced pennywhistle out there.  The tone and volume are a tad thinner than the Susato, which is not necessarily a negative - D pennywhistles can be overpowering, and the Susato is powerful.  Some might prefer the slightly thinner sound of the Smart / Woodi; I prefer the fuller sound of the Susato.  The Susato also comes with a thumb rest, which is not necessary for such a small instrument, but is nice.    But the Smart / Woodi (at least the one I purchased) has some quirks.  The cross-fingered C is quieter than surrounding notes, and doesn\x27t speak as readily.  There\x27s also some wonkiness in response of the upper register.  In particular, I can get a good high A and high B, but if I do a cut ornament on the high A (which involves both the high A and B in quick succession), the Smart / Woodi usually whiffs.  The Susato has none of these quirks.  Granted, if you were to play the Smart / Woodi for a while you\x27d likely learn to compensate; but a fine instrument doesn\x27t require such compromises.    So I\x27d definitely take this Smart / Woodi over any comparably priced pennywhistle, including the standard metal ones like the Clark, Generation, Feadog, etc.  But I wouldn\x27t take it over the Susato.  The $50 Susato plays as well or better than every more expensive custom whistle I\x27ve tried.  Can\x27t say the same about the Smart / Woodi.

product_title: Epiphone Dot Archtop Electric Guitar
review_body: Just picked one of these up from Guitar Center.  I used to be hesitant about buying the display model, but this guitar was a game changer.    At my local GC, a capable member of the staff will give it a decent setup, and make sure it\x27s in good working order as long as its on the floor.  This one was absolutely bang on from the minute I picked it up.    Once I get a new guitar home, I immediately start running in through the ringer, and I start making some OCD tweaks to accommodate my particular playing style.  Aside from putting some 11\x27s on it, and making minor bridge adjustments to accommodate the thicker strings... It was \x5C\x22there\x5C\x22:)    I am most shocked/amazed at the intonation all the way up and down the neck.  I\x27ve had a Gold-Top Gibson LP, two MIM Fender Teles, a USA built Breedlove acoustic, a Canadian built Godin A6, etc... And this Chinese-made EPIPHONE ranks near the top (with the $1500 Breedlove) when it comes to intonation.  Mind. Blown.    Even more stunning in person... Sure some guitar snob MIGHT point out a tiny little overspray inside the F-hole on mine (out of plain view)... But in order to keep the cost low for us, they have to churn these things out quick.... So it may not be as tidy as its Gibson counterpart, but I guarantee I won\x27t lose any sleep once I put my first scratch on it (which I\x27ve done after putting dings on my Gibsons).    Fantastic guitar.  Play one before you buy it. Worth every penny.

review_body: This is a great little banjolin, has a good tone, looks great and fun to play. Don\x27t let the pictures fool you, it\x27s quite small compared to a A-model mandolin, but it\x27s heavy for being smallish. There are a couple of things to do before being able to play it, first you need to tighten the drum on the banjo head with the included wrench, and set your bridge in the correct position, then tune your strings up, which will take a couple of times to even them out. Also if you\x27re like me, I wondered if it had a cover one the back or if it was just a open back banjolin,  and yes it does and you can remove the cover if you wish it has six Philips head screw. It is a very well made instrument, and I plan to buy another one for my Daughter in the future, I hope you find this review helpful, because all the other comments about this mostly nitpicking the small stuff and not really telling you about it.

product_title: Julio S. Sagreras Guitar Lessons Audio CD -Raymond Lohengrin
review_headline: The best of two worlds: a great teaching resource and a great listening experience!
review_body: There are so few quality recordings of  progressive guitar studies in general and this is the only one I know with music from Julio Sagreras. These recordings of the studies are a valuable teaching resource for several reasons: they are skillfully played with close attention to the intention of the composer so the student can hear what the sheet music indicates (get the Sagreras books if you can, they are magnificent!); Lohengrin\x27s playing is very artistic and brings out the melodic quality of each piece so the student can learn to value what it means to play even the simplest compositions with care; each study uses techniques that are the proper foundation for playing classical guitar and the student can hear the effect of those techniques properly played. But that is just one side of the recording. In addition to the Sagreras studies, the CD also has music by Scarlatti, Brouwer, Carcassi, Sanz, Lauro and Eduardo Martin-- the most important Cuban composer for the guitar since Leo Brouwer. The more advanced works are extremely well played, with the same fluidity and attention to musicality as the simpler study pieces. It is rare to get a CD with this kind of quality and quantity of music. The mix of traditional and contemporary music gives a good representation of the compositional range available for students of the classical guitar. If you are a guitarist this is a valuable CD to add to your collection. If you enjoy listening to the classical guitar you will enjoy the full program. This CD gives you a great listening experience from a world class musician.

product_title: Doppler Labs Dubs Acoustic Filters Advanced Tech Earplugs
review_headline: Compared to Etymotics-- Comfortable, cool-looking, good sound earplugs with perhaps false sense of hearing safety
review_body:
I\x27ve worn DUBS competitor, Etymotic high fidelity standard and custom-made earplugs at music events for over 25 years. Here are some difference between DUBS and Etymotic.

Etymotic has two standard sizes of -20 decibel earplugs--this is important because the larger (white color) size can irritate if inserted into a smaller ear canal. When I looked at DUBS still larger earbuds, I thought, no way this would work. But, its earpiece plastic is very cushiony, and actually is more comfortable than the Etymotic larger or smaller (blue) earplugs.

DUBS sounds better than Etymotics, but I\x27m uncertain as to whether this is because Etymotic is -20 and DUBS is -12 decibels. DUBS sounds are clearly crispier and boomier. If you\x27re a music aficionado, DUBS does sound better for popular music.

My custom Etymotics (unfortunately, $300), can reduce -9, -15, and -25db. I have hypersensitive hearing, and believe that -25 is appropriate with loud music. Notice that earbuds only protect the ear channel, the sounds, particularly bass, come in from head bones as well. So, DUBS -12 is less protection than it might seem. Wearing these DUBS is, obviously, better than wearing nothing, but at -12 db, I question whether DUBS might create a false sense of safety. Etymotics -20 is safer.

Carrying case: Etymotic\x27s ER20 case is better. If one\x27s hands are dirty or unsanitary, DUBS case make the earplugs difficult to remove in a sanitary way. And DUBS case is loose--inappropriate for active individuals. But it\x27s easy to find replacement cases to carry these.

As compared to Etymotics:

Comfort 5 star
Sound accuracy 5 star
Aesthetics while wearing 5 star
Hearing protection 2 star (however, some people may be perfectly happy with Dubs -12db.)
Case 2 star.
Occlusion effect (one\x27s own voice (e.g.) sounds more bassy and louder) 3 star.

Overall, a 4 star.

product_title: Zoom G1on Guitar Effects Pedal
review_body:
This may be the most important piece of equipment you will buy if you are a beginner in terms of learning leads or just learning how to layer multiple guitars into a single song. There are certainly better boxes out there but not at this price point. The looper alone makes it worth the cost, especially since it allows you to layer on drums, basic guitar part and then leads or harmonies. Or all of the above. The only real shortcoming is the 30-second limit on the looper. But that\x27s more than enough room to lay down a chord progression against which you can practice your leads.
The bonus is the excellent selection of effects that can be shaped almost endlessly if you want to bother. The very well designed control knobs and LCD scream make it very easy to do whatever you want. Some of the more than 100 effects are pure crap but who cares. Many others are quite good and you are sure to find a big bunch of them to like. And it that\x27s not enough, there a tuner that works surprisingly well.
In my opinion, this box is far superior to the more expensive entry level Digitech effects box (which I also have and have used for years). The sounds on the Zoom are cleaner and there are a lot more of them (100 vs 50). And a its a heck of a lot easier to program and change settings. Plus the Zoom has a looper, the Digitech does not.
Purist mayl sniff about the artificial sound and the plastic construction. Get a life. This thing is a heck of a lot of fun and for $50, you can hardly go wrong. Well, except for one thing. It does not come with an AC adapter (although batteries are included). My Digitech adapter worked fine though. Hopefully you already have on that will work since the "recommended" Zoom adapter costs an outrageous $25.

product_title: Crescendo CR-20 Cup Caddy - Drink Holder - Clamping - Microphone Stand - Music Stand - Unique
review_headline: Good Unit For Disposable Bottles Or Cups
review_body:
Okay, so we\x27ve ordered several of these for the band. They work decent enough. The three things we noticed most:

1. Good for standard water/20 oz bottles and some 32 oz fast food drink cups.

2. When you receive the unit, you have to assemble the actual cup holder to the clamp unit - this connection results in ranges from good and tight on one unit to fairly loose on another unit (we have four of these total).

3. We have these positioned down low on mic stands that we use for personal monitors. As such, we keep them about 2 foot of the floor because trying to put a drink in or pull the drink out means we have to clear the speaker mounted on the stand. In this configuration, cups that have handles (e.g. coffee travel cups - which we use ALOT of!) do not work well. It seems to be the limitation of how wide the unit adjusts open.

So, all in all, a pretty good unit - as long as you want to use standard water bottles or disposable cups - but I would like to see them make the connection from cup holder to clamp tighter, as well as, make them to adjust a little wider for travel cups.

product_title: Dean Markley Blue Steel Acoustic Guitar Strings
review_headline: Punchy, bright and present, these are amazing strings
review_body: I have used Blue Steels on all my electrics for years and when I bought a lightly used Breedlove C250/CMe with the original D\x27Addario (And completely dead) strings I looked to Blue Steels.  They are somewhat reminiscent of the Blue Steel electric strings in that they are very clear, crisp and somewhat bright but they are definitely an acoustic string.  On my guitar they are very resonant and project very well. I generally prefer spruce topped acoustics but got this Breedlove with a cedar top because I loved the feel and playability of it.  I hoped that a brighter string would  offset the normal characteristics of a cedar top and add some sparkle and "Zing" to the tone.  They did that in spades.  They do have a rather unique "Wiry" quality to their sound, so if you are looking for that soft, round, very warm tone such as Martin Phosphor Bronze strings, you will likely be rather disappointed.  However, they provide excellent definition to your playing and even though I am not a finger-picker, they would probably respond well to that.  They bend well and hold their tuning amazingly well.  If you are looking for a bright, resonant, "Punchy" tone with gobs of presence these strings are for you.

product_title: JOYO PEDALS
review_headline: Decent delay for a great price.
review_body:
For the money spent, this pedal is nice. I will start by saying, however, that is is not a total digital delay. In a digital delay, there is no decay of notes played- it keeps repeating perfect copies of the note played. With analogue, there is more decay with each repeat (a copy of a copy of a copy, etc). Analogue delay is great and the pedal sounds good, but as a matter of technicality the title is a bit of a misnomer.

The construction is solid and I have no complaints about durability. It is (as advertised) true bypass and does not color your tone. The sound is good- other than the fact that it is actually analogue it sounds good. It is reasonably versatile and can get a decent range of delay tones. Maybe not ideal for the 800MM "Edge" sounds, but it can give anything from slap-back to Floyd-esque sounds. the pedal is good on it\x27s own, but I feel it works best stacked with other pedals on your board for extra delay, ambiance or texture.

Not amazing, but a very good, usable pedal at an affordable price.

product_title: Pyle-Pro PPEQ100 19\x27\x27 Rack Mount Dual 10 Band 4 Source Input Stereo Spectrum Graphic Equalizer
review_headline: An insult to the landfills it eventually fill up
review_body: It seems almost pointless to add yet another negative review of this product, but it so spectacularly fails on so many levels, I feel it is warranted.    The build quality is sub-par, even by today\x27s low standards of Chinese manufacturing. I can attest to the \x5C\x22Desinged in USA\x5C\x22 typo on the back panel, and I guess that\x27s a good indicator of the level of thought that went into this profoundly dreadful box. My unit arrived, new in box, well packed and complete with greasy fingerprints on the top of the unit.    From there, I powered it up and was shocked by the blinding level of the blue LEDs in the graphic EQ sliders. Folks, there are 20 ultra-bright LEDs on this unit, and they go to 11. If you are ever stranded on a desert island, the PPE100 could perhaps save you, just point it towards space and it would look like a nuclear launch. It\x27s like looking into the sun, highly not recommended.    As for touted \x5C\x22Stereo Spectrum Graphic Equalizer\x5C\x22, well actually, no its not. It does not close to approximating the VU levels of the frequencies being input. It certainly is entertaining to watch, much in the way you would watch a monkey in a cute hat ride around on a goat at a birthday party, but after about 15 seconds, the charm is gone (as are your eyes by this point because they were burned out by the 20 LEDs...)    The display also has bonus features in that it designates 500, 1000, 1500, and 2000 ms. This is of course meaningless... those indicators are on all the time and actually are not connected to any of the innards of the unit. Similarly, there is an indicator for the mightily mysterious Karaoke and SRS modes, which are also permanently on. No mention of these hidden benefits in the manual...it\x27s clear that the Pyle engineers simply sourced a VFD display from a Karaoke box.    To add insult to injury are the tiny, hard-to-read source buttons...    It\x27s almost like Pyle went on a mission to make this unit awful in every way, and the switchgear is no exception.    Tryingto switch from the CD to DVD sources? Well, first turn off the unit because those LEDs (remember them?) will blind you to the point where you can\x27t actually read the tiny print on the buttons. Wait 5 minutes and if you have regained your vision, find the appropriate source button. Turn the unit back on, and press the button from memory. Oh, and when you turn the unit off, it conveniently forgets which source button you had most recently pressed. It always reverts to Tuner. So you have to go through this pain EVERY TIME you turn the unit on.    As to the sound quality, this unit adds a not insignificant amount of noise and hiss. God forbid you put it within 80 meters of a computer...the noise level will be quite phenomenal.    You know, Pyle used to be a reputable company. Back in the day, they were known for good audio products, specifically drivers. Somewhere over the last 5 years, they lost their way. Pyle now churns out a broad catalog of absolute crap. And the PPEQ100 is probably one of the best indicators that Pyle thinks of its customers as unworthy idiots.    So, in closing, skip this one. It has no redeeming qualities and will be an insult to the landfills it eventually fills up.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-M50x Closed-Back Professional Studio Monitor Headphones
review_headline: Sound doesn\x27t at all live up to hype, and poorly suited for studio monitoring.
review_body:
The sound is mediocre at best, and well below that of some other less expensive headphones.
Low bass is exaggerated and not tight, mid-bass has a broad-spectrum muddiness, midrange is recessed.
Look at some of the poor reviews for this model that cite the same characteristics. They are right on the money.

And, don\x27t be suckered by the "Studio Monitor" label, which is nothing but marketing baloney.
The label is there because the uninformed consumer will think that means that these are "reference-quality" and highly accurate.
Neither of which is at all true.

First, professional recording engineers don\x27t use headphones as a reference for mixing, because even if a given pair of headphones were perfectly accurate, they can\x27t reproduce the interactions between two loudspeakers and the way the brain processes imaging when the sound of both the left and right speakers are heard by both ears. Therefore, a mix engineered using the best possible headphones will sound entirely different when played through speakers. Headphones aren\x27t used as references in the studio. Where headphones ARE used in the studio is for musicians to hear themselves play or sing while they are being recorded.

Second, the characteristics that make a great studio monitor headphone are the OPPOSITE of what makes a great high-fidelity listening headphone.

A good studio monitor headphone must be CLOSED BACK so they do not leak sound that will be picked up by the highly sensitive microphones used in a studio.

But, all else being equal, closed back headphones sound inferior to open-back headphones due to all of the resonances, standing waves, etc that take place inside the enclosure and the back pressure on the diaphragm. Open-back headphones are the way to go for the best sound.

SO, the truth is, a good studio monitor is NOT a great hi-fi can.

But, these headphones aren\x27t even good as studio monitors. They leak high frequency sound substantially, so I can\x27t wear them while tracking vocals. The mic pics them up. Second, the recessed midrange and excessive upper treble make it very difficult to sing when using these as a monitor.

Third, if you are a home/project studio experimenter who breaks convention and wants to use headphones as a reference for mixing despite the inherent drawbacks in doing so, these are quite poor for that due to the exaggerated bass and midbass muddiness. You would find yourself reducing these areas in your mix to get a sound that sounds balanced through these headphones, and you\x27d have a mix that sounded awful thin when played on something else.

If you are looking for high-fidelity headphones in this price range, the Grado SR-125e cost less, sound MUCH better, and put out more volume at a given volume setting. This is because they are more efficient. That allows you to get better sound as you can turn the volume down on your player where the internal headphone amp isn\x27t straining or distorting and still achieve desired listening levels. And, the Grado SR-80e is almost half the cost of this headphone and it sounds better as well.

The "Studio Monitor" label is a meaningless buzzword used to sell more headphones. If you were around when Compact Disc first came into being, headphone manufacturers were slapping the label "Digital Ready" on their headphones to sell to the ignorant. The term was meaningless and unquantifiable. Any headphone could play back a signal from a digital source such as a portable CD player just as well as it could play back a signal from a cassette Walkman. Whether it sounds any good doing so is another matter entirely. A $200 pair of quality headphones without the "Digital Ready" label are going to be able to reproduce the sound quality of a CD much better than a $5 drugstore pair with "Digital Ready" printed on them.

THE EXACT SAME PRINCIPLE applies to the "Studio Monitor" label.

Hi-fidelity cans these are not. Good studio monitors, for tracking or mixing, these are not.
It is a run-of-the-mill mid-fi product that is overpriced for the sound it delivers compared to less expensive and far superior products on the market.

However, the blue special edition models look quite nice.
If you are the kind of person that paints the "disco smile" curve on your equalizer, if exaggerated bass and treble is your idea of high-quality sound, and/or if wearing a nice looking piece of head jewelry is more important to you than the best possible sound for a given amount of $, you will probably love these headphones.

product_title: Electro-Harmonix Key 9 Electric Guitar Single Effect
review_headline: I wanted so much to love this thing..
review_body:
I cannot tell you how much my kind of thing this thing is - Hammond B3 is my favorite instrument, even though I\x27m a guitar player since I\x27m 9 years old..

The sounds are quite interesting, varying enough, warm.. the mellotron flutes sounds pretty wonderful..

But the tracking.. the tracking is late, and makes this really not usable as a guitar pedal. It feels like you\x27re not playing in real time, it feels like a MIDI controller.. I had a Casio guitar synthesizer that tracked organ sounds about as fast as this, and could do a million other things as well

Anyway, I would love to buy this thing again if they can figure out a way to make it track faster so that you can sound like you\x27re really playing an instrument

I plugged this into an old Mesa-Boogie Mark III, dialed in a crunchy sound to actually try to make it sound like an overdriven Leslie

but honestly even then it sounds a little bit clean - warm but clean even when driven - it\x27s a very difficult task and probably worth the money when it\x27s right. buy a Hammond B3 or give up, is what God, my kindergarten teacher, and Richard Wright say when I ask them.

product_title: Sony MDR7506 Professional Large Diaphragm Headphone
review_body:
These headphones are the choice if you don\x27t want to spend hundreds of dollars on some headphones because they have the name of an idiotic rapper. They sound fantastic. They have very rich and solid bass, and are very dynamic. I\x27ve seen mention of the bass lacking. If the bass lacks, it is not because these headphones aren\x27t capable. It is either 1) you only function on bass and know no other frequency or 2) you are listening to a recording that isn\x27t meant to have much bass.

I like these headphones because they have a great, well balanced sound with good clarity, they are not too terribly big, and they are VERY comfortable. I could easily wear these for hours if I needed to. They also keep the sound in pretty well and block out quite a bit of outside noise. The coiled cord isn\x27t the best for mobile use, but it is easily do-able for me. I like it not being as easy to snag on something. The construction seems fairly durable. I\x27ve had them for over a year and they look and work like when I got them.

These headphones are used by professionals and non-professionals all over for a reason.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-AD700 Open-air Dynamic Audiophile Headphones
review_body:
Let me state first and foremost that these headphones are not to be taken out places and roughed around like some other headphones. That being said these headphones are really solid. Have had my pair for roughly 4 years now and they\x27ve not failed me yet. They are getting quite old, so the wiring doesn\x27t always project to the right headphones, but that is the only real problem I\x27ve had so far.

They are EXTREMELY comfortable, even for a person who really dislikes headphones on my ears. I have worn these for multiple days of 8 hour stretches at my computer and felt no discomfort at all.

They do not trap sound well, nor do they filter sound out. It\x27s not bad, it\x27s just that you can hear and be heard by the people in the same room as you, depending on the volume.

They sound really, really solid. Very rich and great sound still.

For the price, if you don\x27t plan on taking your headphones outside of your studio/house/whatever, get these. They are awesome.

product_title: Tascam TM-2X Stereo X-Y Microphone for DSLR Cameras
review_headline: Exceptional sound, excellent for high SPL but still quite sensitive
review_body:
I intended to use my Nikon D5300 for video as well as still shots. In particular, I wanted to use it to take video of live music shows. However, my initial efforts using the camera\x27s built-in stereo microphones were in a word, dismal. The microphones in the camera had a very narrow frequency range with a noticeable notch in the middle, as well as virtually nonexistent stereo separation. I knew I needed to do better.

I did quite a bit of research, initially thinking I would go with a shotgun stereo mic, but after reading multiple reviews, decided to go with this Tascam mic. I already had a handheld Tascam digital recorder with very similar mics that made exceptional recordings. I had read several reviews complaining about the plastic shoes on this mic breaking. I figured I would do my best not to bash the mic when mounted (primarily on tripods when taking video) so that this would not be an issue.

The mic arrived, I noticed the box looked like it had been opened before. However, the mic inside was fully packaged. I unpacked it, and first looked at the boom/extension. When I picked it up, the shoe fell off of it. Looking closer, the piece of plastic connecting the shoe to the rest of the boom was in fact broken.

I figured I would use the mic to do testing, and when I picked it up, the shoe fell of it as well! It too had been broken. Obviously someone had broken the shoes on both the boom and the mic, then returned it - it had been refurbished (i.e. repackaged) and shipped out to me (by Amazon) as new! I was extremely unimpressed with this.

To Amazon\x27s credit, they had a replacement (new, this time) unit in my hands two days later, and paid for the return of the broken unit. I then got to use the new mic for the first time that weekend.

The results: spectacular! The difference in sound between the on-camera mics and this external mic are like night and day. The on-camera mics sound muddy and tonally narrow, with limited dynamics. The Tascam mic produces excellent sound, quite flat and with very good dynamics. The stereo imaging was excellent, and there was no evidence of overmodulation, despite the high SPL at the event.

My tests in a quiet room with these mics on my D5300 did produce an audible noise floor in the form of hiss, at probably -30dB. Some other reviews attribute this to the mics, however I tried plugging the mics into my Tascam recorder, and the hiss was not evident. Therefore I attribute the hiss to the preamp and/or phantom power supply inside the D5300, not the microphones themselves. When recording any kind of decent audio levels the hiss is not evident however.

With the boom installed, the sounds of autofocus motors in the lens are barely audible in recordings, and then only when the surrounding area is extremely quiet. Again, when recording any kind of audio level, autofocus motor noise will not be an issue.

Overall I am very pleased with the sound of these mics. I will continue to be vigilant in handling the mics when mounted to the camera to try to avoid the shoe breakage issue that is so clearly a problem with them. That said, the manner in which I saw them broken could very likely be easily fixed with application of some epoxy.
