product_title: Motion Sensor Light - Battery Powered - Efficient Wireless LED Nightlight - Stick-On Anywhere - Guaranteed High Performance and Great Customer Support
review_headline: Great for added security in an apartment!  Love these!
review_body:
I bought these for some extra security in my apartment -- there was a break-in a few doors down recently, and the management of the apartment complex decided to do absolutely nothing. So I bought a door alarm (GE Personal Security Door/Window Alarm, see here http://www.amazon.com/GE-Personal-Security-Window-Alarm/dp/B00032CIJQ/ref=cm_cd_al_qh_dp_t) and a couple of these lights. I mounted the lights right inside the door, so if it opens the lights turn on and the alarm goes off. I hoped the noise and the lights would scare away anyone who breaks in.

Anyway, I used 3M Command strips to mount these, and it works great! Actually I mounted the little magnet base with the 3M strips, so I can still grab the lights and use them as flashlights. What a great feature! I bought these because they use fewer batteries -- 3AAA instead of 4 -- than some of the competitors, yet the light output seems the same according to the specs.

I\x27m extremely happy with these lights, and as an added bonus they turn on when we come home after dark so we don\x27t have to fumble around in the dark with groceries or whatever. Every now and again they turn on for no apparent reason (we were watching a movie in the dark one night and one of them turned on, startling us a little). But there was no motion in the apartment that we could tell -- maybe there was a moth that flew by or something, who knows. Anyway, I\x27m glad I went with these as opposed to a competitor -- fewer batteries to charge or replace. These came with batteries that are still working great months later. I\x27d buy more of these if/when I need them.

product_title: Ecobee3 Thermostat, Wi-Fi, Remote Sensor, 1st Generation, Works with Amazon Alexa
review_headline: Wonderful solution to sweltering/freezing extremes in a 160 year old farm house with steam radiators and no zones
review_body:
This old house has single pipe steam radiators and an oil burning furnace/boiler. I love the clink and clank of the radiators heating up, but if the downstairs is comfortable, the upstairs is sweltering. If the upstairs is comfortable, the downstairs is freezing.

Two weeks ago, I installed the Ecobee3 main thermostat in the sitting room and the remote upstairs. The difference is amazing! The entire house is almost the same temp (the kitchen is still a little chillier than the rest of the house, but nothing like the ice box it was). At night we drop the temp to 59, during the day 64 and 68 in the evening - this is a few degrees warmer than the old thermostat yet the furnace doesn\x27t run as often and the sweltering/freezing extremes between the upstairs and downstairs is no more.

The simple display on the thermostat and app is great. No buttons and an intuitive touchscreen menu. Despite this simplicity, when you log in to your thermostat via the ecobee website, you have a wealth of details available as graphs and downloadable spreadsheets. These show (at 5-minute increments) the exact temps inside, outside, and when and how long the furnace runs. Over the past two weeks we\x27ve had outside temps in the single digits as well as a mild spell where it touched 50 during the day, yet inside our temps were very even and comfortable - upstairs and down.

The first night after installing the Ecobee3 I was reading in bed at 11:20pm and I heard the radiator heating up. Puzzled at why the furnace would kick on so late at night, I opened the app and found that I had made a mistake when setting the schedule -- all other nights were set for the sleeping temp to drop to 59 at 10:30p. But for that day of the week I had set the sleep temp to start at 11:30p - hence the furnace was just following the schedule and keeping the house at 67. I fixed the schedule on the app and two seconds later I heard the furnace shut down. Problem solved without getting out of bed.

Installation: The Ecobee3 replaced a 10-year old Honeywell programmable thermostat that used only 2 wires (R + W) and AA batteries for power. The Ecobee3 needs a C wire (24v common) to power the unit. Unfortunately, the Carlin 60200 circuit controller on my furnace doesn\x27t have a 24v terminal. I simply purchased a 24v doorbell transformer from home deport for $11 and pulled the C wire from it with the R + W coming from the Carlin.

I can\x27t believe that this thermostat has made such a difference - absolutely love it!

product_title: Frigidaire 5303918549 Evaporator Motor Kit for Refrigerator
review_body: My 2008 Kenmore fridge had been getting NOISY over the past few months.  A good smack on the side would sometimes stop the whining noise, but it got more frequent, and besides the irritating noise, I wanted to replace the bad part before it suddenly failed and left me with spoiled food and a puddle of water on my kitchen floor...  Found this was the correct replacement part by entering the model# from the sticker inside the refrigerator on: http://www.searspartsdirect.com/ (searspartsdirect DOT com).  I ordered this item from Amazon seller: partshousesupply and (apparently unlike some other sellers, according to several other reviewers) they included the pictured wiring harness.  It was a perfect fit for my fridge, which made installation significantly simpler and faster.  There are a couple other evaporator motors on Amazon that cost a couple dollars less, but the time saved is easily worth the price difference, and I\x27m quite glad Amazon had the exact replacement part.  Since I took apart my freezer 6 months prior to see what was wrong, I remembered the tricks to taking it apart and reassembling it (including the hassles with the ice maker) and it only took me a total of 30 minutes to swap the motor, so nothing even melted.  Replacement part is working fine (but only time will tell if it holds up), my refrigerator is now nice and quiet operating again, and I expect now has quite a few more years of life in it...  This motor and [[ASIN:B001DPOAHU the thermostat]] are the only two moving parts that are likely to fail, and are both easily user serviceable.  They can both be swapped with non-identical replacements, but having the correct part will save you lots of time.  Will come back and update my review, for better or worse depending on how long it lasts, after I\x27ve had it in use for a year or two...  The click on/off is a bit noisier than my old one, making me a bit concerned, but still working fine (July 2015).

product_title: Rinnai EX08CP Wall Mounted Direct Ventilation Furnace Propane
review_headline: My plumber recommended this propane heater and I was told by the ...
review_body:
I have a cabin in Big Bear Lake, CA and the altitude is about 7,000 ft. I have propane gas and the cabin is only 370 sq ft. My plumber recommended this propane heater and I was told by the same plumber that this heater would have no problem heating up my small cabin. Well winter is here and the plumber was wrong. At night when the temperature gets into the 30s or lower outside the heater can never get higher than 54 degrees inside (and this is with a electric heater turned on as well). This makes for a lot of snuggling, which is okay if you like to snuggle but not okay if you need to get up and walk to the bathroom or the kitchen, etc.

Since the heater can never get the room warm it constantly runs at night and sucks up the propane. This gets very costly to run.

My biggest pet peeve with the heater is not the lack of heat but the fact that you need electricity to run it. I purposely bought a propane heater so that I can have heat regardless if my electricity works or not. Now I found that I have to have the heater plugged in to run it. This defeats the purpose of buying a propane heater as a safety issue. Now if the electricity goes out I will not have heat and that can be deadly when it gets below freezing outside. I didn\x27t read anything in the ad at the time I bought it that said it needed electricity to run so I was very disappointed when I discovered this fact.

Unfortunately I bought the heater at the end of last winter and didn\x27t test it until this winter so I can\x27t return it. I would give less than one star if that was an option.

product_title: Luxe Bidet Neo 180 (Elite Series) - Self Cleaning Dual Nozzle - Fresh Water Non-Electric Mechanical Bidet Toilet Attachment w/ Strong Faucet Valves and Metal Hoses
review_headline: Must have if you use toilets!
review_body:
I\x27ve never used a bidet before ordering this, so I didn\x27t really know what to expect. My only regret is waiting 3 weeks to install it. I\x27ve had it on my toilet for 9 months so far, and it\x27s still works great. These should be on everyone\x27s toilet. It gets you much cleaner than toilet paper. It pretty much pays for itself, because I barely use any toilet paper anymore. The 5 year old had issues with wiping, but after I taught him how to use this, he doesn\x27t have any issues (or skid marks).
It was very easy to install. I did not get the version with the warm water, and I\x27m glad I didn\x27t. The cold water is not an issue after the very first use. I have recommended this to everyone I know.
